```bash
         2026-02-19 2026-03-16 2026-05-21 2026-08-20 2026-11-07; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c WMT; done
```

Every 8-K, 10-Q and 10-K of January 2024 to November 2026 was read (51 filings: 38 8-Ks and two 8-K/As, 8 10-Qs, 3 10-Ks), directly,
with no delegated transcription; the 10-Qs were searched for guidance and carry none. The records are generated by script from the
transcribed raw figures; 472 more strings were checked with `verbatim.py` (2,985 in all), every quoted fragment of the new notes among
them. Thresholds (rule T), signals and the engine are unchanged. Decided on 2026-11-08, before any 2024-2026 date was scored:

- **The end of the range is 2026-11-06,** the last complete week (built on Sunday 2026-11-08 from a price cache fetched that day, whose
  last bar is Friday's close). The Q3 FY27 release (due in mid-November) is after it. The newest dates have no two-year outcome yet.
- **The three-for-one split** (the SHW 2021 encoding, the sheet's first `splits` record). The 8-K of 2024-01-30 (17:40 ET, after the
  close, so published 2024-01-31) announces it; trading on the new basis starts 2024-02-26, the effective date, which matches the price
  data. Until then the models stay on the old basis (the price as traded is Yahoo's split-adjusted close times three); from it every
  per-share fact published before it is divided by three (the EPS history, the guides, the dividend) and share counts are multiplied by
  three. The Q4 FY24 release (2024-02-20) guides on both bases ("$6.70 to $7.12 pre-split; $2.23 to $2.37 post-split"); the pre-split range
  is the guide, published before the split, and the builder's division gives $2.233-2.373. The P/E percentiles run continuously across it
  (the median is 20.2x on 2024-02-21 and 20.3x on 2024-03-01).
- **Three 10-K vintages, Item 6 reserved.** The FY2024 10-K (accepted 2024-03-15 16:54 ET, dated Monday 2024-03-18), FY2025 (2025-03-14
  16:40 ET, dated 2025-03-17) and FY2026 (2026-03-13 16:06 ET, dated 2026-03-16) move the history to fiscal 2015-2024, 2016-2025 and
  2017-2026, each with its three income-statement years and earlier years from the latest 10-K that reports them. Years taken from
  filings published before the split keep their own dates (`eps_published`, `shares_published`), so the builder divides only those.
  First-year diluted shares: 2015's 3,243M (FY2017 10-K), 2016's 3,217M (FY2018 10-K), 2017's 3,112M (FY2019 10-K), each pre-split.
- **EPS: the company's adjusted figure, each year, from the latest release that publishes it:** FY24 $6.65 before the split (reported
  $1.91 after it; the Q4 FY24 release, published before the split, and then $2.22 in the Q4 FY25 release), FY25 $2.51 (reported $2.41), FY26
  $2.64 (reported $2.73: net gains on equity investments, $722 million of incremental non-cash share-based compensation, legal matters,
  reorganization). FY22 and FY23 keep $6.46 and $6.29 from releases published before the split: no later release repeats them. No year is
  excluded.
- **Guides, all in numbers and at constant currency:** the next quarter's net sales and adjusted EPS (except Q4 of each year and Q2 FY26's
  EPS) and the fiscal year's: FY25 +3.0-4.0% and $6.70-7.12 pre-split, then +3.75-4.75% and $2.35-2.43, then +4.8-5.1% and $2.42-2.47; FY26
  +3.0-4.0% and $2.50-2.60, +3.75-4.75% and $2.52-2.62, +4.8-5.1% and $2.58-2.63; FY27 +3.5-4.5% and $2.75-2.85, then +4.0-5.0% and
  $2.80-2.87. The Q1 FY25 update, "High-end or slightly above original guidance", is words (`fy_words`; the ranges stand), and the Q1 FY26
  and Q1 FY27 tables say "Unchanged" (the ranges stand). The next-quarter net sales guide is method r2's first choice and feeds BASE on every
  date but those after a Q3 print, which take the fiscal-year guide. The leap-year and VIZIO effects the guides state are in the notes.
- **Operating one-offs, release by release** (the 2015-2017 rule, from each release's adjusted operating income): Q4 FY24's year-ago
  $849 million; Q1 FY25's $255 million of reorganization (and Q1 FY26's year-ago); Q2 FY25's year-ago $93 million; Q4 FY25's $99 million
  opioid-related legal benefit (a benefit, so the margin is lower without it; and Q4 FY26's year-ago); Q2 FY26's $440 million of legal
  matters and $150 million of reorganization (and Q2 FY27's year-ago); Q3 FY26's $722 million of incremental share-based compensation net
  of a $155 million legal reversal; Q1 FY27's $181 million of reorganization.
- **The Total U.S. comparable sales figure leaves the filings.** From the Q4 FY26 release (2026-02-19) the comparable sales table gives
  Walmart U.S. and Sam's Club U.S. only, and the FY2026 10-K and the 10-Qs give no Total U.S. figure either. The AAPL Mac-unit rule applies
  (as for NIKE's futures and PepsiCo's servings): the signal keeps its name, thresholds and weight and scores BASE with no value ("n/r"),
  and no other measure replaces it (Walmart U.S. is a segment, a different measure); the note keeps the segment rows. The franchise line
  says the FY2026 10-K gives no Total U.S. figure (a builder change, text only). The Q4 FY25 comp (+4.7%) compares 14 weeks with 13, as
  published.
- **Nasdaq** (the PEP 2017 encoding, `listings`; display only). The 8-K of 2025-11-20 (06:58 ET, Item 3.01) moves the listing: NYSE trading
  ends at the close of 2025-12-08 and Nasdaq trading begins 2025-12-09, so the models say Nasdaq from 2025-12-12.
- **A renamed reporting line:** Sam's Club U.S. from the Q4 FY25 release (2025-02-20), the first whose segment table uses it (the ACN rule).
- **Dividends:** $0.83 a year from the FY2024 10-K (2024-03-18; the Q4 FY24 release says only "raises annual dividend 9%"), $0.94 from the
  FY2025 10-K, and $0.99 from the Q4 FY26 release (2026-02-19), the first release of the series to state a rate ("Increased annual dividend
  to $0.99 per share"; the FY14 precedent), repeated by the FY2026 10-K. The FY2023 vintage's $2.28 becomes $0.76 at the split.
- **ECOMMERCE stays on the watch list** in each 10-K's words; the FY2026 10-K adds "emerging agentic shopping tools and platforms" to the
  competitors and "more rapid development of AI capabilities and agentic tools by these competitors" to the risk. GENAI's registered
  scope (software seats, IT services, BPO, professional information, search, education, mobility) does not name retail, and its dated
  evidence names no retailer, so GENAI is not recorded; the words stay in the ECOMMERCE quote. The FY2025 and FY2026 10-Ks name AI as
  Walmart's own investment (the offering side, text only). No filing names GLP-1 drugs or weight-loss medication.
- **Adds nothing:** the 8-K of 2024-02-23 (the certificate of amendment), the investment-community 8-K of 2025-04-09 (the Q1 and FY26
  outlook "remains unchanged", in words), the CEO succession (2025-11-14 and the 8-K/A of 2026-01-16), the other officer, director, vote,
  charter and trading-plan 8-Ks, the derivative-settlement notice (2024-10-18), the debt 8-Ks (2025-04-28, 2026-04-30, 2026-10-23) and the
  10-Qs.
- **Builder changes (the 835 dates of 2008-2023 rebuild byte-identical):** `listings`, the split note in the EPS comment, and the franchise
  line for a year with no Total U.S. comparable sales figure. The firewall's generic plant already covers a later split and a later listing.

## RCL (Royal Caribbean Cruises): the twelfth ticker, in staging

The RCL series is built apart from ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, AVGO, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW and WMT and shares nothing with them but the
machinery: its own fact sheet (`retro/facts/RCL.json`), builder (`retro/build_rcl.py`, the SHW builder with a cruise-line guide encoding)
and engine (`retro/templates/rcl_engine.py.tmpl`, the WMT engine with cruise-line signals). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter,
outcome or finding of another ticker enters an RCL model, and neither does the live `rcl_signal_model.py` or any profile of Royal Caribbean
in `data/business_profiles.json` (2026 judgements, not read for this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/RCL/`, beside the others,
with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`.

Royal Caribbean filed as a foreign private issuer until 2004: its annual reports for FY1998 to FY2003 are on Form 20-F (the FY1998-FY2000
ones plain text), with quarterly releases on Form 6-K; the FY2004 report is its first 10-K. EDGAR holds no annual report before the FY1998
20-F, so 1996 and 1997 come from the five-year tables of the FY1998-FY2001 20-Fs. Read for the history and the decade's signal values: the
selected financial data, statistics and results of operations of the FY1998-FY2003 20-Fs and the FY2004-FY2008 10-Ks, and the Q4
releases of 1998-2006 for full-year figures excluding one-offs. Read for the prints and guides: every 8-K and 10-Q of January 2007 to
January 2010 (53 8-Ks, two of them amendments, and 9 10-Qs, the fuel-supplement, dividend, H1N1 and financing 8-Ks among them). All by Opus directly, with no
delegated transcription. The 2007 releases print their statements as images; they were read as images and every figure was taken from the
same quarter's 10-Q, which prints them as text. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the transcribed raw figures, so every
yield, cost, margin, growth rate and rule-T value is computed, not typed; 378 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own
filings: every statement row behind a print, every stated yield and cost change, every guide table, every quoted sentence, every
five-year row behind the history and rule T. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (converted from UTC; before 2002 EDGAR
gives the filing date only). Decided on 2026-11-08, before any RCL outcome was computed:

- **Fiscal calendar.** Royal Caribbean's fiscal year is the calendar year. The four dates of January 2008 have FY2007 as the current year
  (its EPS guide), until the Q4 2007 print adds FY07 on 2008-01-30.
- **Prices as traded.** Royal Caribbean's only split, two-for-one on 1998-08-03, precedes every date and every per-share fact in the fact
  sheet (the FY1998 20-F is already on the post-split basis), so Yahoo's series is the price as traded: $38.77 on 2008-01-04.
- **Release timing.** The earnings 8-Ks were accepted before the open (Q2 2007 09:10 ET, Q1 2008 08:59, Q3 2008 09:06, Q4 2008 08:44, Q2
  2009 08:55, Q3 2009 08:46) or during the session (Q3 2007 09:34, Q4 2007 10:22, Q1 2009 09:41), each on a Monday to Thursday, so a print
  dates its week the next trading day. The Q2 2008 release was accepted 2008-07-21 18:30 ET, after the close, so it is dated 2008-07-22 and
  its week's date is 2008-07-23 (the AVGO rule). The FY2006 10-K, accepted 2007-02-28 17:17 ET, is dated 2007-03-01; the FY2007 (2008-02-19
  07:25 ET) and FY2008 (2009-02-24 07:33 ET) 10-Ks keep their dates.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it** (the five-year selected financial data): the FY2006 vintage takes 2002-2006
  from the FY2006 10-K, 2001 from the FY2005 10-K, 2000 from the FY2004 10-K, 1999 from the FY2003 20-F, 1998 from the FY2002 20-F and 1997
  from the FY2001 20-F. Revenue is total revenues. Diluted shares of the first year come from the latest filing that reports them (1997's
  152,174K, FY2001 20-F; 1998's 181,165K, FY2002 20-F; 1999's 186,456K, FY2003 20-F). The Q4 2007 and Q4 2008 releases extend the history
  with their years until the 10-K, which moves the window to 1998-2007 and 1999-2008. The 1997 acquisition of Celebrity (from July 1, 1997,
  for shares; 1997 revenue +42.9%) and the Pullmantur acquisition of November 2006 (consolidated from 2007 on a two-month lag) stay in, as
  published (the LOW and PEP rule).
- **EPS** is diluted EPS before extraordinary items and the cumulative effect of accounting changes (the NKE rule): 1997 $1.20 ($1.15 after
  an extraordinary loss), 2005 $3.03 ($3.26 after the change in drydock accounting). The company's figures excluding one-offs replace GAAP
  where a filing publishes them (the ACN rule), each from the latest filing that publishes it: 1998 $1.93 and 1999 $2.15 ("comparable EPS",
  the Q4 1999 release; GAAP $1.83 and $2.06), 2001 $1.65 ("The comparable figures for 2001", excluding the effects of September 11 and ships
  out of service) and 2002 $1.72 (excluding the P&O Princess termination proceeds and a litigation charge), both from the Q4 2002 release.
  EITF 04-8 later restated GAAP for 2001 ($1.32 to $1.31) and 2002 ($1.79 to $1.76); no figure excluding the one-offs was published on the
  new basis, so the excluding figures keep their own (the UNP 2005 rule). The 2005 First Choice gain, the 2006 Alstom settlement gain, the
  2008 restructuring charge and legal-settlement gain stay in (no figure excluding them). **No year is excluded:** no year's one-offs reach
  half its income.
- **Guides: EPS, capacity and Net Yields in numbers.** Every release guides the next quarter and the year: diluted EPS, capacity (the change
  in APCD) and Net Yields (net revenue per APCD); from the Q1 2009 release also Net Yields on a constant dollar basis. Approximate figures
  ("approx. 7%", "≈ 9%") are taken as published, a single figure ("Around $1.40") is a point and "Flat" is 0. Method r2 maps them as follows:
  - current-FY EPS: the midpoint of the latest fiscal-year EPS guide: FY07 $2.825 ($2.80-2.85, Q3 2007 release) to 2008-01-25; FY08 $3.30
    ($3.20-3.40, Q4 2007 release), $2.925 from 2008-04-25, $2.60 from 2008-07-23 (including $0.07 of restructuring) and $2.755 from
    2008-10-29; FY09 $1.40 from 2009-01-30, $1.35 from 2009-04-24, $0.75 from 2009-07-30 and $0.70 from 2009-11-04;
  - BASE growth and the growth factor: the net revenue the next-quarter guide implies, (1 + Net Yields) x (1 + capacity) - 1, Net Revenues
    being Net Yields times APCD by the company's own definition. On a constant-currency basis where the guide states one (Q2 2009 -8.9%, Q3
    2009 -13.4% to -12.4%); where only the fiscal year is guided at constant currency, that one (the ACN fallback, per print: the Q3 2009
    release gives Q4 as reported only, so BASE takes FY2009's -8.6% to -7.5%); before 2009 no guide is at constant currency, so the next
    quarter's as published (the SHW and MSFT reading): Q4 2007 +23.8% (Net Yields ≈ 9% on capacity 13.6%, including Pullmantur), Q1 2008
    +16.4%, Q2 2008 +7.5%, Q3 2008 +6.0%, Q4 2008 -2.2% to -1.2%, Q1 2009 -10.2% to -8.1%;
  - a guide given including and excluding Pullmantur (the 2007 releases' "Including Pullmantur" and "Comparable" columns) keeps the
    consolidated figure, and the comparable one goes in the note (the ACN rule for a guide given with and without an item);
  - no margin guide in numbers, so no margin step: the margin signal takes the latest quarter's operating-margin change. The Net Cruise
    Cost and fuel guides, the next quarter's EPS range and every statement in words are shown in the guide line and feed no input.
- **Dividends,** from the 10-K that states the rate, then the 8-K that ends it: $0.15 a quarter (FY2006 and FY2007 10-Ks), none from
  2008-11-19 (the Board "decided today to discontinue the company’s common stock dividend", 8-K accepted 2008-11-18 16:12 ET, after the
  close), none in the FY2008 10-K.
- **Signals.** Six, with ACN's weights: the change in Net Yields (0.20), the change in Net Cruise Costs per APCD (0.20, lower is better),
  total revenue growth (0.15), the change in occupancy (0.15, in basis points) and in the operating margin (0.15), and the theme slot at
  2/4. The company calls Net Yields "the most relevant measure of our pricing performance" and changes in Net Cruise Costs "the most
  relevant indicator of our performance", and every release states both. Each value is derived from the release's raw figures: Net Yields
  are total revenues less commissions, transportation and other and onboard and other expenses, per APCD; Net Cruise Costs are total cruise
  operating expenses plus marketing, selling and administrative expenses less the same two lines, per APCD; occupancy is as the release
  states it; each against the year-ago quarter in the same release. The builder re-derives them and checks Net Yields and Net Cruise Costs
  against the change each release states (10 of 10 each, within 0.1pp). The values are as reported, including Pullmantur and currency, as
  the decade's are.
- **Thresholds by rule T** over 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04, each change from the latest
  filing published by then that reports both years (the 20-Fs' and 10-Ks' five-year tables). No filing states Net Yields before 2001 (the
  FY2000 20-F says net revenue per available lower berth for 2000 "was approximately the same as in 1999": words, no value) or Net Cruise
  Costs per APCD before 2002, so those signals have six and five values (rule T takes the annual values the filings report, the AVGO rule):
  2001 and 2002 as each 20-F states them, 2003-2006 derived from the 10-Ks' Net Revenues, Net Cruise Costs and APCD. Seams stay in, as
  published: Celebrity in 1997, the FY2003 20-F's reclassification of port costs (the 2001 Net Yields change is on the earlier basis),
  Pullmantur in 2006. The values and the raw figures are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives the values and refuses to
  build if the engine's thresholds differ.

  | Signal | 1997-2006 | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | Net Yields change (2001-2006) | -9.1, -0.7, -0.6, 9.19, 7.37, 3.41 % | -20 / -9 / 1 / 9 % |
  | Net Cruise Costs per APCD (2002-2006, lower is better) | -2.2, 4.93, 5.61, 6.31, 6.44 % | 7 / 6 / 6 / -2 % |
  | total revenue growth | 42.86, 35.96, -3.42, 12.56, 9.75, 9.19, 10.19, 20.38, 7.63, 6.66 % | -17 / -3 / 10 / 43 % |
  | occupancy change | 290, 100, -50, -30, -260, 270, -130, 250, 90, -10 bp | -560 / -260 / 40 / 290 bp |
  | operating margin change | -33.5, 288.4, 32.0, 101.5, -538.8, 155.8, -213.9, 263.8, 123.3, -136.0 bp | -1140 / -540 / 70 / 290 bp |

  Net Cruise Costs per APCD has a median (5.61%) and a worst year (6.44%) that both round to 6%, so its BASE and BULL thresholds coincide:
  a quarter at or under 6% scores BULL, one over it BEAR, and none scores BASE (rule T applied as written; see the sensitivity below).
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2** (the SHW and WMT precedent). The "why" quotes the 10-K: "We are the world’s second largest cruise
  company", "We compete principally on the basis of quality of ships, quality of service, variety of itineraries and price", "We may lose
  business to competitors throughout the vacation market", and "Demand for cruises has been and is expected to continue to be dependent on
  the strength of the economies in the countries in which we market our products" (the FY2008 10-K: "The demand for cruises is affected by
  international, national and local economic conditions"). Demand that depends on the economy is not earnings that are the cycle (XOM's
  "fundamentally a commodity business"), so CYCLICAL is not used; the kind changes the class label only. No disruption theme in
  `taxonomy_eras.json` is live for a cruise company in 2008-2009, so the watch list is empty and the builder refuses events until a theme
  encoding is decided.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): Royal Caribbean reports one segment, so the bridge splits the year's revenues pro rata
  to the latest year's passenger ticket and onboard and other revenues, the total from the fiscal-year net revenue guide (at constant
  currency where stated) applied to total revenues. The EPS check runs on the last full year's operating margin less its other expense
  (interest and other, net); the statement of operations has no income tax line (the Section 883 exemption).
- **Adds nothing:** the fuel-supplement 8-Ks (2008-03-11, 2008-04-23, 2008-06-17, 2008-10-24, 2008-12-05; the first "reaffirms its previous
  yield guidance"); the dividend 8-K's "reaffirms the guidance it then provided"; the H1N1 8-K of 2009-06-09 and the bond-offering 8-K of
  2009-06-29, which give per-share impacts against the April guide ($0.22 for H1N1, $0.12 of fuel, about $0.10 of currency and hedging, about
  $0.05 of interest) without restating a range (the WMT 2010 rule); the Island Cruises and Oceanic sales (2008-10-06, 2009-03-12: "a small
  gain"); the financing, credit-agreement, officer and director 8-Ks; the 8-K/A of 2008-07-24, which corrects only cash-flow lines; and the
  10-Qs beyond the 2007 statement figures (the releases come first and carry every guide).
- **Anachronism list:** Royal Caribbean names first seen in its filings after the start of 2008 (TUI Cruises, Oasis of the Seas, Allure of
  the Seas, Oasis-class, Celebrity Silhouette, Celebrity Reflection, Quantum of the Seas, Celebrity Edge, Silversea, Perfect Day at CocoCay,
  Icon of the Seas) join `taxonomy_eras.json`, each dated from the first Royal Caribbean filing that uses it (EDGAR full-text search). No
  model of any ticker contains them, so no output changes. RCL's source ids are `RC1`-`RC28` (`W0` the prices).

Controls: altering one value of each print (and each Q4 print's full-year EPS), guide (its EPS range, its next-quarter Net Yields and, in
2009, its fiscal-year constant-currency Net Yields), vintage and the dividend changes no date before its publication and changes the
first weekly date on or after it whenever the value is in scope (43 controls; the seven that change nothing are the Q2 2007 print, never
the latest on a 2008 date, and the six guides of the Q4 2006, Q1 2007 and Q2 2007 releases, superseded before 2008). A scan of the 105
models for the figures, notes, guides, texts and sources of every later print, guide, vintage and dividend finds none before its first
publication (0 of 7,659 pairs); no model carries a calendar year after its date outside an FY label. Rebuilding the 2008 dates of ACN, UNP,
LOW, AAPL, NKE, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW and WMT and the 2009 dates of AVGO changes nothing (584 models).

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **2008: CHEAP on all 53 dates;** BUY on 49 and ACCUMULATE on four (2008-01-04, 2008-08-08, 2008-08-15, 2008-09-05). Robustness is 6 to 8
  of 8 throughout.
- **2009: CHEAP to April, then RICH.** CHEAP on 19 dates (2009-01-09 to 2009-04-17, and 2009-06-12, 2009-06-26, 2009-07-02, 2009-07-10),
  FAIR on 7 (between 2009-04-24 and 2009-07-17) and RICH on 26 (2009-05-08, 2009-06-05, 2009-07-24, and every date from 2009-07-30). From
  2009-07-30 Ratio B is infinite: the price is above the BULL case. The legacy tier is BUY on 16, ACCUMULATE on 9, WATCHLIST on 2 and AVOID
  on 25.
- **The EPS anchor carries the call.** The P/E window barely moves (10th percentile 8.8-9.9x, median 13.8-14.6x, 90th percentile about 21x),
  while the current-FY EPS falls from $3.30 (FY08, January 2008) to $2.60 (July 2008) and from $1.40 (FY09, January 2009) to $0.70
  (November 2009). On guided EPS the stock trades at 2.4-13.7x in 2008 (the 0th-37th percentile of its own window) and 3.4-12.7x from January
  to 2009-07-24, then 19.5-37.7x (the 86th-100th percentile) from 2009-07-30.
- **The EPP floor falls with the lows.** The median of the calendar-year P/E lows is 9-11x in 2008 and 8x in 2009,
  once 2008's low (2.5x on 2008-11-21, on FY08 EPS) joins 2001's 5.1x. The price sits under the floor on 34 dates (2008-06-20 to 2008-07-18,
  and 2008-09-26 to 2009-04-09; 78% under it on 2008-11-21) and 144-371% over it from 2009-07-30.
- **BEAR is 2001** (-28.6%/yr: 2000's $2.31 to 2001's comparable $1.65) at the 10th-percentile P/E: $13-17 in 2008, $3-7 in 2009. The
  price is below the BEAR price on 13 dates between 2008-11-07 and 2009-02-20, so Ratio B is negative there. XBULL is the 2003-2005 run
  (+46.1%/yr); BULL is the decade CAGR (+10.5% over 1997-2006, +4.3% over 1998-2007, +2.5% over 1999-2008) or BASE where higher.
- **BASE follows the guides and the share count.** Diluted shares grew 4.1%/yr over 1997-2006 (the Celebrity shares of 1997 and convertible
  dilution), 1.9%/yr over 1998-2007 and 1.5%/yr over 1999-2008, so the buyback term is negative: BASE is +19.7%/yr in January 2008 (the
  Pullmantur-inflated Q4 2007 guide of +23.8%), +13.1% from the Q4 2007 print and +14.6% from the FY2007 10-K, +5.7% from Q1 2008,
  +4.1% from Q2 2008, -3.6% from Q3 2008, -10.8% from Q4 2008 (-10.7% from the FY2008 10-K), -10.4% from Q1 2009, -14.4% from Q2 2009 and
  -9.6% from Q3 2009.
- **The proxy composite** is 2.15 (Q3 2007) and 2.35 (Q4 2007: Net Yields +11.0% with Pullmantur at XBULL, Net Cruise Costs +13.4% at BEAR),
  3.00 on Q1 2008 (every signal at BULL or better), 2.00 on Q2 2008, 2.20 on Q3 and Q4 2008, then 1.75 on Q1 2009 (Net Yields -13.5%,
  revenue -7.2%, occupancy -320bp and the operating margin -629bp at BEAR, Net Cruise Costs -7.0% at XBULL), 1.90 on Q2 2009 and 2.05 on Q3
  2009. Falling fuel prices and a stronger dollar put Net Cruise Costs at XBULL through 2009.

How far each call moves the classes (the 105 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- GAAP EPS for 1998, 1999, 2001 and 2002 instead of the company's comparable figures: 6 classes (CHEAP to FAIR on 2008-08-08, 2008-08-15,
  2008-09-05, 2009-06-12, 2009-06-26 and 2009-07-02) and 9 tiers;
- forward growth on Net Yields alone (capacity left out): 2 classes (CHEAP to FAIR on 2008-01-04 and 2008-01-25) and 5 tiers; the Q4 2007
  guide on the comparable basis (Net Yields ≈ 2% on capacity 4.7%, excluding Pullmantur): the same 2 classes and 4 tiers;
- the 2009 guides as reported instead of at constant currency: 1 class (2009-05-29, FAIR to RICH), no tier;
- the June 2009 8-Ks read as an EPS guide of $0.86 ($1.35 less the stated impacts): 3 classes (2009-07-02 to 2009-07-17, to RICH) and 3 tiers;
- Net Cruise Costs per APCD scored BASE on every date (the signal whose BASE and BULL coincide): 11 classes, all between 2009-04-24 and
  2009-07-17 (to RICH), no tier; every signal at its BEAR value: 20 classes (8 between 2008-05-02 and 2008-09-12, 12 between 2009-04-17
  and 2009-07-17, toward FAIR or RICH), no tier; every signal at XBULL: 10 classes (2009-04-24 to 2009-07-24, toward CHEAP), no tier.
Every move falls in the months where the class already changes from week to week (August-September 2008, April-July 2009) or in January
2008; the CHEAP calls of October 2008 to mid-April 2009 and the RICH calls from 2009-07-30 hold under all of them.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows that yields collapsed in 2009 while costs fell: the two measures the company names as its
  most relevant, with revenue, occupancy and the operating margin (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; Net Cruise Costs scored at
  BASE moves 11 classes in 2009);
- the company's comparable EPS for 1998, 1999, 2001 and 2002 in the history, 2001's excluding the estimated effects of September 11 (6
  classes move at GAAP);
- the net revenue implied by the Net Yields and capacity guides as method r2's revenue guide, and the consolidated 2007 guides including
  Pullmantur (2 classes move either way, both in January 2008);
- the June 2009 per-share impacts read as no guide (3 classes move if they are netted into one);
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL (the class label only), on a 10-K that ties demand to the economy but does not call its earnings the cycle;
- the 2007 statement figures read from images and taken from the 10-Qs (the same figures, checked by eye against the images).

### RCL 2010-2013

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds; the fact sheet only gains facts (its
2008-2009 content is unchanged and the 105 earlier models rebuild byte for byte). Read: every 8-K and 10-Q of February 2010 to February
2014 (52 8-Ks, one an amendment, and 12 10-Qs) and the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks, all by Opus directly; every release prints its statements as
text. 964 strings across both series were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings, 964 found. Decided on 2026-11-08, before
any 2010-2013 outcome was computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (08:35-09:28 ET) except Q2 2011, accepted 2011-07-27 17:18 ET, after
  the close, so it is dated 2011-07-28 (its week's date 2011-07-29). The Q1 2012 release came on a Friday before the open (2012-04-20 08:37
  ET), so its week's date is that day (the UNP 2014 rule). The FY2009 and FY2010 10-Ks (2010-02-23 16:36 and 2011-02-24 16:44 ET) are dated
  the next trading day; the FY2011 (2012-02-29 09:02) and FY2012 (2013-02-25 08:01) 10-Ks keep their dates.
- **History.** Four more vintages, each year from the latest filing that reports it: FY2009 (2000-2009), FY2010 (2001-2010), FY2011
  (2002-2011) and FY2012 (2003-2012); the first year's diluted shares from the FY2004 (2000: 192,935K), FY2005 (2001: 202,004K), FY2006
  (2002: 209,565K) and FY2007 (2003: 211,175K) 10-Ks. The Q4 2009-Q4 2012 prints extend the history until the 10-K.
- **EPS.** FY2009 $0.75 is a trough with no listed one-off: it stays. FY2010 $2.51 keeps Q1 2010's legal settlement gain, which the
  release states only per share ("The results included a $0.39 per share gain from a previously announced legal settlement") with no
  figure excluding it (the 2008 legal-settlement precedent; under half the year's income). The Q2 2011 release revised FY2009 to $0.71 and
  FY2010 to $2.37 ("Management identified an error in the previous accounting treatment of interest expense"; "This revision is not a
  restatement"), and the FY2011 10-K carries the revised figures: from 2011-07-28 they replace $0.75 and $2.51 (the SHW `restates` rule),
  and the FY2011 guide on the revised basis ($2.85-2.95) is used, its "would have been $3.05 to $3.15" in the note. FY2012 is the company's
  $1.97 "before the non-cash impairment charge" of $413.9 million on Pullmantur (GAAP $0.08; the ACN rule); at GAAP the year would be
  distorted, the charge being 96% of the income before it. The Q3 2013 release states the FY2013 guide only as adjusted EPS ($2.30-2.35,
  excluding restructuring and related charges): it is used as the company's figure excluding the item (the ACN rule, `eps_guide_note`).
- **Operating margins keep the Pullmantur impairment** (Q4 2012: operating income $(281,307)K, -2,156bp on the year-ago quarter; FY2012
  5.2%) **and the Q3 2013 restructuring charge** ($12,244K): neither release publishes operating income excluding them. Net Cruise Costs
  exclude both by the company's definition (total cruise operating expenses plus marketing, selling and administrative expenses, which do
  not contain those lines). Rebuilt with both excluded, no class or tier moves.
- **Guides** as before: the current-FY EPS midpoint, FY10 $2.10 ($2.00-2.20, Q4 2009 release, "including $0.39 related to a legal
  settlement"), $2.20 from 2010-04-29, $2.30 from 2010-07-23, $2.45 from 2010-10-27; FY11 $3.35 from 2011-01-28, $3.20 from 2011-04-29,
  $2.90 from 2011-07-29, $2.75 from 2011-10-28; FY12 $2.10 from 2012-02-03 (after the Costa Concordia accident, "Impact of Costa
  Concordia"), $1.95 from 2012-04-20, $1.75 from 2012-07-27, $1.90 from 2012-10-26; FY13 $2.40 from 2013-02-05, $2.25 from 2013-07-26,
  $2.325 (adjusted) from 2013-10-25. BASE takes the next quarter's net revenue guide at constant currency where the release states one
  (every release but Q1 2010, whose Q2 2010 guide is as published: +21.5%, Net Yields approx. 6% on capacity 14.6%); "around flat" and a
  capacity of "Flat" are 0. The constant-currency test is per print. The Q3 2010 release's 2011 outlook ("First quarter 2011 Net Yields
  are currently expected to improve 2%-4%"; "2011 EPS to exceed its previous record of $3.26") is a note: FY2010 is the current year until
  the Q4 2010 print.
- **Stated changes.** From Q2 2011 most releases state Net Cruise Costs only excluding fuel or at constant currency, and the Q4 2012, Q2 2013
  and Q3 2013 releases state Net Yields as a change only at constant currency: the builder checks the as-reported change where the release
  states it (13 of 16 Net Yields, 6 of 16 Net Cruise Costs, within 0.1pp), and the note is then the release's per-APCD table row (as
  reported, at constant currency, a year ago), which `verbatim.py` checks. The signals stay as reported, as the decade's are.
- **Dividends:** reinstated at $0.10 a quarter (Q2 2011 release, 2011-07-28), $0.12 from 2012-10-26 (declared in September 2012 and first
  stated in the Q3 2012 10-Q, accepted 2012-10-25 16:32 ET), $0.25 from 2013-09-12 (8-K accepted 2013-09-11 17:25 ET).
- **Adds nothing:** the Grandeur of the Seas fire 8-K of 2013-05-29 ("a reduction of $0.10 per share") and the investor-day slides of
  2013-05-30 (the fire's $0.10 and about $0.08 of currency and fuel against the April guide), which restate no range (the WMT 2010 rule; the
  July release later bridges them to $2.22); the Rolls-Royce settlement 8-K of 2010-01-11 (no per-share figure; the Q4 2009 release states
  the $0.39); the Project Sunshine letter of intent (2011-02-11) and the ship-order, financing, notes, officer, director and
  shareholder-agreement 8-Ks; the 10-Qs beyond the $0.12 dividend (the releases come first and carry every guide).
- **Anachronism list:** Project Sunshine (from 2011-02-14; the 8-K was accepted 2011-02-11 16:28 ET, after the close) and Quantum-class
  (2013-02-25) join `taxonomy_eras.json`; no model of any ticker contains them. RCL's source ids run to `RC50`.

Controls: altering one value of each print from Q3 2009 (and each Q4 print's full-year EPS), guide (its EPS range, its next-quarter Net
Yields and its fiscal-year constant-currency Net Yields), vintage, dividend and the Q2 2011 restatement changes no date before its
publication and changes the first weekly date on or after it (79 controls from the Q3 2009 release on, every one in scope: the restated FY2009 EPS and the reinstated dividend act from 2011-07-29 until the FY2011 10-K takes over on 2012-02-29). A scan of the 314 models for the figures, notes, guides,
texts and sources of every later print, guide, vintage and dividend finds none before its first publication (0 of 74,363 pairs); the only
calendar year after a date outside an FY label is the Q3 2010 release's 2011 outlook, a forecast, on the ten dates from 2010-10-27 (which
`retro_tool run` reports as a warning). The firewall plants a later restatement of every history year as well (`restates`, as for SHW and
WMT) and passes at all 23 cutoffs above. No shared code changed (the firewall only gains the RCL plant), so no other ticker is rebuilt.

- **BEAR is now 2009** (-72.0%/yr, 2008's $2.68 to 2009's $0.75; -73.5% from 2011-07-28 on the revised $0.71) at the 10th-percentile
  P/E: $1-3 a share, a 91-97% fall on every date from 2010-01-29. With the downside near-total everywhere, Ratio B moves with the upside
  to BULL, so the class follows BASE: BULL is the decade CAGR or BASE where higher, and the decade CAGR (-11.7%/yr over 2000-2009 to
  +5.4%/yr over 2002-2011) is under BASE on every date to 2012-07-20; from 2012-07-27 BULL is the decade CAGR (3.7-5.4%/yr) on 60 of 76
  dates. XBULL is the 2003-2005 run (+46.1%/yr) until the Q4 2011 print adds 2011, then 2009-2011 (+97.5%/yr, $0.71 to $2.77).
- **BASE follows capacity.** Net revenue guides of +9.2% (Q1 2010), +21.5% (Q2 2010, as published), +20.6% (Q3 2010), +13.5% (Q4 2010),
  +11.3% to +12.4% (Q1 2011) and +7.4% to +11.6% (Q2 2011 to Q4 2011) carry capacity growth of 6-15%; with capacity at 0-2.5% from 2012
  they fall to +5.9% to +9.7% (Q1-Q2 2012), -1.8% to -0.8% (Q3 2012), +2.0% to +4.6% (Q4 2012 to Q4 2013). BASE (with the negative buyback
  term) runs from +19-20%/yr in mid-2010 to -1.8% to +3.9%/yr from 2012-07-27, and the price is above BULL on 2013-01-25 and on every
  date from 2013-10-25 (Ratio B infinite on those 12 dates).
- **The P/E window barely moves** (10th percentile 9.2-10.2x, median 13.9-14.6x, 90th 19.6-21.1x). On guided EPS the stock trades at
  10.4-38.8x in 2010 (38.8x in January on FY09's $0.70), 7.5-20.4x in 2011, 9.3-18.6x in 2012 and 13.3-20.4x in 2013. The EPP floor
  (the median of the calendar-year lows) is 8-9x to 2012 and 11x in 2013; the price is under it only on 2011-08-19, 2011-09-23,
  2011-09-30 and 2011-10-07.
- **The proxy composite** is 2.55 on Q4 2009, 3.05 on Q1 2010, 3.20 on Q2 and Q3 2010 (Net Yields +4.9% and +5.2%, Net Cruise Costs
  down, revenue +17-19%, the operating margin +422-489bp), 2.85 on Q4 2010 and Q1 2011, 2.55 on Q2 2011, 2.70 on Q3 2011, 2.15 on Q4
  2011, 2.00 on Q1 2012 (Net Cruise Costs +10.1% at BEAR, the margin -156bp), 2.15 on Q2 2012, 2.05 on Q3 2012, 2.25 on Q4 2012, 2.55
  on Q1 2013 and 2.40 on Q2 and Q3 2013.

How far each call moves the classes (the 209 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- operating income before the Q4 2012 impairment and the Q3 2013 restructuring: no class, no tier;
- FY2012 at GAAP $0.08: 5 classes (2013-03-22 to 2013-04-12 and 2013-06-21, RICH to FAIR), no tier;
- FY2010 without the $0.39 legal gain (a figure no filing publishes): 15 classes (April-June 2011 toward CHEAP or FAIR, eight dates
  of March-July 2012 RICH to FAIR) and 13 tiers;
- the Interest Expense Revision ignored until the FY2011 10-K: no class, 2 tiers;
- the guides as reported (constant currency ignored): 17 classes (July-October 2010 and April-July 2011) and 18 tiers;
- forward growth on Net Yields alone (capacity left out): 42 classes (29 in 2010, 13 in 2011, all toward FAIR or RICH) and 39 tiers;
- every signal at BEAR: 58 classes (2010-01-29 to 2012-06-01, toward FAIR or RICH), no tier; every signal at XBULL: 9 classes (March-July
  2012, RICH to FAIR), no tier; Net Cruise Costs per APCD at BASE: 12 classes (February 2010 FAIR to RICH, March-July 2012 RICH to

The 83 RICH calls from 2012-06-08 hold under every variant but FY2012 at GAAP (5 dates of 2013) and three that move 3-4 dates of June-July
2012 (FY2010 without the gain, every signal at XBULL, Net Cruise Costs at BASE); the 27 CHEAP calls of 2011-07-29 to 2012-01-27 hold
under all but forward growth on Net Yields alone (2 dates) and every signal at BEAR (11 dates). Capacity in BASE is the call that moves
most, all in 2010-2011.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight (beyond the 2008-2009 list):
- the company's FY2012 EPS before the Pullmantur impairment (5 classes move at GAAP), and the FY2010 legal gain kept (15 move without it);
- the Interest Expense Revision applied from the release that published it (no class moves);
- the Q3 2013 adjusted-EPS guide read as the company's figure excluding an item; the operating margins kept after the impairment and

### RCL 2014-2017

208 weekly dates, 2014-01-10 to 2017-12-29, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds; the series starts at 2014-01-06 because
2013-12-31 already holds ISO week 1 of 2014 (the UNP and LOW practice). The fact sheet only gains facts and two optional raw fields; its
2008-2013 content is unchanged and the 314 earlier models rebuild byte for byte. Read: every 8-K and 10-Q of February 2014 to January 2018
(46 8-Ks, one an amendment, and 12 10-Qs), the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks and the Q4 2013 release, all by Opus directly. 1,558 strings across
2008-2017 were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings, 1,558 found; for every 2014-2017 guide the checklist also re-parses
the table rows it checks and asserts they give the fact sheet's numbers. Decided on 2026-11-08, before any 2014-2017 outcome was computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (08:00-08:58 ET); the five on a Friday (2015-07-31, 2015-10-23,
  2016-04-29, 2016-10-28, 2017-04-28) date their week that day (the UNP 2014 rule). The FY2013, FY2014 and FY2016 10-Ks were accepted after
  the close (2014-02-20 17:08, 2015-02-23 16:37, 2017-02-23 17:29 ET) and are dated the next trading day; the FY2015 10-K (2016-02-22 09:04)
  keeps its date.
- **Net Yields and Net Cruise Costs by the company's own definition.** From 2014 the releases state both excluding lines their
  reconciliations list: Pullmantur's non-core businesses (a land tour company and a travel agency) while held for sale and before their
  sale on 2014-03-31, then "other initiative costs" and, in Q3 2016, the net gain on the 51% sale of Pullmantur and CDF Croisières de
  France. The company labels these figures "As-Reported" (against Constant-Currency), and the decade's rule-T values are the company's
  own (2001-2002 stated, 2003-2006 its Net Revenues and Net Cruise Costs), so each print keeps its statement rows and adds the excluded
  lines ('nr_x_k', 'nc_x_k'); the builder subtracts them (zero before 2014, so no earlier value changes). The derived figures equal the
  company's Net Revenues and Net Cruise Costs rows in every release, and its stated as-reported Net Yields change on all 12 quarters that
  state one (the four Q4 releases state the quarter only at constant currency; Net Cruise Costs are stated only excluding fuel, so the
  checklist checks the per-APCD or thousands rows). Statement-derived values, without the exclusions, would read Q4 2014 Net Yields at
  -5.0% against the company's +0.4% (land-tour revenue has no cruise days); rebuilt that way, no class or tier moves. The 2017 releases
  restate the year-ago marketing, selling and administrative expenses to include 2016's restructuring charges; the year-ago figure is
  taken from the same release's Net Cruise Costs reconciliation (as first reported), and the checklist checks both.
- **EPS is the company's Adjusted EPS** (the ACN rule), each year from the latest filing that publishes it: 2013 $2.40 (GAAP $2.14, after
  $56.9 million of restructuring and related charges); from the Q4 2014 release the company's Adjusted EPS also excludes the divested
  businesses and gives 2013 as $2.44, which replaces $2.40 from 2015-01-29 (the SHW `restates` rule) until the FY2014 10-K carries 2012
  $2.02, 2013 $2.44 and 2014 $3.39 (GAAP $3.43). The FY2013 10-K already printed the $2.44 and $2.02 as "excluding estimated impact of
  businesses held for sale", beside its headline $2.40 and $1.97; the headline stands until the company adopts the basis. 2015 is $4.83
  (GAAP $3.02, after the $399.3 million Pullmantur impairment) and 2016 $6.08 (GAAP $5.93); from the FY2015 10-K the five-year selected
  data itself prints Adjusted EPS. No year is excluded. History vintages FY2013 (2004-2013), FY2014 (2005-2014), FY2015 (2006-2015) and
  FY2016 (2007-2016), the first year's diluted shares from the FY2008-FY2011 10-Ks (234,580K, 234,714K, 221,485K, 214,255K).
- **Guides:** every EPS guide is Adjusted EPS ('eps_guide_note'). Current-FY EPS: FY14 $3.30 from 2014-01-28 ($3.20-3.40), $3.35 from
  2014-04-25, $3.45 from 2014-07-25; FY15 $4.75 from 2015-01-30, $4.55 from 2015-04-21, $4.70 from 2015-07-31, $4.80 from 2015-10-23; FY16
  $6.00 from 2016-02-03, $6.25 from 2016-04-29, $6.05 from 2016-08-03; FY17 $7.00 from 2017-01-27, $7.10 from 2017-04-28, $7.40 from
  2017-08-02, $7.375 from 2017-11-08. Every release guides the next quarter at constant currency, so BASE always takes it. Capacity turns
  negative after Pullmantur's deconsolidation (August 2016): -0.2% for Q4 2016, -1.7% to -2.4% for 2017, -4.0% for Q2 and Q3 2017, as
  published. The Q3 2016 release's full-year constant-currency Net Yields of "4.0% or better" is taken at its stated bound.
- **Dividends,** each first stated in the Q3 10-Q, accepted after the close: $0.30 from 2014-10-24, $0.375 from 2015-10-26, $0.48 from

  October 2015 and April 2017) reach the model through the diluted share count and are quoted in the cash-return text.
- **Operating margins keep the Pullmantur impairments and restructuring charges** (Q3 2015 -1,194bp, Q3 2016 +1,844bp against it, Q4 2013
  +1,962bp against Q4 2012's): no release publishes operating income excluding them. Rebuilt with them excluded, no class or tier moves.
- **Adds nothing:** the Pullmantur joint-venture 8-K of 2016-05-10 ("an immaterial one-time gain", no figure); the ship-order, financing,

Controls: altering one value of each print from Q3 2013 (and each Q4 print's full-year EPS), guide (its EPS range, next-quarter Net Yields and fiscal-year constant-currency Net Yields), vintage, dividend and the Q4 2014 restatement must change no date before its publication and the first weekly date on or after it: all 81 did (the FY2013 restatement acts from 2015-01-30 until the FY2014 10-K takes over on 2015-02-24; each dividend until the next 10-K restates the rate). A scan of the 522 models finds no figure, note, guide, text or source of a later print, guide, vintage or dividend

### RCL 2018-2021

209 weekly dates, 2018-01-05 to 2021-12-31, on the same method, rule-T thresholds and signals. The fact sheet only gains facts (sources

108 8-Ks, two 8-K/As, 12 10-Qs, four 10-Ks). Read for the facts, by Opus directly: the 16 earnings releases (Q4 2017 to Q3 2021), the
FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks, the coronavirus, withdrawal and business-update 8-Ks of 2020, and the 8-Ks that mention a guide (SkySea, Silversea,
Cuba); every other 8-K body and exhibit and the 10-Qs were checked for a guided number or a dividend. The records are generated by a script
from the filings' converted rows, so every figure is read by its row label and every yield, cost, margin and growth rate is computed:
490 strings checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings, 490 found, and the 72 numeric fields of the nine guide tables re-parsed
from the rows the checklist checks. Decided on 2026-11-08, before any 2018-2021 date was built or any outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (08:02-08:59 ET) except Q4 2019's, during the session (2020-02-04
  09:37 ET, a Tuesday), so its week's date is 2020-02-05; the Q3 2021 release came on a Friday before the open (2021-10-29 08:16 ET) and
  dates its week that day (the UNP 2014 rule). The FY2017 (2018-02-20 19:14 ET), FY2018 (Friday 2019-02-22 17:15), FY2019 (2020-02-25 17:13)
  and FY2020 (Friday 2021-02-26 16:26) 10-Ks are dated the next trading day: 2018-02-21, 2019-02-25, 2020-02-26 and 2021-03-01.
- **History:** vintages FY2017 (2008-2017), FY2018 (2009-2018), FY2019 (2010-2019) and FY2020 (2011-2020), each year from the latest filing
  that reports it; the first year's diluted shares from the FY2012-FY2015 10-Ks (214,195K, 215,295K, 217,711K, 219,229K).
- **EPS is the company's Adjusted EPS** (the 2014-2017 rule): 2017 $7.53 (equal to GAAP), 2018 $8.86 (GAAP $8.56), 2019 $9.54 (GAAP $8.95).
  **FY2020 is excluded:** Adjusted EPS $(18.31), GAAP $(27.05), a loss even on the company's figure, so no P/E (the XOM FY2020 note of r2).
  As the latest year it is encoded as XOM's was (`excluded_note` on the Q4 2020 print, `eps_excluded` on the FY2020 vintage): its revenue,
  shares and margins stay, its own days leave the P/E window ("10-yr ex-FY20" from 2021-02-23), and FY2019's $9.54 stands as the last full
  year through 2021 (the Q4 2021 print lies after the range).
- **Guides** as before to the Q4 2019 release (Adjusted EPS, `eps_guide_note`): FY18 $8.65 from 2018-01-24 ($8.55-8.75), $8.80 from
  2018-04-26 ($8.70-8.90, repeated on 2018-08-02), $8.80 from 2018-10-25 ($8.75-8.85); FY19 $9.875 from 2019-01-30 ($9.75-10.00), $9.75
  from 2019-05-01, $9.60 from 2019-07-25, $9.525 from 2019-10-30; FY20 $10.55 from 2020-02-04 ($10.40-10.70). Every release guides the
  next quarter at constant currency, so BASE takes it: -1.0% to -0.5% (Q1 2018), +4.2% to +4.7%, +10.4%, +16.8% to +17.4% (Q4 2018),
  +19.1% to +19.7%, +21.6%, +16.2%, +9.2% (Q4 2019) and +4.0% (Q1 2020, whose As-Reported Net Yields "(0.5%) to (1.0%)" is read as -1.0% to
  -0.5%). Silversea (two-thirds from 2018-07-31, consolidated on a three-month lag) is in the guides and prints as published (the
  Pullmantur 2007 rule).
- **The withdrawal.** The 8-K of 2020-03-10 (09:10 ET, before the open): "the company is withdrawing its first quarter and full-year 2020
  guidance". It voids every earlier FY2020 field (`withdrawn`, the LOW, SHW and WMT rule, new in the RCL builder), and no guide in numbers
  follows to the end of 2021: FY2019's $9.54 stands (the rollover rule) and BASE takes the latest quarter's revenue growth (+7.9% for Q4

  change; APCD fell to 5,424 in Q3 2020). The AAPL Mac-unit rule applies: each signal keeps its name, thresholds and weight, has no value
  and scores BASE ("n/r"), and nothing replaces it (`no_ny_ncc`; the note quotes what the release says instead). Q1 2020 still states
  both and keeps them.
- **A ratio needs a positive base.** Q3 2020's total revenues were negative (-$33,688K: refunds and reversals exceeded the quarter's
  ticket and onboard revenues), so its operating margin and margin change, and Q3 2021's revenue growth and margin change against it,
  have no value (`ratio_note`; scored BASE). Occupancy changes are differences of stated percentages and always count. Where the latest
  quarter's revenue growth has no value, BASE takes the same release's year-to-date growth (the quarter-to-year step of the ACN fallback;
  `ytd_sales_pct`): Q3 2021's nine months, -74.7%.

  2017's year-ago marketing expense comes from its reconciliation, as first reported (the 2017 rule).

  will not pay dividends or engage in stock repurchases"; the FY2020 10-K repeats it).
- **COVID enters only through the prints, the withdrawal and the dividend** (the LOW 2020 rule); the registry has no COVID theme and no
  theme is live for a cruise company (ENERGY_TRANSITION is scoped to oil, gas, coal and refining; EV and CRYPTO to other industries), so the

  and BUY 149 (every date from 2019-03-01). Robustness is 8 of 8 on all 53 dates of 2020 and on 46 of 2019, 3-8 of 8 in 2018 and 2021.
- **Why CHEAP from late 2018:** the multiple fell while the guided EPS rose: 10.5-15.3x the FY18 guide in 2018 and 10.7-14.0x the FY19
  guide in 2019 (the 6th-60th percentile of a window whose median is 14.0-14.6x). From the FY2018 vintage (2019-02-25) the 2009 fall leaves
  the history, so BEAR becomes 2012's fall (-27.1%/yr: $2.77 to $2.02) instead of 2009's (-73.5%/yr), and the downside to BEAR shrinks from
  92-96% of the price (2018) to 43-57% (from 2019-03-01); BULL is the decade CAGR (32.4%/yr over 2009-2018, 16.7%/yr over 2010-2019), so
  Ratio B runs 0.26-1.00 from the Q4 2018 print.
- **2020 and 2021 rest on FY2019's $9.54.** After the withdrawal the price ($24-83 in 2020, $65-97 in 2021) is 2.5-8.7x and then 6.8-10.1x
  that anchor, the 0th-11th percentile of its own window, under the EPP floor on 88 consecutive dates from 2020-02-28 to 2021-10-29 (and
  on 100 of the 209), and
  under the BEAR price ($57 in March 2020) on 19 dates between 2020-03-13 and 2020-08-07 (Ratio B negative). BASE collapses with revenue
  (-16.3% to -100.7%/yr), but neither BULL (the decade CAGR) nor the class depends on it, so the class stays CHEAP through 2020; in 2021 the
  proxy composite (1.55-1.85, with occupancy and the margin at BEAR) and the price's rise toward 10x move it among CHEAP, FAIR and RICH.
- **The proxy composite** reads 2.15-2.55 from Q4 2017 to Q3 2019, 2.00 on Q4 2019, 1.35 on Q1 2020 (Net Yields -1.6%, Net Cruise Costs
  +31.4%, revenue -16.7%, occupancy -410bp, the margin -7,734bp), 1.55-1.70 on Q2 2020 to Q2 2021 (revenue, occupancy and, but for Q3 2020, the margin at BEAR,
  the per-APCD signals at BASE with no value) and 1.85 on Q3 2021 (revenue growth and the margin change without a value as well).

How far each call moves the classes (the 209 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted; the
harness reproduces all 209 classes unchanged):
- the withdrawal ignored (the FY2020 guide of $10.55 and its quarter guide standing through 2020): no class, no tier;
- the coronavirus impact of 2020-02-13 ($0.65) or the Cuba impact ($0.30) netted into the year's EPS guide: no class, no tier;
- Q3 2021's BASE on the previous quarter's growth instead of the nine months': no class, no tier;
- Net Yields and Net Cruise Costs derived from the statements and APCD where no release states them, and every ratio computed even over
  a base that is not positive: 34 classes (all from 2021-02-23; 15 CHEAP to FAIR or RICH, 12 to CHEAP, 7 between FAIR and RICH), no tier;
- the Q2 2021 10-Q's statistics ignored: 3 classes (2021-09-24 to 2021-10-08, FAIR to CHEAP), no tier;
- GAAP EPS instead of the company's Adjusted EPS (2012 $0.08 and 2015 $3.02 among the years): 56 classes (35 in 2018, 21 in 2021, all
  toward CHEAP) and 57 tiers;
- every signal at BEAR: 69 classes (68 toward FAIR or RICH); every signal at XBULL: 26 (24 toward CHEAP); Net Cruise Costs at BASE: 4
  (2018); no tier in any.
The CHEAP calls of 2019-2020 hold under every variant but every signal at BEAR (14 of the 105 move); those of 2021 are the most sensitive.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight (beyond the earlier lists):
- the signals without a value scored BASE when the releases stopped stating them (34 classes of 2021 move if values are derived from
  APCD near zero), and the ratios over a negative base read as no value;
- FY2020 excluded and FY2019's $9.54 kept as the anchor through 2021, which no rule could replace while the company gave no EPS guide;
- the withdrawal read as voiding the FY2020 guide (no class moves either way), and the per-share impacts of 2019-2020 read as no guide;
- the Q2 2021 10-Q's statistics taken from its own date, and Q3 2021's BASE from the nine months (no class moves on the alternative);
- the company's Adjusted EPS (56 classes move at GAAP).

### RCL 2022-2026

253 weekly dates, 2022-01-07 to 2026-11-06, on the same method, rule-T thresholds and signals. The fact sheet only gains facts (sources
`RC100`-`RC125`); its 2008-2021 content is unchanged. Listed: every 8-K, 10-Q and 10-K of February 2022 to October 2026 (253 filings:
233 8-Ks, 15 10-Qs, five 10-Ks). Read for the facts, by Opus directly: the 20 earnings releases (Q4 2021 to Q3 2026), the FY2021-FY2025
10-Ks and the 8-K of 2024-02-21 that raises the FY2024 guide; every other 8-K body and exhibit and the 10-Qs were checked for a guided
number or a dividend. The records are generated by a script from the filings' converted rows, as in 2018-2021: 651 strings checked with
`verbatim.py` against their own filings, 651 found, and the 112 numeric fields of the 16 guide tables re-parsed from the rows the
checklist checks by a second parser. Decided on 2026-11-09, before any 2022-2026 date was built or any outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (06:31-08:34 ET). The Q4 2021 release came on a Friday (2022-02-04
  08:34 ET) and dates its week that day; every other one came on a Tuesday or Thursday. The FY2021 10-K (2022-03-01 09:15 ET, before the
  open) and the FY2024 10-K (2025-02-14 06:55 ET) date their own day; FY2022 (2023-02-23 17:28), FY2023 (2024-02-21 17:14) and FY2025
  (2026-02-11 17:21) are dated the next trading day.
- **History.** From FY2021 the 10-Ks reserve Item 6 and report three years, so each vintage (FY2021 to FY2025) takes its own three years
  from its statements (revenue and GAAP EPS), its EPS note (diluted shares: the statements no longer print them) and its MD&A (Adjusted
  EPS), and every earlier year from the latest 10-K that reports it (the ACN FY21, WMT and NKE rule); the first year's diluted shares come
  from the last 10-K whose five-year table reports that year (2012 from the FY2016 10-K to 2016 from the FY2020 10-K). From FY2023 the
  10-Ks, and from Q4 2023 the releases, report in millions: their raw figures are kept in thousands (x1000) and the derived per-APCD
  values are checked against the company's rows within the rounding of millions.
- **EPS is the company's Adjusted EPS** (the 2014 rule). **FY2021 and FY2022 are excluded** as FY2020 was: Adjusted EPS $(19.19) and
  $(7.50) (GAAP $(20.89) and $(8.45)), losses even on the company's figure. Their revenue, shares and margins stay; their own days leave
  the P/E window ("10-yr ex-FY20 ex-FY21" from 2022-02-04, "ex-FY22" from 2023-02-08). FY2023 $6.77 (GAAP $6.31), FY2024 $11.80 ($10.94),
  FY2025 $15.64 ($15.61).
- **2022 has no fiscal-year EPS guide in numbers**: the releases say it in words ("a net loss for the first half of 2022 and a return to
  profitability in the second half", then "a Net Loss in the second half of 2022"), shown in the guide line beside the numbers and
  feeding nothing. FY2019's $9.54 stands through 2023-02-07 (the rollover rule, FY2020-FY2022 excluded). The quarter EPS guides of the Q2
  and Q3 2022 releases ($0.05-0.25; $(1.50)-$(1.30)) are display only.
- **Guides from 2023:** Adjusted EPS ranges, the midpoint the anchor: FY23 $3.30 from 2023-02-08, $4.60, $6.10, $6.605; FY24 $9.60 from
  2024-02-02, $10.00 from 2024-02-22 (the 8-K of 2024-02-21; its "approximately 100 bps" of constant-currency yield is words on a
  range, display only), $10.80, $11.40, $11.595; FY25 $14.50 from 2025-01-29, $15.05, $15.48, $15.605; FY26 $17.90 from 2026-01-30,
  $17.30, $17.80, $17.90. One guide row reads "Approximately Flat" (Q3 2026's Net Yields): 0.0, as "flat" guides are encoded (Q1 2010).
- **BASE (forward growth).** The chain is unchanged (next-quarter Net Yields x capacity at constant currency, the fiscal year's, then as
  published) with one step added before the latest quarter's growth: a next-quarter **total revenues guide in dollars** (`q_rev`, the
  AVGO rule), read against the year-ago quarter's total revenues as published: Q3 2022 "$2.9 billion - $3.0 billion" against $0.457B
  (+534.6% to +556.5%) and Q4 2022 "approximately $2.6 billion" against $0.982B (+164.7%). Guides stated **against 2019** (Net Yields,
  capacity and Net Cruise Costs, in the Q4 2022 to Q3 2023 releases) measure a different base period and are display only (the WMT
  "excluding divestitures" rule). Growth against a year-ago quarter with positive revenues stands however large (the 2018-2021 rule,
  which kept Q2 2021's -71.0%): BASE takes -74.7% (Q3 2021's nine months) to 2022-01-28, then +2,777.2% (Q4 2021), +2,421.1% (Q1 2022),
  the dollar guides, +165.1% (Q4 2022), +172.4% (Q1 2023), +61.3% (Q2 2023) and +39.0% (Q3 2023); from the Q4 2023 release the
  next-quarter constant-currency guides are year-on-year again (+26.4% to +26.9% for Q1 2024 down to +9.4% to +9.9% for Q4 2026). This
  makes BASE, and with it BULL and XBULL (each at least BASE), absurd in 2022-2023 (a BASE price of $112,037 on 2022-02-04): method
  behaviour of the frozen fallback, recorded, not tuned.
- **Net Yields and Net Cruise Costs** are changes against the year-ago quarter, which must be the comparison column of the same release's
  reconciliation, as in every release of 2008-2019. The Q4 2021 and Q1 2022 releases have no yield or cost reconciliation, and those of Q2
  2022 to Q4 2023 reconcile only against 2019 (Net Cruise Costs also against the previous quarter), so both signals have no value and
  score BASE (the AAPL Mac-unit rule, as in 2020-2021; `no_ny_ncc`, the note quoting what the release says instead), although the
  statements and APCD would allow a derivation against the restart quarters of 2021-2022 (sensitivity below). From Q1 2024 the
  reconciliation's comparison column is the year-ago quarter again and both are derived as before; the releases' "Adjusted Gross Margin"
  is Net Revenues by another name (total revenues less commissions, transportation and other and onboard and other). The derived values
  equal the company's per-APCD rows in all 11 releases (within the rounding of millions) and its stated As-Reported Net Yields change in
  the eight that give one (within 0.1pp; Q1-Q3 2024 state only constant currency). The FY2023 10-K's year-on-year table gives FY2023's
  Net Yields (+41.4%, shown in the franchise line) and the FY2022 10-K's gives Net Cruise Costs only.
- **Dividends,** each rate from the first filing that states it: none until $0.40 from 2024-07-25 (the Q2 2024 release, before the
  open); $0.75 from 2025-02-14 (the FY2024 10-K, before the open, which first states both December 2024's $0.55 and February 2025's
  $0.75); $1.00 from 2025-10-28 (the Q3 2025 release); $1.50 from 2026-02-12 (the FY2025 10-K, after the close of 2026-02-11).
- **An income tax line** appears in the FY2025 statements: the EPS check's tax rate becomes its effective rate (1.88%) and other
  income (expense) is income before income taxes less operating income (display only, as before).
- **No theme is live for a cruise company**: GENAI (from 2022-11-30) is scoped to software, IT services, information, search, education
  and mobility, GLP1 (from 2023-08-08) to snacks and beverages, ENERGY_TRANSITION to oil, gas, coal and refining. The watch list stays
  empty.
- **Adds nothing:** the preliminary and offering 8-Ks (2022-09-22's bookings words among them), officer, director, vote, credit and notes
  8-Ks, the Trifecta multi-year targets of 2022-11-03 (the LOW multi-year rule), the Mexico statement of 2026-05-20, the Sandals
  investment of 2026-09-23 (no guide), and the 10-Qs beyond dividends.
- **Builder changes** (`q_rev`; an outlook in words, a display-only guide and a dollar revenue guide shown beside a numeric guide; a
  vintage's annual Net Cruise Costs without Net Yields; the tax line's note). The 731 models of 2008-2021 rebuild byte-identical; the
  engine is unchanged.
- **Anachronism list:** Silver Nova and Celebrity Ascent (2022-03-01), Utopia of the Seas (2022-05-06), Silver Endeavour (2022-07-28),
  Trifecta (2022-11-03), Silver Ray and Hideaway Beach (2023-02-24), Star of the Seas (2023-10-27), Celebrity Xcel (2023-12-26),
  Celebrity River Cruises (2025-01-28), Perfecta (2025-04-21) and Discovery-class (2026-01-29) join `taxonomy_eras.json`, each dated from
  the first Royal Caribbean filing that uses it (EDGAR full-text search, none before 2022); no model of any ticker contains them before
  that date. `retro_tool run` (offline, with its as-of price check run once for all 253 dates against one download: 0 of 253 off by more
  than 0.5%) passes every date and warns of "2087" and "2043" on 28 dates: Q2 2022's capacity change (+2,087.9%) and Q3 2023's margin
  change (+2,043.7bp), numbers, not years.

Controls: altering one value of each new print (its EPS; its Net Yields change, or for the nine releases without one the note that
says so; each Q4 print's full-year EPS or, for FY2021 and FY2022, its exclusion note), guide (its EPS range, and its next-quarter Net
Yields, fiscal-year constant-currency Net Yields, next-quarter EPS, dollar revenue guide and display line where it has them), each
outlook in words, vintage (its first-year EPS) and dividend must change no date before its publication and the first weekly date on or
after it. 133 of the 134 did; the other, FY2022's exclusion note, changes nothing because no model prints it while a numeric FY2023
guide is current, and removing the exclusion itself instead (FY2022 at $1.00) changes 2023-02-08 and 2023-02-17 (until the FY2022 10-K)
and nothing earlier. A scan of the 984 models for the 289 figures, notes, guides, words, texts and sources first published from
2021-12-31 finds none before its first publication (0 of 248,026 pairs; "dividend $0.75 a quarter" and "dividend $1.50 a quarter", the
whole texts of Q2 2025 and Q3 2026, appear earlier only inside the longer texts of the prints before them). The firewall (its RCL plant
now also carries a later dollar revenue guide for every guided quarter and a later vintage with an income tax line and Net Cruise Costs
without Net Yields) passes at all 26 cutoffs above, and rerun with the new plants at 2010-01-01, 2014-01-01, 2018-01-01 and 2022-01-01
changes none of the 105, 314, 522 and 731 earlier models. No other ticker's code changed, so no other ticker is rebuilt.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):

How far each call moves the classes (the 253 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted; the

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight (beyond the earlier lists):

## MAR (Marriott International): the thirteenth ticker, in staging

The MAR series is built apart from ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, AVGO, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT and RCL and shares nothing with them but the
machinery: its own fact sheet (`retro/facts/MAR.json`), builder (`retro/build_mar.py`, the RCL builder with a hotel guide encoding) and
engine (`retro/templates/mar_engine.py.tmpl`, the RCL engine with hotel signals). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or
finding of another ticker enters a MAR model, and neither does the live `mar_signal_model.py` (another branch) or the profile of Marriott
in `data/business_profiles.json` (2026 judgements, not read for this series). Outputs go to
`staging/retrospective/MAR/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`.

```bash
python3 retro/build_mar.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                   # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_mar.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                   # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/MAR/200[89]-*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series MAR
for c in 2008-01-11 2008-02-14 2008-02-19 2008-04-17 2008-06-02 2008-07-10 2008-07-11 2008-10-02 2009-01-01 2009-02-12 2009-02-13 \
         2009-04-23 2009-05-05 2009-06-23 2009-07-16 2009-09-23 2009-10-08 2009-10-09 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c MAR; done
```

Read for the history and the decade's signal values: the selected financial data, statements and lodging statistics of the FY1997-FY2008
10-Ks, and the Q4 2003-Q4 2006 releases for full-year figures excluding synthetic fuel and one-offs (Marriott's earlier releases are not on
EDGAR). Read for the prints and guides: every 8-K of October 2006 to December 2009 (35, the stock-dividend 8-K/A among them; the non-earnings
ones item by item) and the dividend and stock-dividend passages of the 10 10-Qs. All by Opus directly, with no delegated transcription. The
fact sheet is generated by a script from the transcribed raw figures, so every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is computed, not typed;
357 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings: every statement row behind a print, every guide table row and
sentence, every quoted sentence, every five-year row behind the history and rule T. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time
(converted from UTC; before 2003 EDGAR gives the filing date only). Decided on 2026-11-09, before any MAR outcome was computed:

- **Fiscal calendar.** "Our fiscal year ends on the Friday nearest to December 31" (the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks); FY2002 and FY2008 had 53
  weeks. The quarters are 12, 12, 12 and 16 weeks (Q4 2008: 17 against 16, as the release compares it). The builder checks every fiscal
  year end a 10-K states against the rule. The dates of January 2008 have FY2007 as the current year until the Q4 2007 print (2008-02-14).
- **The listing rule** (method r2): the stock's own P/E exists from the March 27, 1998 spinoff of the new Marriott International ("No data
  are presented for the periods prior to the Spinoff since we were not a publicly-held company during that time", FY1998 10-K); Yahoo's
  quotes of 1998-03-23 to 1998-03-26 precede it and stay out. The window is 9.8 years on 2008-01-04 and ten from 2008-03-27.
- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's series times its factors after the as-of date (the June 2006 two-for-one split, the 2009 stock dividends,
  a 1.061 factor of 2011-11-22): $34.12 on 2007-12-28 and $20.06 on 2009-01-02, the two closes the FY2008 10-K states.
- **Splits and stock dividends.** The 2006 split divides the per-share facts published before it (`eps_published`, `shares_published`).
  The 2009 stock dividends are splits too, as the company restates per-share data for them ("all share and per share data ... have been
  retroactively adjusted"), each applying from the later of its ex-date in the price data and the first filing that states its ratio:
  0.00369 (the 8-K/A of 2009-05-05, ex-date 2009-06-23), 0.00379 (ex-date 2009-08-18, ratio first stated in the 10-Q of 2009-10-09, so from
  that date; the guides of July sit 0.38% off the price basis on the seven dates between), and the November one (ex-date 2009-11-17) is in
  no filing by 2009-12-31 and is not applied (0.3% on the last seven dates).
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it.** The FY2006 vintage takes 1999-2006 from the FY2006 10-K's eight-year table,
  1998 from the FY2002 10-K and 1997's revenue from the FY2001 10-K (no per-share data before 1998, so the EPS history starts there; 1997's
  sales are on that filing's basis, with the Senior Living and Distribution Services businesses discontinued in 2002, a seam kept as
  published). The FY2007 10-K (2000-2007) and the FY2008 10-K (1999-2008) follow; the Q4 2007 and Q4 2008 releases extend the history with
  their years until the 10-K.
- **EPS** is diluted EPS from continuing operations before the cumulative effect of accounting changes. The company's figures excluding
  synthetic fuel (a business it says it does "not consider ... to be related to our core business, which is lodging", and excludes from
  every guide from 2006) and one-offs replace GAAP where a filing publishes them (the ACN rule), each from the latest filing that publishes
  it: 2002 $1.45, 2003 $1.55 and 2004 $2.03 before the split (the Q4 2003-Q4 2005 releases; GAAP $1.74, $1.94, $2.47), 2005 $1.33
  (excluding synthetic fuel, the CTF charge and the leveraged lease charge; GAAP $1.45), 2006 $1.65, 2007 $1.89 (excluding the ESOP
  settlement; GAAP $1.75) and 2008 $1.51 (excluding restructuring costs and other charges and certain tax items; GAAP $0.98). From the FY2007
  10-K synthetic fuel is a discontinued operation, so 2002-2004 take that 10-K's continuing figures ($0.72, $0.77, $1.01). 1998-2001 are
  GAAP: no release of those years is on EDGAR and no 10-K publishes a figure excluding the 2001 restructuring and other charges. **No year is
  excluded:** no year's one-offs reach half its income.
- **Revenues and operating income exclude synthetic fuel** (the company's own basis): total revenues less the synthetic fuel revenue line;
  operating income less synthetic fuel revenues plus its expenses, which equals the company's "operating income excluding synthetic
  fuel" (and the FY2007 10-K's restated figures, $455M to $1,087M for 2002-2006). Prints use the release's comparison basis: excluding
  synthetic fuel in Q2-Q3 2007 (Q2 2007 also excluding the ESOP settlement), as reported from Q4 2007, as adjusted from Q4 2008.
- **Guides: EPS and total fee revenue in numbers.** Every release guides the next quarter and the year: diluted EPS, total fee revenue
  (base management, franchise and incentive fees) in dollars, sometimes with its growth stated, and RevPAR. Method r2 maps them as follows:
  - current-FY EPS: the midpoint of the latest fiscal-year EPS guide: FY07 $1.89 ($1.88-1.90, Q3 2007 release); FY08 $2.05 from 2008-02-15,
    $2.03 from 2008-04-18, $1.825 from 2008-07-11 (excluding $0.10 of tax items) and $1.65 from 2008-10-03 (excluding $0.18); FY09 $0.95
    from 2009-02-13 and 2009-04-24 and $0.81 from 2009-07-17. The Q3 2009 release gives Q4 2009 only, so the Q2 2009 range stands;
  - **the 2009 ranges are guides.** From the Q3 2008 release the company calls its fiscal-year numbers "assumptions ... for internal
    planning purposes" and says it "is unable to give its typical annual guidance"; they are numeric ranges it publishes for the year, so
    they are read as guides and the words go in the guide line (a judgement call; below);
  - BASE growth and the growth factor: the next-quarter total fee revenue guide as growth on the year-ago quarter: the release's own
    percentage where it states one (Q4 2007 +14% to +17%, Q4 2008 -5% to -3%, Q1 2009 -25% to -20%), else the dollar range on the year-ago
    quarter's fees from that quarter's own release (the AVGO rule): Q1 2008 +4.7% to +6.4%, Q2 2008 +4.1% to +5.5%, Q3 2008 -0.7% to +2.6%,
    Q2 2009 -34.5% to -31.8%, Q3 2009 -30.7% to -27.4%, Q4 2009 -22.9% to -20.4% (against the 17-week Q4 2008). Fees are the revenue line the
    company guides; it guides neither total revenues nor its operating margin;
  - no margin guide in numbers (house profit margins are a property-level measure), so no margin step: the margin signal takes the latest
    quarter's operating-margin change. RevPAR guides, the outlook tables' other lines and the words are shown in the guide line and feed no
    input. A guide given with and without an item keeps the published figure, the other goes in the note (FY2008 fees +4% to +6%, "8 to 10
    percent" adjusted; the ACN rule).
- **Display-only 8-Ks** add a RevPAR note and nothing else: 2008-06-02 (second-quarter North American RevPAR "approximately 2 percent,
  compared to prior company guidance of 3 to 5 percent") and 2009-09-23 (third-quarter North American systemwide RevPAR down "approximately
  19 percent", and the $760 million of timeshare impairment charges). The other non-earnings 8-Ks (ESOP settlement, financing, timeshare note
  sales, officers and directors, segment and cost-reimbursement schedules) change no guided number and add nothing.
- **Dividends,** the latest declared cash rate: $0.0625 a quarter (FY2006 10-K), $0.0750 (dividends declared in the Q2 2007 10-Q, accepted
  2007-07-13 after the close, so dated 2007-07-16), $0.0875 (the Q2 2008 10-Q), none in cash from 2009-05-05 (a stock dividend in its place:
  "paying a stock dividend helps provide liquidity", the 8-K/A).
- **Signals.** Six, with ACN's weights: North American comparable company-operated RevPAR change across the brands (0.20; "We consider
  RevPAR to be a meaningful indicator of our performance", every 10-K), total fee revenue growth (0.20), total revenue growth (0.15), the
  occupancy change of the same RevPAR composite (0.15, in basis points), the operating-margin change (0.15) and the theme slot at 2/4.
  RevPAR and occupancy are each release's "Composite - All" row of its comparable company-operated North American table; fees, revenues and
  the margin come from its statements; each against the year-ago quarter in the same release.
- **Thresholds by rule T** over 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04, each change from the latest
  filing published by then that reports both years. The 10-Ks state the all-brand company-operated RevPAR in words for 1998, 1999, 2001 and
  2002 ("Across our Lodging brands, REVPAR for comparable company-operated U.S. properties grew by an average of ...") and in the
  "Composite North American" row for 2004-2006; no all-brand figure exists for 1997 (one brand), 2000 (the full-service brands only) or 2003
  (segments only). Occupancy changes are stated for 1998, 1999 ("occupancy remained at 77.5 percent", a change of 0), 2001, 2005 and 2006;
  2002's "declined slightly" is words, no value. Fees are first tabled for 1999 (the FY2003 10-K), operating income likewise, so both from
  2000. Revenues 1997-1999 are each filing's own sales basis; from 2002 synthetic fuel is taken out of revenues and operating income using
  each year's latest statement of income. The values and the raw figures are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives them and
  refuses to build if the engine's thresholds differ.

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2** (the SHW, WMT and RCL precedent). The "why" quotes the 10-K: "Consistent with our focus on management and
  franchising, we own very few of our lodging properties", the system's size, "The lodging industry is highly competitive ...", that the
  profitability of the hotels it operates or franchises "may be adversely affected by ... international, national and regional economic and
  geopolitical conditions", and (FY2006-FY2007) that "if the amount of sales made through Internet intermediaries increases significantly,
  our business and profitability may be harmed" (FY2008: the difficult business environment of 2008). Fees that follow the hotels through
  the economy are a cycle, not earnings that are the cycle, so CYCLICAL is not used; the kind changes the class label only.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the year's revenues split pro rata to the latest year's five lodging segments and other
  unallocated corporate revenues, the total from the fiscal-year fee guide applied to revenues; the EPS check runs on the last full year's
  operating margin less its other items (operating income less income before taxes) and its tax rate, on the company's basis.
- **Anachronism list:** Marriott names Marriott itself created, first seen in its filings after the start of 2008 (Ritz-Carlton Destination
  Club, Autograph Collection, AC Hotels by Marriott, Ritz-Carlton Reserve, Marriott Vacations Worldwide, Moxy Hotels, Marriott Bonvoy), join
  `taxonomy_eras.json`, each dated from the first Marriott filing that uses it (EDGAR full-text search). No model of any ticker contains them,
  so no output changes. The names of hotel companies it later bought (Gaylord, Protea, Delta) predate those deals and are not added. MAR's
  source ids are `MA1`-`MA31` (`W0` the prices).

fact planted after the cutoff with absurd values, and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10) changes no model and leaves no planted text
at any of the 19 cutoffs above (1 to 105 dates each).

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:

    values public on 2008-01-04.

  distributed 2011-11-21 (8-Ks of 2011-10-26 and 2011-11-21).
