Read: the 16 earnings releases Q4 2013-Q3 2017, the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks, the 10-Qs that first state each dividend raise, and every 8-K
of the period (66 filings in all; sources MA63-MA87). Five Opus subagents split the transcription by year and by the 10-Ks, and the
encodings were decided centrally. 2,406 strings across the series were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing, and all
were found. Decided on 2026-11-09, before any 2014-2017 outcome was computed:

- **Release timing.** Every release was accepted after the close (16:43-17:50 ET), so each print is dated the next trading day. The 10-Ks
  (13:27, 12:08, 12:08 and 15:55 ET) and the dividend 10-Qs were accepted during the session and keep their dates. The Q2 2017 call was
  held at 5:30 p.m. ET the same evening (`release_time`).
- **History.** Four more vintages, each with ten years from its own 10-K: FY2013 (2004-2013), FY2014 (2005-2014), FY2015 (2006-2015) and
  FY2016 (2007-2016).
  - The first year's diluted shares: 2004 480.9M (FY2006 10-K), 2005 462.3M (FY2007), 2006 430.2M (FY2008), each restated by the builder
    for the 2009 stock dividends; 2007 401.4M (FY2009 10-K, already restated).
  - The FY2014 10-K recasts the segments to continents and splits out depreciation; the FY2013 10-K's Former Timeshare line (zero in both
    years) is left out.
- **EPS: the company's figures excluding one-offs (the ACN rule).** 2005 $1.33, 2007 $1.87, 2008 $1.49, 2009 $0.93, 2010 $1.02, 2011
  $1.31 and 2012 $1.64 (the Q4 2013 release restates the Courtyard exclusion). 2013 $2.00, 2014 $2.54, 2015 $3.15 and 2016 $2.64 stand at
  GAAP: no release publishes a full-year adjusted figure on the reported basis.
  - FY2016's $2.64 carries $386M of pretax merger-related costs, under half the year's income, so it is not a distorted year. The Q4 2016
    release's "combined" $3.30 is a pro forma figure, not used.
- **Starwood** (closed 2016-09-23; 0.80 Marriott share and $21.00 per Starwood share; 134.4M shares issued) enters only through the
  prints and guides, as published (the LOW 2025 and AVGO rule). The pro formas (8-Ks of 2016-06-06 and 2017-02-15, the 8-K/A of
  2016-11-17), the deal filings and the merger agreement's terms add nothing.
  - **Prints: each release's own comparison.** Q3 2016 is as adjusted (excluding merger-related costs and eight days of Starwood) against
    Q3 2015 as reported. Q4 2016 and 2017 are as adjusted against the "combined" (pro forma) year-ago quarter the release prints. The 2017
    releases' reclassification of branding fees into franchise fees is taken as each release gives it. RevPAR comes from the combined
    "Comparable Company-Operated North American Properties" table ("North American - All" in 2017).
  - **Fee guides: the release's own percentage first.** From the Q3 2016 release, the quarter and year guides state growth "over pro
    forma" or "compared to combined" fees: Q4 2016 +1% to +2% (over $688M), Q1 2017 flat to +1% (over $740M), FY2017 +3% to +6% (over
    $3,072M).
  - **The Q1-Q3 2017 releases state no percentage.** Their quarter guides are read against the year-ago quarter's own release (the
    AVGO rule), whose fees are legacy Marriott's: Q2 2017 $820-835M against $515M (+59.2% to +62.1%), Q3 2017 $810-825M against $491M
    (+65.0% to +68.0%), Q4 2017 $825-835M against $713M (+15.7% to +17.1%).
- **Operating income** is as adjusted only where the release prints adjusted statement columns (Q4 2013-Q4 2014: none; Q3 2016 on). The
  2014-2015 schedules' "Operating income, as adjusted" belongs to a margin excluding cost reimbursements, and in Q1 2014 to a
  three-day calendar estimate, so it is not used. Rebuilt with it, no class moves.
- **Guides, the current-FY EPS midpoint.**
  - FY14: $2.37 from 2014-02-20, $2.46 from 2014-04-30, $2.455 from 2014-07-30, $2.50 from 2014-10-29.
  - FY15: $3.06 from 2015-02-19, $3.14 from 2015-07-30.
  - FY16: $3.775 from 2016-02-18. The Q1 2016 release then withdraws it ("the company is not providing full year 2016 EPS guidance at
    this time", over the merger's timing), so FY15's $3.15 stands from 2016-04-28 to the Q4 2016 print. This is the SHW, LOW, AAPL and
    WMT `withdrawn` rule, now in the MAR builder.
  - FY17: $3.88 (adjusted) from 2017-02-16, $4.005 from 2017-05-09, $4.12 from 2017-08-08, $4.23 from 2017-11-08.
  - Fee growth is stated by every full-year guide from the Q4 2013 release to the Q4 2016 release (7-12% a year before the merger). The
    quarter guides state it in the Q4 2015, Q2 2016 and Q3 2016 releases and in the Q4 2016 release.
- **Unequal quarters:** Q4 2013 (92 days against 112) and Q1 2014 (90 against 93) are as published, with the days in the notes (the 2013
  rule); the Q4 2013 guide read per day moves no class.
- **Dividends:** $0.20 a quarter from 2014-07-30, $0.25 from 2015-07-30, $0.30 from 2016-07-28 (each first stated in the Q2 10-Q; no
  8-K), $0.33 from 2017-05-09 (Q1 2017 10-Q).
- **Adds nothing:**
  - the segment recast (8-K of 2014-07-03; the bridge keeps the latest 10-K's segments);
  - the analyst meetings (2014-09-08: 2017 EPS scenarios on assumed RevPAR; 2017-03-21: rooms and fees by 2019), which are not current-year
    figures;
  - the EDITION sales, Davos and ALIS releases, and the debt, officer, director and vote 8-Ks;
  - Delta Hotels (2015), which is in the prints and guides as published.
- **Durability** stays DURABLE, risk 2. From the FY2015 10-K the competition risk factor names "home and apartment sharing services". No
  theme in `taxonomy_eras.json` covers it, so it stays in the "why" and no theme is live (the PEP rule for an unregistered risk).

Controls and checks:
- **Controls:** 129 controls over the 525 dates (111 in scope); none changes a model before its value's publication. The out-of-scope
  ones are the Q3 releases' next-year outlooks and pre-2008 facts.
- **Leak scan:** 0 hits in 183,089 (string, earlier model) pairs.
- **Firewall:** passes at 19 cutoffs (every 2014-2017 release and 10-K date, the closing, plus 2018-01-01), with 0 files changed and no
  planted text.
- **`retro_tool run`:** passes on all 210 dates, with no warnings.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **2014: RICH on 48 dates, FAIR on 5.** The FY13 anchor and then the FY14 guides ($2.37-2.50) set the floor at $38-47.5, and the price
  ran $49-79, 17-66% above it.
- **2015: RICH on 30, FAIR on 22, CHEAP on 2015-12-18** ($65.11, 9% above the floor of $59.66 on the FY15 guide of $3.14).
- **2016: FAIR on 28, CHEAP on 16, RICH on 8.**
  - CHEAP and BUY at the Q4 2015 print: the price was 3% below the floor on the FY16 guide of $3.775.
  - After the withdrawal the anchor falls to FY15's $3.15 and the floor to $56.70: mostly FAIR.
  - RICH from 2016-11-09: Q4 2016 fees +1% to +2% over pro forma, the price 31% above the floor.
- **2017: RICH to 2017-05-05, CHEAP and BUY from 2017-05-10 to 2017-11-03 (26 dates), RICH from 2017-11-09.**
  - The CHEAP run rests on the Q2 and Q3 2017 fee guides read against legacy-Marriott quarters (+59% to +68%), with the price 25-55% above
    the floor.
  - The Q4 guide (+16%) and a price 48-69% above the floor turn it back.

Sensitivity (each call changed alone, the 210 dates reclassified offline):
- **2017 guides read against the combined 2016 base** the Q4 2016 release states ($3,072M; quarter guides dropped, the year's guide
  +5% to +7%): **all 26 CHEAP dates to RICH.**
- **The 2016 EPS withdrawal ignored:** 31 classes (27 FAIR to CHEAP, 4 RICH to FAIR).
- **GAAP EPS wherever the year is not distorted:** 23 classes, toward FAIR.
- **No class moves:** FY2016 at the combined $3.30; the margin-schedule operating income; the Q4 2013 guide per day.
- **Every signal at its BEAR value:** 73 classes toward RICH. **At XBULL:** 43 toward CHEAP or FAIR.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the 2017 quarter guides read against legacy-Marriott quarters, the AVGO rule (26 classes rest on it);
- the Q1 2016 sentence read as a withdrawal of the FY2016 EPS guide (31 classes);
- FY2013-FY2016 at GAAP where no adjusted figure is published, FY2016 with its merger costs;
- operating income as adjusted only from adjusted statement columns;
- "home and apartment sharing services" left without a theme;
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL (the class label only).

### MAR 2018-2021

211 weekly dates, 2018-01-05 to 2021-12-31, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The fact sheet only gains facts, and the
525 earlier models rebuild byte for byte.

Read: the 16 earnings releases Q4 2017-Q3 2021, the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks, the 8-K of 2018-07-25 recasting FY2017 under the new revenue
standard, the COVID-19 update 8-K of 2020-03-18, the 10-Qs that first state a dividend raise, and every other 8-K of the period (76
filings; sources MA88-MA111). Five Opus subagents split the transcription by year and by the 10-Ks, and the encodings were decided
centrally. 3,799 strings across the series were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing, and all were found. Decided on
2026-11-09, before any 2018-2021 outcome was computed:

- **Release timing.**
  - Accepted after the close and dated the next trading day: Q4 2017-Q3 2018, Q4 2018, Q2-Q4 2019.
  - Accepted before the open (06:04-08:22 ET) and dated that day: Q1 2019 and every release from Q1 2020.
  - The 10-Ks were all accepted during the session and keep their dates.
  - Calls not at 10 a.m. ET (`release_time`): Q1 2019 at 1 p.m., Q3 2019 at 11 a.m., and from Q1 2020 at 8:30 a.m.
- **The new revenue standard (ASU 2014-09, full retrospective from Q1 2018).** The 8-K of 2018-07-25 recasting FY2017 is a vintage
  of its own: the latest filing that reports that year (the MSFT 2017, UNP 2010 and AAPL 2010 rule).
  - Earlier years stay as first published, a seam. The FY2018 10-K recasts 2016 too.
  - The recast has no segment table, so its segments stay the FY2017 10-K's (`groups_rev_m`). Its dividend counts from the 10-K's date
    (`dividend_published`, the UNP encoding), so it does not override the $0.41 first stated on 2018-05-10.
- **EPS.** From the new standard the company's "Adjusted" EPS, operating income and revenues also exclude cost reimbursement revenue
  and reimbursed expenses, a timing effect in every quarter. So they are not figures excluding only one-offs (the NKE FY2007, MSFT and
  XOM 2026 rule), and nothing is derived from the reconciliation lines.
  - FY2017: $4.36 from the Q4 2017 release (old basis, excluding only the merger-related costs, the Avendra gain and the Tax Act
    charge; GAAP $3.61). From the recast (2018-07-25) it is GAAP $3.84; the recast's adjusted $4.21 also excludes cost reimbursements.
  - FY2016 (recast) $2.73, FY2018 $5.38 (adjusted $6.21) and FY2019 $3.80 (adjusted $6.00) stand at GAAP.
  - **FY2020 is excluded:** $(0.82), a loss with no figure excluding only one-offs (the company's $0.18 also excludes cost
    reimbursements). The encoding is the XOM and RCL one: `excluded_note` on the Q4 2020 print, `eps_excluded` on the FY2020 vintage,
    and the window "10-yr ex-FY20" from 2021-02-19. FY2019's $3.80 stands as the last full year through 2021.
- **Prints: as reported.** Fees are base management, franchise and incentive fees. Total revenues include cost reimbursements, and
  operating income is GAAP. The adjusted figures are in each note. Each release's own year-ago column is used: 2017 recast in 2018,
  2019 for the 2020 quarters, 2020 for the 2021 quarters (2019 in the note).
  - RevPAR comes from the comparable company-operated North American table ("US & Canada" from Q4 2020), in constant dollars.
- **Guides: the current-FY EPS midpoint, as published (adjusted, `eps_guide_note`).**
  - FY18: $5.225 from 2018-02-15, $5.49 from 2018-05-09, $5.86 from 2018-08-07, $6.165 from 2018-11-06.
  - FY19: $5.985 from 2019-03-01, $6.08 from 2019-05-10, $6.015 from 2019-08-06, $5.885 from 2019-11-05.
  - FY20: $6.415 from 2020-02-27 ("does not reflect any impact from the Coronavirus outbreak").
  - **Fee growth as the release states it.** FY2018 +10-12% and FY2019 +5-8%; the quarters from Q2 2018 to Q1 2020 between +1-3% and
    +11-13%.
  - The February 2018 outlook gives the year in dollars only: $3,535-3,620M against the old-basis FY2017 fees of $3,327M (the AVGO
    rule). Its Q1 2018 guide is RevPAR only. Read against the recast $3,295M, no class moves.
- **The withdrawal.** The 8-K of 2020-03-18 (17:18 ET, dated 2020-03-19): "Marriott withdraws all aspects of its outlook and
  assumptions for 2020". It voids the EPS, fee, RevPAR and quarter fields and the note (`withdrawn`; the builder now voids the quarter
  guide too, the RCL rule).
  - No guide in numbers follows to the end of 2021, so FY2019's $3.80 stands.
  - BASE takes the latest quarter's fee growth: +7.0% (Q4 2019), then -29.7%, -76.6%, -58.4%, -56.6%, -29.3%, +174.4% (Q2 2021 on
    Q2 2020) and +95.5%.
  - The releases' COVID-19 outlook paragraphs are `words` records, which feed nothing.
- **Dividends:**
  - $0.41 a quarter from 2018-05-10 (Q1 2018 10-Q) and $0.48 from 2019-08-06 (Q2 2019 10-Q).
  - None from 2020-03-19: "Marriott anticipates that its previously announced first quarter 2020 dividend, payable on March 31, 2020,
    will be the last until conditions improve".
- **COVID enters only through the prints, the withdrawal and the dividend** (the LOW 2020 and RCL rule); no theme is live for hotels.
- **Adds nothing:**
  - the Starwood data-security 8-Ks (2018-11-30, 2019-01-04, 2019-07-09; the costs, insurance and the $126M fine accrual are in the
    prints' notes);
  - the analyst meeting of 2019-03-18 (rooms and fees by 2021);
  - the credit-card, credit-facility, debt, tender, officer, director and vote 8-Ks.
- **Builder changes,** none of which changes an earlier output: an excluded year, a withdrawal that also voids the quarter guide,
  `groups_rev_m` and `dividend_published`.

Controls and checks:
- **Controls:** 173 controls over the 736 dates (152 in scope). Each changes no model before its value's publication: the withdrawal
  acts from 2020-03-20, the recast vintage from 2018-07-27 and the excluded year's note from 2021-02-19.
- **Leak scan:** 0 hits in 328,604 (string, earlier model) pairs.
- **Firewall:** passes at 20 cutoffs (every 2018-2021 release, 10-K, recast, withdrawal and dividend date, plus 2022-01-01), with 0 files
  changed and no planted text.
- **`retro_tool run`:** passes on all 211 dates. It warns of "2039" on 51 dates: FY2019's 0.2039 tax rate, a number, not a year.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **2018: RICH to 2018-06-15 (24 dates), then FAIR and CHEAP** as the FY18 guides rise ($5.225 to $6.165) and the price falls toward the
  floor ($80-117).
- **2019: CHEAP on 51 dates, FAIR on 2.** The FY19 guides ($5.885-6.08) put the floor at $112-117; the price ran from 8% below it to 37% above.
- **2020: CHEAP to 2020-05-08, then RICH.** On 2020-03-20 the withdrawal drops the anchor to FY19's $3.80 and the floor to $72.20, and
  the price ($74.58) sits at it. From the Q1 2020 print BASE takes -29.7%, then -76.6%, and the class turns RICH.
- **2021: RICH to 2021-07-30, then CHEAP or FAIR** (14 and 8 dates) on Q2 2021's +174.4% and Q3's +95.5% fee growth against the 2020
  trough, with the price 82-107% above the floor.

Sensitivity (each call changed alone, the 211 dates reclassified offline):
- **The withdrawal ignored** (the February 2020 outlook stands): 38 classes, RICH to CHEAP or FAIR.
- **2021 fee growth against the same quarter of 2019:** 22 classes, every CHEAP or FAIR date from 2021-08-04 to RICH.
- **The company's adjusted EPS for FY2017-FY2019:** 12 classes toward CHEAP.
- **The recast vintage ignored:** 4 classes.
- **No class moves:** the February 2018 fee guide on the recast base.
- **Every signal at its BEAR value:** 86 classes. **At XBULL:** 35.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the 2021 fallback to the latest quarter's fee growth against the 2020 trough (22 classes rest on it);
- the 8-K of 2020-03-18 read as withdrawing every guided field (38 classes);
- the post-ASC 606 adjusted EPS read as not excluding only one-offs (12 classes), and FY2020's exclusion;
- the recast as a vintage of its own (4 classes);
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL (the class label only).

### MAR 2022-2026

255 weekly dates, 2022-01-07 to 2026-11-03, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The fact sheet only gains facts (sources
MA112-MA141), and the 736 earlier models rebuild byte for byte. The builder is unchanged.

```bash
python3 retro/build_mar.py --weekly 2022-01-01 2022-12-31        # 52 dates, 2022-01-07 .. 2022-12-30
python3 retro/build_mar.py --weekly 2023-01-01 2023-12-31        # 52 dates
python3 retro/build_mar.py --weekly 2024-01-01 2024-12-31        # 53 dates
python3 retro/build_mar.py --weekly 2025-01-01 2025-12-31        # 53 dates
python3 retro/build_mar.py --weekly 2026-01-01 2026-11-06        # 45 dates, to 2026-11-03 (the day after the Q3 2026 print)
```

Listed: every 8-K, 10-Q and 10-K of November 2021 to November 2026 (69 filings: 49 8-Ks, 15 10-Qs, five 10-Ks). Read for the facts, by
Opus directly: the 20 earnings releases (Q4 2021 to Q3 2026), the FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks, the dividend 8-K of 2023-02-10 and the four
10-Qs that first state a dividend raise; every other 8-K body and exhibit was checked for a guided number or a dividend. The records are
generated by a script from the filings' converted rows (statement, lodging-statistics and outlook tables parsed; every note quotes its
own filing): 680 strings checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings, 680 found. The quarterly diluted EPS, revenues and
operating income of the 20 prints and the five full-year EPS figures were cross-checked against SEC XBRL company facts (64 of 65 agree;
the other is Q4 2025 EPS, $1.65 in the release, where XBRL has no fourth-quarter figure and the year less nine months, $1.67, is not an
EPS). Each Q4 release's full-year revenues, operating income, fees, EPS and RevPAR equal its 10-K's. Decided on 2026-11-09, before any
2022-2026 date was built or any outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings release was accepted before the open (06:52-07:42 ET) and is dated that day; the weekly date is the
  next trading day (the weekly rule). Each 10-K was accepted during the session on the day of its Q4 release (12:23-15:00 ET). The
  dividend 8-K of 2023-02-10 was accepted 16:10 ET and is dated 2023-02-13. Calls at 8:30 a.m. ET (8:00 for Q3 2022, Q3 2023 and Q3 2026).
- **History.** From FY2021 the 10-Ks reserve Item 6 and report three years. Each vintage (FY2021 to FY2025) takes its three years from its
  own statements and EPS note and every earlier year from the latest 10-K that reports it (the ACN FY21, WMT, NKE and RCL rule). The first
  year's diluted shares come from the EPS note of the 10-K two years later (2012 332.9M from the FY2014 10-K, 2013 313.0M FY2015, 2014
  296.8M FY2016, 2015 272.8M FY2017, 2016 295.7M FY2018), the way 2010 and 2011 were taken.
  - Segments: U.S. & Canada and International to the FY2023 10-K; from the FY2024 10-K four reportable segments (U.S. & Canada, EMEA,
    Greater China, APEC; 2023 recast, Caribbean & Latin America in unallocated corporate and other), as each 10-K gives them.
- **EPS: GAAP for every year from 2016** (the 2018-2021 rule: the company's adjusted figures also exclude cost reimbursement revenue and
  reimbursed expenses, a timing effect). FY2020 stays excluded. FY2021 $3.34, FY2022 $7.24, FY2023 $10.18, FY2024 $8.33, FY2025 $9.51.
  - No year is distorted. FY2023 carries $228M of tax benefits from international intellectual property transactions, a $223M tax
    valuation allowance release and a $63M termination fee ($0.77, $0.75 and $0.16 a share in the Q4 2023 release), well under half its
    $3,083M net income, and no filing publishes a figure excluding only them, so it stays at $10.18 (the ACN rule for a one-off without a
    published figure; its 8.7% tax rate is the EPS check's for FY2023).
- **2022 before the first guide.** The Q4 2021 and Q1 2022 releases give no fee, EPS or operating income outlook: rooms growth, investment
  spending, the CEO's words and (Q4 2021 only) the COVID-19 paragraph. They are display-only `note` records, not `words`: only the Q4 2021
  release has the COVID-19 paragraph, and a `words` record would carry it into the numeric guides from August.
  - FY2019's $3.80 stands to 2022-02-11 (FY2021 current, FY2020 excluded), then FY2021's $3.34 (the rollover rule) to 2022-07-29.
  - BASE takes the latest quarter's fee growth against the 2021 recovery quarters (the 2021 rule): +95.5% (Q3 2021), +96.5% (Q4 2021),
    +83.1% (Q1 2022).
- **Guides from the Q2 2022 release.** Each release has an outlook table: next-quarter and fiscal-year gross fee revenues in dollars,
  "Adjusted EPS – diluted", systemwide constant-dollar RevPAR (against 2019 in the Q2 and Q3 2022 releases, year on year from Q4 2022) and
  other lines.
  - Current-FY EPS, the adjusted midpoint as published (the 2018-2019 rule): FY22 $6.46 from 2022-08-02, $6.545 from 2022-11-03; FY23
    $7.57 from 2023-02-14, $8.195, $8.505, $8.545; FY24 $9.35 from 2024-02-13, $9.48, $9.315, $9.23; FY25 $10.005 from 2025-02-11,
    $10.005, $9.965, $10.02; FY26 $11.445 from 2026-02-10, $11.505, $11.725, $12.105.
  - BASE: the next-quarter fee range, no percentage stated, read against the year-ago quarter's fees from that quarter's own release (the
    AVGO rule): Q3 2022 +30.2% to +35.3% (against Q3 2021's $776M), Q4 2022 +28.8% to +31.2%, Q1 2023 +28.2% to +30.7%, then +12% to +14%
    (Q2-Q3 2023), +4.8% to +8.4% (Q4 2023 to Q3 2024), +2.1% to +5.3% (Q4 2024 to Q4 2025), and +7.1% to +13.1% (Q1-Q4 2026). The 2026
    ranges include the new co-branded credit card terms ("around a 35 percent increase in the co-branded credit card fees", Q4 2025
    release), as published.
  - The RevPAR guides, the other lines and the outlook's words are display only, in the guide line.
- **Prints: as reported** (the 2018-2021 encoding): fees are base management, franchise and incentive fees; total revenues include cost
  reimbursement revenue; operating income is GAAP; the adjusted figures and the release's one-off sentences are in the notes. RevPAR and
  occupancy are the "US & Canada - All" row of the first table ("Comparable Company-Operated US & Canada Properties", constant dollars)
  against the year-ago quarter. Q1 2024 has 91 days against 90, as published.
- **Dividends,** each rate from the first filing that states it: $0.30 a quarter from 2022-05-04 (the Q1 2022 release: "Marriott resumes
  cash dividends"); $0.40 from 2023-02-13 (the 8-K of 2023-02-10); $0.52 from 2023-08-01, $0.63 from 2024-07-31, $0.67 from 2025-08-05 and
  $0.73 from 2026-08-03 (each the Q2 10-Q, the first filing after the May declaration). The 10-K vintages carry the latest rate on their
  own dates. Before the Q1 2022 release the FY2021 10-K's "We also did not declare any cash dividends in 2021" stands.
- **Adds nothing:**
  - the security analyst meeting 8-K of 2023-09-27 ("reiterate its 2023 outlook given in August"; its 2023-2025 growth rates and 2025
    figures are multi-year, the LOW multi-year rule and the MAR analyst meetings of 2014-2019);
  - the director, officer, vote, notes, credit agreement and blackout 8-Ks, and the leadership realignment of 2026-01-09;
  - the acquisitions (City Express, citizenM, the Sheraton Grand Chicago, Lefay), which are in the prints and guides as published.
- **Durability** stays DURABLE, risk 2, each vintage's "why" quoting its own 10-K. The FY2025 10-K's booking-channel risk factor adds that
  "the introduction of AI capabilities by existing and emerging travel intermediaries may change the way guests plan, book, and pay for
  travel". GENAI's scope (software, IT services, information, search, education, mobility) does not cover lodging distribution, so the
  sentence stays in the "why" and no theme is live (the rule for an unregistered risk, as home sharing from FY2015).
- **Anachronism list:** Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection (2023-02-14), Apartments by Marriott Bonvoy (2023-03-28), City Express by Marriott
  (2023-05-02), MGM Collection with Marriott Bonvoy (2023-08-01), StudioRes (2023-09-27), Four Points Flex (2024-11-04), Sonder by Marriott
  Bonvoy (2025-02-11), Series by Marriott (2025-08-05), Outdoor Collection by Marriott Bonvoy (2025-11-04) and Marriott Bonvoy Outdoors
  (2026-03-27) join `taxonomy_eras.json`, each dated from the first Marriott filing that uses it (EDGAR full-text search). No model of any

  added; Homes & Villas by Marriott (first in a 2019 10-Q) predates this batch and is left to the owner.

Controls and checks:
- **Controls:** altering one value of each new print (its RevPAR and quarter EPS, and each Q4 print's full-year EPS), guide (its EPS range,
  next-quarter fee range, display and note), vintage (its first- and last-year EPS) and dividend: 135 controls over the 255 dates. None
  changes a model dated before its value's publication; 129 change the first weekly date on or after it. The six that change nothing are

  session, and the $0.40 dividend of the 8-K of 2023-02-10, superseded by the FY2022 10-K before the next weekly date.
- **Leak scan:** the notes, quoted texts, guide ranges, prints' figures and source ids of every fact first published from 2022 appear in no
  MAR model dated before their publication (0 hits in 324,551 (string, earlier model) pairs, after dropping four strings an earlier fact
  already carries, among them the FY2025 EPS range $9.82-10.19 the Q1 2025 release repeats).
- **Firewall:** passes at 22 cutoffs (every 2022-2026 release and 10-K date, the dividend 8-K's date, and 2026-11-04), with 0 files
  changed and no planted text in 742 to 991 earlier models each.
- **`retro_tool run`:** passes on all 255 dates. It warns of "2024" on nine dates (2023-11-03 to 2023-12-29): the Q3 2023 release's
  words that the MGM rooms "will now be added to its distribution in early 2024", a forecast, not a later fact.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **Classes:** 2022 FAIR 25, CHEAP 27; 2023 CHEAP 49, FAIR 3; 2024 FAIR 39, CHEAP 6, RICH 8; 2025 FAIR 36, RICH 14, CHEAP 3; 2026 RICH 31,
  FAIR 14 (of the 255: CHEAP 85, FAIR 117, RICH 53). The legacy tier is BUY on 89, ACCUMULATE 48, WATCHLIST 65 and AVOID 53. Robustness is
  8 of 8 on 71 dates, 7 on 70, 6 on 86, 5 on 16 and 4 on 12. Ratio B is finite on every date.
- **January to July 2022 rests on trough anchors.** FY2019's $3.80 and then FY2021's $3.34 put the price ($138-183) at 44-54x, the 86th
  to 100th percentile of its own window, and 97-161% over the EPP floor ($80, then $70). BASE runs +83% to +97%/yr on the recovery
  quarters' fee growth, so Ratio B stays at 0.40-0.78 and the class is FAIR on 25 of the 30 dates and CHEAP on five (2022-01-21,
  2022-01-28, 2022-06-24 to 2022-07-08).
- **CHEAP without a break from 2022-08-03 to 2023-12-08 (71 dates).** The FY22 guide ($6.46) lifts the floor to $129, and the FY23 guides
  ($7.57 to $8.545) to $151-179: the price ($137-209) sits 3-38% over it, at the 8th-73rd percentile of its P/E range, while BASE runs
  +29% to +33%/yr on the quarter fee guides against the 2021-2022 recovery quarters, then +12.6% to +12.8% and +5.7%.
- **From December 2023 mostly FAIR, then RICH.** On BASE of +2% to +8%/yr (the quarter fee guides of Q4 2023 to Q4 2025) the class is FAIR
  on 39 dates of 2024 and 36 of 2025. RICH comes at prices 34-59% over the floor: 2024-11-15 to 2025-02-12 (except 2025-01-03 and
  2025-01-10), from 2025-11-05, and on 31 of the 45 dates of 2026 ($313-416, Ratio B 1.79-3.99). CHEAP returns only in the June and August
  2024 dips ($218-231) and in the April 2025 fall (2025-04-04 to 2025-04-17, $215-225, 2-7% over the floor).
- **The proxy composite** reads 3.55-3.70 in 2022 (revenue, fees, RevPAR and occupancy at XBULL against the 2021 quarters), 2.50-3.70 in

How far each call moves the classes (the 255 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline with `retro_tool`'s own
classifier; no outcome consulted; the harness reproduces all 255 classes and tiers unchanged):
- **BASE against the same quarter of 2019, annualized,** wherever the year-ago quarter is a COVID quarter (the latest-quarter fallback of
  Q3 2021 to Q1 2022, and the Q3 2022 to Q1 2023 quarter fee guides): **45 classes** and 59 tiers. All 30 dates of January to July 2022
  move to RICH (25 from FAIR, five from CHEAP), and 15 CHEAP dates of August 2022 to February 2023 move to FAIR. This is the call the 2022
  classes rest on;
- **the company's adjusted EPS** (which also excludes cost reimbursements) for FY2017-FY2019 and FY2021-FY2025: **47 classes** and 61 tiers,
  in both directions (FAIR to CHEAP in January 2022; FAIR to RICH on 32 dates, 15 of them in 2025; CHEAP to FAIR on 11);
- **FY2023 at $8.50**, GAAP less the per-share tax benefits and termination fee the Q4 2023 release states: 7 classes, 7 tiers;
- **the fiscal-year fee guide instead of the next-quarter guide:** 6 classes (FAIR to CHEAP, 2023-12-15 to 2024-01-19), 4 tiers;
- **every signal at its BEAR value:** 152 classes (toward RICH or FAIR), no tier; **at XBULL:** 60 classes (toward CHEAP or FAIR), no tier.
Of the CHEAP run from 2022-08-03 (71 dates), 15 move with BASE against 2019, five (August-December 2023) with the adjusted EPS and 23 with
the signals at BEAR. The RICH dates of 2025-2026 move only with the signals at XBULL and, on two dates, with FY2023 ex-tax.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight (beyond the earlier lists):
- growth against the 2021-2022 recovery quarters kept as the frozen fallback and the AVGO rule compute it, which makes BASE +83% to +97%/yr
  in the first half of 2022 and about +30%/yr from August 2022 to April 2023, rather than a base period chosen for the restart (45 classes
  move against 2019);
- GAAP EPS from FY2021 on, the 2018-2021 reading of the company's adjusted figures (47 classes move);
- FY2023 kept at $10.18 with its tax benefits, no figure excluding only them being published (7 classes);
- the quarter fee guides read against the year-ago quarter's own release rather than the fiscal-year guide (6 classes);
- the Q4 2021 and Q1 2022 outlooks as notes rather than `words` (display only);
- the FY2025 10-K's AI sentence left without a theme (the class label only; no theme in `taxonomy_eras.json` covers lodging distribution);
- the anachronism terms chosen (Marriott-created brand names; Homes & Villas by Marriott, first used in 2019, is left to the owner);
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL (the class label only).

## BKR (Baker Hughes): the fourteenth ticker, in staging

The BKR series is built apart from ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, AVGO, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT, RCL and MAR and shares nothing with them but
the machinery: its own fact sheet (`retro/facts/BKR.json`), builder (`retro/build_bkr.py`, the XOM 2008 builder with oilfield services
encodings) and engine (`retro/templates/bkr_engine.py.tmpl`, the XOM engine with oilfield services signals). The method is still r2. No
fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters a BKR model, and neither does the profile of BKR in
`data/business_profiles.json` (a 2026 judgement, not read for this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/BKR/`, beside the
others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`.

```bash
python3 retro/build_bkr.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                   # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_bkr.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                   # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
python3 retro/build_bkr.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31 ("BKR 2010-2013")
python3 retro/build_bkr.py --weekly 2014-01-01 2017-06-30                   # 183 dates, 2014-01-03 .. 2017-06-30 ("BKR 2014-2017")
python3 retro/build_bkr.py --weekly 2019-01-28 2021-12-31                   # 153 dates, 2019-02-01 .. 2021-12-31 ("BKR 2018-2021")
python3 retro/build_bkr.py --weekly 2022-01-03 2026-11-06                   # 253 dates, 2022-01-07 .. 2026-11-06 ("BKR 2022-2026")
for d in staging/retrospective/BKR/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series BKR
for c in 2008-01-30 2008-01-31 2008-02-22 2008-04-22 2008-07-22 2008-07-30 2008-10-22 2009-01-01 2009-01-28 2009-03-02 \
         2009-04-29 2009-08-05 2009-11-04 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c BKR; done   # later: "BKR 2010-2013", "BKR 2014-2017"
```

Read for the history and the decade's signal values: the selected financial data, statements of operations and tables of revenues by
country of the FY1998-FY2008 10-Ks (the FY1998-FY2001 10-Ks are plain-text filings), and the Q4 2003, Q4 2004, Q4 2006 and Q4 2007
releases for the company's operating profit per share. Read for the prints: every 8-K of October 2006 to January 2010 (43; the
non-earnings ones item by item), with the 10-Qs of 2007-2009 for the dividend rates. All by Opus directly, with no delegated
transcription. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the transcribed raw figures, so every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is
computed, not typed; 267 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (every statement row behind a print, every
selected-data and country row behind the history and rule T, every quoted sentence), and a second script matched every raw figure to
the row it is cited from. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (converted from UTC; before 2003 EDGAR gives the filing
date only). Decided on 2026-11-10, before any BKR outcome was computed:

- **The company and the symbol.** Every date of 2008-2009 is Baker Hughes Incorporated (CIK 808362), listed on the NYSE as BHI. Today's
  BKR is its successor (the 2017 combination with GE's oil and gas business, renamed in 2019), and Yahoo serves BHI's price history under
  BKR (from 1990, as traded: no split after 1990; the July 2017 fall is the combination's special dividend, after every outcome horizon
  of these dates). `TICKER` and the folder are the series key BKR, which `retro_tool.py` needs for the index, the series and the price
  check; every printed line (the report header, the summary, the price source's title) names the listing of the date (`LISTED_SYMBOL =
  "BHI"`). The constant, the folder and the Yahoo URL still say BKR: a residual that names a later symbol, though no fact about the
  later company; the owner may drop `TICKER` at export.
- **Fiscal calendar.** Calendar years from 1998. Fiscal 1997 ended September 30, 1997: the year end moved to December 31 after the August
  1998 merger with Western Atlas (a pooling of interests), and the transition period of October-December 1997 is not a fiscal year, so
  rule T's 1998 change compares calendar 1998 with the year to September 1997, as the filings place them side by side. The builder
  checks every fiscal year end a 10-K states against the rule. The four dates of January 2008 have FY2007 as the current year until the
  Q4 2007 print (2008-01-30).
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of 2007-2009 was accepted before the open (06:01-07:09 ET; the call at 8:30 a.m. ET, 10:00 for
  Q2 2008), on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, so each print's week is dated the next day: 2008-01-31, 2008-04-23, 2008-07-23, 2008-10-23,
  2009-01-29, 2009-04-30, 2009-08-06, 2009-11-05. The FY2006, FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks were accepted after the close (2007-02-23 17:00,
  2008-02-21 16:14, 2009-02-27 16:22 ET), so they are dated 2007-02-26, 2008-02-22 and 2009-03-02.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it.** The FY2006 vintage takes 2002-2006 from the FY2006 10-K, 2001 from the
  FY2005 10-K, 2000 from the FY2004 10-K and 1999 from the FY2003 10-K (EPS, revenues; 1999's diluted shares from the FY2001 10-K, the
  last with its statement of operations). The FY2007 10-K (2003-2007) and the FY2008 10-K (2004-2008, in whole millions) follow; the Q4
  2007 and Q4 2008 releases extend the history with their years until the 10-K. Seams stay as published: the Process segment, shown as
  discontinued in the FY1999 10-K and restored in the FY2000 10-K, and the businesses discontinued later (EIMCO, BIRD, the West Africa
  oil operations, the mining bits, Baker Supply Products).
- **1998 excluded; 1999 and 2000 kept.** 1998 was a loss from continuing operations ($(0.92) per diluted share, the FY2002 10-K: the
  Western Atlas merger costs, an unusual charge and other charges), with no published figure excluding them, so it is excluded and the
  history and the P/E window start with 1999 (`pe_window_start` 1999-01-01, the ACN FY02 and AAPL FY2002 rule): a 9.0- to 9.9-year
  window in 2008, ten years from 2009. 1999 and 2000 are tested by the r2 wording ("listed one-off items larger than the year's net
  income"), with the items summed as the 10-Ks list them, charges against gains (the AAPL FY2003 reading): 1999's $23.5M ($122.8M of
  seismic restructuring less an $11.4M reversal, $54.8M of gains on disposal of assets, a $31.5M gain on trading securities and a
  $1.6M merger-cost reversal) against $33.3M of net income; 2000's $89.3M ($75.5M of losses on oil and gas properties and $35.5M of
  restructuring less $7.6M of gains on product-line sales and a $14.1M trading gain) against $102.3M. Both stay at GAAP ($0.08, $0.21).
  A judgement call: the charges alone would exclude 1999, and income from continuing operations as the comparator (AVGO's FY2014
  wording) would exclude 2000; neither moves a class (below).
- **EPS** is diluted EPS from continuing operations before extraordinary items and the cumulative effect of accounting changes. The
  company's operating profit per diluted share (income from continuing operations excluding identified items) replaces it where a filing
  publishes one (the ACN rule), from the latest filing that does: 2002 $0.94 (Q4 2003 release; GAAP $0.67), 2003 $0.98 (Q4 2004
  release; GAAP $0.52), 2006 $4.10 (Q4 2006 release, then the Q4 2007 release; GAAP $7.21 with the $1,743.5M pre-tax gain on the sale of
  the WesternGeco interest). 2007 had no identified items ($4.73). 2008 is GAAP $5.30: its releases give the per-share effects of its
  items (a $0.13 litigation charge, a $0.06 product-line gain, a $0.10 discrete tax benefit, an $0.08 auction-rate impairment) but no EPS
  excluding them, and nothing is derived (the NKE 2008 rule).
- **No guide in numbers.** Baker Hughes gave EPS guidance through its Q3 2006 release and none from the Q4 2006 release on; no release,
  10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K of 2007-2009 guides EPS, total revenue or a margin in numbers. Each release to Q3 2008 ends with an Outlook
  section: revenue outside North America (fiscal 2007 "up between 20% and 21%" in the Q3 2007 release; fiscal 2008 "in a percentage
  range from the low to mid-teens" in the Q4 2007 and Q1 2008 releases, "14% to 16%" in Q2 2008; the fourth quarter of 2008 "between 14%
  and 15%" in Q3 2008), corporate expenses, capital expenditures, depreciation and the tax rate. The 2009 releases have no Outlook
  section. So, on every date:
  - current-FY EPS: the last full year's EPS stands: FY06's $4.10 to 2008-01-25, FY07's $4.73 from 2008-01-31, FY08's $5.30 from
    2009-01-29 (the UNP, NKE and XOM rule);
  - BASE growth and the growth factor: the latest quarter's total revenue growth, as reported (the UNP and XOM rule);
  - no margin step: the margin signal takes the latest quarter's change in operating margin.
  - The outside-North-America outlook is shown in the guide line and catalyst (3), display only: it guides a region (56-59% of revenue),
    not the company's revenue ("Revenue growth in 2007 from North America remains uncertain", the FY2006 10-K). This differs from MAR, whose fee
    guides are the revenue line the company guides; a judgement call that moves no class (below).
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the rate: $0.13 a quarter (FY2006 and FY2007 10-Ks), $0.15 from the Q2 2008 10-Q
  (accepted 2008-07-29 17:12 ET, dated 2008-07-30; "authorized" on July 24, 2008 in a news release that is not on EDGAR), $0.15 in the
  FY2008 10-K.
- **Region basis.** From the Q2 2008 release, revenue by region follows the region that provides operational support (the 8-Ks of
  2008-07-08, 2008-07-18 and 2008-10-07 re-disclose the history; Trinidad moves to North America); each print takes the year-ago quarter
  its own release shows, so North America in Q2 2008 is +19.7% on a restated $1,055.8M.
- **Signals.** Six, with ACN's weights: North America revenue growth (0.20; the United States and Canada), revenue growth outside North
  America (0.20; Oilfield Operations less North America), total revenue growth (0.15), the gross-margin change (0.15; revenues less cost
  of sales, cost of services and rentals and research and engineering, which matches the 10-Ks' "cost of revenues", research and
  engineering included until the FY2006 10-K's "cost of revenues and research and engineering"), the operating-margin change (0.15) and
  the theme slot at 2/4. Each value is the release's own, against the year-ago quarter in the same release. The rig count, which the
  10-Ks call a key business driver, is shown and not scored: the releases state it by region and in words that change from quarter to
  quarter (U.S. land to Q3 2008, the U.S. in Q4 2008, none in Q1 2009, North America in 2009), and no filing gives a fourth quarter's.
  Services-and-rentals revenue was considered and not used: the 10-Ks split it out only from the FY2006 10-K (2004-2006), too short
  for rule T.
- **Thresholds by rule T** over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04: ten changes, each from
  the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years (selected financial data for revenues, cost of revenues and operating
  income; the tables of revenues by country for North America). The values and the raw figures are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the
  builder re-derives the thresholds and refuses to build if the engine's differ.

  | Signal | Fiscal 1997-2006 | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | North America revenue | 25.67, 16.81, -14.07, 10.24, 3.61, -13.12, 14.04, 14.36, 20.89, 31.18 % | -42 / -14 / 14 / 31 % |
  | revenue outside North America | 16.86, 17.78, -26.67, 2.88, 4.31, 5.81, 4.08, 17.49, 16.28, 21.54 % | -64 / -27 / 11 / 22 % |
  | total revenue growth | 20.19, 18.1, -23.07, -0.45, 4.36, -2.75, 8.05, 16.17, 18.19, 25.63 % | -58 / -23 / 12 / 26 % |
  | gross-margin change | 6.5, -304.7, -8.4, 440.1, 642.3, -116.0, -93.7, 118.8, 278.3, 473.0 bp | -670 / -300 / 60 / 640 bp |
  | operating-margin change | -174.1, -1055.8, 544.9, 374.9, 747.2, -289.9, -90.8, 278.5, 373.7, 426.2 bp | -2440 / -1060 / 330 / 750 bp |

- **Durability: CYCLICAL, risk 2** (the XOM precedent). The 10-K says so in its own words: "Our business is cyclical and is dependent upon
  our customers' forecasts of future oil and natural gas prices, future economic growth and hydrocarbon demand and estimates of future oil
  and natural gas production" (FY2008: "expectations"), and "The primary driver of our business is our customers' capital and operating
  expenditures dedicated to exploring, and drilling for, and developing and producing oil and natural gas". The "why" quotes those, the
  business and "We operate in a highly competitive environment". The kind changes the class label only (CHEAP reads CYCLICAL, RISK
  PRICED IN). From the FY2007 10-K (2008-02-22) a risk factor adds that "demand for hydrocarbons could be impacted by environmental
  regulation targeting reduction of greenhouse gas emissions" (FY2008: "or carbon taxes"); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live only from
  2015-12-12 and scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, so the words join the "why" (the PEP obesity rule). Baker Hughes'
  FY2007 10-K is an earlier verified company acknowledgment than the registry's basis, and earlier than XOM's FY2009 10-K; whether to
  move the date, or to widen the scope to oilfield services, is left to the owner.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the year's revenues split pro rata to the last year's two segments (Drilling and
  Evaluation, Completion and Production), the total from the latest quarter's revenue growth applied to the last year; the EPS check runs
  on the last year's pre-tax margin (FY06 on the company's operating profit before tax excluding the WesternGeco gain) and tax rate.
- **Adds nothing:** the non-earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2009 (officers and directors, credit agreements and note offerings, 10b5-1 repurchase
  plans, the reservoir-consulting acquisitions of 2008-04-17, the ReedHycalog settlement of 2008-05-22 (booked in Q2 2008, which reports
  it), the regional histories of 2008-07-08, 2008-07-18 and 2008-10-07, the Hurricane Ike facility report of 2008-09-19, the
  reorganization by geography of 2009-03-24, interest-rate swaps, and the BJ Services merger agreement of 2009-08-31 and its lawsuits:
  a pending deal with no guided number, the XOM XTO rule), and the Q2 2007 earnings estimate of 2007-07-13, which the Q2 2007 release
  replaced.
- **Anachronism list:** names Baker Hughes created, first in its filings after the start of 2008 (Kymera, TerrAdapt, "Baker Hughes, a GE
  company", BHGE, Leucipa, Cordant), join `taxonomy_eras.json`, each dated from the first Baker Hughes filing that uses it (EDGAR
  full-text search; after-close filings from the next trading day). No model of any ticker contains them, so no output changes. BKR's
  source ids are `BK1`-`BK25`.

Controls: altering one value of each print (its North America revenue, and each Q4 print's full-year EPS), vintage (its last year's EPS)
and the dividend change no date before its publication and change the first weekly date on or after it (16 of 16). A scan of the 105
models for the source ids, notes, quoted texts and figures of every later print, vintage, dividend and source finds none before its
publication (0 of 7,020 pairs, after dropping strings an earlier fact already carries). Rebuilding the 2008 dates of ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL,
NKE, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT, RCL and MAR and the 2009 dates of AVGO changes nothing (658 models). The firewall (every kind of
fact planted after the cutoff with absurd values, and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10) changes no model and leaves no planted text
at any of the 14 cutoffs above (4 to 105 dates each).

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **CHEAP and BUY on all 105 dates,** robustness 8 of 8 on every date.
- **BULL and XBULL start from 1999's trough** (the AAPL pattern): BULL is the decade EPS CAGR, +75.5%/yr over 1999-2006 ($0.08 to
  $4.10), +66.5% over 1999-2007, +59.4% over 1999-2008, at the 75th-percentile P/E: BULL prices of $419-492. XBULL is the 1999-2001 run
  (+298.4%/yr). Ratio B runs from -0.04 to 0.12, so the legacy tier reads BUY throughout, and the market composite sits at the bottom of
  its grid (1.05-1.22).
- **The window holds 1999-2000 at 96-452x** (EPS $0.08 and $0.21), so the 90th percentile is 205-227x in 2008 and the median 26-28x; the
  10th percentile is 16-17x. The EPP floor, the median of the calendar-year P/E lows (1999 208x, 2000 96x, 2001 21x, 2002 24x, 2003 28x,
  2004 20x, 2005 16x, 2006 15x, 2007 13x), is 20x on every date but 2009-12-31 (18x, once 1999 leaves the window).
- **The class follows the floor.** On the last full year's EPS the stock traded at 13.4-19.4x to September 2008 (the 0th-26th
  percentile of its own range), 5.7-10.4x from October and 5.0-8.9x through 2009, 3-75% under the floor ($82 in January 2008, $95 from
  the Q4 2007 print, $106 from the Q4 2008 print).
- **BEAR is 2002** (-26.0%/yr: 2001's $1.27 to 2002's $0.94) at the 10th-percentile P/E: $39-44 in 2008, $37-44 to July 2009 and
  $22-37 after, as 2009's single-digit multiples enter the window.
- **BASE follows the quarter's revenue,** with almost no buyback term (diluted shares 329.9M in 1999, 332.6M in 2006, 309M in 2008):
  +15.8%/yr (Q3 2007), +12.1% (Q4 2007), +8.4% (Q1 2008), +18.5% (Q2 2008), +12.8% (Q3 2008), +17.0% (Q4 2008), +0.6% (Q1 2009),
  -21.4% (Q2 2009) and -25.1% (Q3 2009).
- **The EPS anchor is the last full year:** FY08's $5.30 stands through 2009, while the 2009 quarters earned $0.63, $0.28 and $0.18 (the
  XOM and AAPL pattern).
- **The proxy composite** is 2.55 (Q3 2007), 2.20 (Q4 2007), 2.00 (Q1 2008), 2.55 (Q2 2008), 2.35 (Q3 and Q4 2008), 1.85 (Q1 2009: North
  America -8.0%, the operating margin -860bp), 1.50 (Q2 2009: North America -37.9%) and 1.35 (Q3 2009: revenue -25.8%, the operating
  margin -1,499bp, BEAR).

How far each call moves the classes (the 105 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- 2000 excluded as distorted (the history and the window from 2001): no class, no tier;
- 1999 excluded (the charges alone; the history and the window from 2000): no class, no tier;
- GAAP EPS in every year instead of the company's operating profit per share: no class, no tier;
- the outside-North-America outlook as BASE where it is a number (fiscal 2007 +20.5%, fiscal 2008 +15%, the fourth quarter of 2008
  +14.5%): no class, no tier;
- every signal at its BEAR value, or at its XBULL value: no class, no tier.
The CHEAP calls rest on the stock's own P/E history (the window and the floor) and the last-full-year anchor, which none of these calls
touches.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows that North American drilling collapsed in 2009: the two regions the releases report, total
  revenue, the gross margin and the operating margin, with the rig count shown, not scored (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically);
- keeping 1999 and 2000 (charges netted against gains, net income as the comparator), which sets BULL, XBULL and the window's upper
  percentiles; no class moves either way;
- the outside-North-America outlook as display only;
- CYCLICAL rather than DURABLE (the class label only), on the 10-K's own "Our business is cyclical";
- the greenhouse-gas risk factor left in the "why" rather than putting ENERGY_TRANSITION on the watch list before its registry date
  (text only);
- the series key BKR and the Yahoo URL in each model, which name a later symbol (no class depends on them).

### BKR 2010-2013

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The fact sheet only gains facts: its
2008-2009 content is unchanged and the 105 earlier models rebuild byte for byte after the builder changes below.

```bash
python3 retro/build_bkr.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for c in 2010-01-26 2010-02-26 2010-05-04 2010-08-03 2010-11-01 2011-01-25 2011-02-28 2011-03-03 2011-04-27 2011-07-25 2011-11-01 \
         2012-01-24 2012-02-27 2012-03-21 2012-04-24 2012-07-20 2012-10-19 2012-12-19 2013-01-23 2013-02-14 2013-04-19 2013-07-19 \
         2013-10-18 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c BKR; done
```

Read: the 16 earnings releases from Q4 2009 to Q3 2013 and the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks, every other 8-K of February 2010 to January 2014

share plus the $17.50 special dividend. Yahoo's BKR series runs on through it, but the company does not: BHGE's financial statements are
GE Oil & Gas's (the accounting predecessor), and BHGE has no full year of its own earnings per share before FY2018. None of Baker Hughes'
history, prints or anchors describes the new company, and a BHGE series would need a decision method r2 does not make (a new listing
under the listing rule with no full-year EPS, or the series ending with BHI). The dates from 2017-07-07 are not built; that call is the
owner's. (The owner then asked for 2018-2021: the series resumes on 2019-02-01 as a new listing, "BKR 2018-2021" below.)

### BKR 2018-2021

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** The owner asked for 2018-2021 on the same rules. The company listed in those years is
Baker Hughes, a GE company (BHGE; Baker Hughes Company, BKR, from October 2019), and under method r2 **the first date that can be built is
2019-02-01**: 153 weekly dates, 2019-02-01 to 2021-12-31. No date from 2017-07-07 to 2019-01-25 is built (the 56 weeks of 2018 and
January 2019 among them): a model needs the stock's own P/E, and the new company published no full year of EPS before its Q4 2018 release
(2019-01-31). Building 2018 would take a new rule (an EPS anchor for a first year without one), which is the owner's call and a method
note; nothing was invented to fill the gap.

```bash
python3 retro/build_bkr.py --weekly 2019-01-28 2021-12-31                   # 153 dates, 2019-02-01 .. 2021-12-31
for c in 2019-01-31 2019-02-20 2019-04-30 2019-07-31 2019-10-18 2019-10-30 2020-01-22 2020-02-14 2020-04-13 2020-04-22 2020-07-22 \
         2020-10-21 2021-01-21 2021-02-26 2021-04-21 2021-07-21 2021-10-20 2021-10-28 2021-12-07 2022-01-01; do
  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c BKR; done
```

The series key stays BKR. The fact sheet gains a `listing`, `listings`, the new company's vintages, prints and one display-only outlook
(marked `"era": "bhge"`), its own rule-T values (`rule_t_bhge`) and sources BK69-BK90; the builder sends every date after 2017-07-03 to
`build_bhge`, with its own engine (`retro/templates/bkr2_engine.py.tmpl`, the BKR engine with the AVGO engine's short-history lines and
new signals). The 2008-2017 content of the fact sheet is unchanged and the 497 earlier models rebuild byte for byte. Nothing of Baker
Hughes Incorporated's history, prints, dividends or thresholds enters a model of the new company, and nothing of the new company's
enters an earlier date (checked both ways, below).

Read: the 12 earnings releases from Q4 2018 to Q3 2021, the Q4 2017 and Q2 2018 releases, the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks, the 8-K of 2018-11-13
that recasts the FY2017 statements for the new revenue standard, the 8-K12B of 2017-07-03, and the 28 other 8-Ks of November 2018 to
December 2021 by their item text (their exhibits, agreements and indentures were not read); the four proxy statements of 2018-2021 and
the three conference presentations were searched for a full-year adjusted EPS or a guide in numbers and have none. All by the session's
model directly. The fact sheet's new entries are generated by a script from the transcribed rows, so every growth rate and margin is
computed; 380 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing, and all 380 were found; the script also checks each
release's headline figures against its statement of income and its four segments against its revenue. Each source's date comes from
EDGAR's acceptance time. Decided on 2026-11-10, before any outcome of these dates was computed:

- **A new listing, not a continuation (the listing rule).** The 8-K12B: Baker Hughes Incorporated traded "until the close of NYSE on July
  3, 2017" and "The Class A Common Stock will begin trading on NYSE under the ticker symbol “BHGE” on the opening of NYSE on July 5,
  2017". The new company's statements are GE Oil & Gas's before the closing ("The current year results are not comparable to prior years
  as the results of Baker Hughes are included only from July 3, 2017", FY2018 10-K), with no per-share figures. So its own P/E exists
  only from 2017-07-05 (`pe_window_start`), as AVGO's from its IPO. Yahoo's BKR series runs through the combination; prices before
  2017-07-05 are another company's share and are not read.
- **2017 is not a year of EPS.** The only per-share figure is a loss of $(0.24) per Class A share for July 3 to December 31, 2017 (as
  recast; $(0.31) in the Q4 2017 release). It is excluded (a loss, and half a year), its days leave the window ("ex-FY17"), and until
  the Q4 2018 release the history has no year: the builder refuses those dates.
- **EPS is GAAP diluted income per Class A share; no adjusted full year is published.** Every release gives adjusted EPS for the quarter
  and the two comparison quarters (Table 1b), and no release, 10-K, proxy or presentation of 2018-2021 gives a full-year figure
  excluding identified items. Nothing is derived (the NKE 2008 rule; Baker Hughes' own 2010 precedent, where only the fourth quarter had
  an adjusted figure): the four quarters are not summed. So 2018 is $0.45.
- **The one-off test, on the basis of the per-share figure.** Method r2 excludes a year whose "listed one-off items [are] larger than
  the year's net income, so reported EPS is under half the year's EPS without them". This company's identified items are listed before
  tax and before the noncontrolling interest (General Electric held about 62.5% of the operating company, about 50.4% from November
  2018 and less after its later sales), while its EPS is after both. The test therefore takes the releases' own line "Adjustments
  attributable to BHGE" (Table 1b, after tax and after the noncontrolling interest), the four quarters summed, against net income
  attributable to the company
  (`one_off_test` on each Q4 print; the builder checks it against the year's EPS):
  - 2018: -$32M, $60M, $66M and -$12M, $82M in all, against $195M: kept at $0.45;
  - 2019: $44M, $113M, $57M and $131M, $345M in all, against $128M: **excluded** (GAAP $0.23), as the latest year (the NKE FY2018
    rule), from the Q4 2019 release (2020-01-22);
  - 2020: a loss of $(14.73) per Class A share with the $14,773M goodwill impairment, and no published full-year figure: **excluded**
    from the Q4 2020 release (2021-01-21).
  A judgement call, and the one everything rests on: read on the consolidated pre-tax figures (2018's $691M of operating adjustments
  less $228M of non-operating gains, against $283M of net income before the noncontrolling interest) 2018 would be excluded too, no
  year would have EPS and **no date of 2019-2021 could be built**.
- **So FY18's $0.45 is the EPS anchor on all 153 dates** (the rollover rule: the last full year in the history), and the bounds rule
  applies throughout: BEAR is the 0% cap (no EPS change between two years in the history), BULL takes BASE's rate and XBULL BULL's.
- **Share counts: Class A plus Class B outstanding at year end** (each 10-K's statement of financial position): 1,129M (2017), 1,035M
  (2018), 1,027M (2019), 1,035M (2020). Class B shares and their paired LLC units exchange one for one into Class A, so the weighted
  Class A count of the EPS note (427M, 429M, 557M, 675M) grows with General Electric's exchanges and sales, not with dilution. The net
  buyback is measured from the first count to the last (r2): none on the three dates before the FY2018 10-K (one count), +9.1%/yr from
  2019-02-22, +4.8% from 2020-02-14 and +2.9% from 2021-02-26. The releases give the Class A count only, so a Q4 print adds no share
  count. A judgement call (40 classes move with the Class A count, below).
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it.** Revenue from 2014 (GE Oil & Gas to mid-2017): the FY2017 10-K (2014,
  2015) and the recast 8-K (2016, 2017) on the first three dates, then the FY2018 10-K (2014-2018), the FY2019 10-K (2015-2019) and the
  FY2020 10-K's statement of income (2018-2020; it has no selected financial data). 2017 and 2018 carry the acquisition as published
  (+31.3%, +33.2%; the house rule), which sets the median growth the growth factor reads: 9.1% on the 2019 dates, 4.2% from the Q4 2019
  print and -4.4% from the Q4 2020 print.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (06:34-07:07 ET), on Tuesdays to Thursdays, so each print's week
  is dated the next trading day. The 10-Ks were accepted after the close and are dated 2019-02-20, 2020-02-14 and 2021-02-26.
- **No guide in numbers.** No release, 10-K or other 8-K of the period guides EPS, revenue or a margin (the releases carry the chief
  executive's words on markets; the outlook is given on the calls). The no-guide rules continue: BASE takes the latest quarter's
  revenue growth, as reported, plus the net buyback; no margin step.
- **One display-only outlook:** the 8-K of 2020-04-13 (accepted 08:09 ET), "The Company expects to record a non-cash goodwill
  impairment charge of approximately $15 billion in the first quarter of 2020", about $1.5 billion of restructuring and impairment
  charges in that quarter and 2020 net capital expenditures cut "by over 20%". Shown on 2020-04-17, the one date before the Q1 2020 print.
- **Signals.** Five, with ACN's weights, each against the year-ago quarter in the same release: orders (0.20; the first line of every
  release), revenue (0.20), the gross margin change (0.15; revenue less cost of revenue), the change in total segment operating income
  on revenue (0.15; the segment measure of the 10-K) and the operating margin change (0.15, GAAP), with the theme slot at 2/4. The
  regions Baker Hughes Incorporated's engine scored are no longer reported for the company (the releases give North America and
  international revenue for Oilfield Services only, in a sentence, against the prior quarter). Remaining performance obligations and the book-to-bill ratio are shown,
  not scored.
- **Thresholds by rule T over the years the filings report** (the bounds rule), from the filings public on 2019-02-01, each change from
  the latest one that reports both years; the builder re-derives them and refuses to build if the engine's differ:

  | Signal | Annual values | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | orders | 2016-2018: -26.73, 55.06, 9.55 % | -63 / -27 / 10 / 55 % |
  | revenue growth | 2015-2018: -13.04, -20.49, 31.32, 33.17 % | -50 / -20 / 9 / 33 % |
  | gross margin change | 2015-2018: 122.0, -322.6, -474.0, -24.9 bp | -770 / -470 / -170 / 120 bp |
  | segment operating margin change | 2016-2018: -311.8, -512.1, 188.9 bp | -710 / -510 / -310 / 190 bp |
  | operating margin change | 2015-2018: -1328.6, 579.3, -514.7, 471.7 bp | -2640 / -1330 / -20 / 580 bp |

  GAAP as published, so 2017 and 2018 carry the acquisition. Two 2018 values are on the Q4 2018 release's "combined business basis"
  (orders $23,904M against $21,821M; total segment operating income $1,796M on $22,877M against $1,302M on $21,841M): no filing public
  by 2019-02-01 gives 2018 and 2017 together on a GAAP basis for those lines. On three or four bad years the BULL thresholds of the
  margins are below zero (a gross margin 100bp lower still scores BULL): the rule's result, not a choice.
- **Durability: CYCLICAL, risk 2, unchanged.** None of the four 10-Ks uses the word; each says "Our revenue is predominately generated
  from the sale of products and services to major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies worldwide, and is dependent
  on spending by our customers for oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production". The "why" quotes each 10-K's own
  words: "a fullstream provider of oilfield products, services and digital solutions" (FY2017, FY2018), "an energy technology company"
  (FY2019, FY2020).
- **ENERGY_TRANSITION stays out of scope** (reserves and refining). The 10-Ks' climate wording stays in the "why": legislation "may
  curtail production and demand for hydrocarbons ... by shifting demand towards ... relatively lower carbon energy sources", and from
  the FY2020 10-K "Failure to effectively and timely execute our energy transition strategy could have an adverse effect on the demand
  for our technologies and services". The company now names the theme in its own risk factors; widening the scope remains the owner's
  call. Text only: the theme slot stays at 2/4.
- **Names and listings** (`company_names`, `listings`; each from its filing date): Baker Hughes Company and the NYSE symbol BKR from
  2019-10-18 (8-K accepted 2019-10-17 16:12 ET); Nasdaq from 2021-12-07 (8-K accepted 2021-10-27 16:18 ET). 37 models print BHGE and
  116 BKR. "Baker Hughes Company" joins the anachronism list from 2019-09-17, the first filing that uses it.
- **Dividends:** $0.18 a quarter throughout (every 10-K; each release's statement of income).
- **Adds nothing:** the Master Agreement with General Electric and its amendments (2018-11-13, 2019-02-05, 2019-02-28), General
  Electric's secondary offerings and the repurchases from it (2018-11-13 to 2018-11-19, 2019-09-10, 2019-09-16), the notes and credit
  agreements, the annual-meeting votes, the officer and compensation 8-Ks, and the Barclays presentations of September 2019, 2020 and
  2021.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **Totals: CHEAP 119, RICH 34, no FAIR.** 2019: CHEAP and BUY on all 48 dates, robustness 8 of 8. 2020: CHEAP 42, RICH 11 (2020-07-23,

- **A multiple measured against itself (the AVGO pattern).** On $0.45 the stock trades at 46-62x in 2019, 22-57x in 2020 and 44-60x in
  2021, and every P/E in the window uses the same $0.45, so the scenario prices and the class follow the price's own range since 2018
  and the growth inputs, not the level of EPS.
- **The window loses whole years.** It starts on 2018-01-02 (1.1 years on the first date). From 2020-01-23 the days of 2019 leave it and
  the median jumps from 58x to 71x; 2020's days enter until 2021-01-22, when they leave and the median jumps from 50x to 71x again:
  from then on the window is 2018 and 2021.
- **The EPP floor is 44-47x times $0.45, $19.80-21.15,** but from 2020-02-28 to the end of 2020, when the year's lows pull it to 33-40x
  ($14.85-18.00); the price is under it on 21 dates of 2020 and 2 of 2021.
- **BASE follows the quarter's revenue plus the buyback:** +8.0%/yr on the first three dates, +17.1% from the FY2018 10-K, then +13.1%,
  +17.1%, +12.9%, +10.4%, +6.1% (2020-02-14), +1.4% (Q1 2020), -16.2% (Q2 2020), -9.4%, -8.6%, -10.5%, -9.0%, +11.5% (Q2 2021) and
  +3.8% (Q3 2021).
- **RICH comes from a negative BASE on an unchanged anchor:** from the Q2 2020 print the scenario prices fall to $13-27 and the price
  recovers through them (2020-11-13 on); the class turns back to CHEAP on the Q2 2021 print, when revenue growth is positive again.

  the goodwill impairment, BEAR), 1.80 (Q2 2020), 1.95, 2.15, 2.75 (Q1 2021: the same impairment in the year-ago quarter, XBULL), 2.75
  and 2.90 (Q3 2021).
- **Robustness** is under 8 of 8 on 19 dates of 2020 and 21 of 2021.

The classes rest on the EPS history (which years are in it) and on the share count behind the buyback term; the signals and their
thresholds move far fewer.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- treating the company as a new listing from 2017-07-05 and leaving 2018 unbuilt for want of a full-year EPS (the owner asked for
  2018-2021);
- the one-off test on the attributable figures, which keeps 2018 and excludes 2019 (no date exists the other way; 61 classes move if
  2019 is kept);
- GAAP EPS rather than the sum of the quarters' adjusted figures (34 to 42 classes);
- Class A plus Class B shares for the buyback term (40 classes with the Class A count);
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows 2020: orders and the segment margin beside revenue, the gross margin and the operating
  margin (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically, from three or four annual values; no class moves with the other reading of
  2018);
- the acquisition left in the 2017 and 2018 changes of rule T and of the revenue history (the house rule);
- CYCLICAL although no 10-K of the new company uses the word; ENERGY_TRANSITION out of scope although the FY2020 10-K names the
  energy transition as a risk (text only either way);
- the non-earnings 8-Ks read by their item text, not their exhibits.
