  score BASE for want of a figure.

Sensitivity (each call changed alone, the 253 dates reclassified offline; no outcome consulted):
- **GAAP EPS in 2023-2025** ($1.91, $2.98, $2.60; 2022 stays a loss and excluded): 50 classes (21 CHEAP to FAIR, 7 CHEAP to RICH, 22
  FAIR to RICH; 2024-11-08 to 2026-10-23) and 27 tiers;
- **2022 not taken from the Q4 2023 release:** 41 classes (19 CHEAP to FAIR, 22 FAIR to RICH; from 2024-11-08) and 3 tiers;
- **the quarters' adjusted EPS summed for 2018-2022** (2020 excluded), then as published: 53 classes, both ways (from 2022-01-14),
  and 43 tiers;
- **the Class A share count alone:** 76 classes, toward RICH (2022-06-24 to 2026-05-01), and 74 tiers; **no buyback term:** 21 classes
  and 11 tiers;
- **the FY2026 revenue guide not used:** no class, no tier;
- **every signal at its BEAR value** (the unreported margins too): 104 classes, toward RICH or FAIR; **at its XBULL value:** 24 classes,
  toward CHEAP or FAIR; no tier.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the company's adjusted EPS from the Q4 2023 release, and 2022's taken from it (50 and 41 classes move the other ways);
- FY18's $0.45 as the anchor to January 2024, by the excluded-year rules of 2018-2021;
- the two unreported margins scored BASE rather than derived from segment EBITDA or dropped with their weights (the BEAR and XBULL
  variants bound it);
- Class A plus Class B shares for the buyback term (76 classes with the Class A count);
- the fiscal-year revenue guide read from a conference presentation, with Chart in it (no class moves);
- CYCLICAL and the themes, as before (text only);
- the non-earnings 8-Ks read by their item text.

## PFE (Pfizer): the fifteenth ticker, in staging

The PFE series is built apart from ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, AVGO, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT, RCL, MAR and BKR and shares nothing with
them but the machinery: its own fact sheet (`retro/facts/PFE.json`), builder (`retro/build_pfe.py`, the SHW builder with a dollar
revenue guide and raw rule-T figures) and engine (`retro/templates/pfe_engine.py.tmpl`, the SHW engine with pharmaceutical signals).
The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters a PFE model, and neither does the profile of
PFE in `data/business_profiles.json` (a 2026 judgement, not read for this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/PFE/`, beside
the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`.

```bash
python3 retro/build_pfe.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                   # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_pfe.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                   # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/PFE/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series PFE
for c in 2008-01-23 2008-01-24 2008-02-29 2008-04-17 2008-07-01 2008-07-23 2008-10-21 2009-01-01 2009-01-26 2009-01-27 \
         2009-02-27 2009-04-28 2009-07-22 2009-10-20 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c PFE; done
```

Read for the history and the decade's signal values: the statements of income, financial summaries and geographic data of the
FY1998-FY2008 10-Ks (the annual reports filed as Exhibit 13; the FY1998 and FY1999 10-Ks are plain-text filings). Read for the
prints: the earnings releases of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 and every other 8-K of July 2007 to January 2010 (the non-earnings ones by their
exhibits, for a guided number or a dividend), the 2009 Form 425 merger communications, and the 10-Qs and 10-Ks for the dividend
statements. The S-4 of 2009-03-27 (the Wyeth merger prospectus) was not read for guides: projections in a merger document are not
guides (the UNP and AVGO rule). All by Opus directly, with no delegated transcription. The fact sheet is generated by a script from
the transcribed raw figures, so every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is computed, not typed; 230 strings were checked with
`verbatim.py` against their own filings (every statement row behind a print, every geographic, income-statement and summary row behind
rule T and the vintages, every guide and quoted sentence), and a second script found each of 384 raw figures in the rows cited from its
own source. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (converted from UTC; before 2003 EDGAR gives the filing date only).
Decided on 2026-11-10, before any PFE model was built or any PFE outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's PFE series carries a factor of 1.054 dated 2020-11-17 (Yahoo records that day's distribution as a
  split); every date here precedes it, so the builder multiplies Yahoo's close by it (`split_factor`, as for the splits of other
  tickers) and gets the price as traded: $22.73 on 2007-12-31 and $17.71 on 2008-12-31, the year-end market values per share in the
  FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks. No Pfizer split after the 3-for-1 of 1999 restates a per-share fact in the fact sheet (`splits` is empty).
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year (subsidiaries outside the U.S. close on November 30). The three dates of January 2008 before
  the Q4 2007 print have FY2007 as the current year.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 was accepted before the open or during the session on its release day
  (07:38-11:45 ET), none on a week's last trading day, so each print's week is dated the next trading day: 2008-01-24, 2008-04-18,
  2008-07-24, 2008-10-22, 2009-01-27, 2009-04-29, 2009-07-23, 2009-10-21. The FY2006 10-K was accepted after the close
  (2007-02-28 18:17 ET, dated 2007-03-01); the FY2007 (2008-02-29 15:05 ET) and FY2008 (2009-02-27 12:59 ET) 10-Ks during the session.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it.** EPS is diluted EPS from continuing operations before the cumulative
  effect of accounting changes, from the financial summaries: 2004 $1.43, 2005 $1.02, 2006 $1.52 (FY2006 10-K, with Consumer
  Healthcare discontinued), 2007 $1.21 from the Q4 2007 print (2008-01-23), then $1.18 from the FY2007 10-K (its net income is $154
  million lower than the release's), 2008 $1.19 from the Q4 2008 print and the FY2008 10-K. Revenues and diluted shares from the same
  rows (FY2007 $48.613B in the release, $48.418B in the 10-K).
- **The company's adjusted EPS stays out.** Pfizer's "adjusted income" excludes "purchase-accounting adjustments, acquisition-related
  costs, discontinued operations and certain significant items"; the purchase-accounting adjustments are mostly the amortization of
  acquired intangibles (about $3 billion a year), which recurs, so the figure does not exclude only one-offs (the NKE FY2007 and AVGO
  2009 rule). GAAP stands, and no figure is derived from the reconciliations. The adjusted EPS guides are shown in the guide line only.
- **2003 excluded; the history and the P/E window start with 2004** (`pe_window_start` 2004-01-01). 2003 earned $0.16 a diluted share
  from continuing operations (the FY2006 10-K's basis; $0.22 in the FY2003 10-K): the $5,052 million in-process R&D charge for the
  Pharmacia acquisition alone exceeds the year's $3,910 million net income, and no figure excluding only one-offs was published. A
  distorted year that is not the latest takes the history and the window with it (the r2 wording, "the P/E window starts after it",
  and the AAPL FY2002 precedent, which dropped FY1998-FY2000 with FY2001-FY2002), so the history is 2004-2006 on the first dates
  (three years, the bounds of method r2 not needed) and the window 4.0 years in January 2008, 5.8 years by December 2009.
  2004-2008 are kept: their after-tax acquisition-related costs, certain significant items and in-process R&D ($2,444M, $4,544M,
  $1,662M, $4,672M and $6,495M) are each under the year's net income ($11,361M, $8,085M, $19,337M, $8,144M and $8,104M), so reported
  EPS is more than half the EPS without them. 2008 is the near case: pre-tax, its certain significant items and in-process R&D
  ($8,723M) exceed net income; the r2 test is per share, after tax ("reported EPS is under half the year's EPS without them"), and
  2008's $1.19 is 55% of the $2.15 without them.
- **Guides: reported diluted EPS and revenues, both in numbers, for the fiscal year only.** Every release guides the year; none guides a
  quarter. Method r2 maps them as for SHW and LOW:
  - current-FY EPS: the midpoint of the latest reported diluted EPS range for the current year: FY07 $1.055 ($1.01-1.10, Q3 2007
    release, after the Exubera charges) to 2008-01-18; FY08 $1.855 ($1.78-1.93, Q4 2007 release), $1.805 ($1.73-1.88, Q1 and Q2 2008),
    $1.66 ($1.61-1.71, Q3 2008); FY09 $1.415 ($1.34-1.49, Q4 2008), $1.275 ($1.20-1.35, Q1 2009, Wyeth transaction and financing costs),
    $1.375 ($1.30-1.45, Q2 2009) and $1.475 ($1.45-1.50, Q3 2009);
  - BASE growth and the growth factor: no next-quarter guide, so the fiscal-year revenue guide, a dollar range read as growth on the
    last full year's revenues in the history (the LOW dollar-level rule): FY07 $47.5-48.0B (-1.8% to -0.8% on FY06's $48.37B); FY08
    $47.0-49.0B (-3.3% to +0.8% on the release's FY07 $48.61B, -2.9% to +1.2% on the 10-K's $48.42B), $48.0-49.0B from Q3 2008; FY09
    $44.0-46.0B (-8.9% to -4.8% on FY08's $48.30B; "Adjusted Revenues" in the Q4 2008 release, the same range as "Reported Revenues" in
    the Q1 2009 release), $45.0-46.0B from Q2 2009, and $49.0-50.0B from Q3 2009, which "incorporates Wyeth's operations from the
    acquisition closing date": the business bought stays in (the SHW Valspar rule). The guides are "at current exchange rates", in
    dollars; no filing guides in local currency, so they are used as published (the SHW and MSFT reading);
  - no margin step: the cost-of-sales, expense and tax-rate guides are on the adjusted basis and none is a pre-tax margin, so they
    feed no input (the AAPL gross-margin rule) and the margin signal takes the latest quarter's pre-tax margin change.
  - Reaffirmations add nothing (the ACN rule): the 8-K of 2008-03-05 repeats the FY2008 guide of 2008-01-23, and the Wyeth analyst
    presentation of 2009-01-26 the FY2009 guide of the same morning's release.
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the rate: $0.29 a quarter (FY2006 10-K), $0.32 from the Q4 2007 release
  ("a 10% increase in our first-quarter 2008 dividend to $0.32 a share"), $0.16 from 2009-01-27: the Wyeth announcement 8-K (accepted
  2009-01-26 17:22 ET, after the close) says the Board "will reduce Pfizer's quarterly dividend per share to $0.16" from the second
  quarter; the FY2008 10-K repeats it.
- **Signals.** Six, with ACN's weights: U.S. revenue growth (0.20) and international revenue growth (0.20), from each release's
  revenue table ("TOTAL REVENUES" by worldwide, U.S. and international), total revenue growth (0.15), the gross-margin change (0.15;
  revenues less cost of sales, which excludes the amortization of intangibles), the pre-tax margin change (0.15; income from continuing
  operations before taxes on revenues) and the theme slot at 2/4. Each value is the release's own, against the year-ago quarter as the
  same release shows it (the Q4 2008 release shows Q4 2007's pre-tax income recast to $2,970M from $3,165M). Charges stay in, as
  published: the $2.8 billion Exubera charges in Q3 2007 (mostly in cost of sales), and therefore in Q3 2008's year-ago quarter.
- **Thresholds by rule T** over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04: ten changes, each from
  the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years (the geographic data for U.S. revenues, international being consolidated
  less United States; the statements of income for the gross margin; the financial summaries for total revenues and pre-tax income).
  Seams stay in, as published: the 1997 and 1998 changes come from the FY1998 and FY1999 10-Ks, before the Warner-Lambert pooling, the
  later ones from pooled filings; revenue reclassifications and the Consumer Healthcare discontinuance enter with the filings that made
  them; 2003 carries the Pharmacia purchase (inventory step-up in cost of sales, in-process R&D in pre-tax income). The raw figures and
  values are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives every value and threshold and refuses to build if they differ.

  | Signal | Fiscal 1997-2006 | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | U.S. revenue | 17.25, 34.75, 21.81, 7.83, 13.4, 11.51, 29.99, 10.24, -10.92, 4.33 % | -34 / -11 / 12 / 35 % |
  | international revenue | 6.32, 7.51, 12.19, 8.41, 8.09, 11.59, 53.59, 28.07, 6.84, -0.46 % | -9 / 0 / 8 / 54 % |
  | total revenue growth | 11.9, 21.3, 17.04, -3.65, 11.51, 11.9, 40.42, 17.23, -3.23, 2.04 % | -19 / -4 / 12 / 40 % |
  | gross-margin change | 111.9, 60.4, 116.4, 346.9, 124.5, 67.7, -900.5, 707.5, -221.0, -53.9 bp | -1890 / -900 / 90 / 710 bp |
  | pre-tax margin change | -47.3, -186.6, 667.6, -470.3, 1334.2, 198.3, -3121.4, 2070.5, -457.7, 415.1 bp | -6320 / -3120 / 80 / 2070 bp |

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2,** the default of every ticker whose 10-K does not call its business cyclical. The "why" quotes the
  FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks, whose wording does not change: "is a research-based, global pharmaceutical company", generic competition "is a
  major challenge for us around the world" and on losing patent protection "we can lose the major portion of sales of that product in a
  very short period", Lipitor's U.S. basic product patent expiring "in March 2010" and the enantiomer patent "in June 2011". The kind
  changes the class label only. No disruption theme in `taxonomy_eras.json` is live for a pharmaceutical company in 2008-2009 (GLP1,
  from 2023-08-08, is scoped to snacks, beverages and devices), so the watch list is empty and the builder refuses events until a theme
  encoding is decided. Patent expiry is the business model's own cycle, not a substitution theme, and stays in the "why".
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the last 10-K's segments (Pharmaceutical, Animal Health, Corporate/Other), the total
  from the revenue guide midpoint; the EPS check runs on the last year's pre-tax margin and tax rate.
- **Adds nothing:** the non-earnings 8-Ks (officers and directors, by-laws, the mini-tender recommendation, the pipeline updates of
  2008-03-05 and 2008-09-30, debt offerings and credit agreements), the Lipitor patent settlement with Ranbaxy of 2008-06-18 (a U.S.
  license date, no guided number), the Wyeth merger agreement of 2009-01-26 and its financing (a pending deal with no guided number, the
  XOM XTO rule), the Wyeth financial statements and pro forma statements of 2009-03-13 and 2009-10-14, the closing of 2009-10-15 (its
  guide enters with the Q3 2009 release), and the 10-Qs beyond their dividend statements.
- **Anachronism list:** Pfizer names first seen in its filings after the start of 2008 (Eliquis, Zoetis, Xeljanz, Ibrance, Pfizer
  Innovative Health, Pfizer Essential Health, Viatris, Comirnaty, Paxlovid) join `taxonomy_eras.json`, each dated from the first filing
  under Pfizer's CIK that uses it (EDGAR full-text search; after-close filings from the next trading day). No model of any ticker
  contains them, so no output changes. PFE's source ids are `PF1`-`PF22`.

Controls: altering one value of each print (its U.S./international split, and each Q4 print's full-year EPS), vintage (its last
year's EPS), guide (its reported EPS range and its revenue range) and dividend changes no date before its publication and changes the
first weekly date on or after it (35 of 41; the other 6 are the Q2 2007 release's FY2007 and FY2008 guides and the Q3 2007 release's
FY2008 guide, superseded before any built date). A scan of the 105 models for the source ids, titles, notes, texts and figures of every
later print, guide, vintage, dividend and source finds none before its publication (0 of 5,177 pairs, after dropping 17 strings an
earlier fact already carries). Rebuilding the 2008 dates of ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT, RCL, MAR and BKR and
the 2009 dates of AVGO changes nothing (711 models). The firewall (every kind of fact planted after the cutoff with absurd values,
including a later split on the price data's split date and absurd full-year actuals, and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10)
changes no model and leaves no planted text at any of the 15 cutoffs above (3 to 105 dates each). Every model draws one warning from
`retro_tool run`: the calendar years 2010 and 2011 (Lipitor's patent dates, in the 10-K's own words) and "2070" (the pre-tax margin
signal's XBULL threshold of 2,070bp).

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **CHEAP on 102 of 105 dates** (BUY on 101, ACCUMULATE on 2009-10-16 at Ratio B 0.80), **RICH and AVOID on the three dates of January
  2008** before the Q4 2007 print; robustness 8 of 8 on every date.
- **January 2008 rests on FY2007's depressed guide.** FY07E is the Q3 2007 release's $1.055, after the Exubera charges, so $22.50-24.02
  is 21.3-22.8x (the 34th-46th percentile of a 4.0-year window, median 23.3x); the floor (the median of the calendar-year lows 2004 17.0x,
  2005 20.2x, 2006 14.7x, 2007 21.1x, 2008 21.6x) is 20x, $21.10, 7-14% under the price; BULL and XBULL are the 2004-2006 CAGR (+3.1%/yr),
  so the BULL price ($28) leaves Ratio B at 2.45-3.77.
- **From the Q4 2007 print the guide carries the call.** FY07's $1.21 joins the history and FY08E is $1.855: the stock trades at
  8.4-12.7x the current-year guide through 2008 (the 0th-6th percentile) and 8.7-12.9x in 2009 (the 0th-16th), against a window whose
  median falls from 21.2-21.6x in early 2008 to 19.4x. The floor is 17x in 2008 ($31.50, $30.70 from 2008-04-18, $28.20 from 2008-10-22) and 15x in 2009
  ($24.90, then $21.20, $19.10, $20.60 and $22.10 as the FY2009 guide moves); the price is 14-51% under it.
- **BEAR is 2005** throughout (-28.7%/yr: $1.43 to $1.02) at the 10th-percentile P/E: $14-15 to early June 2008, $10-12 after and
  $8-11 in 2009, as 2008-2009's single-digit multiples enter the window.
- **BULL equals BASE from the Q4 2007 print**, as the history's EPS CAGRs are negative ($1.43 in 2004 to $1.21, $1.18 and $1.19);
  XBULL is the 2005-2007 run (+8.9%/yr, +7.6% on the 10-K's $1.18).
- **BASE follows the revenue guide plus a 2.3-3.1%/yr buyback** (diluted shares 7,614M in 2004, 6,939M in 2007, 6,750M in 2008): +1.0%/yr
  (FY07 guide), +1.9% (2008-01-24), +2.3% (the FY2007 10-K's base), +3.3% (Q3 2008), -3.8% (FY09 guide, 2009-01-27), -2.7% (Q2 2009)
  and +5.6% (Q3 2009, Wyeth in). The growth factor runs from -0.50 (2009) to +0.26 (Q3 2009).
- **The proxy composite** is 1.85 on Q3 2007 (U.S. revenue -14.3% and the gross margin -2,254bp, the Exubera charges, at BEAR), 2.35 on
  Q4 2007, 1.85 on Q1 2008 (U.S. -19.5%), 2.35 on Q2 2008, 2.45 on Q3 2008 (the gross margin +2,079bp, against the Exubera quarter), 1.80
  on Q4 2008 (international -0.8% and revenue -4.1% at BEAR), 1.95 on Q1 and Q2 2009 and 2.10 on Q3 2009.

How far each call moves the classes (the 105 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- the company's adjusted EPS throughout (2004-2008, the adjusted guides; 2004 and 2005 derived from adjusted income for this test
  only, as no filing in hand publishes them per share): no class, 4 tiers;
- only 2003 leaving, with the ten-year history and window (1997/1998-2007 ex-FY03, the reading used for a latest excluded year): 3
  classes (the January 2008 dates, RICH to CHEAP), 4 tiers;
- 2008 excluded (the pre-tax reading of the distorted-year test): no class, 1 tier;
- the dollar revenue guides not used (BASE on the latest quarter's revenue growth): no class, no tier;
- the dividend kept at $0.32 until the first $0.16 declaration (the Q1 2009 10-Q, 2009-05-08): no class, no tier;
- every signal at its BEAR value: 1 class (2009-10-16, CHEAP to RICH); at its XBULL value: none; no tier either way.
The CHEAP calls from the Q4 2007 print rest on the reported-EPS guide against the stock's own 2004-2008 P/E history, which no call but
the window's reach touches; the three RICH dates of January 2008 depend on the window starting in 2004.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows that U.S. exclusivity losses dominated Pfizer's revenues from 2006: the U.S. and
  international split the releases report, total revenue and the two margins (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically);
- GAAP EPS rather than the company's adjusted figure, on the recurring-amortization rule (no class moves);
- 2003 taking the history and the window with it (3 classes in January 2008 depend on it), and 2008 kept on the per-share reading;
- the dollar revenue guides read against the last full year in the history, the Wyeth months included from Q3 2009;
- DURABLE rather than STRUCTURAL or another kind (the class label only), on the 10-K's own description of patent expiry as the
  business's competition;
- the series key PFE and Yahoo's 2020 factor in the price basis (checked against the 10-Ks' year-end market values).

### PFE 2010-2013

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The fact sheet only gains facts: its
2008-2009 content is unchanged and the 105 earlier models rebuild byte for byte after the builder changes below.

```bash
python3 retro/build_pfe.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for c in 2010-01-01 2010-02-03 2010-02-26 2010-05-04 2010-08-03 2010-11-02 2011-02-01 2011-02-28 2011-04-04 2011-05-03 2011-08-02 \
         2011-11-01 2012-01-31 2012-02-29 2012-05-01 2012-07-31 2012-08-14 2012-11-01 2013-01-29 2013-03-01 2013-04-30 2013-06-24 \
         2013-07-30 2013-10-29 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c PFE; done
```

Read: the 16 earnings releases from Q4 2009 to Q3 2013, the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks (the financial reports filed as Exhibit 13, with
Items 1 and 1A), the FY2012 10-K/A, the 12 10-Qs for the dividend statements, every other 8-K of February 2010 to January 2014 (21
filings, by their exhibits) and the 47 Form 425 communications of the 2013 Zoetis exchange offer, all read directly, none
delegated. The source ids are PF23-PF45 (PF45, the Form 425 of 2013-06-24, was added last). 273 strings were checked with
`verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (503 with the 2008-2009 batch's 230, all found), and a script found each of the 741 raw
figures of both batches in the rows cited from its own source. Decided on 2026-11-10, before any 2010-2013 outcome was computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (07:18-09:11 ET) except Q3 2011's (09:35 ET, in the session);
  none on a week's last trading day, so each print's week is dated the next trading day (2010-02-04 .. 2013-10-30). The 10-Ks: FY2009
  2010-02-26 13:43 ET and FY2010 2011-02-28 10:00 ET (dated those days), FY2011 2012-02-28 17:07 ET and FY2012 2013-02-28 16:57 ET
  (after the close, dated 2012-02-29 and 2013-03-01). Three other filings carry a guide: the 8-Ks on the Capsugel sale (2011-04-04,
  13:55 ET) and the over-the-counter Nexium agreement (2012-08-14, 13:38 ET), and the Form 425 announcing the preliminary results of the
  Zoetis exchange offer (2013-06-24, 11:49 ET), each from its own week's date.
- **History: four more vintages,** 2004 to the 10-K's year, each year from the latest 10-K that reports it, on the same basis (diluted
  EPS from continuing operations): FY2009 10-K 2009 $1.23; FY2010 10-K 2010 $1.02; FY2011 10-K, with Capsugel discontinued, 2007 $1.17,
  2008 $1.17, 2009 $1.21, 2010 $1.01, 2011 $1.11; FY2012 10-K, with Nutrition discontinued too, 2009 $1.22, 2010 $1.03, 2011 $1.06,
  2012 $1.26 (revenues 2008-2012 $47.529B, $49.078B, $65.165B, $65.259B, $58.986B). 2004-2006 stay from the FY2006 10-K, the latest
  filing that reports them. 2003 stays excluded and the window starts on 2004-01-01: 6.0 years in January 2010, 10 years by the end of
  2013.
- **Restated years (`restates`).** The Q4 2011 release restates FY2010 without Capsugel ($1.01 and $67.057B against the 10-K's $1.02
  and $67.809B) and the Q4 2012 release FY2011 without Nutrition ($1.06 and $65.259B against $1.11 and $67.425B). Each print replaces
  that year from its date until a 10-K vintage published after it carries the year (four dates each; the XOM, SHW and BKR encoding).
  A builder change that moves no earlier output.
- **The distorted-year test keeps every year.** After tax, per share, the acquisition-related costs and certain significant items are
  $0.41 against 2009's reported $1.23, $0.45 against 2010's $1.02, $0.58 against 2011's $1.11 and $0.45 against 2012's $1.26: reported
  EPS is far above half the EPS without them. GAAP stands; the adjusted figures (2009 $2.02, 2010 $2.23, 2011 $2.31, 2012 $2.19) still
  remove the recurring amortization of acquired intangibles and are shown in the guide line only.
- **Guides: reported diluted EPS and revenues, as published, for the fiscal year only** (no quarter, margin or growth rate is guided
  in numbers), each field from the latest guide that states it:
  - FY2010: $67.0-69.0B and $0.95-1.10 (Q4 2009 release, "with Wyeth for the full year"; repeated in Q1 and Q2 2010), $67.0-68.0B and
    $0.84-0.94 (Q3 2010);

    the other 7).
  - 2016: FY16E $1.605 then $1.785 with the raised Q1 2016 guide (BASE +4.0% then +8.1%/yr): 18.3-20.7x, the 46th-71st percentile,
    14-30% above a 16x floor, Ratio B 1.6-5.2, FAIR on three dates in May. From 2016-08-03 FY15's $1.11 stands: 27.6-31.8x, 66-99% above
    the floor, Ratio B infinite.
  - From the Q4 2016 print (2017-02-01): FY16's $1.17: 27.1-31.8x, the 80th-99th percentile of a window whose median is 19.7-19.8x, 59-87% above a 17x floor
    ($19.89); BASE +1.2% to +2.0%/yr; Ratio B infinite on every date.
- **BEAR** is 2005 (-28.7%/yr) while 2004 is in the history (to 2015-02-27), then 2007 (-23.0%/yr: $1.52 to $1.17) from the FY2014
  10-K, and 2015 (-21.3%/yr: $1.41 to $1.11) from the FY2016 10-K. **XBULL** is the 2011-2013 run (+29.1%/yr, $0.99 to $1.65) from
  the FY2013 10-K.
- **The proxy composite** is 1.45-2.35 throughout: U.S. revenues turn up with Hospira and Medivation (+14.9% to +49.4% in Q3 2015-Q3
  2016), international growth is below its BASE threshold (0%) on 14 of the 16 prints (-13.3% to +1.8%), and the gross margin falls 369-575bp in Q4
  2015-Q3 2016 with Hospira's mix.
- **Robustness:** all eight variants agree on 186 of 209 dates (4 CHEAP, 182 RICH); 20 dates split FAIR/RICH and 3 span all three
  classes (May 2016).

Sensitivity (each call changed alone, the 209 dates reclassified offline with `retro_tool`'s own classifier; no outcome consulted):
- **The adjusted EPS guide as current-FY EPS where no reported guide is in force** (FY14E from 2014-05-06, FY16E from 2016-08-03, FY17E),
  against the GAAP history: **86 classes**, all RICH to CHEAP (12 in 2014, 22 in 2016, 52 in 2017), 86 tiers. The RICH calls of
  August 2016 to December 2017 rest on reading the GAAP-EPS policy as leaving no EPS guide;
- **the dollar revenue guides not used** (BASE on the latest quarter's growth): 21 classes (16 RICH to FAIR, 3 FAIR to CHEAP, 2 RICH to
  CHEAP; February to July 2016, where the quarters carry Hospira), 22 tiers;
- **the Q2 2016 policy not read as a withdrawal** (Q1 2016's $1.72-1.85 standing to the year's end): 17 classes, RICH to FAIR
  (2016-10-07 to 2017-01-27), 17 tiers;
- the history from 2004 in every vintage (no ten-year cut): 3 classes (FAIR to RICH, May 2016), 3 tiers;
- the FY2016 ranges read on the FY2015 10-K's pro forma revenues with Hospira for the year ($52.082B): 3 classes (FAIR to RICH, May
  2016), 3 tiers;
- the Q1 2014 statement not read as a withdrawal: none; the 2016-02-16 reissue ignored: none;
- every signal at its BEAR value: 3 classes (FAIR to RICH, May 2016); at XBULL: 3 (RICH to FAIR, 2016-05-27 to 2016-06-24); no tier
  either way.
The company's adjusted EPS throughout (history and guides) was not re-run for this batch: its 2004-2008 figures were derived offline for
the 2008-2013 tests and are not in the fact sheet. The 86-class line above bounds the direction: on Pfizer's own adjusted figures the
2014-2017 multiple is far lower than on GAAP EPS.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- reading "no longer valid" (Q1 2014) and "does not provide guidance for GAAP Reported financial measures (other than Revenues)" (from
  Q2 2016) as withdrawals, so the last full year's GAAP EPS stands (86 classes against the adjusted guide, 17 against keeping Q1 2016's
  range);
- GAAP EPS rather than the company's adjusted figure, on the recurring-amortization rule of 2008-2009 (the same 86 dates);
- the ten-year history per vintage (3 classes);
- the dollar revenue ranges read on the last full year, acquisitions in and the Hospira Infusion Systems sale out (21 classes without
  the ranges, 3 with the pro forma 2015 base);
- the unfiled 2015-09-30 update left out, and the 2016-02-16 reissue applied from its own date (no class moves);
- the signals and DURABLE, as in 2008-2013.

### PFE 2018-2021

```bash
         2020-01-28 2020-02-27 2020-04-28 2020-07-28 2020-10-27 2020-11-17 2021-01-12 2021-02-02 2021-02-25 2021-05-04 2021-07-28 \
         2021-11-02 2022-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c PFE; done
```

Read: the 16 earnings releases from Q4 2017 to Q3 2021, the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks (the financial reports filed as Exhibit 13 to FY2019;
the FY2020 10-K as one document, with Items 1 and 1A), every other 8-K of December 2017 to January 2022 (48 filings, by their
exhibits), the 25 Form 425 and 3 SC TO-C filings (the 2019 Array tender offer and the Upjohn-Mylan combination) and the 9 DEFA14A
filings, and the 10-Qs for the dividend statements. Downloaded from EDGAR and read directly, none delegated; every raw figure was parsed
by a script from the row it is cited from, and 286 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing, all found. The
source ids are PF67-PF88. Decided on 2026-11-10, before any 2018-2021 outcome was computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (08:04-08:58 ET), none on a week's last trading day, so each
  print's week is dated the next trading day (2018-01-31 .. 2021-11-03). The FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks were accepted during the session
  (15:42, 14:35, 14:15 and 13:59 ET) and keep their dates (2018-02-22, 2019-02-28, 2020-02-27, 2021-02-25).
- **No reported EPS guide in any release.** Each release repeats that Pfizer "does not provide guidance for GAAP Reported financial
  measures (other than revenues)" (`eps_none` on every guide), so the last full year in the history stands as current-year EPS all
  through 2018-2021 (the rollover rule, as for FY2017): FY16's $1.17 in January 2018, FY17's $3.52 from the Q4 2017 print, FY18's $1.86
  from the Q4 2018 print, FY19's $2.87 from the Q4 2019 print and FY20's $1.24 from the Q4 2020 print. The adjusted EPS ranges stay in
  the guide line only (they remove $0.45-0.65 a share a year of purchase-accounting amortization, the 2008-2009 rule).
- **The distorted-year test on the PFE measure keeps every year as first published.** Per share, after tax, acquisition-related costs
  plus certain significant items, as each Q4 release states them (the measure of every test from 2004): 2017 a net benefit of $1.42
  ($0.05 and $(1.47), the $10.7 billion Tax Act benefit inside), so $2.10 without them and reported $3.52 is 1.68 times it; 2018 charges
  of $0.49, $1.86 against $2.35 (0.79); 2019 a net benefit of $0.53 (the $8.1 billion Consumer Healthcare joint-venture gain inside),
  $2.87 against $2.34 (1.23); 2020 charges of $0.53, $1.24 against $1.77 (0.70); the restated 2019 without Upjohn $1.91 against $1.31
  (1.46). r2 excludes a year whose reported EPS is under half, or more than double, the EPS without them; none is. **2017 is the near
  case:** the Tax Act benefit alone ("approximately $10.7 billion", FY2017 10-K) is just larger than the year's $10.65 billion income from
  continuing operations without it (2.004 times), so the benefit-only reading of the AVGO mirror test would exclude 2017; the net measure,
  which also nets the year's one-off charges, is the one every PFE test has used, and it keeps 2017 (see the sensitivity below).
- **History: four more vintages,** each year from the latest 10-K that reports it:
  - FY2017 (2008-2017), FY2018 (2009-2018), FY2019 (2010-2019), ten years each, diluted EPS from continuing operations: 2017 $3.52, 2018
    $1.86, 2019 $2.87;
  - **FY2020: the FY2020 10-K restates 2016-2019 without Upjohn** (a discontinued operation from its spin-off): 2016 $(0.02), 2017
    $2.23, 2018 $0.64, 2019 $1.91, 2020 $1.24. A loss has no P/E, so 2016 is excluded, and an excluded year that is not the latest takes
    the history and the P/E window with it (the r2 wording, "the P/E window starts after it"; the PFE 2003 rule): the FY2020 vintage
    holds 2017-2020 and the window starts on 2017-01-01 (4.1 years on 2021-02-26, 5.0 at the end of 2021). The restated 2017-2019 keep
    their earlier tests (the 2014-2017 rule for restated years); no filing restates their one-offs per share;
  - the FY2017-FY2019 10-Ks give no share counts in the financial summary, so diluted shares come from each statement of income (three
    years) and earlier years keep the latest filing that reports them.
- **The Q4 2020 print restates 2019 without Upjohn** ($1.91 and $41.172B against the FY2019 10-K's $2.87 and $51.750B) from 2021-02-02
  to the FY2020 10-K (the `restates` encoding).
- **The Upjohn spin-off is a distribution, not a split.** Pfizer holders received "approximately 0.124079 shares of Viatris common stock
  for every one share of Pfizer common stock" (8-K of 2020-11-16, after the close, dated 2020-11-17). Yahoo books it as a 1054:1000 split
  on 2020-11-17; the builder undoes that factor for the days before (`distributions`, the MAR 2011 rule), so every price stays as traded
  and the drop stays in the series. A builder change that moves no earlier output (every earlier date already multiplied by the factor).
  The pre-spin P/Es of the FY2020 vintage's window therefore carry Viatris's value against EPS without Upjohn (the MAR judgement call).
- **Guides: revenues as published, for the fiscal year only,** each from the latest guide that states it:
  - FY2018: $53.5-55.5B (Q4 2017, with a full year of Consumer Healthcare; reaffirmed in Q1), $53.0-55.0B (Q2), $53.0-53.7B (Q3);
  - FY2019: $52.0-54.0B (Q4 2018, Q1 2019), $50.5-52.5B (Q2 2019: Consumer Healthcare only to July 31, then Pfizer's share of the
    joint venture's earnings; Array and Therachon in), $51.2-52.2B (Q3 2019);
  - FY2020: the Total Company ranges, with Upjohn for the full year: $48.5-50.5B (Q4 2019, Q1 2020), $48.6-50.6B (Q2), $48.8-49.5B (Q3).
    The "New Pfizer" ranges (as if the Upjohn combination had closed at the start of 2020: $40.7-42.3B, then $40.8-42.4B) go in the note,
    as the reporting entity's guide is the Total Company one. The 8-K of 2020-11-16 says the guidance was "not updated" and now "overstates
    expected total company results": words only, so the last ranges stand and the words go in the note (the ACN rule);
  - FY2021: $59.4-61.4B (Q4 2020, about $15 billion of BNT162b2), $70.5-72.5B (Q1 2021, about $26 billion), $78.0-80.0B (Q2, about $33.5

    superseded by the Q4 2020 release before FY2021 is current (inert);
  - the ranges are read as growth on the last full year in the history: the Consumer Healthcare joint venture and the Upjohn spin-off out
    against a base that includes them until the base is restated (the LOW 2011 rule), Array in (the SHW Valspar rule).
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the rate: $0.34 (Q4 2017 release, "declared a 34-cent first-quarter 2018
  dividend"), $0.36 (Q4 2018 release), $0.38 (FY2019 10-K) and $0.39 (FY2020 10-K; the Q4 2019 and Q4 2020 releases do not state them).
- **Signals,** from each release's revenue table and statement of income as before. From Q4 2020 the table's row reads "TOTAL
  REVENUES(b)"; Upjohn is out of both quarters from Q4 2020, Consumer Healthcare out of the quarters from Q4 2019 and in their year-ago
  quarters to Q2 2020. U.S. plus international misses the worldwide total by $1M in Q4 2020 and Q3 2021 (the release's rounding, allowed
  since 2014).
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2, unchanged.** The FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks keep "is a research-based, global biopharmaceutical company" and
  the generic-competition risk ("the resulting price competition can substantially decrease our revenues for the impacted products, often
  in a very short period of time", FY2020). No theme in `taxonomy_eras.json` is live for a pharmaceutical company through 2021 (GLP1 is
  from 2023-08-08 and scoped elsewhere), so the watch list stays empty; COVID-19 vaccine revenues are a product, not a substitution theme.
- **Segment bridge** (display only): Innovative Health and Essential Health (FY2017, FY2018), Biopharma, Upjohn and Other (FY2019), and
  from the FY2020 10-K, with one operating segment after the spin-off, its six therapeutic categories.
- **Adds nothing:** the Consumer Healthcare joint-venture agreement (2018-12-19) and closing (2019-08-05) 8-Ks ("slightly accretive"),
  the Array tender offer (2019-06-17, its adjusted-EPS dilution), the Upjohn-Mylan agreement and its Form 425s (Mylan's guidance and the
  combined company's pro forma projections are not Pfizer guides), the vote, officer, by-law and debt 8-Ks, the DEFA14A proxy materials,
  and the 10-Qs beyond their dividend statements.
- **Builder changes:** the `distributions` rule above; years excluded from the EPS history as reported (`eps_excluded`, the NKE, AVGO and
  XOM encoding: their days leave the window, growth is measured between years in the history), used here only by the sensitivity tests;
  the distribution's source joins a model's sources from its date. No earlier output changes.

Controls and checks:

- **Firewall:** passes at the 24 cutoffs above and at three earlier ones rerun after the builder change (2009-01-27, 2014-05-05,

- No file shared with another ticker changed, so no other model can move.

## CMCSA (Comcast): the sixteenth ticker, in staging

The CMCSA series is built apart from ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, AVGO, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT, RCL, MAR, BKR and PFE and shares nothing
with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet (`retro/facts/CMCSA.json`), builder (`retro/build_cmcsa.py`, the PFE builder with a
revenue guide in percent) and engine (`retro/templates/cmcsa_engine.py.tmpl`, the PFE engine with cable signals). The method is still r2.
No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters a CMCSA model, and neither does the profile of CMCSA in
`data/business_profiles.json` (a 2026 judgement, not read for this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/CMCSA/`, beside the
others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`.

```bash
python3 retro/build_cmcsa.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                 # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_cmcsa.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                 # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/CMCSA/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series CMCSA
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-02-14 2008-02-20 2008-05-01 2008-07-01 2008-07-30 2008-10-29 2009-01-01 2009-02-18 2009-02-20 \
         2009-04-30 2009-08-06 2009-11-04 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CMCSA; done
```

Read for the history and the decade's signal values: the statements of operations and cash flows and the cable operating tables of the
FY1998-FY2008 10-Ks (FY1998-FY2001 are plain-text filings of the Comcast Corporation that became Comcast Holdings, CIK 22301; from FY2002
the new Comcast Corporation, CIK 1166691; the FY2005 and FY2006 financial statements are in the annual reports filed as Exhibit 13), and
the selected financial data of the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks. Read for the prints: the earnings releases of Q4 2006 to Q3 2009, the Q4 2003 to
Q4 2005 releases for the definition of the company's adjusted income, and every other 8-K of February 2007 to January 2010 by its items
and exhibits. The 10-Qs were not needed: every guide and dividend is in a release. All by Opus directly, with no delegated transcription.
The fact sheet is generated by a script from the transcribed raw figures, so every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is computed, not
typed; 246 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (every statement row behind a print or rule T, every
subscriber row, every guide, dividend and quoted sentence), and a second script found each of the 350 raw figures in the verified rows of
its own source. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (converted from UTC; before 2003 EDGAR gives the filing date only).
Decided on 2026-11-11, before any CMCSA model was built or any CMCSA outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** CMCSA is the Class A common stock (Nasdaq). Yahoo's series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 split of 2017-02-21 and
  a factor of 1.067 dated 2026-01-05 (Yahoo's split event for the Versant Media distribution, the PFE 1.054 case); every date here
  precedes both, so the builder multiplies Yahoo's close by 2.134 and gets the price as traded: $18.26 on 2007-12-31 and $16.88 on
  2008-12-31. The 3-for-2 split (a 50% stock dividend payable 2007-02-21, ex-dividend 2007-02-22, Yahoo's split date) precedes every
  date; it is a `splits` record, so the one per-share fact published before it, the Q4 2006 release's 2006 adjusted EPS of $0.90, is
  restated to $0.60 by the builder (`eps_published`). Every later filing is on the post-split basis.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year. The six dates of January and early February 2008 before the Q4 2007 print have FY2007 as the
  current year.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q4 2006 to Q3 2009 was accepted before the open on its release day (06:51-07:09 ET), none
  on a Friday, so each print's week is dated the next trading day: 2008-02-15, 2008-05-02, 2008-07-31, 2008-10-30, 2009-02-19,
  2009-05-01, 2009-08-07, 2009-11-05. The FY2006 (2007-02-26 12:08 ET), FY2007 (2008-02-20 11:54 ET) and FY2008 (2009-02-20 13:52 ET)
  10-Ks were accepted during the session. Of the older 10-Ks used for rule T, FY2002, FY2003 and FY2005 were accepted after the close
  and are dated the next trading day.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it.** EPS is diluted EPS from continuing operations, replaced by the
  company's figure where that figure excludes only one-offs (the ACN and PEP rule): 2006 $0.60 (the Q4 2006 release's $0.90 before
  the split, then the Q4 2007 release's $0.60; it excludes the Adelphia/Time Warner investment gain and the gain on discontinued
  operations; GAAP $0.70 from continuing operations), 2007 $0.74 from the Q4 2007 release (excluding the $300 million after-tax gain on
  the dissolution of the Texas/Kansas City Cable Partnership; GAAP $0.83), 2008 $0.91 from the Q4 2008 release (excluding the
  partnership gains, favorable income tax adjustments and the Clearwire impairment; GAAP $0.86). 2004 $0.28 and 2005 $0.25 stay GAAP
  from continuing operations: the company's "Adjusted Net Income" of those years (Q4 2004 and Q4 2005 releases) "excludes Investment
  Income and Other Income", which recur, so it does not exclude only one-offs (the NKE FY2007 and PFE rule). One seam stays in: the
  2006 company figure keeps $0.03 of income from the systems transferred to Time Warner, which the continuing-operations line of 2004
  and 2005 excludes. Revenues and diluted shares from the 10-Ks (2004 3,375M, 2006 3,180M, 2008 2,952M); FY2007 enters from the Q4
  2007 print on 2008-02-15 and the FY2007 10-K replaces it on 2008-02-22; FY2008 likewise on 2009-02-19 and 2009-02-27.
- **2003 excluded; the history and the P/E window start with 2004** (`pe_window_start` 2004-01-01). 2003 was a loss from continuing
  operations ($(0.07) a diluted share in the FY2006 10-K), and the company's 2003 figure "as adjusted" strips all
  investment and other income too, so no figure excluding only one-offs exists. A distorted year that is not the latest takes the
  history and the window with it (the ACN FY02, AAPL FY2002 and PFE 2003 rule): the history is 2004-2006 on the first dates and the
  window 4.0 years in January 2008, 6.0 years at the end of 2009. A ten-year history excluding only 2003 was not built: 2002 is also
  a loss from continuing operations ($(469) million, FY2003 10-K), and 2001's $4 million of income from continuing operations follows
  $986 million of investment income, so that reading reaches no earlier year without a further call.
- **Guides: consolidated revenue growth in percent, for the fiscal year only.** Every release guides the year; none guides a quarter,
  EPS or an operating margin. The ranges are pro forma for acquisitions, and are used as the release states them (the MAR rule, "the
  release's own percentage first"). Method r2 maps them as follows:
  - current-FY EPS: no EPS guide, so the last full year's EPS stands (the rollover rule): FY06's $0.60 to 2008-02-08, FY07's $0.74 from
    2008-02-15, FY08's $0.91 from 2009-02-19;
  - BASE growth and the growth factor: FY2007's "Consolidated revenue growth of at least 11%" (Q4 2006 release, reaffirmed in the Q1 and
    Q2 2007 releases and restated as "previously issued" in the Q3 2007 release) is a one-sided bound and gives no field (the PEP, UNP,
    LOW and WMT rule), so the six dates before the Q4 2007 print take Q3 2007's revenue growth as reported, +21.0% (acquisitions in,
    the house rule); FY2008 "Consolidated Revenue and Operating Cash Flow growth of 8% to 10%" (Q4 2007 release, reaffirmed in each
    2008 release) from 2008-02-15; no 2009 outlook in numbers ("For 2009, our goal is to continue to deliver growth even in this
    challenging environment"), so from 2009-02-19 the latest quarter as reported: +9.4% (Q4 2008), +5.3%, +4.5% and +3.0% (Q3 2009);
  - no margin step: the operating cash flow growth guide is not an operating-margin guide (the AAPL gross-margin rule), and the capital
    expenditure ("approximately 18%" of revenue in 2008) and free cash flow guides feed no input; they are shown in the guide line.
  - Reaffirmations add nothing (the ACN rule); the Q3 2007 release's "may have a slight impact on our full year operating results" and
    the Q3 2008 release's free cash flow sentence are words, shown in the guide line.
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the rate: none to 2008-02-08 (the FY2006 10-K: no cash dividends, and none
  intended "for the foreseeable future"); $0.0625 a quarter from the Q4 2007 release ("the first payment of a planned annual dividend
  of $0.25 per share"); $0.0675 from the Q4 2008 release. The FY2008 10-K states only 2008's $0.0625, so the builder takes the latest
  declaration public on AS_OF and the vintage's rate only when none is (the ACN wording, "from the latest print that states one, else
  the vintage"); decided before any model was built.
- **Signals.** Five, with ACN's weights: video subscriber growth (0.20), revenue growth (0.20), the operating cash flow margin change
  (0.15; operating income before depreciation and amortization, as the releases print it), the capital intensity change (0.15; capital
  expenditures on revenues, lower is better) and the operating margin change (0.15), plus the theme slot at 2/4. Each value is the
  release's own, against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it: revenues, operating cash flow and operating income from the
  consolidated statement of operations (GAAP, acquisitions in); quarterly GAAP capital expenditures from the reconciliation table
  (Table 7-A) to Q3 2008 and the free cash flow table from Q4 2008; video subscribers from the customer table, which is pro forma for
  acquisitions (the Insight Midwest systems are in the year-ago quarter from Q1 2008). The column order of that table differs by
  release and is recorded on each print (`video_columns`).
- **Thresholds by rule T** over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04: ten changes, each from
  the latest 10-K published by then whose statements of operations and cash flows (or, for subscribers, whose cable table) report both
  years. Seams stay in, as published: QVC is consolidated until the FY2003 10-K presents it as discontinued (the 2002 change is
  QVC-free), Comcast Cellular is discontinued from the FY1999 10-K, the FY2000 10-K reclassifies electronic-retailing revenue,
  acquisitions (Jones, Lenfest, the AT&T exchanges, AT&T Broadband in November 2002, Adelphia and Time Warner in 2006) enter with the
  filings that report them, franchise amortization stops in 2002, and the FY2006 10-K's cable table excludes the systems transferred to
  Time Warner from every year. The raw figures and values are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives every value and
  threshold and refuses to build if they differ.

  | Signal | Fiscal 1997-2006 | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | video subscriber growth | 2.01, 3.32, 26.8, 33.33, 11.84, 150.59, 0.99, 0.49, -0.98, 15.27 % | -10 / -1 / 8 / 151 % |
  | revenue growth | 23.68, 15.17, 20.49, 25.87, 17.7, 36.47, 126.46, 10.68, 9.65, 18.46 % | 0 / 10 / 19 / 126 % |
  | operating cash flow margin change | -4.1, 14.5, 117.4, 126.4, -226.7, 219.3, -16.6, 224.8, 94.6, -48.2 bp | -510 / -230 / 50 / 220 bp |
  | capital intensity change (lower is better) | 245.8, -33.5, -289.9, 622.7, 259.5, -1148.5, -18.0, -465.5, -186.0, 42.2 bp | 1270 / 620 / -30 / -1150 bp |
  | operating margin change | -245.4, 38.4, -11.1, -1212.9, -565.8, 3368.5, -71.8, 367.1, 198.9, 179.4 bp | -2440 / -1210 / 10 / 3370 bp |

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2,** the default of every ticker whose 10-K does not call its business cyclical. The "why" quotes the latest
  10-K: "We are the largest cable operator in the United States", the competition it names (DBS providers, phone companies building
  fiber-optic networks "to provide video services", and "online services that offer Internet video streaming, downloading and
  distribution of movies, television shows and other video programming", a bullet in every 10-K from FY2006), and from the FY2007 10-K
  the economy ("Intensifying competition and a weakening economy affected our net subscriber additions during the second half of
  2007"). The kind changes the class label only. No disruption theme in `taxonomy_eras.json` is live for a cable operator in 2008-2009:
  STREAMING, whose scope ("cord-cutting / streaming displaces linear TV networks and pay-TV bundles") covers Comcast, is live from
  2015-08-04. So the watch list is empty, the builder refuses events until a theme encoding is decided, and the online-video wording stays
  in the "why" (the PEP obesity rule). Comcast's FY2006 10-K (2007-02-26) is an earlier verified filing naming Internet video streaming as
  competition than the registry's basis (Disney's ESPN outlook of 2015-08-04); whether to move STREAMING's live date is left to the owner
  (the MSFT, XOM, WMT and BKR precedent).
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the last 10-K's segments (Cable, Programming, Corporate and Other, before
  eliminations), the total from the revenue guide midpoint or the latest quarter's growth on the last full year; the EPS check runs on
  the last year's pre-tax margin and tax rate.
- **Adds nothing:** the 3-for-2 split 8-K (its ratio enters through `splits`), the voluntary XBRL 8-Ks (2007-06-21 to 2009-02-25), the
  officer and compensation 8-Ks, the debt 8-Ks (2008-02-04, 2008-05-06, 2009-06-17), the subsidiary merger 8-K (2009-09-02), and the NBC
  Universal joint-venture agreement with GE (8-K accepted 2009-12-03 19:51 ET; a pending deal with no guided number, the XOM XTO and PFE
  Wyeth rule).
- **Anachronism list:** Comcast names first seen in its filings after the start of 2008 (Xfinity, NBCUniversal, Peacock, Versant) join
  `taxonomy_eras.json`, each dated from the first filing under Comcast's CIK that uses it (EDGAR full-text search). No model of any ticker
  contains them, so no output changes. CMCSA's source ids are `CM1`-`CM24`.

Controls: altering one value of each print (its video subscriber growth, and each Q4 print's full-year EPS), vintage (its last year's
EPS), guide (its range, or the words of a one-sided bound), dividend and the split ratio changes no date before its publication and
changes the first weekly date on or after it (23 of 26; the other 3 are the FY2007 guide words of the Q4 2006, Q1 2007 and Q2 2007
releases, superseded by the Q3 2007 release before any built date). A scan of the 105 models for the source ids, titles, notes, texts
and figures of every later print, guide, vintage, dividend and source finds none before its publication (0 of 4,288 pairs, after
dropping 9 strings an earlier fact already carries). Rebuilding the 2008 dates of ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT,
RCL, MAR, BKR and PFE and the 2009 dates of AVGO changes nothing (764 models). The firewall (every kind of fact planted after the cutoff
with absurd values, including absurd full-year actuals for the year after the latest vintage, a later split on the price data's split
date, and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10) changes no model and leaves no planted text at any of the 14 cutoffs above (1 to 105
dates each). All 105 dates pass `retro_tool run`; the 11 dates from 2008-02-15 to 2008-04-25 draw one warning, the calendar year 2009 in
the Q4 2007 release's plan to use the repurchase authorization "by the end of 2009".

read directly, none delegated; the 10-Qs were not needed, as every dividend is in a release. The source ids are CM45-CM64. The fact
sheet's new entries were generated by a script that parses every raw figure from the row it is cited from; 329 strings were checked with

figures in the verified rows of its own source. Decided on 2026-11-11, before any 2014-2017 model was built or outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (06:05-07:06 ET), none on a Friday, so each print's week is dated
  the next trading day (2014-01-29 .. 2017-10-27). The 10-Ks: FY2013 2014-02-12 12:49 ET and FY2014 2015-02-27 13:16 ET (a Friday, so
  it meets that day's close), during the session; FY2015 2016-02-05 17:00 ET, after the close, dated 2016-02-08; FY2016 2017-02-03 14:34
  ET, during the session (a Friday). The next-print timing in each print's text is the same print's a year earlier.
- **History: four more vintages, each with the ten years to its own 10-K's year** (the PFE, MAR and SHW reading of "the ten fiscal
  years"): FY2013 (2004-2013), FY2014 (2005-2014), FY2015 (2006-2015), FY2016 (2007-2016); each year from the latest filing that reports
  it, on the same basis. The company's EPS excluding one-offs from each Q4 release: 2013 $2.47 (GAAP $2.56), 2014 $2.93 ($3.20), 2015
  $3.25 ($3.24), 2016 $3.48 ($3.57, before the split); every listed item is a gain, a tax adjustment, a transaction cost (Time Warner Cable
  and Charter), an investment loss or a legal or agency-agreement item, and each later release repeats the earlier year's figure, so no
  `restates` is needed. The distorted-year test keeps every year (2014's net listed benefits, $699 million after tax, are 8% of its
  income). Revenues and GAAP EPS from each 10-K's selected financial data (no year is recast), diluted shares from each computation of
  diluted EPS (three years; earlier years keep the latest filing that reports them). 2004 leaves the history with the FY2014 10-K and
  2005 with the FY2015 10-K; `pe_window_start` (2004-01-01) no longer binds from 2014.
- **No guide in numbers in any year.** No release or other filing of 2014-2017 gives an outlook in numbers (the Q4 releases give

  year's (FY13's $2.47 from 2014-01-29, FY14's $2.93 from 2015-02-25, FY15's $3.25 from 2016-02-04, FY16's $3.48 from 2017-01-27, $1.74
  after the split) and BASE and the growth factor take the latest quarter's revenue growth as reported: -2.4% (Q3 2013) to +13.7% (Q1
  2014, the Sochi Olympics and the Super Bowl), +14.2% (Q3 2016, the Rio Olympics) and -1.6% (Q3 2017, against them). No margin step.

  FY2016 10-K are on the pre-split basis ("all share and per-share amounts ... are presented on a pre-split basis"), so from 2017-02-21
  every earlier per-share fact is halved and every share count doubled; prices are Yahoo's close times 2.134 before that date and 1.067
  from it. The Q4 2016 dividend is stored as published on the pre-split basis, $0.315 a quarter ($1.26 a year; the release declares
  "$0.1575 a share, on a post-split basis"), so the split halves it with the rest.
- **Signals and thresholds unchanged.** Video customers from each release's own table against the year-ago figure it shows: from Q1 2014
  on the "Billable Customers Method" (MDUs billed under bulk contracts counted by potential billable relationships; each release restates
  its year-ago column), from Q1 2017 the row "Total Video Customers" (residential and business, the same total: 1Q16 is 22,400 in both
  releases). The FY2014 10-K's table gives both methods; the vintage uses the billable one. Operating cash flow is renamed "Adjusted
  EBITDA (formerly Operating Cash Flow)" from Q1 2017 (the renamed-line rule); Q3 2017's excludes a $250 million legal settlement that
  operating income includes (+216bp; +97bp with it, BULL either way). Capital expenditures from each release's free cash flow table.

  Animation (from 2016-08-22). The releases' pro forma and excluding-Olympics growth is shown in each print's note, display only.
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the rate: $0.225 a quarter (Q4 2013 release), $0.25 (Q4 2014), $0.275 (Q4 2015),
  $0.315 before the split (Q4 2016).
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2; STREAMING on the watch list from 2015-08-07.** The "why" follows each 10-K ("a global media and
  technology company with two primary businesses, Comcast Cable and NBCUniversal", its online-video competition sentence and "Weak
  economic conditions may have a negative impact on our businesses"). STREAMING (scoped to linear TV networks and pay-TV bundles) is live

not read), all downloaded from EDGAR and read directly, none delegated; the 10-Qs were not needed, as every dividend is in a release. The
source ids are CM65-CM84. The new entries were generated by a script from the raw figures it parsed out of each filing's rows, orienting

  the same. The 10-Ks were all accepted after the close and are dated the next trading day: FY2017 2018-01-31 16:35 ET (2018-02-01),
  FY2018 2019-01-31 17:00 ET (2019-02-01), FY2019 2020-01-30 16:41 ET (2020-01-31), FY2020 2021-02-03 18:08 ET (2021-02-04).
- **History: four more vintages, the ten years to each 10-K's year** (FY2017 2008-2017 .. FY2020 2011-2020), each year from the latest
  filing that reports it. They are the first vintages after the 2017 split: a year first published before it keeps its published figure
  and its own date (`eps_published`, `shares_published`, the UNP, AAPL and NKE encoding), so the split halves 2008-2015's EPS and doubles
  2008-2014's share counts, and nothing else. All four 10-Ks still carry five-year selected financial data. The FY2018 10-K restates 2016
  and 2017 for the new revenue standard (adopted on 2018-01-01, full retrospective: $80,736M and $85,029M against $80,403M and $84,526M)
  but not 2014-2015, a seam as published (the ACN FY19 rule). Diluted shares from each 10-K's computation of diluted EPS (three years).
- **EPS: the company's figure excluding only one-offs where one is published, else GAAP** (the 2004-2005 rule, unchanged):
  - 2016 $1.74 (the Q4 2017 release, post-split); 2017 $2.06 from the Q4 2017 release (GAAP $4.75 with the $12.7 billion of net income
    tax benefits from the 2017 tax reform legislation), **restated to $2.03 by the Q4 2018 release**, which also excludes fair value
    investments (`restates`, from 2019-01-24 until the FY2018 10-K carries it); 2018 $2.55 (GAAP $2.53);
  - **the 2019 redefinition.** The 8-K of 2019-02-04 (Item 2.02, 07:01 ET) says Comcast "will now present Adjusted EPS ... to also exclude
    amortization expense for acquisition-related intangible assets" (2017 $2.14, 2018 $2.73), and every release from Q1 2019 gives only
    that figure (2019 $3.13, 2020 $2.61). Amortization recurs, so it is not a figure excluding only one-offs (the 2004-2005, AVGO and PFE
    reading): 2017 and 2018 keep the one-off figures, and **2019 ($2.83) and 2020 ($2.28) are GAAP**. The reconciliation's per-share
    lines are not used to derive a figure (the 2009 rule). SHW's amortization-excluding figure is SHW's own rule, not this one;
  - the distorted-year test keeps every year: 2017's GAAP figure is more than double its EPS without the Tax Act benefit (r2's mirror
    test), but the company's figure without it is published and is the one used; 2019's and 2020's listed one-offs (amortization aside)
    net to $0.05 and $0.07 a share.
- **No guide in numbers in any year.** The Q4 releases give buyback plans ("at Least $5 Billion Expected to be Repurchased in 2018") and
  dividends; the 8-K of 2018-10-01 pauses repurchases for 2019 (resumed in May 2021); the COVID 8-K of 2020-03-24 and the Q1 2020 release
  give words only ("it is impossible to predict such extent and duration"; Cable results "will be negatively affected in the second
  quarter"). So current-FY EPS is the last full year's (the rollover rule): FY16's $1.74 to 2018-01-19, FY17's $2.06 from 2018-01-25,
  FY18's $2.55 from 2019-01-24, FY19's $2.83 from 2020-01-24, FY20's $2.28 from 2021-01-29; BASE and the growth factor take the latest
  quarter's revenue growth as reported; no margin step.
- **Sky in growth, as published** (the NBCUniversal rule): Sky is consolidated from 2018-10-09, so revenue grows 26.1% (Q4 2018), 17.8%,
  23.6% and 21.2% (Q1-Q3 2019; the Q1 2019 release rounds 17.85% to 17.9%). The releases' pro forma growth is in each print's note,
  display only; their quarterly pro forma tables (+5.2%, -3.3%, +0.8%, 0.0%) are a sensitivity below.
- **Signals and thresholds unchanged.** Video customers from the "Total Video Customers" row against the year-ago figure each release
  shows (the year-ago columns carry a footnote adjustment from Q1 2019). From Q1 2020 the releases print the current period first; the

  EBITDA from the statement of income to Q1 2020, then from the release's reconciliation table (Table 2), as the releases print it;
  capital expenditures from each release's free cash flow table.
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the rate: $0.19 a quarter (Q4 2017 release), $0.21 (Q4 2018), $0.23 (Q4 2019),
  $0.25 (Q4 2020). The 10-Ks repeat each rate after its release, so their own dividend notes never print.
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2; STREAMING stays on the watch list** (the 2014-2017 encoding), from each 10-K's consumer-behaviour risk

- **Segment bridge** (display only): each 10-K's segments, Sky from the FY2018 10-K (new, no prior year; +319.0% in FY2019 against the

  2024-07-23), so each print's week is dated the next trading day (2022-01-28 .. 2026-10-23). The FY2021, FY2022 and FY2023 10-Ks were

  `excluded_note`, the FY2022-FY2025 vintages carry `eps_excluded`, 2022's revenue and shares stay, its own days leave the P/E window

- **The other years are kept:** 2021 at 1.08 times its EPS without its listed items, 2023 at 1.05, 2024 at 1.10 (a $1.9 billion income
  tax benefit) and **2025 at 1.48** (the $7.1 billion after-tax gain on the sale of the interest in Hulu, $1.90 a share; r2 excludes at
  double, and the benefits, $7,388 million, are under the year's $13,468 million of income without them).
- **No guide in numbers in any filing.** The Q4 releases give dividends and buyback amounts; the 8-K of 2026-06-29 plans a tax-free

  excluded, to 2024-01-19, FY23's $3.71 from 2024-01-26, FY24's $4.14 from 2025-01-31, FY25's $5.39 from 2026-01-30; BASE and the growth

## CAT (Caterpillar): the seventeenth ticker, in staging

The CAT series is built apart from ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, AVGO, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT, RCL, MAR, BKR, PFE and CMCSA and shares
nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet (`retro/facts/CAT.json`), builder (`retro/build_cat.py`, the CMCSA builder with
profit per share and sales and revenues guides in dollars or in percent) and engine (`retro/templates/cat_engine.py.tmpl`, the CMCSA
engine with machinery and engines signals). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters a CAT
model, and neither does the live `cat_signal_model.py` or the profile of CAT in `data/business_profiles.json` (2026 judgements, not read
for this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/CAT/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`.

```bash
python3 retro/build_cat.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                   # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_cat.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                   # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/CAT/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series CAT
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-01-25 2008-02-22 2008-04-18 2008-07-01 2008-07-22 2008-08-29 2008-10-21 2009-01-01 2009-01-26 \
         2009-02-20 2009-04-21 2009-05-15 2009-07-21 2009-10-20 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CAT; done
```

Read for the history and the decade's signal values: the statements of results, the five-year financial summaries and the enterprise-wide
sales tables of the FY1998-FY2008 10-Ks (FY1998 a plain-text filing; from FY1999 the financial statements are in the annual report filed
as Exhibit 13), and the Q4 1997-Q4 2005 results 8-Ks for any per-share figure excluding one-offs. Read for the prints: the results releases
of Q4 2006 to Q3 2009 (Exhibit 99.1, Exhibit 99.7 for Q4 2008), the dividend and split 8-Ks, and every other 8-K of October 2006 to January
2010 by its items and exhibits (the monthly dealer-statistics 8-Ks, Item 7.01, only point to the company's website). The 10-Qs were not
needed: every guide is in a release and every new dividend rate in an 8-K. All by Opus directly, with no delegated transcription. The fact
sheet is generated by a script from the transcribed raw figures, so every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is computed, not typed; 270
strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (every statement, sales-table and five-year row behind a print, a
vintage or rule T, every guide, dividend, buyback and quoted sentence), and a second script found each of the 356 raw figures in the
verified rows of its own source. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (converted from UTC; before 2003 EDGAR gives the
filing date only). Decided on 2026-11-11, before any CAT model was built or any CAT outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** CAT is the NYSE common stock. Yahoo's series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 splits of 1994-09-06, 1997-07-14 and
  2005-07-14; none follows 2005, so from 2008 Yahoo's close is the price as traded: $68.53 on 2008-01-04 and $44.67 on 2008-12-31. The 2005
  split (announced 2005-06-08, shares distributed 2005-07-13, Yahoo's split date 2005-07-14) is a `splits` record: the per-share figures
  published before it (1997-2001 EPS, 1997-2002 diluted shares) carry their publication dates (`eps_published`, `shares_published`) and
  are halved or doubled by the builder. The 1997 split precedes every per-share fact in the fact sheet.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year. The three dates of January 2008 before the Q4 2007 print have FY2007 as the current year.
- **Release timing.** Every results 8-K of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 was accepted before the open on its release day (08:19-09:23 ET) except Q1
  2008's (10:53 ET, during the session). The Q2 2007 to Q1 2008 releases came on Fridays, so those weeks are dated the release day
  (2008-01-25 and 2008-04-18; the builder requires `release_time` to say before the open or during the session); the later ones on
  Mondays and Tuesdays, so each week is dated the next trading day: 2008-07-23, 2008-10-22, 2009-01-27, 2009-04-22, 2009-07-22 and
  2009-10-21. The FY2006 (2007-02-23 14:07 ET), FY2007 (2008-02-22 13:39 ET) and FY2008 (2009-02-20 14:49 ET) 10-Ks were accepted during
  the session. Of the older 10-Ks, FY2002, FY2004 and FY2005 were accepted after the close and are dated the next trading day.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it.** EPS is profit per share - diluted (the five-year summaries), replaced by
  the company's figure where a filing publishes one excluding only one-offs (the ACN rule): 2001 $2.60 before the split, $1.30 after it
  (the Q4 2001 release: "Excluding the nonrecurring charges of 28 cents per share, profit was $902 million, or $2.60 per share", the sale of
  the Challenger tractor line, plant closings and employment reductions; GAAP $2.32, $1.16 after the split in the FY2005 10-K). No other
  year has one: the 2000 Brazilian tax adjustment, the FY2002 10-K's 2001 profit "excluding nonrecurring charges" ($902 million, in dollars
  only) and the $409 million favorable tax item of the fourth quarter of 2008 come with no per-share figure excluding them, and nothing is
  derived (the XOM 1997 rule). The FY2006 10-K presents 2002-2006 after its retrospective adoption of SFAS 123R; earlier years stay as
  published (a seam, the LOW and PEP rule). Sales and revenues and diluted shares likewise (1997 shares 380,540,960 from the FY1999 10-K's
  note, 2003 702.7M from the FY2005 10-K, 2006 683.8M). No year is excluded: no loss, and 2001's charges ($97 million after tax) are a tenth
  of the year's profit. FY2007 enters from the Q4 2007 print on 2008-01-25 and the FY2007 10-K replaces it on 2008-02-22; FY2008 likewise
  on 2009-01-27 and 2009-02-20. The P/E window is the full ten years.
- **A recast is a vintage of its own** (the MSFT recast rule). The 8-K of 2009-05-14 (accepted 16:51 ET, after the close, so dated
  2009-05-15) refiles the FY2006-FY2008 statements for SFAS 160 and the 2009 segments. Sales and revenues, operating profit, profit per
  share, diluted shares and the three lines' external sales are unchanged; consolidated profit before taxes becomes $4,501M for 2008
  (FY2008 10-K: $4,473M) and operating cash flow $4,797M ($4,787M). Each year comes from the latest filing that reports it, so from
  2009-05-15 the history's 2004-2008 figures cite the recast and the display-only EPS check and balance line take its numbers; the
  durability "why" keeps the FY2008 10-K's words (an 8-K has no Item 1A).
- **Guides: the fiscal year only, never a quarter.** Each release guides sales and revenues and profit per share, in dollars or as growth;
  each field comes from the latest guide for the current year that states it, in either form (the WMT rule). Method r2 maps them as follows:
  - current-FY EPS: the profit per share guide midpoint: FY2007 $5.20-5.60 (Q3 2007 release) to 2008-01-18; FY2008 "up 5 to 15 percent
    from 2007" on FY07's $5.37 ($5.91) from 2008-01-25 and "about $6.00" from 2008-07-23 (restated in the Q3 2008 release); FY2009 $2.50
    (Q4 2008 release), about $1.25 (Q1 2009), $1.15-2.25 (Q2) and $1.85-2.05 (Q3), each excluding redundancy costs, the company's figure
    beside the inclusive one (the ACN rule for a guide with and without an announced item; the inclusive figures are in the note: none in
    the Q4 2008 release, about $0.50, $0.40-1.50 and $1.10-1.30);
  - BASE growth and the growth factor: no next-quarter guide, so the fiscal-year sales and revenues guide: a dollar guide read against the
    last full year (the PFE rule): FY2007 "about $44 billion" on FY06's $41.517B (+6.0%) to 2008-01-18; FY2008 "up 5 to 10 percent" as
    stated from 2008-01-25 and "about $50 billion" (+11.2% on $44.958B) from 2008-07-23; FY2009 "plus or minus 10 percent from $40 billion"
    ($36-44B: -29.9% to -14.3% on $51.324B) from 2009-01-27, $35 billion plus or minus 10 percent (-38.6% to -25.0%), $32-36 billion
    (-37.7% to -29.9%) and $32-33 billion (-37.7% to -35.7%);
  - a dollar level stated as "about" is a number (the release's own figure); a one-sided bound or words give no field (the PEP, UNP, LOW,
    WMT and CMCSA rule) and are shown in the guide line: the CEO's "total sales and revenues for 2008 to top $50 billion" (an 8-K under
    Item 7.01, accepted 2008-08-28 17:17 ET, after the close, so dated 2008-08-29), the Q3 2008 release's "sales and revenues to top $50
    billion" (the July figure of about $50 billion stands through both) and its 2009 "about flat with our full-year 2008 results"
    (superseded by the Q4 2008 guide before any date with FY2009 current);
  - a growth guide on another base keeps it (`eps_growth_base`, `rev_growth_base_b`): the Q3 2007 release's preliminary 2008 outlook "from
    the mid-point of the 2007 outlook range" ($5.40) and the Q3 2009 release's preliminary 2010 sales outlook "from the midpoint of the 2009
    outlook range" ($32.5 billion); neither is current on any built date;
  - no margin step: no operating-margin guide in numbers; the capital expenditure ("about $2.3 billion" in 2008) and tax-rate outlooks feed
    no input.
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the rate: $0.30 a quarter (8-K of 2006-12-13), $0.36 from the 8-K of 2007-06-13,
  $0.42 from the 8-K of 2008-06-11 (unchanged through 2009).
- **Signals.** Five, with ACN's weights: Machinery sales growth (0.20), Engines sales growth (0.20), sales and revenues growth (0.15),
  profit per share growth (0.15) and the operating margin change (0.15; operating profit on sales and revenues), plus the theme slot at
  2/4. Each value is the release's own, against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it: Machinery and Engines from the sales
  table by geographic region (external sales, internal engine transfers excluded), the rest from the statement of results of operations
  (GAAP: the 2009 redundancy costs stay in the quarter's profit per share, with the company's figure excluding them in the note).
- **Thresholds by rule T** over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04: ten changes, each from
  the latest 10-K published by then whose statement of results (sales and revenues, operating profit, profit per share - diluted) and
  enterprise-wide sales table (Machinery, Engines) report both years. Seams stay in, as published: revenue reclassifications in the
  FY2005 10-K, SFAS 123R in the FY2006 10-K, Progress Rail in Machinery from June 2006, and 2001's nonrecurring charges in its operating
  profit and profit per share. The raw figures and values are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives every value and
  threshold and refuses to build if they differ.
