  |---|---|---|
  | Machinery sales growth | 12.54, 0.73, -12.96, 1.3, 2.54, -1.51, 14.22, 37.77, 21.69, 13.65 % | -33 / -13 / 8 / 38 % |
  | Engines sales growth | 20.45, 37.06, 5.06, 2.95, -2.65, -2.85, 10.45, 28.79, 16.68, 15.64 % | -19 / -3 / 13 / 37 % |
  | sales and revenues growth | 14.54, 10.84, -6.08, 2.4, 1.36, -1.46, 12.96, 32.88, 19.91, 14.25 % | -24 / -6 / 12 / 33 % |
  | profit per share growth | 24.86, -5.95, -36.01, 14.83, -23.18, -0.86, 36.09, 84.62, 40.28, 27.97 % | -92 / -36 / 20 / 85 % |
  | operating margin change | 78.4, -210.0, -315.7, 102.7, -219.9, 15.9, 84.5, 153.4, 155.7, 144.0 bp | -710 / -320 / 80 / 160 bp |

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2** (the RCL, SHW and WMT precedent). None of the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks calls the business cyclical; they say
  "Caterpillar is the leader in construction and mining equipment, and diesel and natural gas engines and industrial gas turbines in our
  size range", "Decisions to purchase our machines and engines are dependent upon performance of these industries" (the energy and mining
  industries) and "The rates of infrastructure spending, housing starts, and commercial construction, play a significant role in our
  results"; the FY2008 10-K adds "Our results of operations are materially affected by the conditions in the global economy generally and
  in the global capital markets." Demand that depends on the industries served and the economy is not earnings that are the cycle (XOM's
  "fundamentally a commodity business", BKR's "Our business is cyclical"), so CYCLICAL is not used; the "why" quotes the latest 10-K. The
  kind changes the class label only. No disruption theme in `taxonomy_eras.json` is live for a maker of construction and mining equipment,
  engines and turbines in 2008-2009 (ENERGY_TRANSITION, scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, from 2015-12-12; EV, scoped to
  ICE powertrains, from 2020; OFFSHORE to IT services), and the 10-Ks name no climate, emissions-reduction or electrification risk beyond
  emissions standards for their own engines, so the watch list is empty and the builder refuses events until a theme encoding is decided.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the 10-K's three lines of business by external sales and revenues (Machinery, Engines,
  Financial Products) with each one's growth, the total from the sales and revenues guide midpoint; the EPS check runs on the last year's
  pre-tax margin and tax rate.
- **Adds nothing:** the transcript 8-Ks (the releases carry every number), the monthly dealer-statistics 8-Ks, the pricing-action 8-Ks
  (2007-09-04, 2008-04-01, 2008-07-22, 2009-10-05), the analyst-day transcript of 2008-03-12 (its 2010 profit per share range of $8 to $10
  is a multi-year goal, not a current-year input: the LOW and XOM rule) and the capacity-expansion calls (2008-06-12, 2008-06-13), the
  Navistar alliance and joint venture (2008-06-12, 2009-04-07, 2009-09-15), the organizational realignment (2008-10-10), the
  credit-facility, underwriting and debt 8-Ks, the officer, director, bylaw and compensation 8-Ks, and the FY2008 10-K's restatement of
  the 2009 outlook (the Q4 2008 release's numbers, plus "about $2.00 per share" including redundancy costs).
- **Anachronism list:** Caterpillar names first seen in its filings after 2008 (Bucyrus, Electro-Motive, Siwei) join `taxonomy_eras.json`,
  each dated from the first filing under Caterpillar's CIK that uses it (EDGAR full-text search). No model of any ticker contains them, so
  no output changes. CAT's source ids are `CT1`-`CT30`.

Controls: altering one value of each print (its Machinery sales growth, and each Q4 print's full-year EPS), vintage (its last year's EPS),
guide (its first guided field), dividend and the split ratio changes no date before its publication and changes the first weekly date on
or after it (29 of 36, the August 2008 guide words and the recast vintage among them; the other 7 are inert, superseded before any built date: the FY2007 EPS guides of the Q4 2006, Q1 2007 and Q2 2007
releases, the preliminary FY2008 guide of the Q3 2007 release, the FY2009 words of the Q3 2008 release, the preliminary FY2010 guide of
the Q3 2009 release and the dividend of 2006-12-13). A scan of the 105 models for the source ids, titles, notes, texts and figures of every
later print, guide, vintage, dividend and source finds none before its publication (0 of 6,805 pairs, after dropping 25 pairs an earlier
fact already carries: the Q2 2008 release's "about $6.00", restated in the Q3 2008 release, and the FY2008 10-K's durability words, kept
by the recast vintage). Rebuilding the 2008 dates of ACN, UNP, LOW,
AAPL, NKE, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT, RCL, MAR, BKR, PFE and CMCSA and the 2009 dates of AVGO changes nothing (817 models). The firewall (every kind of fact planted after the cutoff with absurd values, including absurd full-year
actuals for the year after the latest vintage, a later guide with every field in both forms and a still later one in the growth forms
only, and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10) changes no model and leaves no planted text at any of the 16 cutoffs above (1 to 105
dates each).
All 105 dates pass `retro_tool run`; the 11 dates from 2008-10-22 to 2008-12-31 draw one warning (2009, in the Q3 2008 release's 2009
outlook words) and the 11 from 2009-10-21 another (2010, the Q3 2009 release's preliminary 2010 outlook).

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **CHEAP on 64 dates, FAIR on 4, RICH on 37.** 2008: CHEAP on 50 of 53 (FAIR on 2008-04-04, 2008-04-18 and 2008-05-16); 2009: CHEAP on
  14 dates to 2009-04-17 (FAIR on 2009-02-06), then RICH on all 37 from the Q1 2009 print (2009-04-22). Legacy tiers: BUY 49,
  ACCUMULATE 18, WATCHLIST 1, AVOID 37. Robustness: 8 of 8 on 75 dates, 7 on 20, 6 on 6; the four FAIR dates hold on 2-5 of 8.
- **The window is the full decade, 1998-2007 and then 1999-2008,** and its multiples are those of realized EPS: median 14.2-14.3x, 10th
  percentile 11.6-11.7x, 75th 18.2-19.1x, 90th 22.0-22.8x. The calendar-year lows are 9.8x (1998), 16.4x (1999), 9.9x (2000), 15.4x, 14.7x,
  13.5x, 12.1x, 10.3x, 11.2x and 10.8x (2007), and each date adds its own year's low, so the floor (their median, rounded down) is 11-12x
  the standing EPS: $64.80 (12x) and $59.40 (11x, from 2008-01-18) on FY07's $5.40, $65.01 on $5.91 and $66.00 on $6.00 (11x) through
  2008, $30.00 (12x) and $27.50 (11x, from 2009-02-20) on FY09's $2.50, $15.00 and $20.40 on $1.25 and $1.70 (12x: each lower guide lifts
  2009's own low multiple) and $21.45 on $1.95 (11x).
- **2008: the price fell through a standing EPS.** At 11.6-12.7x FY07's $5.40 in January, 11-14x the FY08 guide ($5.91, then $6.00)
  from the Q4 2007 print to September (the 1st-53rd percentile of the window), 5.8-8.5x from October to 2009-01-23 (0th-2nd); 31% over to
  48% under the floor. The proxy composite is 2.50 on Q3 2007, 2.20 on Q4 2007,
  2.55 on Q1 2008, 2.70 on Q2 2008 (Machinery +17.3%, Engines +27.8%, sales +20.0% and EPS +40.3% at BULL) and 2.55 on Q3 2008 (EPS -0.7%
  and the margin -244bp at BASE). BASE is the sales guide plus a 1.2-1.4%/yr buyback (+7.2% to +12.4%/yr), BULL the decade EPS CAGR
  (+9.4% to +12.4%), XBULL the 2003-2005 run (+60.9%/yr) and BEAR the 1999 fall (-36.0%: $2.055 to $1.315 after the split).
- **2009: the guide fell faster than the price.** On the Q4 2008 print the FY09 guide ($2.50 excluding redundancy costs, sales of $36-44
  billion) put the price at 12.9x (28th percentile), then 9.3-13.3x to 2009-04-17 ($23.23 on 2009-03-06, 16% under the floor). The Q1
  2009 print cut the EPS guide to $1.25 and sales to $31.5-38.5 billion: 26x at $32.45 (99th percentile), RICH and AVOID, and every later
  date sits at 23-32x (93rd-100th percentile), 90-174% over the floor. BASE turns negative with the sales guide (-20.5%/yr to -35.2%/yr),
  while BEAR is the history's worst year, 2001's -13.9% once the FY2008 10-K drops 1998 (2009-02-20): from 2009-04-22 the BASE price sits
  under the BEAR price on all 37 dates ($9-12 against $11-17). Ratio B is infinite on 33 dates (the price above BULL).
- **The composite follows the quarter:** 2.05 on Q4 2008 (Engines +14.0% at BULL, the margin -680bp at BEAR) and 1.15 on Q1-Q3 2009
  (every signal at BEAR: Machinery -29% to -52%, Engines -8% to -35%, sales -22% to -44%, EPS -54% to -113%, the margin -524bp to
  -1,286bp). The BASE scenario prints as "EPS +-20.5%/yr" when BASE is negative (the engine's "+" before the value; the ACN display quirk,
  left for an engine revision).

How far each call moves the classes (the 105 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- GAAP 2001 ($2.32 before the split) instead of the company's $2.60: 3 classes (FAIR to CHEAP on 2008-04-04, 2008-05-16, 2009-02-06) and 6
  tiers;
- the 2009 profit per share guides including redundancy costs (none in the Q4 2008 release, so FY08's $5.66 stands to 2009-04-17; then
  $0.50, $0.95 and $1.20): 1 class (2009-02-06 FAIR to CHEAP) and 2 tiers;
- "about" dollar levels read as words (the last numeric range stands): no class, 13 tiers (AVOID to BUY or ACCUMULATE from 2009-04-22 to
  2009-07-17: the Q4 2008 guide's $2.50 stands, but the sales guide keeps BASE under BEAR and the class RICH);
- every signal at its BEAR value: 37 classes (CHEAP or FAIR to RICH or FAIR in 2008 and early 2009); at its XBULL value: 4 classes (the
  FAIR dates to CHEAP);
- CYCLICAL instead of DURABLE: no class, no tier; the labels read CYCLICAL, RISK PRICED IN, CYCLICAL, NEUTRALLY VALUED and TOO MUCH CYCLE
  RISK.
The RICH calls of 2009 rest on the EPS guide falling to $1.25-1.95 while the price rose, and on the sales guide's negative BASE; no
encoding above moves them. The 2008 CHEAP calls rest on the price against the FY08 guide and the floor; they move with the signals and
with the 2001 figure.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows that machinery demand collapsed in 2009: Machinery and Engines sales, sales and revenues,
  profit per share and operating margin, all as reported (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; 37 classes move at BEAR);
- the company's 2001 figure excluding the nonrecurring charges (3 classes) and the 2009 guides excluding redundancy costs (1 class);
- "about" dollar levels read as numbers and "to top $50 billion" as a one-sided bound (no class);
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL, although Caterpillar is the textbook capital-goods cyclical: the rule reads the 10-K's own words, which
  never call the business cyclical (the class label only);
- rule T from the statements of results and the enterprise-wide tables rather than the five-year summaries (they agree on every year
  both report except the restated ones, the seam above).

The range starts on the Monday after the last built week (2013-12-31 is that ISO week's date), as the 2009 and 2010 ranges did, so it
has 208 dates. Read for the history: the statements of results, five-year financial summaries and segment notes of the FY2013 and FY2014
10-Ks (Exhibit 13) and of the FY2015 and FY2016 10-Ks (no Exhibit 13 from FY2015), and Exhibits 99.1-99.4 of the 8-K of 2016-05-16, which
recasts the FY2015 10-K; Items 1 and 1A of each 10-K. Read for the prints: the results releases of Q4 2013 to Q3 2017 (Exhibit 99.1), the
dividend 8-Ks, and every other 8-K of December 2013 to January 2018 by its items and exhibits (from 2015 the monthly dealer-statistics
8-Ks carry the rolling three-month retail tables themselves; no method input uses them). The filing list was fetched to 2018-01-31 and so
includes the Q4 2017 release; it was deleted unread and nothing from it enters (every source is published by 2017-10-24). All by Opus
directly, with no delegated transcription. The 25 new sources are `CT56`-`CT80` (by publication date). The records are generated by a
script that parses every raw figure from the row it cites and computes every growth rate, margin and rate; 448 strings (every row a raw
figure is parsed from, every guide, dividend, buyback and quoted sentence) were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings, all
found (1,013 in all). Decided on 2026-11-11, before any 2014-2017 model was built or any 2014-2017 outcome computed (one wording fix after
the first build changes no number: the vintages' normalization note no longer names 2011's and 2012's pre-recast figures as current):

- **Release timing.** Every results 8-K of Q4 2013 to Q3 2017 was accepted before the open (07:30-09:05 ET). Q1 2016 (2016-04-22) came on
  a Friday and is dated the release day; the others on Mondays to Thursdays, so each week is dated the next trading day (2014-01-28,
  2014-04-25, 2014-07-25, 2014-10-24, 2015-01-28, 2015-04-24, 2015-07-24, 2015-10-23, 2016-01-29, 2016-07-27, 2016-10-26, 2017-01-27,
  2017-04-26, 2017-07-26, 2017-10-25). The FY2013 (2014-02-18 14:25 ET), FY2015 (2016-02-16 11:20 ET) and FY2016 (2017-02-15 13:45 ET)
  10-Ks and the recast 8-K (2016-05-16 12:40 ET) were accepted during the session; the FY2014 10-K (2015-02-17 17:15 ET) after the close,
  so dated 2015-02-18.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it,** a vintage per 10-K (2004-2013, 2005-2014, 2006-2015, 2007-2016) and one
  for the recast; each Q4 print extends the history until the 10-K. The P/E window is the full ten years.

    profit per share with and without restructuring costs from 2014, and from 2016 also without mark-to-market pension and OPEB gains and
    losses (WMT's marks on JD.com, excluded as one-offs, are the precedent). 2013 is $5.75 as reported until the Q4 2014 release first
    publishes $5.97 excluding restructuring costs ("Profit in 2013 was $5.75 per share and $5.97 per share excluding restructuring
    costs", the FY2014 10-K); 2014 $6.38 (GAAP $5.88); 2015 $4.64 (GAAP $3.50); 2016 $3.42, the company's adjusted profit per share,
    which also excludes mark-to-market losses, a goodwill impairment and a deferred tax valuation allowance (a GAAP loss of $(0.11): the
    company's figure is not a loss, so the XOM loss rule does not apply).
  - **Mark-to-market pension accounting.** Effective January 1, 2016 Caterpillar recognizes actuarial gains and losses in earnings when
    its plans are remeasured, applied retrospectively (Q4 2015 release, Q&A 10). The Q1 2016 release recasts 2015 ($4.18 GAAP, $5.47
    excluding restructuring costs and mark-to-market losses) and the 8-K of 2016-05-16 recasts 2011-2015, a vintage of its own (the MSFT
    recast rule; 2006-2010 stay as published, a seam): 2011 $4.48 and 2012 $8.06 as recast (no figure excluding their actuarial gains
    and losses is published; $7.40 and $8.48 before), 2014 $7.15 and 2015 $5.47 excluding restructuring costs and mark-to-market losses.
    2013 as recast is $9.95 with $3,441 million of mark-to-market gains in it; its company figure, $5.97 on the earlier pension
    accounting, stays (the FY2014 10-K, the latest filing that publishes a figure for 2013 excluding one-offs: the 2009 rule). The Q4
    2016 release gives 2015 as $5.35 (restructuring costs now at statutory tax rates) and the FY2016 10-K repeats it.
  - **A release that republishes an earlier year's company figure restates it** until a 10-K vintage published after it (`restates`, new
    in the CAT builder: the PFE encoding, EPS only): 2013 $5.97 from the Q4 2014 print (2015-01-28 to 2015-02-13), 2015 $5.47 from the
    Q1 2016 print (2016-04-22 to 2016-05-13) and $5.35 from the Q4 2016 print (2017-01-27 to 2017-02-10).
- **Segments.** From Q1 2014 Power Systems is "Energy & Transportation (formerly Power Systems)", the same segment, still the Engines line
  (`et_m`; the volumes text names it). From Q1 2016 the segments are redrawn (forestry and paving products to Construction Industries,

  2016 segments. No Q4 release has a full-year segment table, so the full-year Machinery and Engines lines read n/r until each 10-K.
- **Guides: the fiscal year only, profit per share excluding restructuring costs,** with the inclusive figure in the note (the ACN rule
  for a guide given with and without an announced item, as for 2009); each field from the latest guide for the current year that states

  - FY2014: "about $56 billion in a range of plus or minus 5 percent" ($53.2-58.8 billion, the figures the Q2 2014 release states for it)

  (FY2009 and FY2010 do not), so "the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks name no climate, greenhouse-gas or electrification risk" is wrong for those two;

- **Adds nothing:** the Gosselies restructuring 8-K (2013-12-23; the outlook comes with the Q4 2013 release), the monthly dealer-statistics

Controls and checks:
- **Controls:** altering one value of each new print (its Machinery growth, and each Q4 print's full-year EPS), restatement, vintage (its
  last year's EPS), guide (its first guided field) and dividend changes no date before its publication and changes the first weekly date

  Q3 2015 and Q3 2016 releases and the 8-K of 2015-09-24's 2016 figure); the 83 controls of 2008-2013, rerun over all 522 dates, give the

- **Leak scan:** the source ids, titles, notes, texts and figures of every print, restatement, guide, vintage, dividend and source appear
  in no model before their publication (0 hits in 281,811 pairs, after setting aside 1,819 whose needle an earlier fact already carries:
  year-ago raw figures that are the previous year's current ones, guide levels a later guide repeats, the repeated durability words).
- **`retro_tool run`:** passes on all 208 dates; the 10 dates from 2014-10-24 to 2014-12-26 draw one warning (2015, the Q3 2014 release's
  preliminary outlook), the 15 from 2015-09-25 to 2015-12-31 another (2016, the 8-K of 2015-09-24 and the Q3 2015 release) and the 10 from
  2016-10-26 to 2016-12-30 another (2017, the Q3 2016 release).
- **Shared code untouched** (the engine template, `retro_tool.py`, `taxonomy_eras.json`; the builder and fact sheet are CAT's own, the
  fact sheet only gains records, and the firewall changes only in its CAT branch, which now also plants Energy & Transportation figures, a
  restatement of every year and a theme-tail note), so no other ticker's model can change.
- **Firewall:** every kind of fact planted after the cutoff with absurd values (as for 2010-2013, the planted print now also carrying
  Energy & Transportation's raw figures and a restatement of every year of the history, the later vintage a planted theme-tail note),
  and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10, change no model and leave no planted text at any of the 28 cutoffs above (every release,
  10-K, recast, outlook and dividend 8-K date of 2014-2017, the theme's live date, 2014-01-01 and 2018-01-01; 314 to 522 dates each).

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **RICH and AVOID on all 208 dates** (label TOO MUCH CYCLE RISK), robust on 8 of 8 variants on 206 dates and 7 on 2 (2015-01-16 and
  2015-01-23, FAIR with the multiples one band richer).
- **Why nothing moves it:** BEAR is 2009's fall (-61.5%/yr: $5.66 to $2.18), in the history on every date, so the BEAR price is $5-11
  and the downside 88-95%. BULL, the decade EPS CAGR (at least BASE), falls with the history from +20.7%/yr in January 2014 to +8.0%
  (2014), +5.2% (2015) and -1.2% to +1.4% (2016), and from the Q4 2016 print it is BASE's rate, so the upside to BULL is small or nil
  (Ratio B infinite on 102 dates, the price above BULL). BASE follows the sales guides: -16.0%/yr on FY13's guide in January 2014, +1.3%
  to +1.4% on the flat 2014 guide and -0.4% on its later ranges, -8.1% to -11.7% in 2015, -9.0% to -15.6% in 2016 (to 2017-01-20), then
  -1.3% to -1.1% on the $36-39 billion 2017 guide, rising to +3.9%, +13.0% and +15.6%. The BASE price reaches the price only from
  2014-12-12 to 2015-01-23 ($90 against $83.86-91.88), and those six dates stay RICH on the 2009 BEAR.
- **The multiple:** 13.9-18.2x the guide in 2014 (48th-92nd percentile, against a 13.7-14.0x median), 12.9-17.9x in 2015 (29th-92nd),
  13.0-29.5x in 2016 (29th-100th) and 21.8-34.1x in 2017 (84th-100th; 34.1x on 2017-01-27, $98.99 on the $2.90 guide). The floor is 10x
  to 2015-05-01, 11x from 2015-05-08 and 12x from 2017-01-06: the price is 18-82% above it in 2014-2015 and 18-184% in 2016-2017. At the January
  2016 low ($59.87, 13.0x $4.60, the 29th percentile, 18% over the floor) the class is still RICH: BASE -11.7%/yr and the 2009 BEAR.
- **The recast moves XBULL and the upper multiples, not the class:** the best two-year run is 2009-2011 throughout; with 2011 at $4.48
  from 2016-05-16 it is +43.4%/yr instead of +84.2%/yr. 2011's recast figure also lifts that year's daily P/Es (its calendar low from
  9.5x to 15.7x): on 2016-05-20 the window's 90th percentile is 21.4x (18.2x a week earlier) and the median 14.3x (14.2x); the floor
  stays 11x.
- **The composite follows the quarter:** 1.15 on Q3 2013, 2.0-2.3 from Q4 2013 to Q1 2015, 1.45 on Q2 2015, 1.15 on Q3 2015 to Q1 2016
  (every signal at BEAR), 1.30 on Q2 and Q3 2016, 1.35 on Q4 2016, 2.0 on Q1 2017, 2.65 on Q2 2017 and 2.95 on Q3 2017 (Machinery +36.4%,
  sales +24.6%, profit per share +268.8%, the margin +857bp).

How far each call moves the classes (the 208 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- the profit per share guides including restructuring costs (and the IronPlanet gain): no class, no tier;
- 2013-2015 at GAAP throughout (no figure excluding restructuring costs or mark-to-market; 2016 kept): no class, no tier;
- 2011 and 2012 kept at their pre-recast $7.40 and $8.48: no class, no tier; 2013 at its recast $9.95: no class, no tier;
- the 8-K of 2016-03-17's first-quarter sales estimate read as a next-quarter guide (-26.8% to -26.0% on 2016-03-18 to 2016-04-15): no
  class, no tier;
- every signal at its BEAR value, or at its XBULL value: no class, no tier.
The RICH calls of 2014-2017 rest on the method's scenario rules, not on any of these encodings: the 2009 BEAR year, a BULL rate that the
falling guides pull below the price, and a price at or above its decade median multiple of the guide on most dates.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- restructuring costs (five years running, 2013-2017) and pension mark-to-market treated as one-offs, through the company's figures and
  guides (no class either way);
- the recast 8-K as a vintage, 2011-2012 at their recast GAAP figures and 2013 kept at the earlier-basis $5.97 (no class either way);
- the 8-K of 2016-03-17's quarter estimate left out (no class either way);
- ENERGY_TRANSITION read as out of scope for an equipment maker that sells to coal, oil and gas producers (text only);
- the signals themselves, chosen by a builder who knows that mining and oil demand fell through 2016 and recovered in 2017 (no class at
  BEAR or XBULL).

### CAT 2018-2022

The same fact sheet, builder and engine, extended; the engine template and rule T are unchanged, and every 2008-2017 model rebuilds
byte for byte (522 of 522) after the builder changes below.

```bash

for d in staging/retrospective/CAT/20{18,19,20,21,22}-*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series CAT
for c in 2018-01-01 2018-01-25 2018-02-15 2018-04-24 2018-06-13 2018-07-30 2018-10-23 2019-01-28 2019-02-14 2019-04-24 2019-05-02 \
         2019-07-24 2019-10-23 2020-01-01 2020-01-31 2020-02-19 2020-03-26 2020-04-28 2020-07-31 2020-10-27 2021-01-29 2021-02-17 \
         2021-04-29 2021-06-09 2021-07-30 2021-10-28 2022-01-28 2022-02-16 2022-04-28 2022-06-14 2022-08-02 2022-10-27 \
         2023-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CAT; done
```

FY2017-FY2021 10-Ks (no Exhibit 13; the FY2021 10-K's Item 6 is "[Reserved]"), and Items 1 and 1A of each. Read for the prints: the results
releases of Q4 2017 to Q3 2022 (Exhibit 99.1; the Q4 2018 release, filed without HTML tables, read from its text), the 8-K/A of

was fetched to 2023-01-31 and so includes the Q4 2022 release; it was not downloaded, and nothing from it enters (every source is
published by 2022-10-27). All by Opus directly, with no delegated transcription. The 30 new sources are `CT81`-`CT110` (by publication
date). The records are generated by a script that parses every raw figure from the row or text span it cites and computes every growth
rate, margin and rate; 506 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings, all found (1,519 in all). Decided on
2026-11-11, before any 2018-2022 model was built or any 2018-2022 outcome computed (two text fixes after the first build change no
number: the withdrawal's note no longer says that no later filing restores an outlook, and the vintages' normalization note no longer

  BUY 106, ACCUMULATE 32, WATCHLIST 29, AVOID 94. Robustness: 8 of 8 on 167 dates, 7 on 46, 6 on 22, 5 or fewer on 26 (mid-2020 and
  2022, the class boundaries).
- **2018-2019: the guide and a boom quarter.** With no sales guide, BASE took Q4 2017's +34.7% sales growth (+35.2% to +35.7%/yr with
  the buyback), then +31.4%, +24.2%, +18.9% and +11.7%, so BULL and XBULL lift to it; the multiple fell from 16-19x the $8.75 guide to
  9.8-11.9x the $11.50 guide by late 2018 (2nd-10th percentile, under the 12x floor) and 9.3-11.7x the $12.25 guide in 2019 (0th-11th),
  CHEAP throughout, while the composite fell from 3.2 to 1.8. Through the Q3 2019 print BASE turned negative (-5.1%/yr), and the class
  stayed CHEAP on the multiple (12.3-13.7x $10.84).
- **2020: the withdrawal.** CHEAP in January on the FY19 guide; on the $9.25 FY20 guide the price stood at 13.1-14.9x (FAIR on 4 dates, RICH
  on 2 in February), then 10.3-10.8x in the March fall (CHEAP from 2020-03-13). From 2020-03-27 FY19's $11.06 stands: CHEAP at 9.5-11.3x to
  the Q1 2020 print; then BASE takes the quarter's -19.5%/yr and the class alternates between CHEAP, FAIR and RICH at 9.8-12.4x in May and
  June; RICH on every date from 2020-07-02 (11.5-16.5x, BASE -19.5%, -29.2% and -21.1%/yr; from the Q2 2020 print every signal at BEAR,
  composite 1.15).
- **2021: RICH on a trough anchor.** With no outlook, FY2020's $6.56 stood all year: 27.9-37.2x (the 93rd-100th percentile), 114-186% over
  the 13x floor, RICH and AVOID on every date, although the composite rose to 3.35 on Q2 2021 (Machinery +40.6%, sales +28.9%).
- **2022: FY2021's $10.81 from 2022-01-28.** 15.2-22.2x (49th-89th percentile) with BASE +12.7% to +25.0%/yr from the quarters' growth:
  FAIR on 23, RICH 21, CHEAP 5, moving with the price (and RICH on the 3 January dates, still on $6.56).
- **BEAR leaves 2009 behind:** -61.5%/yr (2009) to 2019-02-13, -36.1% (2016) from the FY2018 vintage (2019-02-14), -42.5% (2020's $6.56
  against 2019's $11.40) from the Q4 2020 print; XBULL is +81.1%/yr (2016-2018) from the Q4 2018 print.

- 2017-2021 at GAAP throughout (no company figures, no restatement; 2016 kept): 55 classes (12 in 2020, 43 in 2022: RICH to FAIR on 19,
  FAIR to CHEAP on 26, RICH to CHEAP on 10) and 67 tiers;

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:

- the Q1-Q3 2019 guides read from the releases' adjusted reconciliations rather than their headline ranges (no class);
- the withdrawal read as voiding the 2020 guide (8 classes);
- the external column read as the Machinery and Engines lines from 2018 (the same basis as before, but no class test was run);
- EV and ENERGY_TRANSITION read as out of scope for an equipment and off-highway engine maker (text only);

### CAT 2023-2026

The same fact sheet, builder and engine, extended; the engine template and rule T are unchanged, and every 2008-2022 model rebuilds
byte for byte (783 of 783) after the builder change below.

```bash
python3 retro/build_cat.py --weekly 2023-01-02 2026-11-08                   # 201 dates, 2023-01-06 .. 2026-11-06
for d in staging/retrospective/CAT/202[3-6]-*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series CAT
for c in 2023-01-01 2023-01-31 2023-02-15 2023-04-27 2023-05-03 2023-06-20 2023-08-01 2023-08-02 2023-10-31 2023-11-01 2024-02-05 \
         2024-02-16 2024-04-25 2024-05-01 2024-06-17 2024-08-06 2024-08-07 2024-10-30 2024-11-06 2025-01-30 2025-02-14 2025-04-30 \
         2025-05-07 2025-06-13 2025-08-05 2025-08-06 2025-10-29 2025-11-03 2026-01-29 2026-02-13 2026-03-27 2026-04-30 2026-05-06 \
         2026-06-12 2026-08-04 2026-08-05 2026-10-29 2026-11-04 2026-11-07; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CAT; done
```

The range starts on the Monday after the last built week, as the earlier ranges did, and has 201 dates. **The last date is 2026-11-06,**
the last complete week: the series was built on Thursday 2026-11-12 before the open, so a rebuild after the close of 2026-11-13 adds the
week of 2026-11-09. The newest dates have no two-year outcome yet.

Read for the history: the statements of results, adjusted-profit reconciliations, the MD&A's sales by geographic region (external
column), the statements of financial position and cash flow, and Items 1 and 1A of the FY2022-FY2025 10-Ks (Item 6 "[Reserved]" in each),
and Exhibit 99.1 of the 8-K of 2026-03-26, which recasts 2024-2025 for the Rail division's move. Read for the prints: the results releases
of Q4 2022 to Q3 2026 (Exhibit 99.1), the dividend 8-Ks, and every other 8-K of November 2022 to November 2026 by its items and exhibits.
Read for the guides: the "Outlook for Key End Markets" and "Company Trends and Expectations" sections of the four 10-Ks and the twelve
10-Qs of 2023-2026. The 10-Qs are new to the CAT series: the releases give no outlook from 2023, and the outlook sections first appear in
the FY2022 10-K (the FY2021 10-K and the 10-Qs of 2021-2022, checked for this, have none, so the 2021-2022 encoding stands). The filing
list was fetched on 2026-11-12; its last filing is the Q3 2026 10-Q (2026-11-04), so nothing after the last date exists in it. All by Opus
directly, with no delegated transcription. The 37 new sources are `CT111`-`CT147` (by publication date). The records are generated by a
script that parses every raw figure from the row or sentence it cites and computes every growth rate, margin and rate; 341 strings were
checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings, all found (1,860 in all). Decided on 2026-11-12, before any 2023-2026 model was
built or any 2023-2026 outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every results 8-K of Q4 2022 to Q3 2026 was accepted before the open (06:31-06:33 ET), and none came on a Friday, so
  each week is dated the next trading day (2023-02-01, 2023-04-28, 2023-08-02, 2023-11-01, 2024-02-06, 2024-04-26, 2024-08-07,
  2024-10-31, 2025-01-31, 2025-05-01, 2025-08-06, 2025-10-30, 2026-01-30, 2026-05-01, 2026-08-05, 2026-10-30). The FY2022 (2023-02-15
  10:27 ET), FY2023 (2024-02-16 10:05), FY2024 (2025-02-14 09:36) and FY2025 (2026-02-13 10:18) 10-Ks and all twelve 10-Qs (08:43-11:08
  ET) were accepted during the session; the recast 8-K (2026-03-26 17:09 ET) after the close, so it is dated 2026-03-27.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it,** a vintage per 10-K (2013-2022, 2014-2023, 2015-2024, 2016-2025) and one
  for the recast; each Q4 print extends the history until the 10-K. The 10-Ks' statements of results give three years, so earlier years
  keep the latest filing that reported them (the ACN FY21 rule); the generator asserts that each new 10-K agrees with the figures already
  in the history for the years both report. The P/E window is the full ten years.
  - **The company's adjusted profit per share** is the ACN-rule figure, as for 2013-2021, each year's items as its Q4 release lists them:
    2022 $13.84 (GAAP $12.64: the Rail division's $925 million goodwill impairment and restructuring costs, other restructuring costs and
    pension and OPEB mark-to-market gains), 2023 $21.21 (GAAP $20.12: restructuring costs including the Longwall divestiture, a deferred
    tax valuation allowance benefit and mark-to-market gains), 2024 $21.90 (GAAP $22.05: restructuring costs including divestitures of
    non-U.S. entities, a discrete tax benefit for a tax law change related to currency translation and mark-to-market gains) and 2025
    $19.06 (GAAP $18.81: restructuring costs and mark-to-market gains). The 10-Ks publish the same figures; no release restates an earlier
    year, and no company figure is a loss.
- **Segments.** From the Q4 2025 release Energy & Transportation is named Power & Energy (`pe_m`, new in the CAT builder), with no
  "formerly" note: the generator checks that the release's year-ago Power & Energy quarter ($6,516 million) is Energy & Transportation's Q4
  2024 as the Q4 2024 release reported it, so it is the same segment and still the Engines line (the 2014 rename precedent). From
  2026-01-01 the Rail division moves from Power & Energy to Resource Industries (8-K of 2026-03-26), and each 2026 release compares with
  its year-ago quarter recast that way, as the print's own comparison shows it (the 2016 redraw precedent); the Q3 and Q4 2025 releases
  likewise restate their year-ago Resource Industries for transfers of responsibilities ($2,954 million for Q3 2024 against the
  $2,934 million the Q3 2024 release reported). The recast 8-K is a vintage of its own (the 2011 and 2016 recast rule): FY2025's history as
  the FY2025 10-K reports it, the bridge's segments as recast (Resource Industries $15.581 billion, Power & Energy $23.747 billion).
- **Guides: none in numbers.** No release from Q4 2022 to Q3 2026 has an outlook, and the 10-K and 10-Q outlooks state the year's sales and
  revenues in words only, which give no field (the UNP 2016 rule) and are shown in the guide line (`rev_words`, from each filing):
  - FY2023: "sales to increase compared to 2022" (FY2022 10-K), then "a strong top line supported by price realization and higher sales of
    equipment to end users" (the Q1-Q3 2023 10-Qs);
  - FY2024: "sales and revenues will be broadly similar to 2023" (FY2023 10-K, Q1 2024 10-Q), "slightly lower sales and revenues as compared
    to 2023" (Q2 2024 10-Q); the Q3 2024 10-Q has no full-year sales statement ("For 2024, we expect continued services growth."), so the
    Q2 words stand;
  - FY2025: "slightly lower compared to 2024" (FY2024 10-K), "about flat" in "a pre-tariff scenario" (Q1 2025 10-Q, beside "down
    slightly" in its alternative scenario), "slightly higher" (Q2 2025 10-Q), "to increase modestly" (Q3 2025 10-Q);
  - FY2026: "to grow around the top end of our 5 to 7 percent compound annual growth rate (CAGR) target" (FY2025 10-K), "growth in the low
    double digits" (Q1 2026 10-Q), "growth in the mid-to-high teens" (Q2 and Q3 2026 10-Qs). The FY2025 10-K's sentence places the year
    against a multi-year target range ("our 5 to 7 percent compound annual growth rate (CAGR) target", which no filing of the period
    sets out), so it is words, like PEP's "towards the upper end of our long-term target ranges" (the LOW rule for multi-year targets);
    "low double digits" and "mid-to-high teens" are words like NKE's "low double digits".
  So the last full year's company figure stands as the current-year EPS (the rollover rule, as for 2021-2022): FY21's $10.81 to 2023-01-27,
  FY22's $13.84 from 2023-02-01, FY23's $21.21 from 2024-02-06, FY24's $21.90 from 2025-01-31 and FY25's $19.06 from 2026-01-30; BASE and
  the growth factor take the latest quarter's sales growth as reported. The outlooks' quarter-only statements, the third-quarter 10-Qs'

  tariff-cost, restructuring-cost, capital-expenditure and tax-rate estimates feed no input.
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the rate: $1.30 a quarter from the 8-K of 2023-06-20 (accepted 06:48 ET, before

## BMY (Bristol-Myers Squibb): the eighteenth ticker, in staging

The BMY series is built apart from ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, AVGO, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT, RCL, MAR, BKR, PFE, CMCSA and CAT and
shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet (`retro/facts/BMY.json`), builder (`retro/build_bmy.py`, the 2008-2009
PFE builder with the distribution, restatement and currency rules below) and engine (`retro/templates/bmy_engine.py.tmpl`, the PFE engine
with Bristol-Myers Squibb's own rule-T thresholds). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker
enters a BMY model, and neither does the live `bmy_signal_model.py` (other branches) or the profile of BMY in `data/business_profiles.json`
(2026 judgements, not read for this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/BMY/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and
their own `SERIES.md`.

```bash
python3 retro/build_bmy.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                   # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_bmy.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                   # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/BMY/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"

Read for the history and the decade's signal values: the statements of earnings, five-year financial summaries, geographic data and
comparability tables of the FY1998-FY2008 10-Ks (the FY1998 and FY1999 10-Ks are plain-text filings) and the restated FY2001 and FY2003
10-K/As. Read for the prints: the earnings releases of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 with their supplemental exhibits (U.S. and international net
sales), every other 8-K of October 2006 to January 2010 by its items and exhibits (the 8-K/As to the releases only add IMS-revised
prescription data, sales trend tables and a segment gross-margin correction), and the 10-Ks for the dividend statements. All by Opus
directly, with no delegated transcription. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the transcribed filing rows: every raw figure is
typed as the row string it appears in, the numbers are parsed from those strings, and every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is
computed, not typed; the 262 strings (every statement, five-year, geographic and supplemental row behind a print, a vintage or rule T,
every guide, dividend, comparability and quoted sentence) were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings. Each source's date
comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (converted from UTC; before 2003 EDGAR gives the filing date only). Decided on 2026-11-12, before any
BMY model was built or any BMY outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** BMY is the NYSE common stock. Yahoo's series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 splits of 1997-03-03 and 1999-03-01 and
  books the Zimmer Holdings spin-off of 2001-08-06 as a 1000000:951777 split on 2001-08-07. None follows 2001, so from 2002 Yahoo's close
  is the price as traded: $26.52 on 2007-12-31 (the fourth-quarter 2007 low in the FY2007 10-K) and $23.25 on 2008-12-31. The spin-off is
  a distribution, not a split (`distributions`, the MAR and PFE rule): its factor is undone for the days before it. Every P/E window here
  starts in 2002, so no model reads a price it moves. No per-share fact in the fact sheet was published before the 1999 split (`splits`
  is empty). The December 2009 split-off of Mead Johnson was an exchange offer, not a distribution to every holder; Yahoo books no event.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year. The four dates of January 2008 before the Q4 2007 print have FY2007 as the current year.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 was accepted before the open or during the session on its release day
  (07:54-10:31 ET), none on a week's last trading day, so each print's week is dated the next trading day: 2008-02-01, 2008-04-25,
  2008-07-25, 2008-10-24, 2009-01-28, 2009-04-29, 2009-07-24, 2009-10-23. The FY2006 10-K was accepted after the close (2007-02-26 17:25
  ET, dated 2007-02-27) and the FY2007 10-K too (2008-02-21 20:40 ET, dated 2008-02-22); the FY2008 10-K before the open (2009-02-20
  06:11 ET). The guide 8-Ks of 2007-12-05 (12:14 ET) and 2009-12-24 (06:07 ET) were public before the close of their own days.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it.** EPS is diluted EPS from continuing operations from the five-year
  summaries: 2002 $1.06, 2003 $1.59, 2004 $1.21, 2005 $1.52, 2006 $0.81 (FY2006 10-K, Medical Imaging and ConvaTec in); from the FY2007
  10-K (Medical Imaging discontinued) 2003 $1.53, 2004 $1.12, 2005 $1.44, 2006 $0.73, 2007 $0.99; from the FY2008 10-K (ConvaTec
  discontinued too) 2004 $1.02, 2005 $1.35, 2006 $0.62, 2007 $0.88, 2008 $1.59, with 2003 from the FY2007 10-K and 2002 from the FY2006
  10-K. Net sales and diluted shares likewise. Seams stay in, as published (the LOW and PEP rule).
  - A Q4 print restates the year before it (`restates`, the PFE 2010-2013 encoding): the Q4 2007 release (2008-01-31) gives 2006 at $0.73
    and $17.256B without Medical Imaging, the Q4 2008 release (2009-01-27) 2007 at $0.88 and $18.193B without ConvaTec; each stands until
    the next 10-K. FY2007 ($0.99, $19.348B) and FY2008 ($1.59, $20.597B) enter from their Q4 prints.

    shares are unchanged; from 2009-04-28 the history cites the recast and the segment bridge shows its segments. The durability "why"
    keeps the FY2008 10-K's words (an 8-K has no Item 1A).
- **GAAP EPS; the company's non-GAAP EPS stays out.** Bristol-Myers Squibb's non-GAAP figures exclude "specified items", which include
  "upfront and milestone payments for in-licensing of products that have not achieved regulatory approval". Those payments are listed in
  every year from 2005 to 2007 ($44 million, $70 million, $162 million; and in 2003, $102 million), a recurring cost of the business, so
  the figure does not exclude only one-offs (the NKE FY2007 and PFE rule). GAAP stands throughout; the non-GAAP ranges are shown in the
  guide line only, and no figure is derived from the reconciliations.
- **2001 excluded; the history and the P/E window start with 2002** (`pe_window_start` 2002-01-01; the ACN FY02, AAPL FY2002 and PFE 2003
  rule). 2001 earned $0.95 a diluted share from continuing operations ($1,866 million, FY2005 10-K), while the items the FY2003 10-K/A
  lists as affecting its comparability (acquired in-process research and development of $2,772 million for DuPont Pharmaceuticals, $588

  under half on the per-share, after-tax reading of PFE 2008. No per-share figure excluding only one-offs was published (no 2002 earnings
  8-K exists, and the 10-K tables give dollars only). The years before it leave with it, so the history is 2002-2006 on the first dates
  (five years) and the window 6.0 years in January 2008, 8.0 years by December 2009. 2002-2008 are kept: each year's listed items after
  taxes are a fraction of its earnings from continuing operations ($512 million in 2002, $358 million in 2003, $972 million in 2004, $551

- **Guides: GAAP EPS in numbers, revenue in words, the fiscal year only.** Every release guides the year's GAAP and non-GAAP EPS from

    operation for the whole year). The 2008 ranges of the Q2 and Q3 2007 releases ($1.60-1.70) exclude specified items, a non-GAAP basis,
    and are shown only (neither is current on any built date);
  - BASE growth and the growth factor: no next-quarter guide and no revenue guide in numbers, so the latest quarter's net sales growth
    excluding foreign exchange, the release's growth less the currency points it states (the NKE and MSFT rule): -1% (Q2 2007: 1% less 2),
    +19% (Q3 2007: 22 less 3), +28% (Q4 2007: 33 less 5), +15% (Q1 2008: 20 less 5), +11% (Q2 2008: 16 less 5; Q3 2008: 14 less 3), then

    quarters of 2006-2007 depressed by the at-risk generic clopidogrel launch, and the releases say so; the figures are used as stated;
  - no margin step: the gross-margin and expense assumptions are words on the non-GAAP basis, so the margin signal takes the latest
    quarter's pre-tax margin change.
  - The "minimum of 15 percent compounded annual growth rate" of non-GAAP EPS from 2007 to 2010 is a multi-year goal, not a current-year
    input (the LOW, XOM and CAT rule). Reaffirmations restate the last numbers (the ACN rule).
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the rate: $0.28 a quarter (FY2006 10-K), $0.31 from the 8-K of 2007-12-05 ("a

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2,** the PFE precedent for a research-based pharmaceutical company. The "why" quotes the latest 10-K: the
  FY2006 10-K's "is engaged in the discovery, development, licensing, manufacturing, marketing, distribution and sale of pharmaceuticals
  and other health care related products", "In the pharmaceutical industry, the majority of an innovative product's commercial value is
  usually realized during the period in which the product has market exclusivity", the risk factor "The Company faces competition from
  other pharmaceutical manufacturers, including from lower-priced generic products" and the PLAVIX patent litigation with Apotex; the
  FY2007 10-K's "global biopharmaceutical" company and its risk that it "may lose market exclusivity of a product earlier than expected";
  the FY2008 10-K's "record level of industry patent expirations and increasingly aggressive generic competition" and PLAVIX at 27% of net
  sales. The kind changes the class label only. No disruption theme in `taxonomy_eras.json` is live for a pharmaceutical company in
  2008-2009 (GLP1, from 2023-08-08, is scoped to snacks, beverages and devices; OFFSHORE to IT services), so the watch list is empty and the
  builder refuses events until a theme encoding is decided. Exclusivity loss is the business's own cycle, not a substitution theme, and
  stays in the "why".

  BioPharmaceuticals and Mead Johnson from the recast), the total from the last year's net sales grown at the BASE rate; the EPS check

are inert, superseded before any built date: the Q2 2007 print's growth, as that print is never the latest, the FY2007 GAAP ranges of the
Q2 and Q3 2007 releases, their FY2008 non-GAAP ranges and the 8-K of 2007-12-05's FY2008 range). A scan of the 105 models for the source
ids, titles, notes, texts and figures (four significant digits or more) of every later print, guide, vintage, dividend and source finds
none before its publication (0 of 8,326 pairs, after dropping 552 strings an earlier fact already carries; two numeric matches are
coincidences: 2008-07-25's 52-week high of $31.42 and 2008-08-15's close of $21.98 equal the pre-tax margins of Q3 2009 and Q3 2008).

AVGO changes nothing (870 models). The firewall (every kind of fact planted after the cutoff with absurd values, including absurd
full-year actuals for the year after the latest vintage, a later print restating every year of the history, a later guide with every
guided field, and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10) changes no model and leaves no planted text at any of the 15 cutoffs above (1
to 105 dates each). All 105 dates pass `retro_tool run`; the 7 dates from 2008-01-04 to 2008-02-15 draw one warning (2011,
the year the FY2006 10-K gives for the expiry of PLAVIX's composition of matter patent, in the durability "why").

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, the PFE set reused for a second pharmaceutical company by a builder who knows that generic clopidogrel and the later
  exclusivity losses dominated Bristol-Myers Squibb's sales (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; 4 classes move at BEAR);
- GAAP EPS rather than the company's non-GAAP figure, on the recurring licensing payments (1 class);
- 2001 taking the history and the window with it, at 49.5% of the EPS without its listed items, a near case (1 class);
- the 8-K of 2009-12-24's guide without Mead Johnson used as published for the last two dates (no class);
- growth excluding foreign exchange read as each release states it, including the quarters lifted by the 2006 generic launch (1 class);
- the recast 8-K of 2009-04-28 read as a vintage (no number changes);
- DURABLE rather than STRUCTURAL or another kind (the class label only), on the 10-Ks' own description of exclusivity loss as the
  business's competition.

         2016-01-28 2016-02-12 2016-04-28 2016-07-28 2016-10-27 2017-01-26 2017-02-21 2017-04-27 2017-07-27 2017-10-26 2018-01-01; do
  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c BMY; done
```

The RICH calls of 2014-2015 rest on the GAAP guides, cut by the impairments, restructuring and upfront payments of those years, against
the stock's own multiples, and no call above moves one; the 2016-2017 classes rest on the GAAP guides after 2015's exclusion, and the
FAIR weeks move with the signals, the 2015 exclusion and the EPS basis.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the distorted-year measure: every specified item, as every BMY test so far, which excludes 2015; without the recurring licensing
  charges 2015 is kept (16 classes, 30 tiers);
- GAAP EPS rather than the company's non-GAAP figure (12 classes and 35 tiers), on the recurring licensing payments;
- the "Worldwide revenues" ranges read as revenue guides although they sit among the non-GAAP assumptions (no class);
- the GAAP FY2014 guide used with the expected gain on the diabetes divestiture, as published (inside the non-GAAP variant above);
- the signals and DURABLE, as in 2008-2013 (60 classes at BEAR, 21 at XBULL).

### BMY 2018-2021

209 weekly dates, 2018-01-05 to 2021-12-31, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The fact sheet only gains facts and the
builder is unchanged (its excluded-year code, added for 2015, carries 2017, 2019 and 2020); the 523 earlier models rebuild byte for byte.

```bash
python3 retro/build_bmy.py --weekly 2018-01-01 2021-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2018-01-05 .. 2021-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/BMY/201[89]-*/ staging/retrospective/BMY/202[01]-*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series BMY
for c in 2018-01-01 2018-01-08 2018-02-05 2018-02-13 2018-04-26 2018-07-26 2018-10-25 2019-01-03 2019-01-24 2019-02-26 2019-04-25 \
         2019-07-25 2019-10-31 2020-02-06 2020-02-25 2020-05-07 2020-08-06 2020-11-05 2021-02-04 2021-02-10 2021-04-29 2021-07-28 \
         2021-10-27 2022-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c BMY; done
```

Read: the 16 earnings releases from Q4 2017 to Q3 2021 with their supplemental exhibits (and the 2021 earnings slides, for any guide in
numbers), the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks (Items 1, 1A, 5, 6, 7 and 8), and every other 8-K of January 2018 to February 2022 by its items and
exhibits, all read directly, none delegated. The source ids are BM66-BM87. The fact sheet's new content is generated by a script from the
transcribed filing rows, as before; the 303 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (1,129 with the earlier
batches', all found). Decided on 2026-11-12, before any 2018-2021 outcome was computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (07:33-08:54 ET) except Q3 2021's, in the session (2021-10-27
  09:46 ET); none falls on a week's last trading day, so each print's week is dated the next trading day (2018-02-06 .. 2021-10-28). The
  Q4 2018 release was filed through an agent (8-K items 2.02 and 7.01, Exhibit 99.1). The 10-Ks: FY2017 2018-02-13 09:26 ET (before the
  open), FY2018 2019-02-25 16:52 ET and FY2019 2020-02-24 16:10 ET (after the close, so dated 2019-02-26 and 2020-02-25), FY2020 2021-02-10
  15:13 ET (in the session). The tax-reform 8-K of 2018-01-05 was accepted 16:41 ET and is dated 2018-01-08; the 8-K of 2019-01-03 that
  gave the 2019 guide with the Celgene merger agreement, 07:58 ET.
- **History: four more vintages, the ten years to the 10-K's year,** each year from the latest filing that reports it: FY2017
  (2008-2017), FY2018 (2009-2018), FY2019 (2010-2019) and FY2020 (2011-2020). Diluted EPS: 2017 $0.61, 2018 $3.03 in the Q4 2018 release
  and $3.01 in the FY2018 10-K (net earnings $4,920 million against the release's $4,952 million), 2019 $2.01, 2020 $(3.99); total
  revenues $20.776B, $22.561B, $26.145B and $42.518B; diluted shares 1,652M, 1,637M, 1,712M and 2,258M (Celgene, acquired on
  2019-11-20 for cash and shares, from that date). No release restates a year in the history.
- **The distorted-year test excludes 2017, 2019 and 2020,** on the measure of every BMY test (the specified items each Q4 release lists,
  after tax, against the year's net earnings): 2017 $4,022M against $1,007M, reported $0.61 0.20 times the $3.01 without them (the $2,911M
  of taxes attributed to U.S. tax reform alone exceeds the year's earnings); 2018 $1,564M against $4,952M (0.76, kept); 2019 $4,596M
  against $3,439M, $2.01 0.43 times $4.69 (Celgene's inventory step-up of $660M, the $808M tax on the Otezla divestiture and, from the
  Q4 2019 release, the amortization of acquired intangible assets, $1,062M, among them); 2020 a loss, $(3.99) against $6.44 ($23,786M of
  items, the amortization $9,688M among them). No figure excluding only one-offs is published (the non-GAAP EPS also removes the recurring
  licensing charges and, from Q4 2019, the amortization), so each leaves the EPS history. Each is the latest year when first excluded,
  so the encoding is the one for a distorted latest year (the Q4 print's `fy_actual` carries no EPS and an `excluded_note`, the vintages
  carry `eps_excluded`, the year's own days leave the P/E window: "10-yr ex-FY15 ex-FY17 ex-FY19 ex-FY20" from 2021-02-05), and each stays
  a gap after (the PFE 2023 rule). The measure is the near call of 2014-2017, and here it moves only 2015 again: without the recurring
  licensing and amortization charges (the release's one tax line allocated pro rata, the PFE 2022-2026 reading) 2015 is kept at 0.80,
  while 2019 stays under half (0.48) and 2017 and 2020 are excluded on any reading.
- **Guides: GAAP EPS in numbers; revenue in words except FY2020,** each field from the latest guide that states it:
  - current-FY EPS, the GAAP range's midpoint: FY2017 $2.41 to the Q4 2017 print, the 8-K of 2018-01-05 saying only that the tax charge
    "will impact" the GAAP guide (words: the last numeric range stands, the ACN rule; 4 dates); FY2018 $3.075 ($3.00-3.15, Q4 2017
    release), $2.75 ($2.70-2.80, Q1 2018), $2.73 ($2.68-2.78, Q2 2018) and $3.10 ($3.05-3.15, Q3 2018); FY2019 $3.80 ($3.75-3.85, the
    8-K of 2019-01-03, confirmed in the Q4 2018 release), $3.89 ($3.84-3.94, Q1 2019), $3.78 ($3.73-3.83, Q2 2019) and $3.51
    ($3.46-3.56, Q3 2019), each excluding the Celgene acquisition; FY2020 $0.85 ($0.75-0.95, Q4 2019, with Celgene and the Otezla
    divestiture), $0.47 ($0.37-0.57, Q1 2020), **$0.015 ($(0.06)-0.09, Q2 2020)** and $0.52 ($0.47-0.57, Q3 2020); FY2021 $3.22
    ($3.12-3.32, Q4 2020), $3.28 ($3.18-3.38, Q1 2021), $2.87 ($2.77-2.97, Q2 2021) and $2.755 ($2.68-2.83, Q3 2021). The Q2 2020 range
    spans a loss; its midpoint is positive, and BMY has always used distorted GAAP guides as published (2012's $1.00 after the impairment,
    2015's $1.01 after the upfront payments), so it is used, at a P/E near 4,000x. No r2 rule covers a guided range that includes a loss;
    reading it as no numeric guide (FY2018's $3.01 standing) is the sensitivity below. The non-GAAP ranges are shown only, and the FY2021
    non-GAAP-only ranges of the Q4 2019 and Q3 2020 releases add nothing;
  - BASE growth and the growth factor: FY2018, FY2019 and FY2021 revenue is guided in words ("increasing in the low- to mid-single
    digits" .. "in the high-single digits"; the 2021 earnings slides say the same), so BASE takes the latest quarter's revenue growth
    excluding foreign exchange, as each release states it (+2% Q4 2017, +1%, +9%, +10%, +12% Q4 2018, +18%, +13%, +7%, +34% Q4 2019, +83%,
    +63%, then +1% Q1 2021 and +13% Q2 2021) or from the supplement's change less its FX column (+75% Q3 2020, +38% Q4 2020, +10% Q3 2021).
    FY2020 is guided in dollars ($40.5-42.5B in the Q4 2019 release, then $40.0-42.0B, $40.5-42.0B and $41.5-42.0B), read as growth on
    FY2019's $26.145B: +53% to +63%, Celgene's full year against six weeks. Acquisitions stay in, as they have since 2008 (SHW's Valspar,
    BMY's Amylin in 2012); so do the growth rates of the quarters that lap the acquisition;
  - no margin step: the gross-margin assumptions are words or non-GAAP percentages (display only).
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the rate: $0.40 a quarter (FY2017 10-K, "In December 2017, our Board of Directors
  declared a quarterly dividend of $0.40 per share"), then $0.41, $0.45 and $0.49 from the FY2018, FY2019 and FY2020 10-Ks, whose text no
  longer states the December declaration: each rate is the fourth quarter's declared dividend in the 10-K's quarterly data ("Cash
  dividends declared per common share | 0.40 | 0.40 | 0.40 | 0.41 | 1.61"). No release states a rate.
- **Signals,** as before, each against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it (the Q4 2019 release restates Q4 2018's pre-tax
  earnings to $1,505 million from $1,547 million). Celgene is in the quarters from Q4 2019, so U.S. revenues rise 42-96% and
  international 21-62% until Q4 2020, and the pre-tax margin swings with the inventory step-up, the amortization and the acquired IPRD
  charges (Q4 2020: -9,280bp).
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2, unchanged.** The FY2017 and FY2018 10-Ks call Bristol-Myers Squibb "a global specialty biopharmaceutical
  company", the FY2019 and FY2020 10-Ks "a global biopharmaceutical company"; the risk-factor headings keep the competition ("We face
  intense competition from other manufacturers." from FY2018), exclusivity and key-product risks. No theme is live for a pharmaceutical
  company through 2021 (EV and CRYPTO, from 2020, are scoped to other industries; GENAI is live from 2022-11-30); the watch list stays
  empty.
- **Segment bridge** (display only): one segment ("We continue to operate in one segment—Biopharmaceuticals after our acquisition of
  Celgene.").
- **Adds nothing:** the Celgene merger's agreements, financing, CVR, exchange offers, regulatory and closing 8-Ks (2019-01-03 to
  2019-11-22, and Celgene's financial statements and pro forma information of 2020-02-05), the 2019 investor-meeting slides of the merger
  (the "more than 40 percent accretive" words), the UPSA and Otezla divestitures (2018-12-19, 2019-07-01, 2019-08-26; their effects are in
  the guides), the MyoKardia acquisition (2020-10-05, 2020-11-17), the COVID-19 fact sheet (2020-03-25), the 2020-2025 long-term targets
  of the 2021 conference slides (a multi-year goal, the LOW, XOM and CAT rule), the debt exchanges and tenders, the Nektar collaboration
  (2018-02-14), and the officer, director, vote and bylaw filings. The 8-Ks from 2022 lie after the range.

Controls: altering one value of each new print (its U.S./international split and its growth excluding foreign exchange, each Q4 print's
full-year revenues and, where the year is kept, its full-year EPS), vintage (its last EPS in the history and its dividend) and guide (its
GAAP EPS range, its non-GAAP range where it gives no GAAP one, its note where it gives neither, each dollar revenue guide and each
revenue guide in words), rerun over the 235 dates from 2017-07-07 (the firewall below covers every earlier date), changes no date before
its publication and changes the first weekly date on or after it: 76 of 79; the other 3 are inert, superseded before their year is
current: the 8-K of 2019-01-03's FY2019 range (the Q4 2018 release restates it when FY2019 becomes current) and the FY2021 non-GAAP-only
ranges of the Q4 2019 and Q3 2020 releases (the Q4 2020 release replaces them). A scan of the 732 models for the source ids, titles,
texts and figures (four significant digits or more) of every fact finds 52 of 557,740 pairs before publication (after dropping 1,364
strings an earlier fact already carries), none a leak: the 39 coincidences of 2008-2017 and FY_REVENUE_B of $22.85B (FY2017's $20.776B
grown by Q3 2018's +10%) in the 13 models from 2018-10-26 to 2019-01-18, equal to Q1 2021's 22.85% pre-tax margin. The firewall (every kind of fact planted after the cutoff with
absurd values, an excluded year and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10) changes no model and leaves no planted text at any of the 24
cutoffs above (523 to 732 dates each). All 209 dates pass `retro_tool run`, with no warning.

Read: the 20 earnings releases from Q4 2021 to Q3 2026 (with the supplemental exhibits of the 2021-2022 releases; from Q1 2023 the
release carries the tables itself), the FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks (Items 1, 1A, 5, 7 and 8), the Q1 2025 10-Q for its dividend statement,
and every other 8-K of November 2021 to November 2026 by its items and exhibits, all read directly, none delegated. The source ids are
BM88-BM114. The fact sheet's new content is generated by a script from the transcribed filing rows, as before: every raw figure is typed
as the row string it appears in, the numbers are parsed from those strings, and every growth rate, margin, test ratio and dividend is
computed; the 363 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (1,492 with the earlier batches' 1,129, all
found). Decided on 2026-11-12, before any 2022-2026 outcome was computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (07:01-08:43 ET). Four fall on a Friday, the week's last trading
  day: Q4 2021 (2022-02-04), Q1 2022 (2022-04-29), Q4 2023 (2024-02-02) and Q2 2024 (2024-07-26); each is dated its release day and
  meets that day's close (the ACN rule, BMY's Q4 2013 and Q3 2014). The others are dated the next trading day (2022-07-28 ..
  2026-10-30). The Q3 2022 release is dated October 25, 2022 and announces the call for "tomorrow"; its 8-K was accepted before the open
  on October 26, and the fact sheet keeps EDGAR's date (the later reading: the week's date is 2022-10-27). The 10-Ks: FY2021 2022-02-09
  11:44 ET, FY2023 2024-02-13 11:54 ET, FY2024 2025-02-12 12:52 ET and FY2025 2026-02-11 11:35 ET (in the session), FY2022 2023-02-14
  16:24 ET (after the close, dated 2023-02-15).
- **History: five more vintages, the ten years to the 10-K's year,** each year from the latest filing that reports it. The 10-Ks have no
  five-year summary (Item 6 reserved), so each supplies the three years of its statement of earnings and EPS note (the ACN FY21 rule):
  FY2021 (2012-2021: 2019-2021 from it, 2016-2018 from the FY2020 10-K, 2015 from the FY2019 10-K, 2014, 2013 and 2012 from the
  FY2018, FY2017 and FY2016 10-Ks), FY2022 (2013-2022), FY2023 (2014-2023), FY2024 (2015-2024) and FY2025 (2016-2025). Diluted EPS
  2021 $3.12, 2022 $2.95, 2023 $3.86, 2024 $(4.41), 2025 $3.46; total revenues $46.385B, $46.159B, $45.006B, $48.300B, $48.194B;
  diluted shares 2,245M, 2,146M, 2,078M, 2,027M, 2,039M. No release or 10-K restates a year's EPS or revenues (the FY2024 10-K recasts
  the U.S. revenues of 2022-2023 for Puerto Rico; totals unchanged).
- **The distorted-year test excludes 2021, 2022 and 2024 and keeps 2023 and 2025,** on the measure of every BMY test (the specified
  items each Q4 release lists, after tax, against the year's net earnings): 2021 $9,860M against $6,994M, reported $3.12 0.42 times the
  $7.51 without them; 2022 $10,206M against $6,327M, $2.95 0.38 times $7.70; **2023 $7,573M against $8,025M, $3.86 0.51 times $7.51,
  kept, the near case** (before tax $9,868M of items against $8,440M of earnings, 0.46; see the sensitivity below); 2024 a loss, $(4.41)
  against $1.15 (the year's $13,373M of Acquired IPRD is in both figures); 2025 $5,491M against $7,054M, $3.46 0.56 times $6.15 (0.60
  before tax). No figure excluding only one-offs is published: the non-GAAP EPS removes the amortization of acquired intangible assets
  ($10,023M before tax in 2021, $3,317M in 2025), which recurs. Each excluded year is the latest year when first excluded, so the
  encoding is the one for a distorted latest year (the Q4 print's `fy_actual` carries no EPS and an `excluded_note`, the vintages carry
  `eps_excluded`), and each stays a gap after (the PFE 2023 rule): the window is "10-yr ex-FY15 ex-FY17 ex-FY19 ex-FY20 ex-FY21" from
  2022-02-04, "... ex-FY22" from 2023-02-03 and "... ex-FY24" from 2025-02-07 (2015 leaves it with the FY2025 vintage). Without the
  recurring licensing and amortization charges (the release's one tax line allocated pro rata, the 2018-2021 reading) 2015, 2021 and

  so BEAR's rule cannot be measured; the engine now takes the AVGO and BKR lines: BEAR is the 0% cap where no one-year change exists,
  XBULL takes every run whose ends are both in the history and is BULL's rate where none exists. The comment states the rule without

Controls: altering one value of each new print (its U.S./international split and its growth excluding foreign exchange; each Q4
print's full-year revenues and, where the year is kept, its full-year EPS, where it is excluded, its exclusion note), vintage (its last
year's EPS or exclusion note, and its dividend), guide (its GAAP and non-GAAP EPS ranges, each dollar and growth revenue guide and each
revenue guide in words) and dividend, rerun over the 280 dates from 2021-07-02 (the firewall below covers every earlier date), changes no
date before its publication and changes the first weekly date on or after it: 109 of 114. The other 5 are inert by design: the exclusion
notes of 2021 and 2022 on their Q4 prints and vintages (a note shows only while the excluded year lies between the last full year and a
current year without a GAAP guide, and FY2022 and FY2023 have one) and the J.P. Morgan deck's FY2022 revenue figure (the Q4 2021 release
restates it when FY2022 becomes current). A scan of the 985 models for the source ids, titles, texts and figures (four significant
digits or more) of every fact finds 467 of 1,087,677 pairs before publication (after dropping years and 78 texts an earlier fact
already carries), none a leak: the coincidences of 2008-2021 and four new ones, each a price or an earlier fact's figure (the 52-week
high of $77.12 in the 53 models from 2016-07-15 and Q2 2022's 77.12% gross margin; FY2020's $2,124M tax provision in the 53 models from
2021-02-05 and Q4 2022's 2,124M diluted shares; 2010-04-16's close of $25.48 and Q3 2025's 25.48% pre-tax margin; 2025-06-13's close of
$49.75 and the Q3 2026 guide's $49.75B). The firewall (every kind of fact planted after the cutoff with absurd values, now with a guide carrying a dollar range, a growth range
excluding foreign exchange, their label and a non-GAAP note, and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10) changes no model and leaves
no planted text at any of the 29 cutoffs above (732 to 985 dates each). All 253 dates pass `retro_tool run`; 145 draw a warning for "2027", "2039" or
"2078", the diluted share counts of 2024, 2025 and 2023 (2,027M, 2,039M and 2,078M) in the share history, which the year check reads
as years. Two slips were caught before the build was committed and are fixed in it: the FY2021 vintage's normalization text first
named the non-GAAP change of 2022-04-18 (`retro_tool run` refused the 10 dates before it), and the engine comment first named the
excluded years of this batch (text in every model's engine, so in the 732 earlier models too; it now states the rule without dates).
