## NVDA (NVIDIA): the nineteenth ticker, in staging

The NVDA series is built apart from ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, AVGO, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT, RCL, MAR, BKR, PFE, CMCSA, CAT and BMY
and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet (`retro/facts/NVDA.json`), builder (`retro/build_nvda.py`, the AVGO
builder with NVIDIA's fiscal calendar, a per-year share basis and words-only guides) and engine (`retro/templates/nvda_engine.py.tmpl`,
the AVGO engine with NVIDIA's own rule-T thresholds and one-year volatility). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or
finding of another ticker enters an NVDA model, and neither does the profile of NVDA in `data/business_profiles.json` (a 2026
judgement, not read for this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/NVDA/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and
their own `SERIES.md`.

```bash
python3 retro/build_nvda.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                  # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_nvda.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                  # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/NVDA/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series NVDA
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-02-14 2008-03-24 2008-05-09 2008-07-01 2008-08-13 2008-08-21 2008-11-07 2008-12-02 2009-01-01 2009-02-11 \
         2009-03-13 2009-05-08 2009-05-20 2009-08-07 2009-08-21 2009-11-06 2009-11-19 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c NVDA; done
```

Read for the history and the decade's signal values: the selected financial data, statements of income and balance sheets of the
FY1999-FY2009 10-Ks (the FY1999-FY2001 10-K405s are plain-text filings) and the FY2006 10-K/A that restated FY2002-FY2006 for the
stock option measurement dates (the FY2004 10-K/A amends Part III only). Read for the prints: the earnings releases of Q4 FY07 to Q3
FY10 and the Q3 FY10 CFO commentary (8-K exhibits), the 10-Qs of Q1 FY07 (its 10-Q/A) to Q3 FY10 for year-ago inventories and their
revenue words, and every other 8-K of August 2006 to February 2010 by its items and exhibits. All by Opus directly, with no delegated
transcription. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the transcribed filing rows: every raw figure is typed as the row string it
appears in (kept in the fact sheet as `rows`), the script asserts that string is in its own filing and parses the numbers from it, and
every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is computed, not typed; the 258 strings (every statement, selected-data, balance-sheet and
segment row behind a print, a vintage or rule T, every guide, word, split and quoted sentence) were checked with `verbatim.py` against
their own filings. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (converted from UTC; before 2002 EDGAR gives the filing date
only). Decided on 2026-11-12, before any NVDA model was built or any NVDA outcome computed:

- **Prices on the AS_OF share basis** (the UNP and AVGO rule). Yahoo's series is adjusted for the two-for-one splits of 2000-06-27,
  2001-09-12 and 2006-04-07, the three-for-two split of 2007-09-11 and the later 2021-07-20 (4:1) and 2024-06-10 (10:1) splits; the
  builder multiplies it by the splits after AS_OF (x40 in 2008-2009), so every price in the window is on the AS_OF share basis: $30.00
  on 2008-01-04 (the close as traded), $8.07 on 2008-12-31, $18.68 on 2009-12-31.
- **The listing rule** (method r2, "A listing inside the window"). "Public trading of our stock began on January 22, 1999." (FY1999
  10-K405), so the P/E window runs from the listing: 9.0 years on 2008-01-04, 10 years from 2008-12-19.
- **Fiscal calendar.** "We operate on a 52 or 53-week year, ending on the last Sunday in January." (FY2009 10-K): FY2008 ended
  2008-01-27, FY2009 2009-01-25, FY2010 2010-01-31; the builder checks every year end the vintages state. The four dates of January 2008
  and the two of early February before the Q4 FY08 print carry FY2008 as the current year, and the days past its end keep its EPS (the
  rollover rule). **NVIDIA has no fiscal 1998**: it reported calendar years to 1997 (a loss), then the one-month transition period of
  January 1998, and its first fiscal year ending in January is FY1999.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of the period was accepted after the close (16:24-16:51 ET) and is dated the next trading
  day: 2008-02-14, 2008-05-09, 2008-08-13, 2008-11-07, 2009-02-11, 2009-05-08, 2009-08-07, 2009-11-06. Five of those are Fridays, the
  week's last trading day, and meet their own close (public before the open; the AVGO rule): 2008-05-09, 2008-11-07, 2009-05-08,
  2009-08-07, 2009-11-06. The others put the week's date on the next trading day: 2008-02-15, 2008-08-14, 2009-02-12. The FY2007 10-K
  was accepted during the session (2007-03-16 14:12 ET); the FY2008 10-K after the close of 2008-03-21, Good Friday, so it is dated
  2008-03-24; the FY2009 10-K before the open (2009-03-13 09:02 ET).
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it,** the ten fiscal years to the latest one (FY1999-FY2007 on the first
  dates, there being no fiscal 1998). EPS is GAAP diluted EPS (NVIDIA reports no discontinued operations). The FY2007 10-K gives
  FY2003-FY2007 as restated for the option measurement dates ($0.15, $0.14, $0.25, $0.82, $1.15); FY2002 comes from the FY2006 10-K/A
  ($0.84), FY2001 from the FY2005 10-K ($0.62), FY2000 from the FY2004 10-K ($0.28) and FY1999 from the FY2003 10-K ($0.04). The
  FY2008 10-K gives FY2004-FY2008 after the three-for-two split ($0.09, $0.17, $0.55, $0.76, $1.31) and the FY2009 10-K FY2005-FY2009,
  FY2004 then coming from the FY2008 10-K. Revenue and diluted shares likewise. Seams stay in, as published (the LOW and PEP rule):
  FY1999-FY2001 are not restated for the option dates (they carry the 2002 restatement of FY2000-FY2002), FY2002-FY2007 are.
  - **Share basis.** A per-share figure is restated for every split effective by AS_OF on a basis before it, the basis being its
    filing's date, except where the fact sheet's `share_basis` says otherwise: the FY2006 10-K/A of 2006-11-29 says "All of the
    information in this Form 10-K/A is as of January 30, 2006 and does not reflect events occurring after the date of the Original
    Filing, other than the restatement", and its figures confirm it (FY2006 $1.65 against the FY2007 10-K's $0.82), so its FY2002 EPS
    and shares are on the basis before the 2006 split, ÷3 in 2008-2009 rather than ÷1.5. The builder carries its own copy of the
    shared split helper with that one field added.
  - A Q4 print extends the history from its release to the next 10-K: FY2008 ($1.31, $4.098B) from 2008-02-14 to 2008-03-21, FY2009
    from 2009-02-11 to 2009-03-12.
- **GAAP EPS; the company's non-GAAP EPS stays out.** Every release's non-GAAP figure excludes stock-based compensation, which recurs
  (the NKE FY2007 and AVGO rule): FY2008 $1.56 against GAAP $1.31, FY2009 $0.53 against $(0.05). No year from FY1999 is a distorted year:
  each year's listed items are a fraction of its net income (the largest, FY2003's $61.8 million stock option exchange charge less its
  $40.4 million of additional Xbox revenue, against $50.9 million restated; FY2004's $16.6 million against $48.6 million).
- **FY2009 is excluded** (the AVGO FY2009 and XOM FY2020 rule: a loss with no figure excluding only one-offs). It lost $(0.05) a share,
  after the $196.0 million warranty charge for the weak die/packaging material set; the only figure without it is the non-GAAP one. As
  the latest year it leaves the EPS history while its revenue and shares stay, its own days (2008-01-28 to 2009-01-25) leave the P/E
  window from 2009-02-12 ("10-yr ex-FY09"), and FY2008 stays the last full year.
- **Current-FY EPS: no EPS guide in any filing,** so the last full year in the history stands (the rollover rule): FY07's $1.15
  ($0.767 after the three-for-two split) to 2008-02-08, then FY08's $1.31 for FY09E and, FY2009 being excluded, for FY10E.
- **Guides: the next quarter's revenue, from the Q2 FY10 release only.** The releases of Q2 FY08 to Q1 FY10 state no outlook: NVIDIA
  gave it on its calls, which are not filings (the AAPL 2020, NKE and MSFT rule), and the 8-K of 2008-07-02 reports the warranty charge
  but not the revenue range of that day's press release, which was not filed. From the Q2 FY10 release each release guides the next
  quarter's revenue as growth on the quarter just reported, read as a dollar level and then against the year-ago quarter from its own
  release (the AVGO and AAPL rule), rounded to 0.1:
  - Q3 FY10: "NVIDIA expects revenue in the third quarter ending October 25, 2009, to be up 5 to 7 percent over the second quarter." on
    Q2 FY10's $776.5M, i.e. $815.3M-830.9M against Q3 FY09's $897.7M: -9.2% to -7.4%;
  - Q4 FY10: "Revenue is expected to be up slightly, approximately 2 percent, from the third quarter." on Q3 FY10's $903.2M, i.e.
    $921.3M against Q4 FY09's $481.1M: +91.5%. The CFO commentary says the quarter is 14 weeks against the usual 13 ("our fourth quarter
    being 14 weeks versus the usual 13 weeks"); the guide is used as published.
  - Before the first guide (to 2009-07-31) no revenue guide in numbers is in scope, so BASE takes the latest quarter's revenue growth
    (the UNP rule). The 10-Qs' and the FY2009 10-K's revenue words are display only (words are not figures): "grow slightly" (Q3 FY09,
    from the Q2 FY09 10-Q), "decline slightly" (Q4 FY09), "remain flat or improve slightly" (Q1 FY10, FY2009 10-K), "increase slightly"
    (Q2 FY10), "increase" (Q3 FY10, after the numeric guide, so the range stands; the ACN rule), "merely increase slightly" (Q4 FY10).
  - The Q4 FY10 outlook's GAAP gross margin (40-42%) and operating expenses (about $305 million) are display only (the AVGO rule).
- **No margin step:** no fiscal-year margin guide, so the margin signal takes the latest quarter's operating-margin change.
- **No dividend:** "We have never paid and do not expect to pay cash dividends for the foreseeable future." (each 10-K).
- **Signals.** The AVGO set, with ACN's weights: revenue growth (0.20), the gross-margin change (0.20), growth of research and
  development plus sales, general and administrative less revenue growth (0.15, lower is better), inventory growth less revenue growth
  (0.15, lower is better) and the operating-margin change (0.15), plus the theme slot at 2/4. Each value is the release's own, against the
  year-ago quarter in the same release; inventories against the year-ago quarter's end from that quarter's 10-Q (a Q4's from the
  release's prior year-end column). Charges stay in, as published (the $196.0 million warranty charge in Q2 FY09's cost of revenue, the
  $140.2 million stock option tender charge in Q1 FY10, the $119.1 million net warranty charge in Q2 FY10); the opex gap takes the two
  expense lines the statement shows, so separately stated restructuring and tender lines stay out of it.
- **Thresholds by rule T over fiscal 2000-2007,** the decade of the FY2007 10-K (the vintage public on 2008-01-04) being fiscal
  1998-2007 and NVIDIA having no fiscal 1998: eight changes between consecutive fiscal years, each from the latest 10-K or 10-K/A
  published by then that reports the lines it needs for both years (revenue and operating income from the five-year selected data; gross
  profit from the selected data where it is given, FY2002-FY2004 from the original FY2006 10-K, the 10-K/A and the FY2007 10-K giving
  none for those years; research and development and sales, general and administrative from the statements of income, FY1999 from the
  FY2002 10-K's selected data, which lists them; year-end inventories from each year's own 10-K or its restatement, with revenue from the
  same filing). The raw figures and values are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives every value and threshold and refuses
  to build if they differ.

  | Signal | Fiscal 2000-2007 | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | revenue growth | 136.67, 96.33, 86.26, 39.43, -4.53, 10.26, 18.19, 29.17 % | -43 / -5 / 34 / 137 % |
  | gross-margin change | 723.0, -76.2, 80.2, -774.9, -115.4, 340.2, 609.0, 407.1 bp | -1760 / -770 / 210 / 720 bp |
  | opex growth less revenue | -47.42, -22.41, -10.98, 8.92, 20.17, 6.77, -16.95, 22.29 pp | 47 / 22 / -2 / -47 pp |
  | inventory growth less revenue | -105.2, 42.58, 50.39, -71.61, 66.02, 24.44, -37.48, 9.99 pp | 115 / 66 / 17 / -105 pp |
  | operating-margin change | 1279.8, 177.5, 22.4, -947.6, -157.4, 200.4, 943.6, 60.5 bp | -2010 / -950 / 120 / 1280 bp |

- **Durability: CYCLICAL, risk 2** (the XOM and BKR precedent). Each 10-K says so of its own business: "Our business is cyclical in
  nature and an industry downturn could harm our financial results." (FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks; the FY2009 10-K: "Our business is
  cyclical in nature and is currently experiencing a severe downturn, which has harmed and may continue to harm our financial
  results."), BKR's "Our business is cyclical" reading, not AVGO's industry wording. The "why" quotes the latest 10-K: the worldwide
  leader in programmable graphics processor technologies (FY2007), then in visual computing technologies and "the inventor of the
  graphic processing unit" (FY2008, FY2009); a market "intensely competitive and ... characterized by rapid technological change,
  evolving industry standards and declining average selling prices"; Intel's platform focus (FY2007) and, from the FY2008 10-K, "the
  possibility of successfully integrating a central processing unit, or CPU, and a GPU on the same chip, as evidenced by AMD's
  announcement of its Fusion processor project"; the FY2009 10-K adds Intel's February 2009 suit over the 2004 patent license. No
  disruption theme in `taxonomy_eras.json` is live for a GPU maker in 2008-2009 (CLOUD from 2012-10-30, scoped to on-premise IT;
  OFFSHORE to IT services; GENAI from 2022-11-30), and none covers a GPU integrated into the CPU, so those words stay in the "why" (the
  PEP obesity rule) and the watch list is empty; whether the registry should carry such a theme is left to the owner. The builder
  refuses events until a theme encoding is decided. The kind changes the class label only.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the vintage's segments (GPU, MCP, Handheld GPU, Consumer Electronics and All Other
  in the FY2007 10-K; GPU, Professional Solutions, MCP, Consumer Products and All Other from the FY2008 10-K), the total from the last
  year's revenue grown at the BASE revenue rate; the EPS check runs on the last year's pre-tax margin and tax rate (FY2009's negative
  margin from the FY2009 10-K, so the check is negative on the 2009 dates while FY08's EPS anchors the scenarios).
- **Adds nothing:** the 8-Ks on the option grant procedures (2007-06-08), the structured repurchase transactions (2007-06-18, 8-K/A
  2007-06-19), the end of the SEC's option inquiry (2007-10-31) and of the DOJ's graphics investigation (2006-12-04, 2008-10-16), the
  PortalPlayer acquisition (2007-01-11), the Santa Clara land purchase (2008-02-06), the warranty charge (2008-07-02; its effect is in
  the Q2 FY09 print), the workforce reduction (2008-09-18; in the Q3 FY09 print), the derivative and antitrust settlements (2008-09-22,
  2008-09-24, 2008-11-10), the bylaws (2009-02-19), and the officer, director and compensation 8-Ks. None changes a guided number.
- **Anachronism list:** NVIDIA names first seen in its filings after the start of 2008 join `taxonomy_eras.json`, each dated from the
  first filing under NVIDIA's CIK that uses it (EDGAR full-text search; after-close filings from the next trading day): Tegra
  (2008-08-13), 3D Vision (2009-02-11), Fermi (2009-11-06), Optimus (2010-02-18), Kepler (2012-02-16), NVLink and Jetson (2014-05-09),
  GeForce NOW (2015-11-06), DGX (2016-05-13), DLSS (2019-02-15), Omniverse (2019-05-17). PhysX (AGEIA's brand before 2008), Mellanox (a
  company long before NVIDIA named it) and Grace Hopper (a person) are left out. No model of any other ticker contains them, and the
  NVDA models use Tegra only from the FY2009 10-K, so no output changes. NVDA's source ids are `NV1`-`NV38`.

Controls: altering one value of each print (its quarter EPS, and each Q4 print's full-year revenue), guide (its quote or words),
vintage (its last EPS year), split and the listing changes no date before its publication and changes the first weekly date on or after
it (25 of 27; the other 2 are inert, superseded before any built date: the Q1 and Q2 FY08 prints' quarter EPS). The Q4 prints' full-year
figures live exactly from their prints to their 10-Ks (2008-02-15 to 2008-03-20, 2009-02-12 to 2009-03-06). A scan of the 105 models for
the source ids, titles, notes, quotes, words and figures (four significant digits or more) of every later print, guide, vintage, split
and source finds none before its publication (0 of 27,362 pairs after dropping 243 tokens an earlier fact or the engine already carries;
84 hits explained: a template phrase every print note carries, 32; the FY2008 10-K's FY2004-FY2007 diluted shares, which equal the FY2007
10-K's times the 1.5 split factor, 48; the January 25, 2009 cash balance the Q4 FY09 release had already published, 4). Rebuilding the
2008 dates of ACN, UNP, LOW, AAPL, NKE, PEP, MSFT, XOM, SHW, WMT, RCL, MAR, BKR, PFE, CMCSA, CAT and BMY and the 2009 dates of AVGO
changes nothing (923 models). The firewall (every kind of fact planted after the cutoff with absurd values, including absurd full-year
actuals for the year after the latest vintage, a later Q4 print excluding its own year, a later vintage excluding a year with a planted
share basis, a later guide in numbers and in words for every guided quarter, a later split on the price data's next split date, and
prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10) changes no model and leaves no planted text at any of the 19 cutoffs above (1 to 105 dates
each). All 105 dates pass `retro_tool run`; their only warnings are digits of decimals (FY01 EPS
0.2067, a segment's $0.2081B) and fiscal-year words ("fiscal year 2009") read as calendar years.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **CHEAP on all 105 dates, legacy tier BUY on all 105, robustness 8 of 8 on every date.**
- **The decade includes the IPO years, and the rules take them as they are.** The history's EPS on the 2008 share basis runs $0.013
  (FY1999), $0.093, $0.207, $0.28 (FY2002), $0.10 (FY2003), $0.093, $0.167, $0.547, $0.767 (FY2007): BEAR is the FY2003 fall (-64.3%/yr,
  the restated FY2002 to the restated FY2003), BULL the FY1999-FY2007 CAGR (+66.0%/yr) and XBULL the FY1999-FY2001 run (+294.2%/yr), so
  the scenario prices on 2008-01-04 are $1.74 / $46.98 / $106.77 / $883.27. The diluted shares grow from 328.7M (FY1999) to 587.3M
  (FY2007) on that basis, so the net buyback is -7.0%/yr and BASE is the quarter's revenue growth less 7.0 points. From the FY2009 10-K
  (2009-03-13) FY1999 leaves the history: BULL is the FY2000-FY2008 CAGR (+39.1%/yr), XBULL the FY2004-FY2006 run (+147.2%/yr), and the
  buyback -2.6%/yr.
- **January 2008 rests on FY07's $0.767.** $24.84-30.00 is 32.4-39.1x (the 44th-54th percentile of a 9.0-year window whose median is
  36.4-36.7x); the floor (the median of the calendar-year lows 1999 14.6x, 2000 14.9x, 2001 24.1x, 2002 24.6x, 2003 33.9x, 2004 18.9x,
  2005 12.9x, 2006 15.4x, 2007 24.7x and January 2008's own) is 21x, $16.10, 54-86% under the price. BASE is +29.0%/yr (Q3 FY08's +36.0%
  less the dilution); the proxy composite is 2.85 (every signal at BULL); Ratio B 0.28-0.37.
- **From the Q4 FY08 print FY08's $1.31 carries the call.** The stock trades at 14.0-18.9x to June 2008 (the 1st-21st percentile),
  against a floor of 15-16x ($19.65-20.96); the 2007 low falls to 14.4x on the new year's EPS. From 2008-07-03 (the warranty charge
  8-K was filed after the close of 2008-07-02) the price is $6.38-13.61, 4.9-10.4x, 31-68% under the floor, to the end of 2008.
- **BASE follows the quarters down and back.** +30.2%/yr (Q4 FY08), +30.0% (Q1 FY09), -11.2% (Q2 FY09: revenue -4.6%), -26.1% (Q3 FY09:
  -19.5%), -65.0% (Q4 FY09: -60.0%; -62.6% on the FY2009 10-K's dilution), -45.0% (Q1 FY10: -42.4%), then the guides: -10.9%/yr (the Q3
  FY10 range, -9.2% to -7.4% YoY) and +88.9%/yr (the Q4 FY10 guide, +91.5% on the trough quarter, 14 weeks against 13). The BASE price
  sits under the price from 2009-02-12 to 2009-05-01 ($5.10-5.74) and is $146-149 from the Q3 FY10 print.
- **2009 rests on FY08's $1.31 with FY2009 excluded:** 5.8-14.3x (the 0th-12th percentile of a window whose median is 28.7-28.8x to
  2009-02-06 and 31.2-31.9x once FY2009's own days leave it), 11-61% under a 14-17x floor ($18.34-22.27).
- **The proxy composite** is 2.85 on Q3 FY08, 2.65 on Q4 FY08 (gross margin +181bp at BASE), 2.50 on Q1 FY09, 1.50 on Q2 FY09 (gross
  margin -2,854bp, the opex gap +32.2pp and the operating margin -3,716bp at BEAR), 1.35 on Q3 FY09, 1.15 on Q4 FY09 (every signal at
  BEAR: revenue -60.0%, inventories +110.0pp over revenue), 1.30 on Q1 FY10, 2.30 on Q2 FY10 and 2.65 on Q3 FY10 (inventories -47.6pp,
  operating margin +561bp).

How far each call moves the classes (the 105 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- the 10-K/A's FY2002 per-share figures read on its filing date's share basis (FY02 $0.56 on the 2008 basis instead of $0.28): 3 classes
  (2008-01-04, 2008-01-11 and 2008-02-01, CHEAP to FAIR), no tier;
- FY2009 kept at the company's non-GAAP $0.53 (in the history and the window, and FY10E $0.53 instead of FY08's $1.31): 18 classes, all
  from 2009-03-27 on (CHEAP to FAIR or RICH), no tier;
- the next-quarter guides unused (the latest quarter's revenue growth throughout): no class, no tier;
- every signal at its BEAR value: 6 classes (2008-01-04 to 2008-02-08, CHEAP to FAIR), no tier; at its XBULL value: none;
- rule T with calendar 1997 standing in for fiscal 1998 (two more changes from the FY2001 10-K's statement of operations; thresholds
  -72/-5/63/643%, -1910/-770/360/720bp, 59/22/-14/-451pp and -2080/-950/190/6460bp, the inventory gap unchanged as no 10-K reports the
  1996 and 1997 year-end inventories): no class, no tier.
The CHEAP calls from the Q4 FY08 print to March 2009 rest on FY08's GAAP $1.31 against the stock's own 1999-2009 P/E history and its
calendar-year lows, which no call above touches; January 2008 moves with the share basis and the signals, and 2009 from late March with
the FY2009 exclusion.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, the AVGO set reused for a second semiconductor company by a builder who knows that NVIDIA's inventories and margins broke
  in 2008 (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; 6 classes move at BEAR);
- rule T over fiscal 2000-2007 without calendar 1997, and the history from FY1999 with its IPO-era growth, which sets BULL and XBULL
  (both mechanical readings of the decade; no class moves with calendar 1997 in rule T);
- the 10-K/A's FY2002 per-share figures read on the Original Filing's share basis (its own words and figures say so; 3 classes move on
  the other reading);
- FY2009 excluded as a loss rather than kept at the company's non-GAAP $0.53, which excludes stock-based compensation, and FY08's $1.31
  carrying 2009 (18 classes from 2009-03-27);
- GAAP EPS rather than the company's non-GAAP figure;
- the Q4 FY10 guide used as published, a 14-week quarter against a 13-week year-ago quarter at the trough (no class moves without the
  guides);
- CYCLICAL rather than DURABLE (the class label only), and no theme for the GPU integrated into the CPU.

### NVDA 2010-2013

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The fact sheet only gains facts: its
2008-2009 content is unchanged and the 105 earlier models rebuild byte for byte after the builder change below.

```bash
python3 retro/build_nvda.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                  # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for c in 2010-01-01 2010-02-18 2010-03-18 2010-05-14 2010-08-13 2010-08-31 2010-11-12 2010-12-08 2011-02-17 2011-03-17 2011-05-13 \
         2011-08-12 2011-11-11 2012-02-16 2012-03-14 2012-05-11 2012-08-10 2012-11-09 2013-02-14 2013-03-13 2013-05-10 2013-08-09 \
         2013-11-08 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c NVDA; done
```

Read: the 16 earnings releases from Q4 FY10 to Q3 FY14 with the CFO commentaries filed beside them, the FY2010-FY2013 10-Ks (Items 1,
1A, 5, 6, 7 and 8), the 10-Qs of Q1 FY11 to Q3 FY14 for year-ago inventories and their revenue words, and every other 8-K of February
2010 to January 2014 by its items and exhibits, all read directly, none delegated. The source ids are `NV39`-`NV71`. 304 more strings
were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (562 with the 2008-2009 batch's 258, all found). Decided on 2026-11-13,
before any 2010-2013 model was built or any 2010-2013 outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted after the close (16:21-16:50 ET) and is dated the next trading day, except two
  accepted before the open of their own day: Q3 FY11 (2010-11-12 06:11 ET; the release is dated Nov 11) and Q1 FY13 (2012-05-11 07:32
  ET). Twelve of the sixteen fall on a Friday and meet their own close (2010-05-14, 2010-08-13, 2010-11-12, 2011-05-13, 2011-08-12,
  2011-11-11, 2012-05-11, 2012-08-10, 2012-11-09, 2013-05-10, 2013-08-09, 2013-11-08); the four Q4 releases are dated a Thursday and


### NVDA 2022-2026

253 weekly dates, 2022-01-07 to 2026-11-06, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The fact sheet only gains facts (an append:
its 2008-2021 content is unchanged), the builder's code does not change (its docstring gains the 2022-2026 paragraph) and the 731 earlier
models rebuild byte for byte.

```bash
python3 retro/build_nvda.py --weekly 2022-01-03 2026-11-08                  # 253 dates, 2022-01-07 .. 2026-11-06
for c in 2022-01-01 2022-02-17 2022-03-18 2022-05-26 2022-08-08 2022-08-25 2022-09-01 2022-11-17 2023-02-23 2023-02-27 \
         2023-05-25 2023-08-24 2023-11-22 2024-02-22 2024-05-23 2024-06-10 2024-08-29 2024-11-21 2025-02-27 2025-05-29 \
         2025-08-28 2025-11-20 2026-02-26 2026-05-21 2026-08-27 2026-11-07; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c NVDA; done
```

## F (Ford): the twentieth ticker, in staging, 2008-2026

The F series is built apart from the other nineteen and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/F.json`), builder (`retro/build_f.py`, the XOM builder with Ford's signals, display-only adjusted EBIT guides and no
Q4 history extension) and engine (`retro/templates/f_engine.py.tmpl`, the XOM engine with automaker signals and Ford's own rule-T
thresholds). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an F model, and neither does a
profile of F in `data/business_profiles.json` (not read for this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/F/`, beside the
others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. **The first series that starts in 2022:** the owner asked for
2022-2026, so the earliest date is 2022-01-07; the history and the P/E window still reach back ten years, from the 10-Ks public on
each date (FY2011-FY2020 on the first dates).

```bash
python3 retro/build_f.py --weekly 2022-01-03 2026-11-08                     # 253 dates, 2022-01-07 .. 2026-11-06
for d in staging/retrospective/F/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series F
for c in 2022-01-19 2022-02-04 2022-04-28 2022-07-28 2022-09-20 2022-10-27 2023-02-03 2023-05-03 2023-07-28 2023-10-27 2023-11-30 \
         2024-02-07 2024-04-25 2024-07-25 2024-10-29 2025-02-06 2025-05-06 2025-07-31 2025-10-24 2025-12-16 2026-02-11 2026-04-30 \
         2026-07-29 2026-10-29 2026-11-07; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c F; done
```

Read: the earnings releases of Q2 2021 to Q3 2026 (8-K exhibit 99), the 10-Qs of Q2 2021 to Q3 2026 (filed the same evenings), the
FY2011, FY2012 and FY2014-FY2025 10-Ks (Items 1, 1A, 5, 6 where present, 7 and 8) for the history, rule T and the durability words,
the Q4 2011 and Q4 2014 releases for the per-share figures they publish, and every other 8-K of July 2021 to November 2026 by its
items and exhibits (7.01 and 8.01 in full where they carry an outlook). All by the session's model directly, with no delegated
transcription. The fact sheet is generated by a script from row strings of the filings: each figure is the row or sentence it appears
in, the script asserts it is in its own filing, and every growth rate, margin change, Q4 value and rule-T value is computed, not typed;
the 368 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (368/368). Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance
time; the source ids are `F1`-`F69`. Decided on 2026-11-13, before any F model was built or any F outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** F is the NYSE common stock. Yahoo's last split is 2000-08-03, so from 2012 its close is the price as traded:
  $24.44 on 2022-01-07 and $12.44 on 2026-11-06.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year. The four dates of January 2022 have FY2021 as the current year and FY20's EPS as its anchor
  (the rollover rule).
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of 2021-2026 was accepted after the close (16:07-16:14 ET) and its 10-Q or 10-K the same evening
  (18:22-20:44 ET), so each print and its filing are dated the next trading day. Five fell on a Thursday, so the week's date is the Friday
  the print became public before the open (2022-02-04, 2023-02-03, 2023-07-28, 2023-10-27, 2025-10-24); the others put the week's date on
  the trading day after it. The 10-K vintages are dated 2021-02-05, 2022-02-04, 2023-02-03, 2024-02-07, 2025-02-06 and 2026-02-11, the
  same day as each Q4 print, so a Q4 print never extends the history (the fact sheet has no `fy_actual`; the builder refuses one).
- **EPS: the company's adjusted EPS, else GAAP** (the ACN rule): diluted EPS adjusted for pre-tax and tax special items (pension and OPEB
  remeasurement, gains and losses on investments such as Rivian and Argo AI, restructuring and other items), each year from the latest
  filing that publishes it; GAAP diluted EPS from the latest 10-K where none is published. Ford's figure keeps stock-based compensation, so
  it excludes one-offs only (unlike NVIDIA's and Bristol-Myers Squibb's non-GAAP figures), and pension remeasurement is a one-off by the
  CAT 2014-2017 precedent. GAAP losses in 2020, 2022 and 2025 have positive company figures, so those years stay (the CAT 2016 rule).
  - **2011 is excluded** (the AVGO FY2018 mirror test). Its GAAP $4.13 (FY2015 10-K, recast for mark-to-market pension accounting)
    includes the $12.4 billion valuation-allowance release the Q4 2011 release lists as a special item, more than the year's $4,485
    million of net income without it; the only per-share figure without it, "pre-tax operating profit ... $1.51 per share", is pre-tax.
    It is the first year of the FY2020 vintage, so the history is 2012-2020 on the four January 2022 dates and the window starts after it
    (2012-01-01, inside the ten years anyway).
  - **2012 stays at GAAP $0.49** (FY2016 10-K's five-year data, recast). Ford's releases to 2013 give "excluding special items" figures
    pre-tax only, and no filing lists the one-offs of the recast 2012 (its pension remeasurement), so the AAPL FY2002 test cannot be met.
    Its days sit at 18-27x in the window to January 2023 (a call: 28 classes, below).
  - 2013 $1.63 and 2014 $1.16: the Q4 2014 release's after-tax earnings per share excluding special items, on the pension accounting
    before the 2015 change (the CAT 2013 rule: the latest filing that publishes a figure for the year). 2015 $1.93 (FY2015 10-K), 2016
    $1.76 (FY2017 10-K), 2017 $1.78 (FY2019 10-K), 2018 $1.30 (FY2020 10-K).
  - Restatements by later 10-Ks: 2019 $1.19 (FY2020 10-K) becomes $1.16 and 2020 $0.41 becomes $0.36 in the FY2021 10-K (2022-02-04);
    then 2021 $1.59, 2022 $1.88, 2023 $2.01, 2024 $1.84 and 2025 $1.09 (GAAP $4.45, $(0.49), $1.08, $1.46 and $(2.06)).
- **Diluted shares** for the buyback term: the first year's from the latest 10-K's EPS note (2012 4,015M, 2013 4,087M, 2014 3,958M,
  2015 4,002M, 2016 3,999M), the last year's from the adjusted EPS reconciliation, which counts dilutive shares in a GAAP loss year
  (2020 4,002M, 2021 4,034M, 2022 4,056M, 2023 4,041M, 2024 4,021M, 2025 4,035M). The term is small and negative to slightly positive.
- **Revenue** is total revenues, each year from the latest filing that reports it (five-year data to the FY2020 10-K; from the FY2021
  10-K, the supplemental tables of Company excluding Ford Credit and Ford Credit, which sum to the total).
- **No guide in numbers.** No release, 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K of 2021-2026 guides EPS, revenue or a current-year margin in numbers:
  Ford guides company adjusted EBIT and adjusted free cash flow in dollars, and states wholesale-volume assumptions and multi-year
  margin targets (8% then 10% adjusted EBIT margin by 2026, Model e margins). So on every date the current-FY EPS is the last full
  year's (the rollover rule), BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth as reported plus the buyback (the UNP rule), and there is no
  margin step. The adjusted EBIT outlooks (25 quotes: each release, the 8-Ks of 2022-01-18, 2022-09-19, 2023-11-30 and 2025-12-15, the
  2023 withdrawal and the suspension in the Q1 2025 release) are display only (the AVGO 2009 and BKR rule); the multi-year targets add nothing
  (the LOW and XOM rule).
- **Dividends,** each regular quarterly rate from the first filing that states it: $0.10 from the Q3 2021 release (2021-10-28), $0.15
  from the Q2 2022 release (2022-07-28). The supplemental dividends declared with the Q4 2022, Q4 2023 and Q4 2024 releases ($0.65,
  $0.18, $0.15) are quoted in the note, not added to the rate: a one-time amount is not a rate (no class moves either way, below).
- **Signals.** The CAT structure on Ford's two businesses, with ACN's weights: wholesale units growth (0.20), Ford Credit earnings
  before taxes growth (0.20), revenue growth (0.15), adjusted EPS growth (0.15) and the change in the company adjusted EBIT margin
  (0.15, the company's published margin, one decimal), plus the theme slot at 2/4. Each value against the year-ago quarter as the 10-Q
  or release shows it. Q1-Q3 come from the 10-Q filed with the release (its key metrics, segment EBIT table and wholesale units; from
  2023 the units of Ford Blue, Ford Model e and Ford Pro, which exclude sales between the segments and sum to the company total). The
  Q4 releases give the quarter's adjusted EPS and margin in text but wholesales (to Q4 2023) only in an image and Ford Credit's EBT not
  at all, so a Q4 value the release does not state in text is the year (its 10-K, public the same day) less the nine months (the Q3
  10-Q); from Q4 2024 the release's text highlights give the wholesale units. The derived Q4 2023 units are 1,153K; the next year's
  release prints 1,152K (no class moves).
- **Thresholds by rule T** over 2011-2020, the decade of the FY2020 10-K, the vintage public on 2022-01-07: each change from the latest
  10-K published by then that tabulates both years, as tabulated (no sums of regions, no levels derived from narrative). A measure the
  filings tabulate for fewer years takes the changes they give (the AVGO rule): Total Company wholesales first appear as one row in the
  FY2014 10-K, Ford Credit's income before taxes is tabulated in the FY2011, FY2012, FY2019 and FY2020 10-Ks only (charts in between),
  and the company adjusted EBIT margin is first published for 2016-2018 (2017's change from the FY2018 10-K's "down 1.4 percentage
  points"). The values and sources are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives the thresholds and refuses to build if they
  differ.

  | Signal | Annual changes | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | wholesale units | 2013-2020: 11.68, -0.11, 4.93, 0.24, -0.66, -9.46, -9.96, -22.26 % | -44 / -22 / 0 / 12 % |
  | Ford Credit EBT | 2011, 2012, 2018-2020: -21.28, -29.41, 13.72, 14.12, -13.01 % | -46 / -29 / -13 / 14 % |
  | revenue | 2011-2020: 5.84, -1.51, 10.0, -1.93, 3.8, 1.5, 3.28, 2.27, -2.77, -18.45 % | -39 / -18 / 2 / 10 % |
  | adjusted EPS | 2013-2020 (the FY2020 history): 232.65, -28.83, 66.38, -8.81, 1.14, -26.97, -8.46, -65.55 % | -122 / -66 / -9 / 233 % |
  | adjusted EBIT margin | 2017-2020: -140, -170, -30, -190 bp | -220 / -190 / -150 / -30 bp |

  The margin decade is four years of decline, so a quarter whose margin falls less than 150bp scores BULL; 2012's GAAP $0.49 sets the
  EPS XBULL at +233%. Both are mechanical readings of what the filings report (calls, below).
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2** (the CAT, SHW and LOW precedent). No 10-K of FY2020-FY2025 calls the business cyclical; the "why"
  quotes the latest 10-K's business description, its industry-volume risk factor ("Industry sales volume ... can be volatile and could
  decline if there is a financial crisis, recession, or significant geopolitical event") and its dependence on "larger, more profitable
  vehicles, particularly in the United States". The kind changes the class label only.
- **Themes: EV on the watch list from the FY2021 10-K.** EV is live from about 2020 and scoped to "battery-electric vehicles displace ICE
  powertrains". The FY2020 10-K names the transition only in its MD&A trends ("other factors that accelerate the transition to electrified
  vehicles, may increase the cost of vehicles by more than the perceived benefit to consumers and dampen margins") and in a risk that the
  EV market develops too slowly for Ford's own investment, so the four January 2022 dates quote it in the "why" with an empty watch
  list. From the FY2021 10-K (2022-02-04) each 10-K's risk factor says "A shift in consumer preferences away from larger, more profitable
  vehicles with internal combustion engines ... to battery electric or other vehicles in our portfolio that may be less profitable could
  result in an adverse effect", so EV is on the watch list, company-acknowledged, in the latest 10-K's words (the MSFT CLOUD and XOM
  rule; event kind `ev_company_acknowledged`). It is never re-filed: the registry's market-pricing evidence (Tesla joining the S&P 500)
  names no Ford fact, and no press coverage was picked by hand (the ACN, WMT and CMCSA reading). The factor pair nets to zero and the
  theme slot stays at 2/4: text only. GENAI (from 2022-11-30) stays off: the 10-Ks name artificial intelligence only as regulation and
  Ford's own driver-assist features.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the vintage's revenue lines (Automotive, Ford Credit and Mobility in the FY2020 10-K;
  Company excluding Ford Credit and Ford Credit from the FY2021 10-K), the total from the BASE revenue rate; the EPS check runs on the
  adjusted EBIT margin and the adjusted effective tax rate (FY2020's is negative, so its check is not meaningful).
- **Adds nothing:** the segment recasts (8-K of 2023-03-23) and the Capital Markets Day (2023-05-22) beyond their reaffirmed outlooks;
  the multi-year targets (2022-03-02, 2022-07-21); the EV program and impairment 8-Ks (2024-08-21, 2025-12-15: their charges reach the
  prints as special items, outside adjusted EPS); the monthly U.S. sales 8-Ks; the debt, credit-facility, officer, director and vote 8-Ks.
- **Anachronism list:** Ford names first used after the series starts join `taxonomy_eras.json`, each dated from the first Ford filing
  that uses it (EDGAR full-text search; after-close filings from the next trading day): Ford Next (2022-02-04), Model e (2022-03-02),
  Universal EV Platform (2025-12-16), Ford Energy (2026-02-11). No model of any ticker contains them before those dates.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):

- **Leak scan:** 0 hits in 64,432 (model, later token) pairs: the source ids, quotes, notes and figures (four significant digits or more)

  The releases of 2007-2011 state it every quarter (the "After-tax results" and "Earnings per share" rows of their summaries), so the 2022
  section's "releases to 2013 give figures excluding special items pre-tax only" does not hold for 2007-2011; that series was not revisited.
  - **2001 is excluded and takes the years before it** ($(0.44) excluding unusual items, Q4 2002 release; the PFE 2003 rule for an excluded year
    that is not the latest), so every vintage's history starts in 2002 and the P/E window on 2002-01-01 (`pe_window_start`). That also keeps
    the window after Ford's 2000-08-03 recapitalization, whose prices Yahoo adjusts.
  - **2006, 2007 and 2008 are losses even on the company's figure** ($(1.50) then $(1.44); $(0.19) then $(0.21); $(3.13) then $(3.20)) and

    excluded as the latest year when its Q4 print comes and stays a gap after (the NKE FY2018, XOM FY2020 and PFE 2023 rule); its notes follow
    the latest figure (`excluded_updates`). The last full year in the history is therefore **2005's $1.00 from 2008-01-04 to 2011-01-27**.
  - **A year excluded for want of a positive figure re-enters when a later filing publishes one** (`readmits`, new; decided before 2011 was

  decimal); the summary's figure excludes special items, which from 2008 include Jaguar Land Rover's and in 2010 Volvo's revenue in the current
  year only. The margin signal is **the GAAP pre-tax margin change** (pre-tax income from continuing operations on that revenue; the XOM measure):

  as a planning metric). Ford Credit's pre-tax result is the release's (text to Q1 2008, tables after); a change over a base that is not
  positive has no value and scores BASE (the RCL rule; `fc_note`). Wholesales are the summary's, excluding special items, against the year-ago
  quarter as shown. EPS growth is the company's figure; over a base that is not positive it has no value.

  open), FY2015 2016-02-11 (before the open), FY2016 2017-02-09 (before the open), FY2017 2018-02-08 (during the session). Each Q4 print
  extends the history to its 10-K, as before.
- **EPS: the company's figure excluding special items** ("adjusted EPS" from the FY2016 10-K; the same definition), each year from the latest
  filing that publishes it: 2014 $1.16 (Q4 2014 release; GAAP $0.80), 2015 $1.93 (Q4 2015 release, then the FY2015 10-K), 2016 $1.76 (Q4
  2016 release, the FY2016 and FY2017 10-Ks), 2017 $1.78 (Q4 2017 release, the FY2017 10-K). 2006-2008 stay gaps and 2009 stays at $0.01
  (the 2008-2011 decisions). Each 10-K's ten years start one year later, so from the FY2015 vintage (2016-02-11) the first year with an EPS
  is 2009.
  - **A later filing's figure for an earlier year restates it until a vintage published after it** (`restatements_r2008`, the CAT
    `restates` encoding, EPS only): the Q4 2014 release gives 2013 as $1.63 ($1.62 in the Q4 2013 release) from 2015-01-29 to 2015-02-12.
  - **Mark-to-market pension accounting.** The 8-K of 2016-01-07 (before the open) reports that Ford adopted immediate recognition of pension
    and OPEB remeasurement gains and losses on 2015-12-31, applied retrospectively, and revises 2013 and 2014: "Memo: Diluted earnings per
    common share excluding special items" $1.86 and $1.34 (GAAP $2.94 and $0.31). These replace $1.63 and $1.16 from 2016-01-07 (the
    restatement record) and in every later vintage (the 8-K is the latest filing that publishes them); 2009-2012 stay on the earlier
    accounting, a seam (the CAT 2016 precedent). The remeasurement is a special item, so the company figure excludes it.
- **The first EPS guides in numbers** (`eps_guides_r2008`; the CAT encoding: the latest guide for the current year, its midpoint is the year's
  EPS): "2017: Expect full year adjusted EPS of $1.65 to $1.85" (Q2 2017 release, 2017-07-26; the 10-Q: "Effective this quarter, we are
  modifying our approach to Company guidance, adopting a range of adjusted earnings per share"), $1.75-1.85 (Q3 2017 10-Q, the same day as
  the release, whose page with the range is an image), the preliminary 2017 result of $1.78 in the 8-K of 2018-01-16 (after the close, so
  2018-01-17; recorded as a guide until the Q4 2017 print, the SHW rule), 2018 $1.45-1.70 (the same 8-K; current from the Q4 2017 print,
  2018-01-25) and $1.30-1.50 (Q2 2018 release). Reaffirmations of an unchanged range (the 8-Ks of 2017-10-18, 2018-05-09, 2018-05-16 and
  2018-09-06, the Q4 2017 and Q1 2018 releases, the FY2017 10-K and the Q3 2018 release) add nothing. The 8-K of 2017-03-23 gives a first-
  quarter 2017 EPS range ($0.30-0.35): CAT's encoding takes fiscal-year guides only, so it adds nothing. Revenue guides stay in words
  ("Flat To Modestly Higher Than 2017"), so BASE takes the latest quarter's revenue growth on every date, as before; the total company pre-tax
  profit outlooks in dollars of 2015-2017 stay unencoded (the 2012-2014 decision).
- **Release layouts and Q4 values.** The 2015 releases print the year-ago figure in their tables but only the change in their summaries; the
  2016-2018 releases print the GAAP income statement (revenue and pre-tax in millions from Q2 2016) and summaries with changes only. A
  year-ago figure the release states as a change is the current figure less it (computed). Two releases print figures only in images, read
  as images: Q4 2015 (pre-tax $1,896M against the revised $(3,963)M, Ford Credit $556M against $423M, GAAP EPS $0.47, diluted shares 4,002M,
  the year's pre-tax and tax), each checked against the FY2015 10-K's text (quarterly data, the EPS calculation, Ford Credit's $2,086M less the
  Q3 2015 release's nine months); and Q3 2017 wholesales (1,504K, B/(W) (26)K), which the Q4 2017 presentation's 6,607K for the year less its
  quarters confirms. Ford Credit's Q4 2016 and Q4 2017 pre-tax are the year less the nine months ($398M: the FY2015 10-K's $2,086M plus the
  Q4 2016 release's $(207)M, less the three 2016 quarters as their releases state them; $610M and its year-ago $398M: the Q4 2017 release's
  Ford Credit statement less the Q3 2017 release's). The Q3 2018 release's text layer is glyph-encoded, so its statements come from the 10-Q
  filed the same evening and wholesales and adjusted EPS from the presentation. A year-ago GAAP EPS the release does not state is the latest
  earlier filing's (display only).
- **Cash** (display only): Automotive gross cash to Q3 2015, Automotive cash from Q3 2016 (the release, else the 10-Q filed the same day),
  Company cash in 2018 (the 10-Qs); "n/r" where no filing of the day states one (Q4 2015 to Q2 2016, Q4 2017). The 10-Ks' cash-flow measure
  is "Automotive operating cash flow" from FY2016.
- **Dividends:** $0.15 a quarter from the Q1 2015 release (2015-04-28: "Raised first quarter dividend by 20 percent to 15 cents per share";
  no earlier filing states the January 2015 declaration), unchanged in the 8-Ks of 2016-01-12, 2017-01-10 and 2018-01-16 (after the close, so
  2016-01-13, 2017-01-11 and 2018-01-17), which also declare supplemental dividends of $0.25, $0.05 and $0.13: not a rate (the 2022 rule).
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2,** and no theme on the watch list: EV is live from about 2020, so the 10-Ks' risk factors on a "Market shift

  vehicles" (FY2017) stay in the "why". The FY2015 and FY2016 10-Ks call Ford "a global automotive and mobility company", the FY2017 10-K "a
  global company"; the "why" quotes each.

```bash
python3 retro/build_f.py --weekly 2018-12-31 2021-12-31                     # 157 dates, 2019-01-04 .. 2021-12-31
```

## SO (Southern Company): the twenty-first ticker, in staging, 2008-2026

The SO series is built apart from the other twenty and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/SO.json`), builder (`retro/build_so.py`, the F early-era builder with BMY's `distributions` rule) and engine
(`retro/templates/so_engine.py.tmpl`, the F early-era engine with electric utility signals and Southern Company's own rule-T thresholds).
The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an SO model, and neither does the profile of SO in
`data/business_profiles.json` (a 2026 judgement: not read for this series, and first seen by the builder after the build). Outputs go to
`staging/retrospective/SO/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009, then
2010-2013, 2014-2017, 2018-2021 and 2022-2026 ("SO 2010-2013", "SO 2014-2017", "SO 2018-2021" and "SO 2022-2026", below); this part
describes the 2008-2009 build.

```bash
python3 retro/build_so.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2009-12-31                    # 105 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/SO/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series SO
for c in 2008-01-30 2008-02-25 2008-04-30 2008-05-07 2008-07-01 2008-07-30 2008-10-23 2009-01-01 2009-01-28 2009-02-25 2009-04-29 \
         2009-05-08 2009-07-29 2009-10-28 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c SO; done
```

overview), the Southern Company sections of the combined FY1998-FY2008 10-Ks (selected financial and operating data, the statements of
income and cash flows, the segment note, Items 1, 1A and 5) and the two FY2005 10-K/As (they correct a contractual-obligations table and
add certifications: nothing used), the Q1 2007-Q3 2009 10-Qs for the dividend, and every other 8-K of July 2007 to January 2010 by its items
(directors and officers, financing, rate-case and litigation notices, the Vogtle 3 and 4 and leveraged-lease 8-Ks, the 2009-04-02 MC Asset
Recovery settlement, a NYSE notice): none guides a number. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows: each
figure is read from the row it appears in, by its label under an anchored heading, the row is asserted present in its own filing, and every
growth rate, margin, margin change and rule-T value is computed, not typed; 297 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own
filings (297/297). Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (before 2003 EDGAR records the filing date only); the source ids are
`SO1`-`SO24`. Decided on 2026-11-15, before any SO model was built or any SO outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** SO is the NYSE common stock. Yahoo's 2-for-1 split of 1994 precedes every per-share fact. Yahoo books the Mirant
  spin-off ("the tax-free distribution of Mirant shares was completed at a ratio of approximately 0.4 for every share", FY2001 10-K) as a
  10000:6109 split on 2001-04-03, the first day without it: a distribution, not a split, so its factor is undone for the days before (the
  MAR, PFE and BMY `distributions` rule) and the close is the price as traded: $38.71 on 2008-01-04. Unlike BMY's, these windows reach back
  before the spin-off (1998-01 on the first date, 1999-12 on the last), so the days to 2001-04-02 carry Mirant's value against EPS from
  continuing operations, which excludes it (the MAR judgement call; its reach is measured below). The FY2001 10-K's own price table is
  "adjusted to give effect to the Mirant spin off"; the frozen rule is kept all the same.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year. The four dates of January 2008 have FY2007 as the current year and FY06's EPS as its anchor.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 was accepted on the release day before the open or during the session
  (08:29-10:29 ET), always a Wednesday or Thursday, so each week's date is the next trading day (2008-01-31, 2008-05-01, 2008-07-31,
  2008-10-24, 2009-01-29, 2009-04-30, 2009-07-30, 2009-10-29). The 10-Ks came weeks later: FY2006 accepted 2007-02-26 18:11 ET (dated
  2007-02-27), FY2007 2008-02-25 12:28 ET, FY2008 2009-02-25 13:54 ET. So **a Q4 print extends the history** (`fy_actual`, the F early-era
  encoding) from its release to the 10-K, with the release's basic EPS (the only full-year figure it gives: "diluted earnings per share ...
  not more than 1 cent per share" different) and no diluted share count (the shares history waits for the 10-K).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations where the 10-K reports the line, else diluted EPS** (the LOW and UNP rule), each year
  from the latest 10-K that reports it. 1997-2000 exclude Mirant (discontinued operations from the FY2000 10-K): $1.45, $1.41, $1.33, $1.52;
  then 2001 $1.61, 2002 $1.85, 2003 $2.03 (FY2006 10-K; $2.02 from the FY2007 10-K, whose selected data report diluted EPS with no
  continuing-operations line), 2004 $2.06, 2005 $2.13, 2006 $2.10, 2007 $2.28, 2008 $2.25.
  - **The company's figures stay out until they exclude only one-offs.** Its releases give EPS "excluding synthetic fuels" (2006 $2.10,
    2007 $2.21) and, from Q2 2008, "excluding items": the leveraged lease charges ($67 million in Q2 2008, $83 million for 2008) together
    with synthetic fuels (FY2008 $2.37). Synthetic fuel investments contributed every year until their tax credits expired on
    2007-12-31: an ongoing operation, not a one-off, so these figures do not exclude only one-offs (the AAPL 2008, NKE FY2013 and BMY rule)
    and GAAP stands; the notes keep them. From the Q1 2009 release the figure excludes only one-offs (the $202 million MC Asset Recovery
    settlement; in its 2008 comparisons only the leveraged lease charge), so the quarterly EPS signal uses it from that print. The Q4 2008
    release's FY2008 $2.37 also excludes synthetic fuels, so the Q4 2008 print keeps GAAP $2.26 basic; the FY2008 10-K's key performance
    indicators give "EPS, excluding leveraged lease charges | — | 2.37", so FY2008 is $2.37 from 2009-02-25 (corrected on 2026-11-15: this
    section first said no filing public in 2009 gave that figure and kept GAAP $2.25; see below and "SO 2010-2013"). No year is excluded; no
    window starts late.
- **No guide in numbers.** No release, 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K of 2007-2009 guides EPS, revenue or a margin in numbers: each release says the
  CEO and CFO "will discuss earnings and earnings guidance" on the analyst call, and no transcript or slides are filed (the UNP 2008 reading
  of a call: a later date can only lag). So on every date the current-FY EPS is the last full year's (the rollover rule), BASE is the
  latest quarter's total revenue growth as reported plus the buyback (the UNP rule), and there is no margin step. The 10-K's dividend
  payout target ("approximately 70 to 75 percent of net income, excluding earnings from synthetic fuel businesses", then 70%, then 65% to
  70%) is a policy, not a guide, and stays in the dividend note.
- **Dividends,** each regular quarterly rate from the first filing that states it: 38.75 cents (FY2006 10-K: "In January 2007, Southern
  Company declared a quarterly dividend of 38.75 cents per share"), $0.4025 (Q1 2007 10-Q, 2007-05-07), 40.25 cents (FY2007 10-K), $0.42
  (Q1 2008 10-Q, 2008-05-07), 42 cents (FY2008 10-K), $0.4375 (Q1 2009 10-Q, accepted 2009-05-07 17:28 ET, so 2009-05-08). The April
  increases were announced without an 8-K, so each is dated by the 10-Q (this can only lag).
- **Signals.** The F structure on a utility's own lines, with ACN's weights: retail kilowatt-hour sales growth (0.20, as reported, the
  release's "Total Retail Sales" change; the weather-adjusted figure from Q4 2007 is display only), the electric utilities' net income growth
  (0.20, the release's "Total" of the traditional operating companies and Southern Power, which is the 10-K's electric utility segment),
  revenue growth (0.15, total revenues), EPS growth (0.15, basic EPS as the release gives it, on the basis above) and the change in the
  operating margin (0.15, operating income on total revenues, the release's consolidated earnings account), plus the theme slot at 2/4. Each
  value against the year-ago quarter as the release shows it. Customer growth, the natural utility volume, has no quarterly value in the
  releases, so it is text only.
- **Thresholds by rule T over 1997-2006,** the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04: each change from the latest 10-K
  published by then that tabulates both years, as tabulated. The segment is "Integrated Southeast Utilities" in the FY1998-FY1999 10-Ks and
  "Electric Utilities" from FY2000 (its 1999 net income is $1,073 million in both); from the FY2003 10-K its total is the traditional
  operating companies plus Southern Power. 1998's margin change comes from the FY1999 10-K, which still consolidated Southern Energy (later
  Mirant), and the FY1998 10-K's "Operating Income" is after income taxes (the old utility format), a different measure, so the margin has
  1998-2006 only (the AVGO rule). Seams stay in, as published. The values and sources are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder
  re-derives the thresholds and refuses to build if they differ.

  | retail kWh sales | 1997-2006: 1.08, 6.2, 1.73, 4.33, -3.22, 4.5, -0.18, 3.64, 1.23, 1.42 % | -8 / -3 / 2 / 6 % |
  | electric utilities net income | 1997-2006: 1.75, -1.99, -0.92, 3.36, 3.61, 12.79, 9.88, -0.21, 6.47, 4.82 % | -7 / -2 / 3 / 13 % |

  | operating margin | 1998-2006: -87.5, 15.7, -26.8, -34.7, 153.8, 51.8, -157.9, -219.8, 60.4 bp | -410 / -220 / -30 / 150 bp |

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2** (the CAT, SHW and LOW precedent). The "why" quotes each 10-K: Southern Company "owns all of the outstanding
  common stock of Alabama Power, Georgia Power, Gulf Power, and Mississippi Power, each of which is an operating public utility company";
  "Southern Company and its subsidiaries are subject to substantial governmental regulation"; the operating results "are affected by weather
  conditions"; and its risk factor on laws "related to global climate change" (FY2006) or "designed to address global climate change" (FY2007
  and FY2008). No theme in the registry is live for an electric utility on these dates (ENERGY_TRANSITION, scoped to reserves and refining,
  from 2015-12-12), so the watch list is empty, the climate words stay in the "why" (the PEP obesity rule) and the builder refuses events. The
  kind changes the class label only.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the vintage's operating revenue lines (residential, commercial, industrial, other retail,
  sales for resale, renamed wholesale from the FY2007 10-K, other revenues), the total from the BASE revenue rate; the EPS check runs on the
  last year's pre-tax margin (after interest, material for a utility) and tax rate, on the release's average shares.
- **Adds nothing:** the FY2005 10-K/As, the board, officer and compensation 8-Ks, the debt and equity offering 8-Ks, the rate-case and
  regulatory notices (Georgia Power's rate cases and accounting order, Alabama Power's PSC decision), the Vogtle 3 and 4 8-K of 2008-04-14,
  the leveraged lease court decision of 2008-06-26 (its charges reach the prints), the MC Asset Recovery settlement 8-K of 2009-04-02 (its
  charge reaches the Q1 2009 print), the SFAS No. 160 recast of 2009-05-08 (it restates no EPS: diluted $2.25, $2.28 and $2.10, as in the FY2008
  10-K) and the NYSE notice of 2009-10-16.

### SO 2010-2013: four more vintages, the company's figures excluding one-offs, Kemper, and a correction to 2009

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31, on the same fact sheet, builder, engine and method (r2), with the 1997-2006 rule-T thresholds
frozen. Built on 2026-11-15, after the 2008-2009 dates had been scored (their findings are hindsight and were not read for any decision
below; each decision applies a rule that existed before, and the one correction to 2009 is a fact that was missed, not a rule changed).

```bash
python3 retro/build_so.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                    # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/SO/201[0-3]-*/; do

  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series SO
for c in 2008-01-30 2008-07-01 2009-01-28 2009-02-25 2009-04-29 2009-05-08 2009-07-29 2009-10-28 2010-01-01 2010-01-27 2010-02-26 \
         2010-04-28 2010-05-07 2010-07-28 2010-10-27 2011-01-01 2011-01-26 2011-02-25 2011-04-01 2011-04-27 2011-05-09 2011-07-27 \
         2011-10-26 2012-01-01 2012-01-25 2012-02-27 2012-04-25 2012-05-07 2012-07-25 2012-11-05 2013-01-01 2013-01-30 2013-02-28 \
         2013-04-24 2013-05-10 2013-07-31 2013-10-30 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c SO; done
```

  FY2006 and FY2007 charts exclude synthetic fuels (an ongoing operation), so 2006 and 2007 stay at GAAP.

- **No guide in numbers, as before.** Each release points to earnings slides on the website ("including its earnings guidance for 2018",
  "including its updated earnings guidance for 2018", "including its earnings guidance for 2019", "including earnings guidance for 2021",
  "including long-term earnings guidance", "including earnings guidance"); the Q4 2019 8-K's item 7.01 and the Q4 2019, Q2 2021 and Q3 2021
  call words name guidance too. None of it was filed: website posts and calls add nothing (the XOM, NKE and MSFT rule); the guide line now
  also quotes call words that name guidance.
- **GAAP for every quarter's EPS signal.** Every release's "Excluding Items" also removes Wholesale Gas Services (an ongoing business, its
  mark-to-market volatility; in Q3 2021 only in the year-ago column) and, to Q4 2017, the Kemper
  schedule-extension equity return: not only one-offs, so GAAP stands, as from Q3 2016. The releases' figures are in each print's note.
- **FY2017 is excluded, a distorted year with no figure excluding only its one-offs** (the AAPL FY2002 test and the NKE FY2018 encoding):
  GAAP $0.84 a diluted share after the Kemper charges ($3,366M pre-tax for the year); the one-offs exceed the year's $842M net income, and the
  company's $3.02 also excludes Wholesale Gas Services and the Kemper equity return. It leaves the EPS history (`eps_excluded`) from the
  FY2017 10-K; its revenue, shares and margins stay; its own days leave the P/E window ("10-yr ex-FY17"); EPS growth is measured only between
  years in the history; and the rollover's last full year is the last in it, so FY16's GAAP $2.55 stands for FY2018E until the Q4 2018
  print. The builder gains F's early-era encoding of an excluded year (no earlier output changes).
- **FY2018-FY2020 at GAAP diluted from the 10-Ks:** $2.17 (the Vogtle charge of $1.1 billion pre-tax in it), $4.50 and $2.93. FY2019 carries
  the "$2.6 billion pre-tax ($1.4 billion after tax) gain associated with the sale of Gulf Power" (FY2019 10-K); the mirror test (one-off
  benefits larger than the year's income without them) is not met, as the gain is under the $4,739M net income less it, so the year stands
  at GAAP, and $4.50 anchors every 2020 date. BEAR becomes -34.9%/yr (2020 against 2019) from the FY2020 10-K.
- **Growth against a year-ago loss is measured over the loss's absolute value** (the CAT 2014-2017 rule): Q2 2018's EPS and segment (against
  Q2 2017's Kemper loss) read +89.1% and +98.1%, Q2 2019's (against Q2 2018's Vogtle loss) +673.3% and +3,776.9%. No class moves on the
  plain ratio.
- **The Gulf Power sale (2019-01-01) and the 2018 gas dispositions stay in the comparisons, as published**: revenue, retail kWh and the
  segment of the 2019 prints compare a quarter without Gulf Power to one with it, and Q3 2018 to Q2 2019 a year-ago quarter with
  Elizabethtown, Elkton and Florida City Gas (`sales_note`). The 2019 releases' adjusted kWh comparison without Gulf Power is shown, not used
  (`kwh_note`: no class moves on it). Q1 2019's operating income includes the $2,497M gain, so its margin reads +4,661bp.
- **Vintages.** Each 10-K was accepted the evening before its Q4 release (FY2017 2018-02-20 21:22 ET, FY2018 2019-02-19 18:34 ET, FY2019
  2020-02-19 17:55 ET, FY2020 2021-02-17 17:48 ET), so the Q4 prints carry no full-year actuals. The FY2020 10-K has no selected data (Item 6

- **Dividends** from the second-quarter 10-Qs: $0.60 (2018-08-08), $0.62 (2019-07-31), $0.64 (2020-07-30), $0.66 (2021-07-29), each the
  first filing to state the April rate (the first-quarter 10-Qs do not); January rates from the 10-Ks (58, 60, 62 and 64 cents).

  legislation and regulation"), quoted with the lead-in "among its risk factors" (`transition_intro`). The theme's registered

### SO 2022-2026: the FY2022 guide, the company's figure again from Q3 2022, the energy transition out of scope

254 weekly dates, 2022-01-07 to 2026-11-13, on the same fact sheet, builder, engine and method (r2), with the 1997-2006 rule-T thresholds
frozen. Built on 2026-11-17 at the owner's request ("Do 2022-2026"), after the 2008-2021 dates had been scored; their findings were not
read for any decision below, each of which applies a rule that existed before. The last date is 2026-11-13: the price data end on
2026-11-16, inside an unfinished week.

```bash
python3 retro/build_so.py --weekly 2022-01-01 2026-11-15                    # 254 dates, 2022-01-07 .. 2026-11-13
for d in staging/retrospective/SO/202{2,3,4,5,6}-*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
```

Filings read: the FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks (SO97-SO101), the twenty earnings 8-Ks of Q4 2021 to Q3 2026 (SO102-SO121: Exhibits 99.01-99.07 to
Q4 2023, one Exhibit 99 from Q1 2024), the Q2 10-Qs of 2022-2026 (SO122-SO126) and the Q1 10-Qs (their statements show only the January
dividend rate), and the 71 other 8-Ks of the period (the Kemper litigation settlement of 2022-03-18, the expected Q3 2023 Vogtle charge of
2023-10-06, the notice to convertible noteholders of 2025-09-15, financing, forward sales, equity units, officers and meetings). None
guides a number but the Q4 2021 release. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows; its 536 strings pass
`retro/tools/verbatim.py`.

Decisions:
- **The FY2022 guide, the first in numbers in any SO filing.** The Q4 2021 release (2022-02-17): "Southern Company’s adjusted earnings
  guidance range for 2022 is $3.50 to $3.60 per share." Its forward-looking non-GAAP paragraph excludes only acquisition and disposition
  impacts, Kemper and Vogtle charges, asset impairments and debt extinguishment costs, and Wholesale Gas Services was sold on 2021-07-01,
  so the guide is the company's figure excluding only one-offs (the ACN rule). FY2022E is its midpoint, $3.55, from 2022-02-18 to the Q4
  2022 print (`eps_guides`, new in the SO builder: the F, MAR and RCL encoding). The release's first-quarter estimate (90 cents) is display
  only (the UNP 2008 rule); its 5-7% long-term rate "consistent with adjusted earnings in a range of $4.00 to $4.30 per share in 2024" is a
  multi-year target and adds nothing (the LOW rule). No later filing guides: the Q3 2022, Q4 2022, Q4 2023, Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 releases
  point to slides "including earnings guidance" on the website (the XOM, NKE and MSFT rule), so FY22's $3.60, FY23's $3.65, FY24's $4.05
  and FY25's $4.30 stand in turn (the rollover rule).
- **EPS basis.** The Q4 2021, Q1 2022 and Q2 2022 releases' figures exclude Wholesale Gas Services in the year-ago quarter ($78M, $166M,
  $(147)M), so GAAP stands for those quarterly signals. From Q3 2022 both quarter columns exclude only one-offs (Vogtle and Kemper loss
  estimates, acquisitions and dispositions, impairments, debt extinguishment, the Nicor Gas QIP and capital-investment disallowances, a
  tax-reform adjustment and, from Q4 2024, accelerated depreciation from repowering), so the signal uses the company's figure (the SO
  2010-2013 encoding). History: FY2021 GAAP $2.24 (its company figure, $3.41, also excludes Wholesale Gas Services' $18M); FY2022 $3.60,
  FY2023 $3.65, FY2024 $4.05, FY2025 $4.30, each from the latest Q4 release that states it (GAAP $3.26, $3.62, $3.99, $3.92). No year fails
  the AAPL test. FY2017 stays excluded: the window is "10-yr ex-FY17" on every date.
- **Repowering depreciation, a judgement call.** From Q4 2024 the releases exclude "Accelerated Depreciation from Repowering" of Southern
  Power's wind facilities: $9M pre-tax in Q4 2024, $284M in 2025, $414M in the first nine months of 2026. The footnotes tie it to the
  projects' completion ("projected to occur in the third quarter 2026", then "through the third quarter 2027") with a stated remaining
  total, so it is read as a one-off, like the Kemper and Vogtle loss estimates. GAAP from the Q4 2024 print is the sensitivity below.
- **Revenue as reported.** BASE takes the latest quarter's total revenue growth, which fuel cost recovery drives: +12.7% (Q4 2021), +12.5%,
  +38.6%, +34.3% and +22.2% (Q1-Q4 2022), -2.5% to -20.2% (Q1-Q4 2023), then +2.6% to +17.0%. No release notes a divestiture effect (the
  Sequent and gas storage sales), so no revenue note. The Q3 2026 retail kWh change computed from the published millions is +7.8% (the
  release prints 7.7% from unrounded figures): computed, as every growth rate.
- **Dividends:** the January rates from the 10-Ks (66, 68, 70, 72 and 74 cents), the April increases from the Q2 10-Qs ($0.68 from
  2022-07-28, $0.70 from 2023-08-03, $0.72 from 2024-08-01, $0.74 from 2025-07-31, $0.76 from 2026-07-30): no earlier filing states them.
- **ENERGY_TRANSITION out of scope from the FY2021 10-K** (2022-02-17). The sentence on which the theme was carried, "Alabama Power owns
  coal reserves near its Plant Gorgas site and uses their output in its generating plants", is gone, as is Mississippi Power's "mineral
  reserves"; the 10-Ks name only "a lignite mine that was intended to provide fuel for the Kemper IGCC" and its reclamation, "substantially
  completed in 2020". No reserves remain for decarbonisation to strand, so the watch list empties and the GHG risk factor stays in the
  "why" (the PEP obesity rule; `mine_quote`, `reclaim_quote`; text only, as the theme had no factor pair). GENAI (from 2022-11-30) and GLP1
  (from 2023-08-08) are scoped to software, services and information, and to snacks, beverages and devices: out of scope.
- **Release timing.** Every release was accepted before the open, on Thursdays; each 10-K and 10-Q came the evening before its release.
