## CTVA (Corteva): the twenty-second ticker, in staging, from its 2019 listing

The CTVA series is built apart from every other ticker and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/CTVA.json`), builder (`retro/build_ctva.py`, the BKR new-listing builder `build_bhge` with fiscal-year net sales guides,
the `distributions` rule and seed and crop protection encodings) and engine (`retro/templates/ctva_engine.py.tmpl`, the `bkr2` engine
with seed and crop protection signals). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters a CTVA
model; there is no CTVA profile in `data/business_profiles.json`. Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/CTVA/`.

```bash
python3 retro/build_ctva.py --weekly 2021-02-01 2026-09-25                  # 295 dates, 2021-02-05 .. 2026-09-25
for d in staging/retrospective/CTVA/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series CTVA
for c in 2021-02-06 2021-02-13 2021-08-09 2022-02-04 2022-02-12 2022-05-06 2023-02-03 2023-02-10 2023-10-27 2023-11-10 2024-02-02 \
         2024-02-09 2024-11-08 2025-02-07 2025-02-19 2025-08-08 2026-02-05 2026-02-14 2026-07-31 2026-09-26; do
  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CTVA; done
```

### CTVA 2008-2009: requested, no date can be built
**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** On 2026-11-16 the owner asked for CTVA 2008-2009 on the same rules. Under method
r2 **no date of 2008-2009 can be built**, and none was: no fact sheet, builder, engine or staging folder was made for those years. Nothing was
invented to fill the gap (the BKR 2018 precedent). Checked against the filings, before any price or outcome of those years was read:

- **No company.** Corteva, Inc. (CIK 1755672) filed nothing with the SEC before its Form 10 of 2018-10-18. Its information statement
  (Form 10/A of 2019-05-06, exhibit 99.1): "Corteva Parent is a wholly owned subsidiary of DowDuPont that was formed on March 16, 2018 to
  serve as a holding company for Corteva." So no CTVA fact carries a `published` date in 2008-2009.
- **No stock, so no P/E of its own (the listing rule).** The same statement: "there is no current trading market for Corteva common
  stock". The distribution was "on June 1, 2019" (a Saturday), with regular-way trading from the next trading day, 2019-06-03.
  Yahoo's CTVA series starts on 2019-05-24 (when-issued). A model needs the stock's own P/E window, which runs from the listing.
- **No single predecessor (why the BKR/BHI route does not apply).** BKR's 2008-2017 dates are Baker Hughes Incorporated because Yahoo
  serves BHI's history under BKR and the business is the same. Neither holds here. Corteva is "the agriculture business of DowDuPont",
  which in 2008-2009 was split between two separately listed companies: Historical DuPont's agriculture segment ("Historical DuPont
  operating a global business that included agriculture, electronics and communications, ...") and Historical Dow's Dow AgroSciences
  ("Historical Dow operating a global business that included agricultural sciences"). Corteva holds EID, the legal entity of Historical
  DuPont, but Historical DuPont's price history sits under DD on Yahoo (from 1972), not under CTVA, and its 2008-2009 business was a
  diversified chemicals company. A 2008-2009 model of it would be a DD retrospective, not CTVA's.

Building either alternative is the owner's call and a method note, not a rule this request decides: (a) Historical DuPont (EID, NYSE: DD)
as a ticker of its own, with its own fact sheet and builder, 2008 onward; (b) CTVA from its listing, whose first date also needs a full
year of EPS published by Corteva itself (the BKR 2018 rule; not yet determined). For (b): Yahoo's CTVA series records a split event on
2026-10-01 (ratio 6665:1000), which `retro_tool.py` undoes as a split when it rebuilds the close as traded; a build from the listing must
first confirm that the rebuilt close matches a printed one.

Sources (each quoted string checked with `verbatim.py` against its own filing, 9/9): EDGAR submissions for CIK 1755672; Form 10/A
0001193125-19-138437, exhibit 99.1 (accepted 2019-05-06 21:12 UTC); Yahoo chart API, CTVA and DD, read 2026-11-16.


### CTVA from the listing: 2021-02-05 to 2026-09-25

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** On 2026-11-16 the owner asked for CTVA from its listing, on the same rules. Under
method r2 **the first date that can be built is 2021-02-05 and the last is 2026-09-25**: 295 weekly dates. No date from 2019-06-07 to
2021-01-29 (87 weeks) is built: a model needs the stock's own P/E, and Corteva's first full year of EPS is 2020, published in the Q4 2020
release. No date from 2026-10-02 to 2026-11-13 (7 weeks) is built: on 2026-10-01 Corteva distributed its seed business, and the listed
company's only per-share history after it is pro forma. Building either gap takes a new rule (an EPS anchor for a year without one, or
pro forma EPS as a history), which is the owner's call and a method note; nothing was invented to fill them (the BKR 2018 precedent).

Read for the history and rule T: the FY2019-FY2025 10-Ks (statements of operations, the EPS note's share counts, the MD&A segment net
sales and price-volume tables, the cash flow statements, the selected financial data of the FY2019 and FY2020 10-Ks, the dividend
paragraphs and the risk factors) and the Q4 2019 release's twelve-month price-volume-currency analysis. Read for the prints: the 24
earnings releases from Q3 2020 to Q2 2026 (each release and its schedules), the 8-K of 2023-10-27, the Q2 10-Qs of 2021-2025 for the
dividend rates, and every other 8-K of 2020 to 2026-09-25 by its item text and exhibits (none guides a number). All by the session's
model directly. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the transcribed rows, so every growth rate, margin, tax rate and rule-T value
is computed, not typed; 591 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (every statement, segment, price-volume,
balance sheet, cash flow and significant-items row behind a figure, and every quoted guide, dividend, listing and risk-factor sentence),
and all 591 were found. A second check matched each print's two segments to its net sales and each Q4 print's full year to the 10-K
that followed it. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (ET). Decided on 2026-11-16, before any CTVA outcome was
computed:

- **The listing.** "Corteva, Inc.'s common stock began trading the "regular way" under the ticker symbol "CTVA" on June 3, 2019, the
  first business day after June 1, 2019" (FY2019 10-K). The P/E window runs from 2019-06-03 (`pe_window_start`, the listing rule); the
  when-issued days that Yahoo serves from 2019-05-24 are not read.
- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo books the 2026-10-01 distribution of the seed business as a 6665:1000 split. It is a distribution, not a
  split, so its factor is undone for the days before it and every close is the price as traded (the MAR, PFE, BMY and SO `distributions`
  rule): $43.90 on 2021-02-05, $78.52 on 2026-09-25. Yahoo's dividends rebuilt by the same factor are $0.130 to 2021 and $0.180 from late
  2025, the rates the filings declare. Every date is before the distribution, so it enters no model; outcomes keep Yahoo's factor (the
  distributed shares stay in the holding, the MAR rule).
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of the series was accepted after the close (16:28-17:10 ET), so each print is dated the next
  trading day and the week's date is the trading day after that (the AAPL rule): the first date, 2021-02-05, follows the Q4 2020 release
  (accepted 2021-02-03 17:08 ET, dated 2021-02-04). The Q2 2026 release (2026-07-30 16:44 ET) is dated Friday 2026-07-31, the week's last
  trading day, so that day's date meets it (`release_time`). The 8-K of 2023-10-27 was accepted at 08:02 ET, before the open. The 10-Ks
  are dated 2020-02-14 (07:29 ET), 2021-02-12 (2021-02-11 16:11), 2022-02-11 (2022-02-10 16:09), 2023-02-09 (10:33), 2024-02-08 (14:13),
  2025-02-18 (2025-02-14 17:10; the 17th was a holiday) and 2026-02-13 (2026-02-12 17:24).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations, each year from the latest filing that reports it.** Corteva's Operating EPS
  excludes significant items, non-operating benefits (pension and OPEB credits, tax indemnification adjustments, legacy environmental
  and legal costs) and the amortization of intangibles existing at the Separation. The amortization and the pension credits recur, so the
  figure does not exclude only one-offs (the NKE FY2007, AVGO 2009, PFE and BMY rule): GAAP stands, nothing is derived, and the Operating
  EPS and Operating EBITDA guides are shown in the guide line only. 2020 $0.98, 2021 $2.44, 2022 $1.66, 2023 $1.30, 2024 $1.22, 2025
  $1.75, the same in every filing that reports them.
- **Excluded years.** 2018 ($(9.08), with the $4,503M goodwill impairment) and 2019 ($(0.38)) are losses with no figure excluding only
  one-offs, so they are excluded, and so are 2015 ($(0.56)) and 2016 ($(0.29)), the predecessor's agriculture years the FY2019 and FY2020
  10-Ks' selected data report. 2017 is reported only as two periods (January 1 to August 31, September 1 to December 31) and is not a
  year. 2019's own days leave the P/E window ("ex-FY19"), which therefore starts on 2020-01-02 (1.1 years on the first date, 6.7 years
  on the last).
- **The one-off test, every year kept.** The releases' "Annual Total" of significant items after tax against income from continuing
  operations attributable to Corteva: 2020 $110M of charges against $736M, 2021 $176M against $1,812M, 2022 $267M against $1,205M, 2023
  $403M against $929M, 2024 $351M against $851M, 2025 $582M (with the $470M Bayer resolution) against $1,193M. Reported EPS is more than
  half the EPS without them in every year.
- **History.** Net sales from 2015: 2015 and 2016 from the selected data (the predecessor, as published; Dow AgroSciences is not in them),
  none for 2017, then the statements of operations. The seam stays in (the house rule) and sets the median growth the growth factor reads:
  -2.3% on the first dates. Diluted shares from the EPS note, from 2018 (749.4M, the shares distributed); the net buyback is measured from
  the first count to the last.
- **The rollover rule and the bounds rule.** On the first dates the history has one year, so BEAR is the 0% cap, BULL takes BASE's rate
  and XBULL BULL's; from the FY2021 Q4 print each rule measures what the history holds.
- **Guides: fiscal-year net sales in dollars, read against the last year's net sales** (the AAPL and PFE dollar-level rule; no quarter is
  ever guided): FY2021 $14.4-14.6B, $14.6-14.8B, $15.2-15.4B, $15.5-15.7B; FY2022 $16.7-17.0B (twice), $17.2-17.5B (twice); FY2023
  $18.1-18.4B, $18.6-18.9B, $17.9-18.2B, $17.0-17.3B (the 8-K of 2023-10-27, then the Q3 2023 release); FY2024 $17.4-17.7B (twice),
  $17.2-17.5B, $17.0-17.2B; FY2025 $17.2-17.6B (twice), $17.6-17.8B, $17.7-17.9B. The Q3 2024 release's "preliminary outlook" for 2025
  ($17.3-17.7B) is recorded and reaches no date: its year becomes current only with the Q4 2024 release, which guides again. FY2026 has
  no net sales guide in numbers (Operating EBITDA and Operating EPS only), so from the Q4 2025 print BASE and the growth factor take the
  latest quarter's net sales growth as reported (the no-guide rule). Current-FY EPS: no GAAP EPS is ever guided, so the last full year's
  EPS stands (the PFE rule). No margin is guided on the GAAP basis: no guided step.
- **Dividends:** $0.13 a quarter (FY2019 and FY2020 10-Ks), then $0.14, $0.15, $0.16, $0.17 and $0.18, each from the Q2 10-Q that first
  states it (2021-08-09, 2022-08-08, 2023-08-04, 2024-08-02, 2025-08-08).
- **Signals.** Five, with BKR's weights, each against the year-ago quarter in the same release: Seed organic sales growth (0.20) and
  Crop Protection organic growth (0.20) from the price-volume-currency analysis, the total price change (local price and product mix,
  0.15), the gross margin change (0.15; net sales less cost of goods sold) and the pre-tax margin change (0.15; income from continuing
  operations before income taxes on net sales, GAAP), with the theme slot at 2/4. Segment Operating EBITDA is shown nowhere: the
  releases give 2019 only pro forma.
- **Thresholds by rule T over the years the filings public on 2021-02-05 report** (the bounds rule), each change from the latest filing
  that reports both years, as reported; the FY2019 10-K's 2018-vs-2017 analysis is pro forma and is not used:

  | Signal | Annual values | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | Seed organic growth | 2019-2020: -1, 6 % | -4 / -1 / 3 / 6 % |
  | Crop Protection organic growth | 2019-2020: 1, 11 % | -4 / 1 / 6 / 11 % |
  | price | 2019-2020: 0, 3 % | -1 / 0 / 2 / 3 % |
  | gross margin change | 2019-2020: 769.8, 209.4 bp | -70 / 210 / 490 / 770 bp |
  | pre-tax margin change | 2016, 2019, 2020: 129.1, 4535.5, 703.0 bp | -440 / 130 / 700 / 4540 bp |

  2019's margins step up from 2018's merger charges (the inventory step-up in cost of goods sold, the goodwill impairment), so a quarter
  needs +210bp of gross margin to score BASE: the rule's result, not a choice.
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2.** No 10-K calls the business cyclical. The "why" quotes each 10-K: "The company competes with producers
  of seed germplasm, trait developers, and crop protection products on a global basis." and the risk factor "Climate change and
  unpredictable seasonal and weather factors could impact Corteva's sales and earnings." No theme in the registry covers seed and crop
  protection (GLP1 is scoped to snacks, beverages and devices, ENERGY_TRANSITION to reserves and refining), so the watch list is empty
  and the weather and climate wording stays in the "why" (the PEP obesity rule).
- **Adds nothing:** the separation announcement (8-K of 2025-10-01) and the separation 8-Ks to 2026-09-25 (exchange offers, the board's
  approval, the record date), the officer and governance 8-Ks, the debt 8-Ks and the 2020 restructuring 8-K: none guides a number.
- **Names:** "New Corteva" (from 2025-10-01) and "Vylor" (from 2026-05-06) join the anachronism list; no model contains either.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):
- **Controls:** raising one print's Seed organic growth, each Q4 print's full-year EPS, each guide's range (or display), each dividend
  and each vintage's last EPS and net sales changes no model dated before its publication and changes the first weekly date on or
  after it: 62 of 62. Altering the FY2025 preliminary outlook changes no model.
- **Leak scan:** the distinctive texts and figures of every print, guide, dividend, vintage and source appear in no model before their
  publication (0 hits in 75,125 pairs, after dropping strings an earlier fact already carries and figures under five characters).
- **Years after the as-of date:** none in the 295 models and reports, other than FY labels (`retro_tool run` reports no warning).
- **`retro_tool run`:** passes on all 295 dates, with no warnings. A fresh rebuild is byte-identical.
- **Firewall** (run after the build was committed, before any outcome): passes at the 20 cutoffs above (every Q4 print and 10-K, the
  2023-10-27 update, a dividend, mid-year dates and 2026-09-26), with 0 files changed and no planted text (1 to 295 dates each).

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **Totals: RICH 194, CHEAP 77, FAIR 24.** 2021: RICH on all 48 dates; 2022: CHEAP 46, RICH 4, FAIR 2; 2023: CHEAP 27, FAIR 22, RICH 3;
  2024: RICH 48, CHEAP 4; 2025: RICH on all 52; 2026: RICH on all 39.
- **The class follows the anchor.** FY20's $0.98 puts the stock at 43-50x in 2021 (RICH); FY21's $2.44 at 21-28x in 2022 (CHEAP);
  FY22's $1.66 at 26-39x in 2023 (CHEAP and FAIR); FY23's $1.30, FY24's $1.22 and FY25's $1.75 at 39-63x from 2024 (RICH). The P/E window
  holds the anchors that set the class, so the median moves with them: 29x in early 2021, 20x in 2022, 29-35x in 2023-2024, 36-37x
  from 2025.
- **The EPP floor** rises from $29 to $44, then falls to $35-40 with the GAAP years and rises to $54 from the Q4 2025 print; the price is
  above it on every date.
- **BASE follows the net sales guides:** +1.9%/yr on the first dates, +9.6% after the Q3 2021 raise, +8.0% to +11.2% in 2022, -0.9% after
  the 2023-10-27 cut, +0.3% to +2.9% in 2024, +4.1% to +6.5% in 2025, then the latest quarter's net sales growth in 2026 (-0.3%, +12.4%,
  +0.2%).
- **The proxy composite** runs from 1.30 (Q4 2023) to 3.25 (Q3 2021), held down by the gross and pre-tax margin thresholds.

Sensitivity (each call changed alone, the 295 dates rebuilt and reclassified offline; no outcome consulted):
- **Operating EPS as the history** (2019 at its $1.43 pro forma figure, 2020-2025 at $1.50, $2.15, $2.67, $2.69, $2.57 and $3.34, and the
  Operating EPS guide midpoint as current-FY EPS): **129 classes** (RICH to CHEAP 51, RICH to FAIR 28, FAIR to CHEAP 22, CHEAP to RICH
  14, CHEAP to FAIR 12, FAIR to RICH 2) and 205 tiers; the Q4 2019 release would also open 53 more weekly dates (2020-01-31 to
  2021-01-29), 35 of them a year after the listing (the others need the AVGO short-window encodings);
- **net sales without the predecessor's 2015 and 2016:** 1 class (2023-05-26), no tier;
- **rule T for the pre-tax margin without 2016:** no class, no tier;
- **every signal at its BEAR value:** 62 classes, toward RICH or FAIR; **at its XBULL value:** 15 classes, toward CHEAP or FAIR; no tier.
The classes rest on the EPS basis above all; the signals and their thresholds move far fewer.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- GAAP rather than Operating EPS, on the recurring-amortization rule (129 classes), by a builder who knows how the stock traded;
- no date before the first full year of GAAP EPS (2019 at $(0.38) excluded; 87 weeks unbuilt) and none after the 2026 distribution
  (7 weeks), both the owner's call;
- the predecessor's 2015-2016 net sales and 2016 pre-tax margin kept as published (1 class and none);
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows 2021-2026: Seed and Crop Protection organic growth, price and two GAAP margins (rule T then
  sets the thresholds mechanically from two or three merger-distorted years);
- DURABLE although agriculture is exposed to weather and farm income (no 10-K calls the business cyclical);
- the regular-way trading day as the listing rather than the first when-issued day (five trading days, outside every window);
- the non-earnings 8-Ks read by their item text and exhibits for guided numbers only.

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/CTVA/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

## KMI (Kinder Morgan): the twenty-third ticker, in staging, from its 2011 listing

The KMI series is built apart from every other ticker and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/KMI.json`), builder (`retro/build_kmi.py`, the CTVA new-listing builder with KMI's encodings) and engine
(`retro/templates/kmi_engine.py.tmpl`, the CTVA engine with pipeline signals). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding
of another ticker enters a KMI model, and neither does the profile of KMI in `data/business_profiles.json` (a 2026 judgement, not read for
this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/KMI/`.

```bash
python3 retro/build_kmi.py --weekly 2013-01-14 2014-12-31                   # 103 dates, 2013-01-18 .. 2014-12-31
python3 retro/build_kmi.py --weekly 2015-01-01 2018-12-31                   # 210 dates, 2015-01-02 .. 2018-12-31 ("KMI 2015-2018")
python3 retro/build_kmi.py --weekly 2019-01-01 2022-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2019-01-04 .. 2022-12-30 ("KMI 2019-2022")
python3 retro/build_kmi.py --weekly 2023-01-01 2026-11-15                   # 202 dates, 2023-01-06 .. 2026-11-13 ("KMI 2023-2026")
for d in staging/retrospective/KMI/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series KMI
for c in 2013-02-01 2013-03-01 2013-04-18 2013-05-06 2013-07-01 2013-07-18 2013-08-05 2013-10-17 2013-10-31 2014-01-01 2014-01-16 \
         2014-02-24 2014-04-17 2014-05-01 2014-07-17 2014-07-31 2014-10-16 2014-10-30 2015-01-01; do
  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c KMI; done                             # later: "KMI 2015-2018", "KMI 2019-2022", "KMI 2023-2026"
```

### KMI 2008-2009: requested, no date can be built

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** On 2026-11-16 the owner asked for KMI 2008-2009 on the same rules. Under method
r2 **no date of 2008-2009 can be built**, and none was: no fact sheet, builder, engine or staging folder was made, and nothing was invented
to fill the gap (the BKR 2018 and CTVA 2008-2009 precedents). Checked against the filings, before any price or outcome of those years was
read (Yahoo was asked for its series metadata only):

- **No KMI stock in 2008-2009.** The Kinder Morgan, Inc. listed on the NYSE as KMI until 2007 (CIK 54502, formerly K N Energy) was taken
  private: "On May 30, 2007, Kinder Morgan, Inc. (the “Corporation”) completed its merger (the “Merger”) with Knight Acquisition Co.", and
  it "requested that the NYSE file with the Securities and Exchange Commission an application on Form 25 to report that the shares of
  common stock of the Corporation are no longer listed on the NYSE" (8-K accepted 2007-06-04 18:40 ET). The NYSE's Form 25 for the common
  stock was accepted the same day (14:24 ET), and Forms 15-12B followed on 2007-06-04 and 2007-06-05. Through 2008-2009 the company kept
  filing 10-Ks and 10-Qs, as Knight Inc. and from 2009-07-15 as Kinder Morgan, Inc. again, but only as an issuer of public debt: "Knight
  Midco Inc., an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Knight Holdco LLC, owns 100% of our outstanding common stock", its balance sheet shows
  "Common Stock – Authorized and Outstanding – 100 Shares, Par Value $0.01 Per Share", and the 2008 columns of its quarterly price table
  read "n/a" (FY2008 10-K, 2009-03-31 15:50 ET). The FY2009 10-K (2010-03-08 14:47 ET): "As a result of the Going Private transaction, our
  common stock ceased trading on May 30, 2007." So no date of 2008-2009 has a KMI price, a P/E of its own or a per-share EPS of a traded
  share.
- **Today's KMI did not trade until 2011 (the listing rule).** Today's Kinder Morgan, Inc. (CIK 1506307) is the former parent, Knight
  Holdco LLC (later Kinder Morgan Holdco LLC): "We were formed in 2006 in connection with a transaction we refer to as the "Going Private
  Transaction,"" and "Prior to this offering there has been no public market for our common stock." (Form S-1, its first SEC filing,
  accepted 2010-11-23 10:47 ET). It converted to a corporation on 2011-02-10 (FY2010 10-K) and its offering priced at $30.00 (424B1,
  2011-02-11 06:06 ET). Yahoo's KMI series starts on 2011-02-11 (`firstTradeDate` and the first point; none in 2008-2009). A model needs
  the stock's own P/E window, which runs from the listing.
- **No predecessor price under KMI (why the BKR/BHI route does not apply).** BKR's 2008-2017 dates are Baker Hughes Incorporated because
  BHI was listed on those dates and Yahoo serves its history under BKR. Here the business is largely the same (Knight Inc. consolidated
  Kinder Morgan Energy Partners), but no KMI equity was listed on any date of 2008-2009, and Yahoo serves nothing under KMI before 2011. The
  listed Kinder Morgan equities of those years were other securities: "Kinder Morgan Energy Partners is a publicly traded pipeline limited
  partnership whose limited partnership units are traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol “KMP.”" and "Kinder Morgan
  Management’s shares (other than the voting shares held by Kinder Morgan G.P., Inc.) are traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the
  ticker symbol “KMR.”" (FY2008 10-K). Knight Inc. owned "the general partner interest and a significant limited partner interest" in KMP,
  but KMP's units are a partnership's, with their own earnings per unit and distributions; a 2008-2009 model of them would be a KMP
  retrospective, not KMI's. Yahoo serves neither KMP nor KMR ("No data found, symbol may be delisted").

Building either alternative is the owner's call and a method note, not a rule this request decides: (a) KMP (Kinder Morgan Energy
Partners) as a ticker of its own, with its own fact sheet, builder and engine, 2008 onward; it needs a price source other than Yahoo and a
rule for a partnership's earnings per unit after the general partner's incentive distributions; (b) KMI from its 2011-02-11 listing, whose
first date also needs a full year of EPS published by KMI itself (the BKR 2018 rule; not yet determined: a search of the FY2010 10-K, the
first after the listing, finds no earnings per share, since Kinder Morgan Holdco LLC had units, not shares).

Sources (each quoted string checked with `verbatim.py` against its own filing, 29/29): EDGAR submissions for CIK 54502 and CIK 1506307;
8-K 0000054502-07-000044; Form 25 0000876661-07-000471; FY2008 10-K 0000054502-09-000005; 8-K 0000054502-09-000011 (the 2009 name
change); FY2009 10-K 0000054502-10-000002; Form S-1 0001047469-10-010001; 424B1 0001047469-11-000769; FY2010 10-K 0001506307-11-000009;
Yahoo chart API, KMI, KMP and KMR, read 2026-11-16 (metadata only). No model output changes.

The owner then chose option (b), KMI from its listing ("KMI from the listing", below).

### KMI from the listing: 2013-01-18 to 2014-12-31

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** On 2026-11-16 the owner asked for KMI from its 2011 listing, on the same rules.
Under method r2 **the first date that can be built is 2013-01-18**; this part builds the 103 weekly dates to 2014-12-31, the years
before the November 2014 acquisition of KMP, KMR and EPB (later dates follow in their own parts). No date from 2011-02-11 to 2013-01-11
(100 weeks) is built: a model needs the stock's own P/E, and Kinder Morgan's first full year of EPS is 2012, published in the Q4 2012
release. Building that gap takes a new rule (an EPS anchor for a period that is not a year), which is the owner's call and a method note;
nothing was invented to fill it (the BKR 2018 precedent).

Read for the history and rule T: the FY2010-FY2013 10-Ks (the five-year reviews, the statements of income and cash flows, the segment
notes, Items 1A and 5, the EPS notes) and the Q1 2011 10-Q's EPS note. Read for the prints: the nine earnings releases from Q3 2012 to Q3
2014 (each release and its schedules; the Q3 2012 8-K was filed without its exhibit and the 8-K/A of the same evening carries it), the
2012-2014 10-Qs' segment notes, and every other 8-K of 2012 to 2014 by its item text and exhibits (conference presentations, offerings,
the El Paso closing, the drop-downs, the dividend and budget statements: none guides revenue, EPS or a margin in numbers). All by the
session's model directly, with no delegated transcription. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows: each
figure is read from its labelled row (a segment line from the rows just above its table's total), the row is asserted present in its own
filing, and every growth rate, margin, tax rate and rule-T value is computed, not typed; 182 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each
against its own filing, and all 182 were found. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (ET); the source ids are `KM0`-`KM4`
(the 10-Q of 2011 and the 10-Ks), `KM10`-`KM18` (the releases), `KM20`-`KM26` (the 10-Qs) and `KM30` (the 8-K of 2013-05-14). Decided on 2026-11-16, before any KMI model
was built or any KMI outcome computed:

- **The listing.** The Class P common stock, NYSE: KMI. The FY2011 10-K's price table begins "First Quarter (beginning February 11,
  2011)" and Yahoo's KMI series starts on 2011-02-11 (`pe_window_start`, the listing rule). Yahoo records no split or distribution, so its
  close is the price as traded.
- **2011 is not a year of EPS.** Every filing from the Q1 2011 10-Q (2011-05-06) computes EPS "for the period from February 11, 2011 (the
  date of our initial public offering)", and the FY2011 10-K's $0.74 for 2011 is the period February 11 to December 31 (2010 and before:
  units, EPS "N/A"). It is excluded like BKR's and CTVA's 2017, and its days leave the P/E window ("ex-FY11"), which therefore starts on
  2012-01-03 (1.0 years on the first date, 3.0 on the last).
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of the range was accepted after the close (16:08-16:21 ET; the Q3 2012 8-K/A at 18:16 ET, the
  call at 4:30 p.m. ET), so each print is dated the next trading day and the week's date is the trading day after that (the AAPL rule):
  the first date, 2013-01-18, follows the Q4 2012 release (accepted 2013-01-16 16:11 ET, dated 2013-01-17). Good Friday 2014 makes the
  Q1 2014 print's day, 2014-04-17, the week's last trading day, so that day's date meets it (`release_time`, public before the open). The
  10-Ks are dated 2012-02-23 (2012-02-22 20:57 ET), 2013-03-01 (08:16 ET) and 2014-02-24 (2014-02-21 17:55 ET).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations per Class P share, each year from the latest filing that reports it.** The Class P
  diluted count assumes the conversion of the investor retained Class A shares (all converted on 2012-12-26). The releases of 2012-2014 give
  no EPS excluding one-offs (their non-GAAP measure is cash available to pay dividends), so GAAP stands: 2012 $0.70 from the Q4 2012
  release, then $0.56 from the FY2012 10-K (2013-03-01: income from continuing operations restated from $1,333M to $1,204M); 2013 $1.15.
- **The one-off test, every year kept.** 2012: the release's $310M of after-tax expenses of the EP acquisition and EP Energy sale against
  $444M of net income attributable to KMI. 2013: the release lists KMP certain items of $(559)M (net gains: the Eagle Ford remeasurement,
  the Express sale) and KMI certain items of $55M, pre-tax and before the noncontrolling interests; even all $504M of the net benefit
  credited to KMI is less than the year's $1,193M of net income attributable to KMI without it ($689M), the mirror test.
- **History.** Revenues from 2006: 2006 from the FY2010 10-K's five-year review (the Predecessor Company's full year), 2007 only as two
  periods (seven months Successor, five months Predecessor) and so not a year, then each year from the latest 10-K (recast for
  discontinued operations from the FY2012 10-K). Diluted Class P shares from 2011 (707.6M for the IPO period, then 708M, 908M, 1,036M); the
  net buyback is measured from the first count to the last, so the El Paso shares issued in May 2012 read as dilution: -22.1%/yr on the
  first dates, -17.3%/yr from the Q4 2013 print.
- **The rollover rule and the bounds rule.** To the Q4 2013 print the history has one year of EPS, so BEAR is the 0% cap, BULL takes
  BASE's rate and XBULL BULL's; from it, 2012 to 2013 is the only change (+105%, from $0.56 to $1.15), so BEAR stays at the cap and BULL
  and XBULL take that rate.
- **No guide in numbers.** No release, 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K of 2012-2014 guides revenue, EPS or a margin: the budgets are for
  dividends per share and cash available to pay dividends. So current-FY EPS is the last full year's (the PFE rule), BASE is the latest
  quarter's revenue growth as reported plus the buyback (the SO and UNP no-guide rule), and there is no margin step. The dividend outlook
  of each release ("KMI expects to declare dividends of $1.57 per share for 2013") and of the 8-K of 2013-05-14 ("KMI now expects to
  declare dividends of $1.60 per share for 2013", after the Copano acquisition) is shown in the guide line, display only.
- **Dividends:** each quarter's declared rate from its release's statement of income ($0.37 for Q4 2012 to $0.44 for Q3 2014).
- **Signals.** Five, with the house weights, each against the year-ago quarter: total segment EBDA growth (0.20) and Natural Gas Pipelines
  segment EBDA growth (0.20), segment earnings before DD&A being the measure each 10-K says the company evaluates its segments by; revenue
  growth (0.15), the operating margin change (0.15) and the pre-tax margin change (0.15; income from continuing operations before income
  taxes on revenues), from the release's statement of income; the theme slot at 2/4. The releases of 2012-2014 tabulate no segment, so a
  quarter's segment EBDA comes from its 10-Q's segment note, from the 10-Q's own date (the PEP `servings_later` rule); a fourth quarter is
  in no 10-Q and reads n/r (scored BASE). The segment line is "Natural Gas Pipelines—KMP" to Q1 2012 and "Natural Gas Pipelines" from the
  El Paso acquisition, as reported (the acquired pipelines in, so 2012-2013 growth is acquisition growth).
- **Thresholds by rule T over the years the filings public on 2013-01-18 report** (the bounds rule), each change from the latest filing
  that reports both years, as reported. 2008's goodwill impairments ($4,033M) made its segment EBDA and operating income losses, so 2009's
  segment changes are no growth rates and leave rule T, while its margin changes stay in, as reported:

  | Signal | Annual values | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | total segment EBDA | 2010-2011: -9.1, 18.1 % | -23 / -9 / 5 / 18 % |
  | Natural Gas Pipelines EBDA | 2010-2011: 5.1, -6.8 % | -13 / -7 / -1 / 5 % |
  | revenue | 2009-2012: -40.6, 14.0, 0.9, 25.6 % | -89 / -41 / 7 / 26 % |
  | operating margin change | 2009-2012: 4002.4, -394.8, 298.1, 808.5 bp | -1340 / -390 / 550 / 4000 bp |
  | pre-tax margin change | 2009-2012: 3926.2, -958.8, 656.8, 527.4 bp | -2510 / -960 / 590 / 3930 bp |

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2.** No 10-K calls the business cyclical. The "why" quotes each 10-K: "Although the majority of the cash
  generated by KMP’s assets is fee based and is not sensitive to commodity prices, the CO2–KMP business segment is exposed to commodity
  price risk related to the price volatility of crude oil and natural gas liquids." (FY2011; "overwhelming majority" in FY2012,
  "predominantly fee based" in FY2013) and the risk factor "We are dependent on cash distributions received from KMP." ("... from KMP and
  EPB." from FY2012). No theme in the registry is live for a pipeline company on these dates, so the watch list is empty and the builder
  refuses events.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): each 10-K's segment revenues from external customers; the EPS check runs on the last
  year's pre-tax margin and tax rate before the noncontrolling interests (KMP's and EPB's other unitholders), so it overstates KMI's own
  EPS, as its note says.
- **Adds nothing:** the conference-presentation 8-Ks, the debt and equity offering 8-Ks, the El Paso closing 8-K of 2012-05-30 and its
  pro forma 8-K/A, the drop-down and Copano 8-Ks, the officer and governance 8-Ks and the 2014-08-10 announcement of the acquisition of
  KMP, KMR and EPB (8-K of 2014-08-11: it guides dividends, $2.00 a share for 2015 and about 10% a year to 2020, not revenue, EPS or a
  margin); their effects reach the prints.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):
- **Controls:** raising one print's revenues (its growth and margins re-derived), each 10-Q's segment EBDA, each Q4 print's full-year EPS,
  each dividend, each outlook's display and each vintage's last revenue and EPS changes no model dated before its publication and
  changes the first weekly date on or after it: 36 of 36. Three facts published before the first date and superseded by it reach no
  model, as they should: the Q3 2012 print's own figures (only its 10-Q segment value is read, as the previous quarter's), its $0.36
  dividend and its FY2012 outlook.
- **Leak scan:** the distinctive texts and figures of every print, 10-Q value, guide, dividend, vintage and source appear in no model
  before their publication (0 hits in 11,166 pairs, after dropping 125 tokens an earlier fact or the engine already carries, figures under
  four digits, year-like integers and quarter labels such as "the Q2 2014 release", which every model names in advance as its next print).
- **Years after the as-of date:** none in the 103 models and reports other than the FY horizon labels (FY2015E, FY2016E).
- **`retro_tool run`:** passes on all 103 dates, with no warnings.
- **Firewall** (run after the build was committed, before any outcome): passes at the 19 cutoffs above, with 0 files changed and no

  yet" when its 10-Q was in the fact sheet but dated after AS_OF, so a later fact changed earlier text (on 5 of the 19 cutoffs). The clause
  was removed (text only: no class or tier moved), the dates rebuilt and every check rerun.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **Totals: CHEAP 90, RICH 13.** 2013: CHEAP 39, RICH 11; 2014: CHEAP 51, RICH 2. The legacy tier is BUY on all 103 dates.
- **The anchors.** FY12's $0.70 puts the stock at 53-54x on the six dates to 2013-02-22 (window median 50x); the FY2012 10-K's
  restatement to $0.56 puts it at 59-72x from 2013-03-01 against a window median of 63-64x (the window holds only 2012 and 2013 days on one
  anchor, so every P/E scales together, the AVGO observation); FY13's $1.15 puts it at 27-37x in 2014 against a median of 33-35x.
- **BASE follows revenue as reported, less the El Paso dilution:** +36.9%/yr on the first dates (Q4 2012 revenues +59.0%, the El Paso
  pipelines in), +42.8% and +34.1% after the Q1 and Q2 2013 prints, +5.3% after Q3 2013 (+27.3% revenues), then +8.5%, +15.0%, -0.9% and
  -3.1%/yr in 2014. The 13 RICH dates are the Q3 2013 print's (2013-10-18 to 2014-01-10): +5.3%/yr at 63x.
- **BULL and XBULL** take BASE's rate in 2013 (one year of EPS) and the +105%/yr of 2012 to 2013 in 2014, so the BULL price is far above

- **The EPP floor** is $31-35: a 48x floor on $0.70 on the first dates, 56-59x on $0.56 to 2014-01-10, 28-30x on $1.15 in 2014.

scored. Their `FINDINGS.md` was not opened for any decision below; each applies a rule that existed before (the house rules and the

Read: the 16 earnings releases from Q4 2014 to Q3 2018, the FY2014-FY2017 10-Ks (five-year reviews, statements of income and cash flows, segment notes, the dividend statements, Items 1 and 1A), and
every other 8-K of 2015-2018 by its item text and exhibits (all documents of each filing were re-fetched, since some exhibits do not carry
"ex99" in their names). All by the session's model directly. The fact sheet's new entries are generated by the same script: each figure
is read from its labelled row, where a label differs between releases the script lists the candidates and requires exactly one in the
filing, and every rate is computed; 457 strings now pass `verbatim.py` (275 new), each against its own filing. Source ids: `KM5`-`KM8` (the
10-Ks), `KM40`-`KM55` (the releases). Decided on 2026-11-16, before any outcome of these dates was computed:

- **The combination.** KMI acquired KMP, KMR and EPB on 2014-11-26 for shares and cash; the Q4 2014 release (2015-01-21) is the first
  print of the combined company. Its diluted Class P count goes from 1,137M (2014) to 2,193M (2015) and 2,230M (2016-2017). The net buyback
  is still measured from the first count of the history to the last (r2), so the combination reads as dilution: -17.3%/yr from the FY2015
  history (708M in 2011 to 2,193M) and about the same after. BASE is revenue growth as reported plus that term.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted after the close (16:07-16:24 ET; the call at 4:30 p.m. ET), so each print is dated
  the next trading day. The 10-Ks are dated 2015-02-23 (06:07 ET), 2016-02-16 (07:26 ET), 2017-02-13 (2017-02-10 16:47 ET) and 2018-02-12
  (2018-02-09 17:10 ET).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS per Class P common share, from continuing operations where the filing reports the line.** From Q1 2017 the
  releases give "Adjusted earnings per common share" (and from Q4 2014 net income before certain items), but KMI's certain items include
  recurring entries: debt fair value amortization ($143M in 2016, $53M in 2017), the change in fair value of derivative contracts each
  quarter and, in 2014, the pension plan net benefit credit. So the adjusted figure does not exclude only one-offs (the CTVA, NKE FY2007,
  AVGO 2009, PFE and BMY rule): GAAP stands, and the adjusted EPS and DCF per share are shown in the activity line, display only.
- **The one-off test, each year from its Q4 release,** with the release's "Total certain items" (after tax) against the year's income on the
  basis of the per-share figure (net income available to common stockholders once preferred dividends begin in 2015):
  - 2014: a net benefit of $103M against net income attributable to KMI of $1,026M; the mirror test ($103M against $923M without it): kept
    at GAAP, $0.89;
  - 2015: $(1,314)M against $311M (impairments, mostly Natural Gas Pipelines and CO2): **excluded** (GAAP $0.14 in the release, $0.10 in
    the FY2015 10-K), from the Q4 2015 release (2016-01-21);
  - 2016: $(933)M against $552M: **excluded** ($0.25), from 2017-01-19;
  - 2017: $(1,445)M with the $1,381M Tax Act charge against $27M: **excluded** ($0.01), from 2018-01-18.
  Each is the latest year when excluded, so the NKE FY2018 rule applies: its own days leave the P/E window ("ex-FY15 ex-FY16 ex-FY17"), EPS
  growth is measured only between years in the history, and the rollover rule's last full year is the last year in the history.
- **So FY14's $0.89 is the EPS anchor from the Q4 2014 print (2015-01-23) to the end of the range** (FY13's $1.15 on the three dates before
  it). The history's EPS years stay 2012-2014: BEAR is 2014's -22.6% (from $1.15 to $0.89), BULL and XBULL the 2012-2014 CAGR of +26.1%.
- **History,** each year from the latest filing that reports it, kept to the ten fiscal years to the latest one: revenues from 2006 to
  2015 and from 2008 from the FY2016 10-K; diluted Class P shares from 2011.
- **No guide in numbers.** The budgets guide dividends, DCF and Adjusted EBITDA and say "KMI does not provide budgeted net income
  attributable to common stockholders": no revenue, EPS or margin guide, so the 2013-2014 encodings hold. Each release's dividend outlook
  ($2.00 for 2015, $0.50 for 2016 and 2017, $0.80 for 2018) is shown in the guide line, display only.
- **Dividends:** each quarter's declared rate from its release ($0.45 for Q4 2014 to $0.51 for Q3 2015, $0.125 from Q4 2015, $0.20 from Q1
  2018); each 10-K's own statement of the latest quarterly rate for its vintage ($0.45, $0.125, $0.125, $0.125).
- **Signals, unchanged.** From the Q4 2014 release the releases tabulate segment EBDA (GAAP, "Total Segment EBDA" and "Natural Gas
  Pipelines"), so both segment signals are read from the release on its own date; the "before certain items" table is not used (the
  2012-2014 10-Q values are GAAP too). Revenue, the operating margin and the pre-tax margin as before.
- **ENERGY_TRANSITION on the watch list from 2015-12-18,** the first weekly date on or after its live date (2015-12-12). Its scope is
  "decarbonisation strands oil, gas and coal reserves and refining", and each 10-K says "We own approximately 97% working interest in the
  SACROC unit, ..." (the CO2 segment's oil fields) and, of greenhouse gas laws and regulations, "Although we currently cannot predict the
  magnitude and direction of these impacts, greenhouse gas regulations could have material adverse effects on our business, ..." (FY2014)
  or "Such laws or regulations could also lead to reduced demand for hydrocarbon products that are deemed to contribute to greenhouse
  gases, or restrictions on their use, which in turn could adversely affect demand for our products and services." (FY2015-FY2017). That is
  the XOM and SO case (a holder of reserves, company-acknowledged, no market read), not BKR's (no reserves): DURABLE stands, the watch list
  quotes the vintage's 10-K (`reserves_quote`, `transition_quote`), and the theme signal, its name and the summary follow it. Text only: no
  factor pair is added and the theme slot stays at 2/4.
- **The "why"** quotes each 10-K: "The overwhelming majority of cash generated by our assets is fee-based and is not sensitive to commodity
  prices." (FY2014; reworded in FY2015 and FY2016; the FY2017 10-K has no such sentence, so its long-term contract sentence is quoted) and
  the risk factor "A sharp decline in the prices of oil, NGL or natural gas ... could have a material adverse effect on the carrying value
  of our proved reserves" (each 10-K's own wording).
- **Two display formats, text only:** the diluted share count is printed without a padded zero (2.203, not 2.2030) and segment revenues in
  USD bn, so no figure reads as a year; footnote markers leave the segment names. The 2013-2014 models change in text only: every class,
  metric and robustness row of the 103 dates is identical, and their outcomes stand.
- **Adds nothing:** the 2018 budget 8-K of 2017-12-04 (its $0.80 outlook for 2018 is superseded by the Q4 2017
  release before 2018 is the current year), the 2018-05-29 8-K (the Trans Mountain sale; it reaffirms the $0.80 dividend and DCF), the
  2018-09-06 8-K (a leverage expectation), the Southern Natural Gas venture 8-Ks of 2016, the financing, offering, governance and
  conference-notice 8-Ks, and the "mini-tender" notice of 2015-11-16.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):

  of the FY2019 and FY2020 10-Ks give basic EPS and every review basic shares only, so the diluted figures come from each statement of
  income (three years, "Basic and Diluted") and, before it, from the filing that last reported them diluted (2015's 2,193M shares from the
  FY2017 10-K, not the reviews' basic 2,187M); the FY2021 10-K has no review (Item 6 reserved), so it supplies 2019-2021 (the ACN FY21 rule).
  EPS years in the history: 2012-2014 and 2018-2019, then 2021 from the Q4 2021 print; 2011, 2015-2017 and 2020 excluded; 2011 leaves the
  ten years with the FY2021 10-K.

  Q3 2020 say "KMI does not provide budgeted net income", so the PFE rule holds: FY18's $0.66 stands for FY2019E from the Q4 2018 print, FY19's
  $0.96 for FY2020E from the Q4 2019 print. From the 2021 budget the releases guide GAAP net income attributable to KMI, so current-FY EPS
  follows the latest guide: its own per-share figure where it states one, else its net income (midpoint) over the release's own diluted
  weighted-average shares (the PFE and LOW dollar-level rule, applied to earnings), and a guide stated as a percentage on the budget is the
  budget times that percentage (the NKE and WMT rule for an EPS guide stated as growth on a stated base). Words without a number keep the last figure (the ACN rule):
  - FY2021: $0.92 ("$2.1 billion in net income attributable to KMI, or $0.92 earnings per share", Q4 2020 release); $2.7-2.9 billion / 2,264M
    = $1.237 (Q1 2021, after Winter Storm Uri); $1.7 billion / 2,265M = $0.751 (Q2 2021, after the $1,600M South Texas impairment) and
    / 2,267M = $0.75 (Q3 2021);

    (Q2 2022); +3% / 2,253M = $1.143 (Q3 2022).

- GAAP over the company's adjusted EPS (92 classes, 141 tiers);
- the summed segment total from Q1 2023 (10 classes if n/r);
- BASE on revenue as reported when no revenue is guided (18 classes on the dividend outlook);
- the signals (112 classes at BEAR, 62 at XBULL), chosen by a builder who knows 2013-2014;
- ENERGY_TRANSITION kept on the watch list, GENAI and EV not recorded, DURABLE kept (text only);
- the last date set by the build time (2026-11-13), and the website-only budgets and presentations left out.

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/KMI/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

## LMT (Lockheed Martin): the twenty-fourth ticker, in staging, 2008-2026

The LMT series is built apart from the other twenty-three and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/LMT.json`), builder (`retro/build_lmt.py`, the CAT builder with a fiscal-year outlook table) and engine
(`retro/templates/lmt_engine.py.tmpl`, the CAT engine with defense prime contractor signals and Lockheed Martin's own rule-T
thresholds). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an LMT model, and neither does the
profile of LMT in `data/business_profiles.json` (a 2026 judgement: not read for this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/LMT/`,
beside the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009, then 2010-2013, then 2014-2017, then 2018-2021, then 2022-2026.

```bash
python3 retro/build_lmt.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2009-12-31                   # 105 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/LMT/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series LMT
for c in 2008-01-24 2008-02-29 2008-04-22 2008-07-01 2008-07-22 2008-10-21 2009-01-01 2009-01-22 2009-02-26 2009-04-21 \
         2009-07-21 2009-10-20 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c LMT; done
```

One range, as for SO: the ISO week of 2008-12-29 to 2009-01-02 is dated 2009-01-02, so the series has no 2008-12-31 (CAT and BMY built
2008 and 2009 as two ranges and have 2008-12-31 instead).

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the earnings releases of Q4 2006 to Q3 2009 (8-K Exhibit 99 or
99.1: the reported results, the outlook tables, segment results, the statement of earnings, the stockholders' equity notes and the
operating data), the Q4 2005 to Q3 2006 releases for the year-ago backlog, the FY1998-FY2008 10-Ks (FY1998-FY2000 plain text; five-year
summaries, segment tables, backlog charts, the statement of earnings and its share counts, the balance sheet and cash flows, Items 1 and
1A), the Q4 2003-Q4 2005 releases for any EPS excluding unusual items (none; no Q4 2002 release was filed on EDGAR), and every other 8-K of October 2006 to January 2010 by its
items: none changes a guided number (below). The 10-Qs were not needed: every guide and every new dividend rate is in a release. The
fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows: each figure is read from the row it appears in, by its label under
an anchored heading, the row is asserted present in its own filing, and every growth rate, margin, margin change and rule-T value is
computed, not typed; 248 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (248/248). Each source's date comes from
EDGAR's acceptance time (before 2003 EDGAR records the filing date only), each quarter's period end from EDGAR's period of report; the
source ids are `LM1`-`LM27`. Decided on 2026-11-16, before any LMT model was built or any LMT outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** LMT is the NYSE common stock. Yahoo's series carries the 1995-03-16 factor (1.63, the combination of Lockheed and
  Martin Marietta) and the 2-for-1 split of 1999-01-04; both precede every per-share fact in the fact sheet (the history starts with
  FY2003), so Yahoo's close is the price as traded: $106.50 on 2008-01-04, $75.35 on 2009-12-31. The builder refuses a vintage with a
  per-share year before the last split.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year (the quarters end on the last Sunday of the quarter's last month from 2008; EDGAR's periods of
  report). The three dates of January 2008 before the Q4 2007 print have FY2007 as the current year.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q4 2006 to Q3 2009 was accepted before the open on its release day (06:35-07:42 ET), always a
  Tuesday or a Thursday, so each week is dated the next trading day: 2008-01-25, 2008-04-23, 2008-07-23, 2008-10-22, 2009-01-23,
  2009-04-22, 2009-07-22 and 2009-10-21. The FY2006 10-K was accepted 2007-02-26 17:21 ET (dated 2007-02-27), the FY2007 10-K 2008-02-28
  16:21 ET (dated 2008-02-29), the FY2008 10-K 2009-02-26 13:09 ET, during the session. A Q4 print extends the history (`fy_actual`) from
  its release to the 10-K.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS, from continuing operations where the five-year summary reports the line,** each year from the latest 10-K that
  reports it: 2003 $2.34, 2004 $2.83, 2005 $4.10, 2006 $5.80, 2007 $7.10, 2008 $7.86 (no restatement across the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks).
  - **Per-share effects stay in** (the NKE FY2008 rule). Every release and 10-K lists the year's unusual items with their per-share
    effect (2007: "increased net earnings by $105 million ($0.25 per share)"), and no filing publishes an EPS excluding them for 2002-2008
    (the Q4 2003-Q4 2008 releases and the FY2002-FY2008 10-Ks were searched); nothing is derived. The effects are 2003 -$0.22 (with the early repayment of debt), 2004
    -$0.02, 2005 +$0.25, 2006 +$0.45, 2007 +$0.25, 2008 +$0.31, each a fraction of the year's earnings, so no year 2003-2008 is excluded.
  - **FY2002 is excluded** (the AAPL FY2002 test). Its unusual items "decreased earnings from continuing operations before income taxes by
    $1,112 million, $632 million after tax ($1.40 per diluted share)" (FY2002 10-K), more than its $533 million of earnings from continuing
    operations ($1.18 per diluted share), and no per-share figure excluding them was published: the FY2002 10-K's "Adjusting for the
    unusual items and the adoption of FAS 142, earnings from continuing operations would have been $1.2 billion in 2002" is in dollars only
    (the XOM 1997 rule). So the history and the P/E window start with FY2003 (`pe_window_start` 2003-01-01; the ACN FY02 rule): a 5.0-year
    window on 2008-01-04, 7.0 years on 2009-12-31. The FY2001 10-K's continuing-operations figures excluding nonrecurring and unusual items
    (1999 $1.48, 2000 $1.17, 2001 $1.60) are company figures, but they precede the excluded year, so no window reaches them.
  - Revenue and diluted shares span the same years (FY2003's 450.0 million shares from the FY2005 10-K, the latest that reports the year).
- **Guides: the fiscal year only, never a quarter.** Each release's outlook table gives net sales, segment operating profit, diluted EPS and
  cash from operations for the year, in a "Current Update" column beside the previous outlook (the column order flips from the Q1 2009
  release, so the builder's generator reads each table's header); the third-quarter release adds a preliminary outlook for the next year.
  The outlook includes no unusual item before it is booked ("It is the Corporation's practice not to incorporate adjustments ... for ...
  unusual activities until such transactions have been consummated"); booked ones are in it (Q1 2008: "Unusual items, net | 15"). Method r2
  maps them as follows:
  - current-FY EPS: the diluted EPS guide midpoint: FY2007 $6.70-6.85 (Q3 2007 release) to 2008-01-18; FY2008 $7.05-7.25 (Q4 2007),
    $7.15-7.35 (Q1 2008), $7.45-7.60 (Q2 2008) and $7.55-7.70 (Q3 2008); FY2009 $7.05-7.25 (Q4 2008: the FAS/CAS pension adjustment
    turns from income of $125 million to expense of $470 million), $7.15-7.35 (Q1 2009 and Q2 2009) and $7.40-7.60 (Q3 2009);
  - BASE growth and the growth factor: no next-quarter guide, so the fiscal-year net sales guide read against the last full year (the PFE
    and CAT rule): FY2007 $41.0-41.75 billion on FY06's $39.620B (+3.5% to +5.4%), FY2008 $41.8-42.8 billion (-0.1% to +2.2% on FY07's
    $41.862B) and $41.9-42.9 billion from the Q2 2008 release, FY2009 $44.7-45.7 billion (+4.6% to +6.9% on FY08's $42.731B) throughout;
  - no margin step: the segment operating profit guide is a dollar range, display only (no margin is derived from two guided figures: the
    MSFT, AAPL and AVGO rule), and the cash-from-operations bound ("≥ $4,200") and ROIC are display only too;
  - the preliminary outlooks (FY2008 in the Q3 2007 release, FY2009 in Q3 2008, FY2010 in Q3 2009) are superseded by the Q4 release before
    their year is current on any date.
- **Dividends,** each quarterly rate from the first filing that states it: $0.35 (Q4 2006 release), $0.42 (Q3 2007 release, "declared on
  September 27, 2007"), $0.57 (Q3 2008, declared September 25, 2008) and $0.63 (Q3 2009, declared September 24, 2009). The September
  declarations were announced without an 8-K, so each is dated by the release that follows (this can only lag).
- **Signals.** Five, with ACN's weights: backlog growth (0.20: total backlog at the quarter's end against the year-ago quarter's end, the
  year-ago figure from that quarter's own release, the MSFT rule), net sales growth (0.20), segment operating profit growth (0.15),
  diluted EPS growth (0.15) and the segment operating margin change (0.15: segment operating profit on net sales, the release's "Total
  operating segments" margin), plus the theme slot at 2/4. Each value is the release's own, against the year-ago quarter as the same
  release shows it (the 2007 releases' segment profit includes interest income, which the Q4 2007 release reclassifies for both years).
- **Thresholds by rule T over 1997-2006,** the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04: each change from the latest 10-K
  published by then that tabulates both years, as tabulated; measures tabulated for fewer years take the changes the filings give (the
  AVGO rule). Backlog comes from the FY1998-FY2000 10-Ks' charts and the five-year summaries; seams stay in (discontinued operations
  restate 1999 and 2000 backlog and net sales in later 10-Ks). Segment operating profit and the segment margin are tabulated on one basis
  only from the FY2002 10-K, after the 8-K of 2003-01-16 moved unusual items, the FAS/CAS pension adjustment and stock-based compensation
  out of the segments: the FY1998-FY2001 10-Ks report segments that include them, with a Corporate and Other segment, a different measure.
  EPS takes the FY2006 history (FY2003-FY2006; the F and SO rule), as the 10-Ks' 1997-2006 values run through a loss (2000) and a $0.10
  year (2001). The values and sources are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives the thresholds and refuses to build if they
  differ.

  | Signal | Annual changes | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | backlog | 1997-2006: -6.64, -3.64, 1.25, 22.92, 29.4, -1.24, 9.25, -3.79, 1.13, 1.44 % | -14 / -7 / 1 / 29 % |
  | net sales | 1997-2006: 4.44, -7.04, -3.14, -1.83, -2.25, 10.79, 19.74, 11.63, 4.75, 6.47 % | -19 / -7 / 5 / 20 % |
  | segment operating profit | 2001-2006: -0.18, 18.2, 22.18, 20.58, 15.32, 17.95 % | -18 / 0 / 18 / 22 % |
  | diluted EPS (the FY2006 history) | 2004-2006: 20.94, 44.88, 41.46 % | 0 / 21 / 41 / 45 % |
  | segment margin | 2001-2006: 14.8, 47.6, 15.5, 62.2, 84.6, 99.4 bp | -30 / 10 / 50 / 100 bp |

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2** (the CAT and SO precedent). The "why" quotes each 10-K: "In 2006, 84% of our net sales were made to the
  U.S. Government, either as a prime contractor or as a subcontractor" (the same share in 2007 and 2008; the FY2008 10-K adds "Each of our
  business segments is heavily dependent on sales to the U.S. Government") and the risk factor "Reduced funding for defense procurement
  and research and development programs could adversely affect our ability to grow or maintain our sales and profitability" (from the
  FY2007 10-K "could result in terminated or delayed contracts and adversely affect"). Sales that depend on appropriations are not earnings
  that are the cycle, and the 10-Ks never call the business cyclical. OFFSHORE is the only theme in the registry live on these dates (from
  2004-11-05); it is scoped to offshore delivery taking share in Western consulting, systems integration and outsourcing, and Lockheed
  Martin's 10-Ks, whose IT services are sold to government agencies, name no offshore or low-cost foreign competition (the FY2006-FY2008
  10-Ks searched for "offshore", "India" and "low-cost"). So the watch list is empty, the builder refuses events, and it refuses a date on
  which a theme it has no reading of is live. The kind changes the class label only.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the vintage's segments by net sales (five in the FY2006 10-K, four after the 2007
  realignment), the total from the net sales guide midpoint; the EPS check runs on the last year's pre-tax margin and tax rate, on the
  release's average diluted shares, so it does not see the 2009 pension expense.
- **Adds nothing:** the reaffirmation of the 2007 outlook in the 8-K of 2007-08-10 (no numbers, the ACN rule), the segment realignment
  8-K of 2007-02-22 (the Q1 2007 release carries the realigned outlook), the pension scenarios of the Q3 2008 8-K's Item 7.01
  (illustrations, not a guide), the XBRL, annual-meeting, officer, director, bylaw, FCPA-policy and compensation 8-Ks, the
  convertible-debenture conversion and redemption 8-Ks (2007-06-01, 2008-06-02, 2008-06-27) and the debt offering 8-Ks (2008-03-12,
  2009-11-16).
- **Anachronism list:** three Lockheed Martin segment names first seen in its filings after 2009 ("Information Systems & Global
  Solutions", 2010-06-02; "Mission Systems and Training", 2012-10-24; "Rotary and Mission Systems", 2016-10-25) join `taxonomy_eras.json`,
  each dated from the first filing under Lockheed Martin's CIK that uses it (EDGAR full-text search; all accepted before the open). No model
  of any ticker contains them, so no output changes. Names of other companies first named in later Lockheed Martin filings were left out,
  as they predate those filings.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):
- **Controls:** altering one value of each print (its backlog), each Q4 print's full-year net sales, each vintage (its last year's net
  sales), each guide (its EPS range) and each dividend changes no model dated before its publication and changes the first weekly date on
  or after it: 27 of 37; the other 10 are inert, superseded before any built date (the Q4 2006 and Q1 2007 prints and the Q4 2006 full-year
  actuals, the FY2007 guides of the Q4 2006-Q2 2007 releases, the three preliminary outlooks and the $0.35 dividend). Each reaches exactly
  its scope (a print's backlog 26 dates, 13 as the latest print and 13 as the previous one; the Q4 actuals 5 dates, to the 10-K).
- **Leak scan:** 0 hits in 11,860 (model, later token) pairs: the source ids, strings and figures (four significant digits or more) of
  every fact published after each model's date, after dropping 3,472 tokens an earlier fact or the engine already carries. A first pass
  flagged 10 models (2008-01-25 to 2008-02-22 and 2009-01-23 to 2009-02-20) whose tax note carries the income tax and pre-tax figures
  ($1,335M and $4,368M; $1,485M and $4,702M) that the FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks repeat: the Q4 releases published them first, so they are
  dropped. A planted later figure and source id in a copy of an early model are found.
- **`retro_tool run` passes on all 105 dates** with no warning.
- **Firewall** (run after the build was committed, before any outcome): passes at the 13 cutoffs above (every print, vintage and dividend
  date of the range, 2008-07-01, 2009-01-01 and 2010-01-01), 0 files changed and no planted text (3 to 105 dates each). The LMT plant is a
  print whose backlog, net sales, segment operating profit, segment margin, EPS, notes, labels and raw figures are absurd, with absurd
  full-year actuals for the year after the latest vintage, a later guide with every guided field, and a later vintage whose every quoted
  text and figure is planted. A full rebuild is byte-identical.
- **Regression:** no shared code changed (the firewall gains an LMT branch); the 2008-2009 dates of CAT, SO and BMY rebuild byte-identical.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **CHEAP on all 105 dates, tier BUY on all 105, all eight robustness variants agreeing on every date** (the class COMPOUNDER AT LOW
  PRICE). Ratio B is 0.03-0.16 to 2008-10-03; from 2008-10-10 the price is under the BEAR case on 61 of the 65 dates (Ratio B at or
  below zero; the other four, in May, June, September and December 2009, at 0.00-0.03, the price within $4 of it).
- **The upside is the short history's.** With FY2002 excluded, BULL is the FY2003-FY2006 EPS CAGR (+35.3%/yr), then FY2003-FY2007
  (+32.0%) and FY2003-FY2008 (+27.4%), and XBULL the FY2004-FY2006 run (+43.2%/yr): the recovery from 2003's $2.34, when the FAS/CAS
  pension adjustment and unusual items were large charges. BEAR is the 0% cap on every date (no year of the history fell). BASE is the
  net sales guide plus a 1.0-1.9%/yr buyback: +5.5% (FY2007), +2.4% to +2.6% (FY2008) and +7.7% (FY2009).
- **The window is that of realized EPS from 2003:** median 15.6x on 2008-01-04 falling to 14.5x on 2009-12-31; the calendar-year lows are
  17.6x (2003), 15.5x, 13.0x, 11.0x (2006), 12.9-13.5x (2007), then 2008's 8.6x (2008-11-20) and 2009's 7.8x (2009-03-11) as they join,
  so the floor (their median, rounded down) is 14x to 2008-01-18, 13x from 2008-01-25 and 12x from 2008-10-10.
- **2008: the price at the median, then the floor.** To 2008-10-03 $99.62-117.27 is 13.7-16.2x the FY07 and FY08 guides (the 19th-60th
  percentile), 6-20% over the floor; on 2008-10-10 and 2008-10-17 $87-91 is 11.6-12.1x (1st-2nd percentile), at the floor; from the Q3
  2008 print to 2009-01-16 $72-86 is 9.5-11.2x the FY08 guide (0th-4th percentile), 6-21% under it.
- **2009: under the floor on every date.** $59-86 is 8.2-11.9x the current-year EPS (FY08's guide to 2009-01-16, then the FY09 guides,
  $7.15 to $7.50 at the midpoints), the 0th-12th percentile, 1-31% under the floor.
- **The proxy composite** is 2.65 on Q3 2007, 2.20 on Q4 2007-Q3 2008 (the EPS signal at BEAR on every 2008 print, under its 21% BASE),
  1.75 on Q4 2008 (segment profit -0.1%, the margin -31bp), 1.90 on Q1 2009, 1.75 on Q2 2009 and 1.70 on Q3 2009 (EPS -4.0%, -12.6%
  and +7.8%, the margin +4bp, -55bp and -37bp). The market composite is below it on every date: 1.74-2.11 to June 2008, 1.00-1.81 from
  July 2008 and 1.10-1.50 in 2009.

How far each call moves the classes (the 105 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline with `retro_tool`'s own
classifier; no outcome consulted):
- FY2002 kept at GAAP $1.18 (the history and the window from FY2002): no class, no tier;
- EPS excluding the unusual items' per-share effects, derived (2003 $2.56 to 2008 $7.55): no class, no tier;
- every signal at its BEAR value: 39 classes (CHEAP to RICH on 37 and to FAIR on 2, 2008-01-04 to 2008-10-03), no tier; at its XBULL
  value: none;
- the EPS signal alone at its BULL threshold (it sits at BASE or BEAR on every date): none; the segment margin signal alone at BEAR: none.
The 2008 CHEAP calls to October rest on the signals (39 classes move at BEAR); from the Q3 2008 print the price under the EPP floor
carries every call, and no encoding above moves it.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows how defense budgets and Lockheed Martin's programs went after 2009: backlog, net sales,
  segment operating profit, diluted EPS and the segment margin (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; 39 classes move at BEAR);
- rule T's segment measures on six years and EPS on three (the history's), where the earlier filings report other measures;
- excluding FY2002 by the AAPL test, which starts the history at the FY2003 trough and makes BULL and XBULL +27% to +43%/yr (no class
  moves if FY2002 is kept);
- GAAP EPS with the unusual items' per-share effects in, the published figures, rather than figures derived from them (no class);
- DURABLE, risk 2, and OFFSHORE read as out of scope for a government IT business (label only).

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/LMT/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

below, every one of which was made before any 2010-2013 model was built or any 2010-2013 outcome computed. The ISO week of 2013-12-30 to
2014-01-05 is dated 2013-12-31, so a 2014 range starts on 2014-01-06.

         2009-10-20 2010-01-01 2010-01-28 2010-02-25 2010-04-21 2010-07-27 2010-10-19 2011-01-01 2011-01-27 2011-02-28 2011-04-26 \
         2011-07-26 2011-10-26 2012-01-01 2012-01-26 2012-02-23 2012-04-26 2012-07-24 2012-10-24 2012-10-30 2013-01-01 2013-01-24 \
         2013-02-28 2013-04-23 2013-07-23 2013-10-22 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c LMT; done

Read, by the session's model directly: the earnings releases of Q4 2009 to Q3 2013 (8-K Exhibit 99 or 99.1: the summary results, the
outlook tables, the restatement tables of the Q1 2011 release, the statements of earnings and the operating data), the FY2009-FY2012
10-Ks (five-year summaries, segment tables, the EPS notes, balance sheets and cash flows, Items 1 and 1A) and every other 8-K of January
2010 to January 2014 by its items. The 2010-2013 records are generated by the same script from the filings' rows (every figure read from
its labelled row, the row asserted present in its own filing); the 2006-2009 records regenerate exactly as before except the correction
below. 510 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (510/510). The new source ids are `LM28`-`LM47`.

- **Vintages.** The FY2009 10-K (accepted 2010-02-25 15:13 ET, during the session), FY2010 (2011-02-25 18:26 ET, so 2011-02-28), FY2011
  (2012-02-23 14:21 ET) and FY2012 (2013-02-28 11:47 ET). Each year comes from the latest 10-K that reports it: the FY2010 10-K restates
  2006-2010 for the businesses in discontinued operations (FY2006 $5.73, FY2007 $7.03, FY2008 $7.74, FY2009 $7.71, FY2010 $7.18), the

  FY2008 $7.64, FY2009 $7.63, FY2010 $7.10, FY2011 $7.85), and the FY2012 10-K adds FY2012 $8.36; earlier years keep their last
  publication (FY2003 $2.34, FY2004 $2.83, FY2005 $4.10). FY2002 stays excluded while it is in the decade, and the FY2012 vintage's
  decade (2003-2012) no longer reaches it, so the history starts with FY2003 throughout; the P/E window reaches ten years on 2012-11-30.
- **EPS from continuing operations where reported** (the LOW and UNP rule, as before): from the Q2 2010 release PAE, and from Q3 2010 most
  of EIG, are discontinued operations, so a print takes the release's diluted EPS from continuing operations and the year-ago quarter as
  the same release restates it (the Q3 2013 release's discontinued operations are a tax benefit on a business sold earlier). The EPS
  guide is the release's (labelled "from continuing operations" from the Q2 2010 release to the Q4 2012 release).
- **Releases that republish earlier years restate them until a later 10-K** (the PFE and CAT `restates` encoding, EPS only): the Q4 2010
  release's FY2009 from continuing operations ($7.71, against the FY2009 10-K's $7.78), the Q1 2011 release's table "As Reported and
  Adjusted to Reflect the Change in Revenue Recognition" (FY2008 $7.64, FY2009 $7.60, FY2010 $7.03) and the Q4 2011 release's FY2010
  ($7.10). Revenue stays the vintage's (the encoding is EPS only; the adjustment is 0.1% of net sales).
- **One-off items keep their per-share effects** (the NKE FY2008 rule): the 2010 health care tax charge and Voluntary Executive Separation
  Program, the 2011-2013 severance charges (shown outside segment profit as an unusual, then special, item) and tax benefits. No filing of
  2010-2013 publishes an EPS excluding them (every release searched), and no year fails the AAPL FY2002 test.
- **Guides, as before, with three new cases:** the current column is found by its header ("Current Update", from the Q3 2012 release
  "Current", in the Q1 2013 release "Current Outlook"); words in it keep the last numeric range (the ACN rule): the Q1 2013 release's net
  sales "Low-end of range" and "No change" elsewhere, and the Q2 2013 release's net sales "No Change", so the Q4 2012 release's $44.5-46.0
  billion stands until the Q3 2013 release's "~$45,000", a level stated as about and read as $45.0 billion (the CAT rule). Current-FY EPS:
  FY2010 $7.15-7.35, $7.00-7.20 (the health care charge), $7.15-7.35 and $6.75-6.95 (the separation program); FY2011 $6.70-7.00 to
