### LMT 2014-2017: Sikorsky, the IS&GS divestiture and its seam, "about" levels, five live themes out of scope

208 weekly dates, 2014-01-10 to 2017-12-29, on the same fact sheet, builder, engine and method (r2), with the 1997-2006 rule-T thresholds
frozen. Built on 2026-11-17, after the 2008-2013 dates had been scored: their findings are hindsight and were not read for any decision
below, every one of which was made before any 2014-2017 model was built or any 2014-2017 outcome computed. The range starts on the
Monday after the last built week (2013-12-31 is the date of the ISO week to 2014-01-05).

```bash
python3 retro/build_lmt.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2009-12-31                   # unchanged: rebuilt byte-identical
python3 retro/build_lmt.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                   # unchanged: rebuilt byte-identical
python3 retro/build_lmt.py --weekly 2014-01-06 2017-12-31                   # 208 dates, 2014-01-10 .. 2017-12-29
for d in staging/retrospective/LMT/201[4-7]-*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series LMT
for c in 2014-01-01 2014-01-23 2014-02-18 2014-04-22 2014-07-22 2014-10-21 2015-01-01 2015-01-27 2015-02-09 2015-04-21 2015-07-20 \
         2015-08-04 2015-10-20 2015-12-12 2016-01-01 2016-01-26 2016-02-25 2016-04-26 2016-07-19 2016-10-25 2017-01-01 2017-01-24 \
         2017-02-10 2017-04-25 2017-07-18 2017-10-24 2018-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c LMT; done
```

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the earnings releases of Q4 2013 to Q3 2017 (8-K Exhibit 99.1:
the summary results, the outlook tables, the statements of earnings, the cash deployment and dividend paragraphs, the operating data),
the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks (five-year summaries, the segment tables, the EPS notes, balance sheets and cash flows, Items 1 and 1A) and every
other 8-K of January 2014 to December 2017 by its items and exhibits (the Q2 2015 8-K also carries the Sikorsky release and the webcast
charts, which repeat the release's outlook). The filing list was fetched to 2017-12-31; nothing after the Q3 2017 release was read. The
2014-2017 records are generated by a script from the filings' rows (every figure read from its labelled row under an anchored heading,
the row asserted present in its own filing; every growth rate, margin and rate computed); 286 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`
against their own filings (286/286). The new source ids are `LM48`-`LM67`, by publication date. The 2008-2013 records are unchanged.

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q4 2013 to Q3 2017 was accepted before the open (06:30-07:37 ET). Q2 2015 came on a Monday
  (2015-07-20, with the Sikorsky agreement), the others on Tuesdays or a Thursday (Q4 2013), so each week is dated the next trading day.
  The FY2013 10-K was accepted 2014-02-14 16:51 ET, after the close, and is dated 2014-02-18 (Presidents' Day between); the FY2014 10-K
  2015-02-09 12:39 ET, during the session; the FY2015 10-K 2016-02-24 17:21 ET (dated 2016-02-25) and the FY2016 10-K 2017-02-09 16:32 ET
  (dated 2017-02-10).
- **Vintages: the ten fiscal years to the latest one,** each year from the latest 10-K that reports it (2004-2013, 2005-2014, 2006-2015,
  2007-2016). Their decades no longer reach the excluded FY2002, so the P/E window is the full ten years (`pe_window_start` none). One-off
  items keep their per-share effects (the NKE FY2008 rule): the 2013 goodwill impairment ($0.54) and severance ($0.40), the 2014 goodwill
  impairment ($0.33), the 2015 severance ($0.21), Sikorsky transaction costs ($0.09) and full-year R&D credit (+$0.23), the 2016 severance
  ($0.17) and AWE consolidation gain (+$0.34). No filing of 2014-2017 publishes an EPS excluding them, and none is over half a year's
  earnings (the AAPL FY2002 test).
- **Sikorsky** (acquired 2015-11-06) is in the results from that day, under Mission Systems and Training, renamed Rotary and Mission
  Systems from the Q3 2016 release. Growth stays as published (no organic figure is used, the house rule): backlog +23.7% to +32.4% from
  Q4 2015 to Q3 2016 against year-ago figures without it ($15.6 billion of Sikorsky backlog at the end of 2015), net sales +10.9% to +19.4%
  from Q1 2016 to Q4 2016, and the FY2016 net sales guides of $49.5-51.5 billion read on FY2015's $46.132 billion (+7.3% to +11.6%).
- **IS&GS: continuing operations until it was divested,** as the Q4 2015 release says ("Until closing, IS&GS will operate as a business
  segment of the Corporation and financial results for the IS&GS business segment will be reported in continuing operations"); the Q3 2016
  release (2016-10-25) classifies it as discontinued for all periods, and each print from it takes EPS from continuing operations and the
  year-ago quarter as the same release restates it. Three encodings follow from the established rules, none decided for this case:
  - the Q4 2016 release republishes FY2015 from continuing operations ($9.93, against the FY2015 10-K's $11.46), so it restates FY2015's
    EPS until the FY2016 10-K (`restates`, EPS only: 2017-01-25 and 2017-02-03);
  - the FY2016 10-K restates 2012-2016 without IS&GS ($6.99, $8.27, $10.09, $9.93, $12.38; net sales $40.573 billion to $47.248 billion),
    while 2007-2011 keep their last publication with IS&GS: a seam as published (the LOW and PEP rule). Its 2011-2012 step (FY2011's $7.85
    to FY2012's $6.99, -11.0%) is the vintage's worst year, so it sets BEAR from 2017-02-10; the lower 2012-2016 EPS also lifts those
    years' calendar P/E lows, and the floor (their median, rounded down) from 9x to 11x;
  - revenue is the vintage's (the LMT `restates` encoding is EPS only): from the Q3 2016 print to the Q4 2016 print (13 dates,
    2016-10-26 to 2017-01-20) the FY2016 guide without IS&GS (about $46.5 billion) is read against FY2015's $46.132 billion with it
    (+0.8%), and FY2015's $11.46 stays in the P/E series. The pro forma statements of the 8-K of 2016-08-22 (FY2015 net sales $40.536
    billion and diluted EPS from continuing operations $10.24 without IS&GS) are illustrations, not a restatement, and add nothing (the PFE
    rule); the seam is measured below.
  - The year-ago backlog stays the year-ago release's (recast and pro forma backlog tables unused): Q4 2016, Q1 2017 and Q2 2017 compare
    backlog without IS&GS against year-ago figures with it (-3.4% to -4.5%).
- **The 2016 standard on employee share-based payment awards,** adopted in Q2 2016 as of January 1, 2016 ("reported the impacts as though
  the standard had been adopted on Jan. 1, 2016"; $0.37 a share in the first half), stays in GAAP EPS with no figure without it (the ACN
  FY17 rule); the Q1 2017 release compares against Q1 2016 as restated ($2.61).
- **Guides, as before:** the fiscal year only; the current column found by its header ("Current Update", "Current Outlook", and in the
  Q3 2016 release "Current Outlook Adjusted for IS&GS", beside "July Outlook" and "July Outlook Adjusted for IS&GS"); words keep the last
  numeric range (net sales "No Change" in the Q1 2014, Q1 2015 and Q2 2015 releases; cash from operations "No Change" in Q1-Q3 2015, the
  bound kept for display); a level stated as about is a number (the CAT rule, as for Q3 2013): net sales ~$45,000 million and EPS ~$11.15
  (Q3 2014), ~$45,000 million and ~$11.30 (Q3 2015), ~$46,500 million and ~$12.10 (Q3 2016). Current-FY EPS: FY2014 $10.25-10.55,

  billion), then ~$45.0 billion; FY2015 $43.5-45.0 billion, then ~$45.0 billion; FY2016 as above, then ~$46.5 billion; FY2017 $49.4-50.6
  billion to $50.0-51.2 billion on FY16's $47.248 billion (+4.6% to +8.4%). The "Financial Trends" paragraphs of the Q3 releases (2015 to
  2018) are words about years not current on any date before a numeric outlook, and add nothing.
- **Dividends:** $1.50 a quarter from the Q3 2014 release, $1.65 (Q3 2015), $1.82 (Q3 2016) and $2.00 (Q3 2017, "As previously reported
  on Sept. 28, 2017": no 8-K that day, so the release dates it, which can only lag). Buyback words are each release's own.
- **Adds nothing:** the officer, director, compensation, vote, blackout and bylaw 8-Ks; the FCPA-policy 8-K (2014-03-27); the pension-plan
  amendment 8-K of 2014-07-01 (Item 7.01: the 2014 pension estimates "will be updated and communicated" with the Q2 release, the 2010-03-31

multiple sits at the 69th to 100th percentile of its window from the first date and above the 90th from 2015.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:

## MU (Micron Technology): the twenty-fifth ticker, in staging, 2008-2009

The MU series is built apart from the other twenty-four and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/MU.json`), builder (`retro/build_mu.py`, the NVDA builder with Micron's fiscal calendar, figures in millions, no guides
and an exchange change) and engine (`retro/templates/mu_engine.py.tmpl`, the NVDA engine with Micron's own rule-T thresholds). The
method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an MU model, and neither does the live
`mu_signal_model.py` (a 2026 analysis: not read for this series). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/MU/`, beside the others, with
the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009 ("same rules as before"); the code is the newest branch
of the repository (its commit "Stops and S&P 500 hedges on the combined yield-tilt book", 2026-11-17), every other recent retro branch
being its ancestor.

```bash
python3 retro/build_mu.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                    # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_mu.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                    # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/MU/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series MU
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-04-03 2008-04-08 2008-06-27 2008-07-08 2008-10-02 2008-10-28 2008-12-24 2009-01-13 2009-04-03 \
         2009-06-26 2009-09-30 2009-10-28 2009-12-18 2009-12-23 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c MU; done
```

Two ranges, as for NVDA, CAT and BMY: the series has 2008-12-31 and no 2009-01-02.

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the earnings releases of Q4 FY07 to Q1 FY10 (8-K exhibit 99.1:
the narrative, the consolidated financial summary, its balance sheet and cash-flow lines and footnotes), the FY1998-FY2009 10-Ks (the
FY1998 10-K, FY1999 10-K405 and FY2000 10-K are plain text: Item 6 selected data, the statements of operations, balance sheets and cash
flows, the segment notes, Items 1, 1A and 5, the MD&A on other operating income and taxes), the 10-Qs of Q1 FY07 to Q1 FY09 for the
year-ago quarters' inventories, and every other 8-K of June 2007 to February 2010 by its items and exhibits (none changes a guided
number; below). The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows: each figure is found in its own filing by
its row label and the numbers typed for it (the script asserts the row exists with exactly those numbers), the row is kept in the fact
sheet, and every growth rate, margin, gap and rule-T value is computed, not typed; every quoted sentence is asserted present in its own
filing; the 266 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (266/266). Each source's date comes from EDGAR's
acceptance time (UTC in the submissions file, converted to ET; before 2002 EDGAR gives the filing date only); the source ids are
`MU1`-`MU30`. Decided on 2026-11-17, before any MU model was built or any MU outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** MU is the NYSE common stock (the NASDAQ Global Select Market from 2009-12-30, below). Yahoo's series is adjusted
  for the splits of 1994-04-19, 1995-05-23 and 2000-05-02, all before the P/E window's start (2003-08-29), so its close is the price as
  traded: $6.40 on 2008-01-04, $10.56 on 2009-12-31.
- **Fiscal calendar.** "The Company operates on a 52/53 week fiscal year which ends on the Thursday closest to August 31." (FY2007 10-K):
  FY2007 ended 2007-08-30, FY2008 2008-08-28, FY2009 (53 weeks) 2009-09-03; the builder checks every year end the vintages state. Q1
  FY09 had 14 weeks against 13 (the Q1 FY09 release says so; its values are used as published, and the Q1 FY10 print's note quotes it).
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of the period was accepted after the close (16:01-16:05 ET) and is dated the next trading day:
  2007-10-03, 2007-12-21, 2008-04-03, 2008-06-27, 2008-10-02, 2008-12-24, 2009-04-03, 2009-06-26, 2009-09-30, 2009-12-23. Four of
  those are Fridays and meet their own close (public before the open; the AVGO rule): 2007-12-21 (before the series), 2008-06-27,
  2009-04-03 and 2009-06-26. The others
  put the week's date on the next trading day: 2008-04-04, 2008-10-03, 2008-12-26, 2009-10-01, 2009-12-24. The FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks
  were accepted after the close (dated 2007-10-29 and 2008-10-28), the FY2009 10-K during the session (2009-10-28 13:00 ET). A Q4 print
  extends the history from its release to the 10-K: FY2008 from 2008-10-02, FY2009 from 2009-09-30 (4 dates each).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS,** each year from the latest filing that reports it. Micron published no EPS excluding one-offs for any year
  in the history; its releases' non-GAAP figures (from Q2 FY08) exclude the goodwill impairment and, from Q4 FY08, inventory write-downs
  and NAND price adjustments, and every year they cover is a loss on them too. The ten fiscal years to FY2007 hold losses in FY1998,
  FY1999, FY2001, FY2002, FY2003 and FY2007, so:
  - **FY2003 is excluded and takes the years before it** ($(2.11) a diluted share, FY2007 10-K; the PFE 2003 and CMCSA 2003 rule for an
    excluded year that is not the latest): the history starts with FY2004 and the P/E window on 2003-08-29, the day after FY2003 ended
    (`pe_window_start`; 4.4 years on 2008-01-04, 6.3 at the end of 2009). FY2004 $0.24 and FY2005 $0.29 stay at GAAP: their listed items
    are small fractions of their income (FY2004: a $22.5M restructure credit, $7.2M from Virginia and $17.2M of currency losses against
    $157.2M; FY2005: $13M of equipment gains and $12M of anti-dumping receipts against $188M).
  - **FY2006 is excluded, a year distorted by one-off benefits** (the AVGO FY2018 mirror test). Its $408M of net income ($0.57 a
    diluted share) includes "$230 million of net proceeds for the sale of the Company’s existing NAND Flash memory designs and certain
    related technology to Intel" and "$23 million in additional amounts expected to be reimbursed resulting from the extension of an
    economic development agreement" (FY2007 10-K; the FY2006 10-K lists the same two items): $253M of listed benefits against $155M of income without them, so reported
    EPS is 2.7 times the $0.21 without them. The test holds on every reading: the $230M alone against $178M, and with the year's whole
    $18M tax provision charged to the gain (U.S. taxes were "substantially offset by reductions in the valuation allowance"), $212M
    against $196M. No figure excluding them was published.
  - **FY2006 leaves only itself** (a new reading of an existing rule, decided before any MU date was built): on 2008-01-04 FY2006 is not
    the latest year, so the PFE 2003 rule would start the history after it, and FY2007 is a loss, so no year would remain and no date
    could be built. The r2 note for a distorted latest year gives the reason that rule yields ("starting the history and the window
    after it would leave neither, so only the year itself leaves them"); it is applied here to a year that is not the latest, the one case
    where the same reason holds. Whether r2 should say so, or should instead leave MU unbuildable in 2008-2009, is left to the owner.
  - **FY2007, FY2008 and FY2009 are losses with no company figure that is not a loss** ($(0.42), $(2.10) and $(2.29); FY08's non-GAAP
    $(1.32)): each is excluded as the latest year when its Q4 print comes and stays a gap after (the NKE FY2018 and XOM FY2020 rule; F's
    2006-2008). Their revenue and shares stay; their own days leave the P/E window ("4.4-yr ex-FY06 ex-FY07" on 2008-01-04, "ex-FY08"
    from 2008-10-03, "ex-FY09" from 2009-10-01); growth is measured only between years in the history.
  - So **FY05's $0.29 is the anchor on all 105 dates** (the rollover rule: no EPS guide in any filing), and the days of the current
    fiscal year are priced on it: FY2008's until its Q4 print excludes it (2008-10-02), then FY2009's until 2009-09-30, then FY2010's
    (from 2009-09-04).
- **Revenue and shares,** each year from the latest filing that reports it, from FY2004: net sales from the selected data (FY2004 from
  the FY2008 10-K on the 2009 dates); diluted shares from the statements of operations (FY2004's 646M from the FY2006 10-K, FY2005's
  702.0M from the FY2007 10-K, FY2006's 725.1M from the FY2008 10-K). The buyback term is net issuance: -5.6%/yr (FY2004-FY2007),
  -4.4%/yr (to FY2008), -4.2%/yr (to FY2009).
- **No guide in any filing.** No release, 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K of the period guides revenue, EPS or a margin, in numbers or in words:
  the releases estimate fiscal-year capital expenditures ("between $2.5 billion and $3 billion for the 2008 fiscal year"), which method
  r2 has no input for, and the 10-Ks' and 10-Qs' forward words are about product lines (NAND Flash, DDR3, solid-state drives, Imaging
  units), not the company's revenue; the 10-Ks' next-quarter SG&A and R&D estimates are expense lines. None is encoded (the F 2008-2011
  reading). BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth plus the buyback (the UNP rule), and there is no margin step. The builder refuses
  any guide until an encoding is decided.
- **No dividend:** "The Company has not declared or paid cash dividends since 1996 and does not intend to pay cash dividends on its
  common stock for the foreseeable future." (each 10-K's Item 5). No repurchase program.
- **Signals.** The AVGO and NVDA semiconductor set, with ACN's weights: net sales growth (0.20), the gross-margin change (0.20), growth of
  R&D plus SG&A less net sales growth (0.15, lower is better), inventory growth less net sales growth (0.15, lower is better) and the
  operating-margin change (0.15), plus the theme slot at 2/4. Each value is the release's own against the year-ago quarter in the same
  release, in whole millions as published; inventories against the year-ago quarter's end from that quarter's 10-Q (a Q4's from the
  release's prior year-end column). Charges stay in, as published (the inventory write-downs in cost of goods sold, the $463M goodwill
  impairment of Q2 FY08 and the restructure lines in the operating margin); the opex gap takes the SG&A and R&D lines only.
- **Thresholds by rule T over FY1998-FY2007,** the decade of the FY2007 10-K (the vintage public on 2008-01-04): ten changes between
  consecutive fiscal years, each from the latest 10-K published by 2008-01-04 that reports the lines it needs for both years (revenue,
  gross margin and operating income from the five-year selected data; SG&A and R&D with net sales from the three-year statements of
  operations; year-end inventories with net sales from each year's own 10-K). Seams stay in, as published: the selected data from the
  FY2001 10-K on are restated for the discontinued PC operations of Micron Electronics (FY1998's net sales $1,564.5M against the FY1998
  10-K's $3,011.9M), while the FY1998 and FY1999 opex changes (FY1999 10-K405 and FY2000 10-K) and the FY1998-FY2000 inventory changes
  come from 10-Ks that still consolidate them. The raw figures and values are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives every
  value and threshold and refuses to build if they differ.

### MU 2010-2013: the FY2009 10-K as adjusted, FY10's $1.85, FY2011 and FY2013 excluded by the mirror test

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31, on the same method, builder, engine and rule-T thresholds. The fact sheet only gains facts:
its 2008-2009 content is unchanged (the generator's print loop became a function and its footnote pattern takes "(5)(7)"; the regenerated
2008-2009 part is byte-identical) and the 105 earlier models rebuild byte for byte. No builder change was needed.
Built on 2026-11-17 at the owner's request ("do retrospective analysis for MU, 2010-2013. same rules"), in the same session that had
scored the 2008-2009 dates and written their `FINDINGS.md`, so those outcomes were known when this batch was read. No decision below
uses them: each applies a rule that existed before (the AVGO FY2018 mirror test, the XOM FY2020 and NKE FY2018 gap rules, the UNP 2010
vintage rule, the AVGO timing rule, the UNP BASE rule) or a 2008-2009 encoding. The readings that could still carry hindsight (FY2006
kept as a gap, FY2011 excluded) are listed at the end with how far the other reading moves the classes.

```bash
python3 retro/build_mu.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                    # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for c in 2010-03-04 2010-04-01 2010-06-29 2010-10-08 2010-10-26 2010-12-23 2011-03-24 2011-06-24 2011-09-30 2011-10-25 \
         2011-12-22 2012-03-23 2012-06-21 2012-09-28 2012-10-31 2012-12-21 2013-03-22 2013-06-20 2013-10-11 2013-10-29 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c MU; done
```

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the 15 earnings releases of Q2 FY10 to Q4 FY13 (narratives,
financial summaries, balance-sheet lines and footnotes), the 8-K of 2010-03-04 that retrospectively adjusts the FY2009 10-K (its 8-K text,
ex.99.2 selected data and ex.99.5 financial statements), the FY2010-FY2013 10-Ks (Items 1, 1A, 5, 6, 7 and 8), the 10-Qs of Q2 FY09 to Q3
FY12 for the year-ago quarters' inventories (the 10-Q/As of 2012-11-20, 2013-07-17 and 2013-08-07 re-file exhibits or MD&A text only), and
every other 8-K of February 2010 to January 2014 by its items and exhibits. The source ids are `MU31`-`MU63`. 572 strings were checked
with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (572/572, the 2008-2009 batch's 266 included). Decided on 2026-11-17, before any 2010-2013
model was built or any 2010-2013 outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of the period was accepted after the close (16:00-16:05 ET) and is dated the next trading day.
  Ten of those days are the last trading day of their week and meet their own close (public before the open; the AVGO rule): eight
  Fridays (2010-10-08, 2011-06-24, 2011-09-30, 2012-03-23, 2012-09-28, 2012-12-21, 2013-03-22, 2013-10-11) and two Thursdays before a
  market holiday (2010-04-01, before Good Friday; 2010-12-23, before the Christmas holiday of 2010-12-24). The other five put the week's
  date on the next trading day (2010-06-30, 2011-03-25, 2011-12-23, 2012-06-22, 2013-06-21). The FY2010 and FY2011 10-Ks were accepted during the session (dated 2010-10-26, 2011-10-25); the
  FY2012 10-K after the close of 2012-10-29, when the market was shut for Hurricane Sandy, so it is dated 2012-10-31; the FY2013 10-K after
  the close (2013-10-29). A Q4 print extends the history from its release to the 10-K, as before.
- **The FY2009 10-K as adjusted is a vintage of its own** (the UNP 2010, AAPL 2010 and MSFT 2017 rule for a filing that re-presents the
  10-K). The 8-K of 2010-03-04 (accepted 15:27 ET) re-presents FY2005-FY2009 "to retrospectively adjust portions of the Company's Annual
  Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 3, 2009" for the new noncontrolling-interest and convertible-debt standards:
  FY2007 $(0.43), FY2008 $(2.14), FY2009 $(2.35) (as first reported $(0.42), $(2.10), $(2.29)); FY2005's $0.29 and FY2006's $0.57 are
  unchanged. From that date its years replace the FY2009 10-K's; its wording stays the 10-K's (the AAPL 10-K/A rule).
- **FY2010 at GAAP $1.85, kept.** Its listed items, the $437M gain on the acquisition of Numonyx, its $51M tax benefit, the $56M Inotera
  gain and the $41M NAND price benefit against $64M of antitrust accruals (Q3 and Q4 FY10 releases), net to $521M of benefits against
  $1,329M of income without them: the mirror test is not met. It enters the history with the Q4 FY10 print (2010-10-08) and, after the
  gaps, is the last full year from then to the end of 2013.
- **FY2011 is excluded, a year distorted by one-off benefits** (the AVGO FY2018 mirror test, read as for FY2006). Its $167M of net income
  attributable to Micron ($0.17 a diluted share) includes the "Samsung patent cross-license agreement" gains of $275M, with "charges
  aggregating $45 million in connection with the Samsung cross-license agreement" in taxes ($230M after tax), a $54M gain on the sale of
  the Japan facility with a $74M tax charge, and $15M for the release of a debt guarantee, against the $111M loss on the debt repurchase
  and exchange and a $19M tax charge for a change in tax rates. The Q4 FY11 release (public 2011-09-30) lists them all, so the exclusion
  starts there (the AVGO rule). The Samsung gains alone exceed the year's income without them ($(63)M), and net of every listed item ($95M
  of benefits) they exceed the $72M without them: reported EPS is 2.4 times the $0.07 without them. No figure excluding them was
  published. It is the latest year at its Q4 print, so it leaves only itself and stays a gap after.
- **FY2012 is a loss,** $(1.04) a diluted share (Q4 FY12 release, 2012-09-28): excluded, a gap after (the XOM FY2020 rule).
- **FY2013 is excluded:** its $1,190M ($1.13) "include $1,484 million, or $1.31 per diluted share, in purchase accounting gains relating
  to the acquisition" of Elpida (Q4 FY13 release, 2013-10-11); without them the year is a loss ($(294)M), so the mirror test is met on any
  reading, and no figure excluding them was published.
- **FY2006 stays the gap it was in 2008-2009.** From the FY2010 10-K later years return to the history, so the literal PFE 2003 reading
  would now start the history after FY2006 (FY2007 on, leaving FY2010 alone); the encoding is instead the one for a year excluded as a gap,
  which stays one when later years follow (the NKE FY2018, XOM FY2020 and PFE 2023 rule), so FY2004-FY2005 stay in. The other reading is
  measured below.
- **So the anchor is FY05's $0.29 to 2010-10-07 and FY10's $1.85 from the Q4 FY10 print to the end of 2013** (the rollover rule; no EPS
  guide in any filing). The history on the last dates is FY2004, FY2005 and FY2010; FY2006-FY2009 and FY2011-FY2013 are gaps. With the
  FY2013 10-K (2013-10-29) the ten fiscal years are FY2004-FY2013, so FY2003 leaves the decade: no first-excluded year, and the ten-year
  limit sets the window's start (`pe_window_start` null).
- **No guide in any filing,** as in 2008-2009: no release, 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K of 2010-2013 guides revenue, EPS or a margin, in numbers
  or words (the 2011-02-17 8-K gives preliminary first-quarter revenue by new business unit, a past quarter). BASE is the latest
  quarter's revenue growth plus the buyback (the UNP rule); no margin step.
- **Revenue and shares** each year from the latest filing that reports it (FY2004 net sales from the FY2008 10-K, FY2005 from the
  adjusted FY2009 10-K, FY2006 from the FY2010 10-K, and so on; FY2007's 769.1M diluted shares from the adjusted statements). Numonyx's
  138 million shares make the net-issuance term -7.8%/yr on the FY2010 10-K, then -6.2% to -5.2%.
- **Signals,** from each release's statements as before, against the year-ago quarter in the same release (several releases recast the
  comparison quarters: the Q3 FY12 release's Q2 FY12 net sales are $2,009M against $2,067M first reported, after a $58M charge to revenue);
  inventories against the year-ago quarter's end from that quarter's 10-Q (a Q4's from the release's prior year-end column). Charges and
  gains stay in, as published.
- **Segments** (display only): the adjusted FY2009 10-K's Memory and All Other; the FY2010 10-K's Memory (external sales), Numonyx (new,
  no prior year) and All Other; from the FY2011 10-K DSG, NSG, WSG, ESG and All Other (the 2011-04-14 8-K recasts FY2010 to them: it changes
  no input and adds nothing, the ACN rule).
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2, unchanged.** No FY2010-FY2013 10-K calls the business cyclical; the "why" quotes the latest 10-K's
  business sentence ("a global manufacturer and marketer of semiconductor devices, principally DRAM, NAND Flash and NOR Flash memory" from
  FY2010; "one of the world's leading providers of advanced semiconductor solutions" in FY2013) and its two lead risk factors on falling
  selling prices and competition. CLOUD is live from 2012-10-30, scoped to public cloud displacing on-premise IT, and no Micron 10-K of the
  period names the cloud, so the watch list stays empty (the AVGO and NVDA reading); from the FY2012 10-K the "why" says so.
- **Capital return** (display only): no dividend ("We have not declared or paid cash dividends since 1996", each 10-K); the $150M buyback
  of 2011-07-26 ("On July 26, 2011, we paid $150 million to repurchase 19.7 million shares", FY2011 and FY2013 10-Ks; the Q4 FY11 release's
  own sentence on its print).
- **Adds nothing:** the Numonyx and Elpida transaction 8-Ks (their effects reach the prints), the Inotera, Hynix, Nanya, Intel (IM Flash
  restructuring) and TECH agreements, the Rambus and Oracle litigation 8-Ks, the convertible note offerings, exchanges and repurchases (in
  the share counts and the prints), the 2013-02-05 disclosures (Elpida's financials, risk factors, a business presentation), and the
  director, officer, trading-plan, bylaw and vote 8-Ks. None changes a guided number; none states a dividend.

refused. With no numeric guide in scope, a print's `outlook_venue` replaces the 2008-2013 sentence on capital expenditure estimates, which
the 2014-2017 releases no longer give; prints without the field keep their text, so every 2008-2013 model is byte-identical. The firewall
plants a call sentence on its print and a later guide for every quarter guided before the cutoff, in numbers and in words.

  day (2018-06-22, 2018-12-20, 2019-03-22, 2019-06-27, 2019-12-20, 2020-03-27, 2020-07-01, 2020-10-01, 2021-07-02, 2021-09-30,
  2021-12-22). The FY2018-FY2021 10-Ks were accepted during the session (2018-10-15, 2019-10-17, 2020-10-19, 2021-10-08). A Q4 print extends
  the history from its release to the 10-K, as before.
- **History: four more vintages, the ten fiscal years to each 10-K's year,** each year from the latest filing that reports it (five years of
  selected data and three of statements). The FY2021 10-K has no selected data ("ITEM 6. [RESERVED]"), so it gives FY2019-FY2021 from its
  statements and the earlier years keep the latest 10-K that reported them (the ACN FY21 and NVDA FY2021 rule). FY2008 leaves with the FY2018
  10-K, FY2009 with the FY2019 10-K, FY2010 (and with it FY10's $1.85) with the FY2020 10-K and FY2011 with the FY2021 10-K. ASC 606 arrives
  in Q1 FY19 by the modified retrospective method (no year restated), so no seam enters the history.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS, as before,** and **FY2018-FY2021 are all kept**: FY2018 $11.51, FY2019 $5.51, FY2020 $2.37, FY2021 $5.14. The
  company's adjustments are $565M against $14,135M of net income (FY18), $1,001M against $6,313M, $548M against $2,687M and $1,115M against
  $5,861M (each Q4 release's reconciliation; reported EPS 0.96, 0.87, 0.84 and 0.85 times the non-GAAP $11.95, $6.35, $2.83, $6.06, which
  also remove stock-based compensation and the amortization of debt discount, which recur): neither the AAPL FY2002 test nor its AVGO FY2018
  mirror is met. FY2018 keeps the Tax Act items as published (a $174M net benefit in the company's adjustments; no figure excluding only
  them: the NVDA FY2018 reading). FY2021 keeps the $435M write-down of the Lehi assets held for sale, the FIFO change ($133M), the
  cost-absorption change ($160M) and the patent license charges ($128M), which together stay under the tests.

  (2019-09-27), FY20's $2.37 from the Q4 FY20 print (2020-09-30) and FY21's $5.14 from the Q4 FY21 print (2021-09-29) (the rollover rule; no
  fiscal-year EPS guide in any filing; the releases' quarter EPS outlooks are display only).
- **Guides: the next quarter's revenue from filings only, read against the year-ago quarter from its own release** (the NVDA level rule),
  in three forms:
  - **Slides and updates (2018):** the Q2 FY18 guidance slide (an image furnished with the release) gives Q3 FY18 "Revenue $7.20 billion
    – $7.60 billion" (+29.4% to +36.5% on Q3 FY17's $5,566M). Two press releases furnished between earnings update a quarter in numbers and
    are guides of their own (the NVDA 2019-01-28 rule; MU's 2016-11-29 and 2017-03-02 updates): Q2 FY18 "Revenue in the range of $7.20
    billion to $7.35 billion compared to prior guidance of $6.80 billion to $7.20 billion." (8-K of 2018-02-05, accepted 17:21 ET, from

    growth (the UNP rule) and each print's sentence on its call is quoted. Two 8-Ks restate the call's range in numbers, and each is read as a
    numeric guide from its own date (a range stated in a filing is a guide in numbers; the words around it are display only, the ACN rule):

  2024-06-28, 2024-09-27, 2024-12-20, 2025-06-27, 2025-09-25, 2025-12-19, 2026-03-20, 2026-06-26, 2026-10-02). The FY2022 and FY2025 10-Ks
  were accepted during the session (2022-10-07, 2025-10-03), the FY2023 and FY2024 10-Ks after the close (2023-10-06 16:01 ET, dated
  2023-10-09; 2024-10-04 16:12 ET, dated 2024-10-07), and the FY2026 10-K before the open (2026-10-09 08:21 ET). A Q4 print extends the
  history from its release to the 10-K, as before.
- **History: five more vintages, the ten fiscal years to each 10-K's year,** each year from the latest filing that reports it. Item 6 is
  reserved in every 10-K of the range, so each gives three years from its statements of operations and the earlier years keep the latest
  10-K that reported them (the ACN FY21 and NVDA FY2021 rule). FY2013 (an excluded year) leaves the decade with the FY2023 10-K, FY2014 with
  the FY2024 10-K, FY2015 with the FY2025 10-K and FY2016 (a gap) with the FY2026 10-K. The fiscal calendar holds: FY2022 ended 2022-09-01,
  FY2023 2023-08-31, FY2024 2024-08-29, FY2025 2025-08-28 and FY2026 (53 weeks) 2026-09-03.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS, as before.** The releases' non-GAAP figures also remove stock-based compensation and the amortization of debt
  discount, which recur, so they are not figures excluding only one-offs (the NKE FY2007 and AVGO rule).
  - **FY2022 is kept at $7.75:** the company's adjustments, $788M (among them the $189M impact of Idaho income tax reform and the $83M loss
    on debt repurchases), against $8,687M of net income; reported EPS 0.93 times the non-GAAP $8.35.
  - **FY2023 is excluded, a loss:** $(5.34) a diluted share, and the company's non-GAAP $(4.45) is a loss too, so no P/E (the XOM FY2020
    rule). It is the latest year at the Q4 FY23 print (2023-09-28) and a gap after; its own days leave the window ("ex-FY23").
  - **FY2024 is kept at $0.70.** The company's adjustments net to $694M against $778M of net income, and reported EPS is 0.54 times the
    non-GAAP $1.30, so not even the whole adjustment, which includes $821M of stock-based compensation that recurs, meets the AAPL FY2002
    test (one-off items larger than the year's net income, reported EPS under half the EPS without them). Its listed one-off items are a
    $200M patent cross-license agreement gain (Q2 FY24, a benefit under the $578M of income without it, so its AVGO FY2018 mirror is not met
    either) and $1M of restructure. The other reading is measured below.
  - **FY2025 is kept at $7.59** (adjustments $931M against $8,539M; 0.92 times the non-GAAP $8.29) and **FY2026 at $74.33** (adjustments
    $1,789M against $84,969M, among them $500M of patent license charges and $511M of losses on debt prepayments; 0.98 times $75.52).
- **So the anchor is** FY21's $5.14 to 2022-09-23, FY22's $7.75 from the Q4 FY22 print (2022-09-30) and, FY2023 being excluded, for FY24E to
  2024-09-20, FY24's $0.70 from the Q4 FY24 print (2024-09-27), FY25's $7.59 from the Q4 FY25 print (2025-09-25) and FY26's $74.33 from the
  Q4 FY26 print (2026-10-02) (the rollover rule; no fiscal-year EPS guide in any filing; the outlook tables' quarter EPS is display only).

  cyclical downturn in our business or global downturn." The company names the cyclicality of its own business, BKR's "Our business is
  cyclical" and CAT's "The demand for our products and services tends to be cyclical" reading, not AVGO's industry wording, so the kind is
  CYCLICAL from 2025-10-03; the FY2026 10-K repeats both sentences. The kind changes the class label only. The "why" quotes each 10-K's

  scoped to generative AI substituting the core product (software seats, IT services and BPO hours, professional information, search,
  education content, mobility); AI is Micron's own demand, never a substitute for its products (the NVDA and AVGO reading), so the watch

## GOOG (Google): the twenty-sixth ticker, in staging, 2008-2009

The GOOG series is built apart from the other twenty-five and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/GOOG.json`), builder (`retro/build_goog.py`, the MU builder with the calendar fiscal year, figures in thousands, no guides
and a 10-Q restatement field) and engine (`retro/templates/goog_engine.py.tmpl`, the MU engine with receivables in the place of
inventories and Google's own rule-T thresholds). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters a
GOOG model, and no live analysis of Google exists in the repository to keep out. Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/GOOG/`, beside the
others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009 ("same rules as before"); the code is the
newest branch of the repository (its commit "MU retrospective: hindsight findings for 2022-2026", 2026-11-18), every other recent retro
branch being its ancestor.

```bash
python3 retro/build_goog.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                  # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_goog.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                  # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/GOOG/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series GOOG
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-02-01 2008-02-19 2008-04-18 2008-05-13 2008-07-18 2008-08-08 2008-10-17 2008-11-10 2009-01-23 2009-02-17 \
         2009-04-17 2009-07-17 2009-10-16 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c GOOG; done
```

Two ranges, as for MU: the series has 2008-12-31 and no 2009-01-02.

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the earnings releases of Q3 2006 to Q3 2009 (8-K exhibit 99.1:
the narrative, the balance sheet, the statements of income and cash flows, the revenues by source; exhibit 99.2 repeats the tables), the
Q3 and Q4 2004 and Q4 2005 releases for the company's figures excluding one-offs, the initial public offering prospectus (424B4,

  conservative case falls with it, to -16% over two years by December 2009, which with the price 41% above the floor makes the last two

The CHEAP calls rest mostly on the multiple against the stock's own short, post-listing history, which every call above leaves in
place; the BUY tier rests on the hypergrowth years in BULL and XBULL.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows the 2008 advertising slowdown: the receivables gap in the place of inventories (rule T then
  sets the thresholds mechanically; 2 classes move at BEAR), and paid clicks left out for want of a second annual value;
- rule T on every year the filings report, start-up years included, which puts revenue growth at BEAR on every date;
- FY2004 at the company's $1.49 and the later years at GAAP (no class moves either way);
- the Q3 2008 10-Q restatement read as replacing the release from its own date (no class moves);
- CYCLICAL rather than DURABLE (label only), on the 10-K's "cyclicality ... in our business";
- the outlook words, stock-based compensation, dilution and capital-expenditure estimates left unencoded (no input either way).

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/GOOG/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

**A correction to 2008-2009, found while building this batch.** A new scan of every fact's own text for dates, years and quarters after
the fact's publication found that the FY2006 and FY2007 vintages' EPS note (in the `EPS_NORM` comment of each model) named "the Authors
Guild settlement (Q3 2008) and the equity impairments (Q4 2008)" among the items Google's non-GAAP EPS removes: the 2008-2009 build had
given every vintage the note written for the FY2008 10-K. Those two items were not public on the vintages' dates. The two vintages now
carry a note naming only the items public then (the Google Foundation contribution of FY2005); the FY2008 vintage keeps its note. The 59
models of 2008-01-04 to 2009-02-13 change in that comment only: no number, class, report or analysis changes, and their outcomes stand.
The validator could not see it (a year equal to the as-of year is not flagged), nor the leak scan (the text belonged to an earlier
fact), so the new scan joins the checks. The 2010-2013 vintages' notes were written the same way at first and the scan caught it before
any were committed; each now names only the items public by its date.

### GOOG 2014-2017: the Class C split, Motorola Mobile discontinued, Alphabet, the Adjustment Payment, and the EC fine at the company's figure

208 weekly dates, 2014-01-10 to 2017-12-29, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The owner asked for 2014-2017 ("same rules as
before"); the code is the newest branch of the repository (its commit "GOOG retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for
2010-2013", 2026-11-18), every other recent retro branch being its ancestor. Built in a new session; the git log the session started
from carries the 2010-2013 commit message with its hindsight summary, and `FINDINGS.md` was not opened. No decision below uses either:
each applies a rule that existed before (the r2 rollover and decade rules, the UNP BASE rule, the UNP and LOW continuing-operations
rule, the ACN rule for a company figure without a one-off, the ACN rename rule as AVGO and XOM apply it to a successor issuer, the MU
rule for an 8-K that recasts a 10-K, the NVDA split helper) or a 2008-2013 encoding (GAAP EPS, receivables from the year-ago 10-Q,
CYCLICAL). The fact sheet only gains facts (`GOOG62`-`GOOG96`; the 2008-2013 part is unchanged). The builder gains three things, none of
which changes a 2008-2013 model (all 314 rebuild byte for byte): a history figure's share basis is the date of the filing it comes from
(`eps_sources`, `shares_sources`), a change of company name is applied, and a Q4 release without a full-year diluted share count leaves the
share history as it was.

```bash
python3 retro/build_goog.py --weekly 2014-01-06 2017-12-31                  # 208 dates, 2014-01-10 .. 2017-12-29
for c in 2014-01-31 2014-02-12 2014-03-27 2014-04-17 2014-07-18 2014-10-17 2015-01-30 2015-02-09 2015-04-24 2015-07-17 2015-10-05 \
         2015-10-23 2016-02-02 2016-02-12 2016-04-22 2016-05-03 2016-07-29 2016-10-28 2017-01-27 2017-02-03 2017-04-28 2017-07-25 \
         2017-10-27 2018-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c GOOG; done
```

The range starts on Monday 2014-01-06: 2013-12-31, built with 2010-2013, is ISO week 2014-W01.

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the 16 earnings releases of Q4 2013 to Q3 2017 (ex.99.1: the
narrative, balance sheet, statements of income and cash flows, revenues by source or by segment, the paid-click, TAC and headcount
tables), the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks (Items 1, 1A, 5, 6, 7, the statements and the EPS note), the FY2015 10-K/A (Part III only), the 8-K of
2016-05-02 that recasts Items 7 and 8 of the FY2015 10-K, the 10-Qs of Q1 2013 to Q3 2017 (the year-ago receivables, and each quarter's
figures against its release), and every other 8-K of January 2014 to December 2017 under either CIK by its items and exhibits, the
8-K12B of Alphabet Inc. included. Filings from 2015-10-02 are Alphabet's (CIK 1652044; the Q3 2015 release was filed under both). The
fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows, as before (each row asserted present, exactly, in its own filing;
every rate computed); 588 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (588/588). Decided on 2026-11-18, before
any 2014-2017 model was built or any 2014-2017 outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted after the close (16:00:24-16:29 ET) and is dated the next trading day: a Thursday
  release meets the Friday's close (the AVGO rule): 2014-01-31, 2014-07-18, 2014-10-17, 2015-01-30, 2015-04-24, 2015-07-17,
  2015-10-23, 2016-04-22, 2016-07-29, 2016-10-28, 2017-01-27, 2017-04-28, 2017-10-27. Q1 2014 came on a Wednesday before Good Friday
  (dated 2014-04-17, the week's last trading day). Q4 2015 and Q2 2017 came on Mondays (dated 2016-02-02 and 2017-07-25; the weeks'
  dates 2016-02-03 and 2017-07-26). The 10-Ks are dated 2014-02-12, 2015-02-09, 2016-02-12 and 2017-02-03 (all after the close). A Q4
  print extends the history to its 10-K: FY2013 from 2014-01-31 (2 dates), FY2014 from 2015-01-30 (2), FY2015 and FY2016 one date each.
- **The Class C split** (`splits`). The Q4 2013 release announces the distribution and the 8-K accepted 2014-03-26 16:05 ET (dated
  2014-03-27) states it: "its impending dividend of one share of Class C capital stock for each share of Class A common stock and Class B
  common stock outstanding on March 27, 2014". It doubles the share count, and the company restates every per-share figure by two ("the
  stock split, which was effected in the form of a stock dividend", Q1 2014 release), so the ratio is 2, effective on the record date,
  2014-03-27, which is Yahoo's split date for GOOG. Every history figure is restated on the basis of the filing it comes from: the
  FY2013 10-K's $36.05 is $18.025 from 2014-03-28, and the FY2014 10-K's FY2010-FY2014 are already after the split while its FY2005-FY2009
  come from earlier 10-Ks and are divided by two. Yahoo's own price factor is 2.002, and Yahoo adjusts the series again by 1.0027455 on
  2015-04-27 for the Adjustment Payment (below), which the company does not treat as a split: both stay in the price data as Yahoo
  publishes it, so window days before them sit 0.1% and 0.27% lower against EPS than the closes then printed.
- **The security priced.** Yahoo's GOOG series is the Class A common stock to 2014-03-26 and the Class C capital stock from 2014-03-27:
  when-issued until 2014-04-02, NASDAQ: GOOG from 2014-04-03, when the Class A took the symbol GOOGL. The series keeps its symbol, as the
  2010-2013 outcomes already measured it past 2014. One weekly date falls in the when-issued days: 2014-03-28 is priced at the Class C's
  $559.99 (the Class A closed $1,120.15 that day, Yahoo's GOOGL series as traded). From the split the model's price line names the Class C
  capital stock.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS of the priced class.** Every class earns the same per share in every period but those holding Q2 2015: the
  $522M Adjustment Payment to Class C holders (May 2015, "in accordance with the settlement of litigation involving the authorization to
  distribute Class C capital stock") is allocated to the Class C numerator, so FY2015 is $24.34 for the Class C and $22.84 for Class A and
  B (and Q2 2015 $6.43 against $4.93). The Class C figure is used; the other is measured below. No figure excluding only the payment
  exists (the non-GAAP EPS also removes stock-based compensation), so the ACN rule does not apply.
- **Diluted shares** after the split are the EPS note's Class A column (which assumes the conversion of Class B) plus its Class C column
  (FY2012: 332,305 + 332,305 thousand, FY2014: 342,377 + 344,693) and the releases' combined count for quarters; the shares before it are
  multiplied by two. The Q4 2015 and Q4 2016 releases print no full-year diluted share count, so FY2015 and FY2016 join the share history
  only with their 10-Ks (one date each). The Q2 2015 release prints no diluted share count at all: the Q1 2015 release's 689.5M stands
  for the display-only EPS check.
- **Motorola Mobile, as published** (the UNP and LOW rule): from the Q1 2014 release it is a discontinued operation ("On January 29,
  2014, we entered into an agreement with Lenovo Group Limited providing for the disposition of the Motorola Mobile business."), sold on
  2014-10-29. The Q4 2013 print and the FY2013 10-K still carry it in continuing operations ($36.05), and no filing reports FY2013
  without it before the Q4 2014 release, so FY13's $18.025 anchors 2014-03-28 to 2015-01-23 with Motorola Mobile in; the FY2014 10-K
  restates FY2012-FY2013 without it ($17.39, $19.70). The quarters of 2014 are against year-ago quarters without it, as each release
  prints them, while the year-ago receivables (the 2013 10-Qs, and the December 2013 column of the Q4 2014 release) include it: a seam in
  the receivables gap (-16.2pp, -8.1pp, -16.1pp, -9.6pp), as in 2012-2013. Q1 2014's sequential change is against the Q4 2013 release with
  Motorola (display only).
- **The 2015 income tax correction.** The Q2 2015 release and 10-Q revise income taxes for 2008 to Q1 2015 ($711M cumulative, "an
  incorrect classification of certain revenues between legal entities"; revenues and operating income unchanged). Each year comes from
  the latest filing that reports it, so FY2011-FY2014 are revised from the FY2015 10-K (FY2014 $19.82 instead of $20.27), FY2008-FY2010
  stay as last reported, and each release's year-ago quarter is as it prints it. Q1 2015 is revised only by the Q2 2015 10-Q, after the
  Q2 2015 print: no date sees it as the latest quarter and only taxes move, so it is not encoded.
- **The EC fine at the company's figure** (the ACN rule). The Q2 2017 release publishes operating income and diluted EPS excluding only
  the European Commission fine ($6,868M and $8.90; GAAP $4,132M and $5.01; "There is no tax effect as this charge is not tax deductible"),
  so the quarter's operating margin and EPS use them and the note keeps GAAP. Earlier one-offs had no such figure (the non-GAAP measures
  removed stock-based compensation too until 2016) and stayed in, as in 2008-2013. The 8-K of 2017-06-27 (before the open) announcing the
  decision changes no guided number.
- **Alphabet Inc.** is the successor issuer from the holding company reorganization of 2015-10-02 (8-K12B accepted 16:17 ET, dated
  2015-10-05): `company_names` (the ACN rule, as AVGO and XOM apply it). The FY2015 10-K is Alphabet's. Segments from the Q4 2015 release
  (Google and Other Bets) are display only; the signals take the consolidated lines, and the Q1 2015 reclassification of DoubleClick
  revenues between sources is as published.
- **The recast of 2016-05-02** (accepted 20:59 ET, dated 2016-05-03) supersedes Items 7 and 8 of the FY2015 10-K for three accounting
  standards: the statement of income, EPS and shares are unchanged, the operating cash flows are not (FY2015 $26,572M against $26,024M). It
  is a vintage of its own (the MU rule for the 8-K of 2010-03-04), which changes only the display free cash flow.
- **No guide in any filing**, as before; the 10-Ks keep "Our revenue growth rate could decline over time, and we anticipate downward
  pressure on our operating margin in the future." (display only). BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth plus the buyback term.
  **No dividend** ("We have never declared or paid any cash dividend on our common or capital stock." from the FY2014 10-K). The
  repurchases from Q4 2015 (authorizations of $5,099,019,513.59 in October 2015 and $7,019,340,976.83 in October 2016) are display text;
  the buyback term stays the decade's net issuance of diluted shares.
- **Durability: CYCLICAL, risk 2, unchanged.** Each FY2013-FY2016 10-K keeps "As our growth rate has slowed, the cyclicality and seasonality
  in our business has become more pronounced and caused our operating results to fluctuate." The "why" quotes the latest 10-K's business
  sentence (from FY2015: "Alphabet is a collection of businesses -- the largest of which, of course, is Google."), its advertising risk
  factor, its competition sentence and "expenditures by advertisers tend to be cyclical". CLOUD stays out of scope: the 10-Ks name the
  cloud as Google's own products (Google Cloud Platform from FY2013) and, from FY2016, Amazon and Microsoft as competitors in it.
  ECOMMERCE (from 2015-01-01), STREAMING (2015-08-04) and ENERGY_TRANSITION (2015-12-12) are scoped to physical retail, linear TV and
  pay-TV bundles, and fossil fuels: out of scope (the LMT 2014-2017 reading). The watch list stays empty.
- **Adds nothing:** Nest (2014-01-13), the Lenovo agreement (2014-01-29; it reaches the prints), the notes offering (2014-02-25), the
  Class C transfer restriction agreements (2014-03-26; the split's own source), the officer, director, compensation and meeting 8-Ks,
  the derivative settlement (2014-11-17), the founders' trading plans (2015-02-13), the Adjustment Payment record date (2015-03-23), the
  Alphabet announcement and merger (2015-08-10, 2015-10-02), bebop (2015-11-19), the debt exchange (2016-04-12, 2016-04-27), the notes of
  2016-08-09, the founders' letter (with the Q1 2017 release), the EC decision (2017-06-27), Eric Schmidt's step down (2017-12-21) and the
  FY2015 10-K/A (Part III only; the AAPL 10-K/A rule). None changes a guided number; none states a dividend.
- **Anachronism list:** Google and Alphabet names first used in their filings after the start of 2014 join `taxonomy_eras.json`, each
  dated from its first filing under either CIK (EDGAR full-text search; after-close filings from the next trading day): Other Bets
  (2015-10-23), Verily (2016-02-12), Waymo, Google Assistant and Google Home (2017-02-03), DeepMind (2017-04-28), YouTube TV
  (2020-02-04), Google Pixel (2023-04-24) and Tensor Processing Unit (2026-04-27). No model of another ticker contains one, so no lint
  result changes; all 522 GOOG models lint clean.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):

  below the latest quarter's revenue growth less the issuance). The BULL price falls from $3,495 to about $1,046, Ratio B rises from 0.17
  to 4.27, and the tier leaves BUY.
- **BEAR is flat EPS** (the 0% cap) on every date: no year of FY2004-FY2016 fell. The BEAR price is below the price throughout.
- **BASE follows the quarters:** +9.1%/yr on the Q3 2013 print, +14.2-19.3% through 2014, +9.3-13.5% in 2015, +16.0-21.1% in 2016-2017 and
  +22.6% on Q3 2017 (revenue growth less a net issuance of 1.1-2.8%/yr as the decade rolls). The conservative case runs from -21.2% to
  +36.2% over two years.
- **The proxy composite** is 1.80-2.00: revenue at BEAR (the start-up bands), the other signals at BASE, the receivables gap at BULL
  (1.95) on Q4 2013 to Q2 2015 (the 2014 quarters with the seam above) and Q4 2016 to Q2 2017, the gross margin at BULL (2.00) on Q3 2015
  (+284bp).

How far each call moves the classes (the 208 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- EPS of Class A and B where it differs (Q2 2015, FY2015 $22.84): 2 classes (RICH to FAIR, 2017-02-10 and 2017-03-24) and 17 tiers;
- Q2 2017 at GAAP operating income and EPS (with the fine): no class, no tier;
- the split at Yahoo's 2.002: 2 classes (FAIR to CHEAP, 2015-02-27 and 2015-05-22), no tier;
- rule T without the 1999-2000 change: 11 classes (5 FAIR to CHEAP, 6 RICH to FAIR, 2015-02-27 to 2016-03-04); on the FY2006 10-K's own
  years: 43 (5 FAIR to CHEAP, 38 RICH to FAIR, to 2017-04-21); no tier either way;
- every signal at its BEAR value: 90 classes (52 CHEAP and 23 FAIR to RICH, 15 CHEAP to FAIR); at its XBULL value: 100 (54 RICH to CHEAP,
  37 RICH to FAIR, 9 FAIR to CHEAP); no tier;
- BULL and XBULL at BASE's rate (no rule says so; it shows what the tier rests on): 72 classes and 50 tiers;
- not measured: the 2014 receivables without Motorola Mobile (no filing gives the year-ago receivables without it) and FY2013 without it
  before the Q4 2014 release (no filing reports it).
In these years the classes rest on the signals and their rule-T bands far more than in 2010-2013 (13 classes at BEAR then): the multiple
sits near the class boundaries, and the composite decides.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the security priced: Yahoo's GOOG series, the Class C capital stock from the split, rather than the Class A (GOOGL), and its EPS (2
  classes the other way); the when-issued price on 2014-03-28;

### GOOG 2018-2021: the Tax Act year at GAAP by a $69M margin, EC fines at the company's figures, COVID, and RICH throughout

209 weekly dates, 2018-01-05 to 2021-12-31, on the same method, builder, engine and rule-T thresholds; no builder or engine change was
needed. The owner asked for 2018-2021. Built in the session that built and scored 2014-2017, so those outcomes and `FINDINGS.md` were known
when this batch was read; no decision below uses them. Each applies a rule that existed before: the AAPL FY2002 test as PEP applies it
to its 2017 (GAAP when the listed items do not exceed the year's income), the ACN rule for a company figure without a one-off (as GOOG's
Q2 2017), the UNP and LOW continuing-operations rule, the rollover and decade rules, the UNP BASE rule, and the 2014-2017 encodings.

and exhibits. The source ids are `GOOG97`-`GOOG128`; 644 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (644/644).
Decided on 2026-11-19, before any 2018-2021 model was built or any 2018-2021 outcome computed:

  releases meet the Friday's close (2018-02-02, 2018-10-26, 2019-07-26, 2020-07-31, 2020-10-30), the Monday and Tuesday ones are dated
  the next day and their weeks' dates are the day after (2018-04-25, 2018-07-25, 2019-02-06, 2019-05-01, 2019-10-30, 2020-02-05,

  from FY2018 each comes the same evening as its Q4 release, so the Q4 print's full-year actuals never stand alone (FY2017 does for one
  date, 2018-02-02).

  of $9.9 billion", $9,857M in its table) and the year's EC fine ($2,736M, not tax deductible): $12,593M against $12,662M of net income,
  so the AAPL FY2002 test is not met (GAAP $18.00 is 50.1% of the EPS without them, about $35.90). No filing publishes the year's EPS
  without them: the release gives Q4's EPS without the Tax Act ($9.70) and the year's operating income without the fine ($28,882M), the
  10-K neither. So FY2017 stays at GAAP (the PEP 2017 rule) and is in every history from 2018-02-02: BEAR becomes FY2016-FY2017's
  -35.4%/yr on every later date, and from the FY2019 10-K XBULL is FY2017-FY2019's +65.3%/yr. Both alternatives are measured below.

  ($49.16) carries the AdSense fine ($1,697M), FY2020 is $58.61. Every class earns the same per share in these years.
- **Quarters at the company's figure without a one-off** (the ACN rule, as Q2 2017): Q4 2017's EPS without the Tax Act ($9.70; GAAP
  $(4.35)); Q2 2018's operating income and EPS without the EC fines ($7,878M, $11.75; the year-ago Q2 2017 as $6,868M and $8.90); Q1 2019's

  Q2 2018 exclude the EC fine."; $8,116M after the reclassification below, and $8,305M), so those year-ago figures are the company's. Q1
  2018's equity-security effects have no figure without them: GAAP. The full-year operating margins (display) are GAAP.
- **Prior-year figures as each release prints them:** from Q1 2019 performance fees are reclassified from general and administrative

  latest filing that reports it (the FY2017 and FY2018 10-Ks report 2013-2014 from continuing operations; EPS is unaffected by the
  reclassification).
- **Diluted shares** are the releases' summary counts to Q3 2019 and the income statement's from Q4 2019; the Q4 2017 and Q4 2018
  releases print no full-year count, so FY2017 joins the share history with the 10-K (the 2014-2017 encoding). The 10-Ks' counts are the
  Class A plus Class C columns, as before.
- **Revenue types and segments, display only:** Google properties, Network and other revenues and Other Bets to Q3 2019; Search & other,

- **Anachronism list:** Fitbit (2020-02-04, the FY2019 10-K) and Google Workspace (2020-10-30, the Q3 2020 10-Q) join
  `taxonomy_eras.json`; neither is in any model.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):
- **Controls** (every date from 2017 rebuilt with one real fact altered at a time): 25 of 28 alterations change the models exactly from
  the first weekly date on or after their publication until a later fact supersedes them, none earlier; 3 are inert by design (the Q4
  2018-2020 prints' full-year revenue, superseded the same day by their 10-Ks).

- **Firewall** (run after the build was committed and pushed, before any outcome): passes at the 18 cutoffs above (every print and
  vintage date of the range, and 2022-01-01), 0 files changed and no planted text (526 to 731 dates each). As a positive control the plants

  **legacy tier AVOID on 162,** WATCHLIST 44, ACCUMULATE 3 (2020-03-20 to 2020-04-03). Robustness always contains the class and is
  unanimous on 103 dates.

  ($980-1,264, 54.4-70.2x, the 88th-100th: the Tax Act year as the anchor); FY18's $43.70 to 2020-01-31 ($1,066-1,480, 24.4-33.9x, the
  50th-90th); FY19's $49.16 to 2021-01-29 ($1,072-1,901, 21.8-38.7x, the 31st-90th); FY20's $58.61 from 2021-02-04 ($2,036-2,999, 34.7-51.2x,
  the 89th-94th). The window's median is 23.2-26.0x.

How far each call moves the classes (the 209 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):

this batch was built and its firewall run. No decision below uses either: each applies a rule that existed before (the r2 rollover and

2008-2021 model (all 731 rebuild byte for byte): it accepts dividends (the latest declared rate; until now it refused them for want of an

  after the split.

  severance and office-space charges, FY2025's EC fine and Waymo compensation charge, and each year's gains on equity securities are

  so the quarter's operating income is GAAP $31,228M plus the $3.5 billion the release names ($34,728M, which reproduces both published

  10-K states no rate, so the release's $0.20 stands; the FY2025 10-K restates $0.21. The mandatory convertible preferred stock issued in
  June 2026 and its dividends are display text; EPS and diluted shares are as published (per common share from the Q2 2026 release).
- **No guide in any filing.** The releases from Q3 2025 and the equity-raise 8-K of 2026-06-04 give capital-expenditure ranges, for which
  method r2 has no input (as before); the 10-Ks' words change from "we anticipate downward pressure on our operating margin" (FY2021-FY2022)

  FY2024 10-K the note's total column equals it), and the releases' counts for quarters.

  sentence changes from "tend to be cyclical" (FY2021) to "tend to correlate with overall economic conditions" (FY2022 on).

  names search. A theme joins a watch list only from a company filing that names it as a competitive risk (the PEP GLP1 rule, as MSFT
  applies it). The FY2021 10-K predates the live date; the FY2022 10-K (2023-02-03) and the 2023 10-Qs name AI only as Google's own
  products, their challenges and their effect on its own monetization ("We also may develop new products incorporating AI innovations that

  2024-02-01 GOOG carries GENAI on the watch list in the latest 10-K's words (`genai_company_acknowledged`; the FY2024 10-K adds that
  "competitors and new entrants may be able to offer experiences that are, or that are perceived to be, substantially similar to or better
  than ours", the FY2025 10-K "and the consumers may change how they obtain information online, potentially reducing the utility of our
  existing products and services."), company-acknowledged, with no market read: no dated evidence in the registry or the fact sheet shows
  the market pricing generative-AI substitution of Google Search, and no press coverage is added after 2023 (the ACN rule). CYCLICAL, risk

## JPM (JPMorgan Chase): the twenty-seventh ticker, in staging, 2008-2021

The JPM series is built apart from the other twenty-six and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/JPM.json`), builder (`retro/build_jpm.py`, the GOOG builder with a bank's fields, figures in millions, no splits and a
dividend list) and engine (`retro/templates/jpm_engine.py.tmpl`, the GOOG engine with a bank's signals and JPMorgan Chase's own rule-T
thresholds). It is the first bank in the retrospectives. The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker
enters a JPM model, and no live analysis of JPMorgan Chase exists in the repository to keep out. Outputs go to
`staging/retrospective/JPM/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009
("same rules as before"); the code is the newest branch of the repository (its commit "GOOG retrospective: hindsight outcomes and
findings for 2022-2026", 2026-11-19), every other recent retro branch being its ancestor.

```bash
python3 retro/build_jpm.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                   # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_jpm.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                   # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/JPM/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series JPM
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-01-16 2008-02-29 2008-04-16 2008-07-17 2008-08-12 2008-10-15 2008-11-07 2009-01-15 2009-02-24 2009-03-03 \
         2009-04-16 2009-05-29 2009-07-16 2009-10-14 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c JPM; done
```

Two ranges, as for MU and GOOG: the series has 2008-12-31 and no 2009-01-02.

What was read, and how (by the session's model directly, with no delegated transcription). The filing list is EDGAR's for CIK 19617
(acceptance times in UTC, converted to ET). Read by row and by search, not page by page: the financial supplements (8-K exhibit 99.2) of
the Q4 2006 to Q3 2009 earnings releases, from which every quarterly figure comes; the releases' text (exhibit 99.1), searched for
outlook, guidance and dividend sentences; the five-year summaries and selected annual data of the FY2000-FY2008 10-Ks, with Item 1 and
1A of the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks; the 10-Qs of Q1 2007 to Q3 2009, compared by script with their releases on the six rows the signals use;
and the 61 other 8-Ks of November 2007 to December 2009 that carry an item besides 9.01, by their item text, their exhibits scanned by
keyword for per-share, revenue and outlook statements. **Not read:** the 229 8-Ks of that period with item 9.01 only (exhibits to
securities offerings), which were classified by item and not opened; the investor-day and earnings slide decks beyond the keyword scan;
the 10-Qs' and 10-Ks' text outside the rows and sentences named here. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted
rows: each figure is read from its own row by label and column (the row is kept in the fact sheet), every growth rate, margin, gap and
rule-T value is computed, and every quoted sentence is asserted present in its own filing; the 321 strings were checked with
`verbatim.py` against their own filings (321/321). The source ids are `JPM1`-`JPM25`. Decided on 2026-11-19, before any JPM model was
built or any JPM outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's JPM series is the stock of the registrant: The Chase Manhattan Corporation to 2000, J.P. Morgan Chase &
  Co. from the merger of 2000-12-31, JPMorgan Chase & Co. since. Its two splits (1998-06-15, 2000-06-12) precede the P/E window, so the
  close is the price as traded: $40.93 on 2008-01-04, $41.67 on 2009-12-31. NYSE: JPM.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of the period was accepted before the open (06:45-07:18 ET) and keeps its date: 2008-01-16,
  2008-04-16, 2008-07-17, 2008-10-15, 2009-01-15, 2009-04-16, 2009-07-16, 2009-10-14; the weekly date is the next trading day. The FY2007
  10-K was accepted during market hours (2008-02-29 15:24 ET); the FY2008 10-K after the close (2009-03-02 16:12 ET), so it is dated
  2009-03-03. A Q4 print extends the history from its release to the 10-K: FY2007 from 2008-01-16 (6 dates), FY2008 from 2009-01-15
  (7 dates).
- **Revenue: total net revenue on the reported basis** (noninterest revenue plus net interest income), the income statement's own
  total, each year from the latest filing that reports it (the FY2007 10-K restates 2003-2006 for reclassifications). The managed basis,
  which adds back securitized credit card results and tax-equivalent adjustments, is the company's own presentation and is not used.
  Acquisitions are in the figures as published: Bank One from 2004-07-01 (2004 holds six months of the combined firm), Bear Stearns from
  2008-05-30, Washington Mutual's banking operations from 2008-09-25. Nothing is made pro forma.
- **EPS: diluted EPS from continuing operations** (before the extraordinary gain on the Washington Mutual acquisition, from its first
  report on 2008-10-15), each year from the latest filing that reports it:
  - **The company's figure excluding merger costs where a filing on the same basis publishes it** (the ACN rule; the SHW Valspar
    precedent): each supplement prints "Income from continuing operations excluding merger costs" a diluted share. FY05 $2.45 (GAAP
    $2.32) from the Q4 2006 supplement, FY06 $3.87 ($3.82), FY07 $4.42 ($4.38) and FY08 $0.92 ($0.84 before the extraordinary gain;
    net income $1.37). The company itself dropped "operating earnings" on 2006-01-01, saying merger costs and litigation charges "had
    been excluded previously from operating results because they were deemed nonrecurring; they are included now" (FY2006 10-K), and
    keeps this one line as a non-GAAP figure; the difference is $0.04 to $0.13 a share.
  - **FY03 $3.17 and FY04 $1.48 are GAAP.** The operating EPS of the FY2004 and FY2005 10-Ks (which also removes the litigation reserve
    charges) was published before the FY2006 10-K restated 2002-2005 for the corporate trust businesses sold to The Bank of New York
    (discontinued operations), on the earlier basis (the UNP trucking rule; the PEP 2001-2002 reading). FY04's listed nonoperating
    items ($1,365M of merger costs, the $3,700M litigation reserve charge and accounting policy conformity; $3,745M after tax, FY2005
    10-K) are under its $4,260M income from continuing operations, so the AAPL FY2002 test is not met and the year stays: $1.48 is 53% of
    the EPS without them. It is close, and it is the worst year of the history (below).
  - **FY2002 is excluded, a distorted year** (the AAPL FY2002 test). Its special items ($1,210M of merger and restructuring costs, the
    $1,300M Enron-related surety and litigation charge, $98M of excess real estate; $1,721M after tax, FY2002 10-K) exceed its $1,514M
    income from continuing operations as the FY2006 10-K restates it ($0.73 a share), and the operating EPS without them ($1.66) is on
    the earlier basis. So the history and the P/E window start with FY2003 (`pe_window_start` 2003-01-01; the ACN FY02 and LMT rule):
    a 5.0-year window on 2008-01-04, 7.0 years at the end of 2009. FY2001 ($0.80, with $1,715M of after-tax items against $1,694M of net
    income) precedes it, so no window reaches it.
  - **The 8-K of 2009-05-29 is a vintage of its own** (the MU 2010-03-04 encoding). It revises the FY2008 10-K's EPS for unvested share
    awards that participate in dividends (diluted, continuing operations: $1.45, $2.29, $3.78, $4.33, $0.81 for 2004-2008). FY04 takes
    the revised $1.45; the years with a company figure excluding merger costs keep it, first published on the earlier basis and not
    republished in the period (a seam; the XOM 2009 reading of the same accounting change). Each release from Q1 2009 prints its
    year-ago quarter as revised, used as printed.
  - **No EPS guide in any filing**, so the last full year stands (the rollover rule): FY06's $3.87 to the Q4 2007 print, FY07's $4.42
    (2008-01-17 to 2009-01-09), FY08's $0.92 (from 2009-01-16).
- **Diluted shares,** each year from the latest filing that reports it. The buyback term is net issuance: -16.8%/yr (FY2003-FY2006:
  2,055M to 3,574M shares, the Bank One merger), -12.5%/yr (to FY2007), -10.6%/yr (to FY2008). It is the method's reading of a merger paid in shares, and it drives BASE (below).
- **A quarter's figure restated by its own 10-Q** (the GOOG encoding, `restated`): nonperforming assets twice. The Q2 2008 release
  printed $6,591M against $2,586M a year earlier; the Q2 2008 10-Q (accepted 2008-08-11 16:31 ET, dated 2008-08-12) reports $6,233M
  against $2,423M, with subprime mortgage and home equity loans classified on the policy of the other home lending products. The Q3 2008
  release printed $15,910M; the Q3 2008 10-Q (accepted 2008-11-06 21:44 ET, dated 2008-11-07) reports $9,520M, without the loans
  acquired from Washington Mutual that are accounted for as purchased credit-impaired. Each 10-Q's figures replace the release's from its
  own date (2008-08-15 to 2008-10-10; 2008-11-07 to 2009-01-09). Every other signal row of every 10-Q and 10-K matches its release.
- **No guide in any filing.** No release, 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K found gives firm-wide revenue, EPS or a margin in numbers. The
  releases quote the chief executive on the economy in words; the slide decks give credit-loss outlooks (net charge-off rates and
  quarterly loss ranges by portfolio) and, in 2009, segment revenue run-rates; the Q3 2008 release estimates the Washington Mutual
  transaction's addition to 2009 earnings per share, one transaction's effect and not an EPS guide. Method r2 has
  no input for any of them, and none is encoded (the MU and GOOG reading). BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth plus the buyback
  term (the UNP rule), and there is no margin step. The builder refuses any guide, event, listing, split or company name until an
  encoding is decided.
- **Dividends,** the latest declared quarterly rate, each from the first filing that states it: $0.38 from the Q1 2007 release
  (2007-04-18; $1.52 a year on every 2008 date), $0.05 from the 8-K of 2009-02-24 (the press release of the evening before, accepted
  12:09 ET; $0.20 a year from 2009-02-27).
- **Signals.** A bank has no gross margin, inventories or operating margin, so the set is its own, with ACN's weights: total net
  revenue growth (0.20), the change in the provision for credit losses as a share of net revenue (0.20, lower is better: the credit
  cost, in the place of the gross margin), growth of noninterest expense less revenue growth (0.15, lower is better), growth of
  nonperforming assets less growth of loans (0.15, lower is better: in the place of the inventory and receivables gaps) and the change in
  the pre-tax margin (0.15: income before income tax expense over net revenue, in the place of the operating margin), plus the theme
  slot at 2/4. Each value is the supplement's own against the year-ago quarter in the same supplement, charges and acquisitions in, as
  published (Q3 2008's provision includes the $1,976M accounting conformity provision for Washington Mutual). Capital ratios are
  displayed, not scored: no weight was added to the six.
- **Thresholds by rule T over the decade of the FY2006 10-K** (the vintage public on 2008-01-04; 1997-2006): each change from the
  latest 10-K published by 2008-01-04 that reports both years (the FY2000 10-K for 1996-1997, FY2001 for 1997-1998, FY2002 for
  1998-1999, FY2003 for 1999-2000, FY2004 for 2000-2001, FY2005 for 2001-2002, FY2006 for 2002-2006). Ten values, eight for the pre-tax
  margin (the FY2000 and FY2001 summaries give no income tax line; rule T takes the years the filings report). Seams stay in, as
  published: the 1996-2001 figures are the pooled Chase and J.P. Morgan; revenue is "revenue" to FY2003 and "total net revenue" after;
  the provision is "for loan losses" in the FY2000 and FY2001 summaries; loans are each filing's own five-year loan table; 2004 holds
  six months of Bank One. The raw figures and values are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives every value and threshold
  and refuses to build if they differ.

  |---|---|---|

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2.** The 10-Ks tie results to markets and the economy ("JPMorgan Chase's results of operations could be
  adversely affected by U.S. and international markets and economic conditions.", FY2006 and FY2007; "Our businesses have been, and in
  the future will continue to be, materially affected by economic and market conditions", FY2008) and name competition, but do not call

  the company's own label (the LOW and SHW reading, against XOM, CAT and GOOG, whose 10-Ks use the word of themselves). No theme in
  `taxonomy_eras.json` is live for a bank holding company on these dates (OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services), so the watch list is empty.
  The kind changes the class label only.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the vintage's net revenue by component (noninterest revenue, net interest income),
  the total from the last year's revenue grown at the BASE revenue rate; the EPS check runs on the last year's pre-tax margin and tax
  rate (FY2008's tax line is a benefit, so its rate is negative).
- **Adds nothing:** the Bear Stearns merger agreement, amendment, guarantee and pro forma 8-Ks (March to June 2008, November 2008, March
  2009; the acquisition reaches the prints), the Washington Mutual press release (2008-09-26), the
  Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac preferred stock estimate (2008-08-25, one quarter's markdown, no guided number), the Capital Purchase

  (2009-05-08, 2009-06-02), the segment recast (2009-01-23, display), the preferred and trust securities offerings, the officer, bylaw and
  annual-meeting 8-Ks. None changes a guided number; the dividend 8-K is encoded above.
- **Anachronism list:** nothing added. A term check on the models takes its place: "Bear Stearns" first appears on 2008-04-17,
  "Washington Mutual" and "extraordinary" on 2008-10-16, the $0.05 dividend on 2009-02-27, the participating-securities revision on
