  that only look like years: FY2003's 2,055 million diluted shares, and on 13 dates Q1 2008's +2,087.9bp credit cost change.
- **Regression:** the shared code is untouched (the firewall tool gains a JPM entry); rebuilding the 2008-2009 dates of GOOG and the
  2008 dates of MU changes nothing. The other tickers were not rebuilt.
- **Firewall** (run after the build was committed, before any outcome; again after the correction): passes at the 16 cutoffs above
  (every print, vintage, 10-Q restatement and dividend date of the range, 2008-01-10 and 2010-01-01), 0 files changed and no planted
  text (1 to 105 dates each). The planted facts include a print with absurd values in every field, absurd full-year actuals for the year
  after the latest vintage, a later Q4 print excluding its own year, a later 10-Q restatement of the last print before the cutoff, a later
  vintage of the other kind excluding a year with planted texts, figures and window start, a guide, a dividend, a listing, a company
  name and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10. A full rebuild is byte-identical.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned). A price-to-earnings method on a bank through 2008-2009 produces extreme numbers, and
they are left as the rules give them:
- **FAIR on 18 dates, CHEAP on 26, RICH on 61; legacy tier WATCHLIST 20, ACCUMULATE 29, BUY 17, AVOID 39.** In 2008 the class moves
  with the price between FAIR, CHEAP and RICH (RICH on 10 dates, from late April to mid-May and from mid-September to the end of October); CHEAP on
  2008-11-07 to 2009-01-09; RICH on all 51 dates from the Q4 2008 print (2009-01-16), AVOID to 2009-10-09.
- **The 2009 reading rests on FY08's $0.92.** From 2009-01-16 the price ($15.93-47.16) is 17-51x the last full year's EPS, the
  65th-99th percentile of a window whose median is 14x, and 33% to 294% above an EPP floor of $11.96 (13x). On 2009-03-06, the low of the
  series ($15.93), the class is RICH and the tier AVOID.
- **BEAR is the worst year of the history:** -53.3%/yr (FY03's $3.17 to FY04's $1.48, the Bank One merger year with its litigation
  charge), a BEAR price of $8-9 through 2008; -79.2%/yr from the Q4 2008 print (FY07's $4.42 to FY08's $0.92), a BEAR EPS of $0.04 and
  a BEAR price of $0.41.
- **BASE is the quarter's revenue growth less the net share issuance:** -13.2%/yr (Q3 2007's +3.6% less 16.8%), -5.1% (Q4 2007),
  -23.5% (Q1 2008), -15.2% (Q2 2008), -21.0% (Q3 2008), -11.5% (Q4 2008), then +37.6% (Q1 2009: +48.2% with Bear Stearns and Washington
  Mutual in the revenue), +28.7% (Q2 2009) and +70.0% (Q3 2009: +80.6% against the quarter of 2008 with the markdowns). BULL is the
  history's CAGR (+6.9% to +8.7%/yr in 2008) and takes BASE's rate in 2009; XBULL is FY04 to FY06, +61.7%/yr (+63.4% after the revision).
- **The multiple in 2008:** $22.72-48.66 is 5.1-11.0x FY07's $4.42, the 0th-39th percentile of a window whose median is 11-12x; the
  price is under the EPP floor ($39.78, 9x) on 23 of the 52 dates, the deepest -43%.
- **The proxy composite** falls from 2.15 (Q3 2007) to 1.50 on the Q2 to Q4 2008 prints and rises to 3.05 on Q3 2009 (revenue growth and the
  pre-tax margin change at XBULL, both against the third quarter of 2008).

How far each call moves the classes (the 105 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- EPS at GAAP for FY2005-FY2008 instead of the company's figure excluding merger costs: 3 classes, 10 tiers;
- FY2002 kept at $0.73, the history and window from 2002: 39 classes (18 FAIR and 10 RICH to CHEAP, 11 RICH to FAIR) and 61 tiers (44
  to BUY), the largest call of the series: FY02 to FY03 becomes the best run and 2002's high multiples enter the window;
- FY2004 excluded (the AAPL test read as met; it is passed by $515M): 33 classes (10 FAIR to RICH, 8 FAIR to CHEAP, 10 RICH to FAIR, 5
  others) and 47 tiers (40 to BUY): BEAR would lose its -53.3% year;
- Q2 and Q3 2008 nonperforming assets as released (no 10-Q restatement): no class, no tier;
- every year at the revised GAAP figure from 2009-05-29 (the PEP reading of a restatement): no class, 2 tiers;
- no net share issuance in BASE (a flat share history; no rule says so, it shows what BASE rests on): 13 classes (12 RICH to FAIR), 14
  tiers;
- every signal at its BEAR value: 35 classes (18 FAIR and 17 CHEAP to RICH), no tier; at its XBULL value: 27 classes, no tier.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows the 2008 credit losses: the provision and nonperforming assets hold 0.35 of the weight
  (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; 27 to 35 classes move between the signals' extremes), and capital is left unscored;
- FY2002 excluded and FY2004 kept, both by the AAPL test on the items the filings list, and both large (39 and 33 classes); the
  trucking rule is what leaves each without a company figure;
- the company's figure excluding merger costs read as a figure excluding one-offs, though the company itself stopped calling merger
  costs nonrecurring in 2006 (3 classes);
- reported rather than managed revenue, and acquisitions left in the growth rates, which makes 2009's BASE +29% to +70%/yr;
- the Bank One share issuance read as the buyback term (13 classes);
- the 2009-05-29 revision read as the XOM seam rather than the PEP restatement (no class);
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL (label only);
- the credit-loss and segment outlooks and the Washington Mutual accretion estimate left unencoded, and the parts of the filings listed
  above as not read: a guide in an unread exhibit would be missed.

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/JPM/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

### JPM 2010-2013: the Q1 2012 restatements, the last company figures excluding merger costs, three dividend increases, Friday releases

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31 (52, 52, 52, 53), added to the 105 of 2008-2009 at the owner's request ("same rules as
before"). The method is still r2, the engine and its rule-T thresholds are unchanged, and no outcome of the earlier dates was consulted
for a decision here (their findings were written before this batch; none of them is an input). The 105 earlier models rebuild
byte-identical after the changes below.

```bash
python3 retro/build_jpm.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for c in 2010-01-10 2010-01-15 2010-02-24 2010-04-14 2010-07-15 2010-10-13 2011-01-14 2011-03-01 2011-03-18 2011-04-13 2011-07-14 \
         2011-10-13 2012-01-13 2012-02-29 2012-03-14 2012-04-13 2012-05-11 2012-07-13 2012-10-12 2013-01-16 2013-03-01 2013-04-12 \
         2013-07-12 2013-10-11 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c JPM; done
```

What was read, and how (the session's model directly). Nothing published after 2013-12-31 was downloaded or opened: the filing list was
cut at that date, so the Q4 2013 release (January 2014) and the FY2013 10-K were never fetched. Read by row and by search, as for
2008-2009: the financial supplements of the Q4 2009 to Q3 2013 releases (16 prints), the releases' text for outlook, guidance and
dividend sentences, the five-year summaries and Item 1A of the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks, the 10-Qs of Q1 2010 to Q3 2013 and the Q1 2012
10-Q/A compared by script with their releases on seven rows, and all 134 8-Ks of the period by their item text (the period has no
9.01-only batch: every one was opened), their exhibits scanned by keyword for per-share, revenue, margin and outlook statements, with
the eight that could carry guidance or restate figures looked at more closely (their item text and outlook pages; below). **Not read:** the slide decks and the 10-K and 10-Q text beyond
those searches and rows. The fact sheet is generated by the same script; 689 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own
filings (689/689, the 321 of 2008-2009 among them). The new source ids are `JPM26`-`JPM48`. Decided on 2026-11-19, before any 2010-2013
model was built or scored:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (06:39-07:49 ET) and keeps its date. Nine of the sixteen were
  released on a Friday, so the week has no later trading day and the weekly date is the release day itself, public before the open
  (2010-01-15, 2011-01-14, 2012-01-13, 2012-04-13, 2012-07-13, 2012-10-12, 2013-04-12, 2013-07-12, 2013-10-11; the ACN 2013 rule, which
  the builder enforces through `release_time`). 10-Ks: FY2009 before the open on 2010-02-24; FY2010 after the close (2011-02-28 16:27
  ET), dated 2011-03-01; FY2011 during market hours on 2012-02-29; FY2012 after the close (2013-02-28 16:06 ET), dated 2013-03-01. The
  Q4 prints extend the history for 6, 7, 7 and 6 dates.
- **EPS, the same rule:** diluted EPS before the extraordinary gain, each year from the latest filing that reports it, at the
  company's figure excluding merger costs where a supplement publishes it.
  - **FY09 $2.32** (GAAP $2.24) from the Q4 2009 supplement, and **FY08 restated to $0.88** (GAAP $0.81) by the same supplement, which
    republishes the year on the basis revised for participating securities ($0.92 before). A new print field, `restates` on the
    full-year actuals, applies it from 2010-01-15, six weeks before the FY2009 10-K (the PFE and LMT field; the history rule).
  - **FY05 $2.45, FY06 $3.87 and FY07 $4.42 stay**, first published before the revision and never republished: the seam decided for
    2009-05-29 (the XOM reading). The FY2009 10-K gives their revised GAAP figures ($2.29, $3.78, $4.33).
  - **FY10 $3.96** is both figures (no merger costs in the year). **From Q1 2011 the supplements print no figure excluding merger
    costs,** so FY11 $4.48 and FY12 $5.20 are GAAP, and each quarter's EPS is GAAP.
  - **No year 2009-2012 is a loss or a distorted year.** The filings list no one-off for 2009-2011 that approaches a year's income.
    FY2012's losses on the Chief Investment Office's synthetic credit portfolio are trading losses inside principal transactions
    revenue, not a listed one-off, and the year earned $21,284M.
  - **No EPS guide,** so the last full year stands: FY08's $0.92 on 2010-01-08, FY09's $2.32 (2010-01-15 to 2011-01-07), FY10's $3.96
    (to 2012-01-06), FY11's $4.48 (to 2013-01-11), FY12's $5.20 (from 2013-01-17).
- **Revenue and shares,** each year from the latest filing that reports it. From 2010-01-01 the firm consolidates its credit card
  securitization trusts and other entities (new accounting for transfers and consolidation), which adds to reported loans and net
  revenue from Q1 2010 with no restatement of earlier periods: the growth rates of 2010 against 2009 carry it, as published. The FY2009
  10-K restates the diluted share counts of 2005-2008 for participating securities (2005 3,511.9M against 3,557M); 2003 and 2004 keep
  the earlier filings' counts, a seam. The buyback term is net issuance of -10.0%/yr (FY2003-FY2009) falling to -6.7%/yr (FY2003-FY2012).
- **Q1 2012 is restated twice** (`restated` is now a list in publication order; the 2008 entries are its first two):
  - by its own 10-Q (accepted 2012-05-10 16:39 ET, dated 2012-05-11): nonperforming assets $11,953M against $15,149M a year earlier,
    with performing junior liens behind delinquent senior liens reported as nonaccrual on regulatory guidance; the release had
    $11,668M against $14,986M (2012-05-11 to 2012-07-06);
  - by the Q2 2012 release (2012-07-13), which prints the quarter as restated for the valuation of the synthetic credit portfolio
    (the 8-K of the same morning, Item 4.02, and the 10-Q/A of 2012-08-09): total net revenue $26,052M against $26,712M, income before

    the restated quarter is only the "previous quarter" of the trigger text (+3.3% against +5.9%).
  Every other row compared matches between each release and its 10-Q or 10-K.
- **No guide in any filing.** No release, 10-K, 10-Q row or 8-K found gives firm-wide revenue, EPS or a margin in numbers. The 8-Ks of
  2011-09-13 and 2011-12-08 say management "provided guidance": their slides give segment outlooks (Investment Bank markets revenue
  "down 30% +/-", fees of "$1B +/-", a Private Equity loss), and the other decks give credit, expense, capital and mortgage outlooks.
  Method r2 has no input for them, and none is encoded (the 2008-2009 reading). BASE stays the latest quarter's revenue growth plus the
  buyback term.
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the declared rate: $0.25 from the 8-K of 2011-03-18 (accepted 15:58 ET, two
  minutes before the close, so it meets that day's close: the market-hours rule), $0.30 from the 8-K of 2012-03-14 (12:17 ET; the press
  release of the evening before), and $0.38 from the Q2 2013 supplement (2013-07-12: "On May 21, 2013, the Board of Directors ...
  increased the Firm's quarterly stock dividend from $0.30 to $0.38 per share."). The 8-K of 2013-03-15 and the Q1 2013 release say
  the Board "intends to increase" it; an intention is not a declared rate, so the model carries $0.30 for seven weeks after the
  declaration (it can only lag; no class or tier depends on it, below).
- **Signals and thresholds: unchanged** (rule T over 1997-2006, frozen at the 2008 vintage). Each value is the supplement's own
  against the year-ago quarter in the same supplement. The row labels change (the firm-wide nonperforming assets total, period-end
  loans from the balance sheet from Q1 2011, the diluted share row); the series are the same, checked against the overlapping columns.
  Q3 2013's noninterest expense includes the $9.15B legal expense, as published.
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2,** in each 10-K's own words (FY2010-FY2012: "JPMorgan Chase's businesses are materially affected by
  economic and market conditions", "The financial services industry is highly competitive, and JPMorgan Chase's inability to compete
  successfully may adversely affect its results of operations."). The word "cyclical" does not appear in the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks.
  CLOUD, live from 2012-10-30, is scoped to on-premise IT, so the watch list stays empty.
- **Adds nothing:** the segment recasts (2010-04-09, 2011-09-30, 2012-12-04) and the three 8-Ks of 2011-11-04 that re-file the FY2010
  10-K and two 10-Qs for a segment change (their five-year consolidated rows equal the FY2010 10-K's); the capital-plan 8-Ks
  (repurchase authorizations, 2011-12-08 and 2013-03-15, apart from the dividends above); the stress-test results; the Chief
  Investment Office task-force report and the regulatory orders (2013-01-15, 2013-01-16, 2013-09-19); the mortgage and other settlements
  (2012-02-09, 2013-10-25, 2013-11-18, 2013-11-20: amounts reach the prints as legal expense); the debt, preferred and trust
  securities 8-Ks; the officer, bylaw and annual-meeting 8-Ks.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):

- **Controls:** 54 single-value alterations (each print's quarter EPS and revenue, each Q4 print's full-year revenue and EPS, the FY08

  2009-10-02: none changes a model dated before its publication, and all 54 change the first weekly date on or after it.

  is the 2011-01-14 close of $44.91, which equals FY2012's net interest income in billions. As a positive control, 13 to 18 of each
  latest print's own tokens appear in its model.
- **`retro_tool run` passes on all 209 dates.** The year warning fires on every date for FY2003's 2,055 million shares and on 18
  dates (2010-12-31 to 2011-04-29) for trading-day counts in a comment (2,015 to 2,099 days).
- **Regression:** the 105 dates of 2008-2009 rebuild byte-identical with the list form of `restated` and the `restates` field. The
  firewall tool's JPM entry plants a later restatement after any real one and a `restates` of every year. No other ticker's code is
  touched and none was rebuilt.
- **Firewall** (after the build was committed, before any outcome): passes at the 25 cutoffs above (every print, vintage,
  restatement and dividend date, 2010-01-10 and 2014-01-01), 0 files changed and no planted text, 106 to 314 dates each.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **RICH on 37 dates, FAIR on 39, CHEAP on 133; legacy tier AVOID 36, WATCHLIST 62, ACCUMULATE 68, BUY 43.** 2010 is RICH on 36 of
  52 dates (CHEAP on the 13 of the Q4 2009 print), 2011 CHEAP on 49 of 52, 2012 CHEAP on 44 and FAIR on 8, 2013 CHEAP on 27 and FAIR
  on 26. Robustness agrees on a single class on 46 of the 209 dates.
- **The class turns with the anchor year.** On FY09's $2.32 the 2010 price ($35.83-47.81) is 15-21x, the 58th-72nd percentile of a
  window whose median is 14-15x; on FY10's $3.96 the 2011 price ($28.48-48.00) is 7-12x, the 1st-51st percentile; on FY11's $4.48 and
  FY12's $5.20 it is 7-11x. The price is under the EPP floor on 19 of the 52 dates on FY10's EPS and 26 of the 53 on FY11's.
- **BEAR and XBULL are 2008:** BEAR is FY07's $4.42 to FY08's $0.88, -80.1%/yr, on every date from 2010-01-15, a BEAR price of $0.91
  to $1.66; XBULL is FY08 to FY10, +112.1%/yr, from 2011-01-14, an XBULL price near $700. Both sit far outside the price, so Ratio B and
  the tier rest on BULL (+3.2% to +7.0%/yr from 2011) and on where the price sits against the BULL price ($77-96).
- **BASE follows the quarters and the share issuance:** +24.5%/yr on the Q4 2009 print (+34.5% against the fourth quarter of 2008),
  then between -25.5% and +7.0%: revenue growth of -17.7% to +13.7% less 6.7 to 10.0 points of issuance.
- **The proxy composite** peaks at 3.40 on the Q4 2009 print and runs 2.05 to 2.90 afterwards; Q3 2013, with the legal expense in the
  expense gap (+61.8pp) and the pre-tax margin (-3,161bp), is the low at 2.05.

How far each call moves the classes (the 209 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- every year at the FY2009 10-K's revised GAAP figure instead of the company's figures (the PEP reading of the seam): 15 classes

- no net share issuance in BASE (no rule says so): 18 classes, 52 tiers;
- FY2008 out of the history (no rule says so; it shows what BEAR and XBULL rest on): 82 classes (58 CHEAP to FAIR, 13 CHEAP to RICH,

- every signal at its BEAR value: 123 classes (50 CHEAP and 39 FAIR to RICH, 34 CHEAP to FAIR), no tier; at its XBULL value: 16

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:

### JPM 2014-2017: the affordable housing restatement, GAAP every year, outlooks by component only, five declared dividend rates

208 weekly dates, 2014-01-10 to 2017-12-29 (51, 53, 52, 52), added to the 314 of 2008-2013 at the owner's request ("same rules as
before"). The code is the newest branch of the repository (its commit "JPM retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for 2010-2013;
README and CLAUDE.md", 2026-11-19), every other recent retro branch being its ancestor. Built in a new session: the git log it started from
carries the 2010-2013 commit messages, which hold no outcome, and `staging/retrospective/JPM/FINDINGS.md` was not opened until every
decision, check and sensitivity below was written down. The method is still r2, the engine and its rule-T thresholds are unchanged, and
each decision applies a rule that existed before (the r2 history, rollover and distorted-year rules, the UNP BASE rule, the ACN rule for a
company figure, the CMCSA after-close rule, the ACN Good Friday rule, the MSFT segment rule, the LMT window rule, the 2013 dividend rule).
The fact sheet only gains facts (`JPM49`-`JPM73`; the 2008-2013 part is unchanged) and the builder one field, `restates_revenue` (below);
the 314 earlier models rebuild byte-identical.

```bash
python3 retro/build_jpm.py --weekly 2014-01-06 2017-12-31                   # 208 dates, 2014-01-10 .. 2017-12-29
for c in 2014-01-12 2014-01-14 2014-02-20 2014-04-11 2014-07-02 2014-07-15 2014-10-14 2015-01-14 2015-02-25 2015-04-14 2015-07-02 \
         2015-07-14 2015-10-14 2016-01-14 2016-02-24 2016-04-13 2016-06-30 2016-07-14 2016-10-14 2017-01-13 2017-03-01 2017-04-05 \
         2017-04-13 2017-07-14 2017-10-06 2017-10-12 2018-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c JPM; done
```

The range starts on Monday 2014-01-06: 2013-12-31, built with 2010-2013, is ISO week 2014-W01.

What was read, and how (the session's model directly, with no delegated transcription). The filing list is EDGAR's for CIK 19617, cut at
2017-12-31 (nothing filed later was downloaded or opened): the 177 8-Ks, 10-Ks and 10-Qs filed from 2013-10-12. Read by row and by search:
the financial supplements of the Q4 2013 to Q3 2017 releases (16 prints), each compared by script with every later supplement that reprints
its quarters; the releases' text for significant items, figures excluding them, outlook, guidance and dividend sentences; the five-year
summaries, statements of income, Item 1 (competition, segments) and Item 1A of the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks, with each 10-K's and 10-Q's
business outlook section; the twelve 10-Qs of Q1 2014 to Q3 2017, compared by script with their releases on seven rows (net revenue,
provision, noninterest expense, pre-tax income, diluted EPS, nonperforming assets, loans); every other 8-K by its item text, its exhibits
scanned by keyword for per-share, revenue, outlook and dividend statements, and the decks of the 30 Item 7.01 8-Ks (earnings, investor
days, the CCAR and DFAST results, conferences) for firm-wide outlooks. **Not read:** the decks' and the 10-K and 10-Q text beyond those
searches and rows. The facts are generated by a script from the filings' converted rows, as before; 257 strings were checked with
`verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (257/257). Decided on 2026-11-19, before any 2014-2017 model was built or scored:

- **Release timing.** Fifteen of the sixteen earnings 8-Ks were accepted before the open (06:39-07:54 ET; the calls at 8:30 or 10:00 a.m.)
  and keep their date. Q3 2015's was accepted on 2015-10-13 at 16:15 ET, after the close (the release's call was at 5:00 p.m.), so it is
  dated 2015-10-14 and its week's date is 2015-10-15 (the CMCSA after-close rule). Four releases came on a Friday and one on the Thursday
  before Good Friday, so each week's date is the release day itself, public before the open (2014-04-11, 2016-10-14, 2017-01-13,
  2017-04-13, 2017-07-14; the ACN rule, enforced through `release_time`). The 10-Ks were all accepted after the close and are dated the
  next trading day: FY2013 (2014-02-19 20:02 ET) 2014-02-20, FY2014 (2015-02-24 16:04) 2015-02-25, FY2015 (2016-02-23 16:17) 2016-02-24,
  FY2016 (2017-02-28 16:23) 2017-03-01. A Q4 print extends the history to its 10-K for 5, 6, 6 and 7 dates.
- **History: four vintages, each the ten years to its own 10-K's year** (the r2 history rule): FY2013 (2004-2013), FY2014 (2005-2014),
  FY2015 (2006-2015), FY2016 (2007-2016), each year from the latest filing that reports it. FY2003 leaves by itself and, with it, the
  FY2002 exclusion, so `eps_first_excluded` is empty and `pe_window_start` null from the FY2013 vintage (the LMT encoding; the window no
  longer reached 2003). Between a Q4 print and its 10-K the history holds eleven years, the vintage's ten and the new one: the builder's
  rule since 2008, as GOOG and LMT have it (PFE drops the oldest year; below, how much that moves).
- **EPS: diluted EPS before the extraordinary gain, GAAP for every year from FY2011.** FY13 $4.35, FY14 $5.29, FY15 $6.00, FY16 $6.19.
  The supplements still print no figure excluding merger costs. The releases list "significant items" each quarter, and two print a
  quarter's EPS without them (Q4 2013: "excluding these items, EPS and ROTCE1 would have been $1.40 and 15%"; Q3 2015: "$1.32 PER SHARE
  ... EXCLUDING TAX BENEFITS, LEGAL EXPENSE AND NET RESERVE RELEASES"), but no filing prints a full year without them, so every year stays
  GAAP (the ACN rule: a one-off without a company figure excluding it stays in); the quarter's EPS is GAAP and the release's figure goes in
  the print's note. No year is distorted: FY2013's legal expense, $11.1 billion before tax (Q4 2013 supplement), is under its $17,923M of
  net income even with no tax shield, so the AAPL FY2002 test is not met; the other years' listed items are smaller (legal expense $2.9
  billion, $3.0 billion and a $317M benefit in 2014-2016; the 2015 tax benefits are a fraction of $24.4 billion, so the mirror test is not
  met either). FY05-FY07 keep the company's pre-revision figures and FY08-FY10 theirs ($0.88, $2.32, $3.96), as in 2010-2013, while they
  remain in the ten years. No EPS guide, so the last full year stands: FY12's $5.20 on 2014-01-10, FY13's $4.35 from 2014-01-15, FY14's
  $5.29 from 2015-01-15, FY15's $6.00 from 2016-01-15, FY16's $6.19 from 2017-01-13.
- **The affordable housing accounting, adopted on 2015-01-01 retrospectively** ("certain prior period amounts have been revised"; "The
  impact on net income and earnings per share in prior periods was not material", Q3 2015 supplement): the amortization of tax-credit
  investments moves from other income to income tax expense, so revenue and pre-tax income rise and net income barely moves. Each figure
  enters from the first filing on the new basis, by the history rule:
  - the Q1 2015 supplement prints the 2014 quarters revised (Q4 2014 revenue $22,750M against $22,512M as released; Q3 2014 EPS $1.35
    against $1.36). From Q1 2015 every print's year-ago quarter is its own supplement's, on the new basis. Q4 2014's own growth cannot be
    restated (no filing gives Q4 2013 on the new basis), so it stays as released; it is only the "previous quarter" of the trigger text;
  - the Q4 2015 supplement prints FY2014 revenue at $95,112M ($94,205M in the FY2014 10-K) with the same $5.29 of EPS. A new full-year
    field, `restates_revenue` (the revenue counterpart of `restates`, the PFE encoding), applies it from 2016-01-14 to the FY2015 10-K;
  - the FY2015 10-K revises 2011-2014 (revenue $97,843M, $97,680M, $97,367M, $95,112M; EPS FY12 $5.19 and FY13 $4.34 for $5.20 and $4.35),
    while 2010 keeps the FY2014 10-K's $102,694M (the FY2015 10-K's five years start at 2011): a seam in the FY2015 and FY2016 vintages, as
    published (the ACN FY19 reading), one revenue step (2010-2011) on two bases.
- **Revenue and shares,** each year from the latest filing that reports it: 2009 from the FY2013 10-K, 2010 from the FY2014 10-K, 2011
  from the FY2015 10-K. The buyback term is still net issuance, shrinking as Bank One's shares leave the ten years: -3.2%/yr
  (FY2004-FY2013), -0.9%/yr (to FY2014), -0.7%/yr (to FY2015), -0.6%/yr (to FY2016). The Q1 2017 supplement revises the 2016
  quarters' diluted share counts ("The revision had no impact on the Firm’s reported earnings per share"); no filing in range revises
  FY2016's count (3,649.8M), so the history keeps it.
- **No restatement of a quarter.** Every row compared matches between each release and its 10-Q (twelve 10-Qs, seven rows). Later
  supplements revise earlier quarters three times: the Q4 2013 supplement's nonperforming assets ("certain loans that resulted from
  restructurings ... were reclassified as nonperforming loans. Prior periods were revised"; Q3 2013 $10,380M against $10,231M), the
  affordable housing revision above, and the 2016 share counts. None changes a figure a model uses (a revised quarter is at most the
  "previous quarter", whose revenue growth none of them changes), so `restated` is not used.
- **No guide in any filing.** No release, 10-K, 10-Q or 8-K gives firm-wide revenue, EPS or a pre-tax margin in numbers. The 10-Ks' and
  10-Qs' business outlook sections and the decks give components: adjusted expense ("below $59 billion" for 2014, "approximately $57
  billion" for 2015, "$56 billion" for 2016, "$58 billion" for 2017), net charge-offs, core loan growth, segment revenue, and from the Q4
  2015 deck (8-K of 2016-01-14) net interest income ("up ~$2B+" in 2016; "approximately $3 billion", then "$4.5 billion" and "$4 billion"
  higher in 2017) and, for 2016 only, "managed noninterest revenue of approximately $50 billion", on the managed basis the JPM rule does
  not use. No total is stated and none is derived (the MSFT segment rule, from MSFT's 8-K of 2024-08-21); the FY2014 10-K's "managed overhead
  ratio of approximately 55% over the next several years" is a later years' expense ratio, not a pre-tax margin guide (the UNP rule for a
  later year's target). BASE stays the latest quarter's revenue growth plus the buyback term, with no margin step.
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the declared rate. From July 2014 the 8-Ks that adjust the warrants' exercise
  price state each declaration ("This adjustment resulted from the declaration by the Board of Directors of JPMorgan Chase on May 20, 2014
  of a quarterly dividend of $0.40 per share"), ahead of the next supplement: $0.40 from the 8-K of 2014-07-01 (16:14 ET, dated
  2014-07-02), $0.44 from 2015-07-01 (16:41 ET, dated 2015-07-02), $0.48 from the CCAR 8-K of 2016-06-29 ("the current common stock
  dividend of $0.48 per share"; 16:51 ET, dated 2016-06-30), $0.50 from 2017-04-04 (16:30 ET, dated 2017-04-05), $0.56 from 2017-10-05
  (16:34 ET, dated 2017-10-06). The CCAR 8-Ks of 2014-03-26, 2015-03-11 and 2017-06-28 and the releases after them say the Board "intends to
  increase" the dividend: an intention, not a declared rate (the 2013 rule), so the model carries the old rate for two to seven weeks
  after each declaration and 14 to 16 weeks after each intention (no class or tier depends on it, below).
- **Signals and thresholds: unchanged** (rule T over 1997-2006). Each value is the supplement's own against the year-ago quarter in the
  same supplement; legal expense and reserve releases are in, as published (Q3 2014's pre-tax margin +3,157bp and expense gap -38.0pp
  against the quarter of 2013 with $9.3 billion of legal expense). The Tier 1 ratio (display) is the supplement's own: Basel III from 2014.
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2,** in each 10-K's own words ("JPMorgan Chase’s businesses are materially affected by economic and market
  conditions", "The financial services industry is highly competitive, and JPMorgan Chase’s inability to compete successfully may adversely
  affect its results of operations."). "Cyclical" appears in the FY2015 and FY2016 10-Ks only as the regulators' "countercyclical capital
  buffer". The competitors listed include "e-commerce and other Internet-based companies" (FY2013 on) and "financial technology
  companies" (FY2015 on); no theme in `taxonomy_eras.json` is scoped to a bank on these dates (OFFSHORE to IT services, CLOUD to
  on-premise IT, ECOMMERCE to physical retail, STREAMING to linear TV, ENERGY_TRANSITION to oil, gas and coal), so the watch list stays
  empty and the words stay in the "why" (the PEP obesity rule). The business line takes each 10-K's reportable segments (Asset & Wealth
  Management from the FY2016 10-K); the earlier vintages keep theirs.
- **Adds nothing:** the earnings decks and investor days beyond the outlooks above; the CCAR and DFAST results (2014-03-20, 2015-03-05,
  2016-06-23, 2017-06-22) and capital plans, the additional $1.88 billion repurchase (2016-03-17); the settlements (Madoff 2014-01-07, FHA
  mortgage lending 2014-02-05, foreign exchange 2014-11-12, 2015-05-14 and 2015-05-20, Lehman and Ambac 2016-01-25, the DBNTC and FDIC term
  sheet 2016-08-19, the DOJ, SEC and Federal Reserve 2016-11-17, Lehman 2017-02-01; amounts reach the prints as legal expense); the
  resolution-plan 8-K (2016-10-04); the governance, bylaw, officer and annual-meeting 8-Ks; the debt, preferred stock, redemption and
  tender-offer 8-Ks. None changes a guided number; the dividend 8-Ks are encoded above.

  the first one on or after it: none changes a model dated before its publication, and all 54 change the first weekly date on or after it.

  plants actuals that restate every year's revenue as well as its EPS. No other ticker's code is touched and none was rebuilt.

  date, 2014-01-12 and 2018-01-01), 0 files changed and no planted text, 315 to 522 dates each.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **RICH on 195 dates, FAIR on 13, CHEAP on none; legacy tier AVOID 200, WATCHLIST 8.** 2014 is RICH on 49 of 51 dates, 2015 on 47 of
  53, 2016 on 47 of 52, 2017 on all 52. Eleven of the 13 FAIR dates fall between a Q4 print and its 10-K (six in early 2015, five in
  early 2016), the other two are 2014-01-10 and 2014-05-16. Robustness agrees on a single class on 31 dates (28 of them in 2017).
- **BEAR and XBULL are still 2008 on every date:** BEAR is FY07's $4.42 to FY08's $0.88, -80.1%/yr, a BEAR price of $1.34 to $1.98, so
  the downside is about 97% throughout; XBULL is FY08 to FY10, +112.1%/yr. Ratio B therefore rests on the upside to BULL, and RICH follows
  from Ratio B of 1.75 or more (1.27 to 110, and infinite on 48 dates from 2016-12-09, when the price is above the BULL price).
- **BULL falls as the low early years leave the ten years:** +13.0%/yr (FY04's $1.45 to FY13's $4.35), +8.9% (FY05 to FY14), +5.0% (FY06
  to FY15), +3.8% (FY07 to FY16), and between a Q4 print and its 10-K the eleven-year span gives more (+13.8% from FY04 in early 2015,
  +9.4% from FY05 in early 2016), which is where most FAIR dates sit. BASE runs from -14.8%/yr (2014-01-10, Q3 2013's -8.1% revenue less
  issuance) to +7.6%/yr (Q3 2016), and sets BULL where it is higher (the Q3 2016, Q1 2017 and Q2 2017 prints).
- **The multiple:** $53.31-62.70 in 2014 is 11.2-14.4x the anchor year, the 53rd-77th percentile of a window whose median is 10.8x to
  11.7x over the four years; 2015 10.3-14.4x (30th-79th); 2016 9.5-14.5x (19th-84th); 2017 $82.64-107.45 is 13.4-17.4x FY16's $6.19
  (78th-86th). The EPP floor is 9x on every date ($39.15 to $55.71) and the price is never under it.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- everything listed for 2008-2013 still stands where its years remain in the ten: the signals and their 1997-2006 thresholds (now moving
  only 9 to 13 classes), FY2004 kept (5 classes, to 2015-02-24), the company's pre-revision figures for FY05-FY09 (12 classes), reported
  rather than managed revenue;
- the eleven-year history between a Q4 print and its 10-K, the builder's rule, which holds most FAIR dates (10 classes the other way);
- every year at GAAP although two releases print a quarter without significant items (no filing gives a full year without them, so no
  sensitivity can be run);
- the component outlooks (net interest income, managed noninterest revenue, adjusted expense) left unencoded under the segment rule (no
  class either way for 2016's), and the managed overhead ratio target read as a later years' expense target;

  Q4 2014's growth kept as released;
- the warrant-adjustment 8-Ks read as the first filings to state each declared dividend, and the CCAR announcements as intentions;
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL, and "financial technology companies" left without a theme (none in the taxonomy is scoped to a bank
  on these dates);

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/JPM/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

### JPM 2018-2021: FY2017 at the company's figure, revisions by filing, a 10-Q restatement in 2020, CRYPTO on the watch list

209 weekly dates, 2018-01-05 to 2021-12-31 (52, 52, 53, 52), added to the 522 of 2008-2017 at the owner's request. The code is the newest
branch of the repository (this session's push of 2014-2017; no other branch has later commits). **Disclosure:** this batch was decided in
the same session that computed the 2014-2017 outcomes and wrote their findings, so its builder had read the 2008-2017 hindsight results
before any decision here. No decision uses them: each applies a rule that existed before or another ticker's encoding, named in its
bullet, and every alternative is measured below before any 2018-2021 outcome was computed. The method is still r2, the engine and its
rule-T thresholds are unchanged, and the 522 earlier models rebuild byte-identical. The fact sheet only gains facts (`JPM74`-`JPM95`);
the builder gains the CRYPTO watch list (below), which changes no earlier output.

```bash
python3 retro/build_jpm.py --weekly 2018-01-01 2021-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2018-01-05 .. 2021-12-31
for c in 2018-01-02 2018-01-12 2018-02-28 2018-04-13 2018-07-13 2018-10-05 2018-10-12 2019-01-15 2019-02-27 2019-04-12 2019-07-16 \
         2019-10-15 2020-01-14 2020-02-26 2020-04-14 2020-07-14 2020-10-13 2020-10-21 2020-11-03 2021-01-15 2021-02-24 2021-04-14 \
         2021-07-13 2021-10-13 2022-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c JPM; done
```

What was read, and how (the session's model directly). The filing list is EDGAR's for CIK 19617, cut at 2021-12-31: the 152 8-Ks,
10-Ks and 10-Qs filed from 2017-10-20 to 2021-12-17. Read by row and by search, as for 2014-2017: the 16 supplements of the Q4 2017 to Q3
2021 releases, each compared by script with every later supplement that reprints its quarters; the releases' headlines, significant
items, figures excluding them and dividend sentences; the five-year summaries, statements of income, Items 1 and 1A and business outlook
sections of the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks; the twelve 10-Qs of 2018-2021 against their releases on seven rows (net revenue, provision,
noninterest expense, pre-tax income, diluted EPS, nonperforming assets, loans), and their outlook sections; every other 8-K by its item
text, its exhibits searched for per-share, revenue, outlook and dividend statements, and the decks of the 23 Item 7.01 8-Ks for
firm-wide outlooks. **Not read:** the decks' and the 10-K and 10-Q text beyond those searches and rows. 266 strings were checked with
`verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (266/266). Decided on 2026-11-19, before any 2018-2021 outcome was computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (06:43-06:47 ET). Six came on a Friday and are dated their own day
  (2018-01-12, 2018-04-13, 2018-07-13, 2018-10-12, 2019-04-12, 2021-01-15); the others' weeks are dated the next trading day. The 10-Ks
  were accepted after the close: FY2017 (2018-02-27 16:23 ET) dated 2018-02-28, FY2018 (2019-02-26 16:57) 2019-02-27, FY2019 (2020-02-25
  16:31) 2020-02-26, FY2020 (2021-02-23 16:17) 2021-02-24. A Q4 print extends the history to its 10-K for 7, 6, 6 and 6 dates.
- **History: four vintages, the ten years to each 10-K's year** (2008-2017, 2009-2018, 2010-2019, 2011-2020), each year from the latest
  filing that reports it. The 10-Ks revise earlier years as they go: the FY2017 10-K restates the diluted share counts of 2013-2016
  (3,864.9M to 3,690.0M against 3,814.9M to 3,649.8M before; EPS unchanged), the FY2018 10-K puts 2014-2016 revenue on the 2018 basis
  (the revenue recognition guidance, "applied retrospectively"), and the FY2020 10-K revises 2016-2019 revenue for the 2020
  reclassifications. Years older than each 10-K's five keep their earlier filings' figures: seams as published (the ACN FY19 reading).
- **FY2017 at the company's figure excluding significant items, $6.87** (GAAP $6.31). The Q4 2017 release: "FULL-YEAR 2017 RECORD NET
  INCOME OF $26.5 BILLION, OR $6.87 PER SHARE EXCLUDING SIGNIFICANT ITEMS": the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act's estimated $2.4 billion decrease
  in net income and a $406 million after-tax legal benefit (the Washington Mutual settlements). A company-published full year without
  one-offs is used (the ACN rule), as LMT's FY2017 $13.33. The items are well under the year's net income, so the AAPL test would keep
  GAAP; the figure is used because it is published, not because the year is distorted. No later filing republishes 2017 without them
  (the 10-Ks give GAAP $6.31), so the release's figure stays as the latest filing that publishes one (the LMT and CAT rule), in every
  vintage that holds 2017. The quarter's EPS stays GAAP ($1.07; the release's $1.76 in the note), as for Q4 2013.
- **FY2018 $9.00, FY2019 $10.72 and FY2020 $8.88 are GAAP.** No release prints a full year without its significant items (Q4 2020 prints
  the quarter "EXCLUDING CREDIT RESERVE RELEASES OF $2.9 BILLION ($3.07 PER SHARE)", a quarter only). FY2020's credit reserve builds are
  the provision, not a listed one-off, and the year earned $29.1 billion: neither the AAPL test nor its mirror is met in any year.
- **Revenue restated from the first filing that prints it** (`restates_revenue`, the 2014-2017 field): FY2017 at $100,705M from the Q4

  RICH 26, FAIR 20, CHEAP 6. 2020: CHEAP 32, RICH 13, FAIR 8. 2021: RICH on all 52. Robustness agrees on a single class on 116 dates.
- **The 2008 trough leaves in two steps.** BEAR is FY07 to FY08, -80.1%/yr, on the 8 dates to 2018-02-23; from the FY2017 10-K FY2007
  leaves the ten years, so BEAR is FY12 to FY13, -16.4%/yr (a BEAR price of $38-59), and from the FY2020 Q4 print FY19 to FY20, -17.2%.
  XBULL stays FY08 to FY10, +112.1%/yr, to 2019-02-22; then FY09 to FY11 (+39.0%) and from the FY2019 10-K FY17 to FY19 (+24.9%).
  BULL runs from the history's first year: from FY08's $0.88 it is +25.7%/yr (+26.2% in the Q4 2018 interval) from 2018-03-02 to
  2019-02-22, then +16.3% (from FY09), +11.7% (FY10) and +7.9% (FY11), and BASE sets it where higher.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the builder had read the 2008-2017 hindsight findings before deciding this batch (the disclosure above); every decision applies an
  earlier rule, and each alternative's effect is listed above;
- the signals, chosen in 2008 by a builder who knew the credit cycle: with COVID's provision swings beyond their 1997-2006 extremes they
  move 54 classes at BEAR and 37 at XBULL, the largest call here;
- FY2017 at the company's figure rather than GAAP (13 classes, 9 tiers);
- everything listed for 2008-2017 that still reaches these dates: the signals and their 1997-2006 thresholds, the company's figures for
  FY08-FY10 (to FY2010's exit from the ten years), reported rather than managed revenue, the eleven-year history between a Q4 print and
  its 10-K (8 classes);
- the component outlooks left unencoded, the medium-term targets read as later years', the warrant-adjustment 8-Ks as the first
  statements of the 2018 rate, the CCAR announcements as intentions;
- CRYPTO judged on the vintage in force from its live date, so the FY2019 10-K's words carry it for 17 weeks (text only), and DURABLE
  rather than CYCLICAL;
- the decks and the 10-K and 10-Q text read only by the searches and rows above.

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/JPM/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

### JPM 2022-2026: FY2024 at the company's figure, Q4 2024 restated by its 10-K, First Republic and the Visa gains as published, CRYPTO on the FY2025 10-K's distributed-ledger words, the last date 2026-11-13

254 weekly dates, 2022-01-07 to 2026-11-13 (52, 52, 52, 52, 46), added to the 731 of 2008-2021 at the owner's request ("same rules as
before"). The code is the newest branch of the repository (its commit "JPM retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for 2018-2021;
README and CLAUDE.md", 2026-11-19), every other recent retro branch being its ancestor. Built in a new session. What it saw of the
earlier batches before deciding this one: the one-line subjects of the git log, `CLAUDE.md` and the README sections of JPM 2008-2021
(their decisions, checks, point-in-time builds and sensitivities). `FINDINGS.md`, `SERIES.md`, `index.json`, every `outcome.json` and the
full message of the 2018-2021 hindsight commit were not opened until every decision, check and sensitivity below was written down. The
method is still r2, the engine and its rule-T thresholds are unchanged, and each decision applies a rule that existed before (named in its
bullet). The fact sheet only gains facts (`JPM96`-`JPM120`; the 2008-2021 part is byte-identical). The builder gains no rule: its
docstring, and one text fix that also corrects six 2021 models (below, "A leak found and corrected").

```bash
python3 retro/build_jpm.py --weekly 2022-01-03 2026-11-15                   # 254 dates, 2022-01-07 .. 2026-11-13
for c in 2022-01-02 2022-01-14 2022-02-23 2022-04-13 2022-07-14 2022-10-14 2023-01-13 2023-02-22 2023-04-14 2023-07-14 2023-10-13 \
         2024-01-12 2024-02-20 2024-04-12 2024-07-12 2024-10-11 2025-01-15 2025-02-18 2025-04-11 2025-07-15 2025-10-14 2026-01-13 \
         2026-02-17 2026-04-14 2026-07-14 2026-10-13 2026-11-14; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c JPM; done
```

The range starts on Monday 2022-01-03 (2021-12-31, built with 2018-2021, is in ISO week 2021-W52) and ends with the last complete week:
the series was built on Thursday 2026-11-19, during the session, so the week of 2026-11-16 is left out (a build after its close would add
2026-11-20). The newest dates have no outcome yet.

What was read, and how (the session's model directly, with no delegated transcription). The filing list is EDGAR's for CIK 19617, cut at
2026-11-19 (nothing filed later exists): the 158 8-Ks, 10-Ks and 10-Qs filed from 2021-10-14, all downloaded. Read by row and by search, as
for 2014-2021: the 20 supplements of the Q4 2021 to Q3 2026 releases (each compared by script with every later supplement that reprints its
quarters), the releases' headlines, significant items, figures excluding them and dividend sentences; the selected data, Items 1 and 1A
and business outlook sections of the FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks, each compared with its Q4 supplement on revenue, provision, expense, pre-tax
income, tax, diluted EPS and shares, and on year-end nonperforming assets and loans; the fifteen 10-Qs of Q1 2022 to Q3 2026 against their
releases on seven rows (net revenue, provision, noninterest expense, pre-tax income, diluted EPS, nonperforming assets, loans; the current
and year-ago columns), and their outlook sections; every other 8-K by its item text, its exhibits searched for per-share, revenue, outlook
and dividend statements, and the decks of the 32 Item 7.01 8-Ks (earnings, four Investor Days, the 2026 Company Update, the First Republic
call, the DFAST results) for firm-wide outlooks. **Not read:** the decks' and the 10-K and 10-Q text beyond those searches and rows. The
facts are generated by a script from the filings' converted rows, as before (each figure read from its own row by label, every rate
computed by the builder's own `derived`); 340 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (340/340). Decided on
2026-11-19, before any 2022-2026 model was built or scored:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (06:30-06:48 ET) and keeps its date. Eleven came on a Friday and
  are dated their own day (2022-01-14, 2022-10-14, 2023-01-13, 2023-04-14, 2023-07-14, 2023-10-13, 2024-01-12, 2024-04-12, 2024-07-12,
  2024-10-11, 2025-04-11; the ACN rule, through `release_time`); the others' weeks are dated the next trading day. The 10-Ks were all
  accepted after the close: FY2021 (2022-02-22 16:56 ET) dated 2022-02-23, FY2022 (2023-02-21 16:13) 2023-02-22, FY2023 (Friday 2024-02-16
  16:20) 2024-02-20 after Presidents' Day, FY2024 (Friday 2025-02-14 16:17) 2025-02-18, FY2025 (Friday 2026-02-13 16:20) 2026-02-17; every
  10-Q after the close too. A Q4 print extends the history to its 10-K for 6, 6, 6, 5 and 5 dates.
- **History: five vintages, the ten years to each 10-K's year** (2012-2021 to 2016-2025), each year from the latest filing that reports
  it. From FY2021 the 10-Ks give three years of selected data (2019-2021 and so on), so the years before them keep the latest 10-K that
  reported them (the ACN rule for a 10-K without five-year selected data): 2016-2018 stay the FY2020 10-K's, 2012-2015 the earlier 10-Ks'.
  The FY2021 10-K revises 2019 revenue to $115,720M ($115,399M in the Q4 2020 supplement, $115,627M in the FY2019 10-K) for the
  first-quarter 2021 reclassification of deferred investment tax credits (revenue and income tax expense up, net income unchanged): a
  year from the latest filing that reports it.
- **FY2020 revenue restated by the Q4 2021 supplement** (`restates_revenue`, the 2014-2017 field): $119,951M against the FY2020 10-K's
  $119,543M, the same reclassification ("In the first quarter of 2021, the Firm reclassified certain deferred investment tax credits.
  Prior-period amounts have been revised to conform with the current presentation."), from 2022-01-14 to the FY2021 10-K.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS, except FY2017 and FY2024 at the company's figures excluding significant items** (the ACN rule, as FY2017's
  $6.87). The Q4 2024 release: "RECORD FULL-YEAR 2024 NET INCOME EXCLUDING SIGNIFICANT ITEMS OF $54.0 BILLION ($18.22 PER SHARE)" (GAAP
  $19.75: "a $7.9 billion net gain related to Visa shares, a $1.0 billion donation of Visa shares to pre-fund contributions to the Firm’s
  Foundation, $546 million of net investment securities losses and a $725 million increase to the estimated FDIC special assessment").
  FY24 is $18.22 from 2025-01-15 in every vintage that holds 2024; no later filing republishes the year without those items (the 10-Ks
  give GAAP), so the release's figure stays (the LMT and CAT rule). The items are well under the year's $58.5 billion of net income, so
  neither the AAPL test nor its mirror is met: the figure is used because it is published, not because the year is distorted. Revenue
  and the pre-tax margin stay as reported: the JPM revenue rule names the income statement's total, and the release's revenue excluding
  significant items ($170.2 billion) is another basis. FY21 $15.36, FY22 $12.09, FY23 $16.23 and FY25 $20.02 are GAAP: their releases
  print quarters without significant items (Q4 2021 without credit reserve releases, Q2 2023, Q4 2023, Q1 2024, Q2 2024, Q2 2025, Q4
  2025, and Q2 and Q3 2026 after the range's years) but no full year. No year meets the AAPL test or its mirror: FY2023's $2.7 billion
  First Republic bargain purchase gain and $2.9 billion FDIC special assessment, FY2025's $2.2 billion Apple card reserve and $774 million
  tax benefit are fractions of $49.6 billion and $57.0 billion. Each quarter's EPS is GAAP; the release's figure goes in the print's
  note. No EPS guide: the last full year anchors each date (FY20's $8.88 on 2022-01-07, FY21's $15.36 from 2022-01-14, FY22's $12.09
  from 2023-01-13, FY23's $16.23 from 2024-01-12, FY24's $18.22 from 2025-01-16, FY25's $20.02 from 2026-01-14).
- **Q4 2024 restated by its own 10-K** (`restated`, the 2008, 2012 and 2020 encoding for a quarter its own periodic report revises): the
  FY2024 10-K reports year-end nonperforming assets of $9,300M against the release's $9,291M (consumer nonaccrual loans retained $3,233M
  against $3,224M; the 10-K's row "Nonperforming assets | 9,300 | 7,597 | 7,247"), from its date (2025-02-18) to the Q1 2025 print. Every
  other compared row of every 10-K and 10-Q matches its release; the later supplements revise no other figure a model uses.
- **Acquisitions and accounting changes as published** (the JPM rule since 2008): First Republic's banking operations, acquired from
  the FDIC on 2023-05-01, are in the figures from Q2 2023 (loans of $1,300,069M against $1,128,896M the quarter before; the $2.7 billion
  bargain purchase gain in Q2 2023 revenue); nothing is made pro forma, and the deck's "Expected to generate >$500mm in net income" is one
  transaction's effect, not an EPS guide (the Washington Mutual reading of 2008). The Visa B-1 exchange gain ($7.9 billion, Q2 2024) and the
  Q2 2026 Visa and equity-investment gains ($4.6 billion and $1.0 billion) are in their quarters' revenue as published, so Q2 2024's and
  Q2 2026's growth (+21.5% and +27.7%) set BASE for their quarters, and Q2 2025's (-10.5%, against Q2 2024 with the gain) for its own.
  The tax-credit-structures accounting adopted on 2024-01-01 under the modified retrospective method revises no prior period, so 2024's
  growth carries it as published (the 2010 consolidation reading).
- **No guide in any filing.** The 10-Ks', 10-Qs' and decks' outlooks give net interest income (with and without Markets), adjusted
  expense and the card net charge-off rate: components, so nothing is derived (the MSFT segment rule; unlike 2016 and 2018, no
  noninterest revenue outlook is given, so not even a test total can be formed). The Investor Days' "~17% ROTCE target" is a
  through-the-cycle target (the UNP rule for a later years' target). BASE stays the latest quarter's revenue growth plus the buyback term,
  now a net buyback (diluted shares from 3,822.2M in 2012 to 2,781.5M in 2025).
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states the declared rate, every one a supplement's footnote: $1.05 from the Q3 2023
  supplement (2023-10-13: "On September 19, 2023, the Board of Directors declared a quarterly common stock dividend of $1.05 per
  share."), $1.15 from Q1 2024 (2024-04-12), $1.25 from Q3 2024 (2024-10-11), $1.40 from Q1 2025 (2025-04-11), $1.50 from Q3 2025
  (2025-10-14) and $1.65 from Q3 2026 (2026-10-13). The CCAR 8-Ks (2023-06-30 and its 8-K/A of the same evening, 2024-06-28, 2025-07-01,
  2026-06-24) and the Q2 10-Qs state intentions (the 2013 rule); the 8-K of 2022-06-27 an intention to maintain $1.00.
- **Signals and thresholds: unchanged** (rule T over 1997-2006). Each value is the supplement's own against the year-ago quarter in the same
  supplement; the reserve builds and releases, the Apple card reserve (Q4 2025's provision), the FDIC special assessment (Q4 2023's
  expense) and the securities losses are in, as published.
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2,** in each 10-K's own words ("Unfavorable market and economic conditions can have an adverse effect on
  JPMorgan Chase’s wholesale businesses.", the FY2025 10-K's "could adversely affect JPMorganChase’s wholesale businesses."; the
  competitive-environment sentence of each); "cyclical" appears only in "countercyclical capital buffer". The business line is each 10-K's
  segments: four and Corporate to the FY2023 10-K, three and Corporate from the FY2024 10-K (the Commercial & Investment Bank formed in
  the second quarter of 2024; the 8-Ks of 2024-01-25 and 2024-05-15 recast segments only).
- **CRYPTO stays on the watch list, on the words of the 10-K in force** (the 2018-2021 rule; `crypto_quote`). The FY2021-FY2024 10-Ks keep
  the competition risk factor's sentence with small changes (FY2021: "could be significantly disrupted by the use of new technologies,
  such as cryptocurrencies and other applications that use secure distributed ledgers, that require no intermediation"; FY2023 and
  FY2024: "... using secure distributed ledgers, that may not require intermediation"). The FY2025 10-K drops the word cryptocurrencies
  from that sentence ("face the risk of disruption to payments processing and other products and services from the use of new
  technologies that may not require intermediation, such as tokenized securities or other products that leverage distributed ledger
  technology") and lists "cryptocurrency, including stablecoins" and "tokenized securities" among the products non-depository institutions
  offer, and "digital asset and other financial technology companies" among competitors. CRYPTO's registered scope is crypto and DeFi
  disintermediating payments networks and banks, so the reworded risk stays on the list from 2026-02-20 (the NKE FY2024 reading of a
  reworded risk; a judgement call, text only). No dated evidence shows the market pricing crypto disintermediation of JPMorgan Chase, so
  DURABLE stands; the factor pair is absent and the theme signal stays at 2/4.
- **GENAI out of scope.** GENAI is live from 2022-11-30, but its registered scope (software seats, IT services and BPO hours,
  professional information, search, education content and mobility) names no bank. The FY2021-FY2024 10-Ks name artificial intelligence
  only as regulation, a fraud and model risk, training and workforce displacement; the FY2025 10-K adds a risk factor ("JPMorganChase’s operations, results, and competitive
  standing could be adversely affected by the development of advanced technologies such as AI."), among its risks "replacement or
  disintermediation of direct customer relationships if AI agents autonomously manage or intermediate financial decisions and product
  selection or other services for customers". Those words stay in the FY2025 vintage's "why" (the PEP obesity rule); whether GENAI's scope
  should reach banking is the owner's call. ECOMMERCE, STREAMING, ENERGY_TRANSITION, EV, CLOUD and GLP1 are scoped to other industries.
- **Adds nothing:** the earnings decks beyond the outlooks above; the Investor Days (2022-05-23, 2023-05-22, 2024-05-20, 2025-05-19) and
  the Company Update (2026-02-23); the First Republic press release and call (2023-05-01); the Visa exchange-offer 8-K (2024-05-06; the
  gain reaches the Q2 2024 print); the segment and organization 8-Ks (2024-01-25, 2024-05-15); the CCAR and DFAST results and capital
  plans; the officer, director, compensation, by-law, annual-meeting and stock-sale 8-Ks; the
  debt, preferred stock, redemption and reference-rate 8-Ks. None gives firm-wide revenue, EPS or a margin in numbers or states a declared
  dividend rate.
- **Anachronism list:** nothing added (the JPM 2008-2009 precedent); the term check below takes its place.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):
- **A leak found and corrected.** The term check found the next 10-K named before it was filed: between a Q4 print and its 10-K the
  CRYPTO watch-list line read "JPMorgan Chase's own FY2025 10-K says '...'" (from 2026-01-14) while quoting the FY2024 10-K, because the
  builder labelled the quote with the year the Q4 print adds to the history. It names a filing not yet public, so it is a leak of a kind,
  though no figure comes with it. The builder now labels the quote with the 10-K in force (text only). The same line had the same error in
  the 2018-2021 batch: 2021-01-15 to 2021-02-19, six dates that named the FY2020 10-K before 2021-02-24 while quoting the FY2019 10-K's
  words. Those six models and their `analysis.json` are corrected (one word each; no number, class or tier changes; their outcomes are
  untouched, being price-only), and 28 of the new dates changed the same way before any outcome existed. After the fix, every "FY20xx
  10-K" label in all 985 models first appears on the first weekly date after that 10-K's filing.
- **Term check:** 45 dated wordings and figures of the new facts (each EPS anchor, FY24's $18.22 and its quote, the Q4 2024 restatement,
  FY20's revised revenue, each 10-K's new sentences and label, the stablecoin, tokenized-securities and AI-agent words, each dividend's
  declaration date, First Republic, the Visa gains, the Apple card reserve, the tax-credit accounting note) were searched in all 985 models:
  each first appears on or after its filing (most on the first weekly date after it; "First Republic" in the Q2 2023 print's note, after
  the 2023-05-01 announcement). One generic figure ("1.05") also occurs in older models as other numbers; the dividend sentence itself
  first appears on 2023-10-13.
- **Controls:** 73 single-value alterations (each print's quarter EPS and revenue, each Q4 print's full-year revenue and EPS, the FY2020
  revenue restatement, the Q4 2024 restatement, each vintage's last-year EPS, last-year revenue and CRYPTO words, each dividend), each
  rebuilt over the eight weekly dates before it and the first on or after it: none changes an earlier model, and all 73 change the first
  date on or after their filing.
- **Leak scan:** 109 hits in 205,159 (model, later token) pairs over the 306 dates from 2021-01-01, after dropping 33,687 tokens an
  earlier fact or the engine carries. All are later facts repeating text an earlier fact had already published: the FY2024 vintage's list
  of GAAP years inside the FY2023 vintage's (52 models), the FY2025 vintage's "the 10-K's three reportable segments" inside the FY2024
  vintage's (52), and the FY2024 vintage's quote of the Q4 2024 release's significant items, which the Q4 2024 print carries (5). As a
  positive control, 10 to 12 of 13 of each latest print's own tokens appear in its model. **Fact scan:** no fact published from 2022 names
  a date, year or quarter after its own publication.
- **`retro_tool run` passes on all 254 dates,** with no warning (the 34 corrected dates re-run after the fix).
- **Regression:** with the new fact sheet the 731 dates of 2008-2021 rebuild byte for byte, with a fresh price cache, before the text fix;
  after it, all but the six corrected 2021 dates.
- **Firewall** (run after the build was committed and pushed, before any outcome): passes at the 27 cutoffs above (every print,
  vintage, restatement and dividend date of the range, 2022-01-02 and 2026-11-14), 0 files changed and no planted text (731 to 985 dates
  each), with the JPM plants of 2008-2021 (a print absurd in every field with absurd full-year actuals, a later Q4 print, a later 10-Q
  restatement of the last print before the cutoff, a later vintage with planted CRYPTO words, a guide, a dividend, a listing, a company
  name and prices multiplied by 10). The 73 controls above are the positive control: each real fact reaches the first date after it.

  all from 2024-07-12 to 2024-10-04;
- no buyback term in BASE (a flat share history; no rule says so): 8 classes (5 FAIR to RICH, 3 CHEAP to FAIR), 18 tiers (down);
- the Q4-print intervals with ten years (the oldest year leaves with the Q4 print, the PFE reading): 28 models, no class, no tier;
- Q4 2024 as released (no 10-K restatement): 7 models; FY2020 at the FY2020 10-K's revenue (no `restates_revenue`): 6 models; the
  dividends from the intention 8-Ks: 59 models; CRYPTO off the watch list from the FY2025 10-K: 39 models (text only); none moves a class
  or a tier;
- every signal at its BEAR value: 83 classes (32 CHEAP and 40 FAIR to RICH, 11 CHEAP to FAIR); at its XBULL value: 33 classes (24 FAIR to
  CHEAP, 9 RICH to FAIR); no tier either way.
The classes rest on the multiple against a window whose median stays near 11x and on the signals' rule-T bands; the tier rests on BEAR
(FY21 to FY22) and XBULL (FY17 to FY19), which sit far from the price.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- FY2024 at the company's figure excluding significant items, the FY2017 rule applied to a year whose items were gains (2 classes, 4
  tiers), while revenue keeps the Visa gain;
- the Visa and equity gains left in the quarters' revenue growth, which sets BASE at +24.5% and +30.9% in two quarters and -7.4% in the
  quarter after (13 classes and 13 tiers in the test above): the largest encoding call of the batch, and the rule's own reading;
- the signals and their 1997-2006 thresholds, chosen in 2008 by a builder who knew the credit cycle (83 classes at BEAR, 33 at XBULL);
- CRYPTO kept on the FY2025 10-K's distributed-ledger and stablecoin words, and GENAI read as out of scope although the FY2025 10-K names
  AI agents that could disintermediate customer relationships (label only either way); DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL;
- First Republic and the 2024 accounting change in the growth rates as published;
- the component outlooks left unencoded and the ROTCE target read as through-the-cycle;
- the decks and the 10-K and 10-Q text read only by the searches and rows above: a firm-wide guide in an unread passage would be missed.

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/JPM/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

## V (Visa): the twenty-eighth ticker, in staging, 2008-2026 (from the Q4 FY09 print)

The V series is built apart from the other twenty-seven and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/V.json`), builder (`retro/build_v.py`, the GOOG builder with Visa's September fiscal year, figures in millions, a fiscal-year
revenue range and a dividend list) and engine (`retro/templates/v_engine.py.tmpl`, the GOOG engine with the share of gross revenues kept
after client incentives in the place of the gross margin and Visa's own rule-T thresholds). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter,
outcome or finding of another ticker enters a V model. The live `v_signal_model.py` (on other branches) and today's V profile in
`data/business_profiles.json` are 2026 analyses; neither was opened for this series, and neither is an input. Outputs go to
`staging/retrospective/V/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009 ("same
rules as before"); the code is the newest branch of the repository (its commit "JPM retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for
2022-2026; README and CLAUDE.md", 2026-11-19), every other recent retro branch being its ancestor.

```bash
python3 retro/build_v.py --weekly 2009-10-26 2009-12-31                     # 10 dates, 2009-10-29 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/V/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series V
for c in 2009-10-30 2009-11-23 2009-11-28 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c V; done
```

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** Under method r2 **10 of the 94 weekly dates of 2008-2009 can be built: 2009-10-29
to 2009-12-31**, and only they were. Nothing was invented to fill the rest (the BKR 2018, CTVA and KMI precedents):

- **2008-03-20 to 2008-10-24 (32 weeks): no full year of EPS.** Visa Inc.'s class A common stock listed on 2008-03-19 ("Our Class A common
  stock commenced trading on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “V” on March 19, 2008.", FY2008 10-K), but its predecessor had no
  shares: "There is no comparable earnings per share measure for 2007 as we were a non-stock company." (Q4 FY08 release). The first year
  with EPS is FY2008 (to 2008-09-30), first published in the Q4 FY08 release (2008-10-30). A model needs the stock's own current-FY P/E,
  so no date precedes it (the KMI and CTVA rule; a 2008 date would need an EPS anchor for a period that is not a year).
- **2008-10-31 to 2009-10-23 (52 weeks): FY2008 is a distorted year with no figure excluding only one-offs**, and it is the only year. Its
  GAAP $0.96 a diluted class A share carries the $1,457M covered-litigation reserve (the Discover settlement among it; $1,470M of
  litigation provision), about $874M after the year's 40% GAAP tax rate ("Visa’s GAAP effective tax rate was 40% for the twelve months
  ended September 30, 2008.") against $804M of net income, so reported EPS is under half the EPS without it (the AAPL FY2002 test, met by
  about $70M on the reserve alone). The company's adjusted $2.25 ("Adjusted full-year 2008 net income of $1.7 billion or $2.25 per diluted
  Class A common share") also removes asset step-up amortization, $68M a year ("Non-cash amortization and depreciation of the incremental
  basis in technology and building assets acquired in the reorganization."), which recurs, applies "a normalized tax rate of 41%" and
  counts the IPO shares as issued at October 1, 2007, so it is not a figure excluding only one-offs (the NKE FY2007, AVGO and PFE rule).
  FY2008 is excluded; as the first year it takes the history and the window with it (the ACN FY02 and JPM FY2002 rule), and until the
  Q4 FY09 print no year is left: the builder refuses each such date ("no fiscal year in the EPS history yet").
- **From 2009-10-29:** the Q4 FY09 print (2009-10-28) adds FY2009, GAAP $3.10, and the series runs to 2009-12-31.

Building either gap takes a new rule, which is the owner's call and a method note, not something this request decides: (a) FY2008 at the
company's $2.25 despite the recurring amortization in it (the SHW Valspar reading, which kept purchase-accounting amortization in a
company figure), which would also allow the 52 dates from 2008-10-31; or (b) an EPS anchor for the listing year. The sensitivity below
shows that (a) is the call that decides every built date.

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the reorganization proxy statement-prospectus (S-4/A No. 5,
2007-09-13: Visa U.S.A.'s selected data for fiscal 2002-2006 and its 2005-2006 balance sheets), the IPO prospectus (424B4, 2008-03-20:
Visa U.S.A.'s selected data for 2003-2007 and its audited fiscal 2005-2007 statements), the FY2008 and FY2009 10-Ks (Items 1, 1A, 5, 6, 7,
the statements of operations, balance sheets and cash flows, the EPS lines), the Q4 FY08 release (the fiscal 2008 GAAP and adjusted
figures and their reconciliation), the Q3 FY09 and Q4 FY09 releases (each release and its schedules; the Q4 FY09 presentation, exhibit
99.2, for gross revenues), the Q3 FY08 and Q3 FY09 10-Qs (receivables), the dividend 8-Ks of 2008-06-11 and 2009-10-21, and the other 8-Ks
of August to December 2009 by their items and exhibits (none guides a number; below). **Not read:** the FY2007 10-K and its two
amendments beyond their selected data (the 424B4 is later and reports the same years), the S-1 and its amendments, the releases and 10-Qs
of Q2 FY08 to Q2 FY09 (no built date uses them: the Q3 FY09 print is the previous quarter on every date), and the 8-Ks of 2007 to July
2009 other than the dividend and earnings ones. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows: each figure is
read from its own row by label and number (the script asserts the row exists exactly; the row is kept in the fact sheet), every growth
rate, share, margin, gap and rule-T value is computed, not typed, and every quoted sentence is asserted present in its own filing; the
127 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (127/127). Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time
(UTC, converted to ET); the source ids are `V1` and `V3`-`V11`. Decided on 2026-11-19, before any V model was built or any V outcome
computed:

- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's V series is the class A common stock, NYSE: V, from its 2008-03-19 listing (Yahoo's first point); Yahoo
  adjusts it for the four-for-one split of 2015-03-19, which the builder and `retro_tool` undo (`split_factor`), so the close is the price
  as traded: $77.28 on 2009-10-29, $87.46 on 2009-12-31.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The fiscal year ends on September 30 ("For the fiscal year ended September 30, 2008"): FY2009 is 2008-10-01 to
  2009-09-30.
- **Release timing.** Each earnings 8-K was accepted after the close (Q3 FY09 2009-07-29 16:29 ET, Q4 FY09 2009-10-27 16:13 ET; the call at
  5:00 p.m. ET) and is dated the next trading day, public before its open; the weekly date is the trading day after that (the MU
  encoding): 2009-10-29. The FY2009 10-K was accepted after the close (2009-11-20 16:07 ET) and is dated 2009-11-23. A Q4 print extends
  the history from its release to the 10-K: FY2009 from 2009-10-28 (4 dates).
- **Revenue: total operating revenues**, net of volume and support incentives (the income statement's own total), each year from the
  latest filing that reports it.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS of the class A common stock** (the two-class method; class B and C as converted), each year from the latest
  filing that reports it. FY2008 is excluded (above). FY2009 stays at GAAP $3.10: its gain on the sale of the VisaNet do Brasil stake ($237M
  after tax, Q3 FY09 release) is a fraction of the year's $2,353M net income (the mirror test is not met), and the company's adjusted $3.23
  ($2.92 excluding the sale) also removes the recurring step-up amortization. The history is FY2009 alone on every built date.
- **Current-FY EPS:** the FY2010 guide, "Annual diluted class A common stock earnings per share growth of greater than 20%.", is a
  one-sided bound and gives no field (the PEP, UNP and LOW rule), so FY09's $3.10 stands (the rollover rule).
- **Forward revenue growth: the fiscal year's range.** Visa guides no quarter, so method r2's fallback ("No next-quarter guide") takes
  the fiscal-year net revenue growth range: the Q4 FY09 release "affirms its financial outlook for the following metrics for 2010:", with
  "Annual net revenue growth at the lower end of the 11% to 15% range, given certain economic recovery assumptions; and". The 11-15% range
  stands and its words go in the note (the ACN words rule); BASE takes its 13% midpoint. "Annual operating margin in the mid 50% range;"
  is words and gives no margin step; the incentive, advertising, tax, capital expenditure and free cash flow outlooks have no input in
  method r2. The Q3 FY09 release's outlook ("high single digits in 2009 and at the lower end of the 11% to 15% range in 2010") is in the
  previous print only and reaches no input.
- **The bounds rule** (method r2, "A history too short to measure a rule"; the AVGO precedent): with FY2009 alone there is no EPS change,
  CAGR or two-year run, so BEAR is flat EPS (the 0% cap), BULL and XBULL take BASE's rate, the net buyback is 0 (one diluted share count,
  758M), the growth factor is 0 and the segment bridge's bull is flat.
- **The P/E window** runs from 2008-10-01, the first day of FY2009 (FY2008 and the days from the listing leave with it): 1.1 years on
  2009-10-29, 1.2 years at the end of 2009. Days of FY2010 keep FY09's $3.10 (no FY2010 EPS field).
- **Dividends,** the latest declared quarterly rate, each from the first filing that states it: $0.105 from the 8-K of 2008-06-11 (after
  the close; dated 2008-06-12), $0.125 from the 8-K of 2009-10-21 (before the open; "Increases Dividend Rate 19%"): $0.50 a year on every
  built date. The $1 billion repurchase plan of the Q4 FY09 release is a plan, not a guided number, and adds nothing.
- **Signals.** The GOOG set, with ACN's weights: revenue growth (0.20); the change in total operating revenues as a share of gross
  operating revenues (service, data processing, international transaction and other revenues before volume and support incentives; 0.20:
  the share of gross revenues kept after client incentives, which Visa calls "a form of price reduction", in the place of the gross
  margin); growth of operating expenses excluding the litigation provision line, less revenue growth (0.15, lower is better; the GOOG
  reading, whose opex sum leaves out the separate settlement lines); growth of accounts receivable less revenue growth (0.15, lower is
  better: no inventories, the GOOG and MSFT collection signal); and the operating-margin change (0.15; the litigation provisions in, as
  published), plus the theme slot at 2/4. Payments volume and processed transactions, the drivers Visa names, are shown in the revenue
  text, not scored: the prints give them for different periods (volume for the quarter before), and no weight was added to the six. Each
  value is the release's own against the year-ago quarter in the same release; receivables against the year-ago quarter's end from the
  release's September 30 column (Q4) or the year-ago 10-Q (Q3). The Q4 FY09 gross revenues ($2,205M against $2,008M) match the release's
  presentation.
- **Thresholds by rule T over the decade of the FY2008 10-K** (the vintage public on 2009-10-29; FY1999-FY2008, of which the filings report
  2002 on): Visa U.S.A., the accounting acquirer, for 2002-2007 and Visa Inc. for 2008, as published: nothing is made pro forma (the JPM
  rule), so the 2007-2008 change carries the October 2007 reorganization (Visa International and Visa Canada in from 2007-10-01, the
  first day of fiscal 2008). Each pair of years comes from the latest filing published by 2009-10-29 that reports both: the S-4/A for
  2002-2003 (and the incentives to 2004-2005, which no later filing reports), the 424B4 for 2003-2004 and for the 2005-2006 incentives and the
  2006-2007 receivables, the FY2008 10-K for the rest; receivables from the S-4/A for 2005-2006 (no filing gives an earlier pair). Six
  values, three for receivables. The raw figures and values are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives every value and
  threshold and refuses to build if they differ.

  | Signal | Annual values | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | revenue growth | 2003-2008: 26.60, 22.68, 9.72, 10.62, 21.78, 74.46 % | -3 / 10 / 22 / 74 % |
  | net-to-gross change | 98.6, -49.6, -33.5, -18.6, 429.7, -330.6 bp | -640 / -330 / -30 / 430 bp |
  | opex (ex litigation) growth less revenue | 1.82, -19.30, -3.70, -5.09, -13.08, -25.21 pp | 13 / 2 / -9 / -25 pp |
  | receivables growth less revenue | 2006-2008: -1.37, -8.55, -34.86 pp | 6 / -1 / -9 / -35 pp |
  | operating-margin change | -7711.5, 8931.9, -70.5, 776.4, -6512.5, 6003.3 bp | -15780 / -7710 / 350 / 8930 bp |

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2.** The 10-Ks tie results to spending ("The global payments industry depends heavily upon the overall level
  of consumer, business and government spending.", FY2008; "We depend heavily upon the overall level of consumer, business and government
  spending.", FY2009) and name competition ("we face substantial and intense competition worldwide") and, in the FY2009 10-K, the
  interchange hearings, but never call the business cyclical (the LOW, SHW and JPM reading). No theme in `taxonomy_eras.json` is live for
