- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the year's operating revenues by line, the incentives as a negative line, the total from
  the last year's revenues grown at the BASE revenue rate; the EPS check runs on the last year's pre-tax margin (FY2009's includes the
  VisaNet do Brasil gain) and tax rate.
- **Adds nothing:** the 8-Ks of 2009-08-31 (an agreement), 2009-09-14 (July and August payments volume and transactions ahead of a
  conference, no guided number), 2009-10-06 and the officer 8-K of 2009-10-21. None changes a guided number; the dividend 8-K is encoded
  above.
- **Anachronism list:** nothing added. A term check on the models takes its place: no later Visa product, acquisition or regulation name
  appears; the FY2009 10-K's words ("a leading global payments brand", its $558M operating cash flow) first appear on 2009-11-27, after
  its filing.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):
- **`retro_tool run` passes on all 10 dates,** with no warning. A first build failed it: the "why" named the CRYPTO theme's live date
  (2020), which the validator rejected; the clause was cut before any outcome existed, and a source description's "fiscal 2010 outlook"
  became "FY2010 outlook" to clear the year warning.
- **Controls:** altering one value of each print (the Q3 FY09 revenue, the Q4 FY09 quarter EPS and its full-year revenue), each vintage
  (the FY2008 10-K's free cash flow, the FY2009 10-K's FY09 EPS) and each dividend changes no model dated before its publication: the Q3
  FY09 print, the Q4 FY09 quarter and the $0.125 dividend change all 10 dates; the Q4 FY09 full-year figures and the FY2008 10-K live from
  2009-10-29 to 2009-11-20 (4 dates), the FY2009 10-K from 2009-11-27 (6); the $0.105 dividend is inert, superseded before any built date.
- **Leak scan:** 0 hits in 100 (model, later token) pairs: the source ids, titles, notes, quotes and figures (four significant digits or
  more) of every fact published after each model's date, after dropping 53 tokens an earlier fact or the engine already carries. As a
  positive control, 11 of the latest print's own tokens appear in each model. Each fact's own text was scanned for dates and years after its
  publication: the only hits are the outlooks' own years (2010, 2011), forecasts in the filings' words.
- **Regression:** the shared code is untouched (the firewall tool gains a V entry); rebuilding the 2008-2009 dates of GOOG and JPM, MU's
  2008 and AVGO's 2009 changes nothing.
- **Firewall** (run after the build was committed, before any outcome): passes at the 4 cutoffs above (the first built date, the FY2009
  10-K, the first date after it, and 2010-01-01), 0 files changed and no planted text (1, 4, 5 and 10 dates). The planted facts include
  a print with absurd values in every field and an absurd fiscal-year guide, absurd full-year actuals for the year after the latest
  vintage, a later Q4 print excluding its own year, a later vintage of the other kind that excludes a year and readmits FY2008, with
  planted texts, figures, listing and window start, a guide, a dividend, a listing, a company name, a split on the price data's next
  split date and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10. As a positive control the plants reach the first date after them: rebuilding
  2009-11-13 (cutoff 2009-10-30) and 2009-12-04 (cutoff 2009-11-23) with the plants stops at the builder's refusal of the planted guide
  ("no encoding for guides"), and with the guide, dividend, listing, split and name taken out, at its check of the planted print. A full
  rebuild is byte-identical.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **RICH on all 10 dates; legacy tier AVOID on all 10.** Robustness agrees on every date (every variant RICH).
- **The multiple is at the top of a crisis-year window.** $77.28-88.97 is 24.9-28.7x FY09's $3.10, the 96th-100th percentile of a 1.1-1.2
  year window (2008-10-01 on) whose median is 19.1-19.8x and whose calendar-year lows are 15.0x (2008-11-21) and 13.7x (2009-01-20): an EPP
  floor of 14x, $43.40, which the price is 78-105% above.
- **The scenarios are the guide's.** BASE is +13.0%/yr (the 11-15% range's midpoint, no margin step, no buyback), and with FY2009 alone
  BULL and XBULL take BASE's rate and BEAR is flat (the bounds rule): BEAR $49.91-50.84 (16.1-16.4x), BULL $86.72-89.50. From 2009-12-18 the
  price is at or above BULL (Ratio B `inf` on 2009-12-18, 12.6 and 18.0 on the last two dates).
- **The proxy composite** is 2.15 on every date: revenue (+9.9%, just under the 10% BASE band) and receivables (+19.9pp against revenue)
  at BEAR; net-to-gross (+10.6bp), the opex gap (-11.4pp) and the operating margin (+7,217bp against Q4 FY08's litigation-laden loss) at BULL.

How far each call moves the classes (the 10 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- **FY2008 in the history** (at the company's $2.25, the window from the 2008-03-19 listing): all 10 classes (7 RICH to CHEAP, 3 RICH to
  FAIR) and all 10 tiers (AVOID to BUY); at GAAP $0.96 (the AAPL test read as not met): all 10 classes (8 to CHEAP, 2 to FAIR) and all 10
  tiers (to BUY). The largest call by far: FY2008 brings an EPS run into BULL and XBULL and the listing year's higher multiples into the window;
- rule T on the pro forma 2007 for the 2007-2008 pair: no class, no tier (revenue's XBULL band falls from 74% to 27%);
- operating expenses with the litigation provision in: no class, no tier;
- every signal at its BEAR value, or at its XBULL value: no class, no tier;
- no FY2010 revenue range (Q4 FY09's +9.9% instead): no class, no tier;
- the EPS bound read as a point (+20%, FY10E $3.72): no class, 9 tiers (6 to ACCUMULATE, 2 to WATCHLIST, 1 to BUY).
The RICH calls rest on the exclusion of FY2008, which leaves a one-year history and a window that starts in the crisis.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- FY2008 excluded: the AAPL test met by about $70M on the reserve alone, at the year's GAAP tax rate (no filing states the reserve after
  tax), and the company's $2.25 read as not excluding only one-offs for its $68M of step-up amortization, its tax normalization and its
  share basis; it decides every built date and 52 unbuilt ones;
- the covered-litigation reserve read as a one-off (the company's own reading, funded by the escrow) although Visa recorded such provisions
  in fiscal 2003, 2007 and 2008;
- the signals, chosen in 2026 by a builder who knows the 2009 volume decline: the net-to-gross share in the place of the gross margin,
  the opex sum without the litigation line, and receivables; their extremes move no class here;
- rule T on Visa U.S.A. to 2007 and Visa Inc. in 2008, as published, with the reorganization in the 2007-2008 change (no class moves on
  the pro forma reading);
- the "at the lower end" words left in the note with the 11-15% range standing, and the EPS bound read as no field (tiers only);
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL (label only);
- the filings listed above as not read: a guide in an unread passage would be missed, though none could reach a built date but the
  FY2010 one, which is read.

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/V/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

on revenue, expenses, operating income and receivables (all twelve do: no 10-Q restatement), and each 10-K vintage matches its Q4 print on

(the year-ago lines, asserted word for word against their own files), the FY2022-FY2026 10-Ks (the statements of operations, cash flows
and balance sheets, the revenue note, Items 1, 1A and 5 by the sentences quoted, and a search of each for "cyclical" and for its crypto,

The fact sheet is extended by a fifth script (kept in the session scratchpad, like the four before it): each figure is read from its

releases), `V210`-`V224` (the 10-Qs); the dividend rates come from the Q4 releases, so no dividend 8-K is added. Decided on 2026-11-20,

  2025-11-06 16:09 (2025-11-07) and 2026-11-05 16:07 (2026-11-06). A Q4 print extends the history to its 10-K: 3, 3, 2, 1 and 1 dates.
  Each Q1 release came on a Thursday, so its print is dated the Friday, the week's last trading day, and that Friday is the week's date,
  public before its open (the Q1 FY21 encoding).

  AAPL test or its mirror. The litigation provisions stay in, as published: the releases' special items are mostly U.S. covered litigation
  (the interchange multidistrict litigation), on 13 of the 20 quarters ($129M to $1,000M; Q2 FY25 $1,000M, Q4 FY25 $903M).

  Full-Year 2024" table whose every cell is words ("High single-digit to low double-digit" net revenue growth on the GAAP nominal-dollar

  Q1 FY25 no release names an outlook. BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth on every date (the UNP rule), and no margin is guided.
- **No operating one-off** (the V 2018-2021 rule from fiscal 2020: the non-GAAP operating figures also remove recurring amortization): the

## SPGI (The McGraw-Hill Companies): the twenty-ninth ticker, in staging, 2008-2026

The SPGI series is built apart from the other twenty-eight and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/SPGI.json`), builder (`retro/build_spgi.py`, the CAT builder with segment revenue signals, EPS guides as ranges or as growth on
a stated base, a consolidated revenue range, segment guides as words and BKR's listed-symbol encoding) and engine
(`retro/templates/spgi_engine.py.tmpl`, the CAT engine with ratings, education and information signals and McGraw-Hill's own rule-T
thresholds). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an SPGI model. The live
`spgi_signal_model.py` (on other branches) and today's SPGI profile in `data/business_profiles.json` are 2026 analyses; neither was opened
for this series, and neither is an input. Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/SPGI/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and
their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009 ("same rules as before"); the code is the newest branch of the repository (its commit
"V retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for 2022-2026", 2026-11-20), every other recent retro branch being its ancestor.

```bash
python3 retro/build_spgi.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                  # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_spgi.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                  # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/SPGI/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series SPGI
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-01-25 2008-02-29 2008-04-30 2008-07-01 2008-07-30 2008-10-29 2009-01-01 2009-01-28 2009-02-27 \
         2009-04-29 2009-07-29 2009-10-27 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c SPGI; done
```

**The company and the series key.** In 2008-2009 the company is The McGraw-Hill Companies, Inc., listed on the NYSE as MHP ("The
McGraw-Hill Companies (NYSE: MHP)", every release). It became McGraw Hill Financial in 2013 and S&P Global in 2016. SPGI is only the
series key (TICKER, the folder, the index) and the symbol under which Yahoo serves the history; every printed line names MHP and the
company of the date (`LISTED_SYMBOL`, the BKR encoding).

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the FY2006, FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks (Items 1, 1A and 5; Exhibit 13:
the Eleven-Year Financial Review, the statements of income, balance sheets and cash flows, the earnings-per-share notes, the dividend
paragraphs and the MD&A outlook passages); the FY1999, FY2000 and FY2001 10-Ks (the earnings-per-share notes, for 1997-1999 diluted shares,
and their MD&A); the FY1997, FY1998 and FY2002-FY2005 annual reports, searched for EPS figures excluding one-offs; the Q4 2003-Q4 2006
releases (their headlines and one-off statements); the releases of Q1 2007 to Q3 2009 (each outlook; the statements of income and
segment tables of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009, the year-ago quarters as each release shows them); the 8-K of 2007-09-18 (the 2007 outlook in
words); the 10-Qs of Q3 2007 to Q3 2009 (their currency effects and outlook passages only); and every other 8-K of July 2007 to December
2009 by its items and exhibits. **Not read:** the 10-Qs beyond those passages, the proxy statements, and the FY2002-FY2005 10-Ks beyond
the searches above. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows: each figure is read from its own row by
label (the script asserts the row exists exactly and checks every identity a review or table carries: segments sum to revenue and to
operating profit, operating profit, corporate expense and interest to pre-tax income, each Q4 release's year to the 10-K that follows),
every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is computed, not typed, and every quoted sentence is asserted present in its own filing; the
237 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (237/237). Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time
(converted from UTC; before 2003 EDGAR gives the filing date only); the source ids are `SP1`-`SP17`. Decided on 2026-11-20, before any
SPGI model was built or any SPGI outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's SPGI series is MHP's history, adjusted for the 2-for-1 splits of 1996, 1999-03-09 and 2005-05-18 and for a
  1057:1000 factor dated 2026-07-01, Yahoo's booking of the Mobility Global distribution ("each of the stockholders of S&P Global received
  one share of Mobility Global common stock for every share", 8-K of 2026-07-02). That is a distribution, not a split (the MAR, PFE and
  CMCSA rule), but it follows every built date, so Yahoo's close times 1.057 is the price as traded: $40.81 on 2008-01-04, $23.19 on
  2008-12-31 and $33.51 on 2009-12-31. The builder refuses any date on or after 2026-07-01 until the distribution is encoded. The 2005
  split is a `splits` record ("All per share amounts have been restated to reflect the Company’s two-for-one stock split, completed on May
  17, 2005.", FY2006 10-K; Yahoo's date 2005-05-18): the 1997-1999 diluted share counts, published before it, are doubled by the builder;
  every EPS figure used is from a later filing. The 1999 split precedes every per-share fact.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year. The three dates of January 2008 before the Q4 2007 print have FY2007 as the current year.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 was accepted before the open (06:59-07:58 ET; the conference call at 8:30
  a.m. ET), on a Tuesday, Thursday or Monday, so each week is dated the next trading day: 2008-01-25, 2008-04-30, 2008-07-30, 2008-10-29,
  2009-01-28, 2009-04-29, 2009-07-29 and 2009-10-27. The FY2006 10-K (2007-02-28 14:02 ET) and the FY2008 10-K (2009-02-27 10:50 ET) were
  accepted during the session, the FY2007 10-K (2008-02-29 06:09 ET) before the open; each keeps its date. A Q4 print extends the history
  from its release to the 10-K: FY2007 from 2008-01-24 (5 dates), FY2008 from 2009-01-27 (4 dates).
- **History: the Eleven-Year Financial Review of each 10-K.** Each review reports revenue and operating profit by segment, pre-tax income
  and diluted EPS for eleven years on one basis (restated for the 2005 split, the 2004 shipping-and-handling reclassification and the 2003
  discontinued operations, S&P ComStock and the juvenile retail publishing business), so each vintage takes its ten years from its own 10-K:
  1997-2006 (FY2006), 1998-2007 (FY2007), 1999-2008 (FY2008). The three reviews agree on every year they share. Diluted shares of the first
  year come from the latest earnings-per-share note that reports it (1997's 199,504K from the FY1999 10-K, 1998's 199,104K from the FY2000
  10-K, 1999's 198,557K from the FY2001 10-K, each doubled for the 2005 split), the last year's from its own 10-K (366,878K, 344,785K,
  318,687K): a net buyback of 0.9%/yr over 1997-2006, 1.6% over 1998-2007 and 2.5% over 1999-2008.
- **EPS: diluted EPS from continuing operations before the extraordinary item and the cumulative adjustment, as reported.** No filing
  publishes a figure excluding only one-offs on that basis: the releases list each one-off's per-share effect ("Including the $0.08
  restructuring charge in the fourth quarter of 2007, diluted earnings per share for the period were $0.43 compared to $0.56 in 2006,
  which included a $0.03 restructuring charge.") without a figure excluding it, and nothing is derived (the XOM 1997 rule); the FY1998 and
  FY1999 10-Ks' figures "Excluding the extraordinary loss and other one-time items" ($1.68 for 1998, $2.02 for 1999, before the 2005
  split) predate the 2003 discontinued-operations restatement, an earlier basis, so they do not replace the review's (the UNP trucking and
  PEP rule). **No year is excluded:** no year's listed one-offs come near its income (2001's $159.0M restructuring charge and $22.8M of
  losses against $616.1M of pre-tax income; 2003's $131.3M real-estate gain against $1,130.3M). So 2001's $0.96 carries its restructuring,
  2003's $1.79 its gain, 2007's $2.94 and 2008's $2.51 their restructuring charges.
- **Current-FY EPS: the fiscal-year guide.** McGraw-Hill guides the year, never a quarter's revenue (Q3 2008's "earnings per share of $0.40
  to $0.42 in the fourth quarter" is a quarter's EPS, with no input in method r2, in the note):
  - FY2007 is guided in words only ("double-digit earnings growth in 2007", from the Q4 2006 release to the 8-K of 2007-09-18 and "We are
    still on course to produce double-digit earnings per share growth in 2007", Q3 2007): a one-sided bound gives no field (the PEP, UNP and
    LOW rule), so FY06's $2.40 stands on the three January dates (the rollover rule);
  - FY2008, growth on its stated base from the Q4 2007 release: "earnings per share increasing by 3% to 5% in 2008", and "Guidance for 2008
    excludes: $0.08 restructuring charge in the fourth quarter of 2007, and $0.03 gain from the divestiture of a mutual fund data business
    in 2007." The guide's base is FY07's $2.94 without those two items, $2.99, read from the release's own per-share figures (the CAT
    `eps_growth_base` rule, whose Q3 2007 base was the midpoint of a range): FY08E $3.11 from 2008-01-25;
  - FY2008, ranges from Q1 2008: $2.65-2.75 ("If current trends in financial markets continue for the balance of the year, we would expect
    earnings per share in the $2.65 to $2.75 range for 2008", a conditional range in numbers, read as the guide), the same range
    "Excluding second quarter restructuring charges and related benefits" (Q2 2008) and $2.63-2.65 excluding the restructuring charges
    (Q3 2008): $2.70 from 2008-04-30 and $2.64 from 2008-10-29 (the ACN rule for a guide that excludes an announced item);
  - FY2009: $2.20-2.30 (Q4 2008, maintained in Q1 2009) and $2.20-2.25 excluding the second quarter restructuring charge and the Vista

  percentile 18.6x falling to 13.9x); MHP trades at 16.1-17.8x FY06's $2.40 in January 2008, 11.4-16.7x the FY08 guide from the Q4 2007

  guide from April: the 0th to 16th percentile of its own range on every date.

  $0.96; 14.7x in 2003), so the EPP floor is 18x the standing EPS through 2008-12-26 ($43.20 on FY06's $2.40,

  then -2.0%, -3.5% and -4.5% as the guide is cut. The BASE scenario prints as "EPS +-4.5%/yr" when BASE is negative (the CAT display

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows that structured-finance ratings collapsed in 2007-2009: Financial Services and Education revenue (the two largest segments), revenue, diluted EPS and the segment margin, all as reported
  (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; 7 classes move at BEAR);
- the EPS history at GAAP with every one-off in, because no figure excluding only one-offs exists on the same basis: 2001's restructuring
  sets BEAR and XBULL and lifts the EPP floor to 17-18x; no class moves on any encoding tried, but no excluding figure could be tried;
- the FY2008 growth guide read on $2.99, a base the company states by its two items but never prints (no class);
- the Q1 2008 range read as a guide despite its condition (no class);
- the segment revenue guides read as components, so BASE takes the reported quarter in 2008, and reported rather than currency-neutral
  growth (no class either way);
- quarter values as reported, the releases' "as adjusted" segment profit in the notes only (no class);
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL, and no theme for the rating-agency regulation the 10-Ks name (label only);
- the filings listed above as not read: a guide in an unread passage would be missed, though every release and 10-K outlook was read.

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/SPGI/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

### SPGI 2010-2013: four vintages, the company's figures excluding one-offs, Broadcasting and McGraw-Hill Education discontinued, McGraw Hill Financial

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31, on the same method, builder, engine and rule-T thresholds. The owner asked for 2010-2013
("same rules"). Built on 2026-11-20 in the same session that had scored the 2008-2009 dates and written their `FINDINGS.md`, so those
outcomes were known when this batch was read. No decision below uses them: each applies a rule that existed before (the r2 rollover and
decade rules, the ACN and PEP rule for a company figure excluding only one-offs on the same basis, the CAT and PFE `restates` field, the
LMT and SO seam rule, the ACN words rule, the BKR listed-symbol and rename encodings, the BKR `bkr3` None-tolerant engine, the AAPL 10-K/A
rule) or a 2008-2009 encoding (the latest quarter's growth as reported for BASE, quarter values as reported, DURABLE). The readings that
could still carry hindsight are listed at the end with how far the other reading moves.

```bash
python3 retro/build_spgi.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                  # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for c in 2010-01-27 2010-02-25 2010-04-28 2010-07-23 2010-10-27 2011-02-02 2011-02-24 2011-04-27 2011-07-29 2011-10-21 2012-02-01 \
         2012-02-08 2012-04-25 2012-07-27 2012-11-02 2013-02-13 2013-03-01 2013-03-21 2013-05-01 2013-05-07 2013-05-15 2013-07-26 \
         2013-09-11 2013-10-23 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c SPGI; done
```

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the 16 earnings releases of Q4 2009 to Q3 2013 (ex.99: the
narrative and outlook, the statements of income, the segment tables, the tables of adjusted information); the FY2009 and FY2010 10-Ks
with their Exhibit 13 (Items 1, 1A and 5; the Eleven-Year and Five-Year Financial Reviews, the statements, the earnings-per-share and
segment notes, the dividend paragraphs); the FY2011 and FY2012 10-Ks (the same items, and Item 6) and the FY2012 10-K/A of 2013-03-20 (its
explanatory note and Item 6); the FY2002-FY2005 10-Ks' earnings-per-share notes (the first year's diluted shares of each vintage); and
every other 8-K of January 2010 to December 2013 by its items and exhibits. **Not read:** the 10-Qs and the proxy statements. The source
ids are `SP18`-`SP44`. 540 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (540/540, the 2008-2009 batch's 237
included). The fact sheet only gains facts: its 2008-2009 entries are unchanged (the generator asserts it). Decided on 2026-11-20,
before any 2010-2013 model was built or any 2010-2013 outcome computed:

  during the session, the FY2012 10-K (2013-02-28 06:03 ET) before the open; each keeps its date. A Q4 print extends the history from its
  release to the 10-K.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it.** The FY2009 10-K's Eleven-Year Financial Review gives 2000-2009 on one basis
  (it agrees with the FY2006-FY2008 reviews on every shared year). The FY2010 10-K's review covers five years (2006-2010), so 2001-2005
  come from the FY2009 review. The FY2011 10-K's selected data gives revenue for 2007-2011 without the Broadcasting Group (discontinued

### SPGI 2014-2017: McGraw Hill Construction discontinued and recast, the legal settlements at the company's figure, GAAP from 2016 (amortization recurs), a flat FY2017 revenue guide, S&P Global and NYSE: SPGI

208 weekly dates, 2014-01-10 to 2017-12-29, on the same method, builder, engines and rule-T thresholds. The owner asked for 2014-2017
("same rules as before"); the code is the newest branch of the repository (its commit "SPGI retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings
for 2010-2013", 2026-11-20), every other recent retro branch being its ancestor. Built in a new session: the 2008-2013 outcomes,
`SERIES.md` and `FINDINGS.md` were not opened before this batch was built, checked and committed. Each decision below applies a rule
that existed before (the r2 rollover, decade and words rules, the ACN and PEP company-figure rule, the CMCSA, PFE and AVGO reading of
amortization, the MSFT and CAT recast rule, the ACN and MSFT segment-recast rule, the RCL and LOW "flat is 0" rule, the CAT year-ago-loss
rule, the LMT and SO seam rule, the BKR listed-symbol and rename encodings) or a 2008-2013 SPGI encoding. The readings that could still
carry hindsight are listed at the end with how far the other reading moves.

```bash
python3 retro/build_spgi.py --weekly 2014-01-06 2017-12-31                  # 208 dates, 2014-01-10 .. 2017-12-29
for c in 2014-02-05 2014-02-08 2014-04-30 2014-07-30 2014-10-30 2014-11-07 2015-02-13 2015-02-14 2015-04-29 2015-07-28 2015-11-04 \
         2016-02-05 2016-02-13 2016-04-27 2016-05-03 2016-07-01 2016-07-29 2016-11-04 2017-02-08 2017-02-10 2017-04-26 2017-07-28 \
         2017-10-27 2018-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c SPGI; done
```

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the 16 earnings releases of Q4 2013 to Q3 2017 (ex.99: the
headlines and narrative, the outlook, return of capital and dividend paragraphs, the statements of income, the segment tables and the
reconciliations of adjusted information); the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks (Item 1's overview, Item 1A, Item 6, the statements of income, balance
sheets and cash flows, the segment notes and the dividend sentences, each searched for "cyclical"); the recast 8-K of 2014-11-05 (its
exhibit in full); the name-change 8-K of 2016-04-29; the S-3 of 2016-06-29 (its listing sentence); the FY2005 10-K's earnings-per-share
note (2004 and 2005 diluted shares); and every other 8-K of January 2014 to December 2017 by its items and exhibits. **Not read:** the
10-Qs, the proxy statements, the Investor Day presentations of 2014-03-18 beyond its press release, SNL Financial's own statements (the
8-K/A of 2015-10-29) and the 10-Ks beyond the passages above. The source ids are `SP45`-`SP68`. The fact sheet is generated by a script
from the filings' converted rows (each figure read from its own row by label, every rate computed, every identity the builder checks
re-derived); 560 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (560/560). The fact sheet only gains facts: its
2008-2013 entries are unchanged (the generator asserts it; the diff is 2,112 added lines and none removed). Decided on 2026-11-20, before
any 2014-2017 model was built or any 2014-2017 outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (07:10-07:37 ET; the call at 8:30 a.m., at 9:00 a.m. for Q2 2015),
  so each week is dated the next trading day: 2014-02-05, 2014-04-30, 2014-07-30, 2014-10-30, 2015-02-13, 2015-04-29, 2015-07-28,
  2015-11-04, 2016-02-05, 2016-04-27, 2016-07-29, 2016-11-04, 2017-02-08, 2017-04-26, 2017-07-28 and 2017-10-27. The FY2013 10-K
  (2014-02-07 09:09 ET) and the FY2016 10-K (2017-02-09 08:45 ET) were accepted before the open and the FY2014 10-K (2015-02-13 14:34 ET)
  during the session; each keeps its date. The FY2015 10-K (2016-02-11 18:16 ET), the recast 8-K (2014-11-05 16:11 ET), the name-change
  8-K (2016-04-29 16:54 ET) and the S-3 (2016-06-29 16:18 ET) were accepted after the close and count from the next trading day:
  2016-02-12, 2014-11-06, 2016-05-02 and 2016-06-30. A Q4 print extends the history from its release to the 10-K.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it** (the 2010-2013 rule). The FY2013 10-K's selected data gives 2009-2013 on
  the FY2012 10-K/A's basis (they agree on 2009-2012). **The 8-K of 2014-11-05 is a vintage of its own** (the MSFT and CAT recast rule):
  it recasts FY2013 without McGraw Hill Construction (discontinued from the Q3 2014 release, sold in November 2014): revenue $4,702M,
  segment operating profit $1,693M, pre-tax income $1,299M and diluted EPS $2.80, "Performance" $3.22; every other year, the segments,
  cash and the 10-K's words stay the FY2013 10-K's (an 8-K has no segment table or Item 1A). The FY2014, FY2015 and FY2016 10-Ks give
  2010-2014, 2011-2015 and 2012-2016 without Construction; earlier years keep the latest filing that reports them. **Seams stay as
  published** (the LMT and SO rules): 2007 with McGraw-Hill Education beside 2008 without it on every date (it sets BEAR, -39.1%/yr, on
  all 208), 2012 with Construction beside 2013 without it in the recast vintage, and 2009 with it beside 2010 without it from the FY2014
  10-K. Diluted shares of the first year: 2004's 385,824K and 2005's 382,570K from the FY2005 10-K (`SP47`, a second citation of `SP21`'s
  document so that `SP21`'s own text is unchanged), 2006's 366,878K (FY2006 10-K) and 2007's 344,785K (FY2007 10-K); the last year's from
  its own 10-K (279.8M, 271.5M, 274.6M, 265.2M; FY2014's 271.5M is the reported diluted count of a loss year, equal to the basic count).
- **EPS: the company's figure excluding only one-offs where a release on the same basis publishes it, else diluted EPS from continuing
  operations as reported** (the 2010-2013 rule, unchanged). FY2013 $3.33 (Q4 2013 release; GAAP $2.90), $3.22 without Construction from
  the recast (GAAP $2.80); FY2014 **$3.88** (Q4 2014 release: "Excluding the impact of charges related to legal and regulatory settlements

  prints them without Construction and one-offs). **From 2016 the company's adjusted figures also remove deal-related amortization**

  Amortization recurs, so they are not figures excluding only one-offs (the CMCSA, PFE and AVGO reading; SHW's adjusted-EPS rule is SHW's
  own): **FY2016 enters at GAAP $7.94** (the Q4 2016 release's $5.35 also removes $0.23 of amortization; no figure without only the
  one-offs is printed, and none is derived from the reconciliation's per-share columns: the 2009 rule). The year is kept: its listed

  does not exclude it. FY2015 keeps $4.53 (the Q4 2016 release's $4.69 also removes amortization). No year is excluded.

  2014), $3.80-3.90 (Q2) and $3.78-3.83 from continuing operations without Construction (Q3); FY2015 $4.35-4.45 (Q4 2014 to Q2 2015) and

- **The floor** (the median of the calendar-year P/E lows, rounded down) is 15x to 2015-02-06, 18x to 2016-01-29, 17x to 2017-02-03 (16x
  on the two year-end dates, 2015-12-31 and 2016-12-30) and 14x from 2017-02-08, when FY2016's GAAP $7.94 lowers 2016's P/E lows: an EPP
  of $49-88. The price is above it on every date, from 3.3% (2016-01-15) to 95.7% (2017-10-13).
- **BEAR is the 2007-2008 seam on every date** (-39.1%/yr: 2007's $2.94 with Education to 2008's $1.79 without it; the BEAR price $19-32).
  **BULL** is the decade CAGR where it exceeds BASE (+6.4% and +6.1%/yr, 2014-02-05 to 2014-04-25) and BASE's rate otherwise until the
  Q4 2016 print, then the decade CAGR onto GAAP 2016's $7.94: +12.7%/yr (2006-2016, 2017-02-08) and +11.7% (2007-2016, from the FY2016
  10-K). **XBULL** is 2010-2012's +21.6% (January 2014), 2011-2013's +26.2% (+24.1% on the recast's $3.22), 2012-2014's +30.2% from the
  FY2014 10-K (the step from GAAP 2012's $2.29 to the company's 2014 $3.88) and 2014-2016's +43.1% from 2017-02-08.
- **BASE follows the quarters:** +10.4%/yr on Q3 2013 to 2014-01-31, +5.2% to +13.7% on the 2014-2016 quarters (the lowest on Q4 2013's
  +2.0% revenue, the highest on Q2 2016's +10.4%), and +3.0% through 2017 on the 0% revenue guide.
- **The proxy composite** is 1.65-2.80. The FAIR dates of January and February 2016 are the market's fall to 18.6-19.7x (the 26th-39th
  percentile), 3-16% above the floor.

How far each call moves the classes (the 208 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- the history and the P/E window from 2008, so no 2007-2008 Education seam (BEAR from the later years): 34 classes (23 RICH to FAIR, 4
  RICH to CHEAP, 7 FAIR to CHEAP; 2014-04-30 to 2017-04-26) and 89 tiers, the batch's largest call;
- the amortization-excluding company figures from 2016 (the SHW reading: FY2016 $5.35, FY2015 $4.69 from the Q4 2016 release, the FY2016
  and FY2017 adjusted ranges as the guide): 10 classes (6 RICH to FAIR, 4 FAIR to CHEAP, 2016-02-05 to 2016-04-08) and 8 tiers;
- FY2016 at $5.12, GAAP less its listed one-offs (a figure the 2009 rule bars): no class, no tier;
- the recast 8-K unused (FY2013 at $3.33 with Construction until the FY2014 10-K): no class, no tier;
- FY2017's "unchanged" read as words (BASE on the latest quarter), or the Q1 2017 "low single-digit growth" as 1-3%: no class, no tier;
- every revenue word read as a number (mid single-digit 4-6%, mid-to-high 5-8%, low single-digit 1-3%): no class, no tier;
- the one-off quarters' EPS and margin signals at BASE (Q4 2014, Q4 2015, Q3 2016, Q4 2016, Q3 2017): 1 class (2016-02-26, FAIR to RICH),
  no tier;
- the Financial Services signal at BASE from the Q4 2016 print (the old scope not rebuilt from Market Intelligence's row): no class, no
  tier;
- every signal at its BEAR value: 7 classes (the FAIR dates to RICH) and 6 tiers; at its XBULL value: 78 classes (66 RICH to FAIR, 5 RICH
  to CHEAP, 7 FAIR to CHEAP; 2014-02-05 to 2016-06-24) and 56 tiers;
- CYCLICAL instead of DURABLE: no class, no tier (label only).
The RICH calls rest on the multiple in the upper part of its own decade against a BASE of the reported quarters (2014-2016) or the flat
revenue guide (2017), with BEAR at the seam; no single encoding call above but the seam moves more than 10 classes.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the 2007-2008 seam as published, which sets BEAR at -39.1%/yr on every date and keeps 2004-2007 with Education in the P/E window (34
  classes and 89 tiers if the history starts at 2008);
- GAAP from 2016 because the company's adjusted figures remove recurring amortization, so FY2016 is $7.94 with the J.D. Power and SPSE/CMA
  gains and FY15's $4.53 stands through 2016 (10 classes on the SHW reading), and the mix of GAAP 2010-2012 with the company's 2013-2015
  figures, which lifts XBULL;
- FY2017's "unchanged" as 0% and its later words as words (no class either way);
- the Financial Services line rebuilt from Market Intelligence's row inside Market and Commodities Intelligence, divestitures and SNL
  included as reported (no class if it scores BASE);
- the quarters as reported through the settlements, gains and their lapping (1 class at BASE);
- the signals and rule T as in 2008-2013, chosen by a builder who knows how 2008-2017 went (7 classes at BEAR, 78 at XBULL);
- the recast 8-K as a vintage (no class), NYSE: SPGI from the S-3 rather than the insiders' Forms 4 (display only);
- DURABLE, and the live themes read as out of scope (label only);
- the filings listed above as not read: a guide in an unread passage would be missed, though every release outlook and every 8-K's items
  were read.

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/SPGI/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

### SPGI 2018-2021: GAAP every year, the GAAP ranges as the guides, a guided margin step in 2018, four segments, no FY2021 GAAP guide until October, the seam leaves BEAR

209 weekly dates, 2018-01-05 to 2021-12-31, on the same method, builder, engines and rule-T thresholds. The owner asked for 2018-2021
("same rules as before"); the code is the newest branch of the repository (its commit "SPGI retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings
for 2014-2017", 2026-11-20). **This batch was decided in the session that had scored 2014-2017 and written its findings** (and had read
the 2008-2013 findings while writing them), so those outcomes were known when it was read. No decision below uses them: each applies a
rule that existed before (the 2014-2017 SPGI amortization, words, "flat is 0", recast and Financial Services encodings, method r2's guided
margin step, the ACN restated-base and words rules, the WMT latest-field rule) or applies the rollover rule; the readings that could still
carry hindsight are listed at the end with how far the other reading moves.

```bash
python3 retro/build_spgi.py --weekly 2018-01-01 2021-12-31                  # 209 dates, 2018-01-05 .. 2021-12-31
for c in 2018-02-07 2018-02-13 2018-03-08 2018-04-27 2018-05-25 2018-07-27 2018-10-26 2019-02-08 2019-02-14 2019-05-03 2019-08-02 \
         2019-10-30 2020-02-07 2020-02-12 2020-04-29 2020-07-29 2020-10-28 2021-02-10 2021-02-11 2021-04-30 2021-07-30 2021-10-27 \
         2022-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c SPGI; done
```

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the 16 earnings releases of Q4 2017 to Q3 2021 (ex.99: the
headlines and narrative, the outlook, return of capital and dividend paragraphs, the statements of income, the segment tables and the
reconciliations); the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks (Item 1's overview, Item 1A, Item 6, the statements, the segment notes and the dividend
sentences, each searched for "cyclical", "crypto", "blockchain", "digital asset" and "energy transition": none is present); the Kensho
8-K of 2018-03-06 and the Investor Day 8-K of 2018-05-24 (their exhibits); the segment-allocation recast 8-K of 2020-03-26; and every
other 8-K of January 2018 to January 2022 by its items and exhibits. **Not read:** the 10-Qs, the proxy statements, the S-4 and the IHS
Markit filings, the earnings slides (not filed) and the 10-Ks beyond the passages above. The source ids are `SP69`-`SP90`. 591 strings
were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (591/591). The fact sheet only gains facts (2,061 lines added, none
removed). Decided on 2026-11-20, before any 2018-2021 model was built or any 2018-2021 outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (07:11-07:51 ET; the call at 8:30 a.m.), so each week is dated the
  next trading day: 2018-02-07, 2018-04-27, 2018-07-27, 2018-10-26, 2019-02-08, 2019-05-03, 2019-08-02, 2019-10-30, 2020-02-07,
  2020-04-29, 2020-07-29, 2020-10-28, 2021-02-10, 2021-04-30, 2021-07-30 and 2021-10-27. All four 10-Ks were accepted after the close
  (2018-02-09 16:40, 2019-02-12 18:15, 2020-02-10 17:30 and 2021-02-09 17:08 ET) and count from the next trading day: 2018-02-12,
  2019-02-13, 2020-02-11 and 2021-02-10. The Kensho 8-K (2018-03-06 17:52 ET) counts from 2018-03-07; the Investor Day 8-K (2018-05-24
  08:17 ET) was before the open.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it.** The FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks' selected data agree on every shared year (no
  restatement of revenue or EPS); earlier years keep the latest filing that reports them. 2007 leaves the decade with the FY2017 10-K, so
  **the 2007-2008 Education seam leaves BEAR from 2018-02-12** (the Q4 2017 print's eleven-year history keeps it on 2018-02-07); the
  2009-2010 Construction seam stays as published until 2009 leaves with the FY2019 10-K. Diluted shares of the first year from its own
  10-K (2008's 318,687K, 2009's 313,296K, 2010's 312,220K, 2011's 304,000K), the last year's from its own 10-K.
- **EPS: GAAP every year** (the 2016 rule, unchanged: the company's adjusted figures also remove deal-related amortization, which recurs):
  FY2017 $5.78 (the $149 million Tax Act charge in; its listed one-offs are far under its income, so it is kept), FY2018 $7.73, FY2019
  $8.60 and FY2020 $9.66; 2013-2015 keep the company's figures excluding only one-offs ($3.22, $3.88, $4.53). So BEAR is 2016-2017's
  -27.2%/yr (GAAP 2016's $7.94 with the divestiture gains against 2017's $5.78) from 2018-02-12 on every date, and XBULL 2014-2016's
  +43.1%/yr throughout.

  EPS guidance by approximately twenty cents"; Q1 2018), $7.75-7.90 (the Investor Day 8-K, after "its final significant financial crisis
  litigation"; Q2 2018) and $7.77-7.87 (Q3 2018); FY2019 $8.50-8.70, $8.16-8.36 (the pension charge), $8.20-8.35 and $8.56-8.66; FY2020
  $10.00-10.20, $9.50-9.70 (the baseline COVID-19 scenario, whose alternatives are on unfiled slides), $10.25-10.45 and $10.00-10.15.
  **FY2021: no GAAP guide until the Q3 2021 release** ("The Company is not providing 2021 GAAP guidance because given the inherent

  2021-02-10 to 2021-10-22** (the rollover rule, the 2016 encoding); $12.50-12.65 from 2021-10-27. The adjusted ranges are in the guide line.
- **A guided margin step, once.** The Investor Day 8-K guides the FY2018 GAAP operating margin: "updated from 45% - 46% to a range of 44% -
  45%" (the 45-46% is in no filing). A consolidated margin guide in numbers is method r2's guided margin step (the 2008-2017 SPGI margin

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2**, on each 10-K's own words (no 10-K calls anything cyclical). The themes live on these dates are scoped to

## CB (ACE Limited, then Chubb Limited): the thirtieth ticker, in staging, 2008-2026

The CB series is built apart from the other twenty-nine and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/CB.json`), builder (`retro/build_cb.py`, the JPM builder with an insurer's fields, a fiscal-year EPS range as a guide and BKR's
listed-symbol encoding) and engine (`retro/templates/cb_engine.py.tmpl`, the JPM engine with a property and casualty insurer's signals and
ACE's own rule-T thresholds). It is the first insurer in the retrospectives. The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding
of another ticker enters a CB model. Today's CB profile in `data/business_profiles.json` (Chubb Limited) is a 2026 analysis; it was not
opened for this series and is not an input (only `retro_tool outcome` reads it, for the hindsight `profile_drift` label). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/CB/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for
2008-2009 ("same rules as before"); the code is the newest branch of the repository (its commit "SPGI retrospective: hindsight outcomes and
findings for 2022-2026", 2026-11-20), every other recent retro branch being its ancestor.

```bash
python3 retro/build_cb.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                    # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_cb.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                    # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/CB/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series CB
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-02-06 2008-02-29 2008-04-30 2008-07-14 2008-07-30 2008-10-29 2008-11-10 2009-02-04 2009-02-27 2009-04-29 \
         2009-07-28 2009-07-29 2009-10-28 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CB; done
```

Two ranges, as for JPM and SPGI: the series has 2008-12-31 and no 2009-01-02.

**The company and the series key.** In 2008-2009 the company is ACE Limited, listed on the NYSE as ACE ("ACE Limited (NYSE: ACE)", every
release; CIK 896159), a Cayman Islands company with its headquarters in Bermuda that continued into Switzerland on 2008-07-18. It acquired
The Chubb Corporation and took the name Chubb Limited in 2016; CB is only the series key (TICKER, the folder, the index) and the symbol under
which Yahoo serves ACE's history, and every printed line names ACE and the company of the date (`LISTED_SYMBOL`, the BKR and SPGI encoding).
Yahoo's CB series is ACE's: its first trade is 1993-03-25 (ACE's listing), its one split is ACE's 3-for-1 of 1998-03-03, and its 2007-2008
dividends are ACE's ($0.27 and $0.29 a quarter). **The CB of 2008-2009 is not this company:** The Chubb Corporation (CIK 20171) traded as CB
on those dates. It is a different company, whose history Yahoo does not serve under CB; a retrospective of it would need its own fact sheet,
builder and a price source other than Yahoo, the owner's call (the KMI precedent for KMP). Checked before any price or outcome of the period
was read (Yahoo was asked for its series metadata and its 2006-2008 dividends only).

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the FY2006, FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks (Item 1's segment premium table
and opening, Item 1A searched for the cycle and catastrophe risk factors, Item 5's dividends, Item 6, the statements of operations); the
selected financial data of the FY2000-FY2005 10-Ks and the FY2004 10-K/A (2005-08-12, the restatement of 2000-2004), with the FY2002 and

supplement's previous quarter); the Q4 2003 to Q4 2005 releases (their figures excluding realized gains, catastrophe losses and the A&E
charge, for the 2005 one-off test and the operating-EPS test below); the 10-Qs of Q1 2007 to Q3 2009 (their statements of operations, compared

2009-05-05, 2009-06-09 and 2009-08-17 say were posted on the website (not filed). The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings'
converted rows: each figure is read from its own row by label (the script asserts the row exists and checks every identity a table carries:
total revenues and pre-tax income against each 10-K's statement of operations, the segments against net premiums earned, each Q4 release's

converted to ET; before 2003 EDGAR gives the filing date only); the source ids are `CB1`-`CB26`. Decided on 2026-11-21, before any CB
model was built or any CB outcome computed:

- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's split of 1998-03-03 precedes the P/E window (2003-01-01 on), so the close is the price as traded: $60.74 on
  2008-01-04, $52.92 on 2008-12-31 and $50.40 on 2009-12-31. NYSE: ACE throughout (the Continuation kept the listing and the symbol).
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year from 1999. "On July 2, 1999, the Company changed its fiscal year end from September 30 to December
  31." (FY2000 10-K): fiscal 1996-1998 ended September 30, and the three-month transition period to December 31, 1998 is not a fiscal year
  (the BKR rule), which only rule T's 1997-1999 changes reach. The five dates before the Q4 2007 print (2008-01-04 to 2008-02-01) have FY2007
  as the current year.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q4 2006 to Q3 2009 was accepted after the close (16:09-21:47 ET; the call, where the release
  states it, at 8:30 a.m. the next morning) and is dated the next trading day, public before its open; each week's date is the trading day after that: 2008-02-07, 2008-05-01,
  2008-07-31, 2008-10-30, 2009-02-05, 2009-04-30, 2009-07-29 and 2009-10-29. The FY2006 and FY2007 10-Ks were accepted after the close
  (2007-02-28 21:19, 2008-02-28 20:21 ET) and are dated 2007-03-01 and 2008-02-29; the FY2008 10-K during the session (2009-02-27 14:43 ET).
  A Q4 print extends the history from its release to the 10-K: FY2007 from 2008-02-06 (3 dates), FY2008 from 2009-02-04 (3 dates).
- **Revenue: total revenues as the statement of operations adds them**, net premiums earned, net investment income and net realized gains
  (losses), as reported (the JPM rule: the income statement's own total), each year from the latest filing that reports it; the 10-Ks'
  "Total revenues" rows agree with the sum on every year they print. Realized losses are in, so 2008's revenue falls 3.7% while net premiums
  earned rise 7.4%; Combined Insurance (from 2008-04-01) is in as published. Nothing is made pro forma.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS before the cumulative effect of a change in accounting principle**, each year from the latest filing that reports it
  (the FY2006 10-K for 2002-2006, then the FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks; FY2006 is $6.90 before its $0.01 cumulative effect):
  - **The company's operating figure is not used.** Its "income excluding net realized gains (losses)" is "a common performance measurement
    for insurance companies", but it removes realized investment and derivative gains and losses, which recur ("We exclude net realized gains
    (losses) ... because the amount of these gains (losses) is heavily influenced by, and fluctuates in part according to, the availability of
    market opportunities.", every release): it is not a figure excluding only one-offs (the NKE FY2007, AVGO, PFE and V rule), and it is
    shown in each print's EPS note, display only. FY2008 is GAAP $3.53 with $1,633M of pre-tax realized losses in it (the company's figure
    $7.72): the largest call of the series (below).
  - **FY2002 is excluded, a distorted year** (the AAPL FY2002 test): the asbestos reserve strengthening the FY2002 10-K lists ("a $354 million
    net after-tax charge to fourth quarter 2002 earnings") exceeds the year's $100M net income as the FY2006 10-K restates it ($0.27 a share;
    $0.19 in the FY2002 10-K, before the FY2004 10-K/A restated 2000-2004), and no filing on the restated basis publishes the year without it.
    So the history and the P/E window start with FY2003 (`pe_window_start` 2003-01-01; the ACN FY02, LMT and JPM rule): a 5.0-year window on
    2008-01-04, 7.0 years at the end of 2009. 2001, a loss of $(0.88), precedes it, as do the September fiscal years.
  - **FY2003-FY2008 are kept.** No year meets the test on the items the filings list, summed as listed, charges against gains (the BKR and
    AAPL FY2003 reading): FY2004's asbestos and run-off charge ($302M after tax, the FY2004 10-K/A) is under its $1,153M; the Q4 2005 release
    lists FY2005's A&E charge and catastrophe losses ($2,005M excluding them and realized gains, against $956M excluding realized gains alone:
    $1,049M after tax) beside its net realized gains (a $73M benefit: $1,029M of net income against $956M), $976M against $1,029M. Catastrophe
    losses also recur: each supplement prints a "Catastrophe and other large losses" row, and the guides budget them ("Catastrophe Losses
    included in our estimated earnings are $300 million pre-tax for the second half of the year."). Read as charges alone, $1,049M exceeds
    $1,029M by $20M and FY2005 would be excluded: a close call, tested below. FY2008's realized losses are recurring items, not listed
    one-offs, so it is kept at GAAP.
- **Current-FY EPS: a fiscal-year EPS range stated as earnings per share.** ACE guides the year in its releases, never a quarter:
  - FY2007, from the Q2 2007 release: "Earnings per Common Share are expected to range between $7.15 and $7.50." The release states no other
    basis beside it, so it is read as published: FY2007E $7.325 on the five dates before the Q4 2007 print (the CAT and SPGI range rule). Reading it as
    operating would interpret it through the Q1 2008 release's later wording; it is tested below.
  - FY2008, from the Q1 2008 release: "Operating Income per Share is expected to range between $7.40 and $7.90. The previous range was between
    $7.00 and $7.50." Operating income per share also removes realized gains and losses, so the range feeds nothing (the SPGI
    `eps_guide_amort` rule, guide line only, as `eps_guide_operating`) and FY07's $7.66 stands from the Q4 2007 print (the rollover rule);
    the previous range is in no filing (the Q4 2007 release gives no guide).
  - FY2009: "Earnings guidance announced on December 18, 2008, for the ACE Group for the full year 2009 has not changed." (Q1 2009 release):
    the guide itself is in no filing (no 8-K between 2008-12-17 and 2009-01-26), so the words are in the guide line, no field, and FY08's
    $3.53 stands from the Q4 2008 print.
- **Forward revenue growth.** No next-quarter guide, so method r2's fallback takes the fiscal year, and the fiscal-year guides are net premiums
  earned ("Property & Casualty Net Earned Premium Growth is expected to average from 2% to 4%." for FY2007; P&C +1% to +3% and "Consolidated
  Net Premiums Earned are expected to increase 8% to 10%." for FY2008): a component of revenue, so no total is derived (the MSFT segment rule;
  JPM's net interest income outlooks), and BASE takes the latest quarter's total revenue growth (the UNP, JPM and SPGI rule) plus the buyback
  term. There is no margin guide, so no margin step; the margin signal takes the latest quarter's change.
- **Diluted shares,** each year from the latest filing that reports it. The buyback term is net issuance: -5.6%/yr over FY2003-FY2006
  (275.7M to 327.2M shares, the 2005 offerings after the hurricanes among them), -4.4%/yr to FY2007, -3.7%/yr to FY2008.
- **Dividends,** the latest declared quarterly rate in US dollars, each from the first filing that states it: $0.25 (FY2006 10-K), $0.27
  ("On July 13, 2007, we paid dividends of 27 cents per share", Q2 2007 10-Q, dated 2007-08-08: $1.08 a year on every date to July 2008),
  $0.29 (8-K of 2008-07-14), $0.26 ("CHF 0.30 ($0.26)", the first par value distribution, Q3 2008 10-Q, dated 2008-11-10) and $0.31 ("or $0.31
  per quarter, at the time of the annual general meeting", 8-K of 2009-07-28, dated 2009-07-29). From the Continuation the rate is declared in
  Swiss francs and paid in dollars at the exchange rate of the day; the dollar figure is the one the filing states. The 8-Ks that restate the
  2008 approval's dollar equivalent (2008-09-30, 2008-12-17, 2009-03-31) and the board's 2009 proposal "subject to shareholder approval"
  (2009-03-31) declare nothing new.
- **Signals.** An insurer has no gross margin or inventories, so the set is its own, with ACN's weights: net premiums earned growth (0.20,
  the premium revenue), the change in the P&C combined ratio (0.20, lower is better: the underwriting cost, in the place of the gross margin),
  net investment income growth (0.15), book value per share growth (0.15: the balance sheet's marks, in the place of the inventory gap) and the
  change in the pre-tax margin (0.15: income before income tax over total revenues), plus the theme slot at 2/4. Each value is the
  supplement's own against the year-ago quarter in the same supplement (the consolidating statement's ACE Consolidated column, the highlights'
  combined ratio and book value per share against the year-ago quarter end), as reported: catastrophe losses, realized losses and Combined

- **Thresholds by rule T over fiscal 1997-2006**, the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04: each change from the latest
  10-K published by 2008-01-04 that reports both years (the FY2000 10-K for fiscal 1996-1997, FY2001 for fiscal 1997-1998, FY2002 for fiscal
  1998 against calendar 1999, FY2003 for 1999-2000, the FY2004 10-K/A for 2000-2001, FY2005 for 2001-2002, FY2006 for 2002-2006). Seams stay
  in, as published: 1999 compares calendar 1999 with fiscal 1998 and holds the CIGNA property and casualty acquisition (net premiums earned

  the dollar figures are in thousands to FY2004. The raw figures and values are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives every
  value and threshold and refuses to build if they differ.

- **Durability: CYCLICAL, risk 2.** Each 10-K's risk factors call the company's own business cyclical: "The insurance and reinsurance business

  "Insurance and reinsurance markets are historically cyclical, and we expect to experience periods with excess underwriting capacity and

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned). A price-to-earnings method on an insurer through 2008-2009 turns on which year's EPS
anchors the multiple, and the classes follow it:
- **CHEAP on 51 dates, FAIR on 6, RICH on 48; legacy tier BUY 41, ACCUMULATE 15, WATCHLIST 1, AVOID 48.** CHEAP or FAIR on every date of 2008
  and January 2009 (FAIR on 3 of the 5 dates before the Q4 2007 print, on 2008-05-01, on 2008-06-06 and on 2008-09-19, the week of the
  short-selling ban, when the price reached $66.00); RICH and AVOID on all 48 dates from the Q4 2008 print (2009-02-05).
- **2008 rests on FY07's $7.66** (FY2007E $7.325 in January): $40.75-66.00 is 5.3-8.6x, the 2nd to 64th percentile of a 5.0-6.1-year
  window whose median is 7.9-8.3x; the EPP floor is 6-7x (the calendar-year lows of 2003-2008 run from 4.5x in 2003, a record GAAP year on a
  low price, to 11.7x in 2005), and the price is under it on 2008-10-10 (-11%), 2008-11-21 and 2009-01-23 to 2009-01-30.
- **2009 rests on FY08's $3.53:** $32.50-54.85 is 9.2-15.5x, the 49th-90th percentile of a window whose median is 9.8-10.7x, and 15% to 94%
  above an EPP floor of 8x ($28.24). On 2009-03-06, the low of the series ($32.50), the class is RICH and the tier AVOID.
- **BEAR is the worst year of the history:** -26.1%/yr through 2008 (FY03's $5.25 to FY04's $3.88, the four Florida hurricanes and the run-off
  charge), a BEAR price of $25.60-26.75; -53.9%/yr from the Q4 2008 print (FY07's $7.66 to FY08's $3.53), a BEAR price of $4.88-4.95.
- **BASE is the quarter's total revenue growth less the net share issuance:** +1.9%/yr (Q3 2007's +7.5% less 5.6%) in January 2008, then
  -3.7% (Q4 2007), -17.7% (Q1 2008, revenue -13.3% with $353M of realized losses), +6.2% (Q2 2008), -5.0% (Q3 2008), -14.9% (Q4 2008: revenue
  -11.2%), +12.5% (Q1 2009: +16.2% against the first quarter of 2008), -11.2% (Q2 2009) and -2.0% (Q3 2009). BULL is the history's CAGR
  (+9.5% to +9.9%/yr in 2008, -7.6% to -2.0% in 2009, or BASE's rate where higher) and XBULL the FY05 to FY07 run, +52.1%/yr (+33.4% before the
  Q4 2007 print).
- **Ratio B is infinite on 29 dates of 2009** (the price above the BULL case) and never negative (the BEAR price stays under the price).
- **The proxy composite** is 2.30 on Q3 2007, 2.15 on Q4 2007, 2.00 on Q1 2008, 2.35 on Q2 2008, 2.05 on Q3 and Q4 2008, 2.00 on Q1 2009,
  1.50 on Q2 2009 (premiums, investment income and book value per share at BEAR) and 2.15 on Q3 2009.

- the FY2007 range read as operating (no field, FY06's $6.90 standing in January 2008): 2 classes (CHEAP to FAIR), 3 tiers;

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the EPS basis: GAAP, with realized gains and losses in, because the company's figure also removes them, which recur (52 classes; the
  insurance industry's own convention is the operating figure, and a builder who knows that 2008's realized losses reversed in 2009 might have
  chosen either way);
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows the 2008 marks and the 2008 hurricanes: book value per share and the pre-tax margin hold 0.30 of
  the weight and the combined ratio 0.20 (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; 44 classes move at BEAR);
- FY2002 excluded by the AAPL test on its asbestos charge (42 classes), and FY2005 kept by $53M on the items summed as listed (charges alone:
  46 classes the other way);
- the FY2007 "Earnings per Common Share" range read as published (2 classes);
- net premiums earned guides read as components of revenue rather than the revenue guide (1 class);
- the series itself: ACE Limited under the CB key, not The Chubb Corporation that traded as CB in 2008-2009;
- CYCLICAL rather than DURABLE (label only);
- the parts of the filings listed above as not read: a guide in an unread exhibit or a posted presentation would be missed, though every
  release, 10-Q statement and 10-K outlook passage was read.

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/CB/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

### CB 2010-2013: two EPS restatements as published, operating guides only, dividends from Swiss reserves

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31 (52, 52, 52, 53), added to the 105 of 2008-2009 at the owner's request ("same rules as
before"). The method is still r2, the engine and its rule-T thresholds are unchanged, and the 2008-2009 entries of the fact sheet are
unchanged (the generator asserts it). The 105 earlier models rebuild byte-identical.

```bash
python3 retro/build_cb.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                    # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for c in 2010-01-10 2010-02-03 2010-02-25 2010-04-29 2010-07-28 2010-10-28 2011-02-03 2011-02-28 2011-05-05 2011-07-27 2011-08-04 \
         2011-10-26 2012-02-01 2012-02-27 2012-04-25 2012-07-25 2012-08-01 2012-10-24 2013-01-30 2013-02-28 2013-04-23 2013-07-24 \
         2013-07-25 2013-10-23 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CB; done
```

One range, as for JPM: an ISO week that starts on 2012-12-31 belongs to 2013 (per-year ranges would add a 2012-12-31 date beside
2013-01-04).

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the EPS basis, GAAP with realized gains and losses in, kept from 2008-2009 by the same rule (79 classes, above);
- the restatements taken from the release that first prints each one, and the Q1 2012 supplement's restated net income not turned into a
  per-share figure;
- every operating guide read as feeding nothing, so the current year is always the last full year;
- FY2002 excluded (81 classes) and FY2005 kept (63), unchanged from 2008-2009;
- the signals and their weights, chosen in 2008-2009 by a builder who knows the period (86 classes move at BEAR, 37 at XBULL);
- revenue as total revenues with realized gains and losses in, rather than net premiums earned (27 classes);
- CYCLICAL rather than DURABLE (label only);
- the parts of the filings listed above as not read, the two posted decks among them.

call wrong. No decision here uses an outcome: every rule applied existed before 2008-2009 was scored, the GAAP basis among them, kept as
the rule requires though that finding points the other way. The 2010-2013 outcomes were computed only after the firewall passed.

### CB 2014-2017: no guide in any filing, The Chubb Corporation as published, Chubb Limited and NYSE: CB, a correction to 2010-2012

208 weekly dates, 2014-01-10 to 2017-12-29 (51, 53, 52, 52), added to the 314 of 2008-2013 at the owner's request ("same rules as
before"). The method is still r2, the engine and its rule-T thresholds are unchanged, and the code is the newest branch of the repository
(its commit "CB retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for 2010-2013", 2026-11-21, every other recent retro branch being its
ancestor). Built in a new session that did not open the 2008-2013 outcomes or `FINDINGS.md` before the build was committed; the README's
own one-line summaries of them (the 2010-2013 section's last paragraph) were read with the rules, and no decision below uses them.

```bash
python3 retro/build_cb.py --weekly 2014-01-06 2017-12-31                    # 208 dates, 2014-01-10 .. 2017-12-29
for c in 2014-01-06 2014-01-28 2014-02-28 2014-04-29 2014-07-22 2014-07-24 2014-10-21 2015-01-27 2015-02-27 2015-04-21 2015-07-21 \
         2015-08-04 2015-10-20 2016-01-15 2016-01-26 2016-02-26 2016-05-04 2016-07-26 2016-08-05 2016-10-25 2017-01-31 2017-02-28 \
         2017-04-25 2017-07-25 2017-08-03 2017-10-26 2018-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CB; done
```

The range starts on 2014-01-06, the Monday after the last built week (2013-12-31 sits in the ISO week that 2014-01-03 would take; the
JPM, SPGI, V and GOOG precedent).

highlights for the P&C combined ratio and its book value reconciliation for book value per share now and a year earlier); the 10-Qs of Q1

(losses), total revenues, income tax and net income, the quarter and the year-ago quarter: all 12 match), and their dividend passages; and
all 56 8-Ks of December 2013 to December 2017 (one an 8-K/A) by their item text, their exhibits searched by keyword. Every release's

findings for 2018-2021", 2026-11-21), every other recent retro branch being its ancestor. **Built in a new session that did not open the
2008-2021 outcomes, `SERIES.md` or `FINDINGS.md` before this batch was built, checked and committed.** This README's point-in-time sections
and CLAUDE.md were read, as every batch reads them. That includes the one-line summaries of earlier findings that the 2010-2013 and
2018-2021 sections carry, and no decision below uses them. Each decision applies a rule that existed before or an earlier CB encoding:
- the r2 rollover, decade and bound rules;
- the ACN, UNP 2005, LMT and JPM rule for a company figure excluding only a one-off;
- the CB 2010-2013 rule that a restatement applies from the release that first prints it;
- the LMT, PFE and CAT print-level `restates` encoding;
- the JPM, CMCSA and PFE reading of acquisitions in the growth rates;
- the ACN rule for a 10-K without selected data.

```bash
python3 retro/build_cb.py --weekly 2022-01-03 2026-11-20                    # 255 dates, 2022-01-07 .. 2026-11-20
for c in 2022-01-03 2022-02-02 2022-02-25 2022-04-27 2022-07-27 2022-07-29 2022-10-26 2023-02-01 2023-02-24 2023-04-26 2023-07-26 \
         2023-07-28 2023-10-25 2024-01-31 2024-02-26 2024-04-24 2024-07-24 2024-07-26 2024-10-30 2025-01-29 2025-02-27 2025-04-23 \
         2025-07-23 2025-07-29 2025-10-22 2026-02-04 2026-02-27 2026-04-22 2026-07-22 2026-07-29 2026-10-21 2026-11-21; do
  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CB; done
```

The range starts on Monday 2022-01-03 (2021-12-31, built with 2018-2021, is in ISO week 2021-W52) and ends with the week of 2026-11-16.
The series was built on Saturday 2026-11-21, after Friday's close (Yahoo's last bar is stamped 2026-11-20 16:00:03 ET), so 2026-11-20 is a
built date. The newest dates have no outcome yet.

What was read, and how (the session's model directly, no delegated transcription):
- **Releases.** The 20 earnings releases of Q4 2021 to Q3 2026. From exhibit 99.1: the summary consolidated financial data, the quarter
  and full-year summaries (net income to core operating income) and the definitions of the non-GAAP measures; the text was searched for
  "guidance", "outlook", "expect", "run rate", "range" and dividend sentences. From exhibit 99.2: the financial highlights' P&C combined
  ratio, the book value per share reconciliation and the Q1 2023 supplement's accounting adoption page.
- **10-Ks.** The FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks: the statements of operations, the earnings per share note's diluted shares, the MD&A's P&C combined
  ratio, the segment note's net premiums earned, Item 1's opening, Item 1A's cycle and catastrophe risk factors, and Item 6.
- **10-Qs.** The 15 10-Qs of Q1 2022 to Q3 2026, compared by script with their releases on six rows (net premiums earned, net investment
  income, net realized gains (losses), total revenues, income tax and net income, the quarter and the year-ago quarter: all 15 match), and
  the Q2 10-Qs' dividend sentences.
- **Other 8-Ks.** All 25 other 8-Ks of January 2022 to November 2026, by their item text, their exhibits searched by keyword.

**Not read:** the 10-K and 10-Q text beyond those rows and passages; the proxy statements, their additional materials and the exempt
solicitations; the S-3ASR of 2024-10-03; the notes offerings' exhibits; and the investor decks that the Item 7.01 8-Ks of 2022-12-05,
2023-12-04, 2024-12-09 and 2025-12-08 say were posted on the website (not filed).

How the fact sheet was made. The scripts behind the 2008-2021 entries are not in the repository, so the new entries come from a new
generator. It reads each figure from its own row by label and computes every rate. It asserts every identity a table carries:
- total revenues equal their components in each release and each 10-K;
- each release agrees with its 10-Q, and each Q4 release's year with the 10-K that follows;
- the supplement's combined ratio agrees with the release's;
- the segments sum to net premiums earned;
- the 2008-2021 entries are unchanged.

It also notes, on every print, each year-ago figure that differs from its own year-ago release. 382 strings were checked with
`verbatim.py`, each against its own filing (382/382), and no new fact's own text names a year after its publication (the scan that found
the 2010-2012 leak, which caught and corrected a first draft whose FY2021 and FY2022 vintages named the FY2023 10-K's EPS label). The fact
sheet only gains facts: 2,576 lines added and none removed (git's histogram diff). The new source ids are `CB100`-`CB129`. Decided on
2026-11-21, before any 2022-2026 model was built or scored:

- **Release timing.**
  - All twenty earnings 8-Ks were accepted after the close (16:10-19:03 ET) and are dated the next trading day, public before its open.
    Each week's date is the trading day after that: 2022-02-03, 2022-04-28, 2022-07-28, 2022-10-27, 2023-02-02, 2023-04-27,
    2023-07-27, 2023-10-26, 2024-02-01, 2024-04-25, 2024-07-25, 2024-10-31, 2025-01-30, 2025-04-24, 2025-07-24, 2025-10-23, 2026-02-05,
    2026-04-23, 2026-07-23 and 2026-10-22.
  - 10-Ks: FY2021 after the close (2022-02-24 17:10 ET, dated 2022-02-25); FY2022 during market hours (2023-02-24 15:47 ET); FY2023 after
    the close (Friday 2024-02-23 17:08 ET, dated Monday 2024-02-26); FY2024 during market hours (2025-02-27 15:56 ET); FY2025 during
    market hours (2026-02-27 15:08 ET).
  - A Q4 print extends the history from its release to the 10-K: 3, 3, 4, 4 and 3 dates.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS, the same rule, unless a filing publishes the year excluding only a one-off.** Each year comes from the latest
  filing that reports it. FY21 $19.27, FY22 $12.55, FY23 $19.06, FY24 $22.56, FY25 $25.68. The company's core operating income per share
  ($12.56, $15.24, $22.54, $22.51 and $24.79 as first published) is display only, as before: it removes realized gains and losses, which
  recur, and from 2023 market risk benefits gains and losses.
  - **FY2023 is the company's $19.06,** not GAAP $21.80. Its income tax line carries "a one-time deferred tax benefit of $1.14 billion,
    or $2.76 per share, related to the enactment of Bermuda's new income tax law". The Q4 2023 release's Full Year Summary publishes the
    year without it: "Net income excluding tax benefit | $7,893 | ... | $19.06". That figure excludes only the one-off, so it replaces GAAP
    (the ACN rule; UNP 2005 for a tax reduction; LMT and JPM for the 2017 Tax Act). CB's FY2017 benefit stayed at GAAP for the opposite
    reason: its only figure without the benefit was on the core basis. The benefit is under the year's income without it, so the mirror
    test is not met either way. The pre-tax margin and the display-only tax rate stay as published.
  - **FY2024 is the company's $22.56,** not GAAP $22.70. It excludes the incremental $55M Bermuda deferred tax benefit of Q1 2024 (the
    Q4 2024 release, the same row). It leaves in the $24M after-tax Charitable Foundation contribution of the same quarter, which no
    figure excludes alone. From the FY2024 10-K both years cite the Q4 2024 release, the latest filing that prints them.
  - **FY2025 is GAAP.** The "Amortization of deferred tax asset from Bermuda law" ($124M) recurs, as the Q1 2025 release's redefinition
    says ("as well as the subsequent years' amortization of the related deferred tax asset"), and no figure excludes only it.
  - **No year is distorted.** Each Q4 release lists, after tax, realized gains and losses (FY21 $3,023M of gains; FY22 $1,087M of losses
    as first published), the fair value amortization, the Cigna integration expenses, the market risk benefits and the integration
    expenses and severance, never near a year's net income ($8,539M, $5,313M, $9,028M, $9,272M and $10,310M).
  - **From Q3 2023 EPS is Chubb net income per share.** Huatai Group is consolidated at 100% from 2023-07-01, and its noncontrolling
    interests are out of EPS. The pre-tax margin is income before income tax over total revenues, both at 100%, as the statement prints
    them.
- **The LDTI restatement from the Q1 2023 supplement (2023-04-26).** The company adopted the long-duration targeted improvements on
  2023-01-01 with a transition date of 2021-01-01. The Q1 2023 supplement's accounting adoption page prints FY2021 and FY2022 per share
  "As Adjusted": $19.24 and $12.39, against $19.27 and $12.55 reported. This is the first filing that prints them, so they apply from
  its date (the CB 2010-2013 rule; the DAC restatement waited for the Q4 2012 release only because the Q1 2012 supplement gave no
  per-share figure). The encoding is the print-level `restates` of LMT, PFE and CAT, new in `build_cb.py`. It applies until a 10-K
  vintage published after the print carries the years: the FY2023 10-K, whose statement gives 2021-2023 as adjusted.
  - The supplement also republishes FY2022's revenue components, but no total and no FY2021. So revenue keeps the FY2022 10-K until the
    FY2023 10-K, which can only lag, never leak; the restatement is EPS only, as in LMT.
  - From Q1 2023 to Q4 2023 each release's year-ago quarter is as adjusted. Each print is read against its own year-ago column, as
    before, and its note lists every year-ago figure that differs from the year-ago release.
- **Revenue: total revenues as the statement of operations adds them,** each year from the latest filing that reports it.
  - From Q1 2023 (and in the FY2023 10-K for 2021-2023) the statement adds a new line: "Market risk benefits gains (losses)". It is in,
    as published; its 10-Q totals confirm it.
  - Cigna's Asian accident and health and life business is in the figures from 2022-07-01 ("On July 1, 2022, the company completed the
    acquisition of Cigna's accident and health (A&H) and life business for $5.36 billion.", the Q2 2022 release), and Huatai Group at
    100% from 2023-07-01, both as published (the JPM, CMCSA and PFE rule). Nothing is made pro forma.
- **The ten-year roll.** The FY2021 10-K holds FY2012-FY2021, and each later 10-K moves the window a year.
  - Item 6 is "[Reserved]" from FY2021, so each 10-K gives the three years of its statement, and earlier years keep the latest 10-K
    that reported them (the ACN rule; JPM and SPGI).
  - BEAR is FY13 to FY14 (-22.9%/yr) to the Q4 2022 print, then FY21 to FY22: -34.9%/yr from 2023-02-02 ($19.27 to $12.55), and
    -35.6%/yr from the Q1 2023 print ($19.24 to $12.39).
  - XBULL is FY11 to FY13 (+55.4%/yr) to 2022-02-18, then FY19 to FY21 (+40.9%/yr; +40.8% on the adjusted FY21).
- **No guide in any filing**, as in 2014-2021. No release, 10-Q, 10-K or 8-K guides revenue, EPS or a margin in numbers. The releases'
  words feed nothing and are not encoded:
  - "we expect investment income to increase from here." (Q1 2022);
  - "we expect EPS to continue to grow at a healthy rate into the future." (Q3 2022);
  - "Our investment income run rate will continue to grow as we reinvest cash flow at higher rates and compound income." (Q2 2023);
  - the USI sale "expected to result in a realized gain of $460 million" (Q3 2026), which is not a guide of any r2 input.

  So the current year's EPS is the last full year's on every date. BASE is the latest quarter's total revenue growth less the net share
  issuance, which is a net buyback throughout: diluted shares fall from 443.2M (FY21) to 401.5M (FY25). By print: +3.6% to +3.8% (Q4
  2021), -5.8% (Q1 2022, $887M of realized gains a year earlier), +0.1%, +9.0%, +6.7% (Q4 2022), +12.5% (Q1 2023), +17.2%, +12.0%
  (Q3 2023, Huatai in), +11.3% (Q4 2023), +14.4%, +14.7%, +5.0%, +6.7% (Q4 2024), +1.2% (Q1 2025), +4.8%, +6.3%, +8.0% (Q4 2025),
  +12.3% (Q1 2026), +8.3% and +2.0% (Q3 2026, revenue +0.3% with $455M of realized losses).
- **Dividends,** each from the first filing that states it. $0.83, $0.86, $0.91, $0.97 and $1.02 a quarter, from the Q2 2022-2026 10-Qs:
  2022-07-29, 2023-07-28 and 2024-07-26 (during market hours), 2025-07-29 and 2026-07-29 (after the close, dated the next trading day).
  The sentence is "... expected to be paid in four quarterly installments of $0.83 per share after the general meeting". The meeting
  8-Ks give the votes only and the releases the dividends paid, as before.
- **Signals, thresholds, durability: unchanged.**
  - Catastrophe losses (the California wildfires of Q1 2025 among them: a combined ratio of 95.7%, +970bp), realized gains and losses,
    market risk benefits, Cigna and Huatai are in, as reported.
  - CYCLICAL, in each 10-K's own words: the same three sentences in FY2021-FY2025.
  - GENAI (from 2022-11-30) and GLP1 (from 2023-08-08) join the live themes the "why" quotes. Neither registered scope names insurance,
    so the watch list stays empty.
  - The six segments of 2016 throughout (display only).
- **Adds nothing:** none of these states a guided number.
  - The share-capital 8-Ks: cancellations and par value (2022-01-20, 2022-08-09, 2025-03-10, 2026-03-11).
  - The meeting results (2022-05-20, 2023-05-17, 2024-05-16, 2025-05-16, 2026-05-22).
  - The posted decks (2022-12-05, 2023-12-04, 2024-12-09, 2025-12-08).
  - The officer and director 8-Ks (2022-12-07, 2024-03-15, 2024-07-09, 2024-08-12, 2025-11-04).
  - The Credit Suisse statement (2023-03-21), the notes offerings (2024-03-07, 2024-07-31, 2025-08-06, 2026-05-20, 2026-06-10) and the
    S-3 exhibits (2024-10-03).

  print's full-year EPS, the Q1 2023 restatement's FY2022, each vintage's last-year EPS and each dividend. None changes a model dated
  before its publication, and each changes the first weekly date on or after it: 36 controls, all effective. The FY2022 vintage's

- **Leak scan.** For each of the 255 new models: the source ids, titles, urls, notes and their clauses, quotes, rows and figures (four
  significant digits or more) of every fact published after its date. Tokens that an earlier fact's text or the engine already carries
  are dropped first. Result: 0 text hits in 178,979 (model, later token) pairs. The 12 figure hits are all coincidences: the bare 2022
  and 2023 of the 10-Ks' year headers against FY labels in January 2022 and January 2023. All four of the latest print's notes appear in
  each model. The 731 earlier models are byte-identical to before, so no new fact reaches them.
- **Regression.** `build_cb.py` gains the print-level `restates`, and the firewall tool's CB entry a planted print-level restatement of
  every year. With the new fact sheet the 731 dates of 2008-2021 rebuild byte-identical. No other ticker's code or output is touched.
- **Firewall** (after the build was committed and pushed, before any outcome). It passes at the 32 cutoffs above: 0 files changed and no
  planted text, 731 to 986 dates each. The cutoffs are every print, vintage, restatement and dividend date of the range, 2022-01-03 and
  2026-11-21. The planted facts are 2008-2021's plus a later print-level restatement of every year the latest vintage reports. The
  2026-11-21 run rebuilds all 986 dates byte-identical.
