Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- **The EPS basis.** GAAP, with realized gains and losses in, kept by the same rule (133 classes). FY21's $19.27, inflated by $3,023M of
  realized gains, anchors every CHEAP date of 2022. A builder who knows how 2022 went might have reached for the core figure; the rule
  existed before, and was kept.
- **FY2023 and FY2024 at the company's figures excluding the Bermuda tax benefits** (44 classes). The rule is old and the figure is
  printed, but the ACN, UNP, LMT and JPM precedents are other tickers' readings, and CB's own FY2017 stayed at GAAP.
- **The LDTI restatement** taken from the Q1 2023 supplement (it moves no class), with revenue left to the FY2023 10-K.
- **Market risk benefits in revenue, as the statement adds them** (12 classes). Cigna and Huatai are in as published; the
  consolidation's quarters (Q3 2023 to Q2 2024) carry BASE at +12% to +15%.
- **Revenue as total revenues** rather than net premiums earned (27 classes).
- **The signals and their weights,** chosen in 2008-2009 (152 classes at BEAR, 50 at XBULL).
- **CYCLICAL rather than DURABLE** (label only).
- **The parts of the filings listed above as not read,** the four posted decks among them.

The 2022-2026 outcomes were computed only after the firewall passed. The hindsight results are in
`staging/retrospective/CB/FINDINGS.md` ("2022-2026"): hypotheses, never inputs.

## LLY (Eli Lilly and Company): the thirty-first ticker, in staging, 2008-2009

The LLY series is built apart from the other thirty and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/LLY.json`), builder (`retro/build_lly.py`, the BMY builder with BMY 2014-2017's excluded-year handling, company-wide U.S.
and outside-U.S. growth from the filing that first states it, and a loss-guide reading) and engine (`retro/templates/lly_engine.py.tmpl`,
the BMY engine with Eli Lilly's own rule-T thresholds; a figure no filing public on AS_OF states scores BASE and prints "n/r", the spgi2
and bkr3 encoding). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an LLY model, and neither
does the live `lly_signal_model.py` (other branches) or the LLY profile in `data/business_profiles.json` (2026 analyses, not read for
this series; only `retro_tool outcome` reads the profile, for the hindsight `profile_drift` label). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/LLY/`,
beside the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009 ("same rules as before"); the code
is the newest branch of the repository (its commit "CB retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for 2022-2026", 2026-11-21), every
other retro branch being its ancestor.

```bash
python3 retro/build_lly.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                   # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_lly.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                   # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/LLY/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series LLY
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-01-29 2008-02-29 2008-03-13 2008-04-21 2008-05-06 2008-07-24 2008-08-06 2008-10-21 2008-10-23 2008-11-04 \
         2008-12-11 2009-01-29 2009-02-27 2009-04-20 2009-07-22 2009-10-21 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c LLY; done
```

the 10-Qs of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 (their MD&A sales passages and tables, searched for dividends and repurchases); the guidance 8-Ks of
2008-03-13 and 2008-12-11; and every other 8-K of October 2006 to January 2010 by its item text, its exhibits searched for guidance and
per-share sentences. **Not read:** the 10-Qs and 10-Ks beyond those passages, the proxy statements, the ImClone tender offer documents
(SC TO-T, 2008), the Q1 2008 10-Q/A (a balance-sheet restatement), and the slide presentations of the investment community meetings
(not filed). The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows: each figure is read from its own row by label
(the script asserts every identity a table carries: the five-year summaries against the statements of income, the geographic totals
against net sales, the product classes against net sales, the 10-Qs' U.S. and outside-U.S. sales against the release, each stated
percent against the stated dollar change, each Q4 release's year against the 10-K that follows, the 10-K/A's history fields against the
10-K's), every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is computed, not typed, and every quoted sentence is asserted present in its own
filing; the 335 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (335/335). Each source's date comes from EDGAR's
acceptance time (UTC, converted to ET; before 2003 EDGAR gives the filing date only); the source ids are `LL1`-`LL32`. Decided on
2026-11-21, before any LLY model was built or any LLY outcome computed (Yahoo was asked for its series metadata, splits and 2006-2009
dividends only):

- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's LLY series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 splits of 1995-12-21 and 1997-10-16 and books no event after
  them, so from 1997-10-16 the close is the price as traded; every P/E window here starts in 1998 or later. NYSE: LLY throughout, and no
  change of company name.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year. The four dates before the Q4 2007 print (2008-01-04 to 2008-01-25) have FY2007 as the current
  year.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 was accepted before the open or during the session on its release day
  (06:30-14:25 ET; the release states a 9:00 a.m. call on most days) and none of 2008-2009 on a week's last trading day, so each
  print's week is dated the next trading day: 2008-01-30, 2008-04-22, 2008-07-25, 2008-10-24, 2009-01-30, 2009-04-21, 2009-07-23,
  2009-10-22. The FY2006 10-K was accepted after the close (2007-02-28 17:18 ET, dated 2007-03-01), the FY2007 10-K (2008-02-29 09:54 ET),
  the 10-K/A (2008-10-21 15:53 ET) and the FY2008 10-K (2009-02-27 11:19 ET) during the session; the Q2 2007 and Q3 2008 10-Qs after the
  close (dated 2007-08-07 and 2008-11-04). A Q4 print extends the history from its release to the 10-K: FY2007 from 2008-01-29 (4
  dates), FY2008 from 2009-01-29 (4 dates).
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it,** ten fiscal years to the latest one, from the five-year summaries:
  diluted EPS from continuing operations before extraordinary items and the cumulative effect of a change in accounting principle, net
  sales and diluted shares. 1997 is $1.78 from the FY2001 10-K (PCS discontinued from the FY1998 10-K, so its 1997 write-down is out;
  the DowElanco gain is in), 1998 $1.87 (FY2002 10-K), 1999 $2.30 (FY2003), 2000 $2.79 (FY2004), 2001 $2.55 (FY2005; $2.58 before the
  debt-repurchase loss in the FY2001-FY2002 10-Ks, which SFAS 145 moves into income), 2002-2006 from the FY2006 10-K, 2005 at $1.83
  before its $.02 cumulative effect ("The net income per diluted share before the cumulative effect of a change in accounting
  principle was $1.83.", each five-year footnote), then the FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks. Seams stay in, as published.
  - **A restated 10-K is a vintage of its own** (the MSFT, CAT and BMY recast rule). The FY2007 10-K/A of 2008-10-21 restates the
    balance sheets for product return reserves ("The consolidated statements of income were not adjusted for any of the years or
    quarters"); its EPS, net sales, shares, margins, tax rate, free cash flow and cash equal the 10-K's (asserted), and from 2008-10-21
    the history cites it.
- **GAAP EPS; the company's adjusted and pro forma figures stay out.** Lilly's "adjusted" (2006), "pro forma adjusted" (2007-2008) and
  "pro forma non-GAAP" (2008-2009) EPS exclude acquired in-process research and development, which is on the statements of income in
  2001 ($190.5M: the Isis, 3M and Bioprojet collaborations), 2002 ($84.0M: Amylin), 2004 ($392.2M), 2007 ($745.6M, the OSI, MacroGenics
  and Glenmark in-licensing transactions among them) and 2008 ($4,835.4M, BioMS and TransPharma among them): a recurring cost of the

  from 2009 ImClone) as if acquired at the start of the prior year. They are shown in each print's EPS note and the guide line, never
  used, and no figure is derived from the reconciliations.
- **No year to 2007 is distorted** (the AAPL FY2002 test and its mirror), on the items each 10-K lists: 1997 $1.78 against the company's
  $1.62 without its unusual items (the DowElanco gain net of the litigation and Somatogen charges: listed benefits far under the income
  without them); 1998-2000 within 7% of the company's figures; 2004, the near case, $1.66 against $2.82 without $.35 of in-process
  research and development, the $.43 repatriation tax and $.38 of impairment, restructuring and Evista investigation charges (59%);
  2005 $1.83 against $2.87 (64%); 2006 and 2007 over 75%. So the P/E window starts ten years back (`pe_window_start` none): 1998-01-05
  on 2008-01-04.

  - **A guided loss has no P/E** (decided here: no r2 rule covers a range whose midpoint is a loss; BMY 2018-2021 used a range that
    spans a loss only because its midpoint was positive). The 8-K of 2008-12-11 lowers FY2008's reported guide to "a loss of $1.56 to
    $2.06 per share" after the ImClone charge; read as no numeric guide (the r2 loss rule), so FY07's $2.71 stands on the 7 dates from

- **Forward revenue growth.** No next-quarter revenue guide, and every fiscal-year revenue guide is words ("reported sales to grow in
  the mid-teens", "pro forma sales to grow in the mid- to high-single digits", "reported sales are expected to grow in the low-single
  digits", "mid-single digit revenue growth on a reported basis"), which give no field (the PEP, UNP, LOW, WMT, CMCSA and BMY rule). So
  BASE takes the latest quarter's growth excluding foreign exchange, the release's stated growth less the exchange-rate points it states
  (the NKE, MSFT and BMY rule): +17% (Q2 2007: 20 less 3), +16% (Q3 2007: 19 less 3), +18% (Q4 2007: 22 less 4), +9% (Q1 2008: 14 less 5),
  +5% (Q2 2008: 11 less 6), +10% (Q3 2008: 14 less 4), +3% (Q4 2008: "essentially flat", read as 0 by the SPGI "flat is 0" rule, less -3),

- **Dividends,** the latest declared quarterly rate, each from the first filing that states it: the 10-Ks ("In the fourth quarter of

- **Signals.** The PFE set, as BMY reused it, with ACN's weights: U.S. revenue growth (0.20) and international revenue growth (0.20), total
  revenue growth (0.15), the gross-margin change (0.15; net sales less cost of sales) and the pre-tax margin change (0.15; income before

  against the year-ago quarter in the same release; charges stay in, as published (Q3 2008's Zyprexa charges and Q4 2008's ImClone
  in-process research and development make those pre-tax margins -4.47% and -64.05%). Company-wide U.S. and outside-U.S. growth is as

  2008-01-30 to 2008-04-18.

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2,** the PFE and BMY precedent for a research-based pharmaceutical company; no 10-K calls the business
  cyclical. The "why" quotes the latest 10-K: the FY2006 10-K's "We discover, develop, manufacture, and sell products in one significant

Controls and checks (before any outcome):
- **`retro_tool run` passes on all 105 dates**; the 97 dates from 2008-02-29 draw one warning, the calendar year 2011 (the FY2007 and
  FY2008 10-Ks' own patent-expiry words, in the durability "why").
- **Controls:** altering one value of each print (its growth ex-FX; its release-stated U.S. growth; each Q4 print's full-year revenue),
  each 10-Q's U.S. growth (`geo_later`), each vintage (its last year's EPS, its dividend) and each guide (its reported range) changes no
  model dated before its publication: 42 controls, of which 39 change the first weekly date on or after it and 3 are inert, superseded
  before any built date (the Q2 2007 print's growth, the Q2 2007 release's FY2007 guide, and the FY2009 guide of the 8-K of 2008-12-11,
  which the Q4 2008 release restates before FY2009 is current).
- **Leak scan:** 0 hits in 15,970 (model, later token) pairs (on the final models): the source ids, titles, notes, quotes, rows and figures (four significant digits
  or more) of every fact published after each model's date, after dropping the tokens an earlier fact or the engine already carries. As
  a positive control, the latest print's own notes appear in each of the 105 models.
- **Self-text scan** (new for this series, after a leak the term check below found): every capitalized word, dollar figure and year in
  each fact's own text must appear in a Lilly filing filed by the fact's own date. It found that the first draft's history note, shared
  by all four vintages, named later deals and charges (ImClone, BioMS and TransPharma in every model from 2008-01-04); each vintage's note
  now describes only what was public on its own date, and the scan passes on all 32 facts (one tokenizing artifact, "K's").
- **Term check:** "ICOS" first appears on 2008-01-04 (the Q3 2007 print's note), "BioMS" on 2008-04-22, "OSI", "MacroGenics" and
  "Glenmark" on 2008-02-29 (the FY2007 vintage), "ImClone" and "Zyprexa investigations" on 2008-10-24, "10-K/A" on 2008-10-24, "SGX",
  "TransPharma" and "$(1.89)" on 2009-01-30, "Erbitux" and "total revenue" on 2009-04-21, each after its filing; "Effient" and every
  later product name appear in no model.
- **Regression:** the shared code is untouched (the firewall tool gains an LLY entry, `taxonomy_eras.json` the terms above); rebuilding
  the 2008-2009 dates of BMY, PFE and CB changes nothing (315 models).
- **Firewall** (run after the build was committed, before any outcome): its first run failed at three cutoffs (2008-02-29, 2008-03-13 and
  2008-04-21: 4, 6 and 12 models changed). For a print whose company-wide U.S. and outside-U.S. split no filing public on AS_OF states, the
  builder had printed that the quarter's 10-Q, "not yet filed, will" state it, and the Q4 2007 print's own note that no filing states it:
  words that depended on filings after AS_OF, which the planted later 10-Q exposed. The slot now reads the same either way ("the Q4 2007
  release gives no company-wide U.S. and outside-U.S. split, and no filing public on AS_OF states it (n/r)"); 18 models changed in text
  only (the 12 dates on the Q4 2007 print and the 6 between a 2008 release and its 10-Q), no class or tier, and the controls and leak scan
  were rerun (39 of 42, 0 of 15,970). The rerun passes at all 18 cutoffs above (the first built date, every print, 10-Q, vintage and guide
  date of the range, and 2010-01-01: 1 to 105 dates each), 0 files changed and no planted text. The planted facts include a print with
  absurd sales, growth ex-FX, U.S. and outside-U.S. growth, margins, quarter EPS, notes and raw figures, absurd full-year actuals for the
  year after the latest vintage (or Q4 print), a later Q4 print whose full-year actuals exclude its own year, a later 10-Q split on the
  last print before the cutoff, a later guide for every guided year (a reported range, an adjusted range, words and a note) and a still
  later loss range, a later vintage excluding a year with planted texts, a dividend, a company name and prices from the cutoff multiplied
  by 10. As positive controls, a planted print dated 2008-07-01 with its own source reaches 2008-07-03 (its text in the model) and not

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned). Lilly's own decade of P/Es (1998-2007, the years of 30x multiples) is far above what it
traded at in 2008-2009, so every rule that reads the window says cheap:
- **CHEAP and BUY on all 105 dates; robustness 8 of 8 on every date.**
- **January 2008 rests on FY2007's guide** ($2.785): $50.74-56.81 is 18.2-20.4x, the 0th-7th percentile of a ten-year window whose median
  is 29.6-29.7x; the EPP floor (the median of the calendar-year lows 1998 31.1x, 1999 26.7x, 2000 19.5x, 2001 28.5x, 2002 19.3x, 2003
  22.7x, 2004 30.4x, 2005 27.2x, 2006 20.6x, 2007 17.6x and 2008's own) is 22x, $61.27, 7-17% above the price.
- **From the Q4 2007 print the guide carries the call.** FY08E is $3.815-3.975 to the Q3 2008 print, then $2.465, then FY07's $2.71 on the
  loss-guide dates: $30.43-52.28 is 8.1-14.9x (the 0th-3rd percentile, median 27.7-29.5x), and the price is 29-63% under a 20-22x floor
  ($54-87) on every date. FY09E is $3.95-4.19 from the Q4 2008 print: $27.98-38.18 is 6.8-9.5x (the 0th-9th percentile of the window ex-FY08,
  median 26.7-28.8x), 55-68% under the floor ($79-88). The low of the series, $27.98 on 2009-03-06, is 6.8x.
- **BEAR is 2004's fall** on every date (-30.0%/yr: $2.37 to $1.66, the in-process R&D, repatriation-tax and Evista year) at the
  10th-percentile P/E, a BEAR price of $18-42; the BEAR price exceeds the price on 44 dates (2008-10-10, 2008-10-17 and 2009-01-30 to
  2009-11-13), so Ratio B is negative there (the price under the BEAR case; the BUY tier reads rb < 0.75).
- **BASE is the quarter's growth ex-FX plus the buyback:** +16.4%/yr in January 2008, +18.3-18.4% (Q4 2007), +9.3% (Q1 2008), +5.3% (Q2
  2008), +10.3% (Q3 2008), +3.1-3.2% (Q4 2008), +11.1% (Q1 2009), +10.1% (Q2 and Q3 2009). BULL equals BASE except after the Q4 2008 print,
  when the 1998-2007 EPS CAGR (+4.2%/yr) exceeds it for 4 dates; XBULL is the 1998-2000 run (+22.1%/yr), then 2005-2007 (+21.7%) from the
  FY2008 10-K. The growth factor runs from -0.50 (Q4 2008) to +0.50 (Q3 and Q4 2007).
- **The proxy composite** is 2.90 on Q3 2007 (U.S. +18% at BULL, international +20% and revenue +18.7% at XBULL), 2.60 on Q4 2007 (the
  U.S. split n/r), 2.30 on Q1 2008 (2.70 from its 10-Q), 2.30 on Q2 2008 (2.50 from its 10-Q), 2.15 on Q3 2008 (2.55 from its 10-Q; the
  pre-tax margin at BEAR on the Zyprexa charges), 1.95 on Q4 2008 (international -3% and the pre-tax margin, -8,433bp on the ImClone charge, at
  BEAR; the gross margin +696bp at XBULL), 2.60 on Q1 2009, 2.45 on Q2 2009 and 2.60 on Q3 2009.

How far each call moves the classes (the 105 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline; no outcome consulted):
- FY2008 kept at the company's $4.02 (instead of excluded): no class, no tier;
- the company's adjusted guide midpoints as current-year EPS (history unchanged): no class, no tier;
- the FY2008 loss range read as the $2.44-2.49 range standing (the ImClone sentence): no class, no tier;
- BASE on reported growth instead of growth excluding exchange rates: no class, no tier;
- U.S. and outside-U.S. growth from the releases only (no 10-Q values): no class, no tier;
- every data signal at its BEAR value (on 2009-06-05 the proxy composite falls from 2.60 to 1.15 and the gap from 2.00 to 0.55): no
  class, no tier; at its XBULL value: none;
- a five-year P/E window instead of ten (no rule says so; it shows what the call rests on): no class, no tier (on 2009-06-05 the median falls from
  28.0x to 22.8x and the price moves from the 3rd to the 7th percentile).
The CHEAP calls rest on Lilly's 2008-2009 multiple of 7-15x its own reported EPS guide against its own 1998-2007 P/E history and
calendar-year lows (17.6-31.1x); no encoding tested moves a class.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, the PFE set reused for a third pharmaceutical company by a builder who knows that Lilly's U.S. patent expirations
  (Zyprexa from late 2011) dominated its next decade (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; no class moves at BEAR or XBULL);
- the company-wide U.S. and outside-U.S. growth taken from the 10-Qs for the quarters whose releases give none (no class moves), and the
  Q4 2007 slot left empty;
- GAAP EPS rather than the company's adjusted or pro forma figures, on the recurring in-process research and development (no class);
- FY2008 excluded as a loss, and the FY2008 loss guide read as no numeric guide (no class either way);
- 2004 kept at 59% of its EPS without the listed items, the near case of the distorted-year test;
- DURABLE rather than STRUCTURAL or another kind (the class label only), on the 10-Ks' own description of patent expiry as the
  business's risk;
- the parts of the filings listed above as not read: a guide in an unread exhibit or a presentation not filed would be missed, though
  every release, 10-Q sales passage and guidance 8-K was read (the 8-K of 2008-03-13 was found by a per-share search of every 8-K, after
  the first pass).

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/LLY/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
Lilly's ten-year window holds two regimes, 2003-2007 at calendar-year lows of 18-30x and 2009-2013 at 7-11x (2008 out), and the
stock trades at the second regime's multiples throughout, so every rule that reads the window says cheap until its median crosses:
- **CHEAP and BUY on all 209 dates; robustness 8 of 8 on 173 and 7 on 36** (2012-07-26 to 2012-10-19 and 2013-07-05 to 2013-12-31,
  where "multiples one band cheaper" reads RICH on 34 and FAIR on 2).
- **2010:** FY09E $3.95 on the first three dates, then FY10E $4.75 (from the Q4 2009 print), $4.425, $4.515 and $4.60: $32.37-37.76 is
  7.1-9.1x, the 0th-11th percentile of a window whose median is 24.4-26.7x, 55-65% under an EPP floor of 20-21x ($79.00-99.75). BASE is
  the quarter's growth ex-FX with the buyback term: +10.1%/yr, +11.0-11.1% (Q4 2009), +6.0% (Q1 2010), +8.0% (Q2), +3.0% (Q3); BULL equals
  it except from the Q3 2010 print (the EPS CAGR, +3.9%). Ratio B 0.09-0.16.
- **2011:** FY11E $3.995 to $3.865: $34.09-41.64 is 7.6-10.6x, the 5th-33rd percentile (median 22.3-24.3x), 44-60% under the floor
  ($74.10-87.40). BASE +4.8-4.9%/yr (each quarter +5% ex-FX), BULL +5.1-6.7%. Ratio B 0.14-0.31.
- **2012:** from the Q4 2011 print BASE is -8.4%/yr, the FY2012 dollar guide (-10.2% to -6.1%) with the margin and buyback terms; FY12E
  $3.15, $3.215, $3.34, then $3.77 with the $.43 Amylin income (2012-08-10) and $3.73: $39.05-52.86 is 10.1-14.0x, the 33rd-43rd
  percentile (median 20.6-22.3x), 24-44% under the floor ($56.70-71.63). BULL +4.3-5.1%. Ratio B 0.28-0.60.
- **2013:** FY13E $4.175, $4.33 and $4.355, BASE +1.4-1.5%/yr (the FY2013 guide, -0.0% to +3.5%): $48.38-57.51 is 11.2-14.4x, the
  37th-47th percentile; the window's median falls from 20.2x to 12.6x as 2003's days leave and the 2009-2013 regime becomes its
  majority, and the floor, 4-20% above the price to 2013-12-27, falls to $43.55 (10x) on 2013-12-31, when the window starts on
  2004-01-02 and 2003's low leaves the median of calendar-year lows: the price is 17% above it on that date. Ratio B 0.43-0.66.
- **BEAR is 2004's fall** (-30.0%/yr, $2.37 to $1.66) and **XBULL the 2005-2007 run** (+21.7%/yr, $1.83 to $2.71) on every date (the
  2007-2009 run across the excluded FY2008 is +20.6%); the BEAR price stays under the price. The proxy composite runs from 2.70 (Q4
  2009, Q2 2010) to 1.65 (Q2 2012).

(the generator asserts every earlier source, vintage, print and guide, the rule-T figures and the other lists equal to the committed
sheet) and the 523 earlier models rebuild byte for byte. No builder or engine change.

```bash
         2019-10-23 2019-10-24 2019-12-17 2020-01-30 2020-02-19 2020-04-23 2020-07-30 2020-10-27 2020-12-15 2021-01-29 2021-02-17 \

```

## UNH (UnitedHealth Group): the thirty-second ticker, in staging, 2008-2009

The UNH series is built apart from the other thirty-one and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/UNH.json`), builder (`retro/build_unh.py`, the CB builder with a health benefits company's fields, LLY's reported EPS ranges
and dollar revenue guides, SPGI's guided margin step, the shared `on_basis` split helper and a dated print restatement) and engine
(`retro/templates/unh_engine.py.tmpl`, the CB engine with a managed-care signal set and UnitedHealth Group's own rule-T thresholds). It is
the first health benefits company in the retrospectives. The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker
enters a UNH model. Today's UNH profile in `data/business_profiles.json` is a 2026 analysis; it was not opened for this series and is not an
input (only `retro_tool outcome` reads it, for the hindsight `profile_drift` label). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/UNH/`, beside the
others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009 ("same rules as before"); the code is the newest
branch of the repository (its commit "LLY retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for 2022-2026", 2026-11-23), every other retro
branch being its ancestor.

```bash
python3 retro/build_unh.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                   # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_unh.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                   # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/UNH/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series UNH
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-01-22 2008-02-22 2008-04-22 2008-07-02 2008-07-22 2008-10-16 2008-12-02 2009-01-22 2009-02-12 2009-04-21 \
         2009-07-21 2009-10-20 2009-11-30 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c UNH; done
```

**The company.** UnitedHealth Group Incorporated, NYSE: UNH (CIK 731766), on every date; the filer of 1998 was United HealthCare Corporation
(the name in the FY1998 10-K/A), which no 2008-2009 model prints. Fiscal year: the calendar year. The four dates before the Q4 2007 print
(2008-01-04 to 2008-01-18) have FY2007 as the current year.

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the statements of operations and five-year summaries of the FY1998
10-K/A and the FY1999-FY2008 10-Ks (the FY1999-FY2003 annual reports are Exhibit 13s, the FY1998-FY2002 ones plain text; the FY2000 report
from the 10-K/A of 2001-04-02 that refiles Exhibit 13), the FY2006 10-K's restatement tables (2002-2003, APB 25 and FAS 123R) and quarterly
data, the segment notes and the dividend, listing and split sentences of the FY2000-FY2008 10-Ks, the cautionary statements (FY2006,
FY2007) and Item 1A (FY2008) searched for the "why" and for any cyclical label; every earnings release of Q4 2006 to Q3 2009 (the statements
of operations, the reconciliations of figures excluding the IRS Section 409A charges and the special items, the outlook paragraphs and the
Q1 and Q2 2008 outlook schedules); the Q2 2007 10-Q's statement of operations; every 8-K of October 2006 to February 2010 by its item text,
its exhibits searched for guidance, per-share and outlook sentences (the guidance 8-Ks of 2007-08-06, 2007-12-04, 2008-07-02, 2008-12-02 and
2009-11-30 read in full). **Not read:** the 10-Qs and 10-Ks beyond those passages, the proxy statements and the investor conference slide books and "supplementary data points" the 7.01 8-Ks of 2006-12-19, 2007-12-04, 2008-12-02
and 2009-11-30 say were posted on the website (not filed; the slide book filed with the 8-K of 2006-12-19 was searched for guide sentences only, and its FY2007 outlook is
superseded before any built date). The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows: each figure is read from its own row by
label (the script asserts every identity a statement carries: revenues as the sum of premiums, services, products and investment income,
earnings from operations as revenues less every cost line, net earnings as pre-tax less tax; the five-year summaries against the statements;
each Q4 release's year against the 10-K that follows; the Q2 2008 release's year-ago quarter against the Q2 2007 10-Q), every growth rate,
ratio, margin and rule-T value is computed, not typed, and every quoted sentence is asserted present in its own filing; the 398 strings were
checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (398/398). Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (UTC, converted to ET;
before 2002 EDGAR gives the filing date only); the source ids are `UH1`-`UH28`. Decided on 2026-11-24, before any UNH model was built or
any UNH outcome computed (Yahoo was asked for its series metadata, splits and 2005-2009 dividends only):

- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's UNH series is adjusted for the two-for-one splits of 1992, 1994, 2000-12-26, 2003-06-19 and 2005-05-31 and
  books none after, so every 2008-2009 close is the price as traded ($56.00 on 2008-01-04, $26.60 on 2008-12-31, $30.48 on 2009-12-31) and
  the window's earlier days are on the post-2005 share basis. The history's per-share figures published before a split (1997-2000, from the
  FY2001-FY2003 10-Ks) are divided by the splits after their own filing and share counts multiplied (`splits`, the GOOG and V use of the
  shared `on_basis` helper), each split from the filing that states it ("The dividend was issued on December 22, 2000", FY2000 10-K/A; "The
  stock dividend was issued on June 18, 2003", FY2003 10-K; "In May 2005, our board of directors declared a two-for-one stock split.", FY2005
  10-K), effective on Yahoo's split date (the first trading day on the new basis; the builder asserts the dates match).
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q1 2007 to Q3 2009 was accepted before the open on its release day (06:07-06:34 ET; the call
  "at 8:45 a.m." or "9:00 a.m. Eastern time today"), so each print's week is dated the next trading day: 2008-01-23, 2008-04-23, 2008-07-23,
  2008-10-17, 2009-01-23, 2009-04-22, 2009-07-22, 2009-10-21. The guidance 8-Ks were accepted before the open too (2007-12-04 06:01,
  2008-07-02 06:12, 2008-12-02 06:39, 2009-11-30 07:15 ET). The FY2006 10-K before the open (2007-03-06 06:18 ET); the FY2007 and FY2008
  10-Ks after the close (2008-02-21 17:12, 2009-02-11 17:25 ET), dated 2008-02-22 and 2009-02-12. A Q4 print extends the history from its
  release to the 10-K, eleven years in between (the CB and JPM builders): FY2007 from 2008-01-22 (4 dates), FY2008 from 2009-01-22 (3 dates).
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it,** ten fiscal years to the latest one: diluted EPS (net earnings applicable to
  common shareholders), revenues and diluted shares. 2002-2006 come from the FY2006 10-K, which restates them for the stock option review
  under FAS 123R, the company's "Current Accounting Method" (it adopted FAS 123R by modified retrospective restatement; its APB 25 table is
  the historical method, not used): $0.95, $1.34, $1.83, $2.31, $2.97. "The cumulative after tax impact of all restatement adjustments related
  to years prior to 2002 ... has been reflected as an adjustment to retained earnings at December 31, 2001", so no filing restates 2001 or
  earlier: they stay as first published, a seam (the reinsurance gross-up and the products reclassification also start in 2002).
- **EPS: the company's figure excluding only one-offs where a filing on the same basis prints it** (the ACN rule), GAAP otherwise:
  - 1997 $1.13 (FY2001 10-K; no item listed); 1998 $1.31, "Excluding the operational realignment and other charges of $725 million, $175
    million of charges related to contract losses associated with certain Medicare markets and other increases to commercial and Medicare
    medical costs payable estimates, and the $20 million convertible preferred stock redemption premium" (FY2002 10-K, the latest filing
    that reports 1998; GAAP $(0.56), a loss); 1999 $0.79 without the UnitedHealth Capital tax benefit and 2000 $1.05 without that benefit and
    the disposition gain (FY2003 10-K; GAAP $0.80 and $1.09; the FY2004 10-K, the latest for 2000, prints the same GAAP $1.09 without the
    footnote); 2001 $0.70 (FY2005 10-K, already after the 2005 split). On the 2008 share basis: $0.2825, $0.3275, $0.395, $0.525, $0.70.
  - FY2007 $3.50 excluding the IRS Section 409A charges ($176M of operating costs, $0.08; GAAP $3.42) and FY2008 $2.95 excluding special
    items ($0.55: the two stock option class action settlements and legal costs, the out-of-network class action settlement net of insurance
    recoveries, severance, and the gain on the Nevada Medicare Advantage sale; GAAP $2.40), each from its Q4 release's reconciliation in every
    vintage that holds it (the JPM FY2017 rule: the 10-Ks print GAAP only).
  - **No year is distorted.** The AAPL FY2002 test and its mirror pass on every year as encoded: 1998 is a GAAP loss, but the company's
    figure without its listed charges stands (the ACN rule comes first; a 1998 read as a loss is tested below); 1999 and 2000's benefits are
    1-4% of income. The P/E window starts ten years back (`pe_window_start` none): 1998-01-05 on 2008-01-04. Every one-year change in the
    history is a gain (+15.9% to +41.1%), so BEAR is the 0% cap until FY2008 enters.
- **Current-FY EPS: the fiscal-year EPS range's midpoint,** at the company's figure where a guide is given with and without announced items
  (the ACN rule: the 409A charges in 2007; the 2008 settlements, severance and the Nevada gain), each from the latest guide that states it:
  FY2007 $3.495 ($3.49-3.50 "excluding" the 409A charges, $3.41-3.42 including them; the Q3 2007 release and the 8-K of 2007-12-04) to
  2008-01-18; FY2008 $3.975 ($3.95-4.00, the 8-K of 2007-12-04 and the Q4 2007 release), $3.575 ($3.55-3.60, Q1 2008), $3.00 ($2.95-3.05 "as
  adjusted", the 8-K of 2008-07-02 and the Q2 2008 release; GAAP $2.56-2.66) and $2.965 ($2.95-2.98 "as adjusted", the 8-K of 2008-12-02);
  FY2009 $3.025 ($2.90-3.15, the 8-K of 2008-12-02, maintained in the Q4 2008 and Q1 2009 releases), $3.075 ($3.00-3.15, Q2 2009) and $3.15
  ("approximately $3.15", Q3 2009 and the 8-K of 2009-11-30). Next-quarter EPS ranges are not method r2 inputs; the Q3 2008 release gives only
  Q4's, so the July range stands. The FY2010 guide (8-K of 2009-11-30) is current only from the Q4 2009 print, after the range.
- **Forward revenue growth.** The company guides next-quarter EPS, never next-quarter revenue, so r2's fallback takes the fiscal-year guide,
  in dollars, read as growth on the last full year's revenues (the PFE, LOW, BMY and LLY dollar-level rule): FY2007 "approximate $76
  billion" (Q2 2007) on FY06's $71.542B, +6.2%; FY2008 "approximately $83 billion" (8-K of 2007-12-04, "assuming the closing of the pending
  acquisition of Sierra Health Services, Inc. prior to the end of 2007"; the Q4 2007 release restates no revenue, so it stands) on FY07's
  $75.431B, +10.0%; $81,000-81,750M (the Q1 2008 outlook schedule; the text's "$81 billion to $82 billion range" rounds it), +7.4% to +8.4%;
  "in the $81 billion range" (8-K of 2008-07-02) and "Approximately $81,000" (the Q2 2008 schedule), +7.4%; FY2009 $85-86 billion (8-K of

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, a managed-care set chosen by a builder who knows that 2008's problem was medical costs against premium yields and that the
  settlements landed in operating costs (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; no class moves at BEAR or XBULL);
- the company's figures excluding one-offs for 1998-2000 and 2007-2008, and the company's guides with and without announced items, rather
  than GAAP (no class either way); 1998's figure also removes $175M of contract-loss and reserve charges, kept as the company's listed
  charges of that year (no class either way);
- the July 2008 margin derived from guided earnings from operations and revenues (no class either way);
- FAS 123R rather than APB 25 for the restated 2002-2005 (the company's current method; not tested, the differences are 0-4 cents);
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL or another kind (the class label only);
- the parts of the filings listed above as not read: a guide in a posted slide book or "supplementary data points" would be missed, though
  every release, guidance 8-K and outlook schedule was read.

## CRM (salesforce.com): the thirty-third ticker, in staging, 2008-2009

The CRM series is built apart from the other thirty-two and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/CRM.json`), builder (`retro/build_crm.py`, the NVDA builder with salesforce.com's fiscal calendar and fields, UNH's
fiscal-year EPS guide midpoint and NVDA's dollar-level next-quarter revenue guide) and engine (`retro/templates/crm_engine.py.tmpl`, the
NVDA engine with a subscription software company's signal set and salesforce.com's own rule-T thresholds). It is the first subscription
software company in the retrospectives. The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters a CRM model.
Today's CRM profile in `data/business_profiles.json` and `scripts/quality_classify.py` is a 2026 analysis; it was not opened for this series
and is not an input (only `retro_tool outcome` reads it, for the hindsight `profile_drift` label; its one-line summary was seen in a grep's
output after every CRM model had been built and validated). Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/CRM/`, beside the others, with the same
`index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009 ("same rules as before"); the code is the newest branch of the
repository (its commit "UNH retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for 2022-2026", 2026-11-26), every other retro branch being its
ancestor.

```bash
python3 retro/build_crm.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                   # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_crm.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                   # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/CRM/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series CRM
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-02-28 2008-03-03 2008-05-22 2008-08-21 2008-11-21 2009-02-26 2009-03-10 2009-05-22 2009-08-21 2009-11-18 \
         2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CRM; done
```

**The company.** salesforce.com, inc., NYSE: CRM (CIK 1108524), on every date. Fiscal year: "Our fiscal year ends on January 31." (FY2007
10-K); FY2009 runs from February 1, 2008 to January 31, 2009. The eight dates before the Q4 FY08 print (2008-01-04 to 2008-02-22) have FY2008
as the current year, and the days of February 2008 before the print keep its EPS (the rollover rule).

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the IPO prospectus (424B1 of 2004-06-23: selected data for the
inception period to January 31, 2000 and fiscal 2001-2004, the lease recovery paragraphs); the selected financial data, statements of
operations, balance sheets, cash flows and geographic revenues of the FY2005-FY2009 10-Ks; their Item 1, Item 1A and Item 5 searched for the
"why", the listing, the dividend sentence and any cyclical label; every earnings release of Q1 FY07 to Q3 FY10 (8-K exhibits 99.1: the
statements of operations, balance sheets, Additional Metrics tables and outlook paragraphs; the Q4 FY06 release for its GAAP/non-GAAP
reconciliation); every 8-K of January 2005 to April 2010 with item 2.02, 7.01 or 8.01 by its text (the 8-K of 2006-12-12, which raised the
FY2008 revenue outlook, read in full). **Not read:** the 10-Qs beyond their listing, the proxy statements, the S-1 and its amendments before
the final prospectus, and the investor presentations and call transcripts the releases point to (not filed). The fact sheet is generated by
a script from the filings' converted rows: each figure is read from its own row by label (the script asserts every identity a statement
carries: gross profit as revenues less cost of revenues, operating income as gross profit less the operating expenses, those expenses as
the sum of research and development, marketing and sales and general and administrative), every growth rate, margin, gap and rule-T value
is computed, not typed, every Additional Metrics column is checked against its header's date (the quarter end and the year-ago quarter end),
and every quoted sentence is asserted present in its own filing; the 316 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings
(316/316). Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (UTC, converted to ET); the source ids are `CR1`-`CR23`. Decided on
2026-11-26, before any CRM model was built or any CRM outcome computed (Yahoo was asked for its series metadata, splits and dividends, and
for three closes inside the range to check the share basis):

- **The listing rule** (method r2, "A listing inside the window"). "Our common stock has been quoted on the New York Stock Exchange under the
  symbol “CRM” since June 23, 2004." (FY2005 10-K); Yahoo's series starts that day (the builder asserts it). The P/E window runs from the
  listing: 3.5 years on 2008-01-04, 5.5 at the end of 2009.
- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's series is adjusted for the four-for-one split of 2013-04-18, after every built date; the builder multiplies
  it by the splits after AS_OF (x4), so every price is the price as traded ($58.86 on 2008-01-04, $32.01 on 2008-12-31, $73.77 on 2009-12-31).
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q1 FY07 to Q3 FY10 was accepted after the close (16:21-16:51 ET; the call "at 2:00 p.m. Pacific"),
  so each print is dated the next trading day: 2007-11-16 (Q3 FY08), 2008-02-28, 2008-05-22, 2008-08-21, 2008-11-21, 2009-02-26, 2009-05-22,
  2009-08-21, 2009-11-18. Four of those are Fridays, the week's last trading day, and meet their own close (public before the open; the AVGO
  rule): 2007-11-16, 2008-11-21, 2009-05-22, 2009-08-21. The others put the week's date on the next trading day: 2008-02-29, 2008-05-23,
  2008-08-22, 2009-02-27, 2009-11-19. The FY2007, FY2008 and FY2009 10-Ks were accepted after the close (2007-03-09 17:16, 2008-02-29 16:53,
  2009-03-09 17:24 ET) and are dated 2007-03-12, 2008-03-03 and 2009-03-10. A Q4 print extends the history from its release to the 10-K:
  FY2008 on 2008-02-29 (1 date), FY2009 on 2009-02-27 and 2009-03-06.
- **History: each year from the latest filing that reports it,** the ten fiscal years to the latest one: diluted EPS, total revenues and
  diluted shares. The company's first period runs from its inception (February 3, 1999) to January 31, 2000, and it lost money in it and in
  fiscal 2001-2003 ($(0.55), $(2.38), $(1.36), $(0.37)).
  - **FY2004 is excluded, a year distorted by a one-off benefit** (the AVGO FY2018 mirror test): "Operating income during fiscal 2004 was
    $3.7 million and included the $3.4 million lease recovery described above." (the prospectus); the selected data's "Lease recovery" of
    $3,445K is larger than the year's pre-tax income without it ($794K: $4,239K less $3,445K, derived), so the reported $0.04 is more than
    double the year's EPS without it, and no filing publishes a figure excluding it. FY2004 is not the latest year of any vintage, so it takes
    the years before it (the PFE 2003 and MU FY2003 rule; they are losses as well): the history starts with FY2005 and the P/E window after
    January 31, 2004 (`pe_window_start` 2004-02-01), i.e. at the listing.
  - **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS,** except **FY2006 at the company's $0.181** (the Q4 FY06 release's "Non-GAAP diluted net income per share",
    which excludes only "the lease recovery item recorded in the first quarter of fiscal 2006 and the partial reversal of the deferred tax
    valuation allowance reserve in the third quarter of fiscal 2006"; GAAP $0.240): the ACN rule, the figure kept in every vintage that holds
    FY2006 (the JPM FY2017 rule: the 10-Ks print GAAP only, with the footnote "This benefit represented $0.06 of basic and diluted net income
    per share"). The releases of Q4 FY07 to Q3 FY10 print GAAP only. FY2005 $0.07, FY2008 $0.15 (with the Q3 FY08 gain on the sale of a
    minority investment, "approximately $0.01 per share" in words, a fraction of the year's $18.4M net income, so it stays in: the ACN rule
    for a one-off with no figure without it) and FY2009 $0.35.
  - **FY2007 is excluded: its GAAP diluted EPS is $0.00** ("For the full year, GAAP earnings per share were breakeven", the Q4 FY07 release;
    net income $481K), which has no P/E (Ford's $0.00 year, the F rule), and nothing in it is listed as a one-off (its stock-based
    compensation, $39.2M from the adoption of SFAS 123R, recurs). It is the latest year of the FY2007 10-K, so only it leaves (the r2 note
    for a distorted latest year): its own days (2006-02-01 to 2007-01-31) leave the P/E window ("3.5-yr ex-FY07"), and it stays a gap after
    (the NKE FY2018 and XOM FY2020 rule), so EPS growth is measured only between years in the history.
- **Current-FY EPS: the midpoint of the fiscal-year GAAP diluted EPS range** from the latest guide public on AS_OF that states one (the UNH
  rule): FY2008 $0.125 ($0.12-0.13, the Q3 FY08 release: "This GAAP EPS estimate includes ... the third quarter gain on the sale of a
  minority investment"); FY2009 $0.325 ($0.32-0.33, Q4 FY08), $0.335 ($0.33-0.34, Q1 FY09) and $0.295 ($0.29-0.30, Q2 FY09, standing to the
  Q4 FY09 print, as the Q3 FY09 release restates no FY2009 range); FY2010 $0.545 ($0.54-0.55, Q4 FY09), $0.595, $0.605 and $0.625
  ($0.62-0.63, Q3 FY10). The Q2 FY09 release gives FY2009 with and without the InStranet acquisition ("Including the effect of the InStranet
  acquisition, estimated at $0.05 for the full year ... $0.29 to $0.30"; $0.34-0.35 without it): the acquisition's effect is its own results
  and the amortization of its intangibles, which recur, so it is not a one-off and the GAAP range stands (the NKE FY2007 and AVGO rule; the
  range without it is quoted in the guide line). Next-quarter EPS ranges are display only. The FY2011 revenue guide of the Q3 FY10 release
  ("growth in the range of approximately 15% to 16% when compared to projected fiscal year 2010") is current only from the Q4 FY10 print,
  after the range (it joined the fact sheet with 2010-2012, below, and changes no 2009 model).
- **Forward revenue growth: the next-quarter revenue guide,** a dollar range in every release, read against the year-ago quarter's revenues
  from that quarter's own release (the AAPL, AVGO and NVDA level rule): Q4 FY08 $206-208M on Q4 FY07's $144.2M (+42.8% to +44.2%), Q1 FY09
  $233-235M (+43.5% to +44.7%), Q2 FY09 $258-259M (+46.1% to +46.7%), Q3 FY09 $273-274M (+41.6% to +42.1%), Q4 FY09 $284-285M (+30.9% to
  +31.4%), Q1 FY10 $304-305M (+22.8% to +23.2%), Q2 FY10 $312-313M (+18.6% to +19.0%), Q3 FY10 $323-324M (+16.8% to +17.2%), Q4 FY10
  $340-342M (+17.4% to +18.1%). The fiscal-year revenue ranges set the segment bridge's total only (display).
- **No margin guide** in any filing, so no guided step: the margin signal takes the latest quarter's operating margin change.
- **No dividend:** "We have never paid any cash dividends on our common stock." (each 10-K); no repurchase program (the 10-Ks' only
  repurchases are of unvested shares).
- **Signals.** A subscription software company has no inventories, so the set is the NVDA set's counterparts, with ACN's weights:
  subscription and support revenue growth (0.20, the recurring line, 91% of revenues), deferred revenue growth (0.20, current and noncurrent,
  the quarter end against the year-ago quarter end, both from the release's own Additional Metrics row: billings run ahead of revenue), the
  gross margin change (0.15), operating expense growth less revenue growth (0.15, research and development, marketing and sales and general
  and administrative; the separately stated lease lines stay out; lower is better) and the operating margin change (0.15), plus the theme
  slot at 2/4. Each quarterly value is the release's statement of operations against the year-ago quarter in the same release, GAAP as
  reported (the stock-based compensation in, the InStranet acquisition in from Q3 FY09).
- **Thresholds by rule T over fiscal 1998-2007,** the decade of the FY2007 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04: the inception period to
  January 2000 has no revenue ("Total revenues | — | 5,435 | ...", the prospectus), so the changes are fiscal 2002-2007, each from the latest
  filing published by then that reports both years (the FY2005 10-K's five-year data for fiscal 2001-2002, the FY2006 10-K's for 2002-2003,
  the FY2007 10-K's for 2003-2007); deferred revenue has five (fiscal 2003-2006 from the FY2006 10-K's selected balance sheet data, fiscal
  2007 from the FY2007 10-K's balance sheet; no filing reports the January 31, 2001 balance). The start-up years stay in, as the filings
  report them (the GOOG and NVDA reading). The raw figures and values are in the fact sheet (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives every value
  and threshold and refuses to build if they differ.

  | Signal | Fiscal 2002-2007 | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|

### CRM 2013-2017: a reduced-data batch (SEC XBRL only), the four-for-one split, five loss years, RICH throughout

261 weekly dates, 2013-01-04 to 2017-12-29, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The owner asked for 2013-2017 ("find newest
code. do retrospective analysis for CRM, 2013-2017. same rules as before"). The newest code was the branch with CRM 2008-2012 (its commit
"CRM retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for 2010-2012", 2026-11-26); this branch was fast-forwarded to it.

```bash
python3 retro/build_crm.py --weekly 2013-01-01 2017-12-31                   # 261 dates, 2013-01-04 .. 2017-12-29
for d in staging/retrospective/CRM/201[3-7]-*/; do python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"; done
for c in 2013-01-01 2013-02-25 2013-03-11 2013-04-18 2013-05-28 2013-09-03 2013-11-26 2014-03-06 2014-05-30 2014-08-27 2014-11-26 \
         2015-03-06 2015-05-26 2015-08-25 2015-11-23 2016-03-07 2016-05-23 2016-09-01 2016-11-22 2017-03-07 2017-05-23 2017-08-28 \
         2017-11-24 2018-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CRM; done
```

**A reduced-data batch.** This session could not download the filing documents. SEC's `www.sec.gov`, which serves them, refused every
request without a deliverable contact address in the `User-Agent`, including a GitHub no-reply address. The owner's own email was ruled
out: CLAUDE.md forbids it, and the session's privacy guard blocked it. `data.sec.gov`, which serves the filing index and the XBRL company
facts, accepted a plain client name. The owner chose to build from those ("go XBRL") over stopping. So, from the first filing of the
period that was not read, the fact sheet holds only what the 10-Qs' and 10-Ks' XBRL carries:
- that filing is the 8-K of 2013-02-22 (item 8.01, accepted after the close), so the date is 2013-02-25 (`reduced_data.first_unread`);
- the XBRL covers the statements of operations, balance sheets and cash flows, each dated by its filing's EDGAR acceptance time.

**Not in it:** salesforce.com's earnings releases and their guidance, every other 8-K, and the 10-Ks' text. The models say so: every
text that would read "no guide in numbers" reads "not in this fact sheet (reduced-data batch)", and `METHODOLOGY` carries the flag, so
no model claims that a guide was not given. The 8 dates before 2013-02-25 (2013-01-04 to 2013-02-22) are full-data, built from the
Q3 FY13 release as before. The batch should be redone from the filings themselves when they can be downloaded. Its outputs are labels
of a different information set and stay apart in this section.

The generator (a script in the session scratchpad, not the repository) reads every figure from the company facts by accession, tag and
period, and requires it to be unique there; the `rows` of each print keep tag, period and value. It asserts:
- every identity of the statements: gross profit less operating expenses is the operating result; operating expenses are R&D, marketing
  and sales, G&A and any separately stated line; cost of revenues plus gross profit is total revenues where both are tagged; pre-tax
  income less tax is net income;
- that every fourth quarter derived from the 10-K equals the 10-K's own tagged quarterly revenues, gross profit and operating result;
- that every year a later 10-K reports equals the earlier vintage's figure (revenue; EPS and diluted shares on each filing's share basis);
- that each Q1-Q3 FY14 print's year-ago deferred revenue, taken from the Q1-Q3 FY13 10-Qs' XBRL, equals the 2012 release's figure.
The source ids are `CR39`-`CR60`. The earlier fact sheet content is unchanged (asserted), and no filing published after 2017-12-31 is
read. Disclosed: one exploration output in this session showed the FY2018 10-K's XBRL (published 2018-03-09) before the generator was
written to stop at 2017-12-31. No figure from it is in the fact sheet.

Same-session disclosure: none in the earlier sense. This batch was built in a new session. It did not open the 2008-2012 outcome files
or `FINDINGS.md`, which it opened only after the firewall result below was pushed. It did read this README, including the 2010-2012
section's summary of the 2008-2009 findings' two hypotheses (above). Like every builder, it knows salesforce.com's later history from
its training. Decided before any 2013-2017 outcome was computed:

- **Prints are the 10-Qs and 10-Ks,** dated by acceptance. Every one was accepted after the close (16:05-21:40 ET), so each is public
  from the next trading day, and the weekly dates follow them (the first trading day after each, or the week's last when it is that
  day: 2014-05-30, 2015-03-06 and 2017-11-24 meet their own close). The earnings releases' days are not print days in this batch.
- **Revenue tags change in 2015.** Up to the Q3 FY15 10-Q, `Revenues` is total revenues and `SalesRevenueServicesNet` professional
  services and other. From the FY2015 10-K on, `SalesRevenueServicesNet` is total revenues (equal to `Revenues` where both are tagged)
  and `TechnologyServicesRevenue` professional services and other. Subscription and support is not tagged in the company facts: it is
  total revenues less professional services and other (derived, and said so in each print's note). The generator asserts professional
  services at 3-12% of revenues and the gross margin at 70-82% on every period.
- **Q4 is derived:** the 10-K's fiscal year less the Q3 10-Q's nine months, both years, for revenues, subscription and support, gross
  profit, R&D, marketing and sales, G&A and the operating result. The 10-K tags Q4 EPS for both years; the Q4 diluted share count is
  not tagged, so the fiscal year's weighted average is shown (display only, said so).
- **Deferred revenue** is current and noncurrent where the filing tags both. The Q1-Q3 FY18 10-Qs tag no noncurrent deferred revenue,
  so those three prints compare current against the year-ago current balance, on the same basis (said so in the note). Noncurrent was
  0.4-0.7% of the total in the four FY2017 quarters.
- **One separately stated operating line:** Q1 FY16's $36.6M gain on contract termination (`GainLossOnContractTermination`, the
  residual of operating expenses less the three lines) stays out of the opex signal, which counts R&D, marketing and sales and G&A
  only, as before.
- **The split.** The four-for-one split, effective 2013-04-18, is sourced to the price series' own split event, public on its day (`CR41`;
  the FY2014 10-K's XBRL later tags the ratio, 4). From that date every earlier per-share figure is divided by 4 and every share count
  multiplied by 4 (`eps_published` on each vintage gives each year's share basis). Prices are as traded: x4 before the split, x1 after.
- **History: five more vintages,** the FY2013-FY2017 10-Ks, each taking its three income-statement years from its own XBRL; earlier years
  keep the latest earlier filing that reported them (the ACN rule for a 10-K without five-year data), the ten fiscal years to the latest.
  - **FY2013 to FY2016 are GAAP losses,** $(1.92) (pre-split; $(0.48) after), $(0.39), $(0.42) and $(0.07) a share, with no figure
    excluding only one-offs in the sheet. Each is excluded as the latest year of its 10-K, its own days out of the P/E window, then a gap
    (as FY2007 and FY2012). The window label reaches "10-yr ex-FY12 ex-FY13 ex-FY14 ex-FY15 ex-FY16".
  - **FY2017 is GAAP $0.26.** Its pre-tax income is $25.4M and its tax line a $154.2M benefit (XBRL). No item is listed as a one-off in
    this fact sheet, so the year stays at GAAP; the mirror test cannot be applied without the release or 10-K text (tested below).
  - The history drops FY2005 with the FY2015 vintage and FY2007 with the FY2017 vintage; the FY2004 note leaves with the FY2014 vintage.
    FY2006 stays at the company's $0.181 while it is in the decade.
- **Current-FY EPS: the rollover rule.** Up to the FY2013 10-K the FY2013 range is a loss and FY11's $0.47 stands, as before. From the
  FY2013 10-K no EPS guide is in the sheet, so the last full year stands:
  - FY11's $0.1175 (post-split; $0.47 before) from 2013-03-11 to 2017-03-03, for FY2014 to FY2017;
  - FY17's $0.26 from 2017-03-07, for FY2018.
  - In the full-data reading, FY2014-FY2016 would rest on the same figure if their guides were losses. Whether they were is not in the
    sheet, and FY2017's and FY2018's guides could have been positive.
- **Forward revenue growth:** with no next-quarter guide in the sheet, the latest quarter's revenue growth stands in (the UNP rule):
  +23.2% to +37.8% over the batch. The FY2014 revenue guide of the Q3 FY13 release ($3.80-3.85B) sets the bridge's total until the
  FY2014 10-K. After it the bridge has the forward growth applied to the year, and one group, total revenues (the geographic split is
  not in the company facts).
- **Display only:**
  - cash is cash and equivalents plus marketable (available-for-sale) securities;
  - the convertible notes are the tagged convertible lines, other borrowings not shown;
  - the tax rate is the 10-K's tax line over its pre-tax result (negative in loss years, so the EPS check reads oddly);
  - free cash flow is operating cash flow less capital expenditures;
  - no dividend and no repurchase in any cash flow statement.
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2,** carried from the FY2012 10-K, the last whose text is in the sheet, and said so in the "why".
- **Themes.** ECOMMERCE (live 2015-01-01), STREAMING (2015-08-04) and ENERGY_TRANSITION (2015-12-12) are scoped to physical retail,
  pay-TV and fossil fuels: none names a software business, so the "why" quotes their scopes and says so, and the watch list stays empty.
  CLOUD is read as before (salesforce.com's own model, on the FY2012 10-K's words).
- **Builder change** (`retro/build_crm.py`):
  - the reduced-data texts and `METHODOLOGY` flag from `reduced_data.first_unread`;
  - the three 2015 themes allowed, with their sentence;
  - the docstring.
  The 262 models of 2008-2012 rebuild byte for byte. The firewall tool plants a later reduced-data flag.

- **January to mid-April 2013** (15 dates): on FY11's $0.47 the as-traded $165-186 is 352-395x, the 93rd-99th percentile of an 8.5-8.7
  year window (median 181-197x).
- **From the split to the FY2017 10-K** (203 dates): on FY11's $0.1175, $37.56-82.75 is 320-704x, the 80th-100th percentile (median
  169-219x). The EPP floor runs $16.10-30.43, 92-334% under the price, as the window loses FY2012-FY2016's days and gains 2014-2016's
  own lows (2014's 418x among them). Ratio B is infinite (the price above BULL) on 79 dates between 2014-03-07 and 2016-08-26.
- **From the FY2017 10-K** (43 dates): on FY17's $0.26, $81.61-107.58 is 314-414x, the 88th-99th percentile of a window that is now
  FY2008-FY2011 and FY2017-FY2018 (median 211x). The floor is $53.82, 52-100% under the price.
- **The proxy composite** is 1.60 on every print but Q3 FY15 (1.75). Subscription and support growth (+22.5% to +36.9%) and deferred
  revenue growth (+22.8% to +35.4%) sit under their BEAR lines (40% and 43%) on every print. Those lines are rule T over the start-up
  decade; the 2008-2009 findings' second hypothesis is about exactly this.

How far each call moves the classes (the 261 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline with `retro_tool`'s own
`cmd_run`; no outcome consulted):

| Encoding changed | Models changed | Classes moved | Tiers moved |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY2017 excluded by the mirror test (its $154.2M tax benefit read as a one-off against $25.4M of pre-tax income) | 43 | 0 | 0 |
| FY2006 at GAAP $0.24 instead of the company's $0.181 | 156 | 0 | 0 |
| every data signal at its BEAR value | 261 | 0 | 0 |
| every data signal at its XBULL value | 261 | 0 | 0 |

The RICH calls rest on the GAAP multiple of a year's EPS that is small against the price: FY11's, then FY17's. They are read against a
history thinned by five loss years. None of the tested encodings moves a class or a tier. The untested one matters most: the guided
EPS the earnings releases would have supplied.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight, or limit the batch:
- **The reduced data itself:** without the releases, the current year's EPS is the last full year's. A positive guided EPS for FY2017
  or FY2018, if one was given, would have stood instead. That is the largest gap, not tested because it is not in the sheet. Without the
  10-K text, DURABLE and the theme reading are carried from the FY2012 10-K.
- **Fact by fact:**
  - FY2017 at GAAP despite a tax benefit six times its pre-tax income (no class either way);
  - the split dated from the price series' own event;
  - subscription and support derived as total less professional services;
  - Q4 derived as the fiscal year less nine months;
  - the FY18 deferred revenue on current balances only.
- The tag reading of 2015, where the same tag changes meaning, was decided from the figures. An error would show as a broken identity or
  a year-ago mismatch; none occurs.
- The signals, rule T and DURABLE, as in 2008-2012, by a builder who knows how salesforce.com's growth, margins and acquisitions turned
  out after these dates.

The hindsight results for 2013-2017 are in `staging/retrospective/CRM/FINDINGS.md`, computed after the firewall result was pushed:

The owner asked for 2018-2021 ("do 2018-2021"). This branch was still the newest code. `www.sec.gov` was not retried, as no deliverable
contact was available. Sources are `CR61`-`CR76` (the FY2018-FY2021 10-Ks and the Q1 FY19-Q3 FY22 10-Qs). The fact sheet only gains
facts, asserted, and the 523 earlier models rebuild byte for byte.

```bash
python3 retro/build_crm.py --weekly 2018-01-01 2021-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2018-01-05 .. 2021-12-31

         2020-08-28 2020-12-04 2021-03-18 2021-06-02 2021-08-27 2021-12-03 2022-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CRM; done
```

**Same-session disclosure** (the CRM 2010-2012 precedent). This batch was decided in the session that built and scored 2013-2017 and
wrote its findings. Those outcomes' three-year horizons run to 2020-12-29, so the session had seen salesforce.com's price path through
2020 before choosing these encodings, and the FY2018 10-K's XBRL in an exploration output. No 2018-2021 outcome was computed before the
firewall result was pushed. No decision below changes a rule, threshold, signal or window. Each follows the 2013-2017 encodings or an
earlier ticker's, and each that could move a class is tested at the end. Decided before any 2018-2021 outcome was computed:

- **Timing.** Of the 16 filings, 9 were accepted after the close (public the next trading day). 5 were accepted before the open, public
  that day: the FY2019 10-K at 08:04 ET and four 10-Qs at 07:59-08:43 ET. Four of those five are Fridays, the week's last trading day,
  so they meet their own close: 2019-03-08, 2020-08-28, 2020-12-04 and 2021-08-27.
- **Two re-accepted filings.** The EDGAR index lists the Q1 FY21 10-Q (filing date 2020-06-01) and the FY2021 10-K (filing date
  2021-03-17) only by a later re-acceptance, whose time is not theirs.
  - Each is dated from the next trading day after its filing date, 2020-06-02 and 2021-03-18. That is later than or equal to any
    actual dissemination, never earlier.
  - The FY2021 10-K's figures are read from its original accession, which the company facts hold with the same 251 facts.
  - The Q1 FY21 10-Q's are read from the re-accepted accession, the only one the company facts hold. The generator asserts that every
    income-statement figure equals the Q2 FY21 10-Q's six months less its quarter (public 2020-08-28). The Q1 FY22 10-Q's year-ago
    column agrees too.
  - No text names the re-acceptance or its accession. `retro_tool run` caught a first draft that did: its date was after AS_OF on 83
    models, which failed. The text was corrected before any model was kept.
- **ASC 606.** The FY2019 10-K restates FY2017 and FY2018, full retrospective as tagged: FY17 $0.26 to $0.46 (revenues $8.392B to
  $8.437B) and FY18 $0.17 to $0.49 ($10.480B to $10.540B). Each year comes from the latest filing that reports it (the ACN FY19 rule), so
  FY2016 and earlier stay on the earlier basis, a seam (`restated_note`). From Q1 FY19 each 10-Q restates its own year-ago quarter, so
  every print compares like with like within its filing.
- **Unearned revenue replaces deferred revenue** from Q1 FY19: the contract liability, current, the only balance tagged. Q1-Q3 FY19
  compare it with the year-ago quarter's pre-606 deferred revenue as published (a seam, said so in the note). From Q4 FY19 both sides
  are under ASC 606.
- **Subscription and support** is derived only where professional services is tagged in both columns (Q4 FY18, Q1 FY19). From Q2 FY19
  professional services is tagged only in segment detail, which the company facts leave out, so total revenues stand in for the
  signal, and each note says so. The dashboard row keeps the engine's label "Subscription and support growth", as changing it is an
  engine revision (the display quirk above). The franchise line says "not in the company facts".
- **Q4** is the fiscal year less the Q3 10-Q's nine months, as before.
  - The FY2019 and FY2020 10-Ks' tagged quarters agree.
  - The FY2021 10-K tags no quarterly data, so Q4 FY21 is unchecked. Its EPS is derived as the year's net income less the nine months',
    over the year's diluted shares: $0.29, and $(0.29) for the year-ago quarter, against the FY2020 10-K's tagged $(0.28). Display only,
    labelled.
- **One separately stated operating line:** Q2 FY20's $166.0M, the residual of operating expenses less the three lines, has no tag in
  the company facts and is not named. It stays out of the opex signal.
- **History: four more vintages.**
  - FY2018 is $0.17 from the FY2018 10-K, until the FY2019 10-K restates it. FY2019 ($1.43), FY2020 ($0.15) and FY2021 ($4.38) are GAAP.
  - No item is listed as a one-off in the sheet, so every year stays at GAAP (the FY2017 encoding of 2013-2017).
  - FY2021 carries $2,170M of gains on strategic investments and a $1,511M tax benefit, against $455M of operating income. FY2019
    carries $542M of gains but would pass the mirror test even if they were listed. Both are tested below.
  - The decade rolls: FY2008 leaves with the FY2018 vintage, FY2009 with FY2019, FY2010 with FY2020 and FY2011 with FY2021. From
    2021-02-05 FY2011's last days pass the ten years, so the P/E window holds FY2017 on (5.0-5.9 years, ex-FY12 to ex-FY16).
- **Current-FY EPS: the rollover rule,** the last full year with no guide in the sheet:
  - FY17's $0.26 on the 10 dates to 2018-03-09;
  - FY18's $0.17 to 2019-03-01;
  - FY19's $1.43 to 2020-02-28;
  - FY20's $0.15 to 2021-03-12;
  - FY21's $4.38 from 2021-03-19.
  Forward growth is the latest quarter's revenue growth, +19.9% to +34.6%.
- **Display:** debt is the tagged `LongTermDebt`, current and noncurrent. Cash, free cash flow, the tax rate and the single revenue group
  are as in 2013-2017. No dividend and no repurchase in any cash flow statement.
- **Themes.** EV (live 2020-01-01) and CRYPTO (2020-10-21) are scoped to automotive and to payments, banks and exchanges, so they name no
  software business. The watch list stays empty, and DURABLE is carried from the FY2012 10-K as before.
- **Builder change** (`retro/build_crm.py`):
  - EV and CRYPTO join the out-of-scope themes;
  - the franchise line handles a missing subscription growth and says "unearned" after ASC 606;
  - the docstring.
  The 523 earlier models rebuild byte for byte.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):

- **Year and term check:** no 2018-2021 model prints a year after its date, a later accession, or a later product or acquisition name.
- **Regression:** the 523 models of 2008-2017 rebuild byte for byte.
- **Firewall.** It was run after the build, validation outputs and README section were committed and pushed, before any 2018-2021
