### CRM 2022-2026: full data again, the decade's one-off tests, GAAP margin guides, the first dividends, GENAI on the watch list from the FY2025 10-K, the last date 2026-11-20

255 weekly dates, 2022-01-07 to 2026-11-20 (52, 52, 52, 52, 47), on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The owner asked for
2022-2026 ("find newest code. do retrospective analysis for CRM, 2022-2026. same rules as before"). The newest code was the branch with
CRM 2008-2021 (its commit "CRM retrospective: hindsight outcomes and findings for 2018-2021", 2026-11-27), every other retro branch being
its ancestor, and this branch was fast-forwarded to it. The series was built on Friday 2026-11-27 before the close (Yahoo's last bar is
2026-11-25), so the week of 2026-11-23 has no date (the UNH precedent; a rebuild after that day's close adds it). The newest dates have no
outcome yet.

```bash
python3 retro/build_crm.py --weekly 2022-01-03 2026-11-22                   # 255 dates, 2022-01-07 .. 2026-11-20
for d in staging/retrospective/CRM/202[2-6]-*/; do python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"; done
for c in 2022-01-01 2022-03-02 2022-03-11 2022-04-04 2022-06-01 2022-08-25 2022-11-30 2022-12-01 2023-03-02 2023-03-09 2023-06-01 \
         2023-08-31 2023-11-30 2024-02-29 2024-03-07 2024-05-30 2024-08-29 2024-12-04 2025-02-27 2025-03-06 2025-05-29 2025-09-04 \
         2025-12-04 2026-02-26 2026-03-03 2026-05-28 2026-08-27 2026-11-21; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CRM; done
```

**Full data again.** On 2026-11-27 SEC's `www.sec.gov`, which refused the 2013-2021 batches' downloads, served every filing document this
session asked for to a generic client name with no contact address (the owner's email was not used). So this batch reads the filings
themselves, and the reduced reading ends at the range: `reduced_data.full_from` is 2022-01-01. The builder reads a fact marked
`full_data` only on dates from that day; on those dates the reduced-data vintages and prints (CR39-CR76) give way to the full-data ones.
Before it no full-data fact is seen, so the 732 models of 2008-2021 rebuild byte for byte. Redoing 2013-2021 from the filings is now
possible and is left to the owner. The full-data facts current on the first dates were published before the range: the Q3 FY22 release
(2021-11-30) and its guides, the FY2021 10-K (filed 2021-03-17, dated 2021-03-18 as CR73 was: EDGAR now serves the filing's later
re-acceptance, whose XBRL holds the same 555 facts as the original accession; the text is read from that copy, and no text names it), the
Q4 FY21 release and the FY2020 10-K's selected data, read for the decade's one-off tests (below).

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the 23 earnings releases of Q4 FY21 to Q2 FY27 (8-K exhibits 99.1:
the statements of operations, balance sheets and unearned revenue roll-forwards, the headline and guidance sections, the GAAP to non-GAAP
reconciliations, the dividend paragraphs); the FY2020-FY2026 10-Ks (Items 1, 1A and 5 searched for the "why", the competition risk factor,
any cyclical, cloud, offshore, e-commerce, streaming, climate, electric-vehicle, crypto, artificial-intelligence or GLP-1 wording, the
dividend and repurchase passages; the statements of operations, cash flows, balance sheets and revenues by geography; the FY2020 10-K's
selected data and footnotes; the FY2019 10-K searched for the Tax Act note); every other 8-K of 2021-11-30 to 2026-11-20 by its text (33:
the officer, vote, bylaw, debt and acquisition 8-Ks, the investor days of 2022-09-21, 2025-10-15 and 2026-09-16, the restructuring plan
of 2023-01-04, the change of name of 2022-04-04) and the two 8-Ks of 2021-09-23 (a guidance update and an investor day); the Q1 FY26
10-Q's dividends table. **Not read:** the other 10-Qs beyond their XBRL, the proxy statements and annual reports to security holders, the
call transcripts, and the 2025 investor day presentation (exhibit 99.2 of 2025-10-16 is 37 slide images without a text layer; its press
release, exhibit 99.1, states a fiscal 2030 target and no guided number).

The fact sheet's 2022-2026 content is generated by a script (in the session scratchpad, not the repository) from the converted rows. Each
figure is read from its own row by label, and the script asserts every identity a statement carries: revenues as subscription and support
plus professional services; gross profit; operating expenses as R&D, marketing and sales, G&A and every separately stated line;
operating income; pre-tax income as operating income plus every non-operating line (the strategic investments, interest, other); net
income. Each print's unearned revenue roll-forward ends at its balance sheet's figure. Every growth rate, margin and one-off ratio is
computed, not typed, and the 584 quoted strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (584/584). The sources are
`CR77`-`CR108`, each dated from EDGAR's acceptance time (ET): every release was accepted after the close (16:02-16:18 ET) and is public
the next trading day; the FY2022 10-K was accepted at 08:06 ET and is public that day; the change of name at 08:31 ET. The fact sheet
only gains facts (asserted).

Same-session disclosure: none. This batch was built in a new session, which did not open the 2008-2021 outcome files or `FINDINGS.md`
before the firewall result below was pushed. It read this README, including the earlier CRM sections' class counts and the 2018-2021
section's remark that in a full-data reading "the mirror test would then likely exclude" FY2021. Like every builder, it knows
salesforce.com's later history from its training. Decided before any 2022-2026 outcome was computed:

- **Prints are the earnings releases.** Subscription and support is the release's own line again (the reduced batches used total
  revenues from Q2 FY19). Unearned revenue (the current contract liability, the only balance) is read against the year-ago quarter end
  from the release's own roll-forward ("Unearned revenue, end of period"). The opex signal counts R&D, marketing and sales ("Sales and
  marketing" from FY2025) and G&A; restructuring, a separately stated line from Q4 FY23, stays out (the 2008 lease lines' rule). The
  first full-data print is Q2 FY22 (2021-08-26), the previous quarter of Q3 FY22; its own previous quarter comes from the Q1 FY22
  release. The release's sentence on the strategic investments' effect on GAAP EPS is display only.
- **The decade's years under the AAPL FY2002 test and its mirror.** The full-data reading reaches the items the filings list for each
  year of the decade, which the reduced data could not. Each year is read from the latest filing that reports it. A year whose listed
  one-off items fail the test or its mirror, with no figure excluding only them (the non-GAAP figures also remove stock-based
  compensation and amortization, which recur), is excluded and stays a gap (the CRM FY2007 and NKE FY2018 rule):
  - **FY2017 excluded** (the mirror): the FY2020 10-K's selected data list "a benefit related to the partial release of the valuation
    allowance of $612 million, $2 million, $226 million, and $1 million for fiscal 2019, 2018, 2017 and 2016"; FY2017's $226M is more
    than its $323M net income (as adjusted for ASC 606) without it, $97M.
  - **FY2018 kept, $0.49:** its listed items are fractions of $360M (the $2M release; the FY2019 10-K's $126M Tax Act remeasurement
    "offset by a reduction in valuation allowance of $136 million").
  - **FY2019 excluded** (the mirror): the $612M release against $1,110M, $498M without it (reported EPS 2.2 times the EPS without it).
  - **FY2020 excluded** (the test): "a $166 million one-time non-cash charge" (the Salesforce.org reseller agreement) against $126M of
    net income.
  - **FY2021 excluded** (the mirror): the Q4 FY21 release lists "unrealized gains of $1.7 billion" from two strategic investments'
    initial public offerings and "approximately $2.0 billion of one-time benefit from a discrete tax item", against $4,072M. With the
    tax item alone the mirror fails by $66M; both are listed, so both count.
  - **FY2022 excluded** (the mirror): "Mark-to-market accounting of the company’s strategic investments benefited GAAP diluted earnings
    per share by $0.93" of $1.48, $0.55 without it (2.7 times). The strategic investments' gains and losses count as listed items
    wherever a filing states their effect (CRM's own FY2008 investment gain; the GOOG and NVDA readings of equity gains), though the
    company keeps them in its non-GAAP results: tested below.
  - **FY2023 excluded** (the test): "Restructuring impacted fiscal 2023 GAAP and non-GAAP diluted EPS by (83) cents" and $(0.18) of
    investment losses: the $0.21 reported is 0.17 times the $1.22 without them.
  - **FY2024 kept, $4.20** (restructuring $(1.00) and losses $(0.21): 0.78 times); FY2025 $6.36 and FY2026 $7.80 kept (fractions).
  - FY2012-FY2016 stay excluded as losses, with their reduced-data texts (no full-data release of those years was read).
  - So the history is thin: FY2018 alone to 2024-02-23, then FY2018 and FY2024, with FY2025 from 2025-02-28 and FY2026 from 2026-02-27
    (their Q4 prints). The bounds rule applies (BEAR the 0% cap, BULL BASE's rate until FY2024 enters, then the FY2018-FY2024 CAGR of
    +43.1%/yr), and the P/E window is FY2018's days (2017-02-01 to 2018-01-31, 160x-232x) and the current and kept years' days.
- **Current-FY EPS: the GAAP guide midpoint** (the UNH rule, as 2008-2012): FY22 $1.285 (Q3 FY22); FY23 $0.47, $0.39, $0.39, $0.56; FY24
  $2.60, $2.68, $3.51, $3.995; FY25 $6.11, $6.08, $6.09, $6.175; FY26 $6.99, $7.18, $7.01, $7.23; FY27 $7.89, $7.96, $10.23. "Our guidance
  assumes no change to the value of the company's strategic investment portfolio", so gains already booked are in the range, and the
  published figure stands (the ACN FY20 rule). Informatica (closed in November 2025) is in the guides from Q3 FY26: its effect recurs (the
  InStranet rule). The 8-K of 2023-01-04 estimates $800M-1.0B of Q4 FY23 restructuring charges but restates no EPS range, so $0.55-0.57
  stands to the Q4 FY23 print (the last numeric range).
- **Forward revenue growth:** the next-quarter dollar range against the year-ago quarter's revenues from that quarter's own release (the
  level rule), from +24.2% to +24.4% (Q4 FY22) to +6.3% to +6.9% (Q1 FY26) and +11.3% to +12.1% (Q3 FY27).
- **A guided margin step, new for CRM.** From the Q3 FY22 release every release guides the fiscal year's GAAP operating margin (~1.8% for
  FY22; 3.6-3.8% FY23; 10.8-14.5% FY24; 19.7-20.4% FY25; 20.3-21.6% FY26; 20.1-20.9% FY27). The 2008-2021 sheets had none, so the signal
  took the latest quarter's change. Now the guide is a guided step from the last full year's GAAP operating margin (the ACN rule; UNH
  2022-2026), and the margin signal takes the step. The steps are large because the GAAP margins are small: BASE is +48.6%/yr on
  2022-12-02 and +74.3% on 2023-03-03 (10.8% guided on FY23's 3.29%), +8.5% on 2026-11-20. Tested below.
- **Dividends, new:** $0.40 a quarter from the Q4 FY24 release (2024-02-29, the first: "declared a cash dividend of $0.40 per share"),
  $0.416 from the Q1 FY26 10-Q (2025-05-29, the first filing that states the rate) and $0.44 from the Q4 FY26 release (2026-02-26), each
  from the first filing that states it (the NVDA rule). The 10-Ks' dividend words are kept as text.

## SCHW (The Charles Schwab Corporation): the thirty-fourth ticker, in staging, 2008-2009

The SCHW series is built apart from the other thirty-three and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/SCHW.json`), builder (`retro/build_schw.py`, the JPM builder with a securities broker's fields and a same-day print
accepted during the session) and engine (`retro/templates/schw_engine.py.tmpl`, the JPM engine with a broker's signal set and Schwab's own
rule-T thresholds). It is the first securities broker in the retrospectives. The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or
finding of another ticker enters a SCHW model, and no live analysis of Schwab exists in the repository to keep out. Outputs go to
`staging/retrospective/SCHW/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009
("same rules as before"); the code is the newest branch of the repository (its commit "CRM retrospective: README section and CLAUDE.md
for 2018-2021", 2026-11-27), every recent retro branch being its ancestor, and this branch was fast-forwarded to it.

```bash
python3 retro/build_schw.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-12-31                  # 53 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_schw.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31                  # 52 dates, 2009-01-09 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/SCHW/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series SCHW
for c in 2008-01-10 2008-01-16 2008-02-27 2008-04-15 2008-07-16 2008-08-07 2008-10-15 2009-01-16 2009-02-26 2009-04-15 2009-07-16 \
         2009-10-15 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c SCHW; done
```

**A full-data batch.** SEC's `www.sec.gov`, which serves the filing documents and refused this session's predecessor (CRM 2013-2017, the
same day), accepted a plain client name with no contact address in the `User-Agent` this time; no personal or guessed address was sent.
So every filing below was downloaded and read as a document, as for the tickers before CRM 2013.

What was read, and how (by the session's model directly, with no delegated transcription). The filing list is EDGAR's for CIK 316709
(acceptance times in UTC, converted to ET; no filing accepted after 2009-12-31 was opened). Read: the selected financial and operating
data of the FY2000-FY2008 10-Ks (the annual report, exhibit 13, for FY2000-FY2003), their MD&A overview tables of client activity
metrics (FY2004 on), the FY2002 10-K's reconciliation of adjusted operating income, the FY2005-FY2008 10-Ks' restructuring and
statement-of-income rows, and Items 1, 1A and 5 of the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks searched for the "why", the listing, the dividend sentence and
any cyclical label; every earnings release of Q4 2006 to Q3 2009 (8-K exhibits 99.1: the narrative in full, the statements of income,
the financial and operating highlights, the growth in client assets and accounts and the monthly activity report); all 41 8-Ks of
October 2006 to December 2009 by their item text (exhibits of the debt, trust-preferred and bylaw 8-Ks not opened); the 10-Qs of Q3 2006
to Q3 2009, compared by script with their releases on the five rows the signals use (every one matches) and searched for dividend
sentences. **Not read:** the FY1996-FY1999 10-Ks (downloaded; rule T takes each pair of years from the latest 10-K that reports both, all
FY2000 or later), the proxy statements, the 10-Qs' and 10-Ks' text outside the rows and sentences named here, and any investor
presentation or business update the company did not file. The Q4 2007 release says "Schwab’s financial objectives for 2007 included
revenue growth of at least 12% and pre-tax profit margin expansion of about 200 basis points, to 36%": objectives set somewhere not filed,
so a 2008 or 2009 objective stated only there would be missed. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows:
each figure is read from its own row by label inside its own table (the row is kept), every growth rate, margin, gap and rule-T value is
computed, every quoted sentence is asserted present in its own filing, and the 217 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their
own filings (217/217). The source ids are `SCHW1`-`SCHW23`. Decided on 2026-11-27, before any SCHW model was built or any SCHW outcome
computed (Yahoo was asked for its series metadata, splits and dividends):

- **The company and the listing.** The Charles Schwab Corporation (CSC) on every date: "CSC’s common stock is listed on The Nasdaq Stock
  Market under the ticker symbol SCHW." (Item 5 of the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks). The models print Nasdaq: SCHW (Yahoo's metadata names
  today's exchange and is not used).
- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's SCHW splits (the last, three-for-two, on 2000-05-31) precede the P/E window, so the close is the price as
  traded ($23.95 on 2008-01-04, $18.82 on 2009-12-31). The special dividend of $1.00 a share (paid 2007-08-24, record 2007-07-24) is a
  distribution, not a split; Yahoo's closes are not adjusted for it, so the window's 2007 days are priced as traded (the SO and SPGI
  `distributions` reading; the 2007 days before it trade with the dividend in the price).
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year ("Results for the years ended December 31, 2006, 2005, and 2004", FY2006 10-K).
- **Release timing.** The Q4 2006 and Q1 2007 earnings 8-Ks were accepted after the close (16:18 and 16:38 ET) and are dated the next
  trading day (2007-01-18, 2007-04-18); every later one was accepted during the session (14:17-15:56 ET) and keeps its day: 2007-07-17,
  2007-10-15, 2008-01-16, 2008-04-15, 2008-07-16, 2008-10-15, 2009-01-16, 2009-04-15, 2009-07-16, 2009-10-15. No filing states the
  release time. The weekly date is the next trading day, except the Q4 2008 print, released on Friday 2009-01-16, the week's last trading
  day: that day is the week's date and meets its close, public before it by its 8-K's acceptance at 14:59 ET (the UNP Good Friday 2014
  and SHW 2011 rule; the JPM builder accepted a same-day print only "before the open", so `build_schw.py` also accepts one "during market
  hours" and tags the date "released during the session"). The FY2006, FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks were accepted after the close
  (2007-02-26 16:33, 2008-02-26 19:50, 2009-02-25 16:15 ET) and are dated 2007-02-27, 2008-02-27 and 2009-02-26. A Q4 print extends the
  history from its release to the 10-K: FY2007 from 2008-01-16 (6 dates), FY2008 from 2009-01-16 (6 dates).
- **Revenue: net revenues** as the statement of income totals them (asset management and administration fees, net interest revenue,
  trading revenue and other; interest expense is netted), continuing operations, each year from the latest filing that reports it. U.S.
  Trust is discontinued from the FY2006 10-K (agreement with Bank of America of November 19, 2006; the sale closed on July 1, 2007, a
  fact the models carry only from the FY2007 10-K); the earlier 10-Ks' figures include it, and their pairs of years feed rule T as
  published (a seam). Nothing is made pro forma.
- **EPS: diluted EPS from continuing operations,** GAAP, each year from the latest filing that reports it: FY03 $0.29, FY04 $0.26, FY05
  $0.48, FY06 $0.69 (FY2006 10-K), FY07 $0.92 (Q4 2007 release, then the FY2007 10-K), FY08 $1.06 (Q4 2008 release, then the FY2008 10-K;
  FY03 from the FY2007 10-K, whose selected data still reaches it).
  - **FY2002 is excluded, a distorted year** (the AAPL FY2002 test). The FY2002 10-K excludes from its adjusted operating income $373M of
    restructuring charges, $61M of goodwill and other impairment charges and $27M of merger- and acquisition-related charges, less a $22M
    extraordinary gain: $287M after tax, more than the year's $117M income from continuing operations as the FY2006 10-K restates it
    ($0.09 a share). The adjusted figure is in dollars, on the earlier basis (U.S. Trust in) and with no per-share figure, so no filing
    excludes the items on the continuing-operations basis (the JPM FY2002 reading). FY2002 is not the latest year, so it takes the years
    before it: the history and the P/E window start with FY2003 (`pe_window_start` 2003-01-01): a 5.0-year window on 2008-01-04, 7.0
    years at the end of 2009. FY2001 ($0.05, with $208M of excluded items after tax) precedes it.
  - **No year from FY2003 meets the test:** FY2004's $186M of restructuring charges before tax, the largest, against $350M of income from
    continuing operations; FY2003's $76M (FY2005 10-K) against $402M.
  - **No company figure excluding one-offs.** No release or 10-K of the period prints an EPS without an item. The Q3 2008 release says
    the quarter's "EPS from continuing operations of $.26, ... includes $.04 of previously disclosed charges" ($73M before tax on two
    corporate debt securities, estimated in the 7.01 8-K of 2008-09-29), with no figure without them, so FY08 stays at $1.06 (the ACN rule
    for a one-off with no published figure without it); the severance, expense-reduction and FDIC charges of Q4 2008 to Q2 2009 and the
    Q1 2009 debt repurchase gain stay in their quarters, as published.
  - **The two recast 8-Ks add nothing.** The 8-K of 2007-07-17 recasts the FY2006 10-K's segments (Schwab Corporate and Retirement
    Services split out); the 8-K of 2009-06-01 recasts the FY2008 10-K for a segment change and FSP EITF 03-6-1, which "did not change any
    of the previously reported EPS data ... except for the years ended December 31, 2007 and 2006", and only their net-income EPS. Their
    net revenues, continuing-operations EPS and diluted shares equal the 10-Ks' (asserted), so neither is a vintage of its own.
  - **No EPS guide in any filing**, so the last full year stands (the rollover rule): FY06's $0.69 to the Q4 2007 print (2008-01-04 and
    2008-01-11), FY07's $0.92 (2008-01-17 to 2009-01-09), FY08's $1.06 (from 2009-01-16).
- **Diluted shares,** each year from the latest filing that reports it (1,364M in FY2003 to 1,157M in FY2008). The buyback term is the
  history's net repurchase: +2.0%/yr (FY2003-FY2006), +2.8%/yr (to FY2007, the tender offer of 2007 in), +3.4%/yr (to FY2008).
- **No guide in any filing.** No release, 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K of the period gives revenue, EPS or a margin in numbers. The Q4 2008
  release's "current expectation of identifying and implementing cuts totaling 7 to 8% of our 2008 total spending" (restated "on track" in
  the Q2 2009 release) is a cost component, not a revenue or margin guide: method r2 has no input for it, and nothing is derived from it
  (the JPM and MSFT segment reading); it is quoted in the print notes and the guide line. BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth plus
  the buyback term (the UNP rule), and there is no margin step. The builder refuses any guide, event, listing, split or company name until
  an encoding is decided.
- **Dividends,** the latest declared quarterly rate, each from the first filing that states it: $0.05 from the Q3 2006 10-Q (2006-11-06:
  "On October 19, 2006, the Board of Directors increased the quarterly cash dividend from $.03 to $.05 per share"; $0.20 a year to
  2008-08-01), $0.06 from the Q2 2008 10-Q (2008-08-07: "on July 22, 2008, the Board of Directors increased the quarterly cash dividend
  from $.05 per share to $.06 per share"; $0.24 a year from 2008-08-08). The 2007 special dividend is not a rate.
- **Signals.** A securities broker has no gross margin, inventories or loan book worth the JPM credit slots, so the set is its own,
  taken from the key metrics the FY2006 10-K's MD&A overview names (net new client assets, client assets, daily average revenue trades,
  net revenue growth, pre-tax profit margin, return on equity, net revenue per employee), with the expense gap of the earlier sets and
  ACN's weights: net revenue growth (0.20), client assets growth (0.20, the quarter end against the year-ago quarter end: "growth in
  certain components of client assets ... directly impacts asset management and administration fee revenues"), growth of expenses
  excluding interest less revenue growth (0.15, lower is better), daily average revenue trades growth (0.15, "the most prominent driver of
  trading revenues") and the change in the pre-tax margin (0.15: income from continuing operations before taxes on income over net
  revenues), plus the theme slot at 2/4. Each value is the release's own against the year-ago quarter in the same release (its five-quarter
  highlights and client assets tables). Net new client assets, return on equity and revenue per employee are displayed or left out, not
  scored: no weight was added to the six.
- **Thresholds by rule T over the decade of the FY2006 10-K** (the vintage public on 2008-01-04; 1997-2006): each change from the latest
  10-K published by 2008-01-04 that reports both years (the FY2000 10-K for 1996-1997, FY2001 for 1997-1998, FY2002 for 1998-1999, FY2003
  for 1999-2000 and the 2000-2002 trades, FY2004 for 2000-2001 and the 2002-2003 trades, FY2005 for 2001-2002, the 2002-2004 client
  assets and the 2003-2004 trades, FY2006 for the rest). Ten values each. Seams stay in, as published: the FY2000-FY2005 figures include
  U.S. Trust (pooled from its 2000 merger), the FY2003-FY2005 10-Ks exclude Charles Schwab Europe and the FY2004-FY2005 ones Schwab
  SoundView Capital Markets as discontinued, "Revenues" becomes "Net revenues" from the FY2006 10-K, and the pre-tax margin is the ratio
  each 10-K prints to a decimal (its income before taxes is not in the selected data). The raw figures and values are in the fact sheet
  (`rule_t`); the builder re-derives every value and threshold and refuses to build if they differ.

  |---|---|---|
  | net revenue growth | 22.91, 18.94, 41.16, 29.28, -21.75, -3.05, -0.79, 4.56, 5.94, 19.07 % | -56 / -22 / 12 / 41 % |
  | client assets growth | 34.90, 35.93, 42.35, 3.04, -2.96, -9.59, 26.40, 11.84, 11.84, 17.63 % | -34 / -10 / 15 / 42 % |
  | expense growth less revenue | 2.30, -2.17, -5.68, 5.37, 15.97, -3.19, -13.99, 4.11, -15.60, -9.77 pp | 35 / 16 / -3 / -16 pp |
  | daily average revenue trades growth | 32.96, 35.38, 67.80, 48.38, -34.01, -16.03, 5.00, 11.08, 26.53, 18.44 % | -91 / -34 / 22 / 68 % |
  | pre-tax margin change | -140, 140, 320, -330, -1640, 320, 1330, -320, 1240, 590 bp | -3510 / -1640 / 230 / 1330 bp |

- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2.** The 10-Ks tie results to markets, rates and investor engagement ("Developments in the business,
  economic, and geopolitical environment could negatively impact the Company’s business.", FY2006-FY2008) and name price competition
  ("There has been aggressive price competition in the Company’s industry, which may continue in the future.", FY2006; "The Company’s
  industry is characterized by aggressive price competition.", FY2007 and FY2008), but none contains the word "cyclical" (asserted). That
  is a cycle and a competitive field in the "why", not the company's own label (the JPM, LOW and SHW reading). No theme in
  `taxonomy_eras.json` is live for a securities broker and bank on these dates (OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services; CRYPTO, the one theme
  whose scope names banks and exchanges, is not live before 2020-10-21), so the watch list is empty. The kind changes the class label
  only.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the vintage's net revenues by component (asset management and administration fees,
  net interest revenue, trading revenue, other), the total from the last year's revenue grown at the BASE revenue rate; the EPS check runs

- **Firewall** (run after the build, validation outputs and README section were committed and pushed, before any outcome): it passes at

  changed and no planted text, on its first run. The planted facts include a print with absurd net revenues, client assets, trades, net

  2008 release) stops at the builder's check that every source is public on AS_OF.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned). Schwab's history from FY2003 is one of rising EPS ($0.29 to $1.06, one down year), so
BULL and XBULL are steep and BEAR shallow, and the rules read each date against a 5-7-year window whose 10th to 90th percentiles span 17x-42x:
- **CHEAP on all 105 dates; legacy tier BUY on all 105.** Robustness 8 of 8 (BUY in every variant) on 103 dates and 7 of 8 on 2008-01-04 and 2008-01-11 (ACCUMULATE with multiples one band cheaper, Ratio B 0.96 and 0.75); the robustness block shows no other class on any date.
- **January 2008 rests on FY06's $0.69** (no EPS guide; the Q4 2007 print comes on 2008-01-16): $22.55-23.95 is 32.7-34.7x, the
  62nd-69th percentile of a 5.0-year window whose median is 29.6-29.7x, 36-45% above an EPP floor of 24x ($16.56). BASE is +23.1%/yr
  (Q3 2007's +21.1% revenue growth and a +2.0%/yr buyback), BULL the FY2003-FY2006 CAGR (+33.5%/yr), XBULL the FY2004-FY2006 run
  (+62.9%/yr) and BEAR FY2003 to FY2004 (-10.3%), so Ratio B is 0.45-0.55.
- **From the Q4 2007 print to the Q4 2008 print FY07's $0.92 carries the call** (52 dates): $15.14-25.25 is 16.5-27.4x, the 0th-57th
  percentile (median 25.4-26.8x), against floors of 21x and then 20x ($19.32, $18.40) as 2008's own low falls; the price is under the
  floor on 12 dates (2008-03-28, 2008-04-11, then 2008-10-24 to 2009-01-09, the deepest -17.7% on 2008-12-19). BASE follows the quarters
  down: +25.5%/yr (Q4 2007's +22.7%), +16.2% (Q1 2008), +11.3% (Q2 2008), -0.3% (Q3 2008's -3.1%), each with a +2.8%/yr buyback.
- **2009 rests on FY08's $1.06** (51 dates): $11.36-19.49 is 10.7-18.4x, the 0th-17th percentile of a 6-7-year window whose median is
  23.8-24.9x, 8-46% under a floor of 20x ($21.20) on every date; the low of the series, $11.36 on 2009-03-06, is 10.7x. BASE is -1.1%/yr
  (Q4 2008), -11.7% (Q1 2009), -13.7% (Q2) and -15.9% (Q3 2009's -19.2% revenue growth), BULL the FY2003-FY2008 CAGR (+29.6%/yr), BEAR
  still -10.3%; Ratio B is negative (the price under the BEAR case) on 13 dates, 2008-12-19 to 2009-03-27.
- **The growth factor** is +0.50 to the Q4 2007 print (+21.1% and +22.7% against a 5.9% median revenue growth), +0.25 and -0.24 on the
  Q1 and Q2 2008 prints and -0.50 from the Q3 2008 print on. **The proxy composite** falls from 2.85 (Q3 and Q4 2007: all five data
  signals at BULL) to 2.50, 2.30 and 2.00 on the Q1-Q3 2008 prints (every data signal at BASE by Q3 2008), 1.95 on Q4 2008 (client
  assets -21.3% at BEAR, trades +30.1% at BULL), 1.80 on Q1 and Q2 2009 (client assets at BEAR) and 2.00 on Q3 2009.

How far each call moves the classes (the 105 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed and classified offline with `retro_tool`'s own

The CHEAP calls rest on Schwab's 2008-2009 multiple of its last full year's GAAP EPS against its own 2003-2009 P/E history and

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows that Schwab's revenues fell in 2009 with rates and markets while its trades held up: the
  five come from the company's own list of key metrics, but which three of that list are scored (client assets and trades, not net new

- the expense goal left unencoded, and FY08 at GAAP with the Q3 charges in (no class either way);
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL (label only);
- the parts of the filings listed above as not read, and above all any unfiled financial objectives for 2008 or 2009.

### SCHW 2010-2013: four more vintages, the NYSE listing, Q1 2010 restated twice, the YieldPlus charges at GAAP, outlooks in bounds and words

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31, on the same method, engine and rule-T thresholds. The owner asked for 2010-2013 ("do
2010-2013"). This branch was still the newest code once the two commits that the CRM branch gained after it (CRM 2018-2021's firewall
result and findings) were merged in. `www.sec.gov` again accepted a plain client name, so this is a full-data batch. Sources are
`SCHW24`-`SCHW45`. The fact sheet only gains facts (a second generator loads it and asserts every earlier source, vintage, print, rule-T
value and dividend unchanged), and the 105 earlier models rebuild byte for byte.

```bash
python3 retro/build_schw.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2013-12-31                  # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/SCHW/201[0-3]-*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series SCHW
for c in 2010-01-04 2010-01-20 2010-02-25 2010-03-05 2010-04-15 2010-04-20 2010-05-07 2010-07-16 2010-10-15 2011-01-18 2011-02-25 \
         2011-04-18 2011-07-18 2011-10-18 2012-01-18 2012-02-24 2012-04-16 2012-07-17 2012-10-15 2013-01-16 2013-02-25 2013-04-15 \
         2013-07-16 2013-10-16 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c SCHW; done
```

**Same-session disclosure** (the CRM 2010-2012 precedent). This batch was decided in the session that built and scored 2008-2009 and wrote
its findings. Those outcomes' three-year horizons run to 2012-12-31, so the session had seen Schwab's price path through 2012, and the
findings quote FY2009's $0.68 and FY2010's $0.38 from the Q4 2009 and Q4 2010 releases, before choosing these encodings. No 2010-2013
outcome was computed before the firewall result was pushed. No decision below changes a rule, threshold, signal or window. Each follows the
2008-2009 encodings or an earlier ticker's, and each that could move a class is tested at the end.

What was read (by the session's model directly, no delegated transcription; no filing accepted after 2013-12-31 opened): the FY2009-FY2012
10-Ks (selected financial and operating data, the MD&A overview's client activity metrics, the statements of income, Items 1, 1A and 5,
searched for "cyclical", "cloud" and "offshore", none found); every earnings release of Q4 2009 to Q3 2013 in full (narrative, statements
of income, highlights, the reconciliations of figures excluding certain items, client assets and the monthly activity report); all 51 8-Ks
and 8-K/As of 2010-2013 by their item text; the 10-Qs of Q1 2010 to Q3 2013, compared by script with their releases on the five signal
rows (every one matches but Q1 2010, below), and the 10-Q/A of 2010-08-13 (exhibit 101 only). **Not read:** the proxy statements, the
exhibits of the debt, preferred and merger 8-Ks beyond their item text, and every presentation and press release the company did not
file: the Q4 2009 release says its results are "consistent with the outlook expressed in the company’s press release dated December 14,
2009", and the Q1 2013 release the same of a press release of March 14, 2013. Neither was filed, so their outlooks are unused (the CRM
rule for unfiled guidance) and a guide stated only there is missed. The 234 strings of this batch were checked with `verbatim.py`
against their own filings (234/234). Decided on 2026-11-27, before any 2010-2013 model was built or outcome computed:

- **The listing moves to the NYSE.** "On February 22, 2010, CSC announced that it is transferring the listing of its common stock to the
  New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). CSC expects its common stock to begin trading on the NYSE on March 5, 2010, using its current symbol."
  (FY2009 10-K, accepted 2010-02-25 14:43 ET; the announcement itself was not filed). `listings` takes the PEP encoding: the new exchange
  from its stated effective date once the filing is public. Nasdaq: SCHW to 2010-02-26, NYSE: SCHW from 2010-03-05; the FY2010-FY2012
  10-Ks' Item 5 says "listed on The New York Stock Exchange". Label only.
- **Release timing.** The Q4 2009, Q1 2011, Q3 2011 and Q3 2013 earnings 8-Ks were accepted after the close (16:35, 17:10, 16:02 and 16:20
  ET) and are dated the next trading day (2010-01-20, 2011-04-18, 2011-10-18, 2013-10-16); the others during the session (12:39-15:55
  ET). Two Friday prints date their own weeks and meet their own closes, "released during the session": Q2 2010 (2010-07-16, 15:55 ET)
  and Q3 2010 (2010-10-15, 15:32 ET). The FY2009, FY2010 and FY2011 10-Ks were accepted during the session and keep their days
  (2010-02-25, 2011-02-25, 2012-02-24); the FY2012 10-K after the close (2013-02-22 16:58 ET), so it is dated 2013-02-25.
- **History: four vintages,** each year from the latest filing that reports it, the ten fiscal years to the latest one (FY2003-FY2012 at
  the end; FY2002 stays excluded and the window still starts 2003-01-01, reaching ten years in November 2012). GAAP diluted EPS: FY09
  $0.68, FY10 $0.38, FY11 $0.70, FY12 $0.69 (per common share, after the preferred dividends that start in 2012). Every year a later 10-K
  reports equals the earlier vintage's figure (asserted). FY2009's 10-K moves the provision for loan losses into net revenues and
  restates net interest revenue; total net revenues are unchanged, and the segment bridge's "other" becomes the residual (the provision
  and the net impairment losses on securities in), display only.
- **EPS: GAAP, the YieldPlus and other charges in.** From Q3 2010 the releases reconcile "Net Income Excluding Certain Charges" (FY2010
  $775M against $454M reported: $482M of class action and regulatory reserves, money market mutual fund charges and credit card program
  costs, $321M after tax), and from Q4 2011 "Net Income Excluding Certain Items" (optionsXpress, the vendor-dispute gain), always in
  dollars and never per share. So no filing publishes an EPS without them, and FY10 stays $0.38 (the ACN rule needs a company figure; the
  CB 2010-2013 reading of a net-income-only figure). FY2010 does not meet the AAPL test either: its listed charges after tax ($321M) are
  under its $454M net income ($0.38 is 59% of the year without them). This is the batch's largest call (below).
- **Q1 2010 is restated twice** (the JPM Q1 2012 encoding, `restated`, each from its own filing): the release (2010-04-15) prints
  expenses of $780M and pre-tax income of $198M; the 8-K of 2010-04-20 (accepted 15:04 ET) says the company "has increased the contingency
  reserve ... by $172 million pre-tax", so from that day the quarter carries $952M and $26M (EPS about $0.01, the release's $0.10 less the
  8-K's "approximately ... $0.09"); the Q1 2010 10-Q (2010-05-07, 12:46 ET) reports $965M and $13M with "a reserve of $196 million"
  (EPS $0.00). The builder now takes `restated` (the JPM `as_restated`), re-deriving every restated value from its raw figures.
- **No guide in a range or a level, so the rules are unchanged:** the last full year's EPS stands, BASE is the latest quarter's revenue
  growth plus the net share change, and there is no margin step. Two releases give an outlook for the current year in bounds and words,
  text only (`outlook_words` on the print, shown in the guide line and the third catalyst while its year is current):
  - Q1 2010: "the company should achieve revenue growth at least in the low single digits, limit expense growth to about 4%, and deliver
    a pre-tax profit margin of at least 25%": one-sided bounds and a cost component (the UNH `eps_bound` and SPGI rules), no field;
  - Q3 2013: "we expect our 2013 revenue growth will outpace expenses by approximately 100 to 200 basis points, helping us to achieve a
    pre-tax profit margin of at least 30% and earnings per share in the mid-$.70s for the year", and a 2014 aim of "a gap of
    approximately 300 to 500 basis points between revenue and expense growth": "mid-$.70s" is words, not a range or a level (the SPGI
    "high single-digit" rule; the EPS label says so), "at least 30%" a bound, the gaps components. The other releases' outlook sentences
    are words ("our expectations for the company’s 2010 financial performance have not changed", "about where we’d expect to be").
- **The 2009 expense goal** stays in the guide line only while 2009 is the current year (a text condition that changes no 2008-2009 model).
- **Acquisitions and capital as published:** the January 2010 offering of 26.3M shares, Windward (2010), optionsXpress (merged
  2011-09-01 for 1.02 Schwab shares each, in revenue, trades and shares from Q3 2011), ThomasPartners (2013), the Series A and B preferred
  stock (2012). The net share term turns to issuance: +1.9%/yr to FY2010, +1.3% to FY2011, +0.75% to FY2012.
- **Client assets as published:** from Q3 2013 the total is cut by $24.7B for "the consolidation of its retirement plan recordkeeping
  platforms" while the year-ago total is not (a seam in that signal, noted on the print).
- **Dividends:** $0.06 a quarter on every date (each release's "Dividends declared per common share"; no new rate in 2010-2013).
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2,** the same reading of the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks, which repeat the market-environment and price-competition
  headings and never use "cyclical". From 2012-11-02, the first weekly date on or after CLOUD's live date (2012-10-30), the "why" quotes
  every live theme's registered scope (the CB 2014-2017 and UNH wording): OFFSHORE's and CLOUD's name no brokerage or bank, and no 10-K
  names cloud or offshore delivery, so the watch list stays empty.
- **Adds nothing:** the 8-Ks on the YieldPlus class action and regulatory settlements (2010-10-15, 2010-11-08, 2010-11-30, 2011-01-14;
  their charges reach the prints), the replacement capital covenant termination, the optionsXpress merger agreement and completion, the
  common, preferred and debt offerings, the debt exchange, the trust preferred redemption, the segment recast of the FY2012 10-K (8-K of
  2013-06-24; net revenues unchanged, asserted), the officer, director and bylaw 8-Ks.

Decided on 2026-11-27, before any 2022-2026 model was built or outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q4 2021 to Q3 2026 was accepted after the close (16:16-16:47 ET) and is dated the next trading
  day. From the Q1 2023 release the text says the company "will host its Spring Business Update for institutional investors this morning
  from 8:00 a.m. - 9:00 a.m. CT, 9:00 a.m. - 10:00 a.m. ET" (8:30 a.m. ET from Q2 2023), so the release went out before the open of its
  dateline day, hours before its 8-K. The 8-K is the dated filing and its acceptance governs, as for AVGO's Q3 FY11 release (issued after
  the close, its 8-K the next morning) and in every earlier SCHW batch (`release_time` says so on each print; the release-morning dating is
  tested below). Three prints land on a Friday, the week's last trading day, and meet that Friday's close as public before its open (the
  AVGO and CRM rule): Q3 2025 (2025-10-17), Q1 2026 (2026-04-17) and Q3 2026 (2026-10-16). Q1 2025 was accepted on Thursday 2025-04-17
  before Good Friday and Q2 2025 on Friday 2025-07-18, both dated the Monday. The FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks were accepted after the close (dated
  2022-02-25, 2023-02-27, 2024-02-26, 2025-02-27, 2026-02-26).
- **History: five vintages from three-year statements.** Item 6 is "Reserved" in every 10-K of the range, so each vintage takes its three
  years (EPS and net revenues from the MD&A overview, asserted equal to the statements of income; diluted shares from the statements) and
  keeps earlier years from the latest earlier vintage (the JPM 2022-2026 reading), the ten fiscal years to the latest one (FY2012-FY2021 to
  FY2016-FY2025). GAAP diluted EPS per common share: FY21 $2.83, FY22 $3.50, FY23 $2.54, FY24 $2.99, FY25 $4.65. Every year a later 10-K
  reports equals the earlier vintage's figure (asserted: no restatement), and each Q4 print's year equals its 10-K's. Between a Q4 print and
  its 10-K the history holds eleven years. The components ("Other" now bank deposit account fees and other revenue) are each 10-K's.
- **EPS: GAAP every year.** The releases' adjusted diluted EPS excludes the acquisition and integration-related costs, from Q3 2023 the
  restructuring costs ("Beginning in the third quarter of 2023, these adjustments also include restructuring costs ..."), and every quarter
  the amortization of acquired intangible assets, which "will continue in future periods over their remaining useful lives": a recurring
  item, so the adjusted figure is not one excluding only one-offs (the NKE FY2007, AVGO, PFE, V and CB rule, as in 2020-2021), and no filing
  publishes an EPS without only the one-offs. In FY2025 the adjustment is the amortization alone ($4.87 against GAAP $4.65). No year meets
  the AAPL FY2002 test (each vintage's normalization states it from the Q4 release's reconciliation): FY2023, the nearest, has $401M of
  acquisition and integration-related costs and $495M of restructuring costs before tax against $5,067M of net income. Stay in as
  published: the Q1 2023 "$97 million one-time breakage fee" in bank deposit account revenue and the Q4 2023 "$172 million FDIC special
  assessment" (in the company's adjusted expenses too). FY2023's $2.54 (-27.4%) is the batch's largest EPS call (below).

  quarter's revenue growth plus the net share change, and there is no margin step. The 2023 run-rate savings and exit-cost ranges are a cost
  component (unencoded); the Forge Global announcement's investor presentation is no guide for Schwab's year (the AVGO and UNP merger rule).
- **Acquisitions and capital as published:** Forge Global (closed 2026-03-02, its 8-K) is in the figures from the Q1 2026 release, noted on

- **Dividends,** each rate from the first filing that states it: $0.20 a quarter from the FY2021 10-K (2022-02-25, declared January 26,

- the company's adjusted EPS for FY2021-FY2025 (FY21 $3.25, FY22 $3.90, FY23 $3.13, FY24 $3.25, FY25 $4.87; it also removes the recurring
  amortization): 69 classes (43 RICH to FAIR, 16 FAIR to CHEAP, 7 RICH to CHEAP, 3 CHEAP to FAIR), 118 tiers: the batch's largest call;
- FY2023 at $2.91 without only the restructuring and integration costs (derived: $2.54 plus $.22 and $.27 less their share of the stated
  $(.19) tax effects; no filing prints it): 22 classes (18 RICH to FAIR), 47 tiers;
- no net share change in BASE: 22 classes, 17 tiers;
- each print from Q1 2023 dated its release morning instead of the 8-K's next day: 1 class, no tier;
- the three Friday prints from the next trading day: no class, no tier;
- CRYPTO off the watch list: no class, no tier; DATs as the trades signal instead of n/r: no class, no tier;
- every data signal at its BEAR value: 109 classes (67 CHEAP to RICH, 37 FAIR to RICH, 5 CHEAP to FAIR), no tier; at its XBULL value:
  31 classes (19 RICH to FAIR, 11 FAIR to CHEAP, 1 RICH to CHEAP), no tier.
The 2023 and 2026 CHEAP calls rest on Schwab's multiple of its last full year's GAAP EPS falling under its own ten-year median; the 2024-2025
RICH calls rest on FY2023's GAAP $2.54, which carries the restructuring and integration costs and the FDIC assessment (the GAAP rule) and
falls 27% as client cash moved to higher-yielding products.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- GAAP throughout, the adjusted EPS left out for its recurring amortization (69 classes), FY2023 with its restructuring costs (22 classes);
- the 8-K's acceptance, not the release's "this morning" business update, dating each print from Q1 2023 (1 class);
- the unfiled business-update outlooks and CFO commentary unused, the cost-savings targets and the Forge Global presentation read as no guide;
- CRYPTO on the watch list from the FY2025 10-K and GENAI and CLOUD out of scope (text only), DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL (label only);
- the last date set by the build time (2026-11-20), and the parts of the filings listed above as not read.

The hindsight results for 2022-2026 are in `staging/retrospective/SCHW/FINDINGS.md`, computed after the firewall result was pushed:

## NEE (FPL Group): the thirty-fifth ticker, in staging, 2008-2009

The NEE series is built apart from the other thirty-four and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/NEE.json`), builder (`retro/build_nee.py`, the SO builder with UNP's split encoding and SPGI's listed symbol) and engine
(`retro/templates/nee_engine.py.tmpl`, the SO engine with FPL Group's own lines and rule-T thresholds). It is the second electric utility in
the retrospectives. The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an NEE model. Today's NEE profile
in `data/business_profiles.json` and the live `nee_signal_model.py` (another branch) are 2026 analyses; neither was opened for this series
and neither is an input (only `retro_tool outcome` reads the profile, for the hindsight `profile_drift` label). Outputs go to
`staging/retrospective/NEE/`, beside the others, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009
("find newest code. do retrospective analysis for NEE, 2008-2009. same rules as before"). The code is the newest branch of the repository:
its commit "CRM retrospective: README section and CLAUDE.md for 2018-2021" (2026-11-27), every other retro branch being its ancestor; this
branch was fast-forwarded to it.

```bash
python3 retro/build_nee.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2009-12-31                   # 105 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/NEE/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series NEE
for c in 2008-01-11 2008-01-28 2008-02-28 2008-04-30 2008-07-31 2008-10-27 2009-01-27 2009-02-17 2009-02-27 2009-04-28 2009-07-28 \
         2009-10-27 2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c NEE; done
```

**A full-data batch.** SEC's `www.sec.gov` served every filing document to this session with a plain client name in the `User-Agent`
(no contact address), unlike the session of "CRM 2013-2017" earlier the same day, so nothing here is reduced.

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the ten earnings releases of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 (8-K exhibits 99:
the segment statements of income for the quarter, the year-ago quarter and the year to date, the reconciliations to adjusted earnings, the
Florida Power & Light statistics and the outlook paragraphs); the selected financial data, consolidated statements of income and cash flows,
segment note, Items 1, 1A and 5 of the FY1998-FY2008 10-Ks (FY1998-FY2000 as plain text), and the FY2000 10-K/A of 2001-04-09, which re-files
that 10-K in full with the same figures (the rows used are asserted present in both); the FY2005 10-K/A (Part III only: nothing used); and every
8-K of October 2006 to February 2010 by its items and text (the Item 7.01 8-Ks restate or revise the adjusted EPS expectations; the rest are
financing, officer, bylaw, dividend and rate-case filings). **Not read:** the 10-Qs beyond their listing, the proxy statements, and the investor
presentations and call transcripts the releases point to (not filed). The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted
rows: each figure is read from its own row by label under an anchored heading, the segment columns are asserted to sum to FPL Group's total,
every growth rate, margin, margin change and rule-T value is computed, not typed, and every quoted sentence is asserted present in its own
filing; the 407 strings were checked with `verbatim.py` against their own filings (407/407). Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance
time (UTC, converted to ET; before 2003 EDGAR records the filing date only); the source ids are `NE1`-`NE31`. Decided on 2026-11-27, before
any NEE model was built or any NEE outcome computed (Yahoo was asked for its series metadata and splits, and for the first date's close to
check the share basis):

- **The company and its listing.** FPL Group, Inc., NYSE: FPL, on every date ("FPL Group, Inc. (NYSE: FPL)", every release of the range);
  it became NextEra Energy, Inc. in 2010. NEE is the series key and the symbol under which Yahoo serves the history; every printed line names
  the listing of the date (`LISTED_SYMBOL = "FPL"`, the SPGI and BKR encoding). FPL Energy, LLC was renamed NextEra Energy Resources, LLC on
  2009-01-07 (its 8-K); the models name the competitive segment as each release does: FPL Energy to the Q3 2008 release, NextEra Energy
  Resources from the Q4 2008 release (2009-01-27).
- **Prices as traded.** Yahoo's series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 split of 2005 and the 4-for-1 split of 2020-10-27; the builder multiplies
  it by the splits after AS_OF (x4), so the close is the price as traded ($68.82 on 2008-01-04). The 2005 split ("effective March 15, 2005",
  the FY2005 10-K; Yahoo's date 2005-03-16) restates the per-share facts published before it through `splits` (UNP's `on_basis`): the FY2004
  10-K says "The per share information does not reflect the effect of the 2005 stock split", so its and every earlier filing's EPS is halved
  and its share counts doubled. No print, guide or dividend of the range precedes it.
- **Fiscal calendar.** The calendar year. The four dates of January 2008 have FY2007 as the current year and FY06's EPS as its anchor.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 was accepted before the open (08:02-08:21 ET) on a Monday, Tuesday,
  Wednesday or Thursday, so each week's date is the next trading day (2008-01-29, 2008-05-01, 2008-08-01, 2008-10-28, 2009-01-28,
  2009-04-29, 2009-07-29, 2009-10-28). The 10-Ks came weeks later: FY2006 accepted 2007-02-27 13:47 ET, FY2007 2008-02-28 15:34 ET (both
  during the session, dated that day), FY2008 2009-02-26 19:15 ET (dated 2009-02-27). So **a Q4 print extends the history** (`fy_actual`)
  from its release to the 10-K, with the release's full-year diluted EPS, revenue, weighted-average diluted shares, margins and FPL figures:
  FY2007 on 2008-01-29 to 2008-02-22 and FY2008 on 2009-01-28 to 2009-02-20 (4 dates each).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS before the cumulative effect of accounting changes,** each year from the latest 10-K that reports it (FPL Group has
  no discontinued operations in these years; the cumulative effects of FAS 142 in 2002 and FIN 46 in 2003 sit below that line).
  - **The company's adjusted earnings stay out.** From 2001 the company's figures without its listed items also exclude "the mark-to-market
    effect of non-qualifying hedges" (and, from 2008, "other than temporary impairment losses" on the nuclear decommissioning funds): a
    recurring item ("While the unrealized marked-to-market gains and losses on non-qualifying hedge activity may be significant in any given
    period, the cumulative impact on FPL Group's balance sheet at December 31, 2006 was not material.", the FY2006 10-K), not a one-off, so
    GAAP stands (the PEP 2008 core rule, as XOM's timing effects). The releases' adjusted EPS is in each print's note.

    also excludes FAS 133 mark-to-market gains, so 2001 is GAAP $2.31 (FY2005 10-K).

### NEE 2010-2013: NextEra Energy and NYSE: NEE, six Friday prints, the FY2009-FY2012 vintages, CLOUD out of scope

209 weekly dates, 2010-01-08 to 2013-12-31 (52, 52, 52, 53), added to the 105 of 2008-2009 at the owner's request ("do retrospective
analysis for NEE, 2010-2013. same rules as before"), on the same fact sheet, builder, engine, method (r2) and 1997-2006 rule-T thresholds.
**Disclosure:** this batch was decided in the session that computed the 2008-2009 outcomes and wrote their findings, so its builder had read
the 2008-2009 hindsight results before any decision here. No decision uses them: each applies a rule that existed before, named in its
bullet, and every alternative is measured below before any 2010-2013 outcome was computed. Two parallel sessions (CRM 2022-2026, SCHW) had
pushed branches from the same base; they change only their own tickers' entries in the shared files, so this branch was not merged with them.


**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every document to a plain client name (no contact address). Read, by the session's model
directly with no delegated transcription: the sixteen earnings releases of Q4 2017 to Q3 2021 (8-K exhibits 99: the segment statements of
income for the quarter, the year-ago quarter and, in Q4, the twelve months; the reconciliations to adjusted earnings; the outlook
paragraphs); the selected data (FY2017-FY2019), the NEE and FPL statements of income, the cash flow statement, the EPS note, the segment
note, Items 1, 1A and 5 of the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks; the diluted share counts of the FY2010-FY2013 10-Ks' statements of income (each new
vintage's first year, the earlier vintages' encoding); and every 8-K of January 2018 to December 2021 by its items and text. **Not read:**
the 10-Qs, the proxy statements, the investor presentations and call transcripts (not filed; the June 2019 investor conference the Q2 2019
release cites among them), and the acquisition and merger exhibits beyond their outlook sentences. The facts are appended by a new
committed generator, `retro/generators/nee/gen_nee_1821.py` (the 2014-2017 generator's discipline: each figure from its own row by label
under an anchored heading, the segment columns read by name and asserted to sum to NextEra Energy's total, each Q4 release's full year
asserted equal to the next 10-K's, every rate computed, every quotation asserted in its own filing); the 805 strings were checked with
`verbatim.py` (805/805). Source ids `NE93`-`NE96` (the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks), `NE97`-`NE112` (the releases) and `NE113` (the split 8-K).
Decided on 2026-11-27, before any 2018-2021 model was built or outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of Q4 2017 to Q3 2021 was accepted before the open (07:35-08:10 ET). Five came on a Friday
  (2018-01-26, 2019-01-25, 2020-01-24, 2020-07-24, 2021-07-23) and date their own weeks ("day of the print, public before the open").
  The 10-Ks: FY2017 accepted 2018-02-16 15:44 ET (dated that day), FY2018 2019-02-15 17:22 ET (2019-02-19, after Presidents' Day),
  FY2019 2020-02-14 15:24 ET (that day), FY2020 2021-02-12 16:07 ET (2021-02-16). A Q4 print extends the history to its 10-K: FY2017 on
  2018-01-26 to 2018-02-09 (3 dates), FY2018 on 2019-01-25 to 2019-02-15 (4), FY2019 on 2020-01-24 to 2020-02-07 (3), FY2020 on
  2021-01-27 to 2021-02-12 (3).
- **FPL's energy sales and customer accounts n/r from the Q4 2017 print.** The releases of Q4 2017 on carry no FPL statistics table (the
  generator asserts its absence in all sixteen), and no 10-K of the period tabulates energy sales or customer accounts (the FY2016 10-K
  had already dropped them from its selected data). So the print's energy sales are None: the signal scores BASE and prints "n/r"
  through `nee2_engine.py.tmpl`, the None-tolerant copy (the BKR `bkr3`, SPGI `spgi2` and SCHW `schw2` encoding), which the builder
  derives from `nee_engine.py.tmpl` by six exact edits (`nr_engine`, each asserted once; the committed copy is checked equal to it), so
  rules, thresholds and weights are the engine's line for line. The franchise line's FPL energy sales and customer accounts are n/r too
  (`franchise_note`). The 10-Qs were not read (as in 2008-2017); a kWh figure there would be missed. Measured below.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS before the cumulative effect of accounting changes, each year from the latest 10-K that reports it** (FY17
  $11.38, then $11.39 as the FY2018 and FY2019 10-Ks restate it; FY18 $13.88; FY19 $7.76; FY20 $1.48 on the post-split basis, $5.92 on the
  old), on net income attributable to NEE. The FY2020 10-K omits Item 6 ("Omitted/Not Applicable"), so its vintage takes 2018-2020 from its
  statements of income and keeps 2011-2017 as the FY2019 vintage holds them (the ACN FY21, LLY and UNH rule). 2013 stays at $4.47 on net
  income, the Maine hydro gain in (the 2014-2017 rule), noted in every vintage that carries it.
- **FY2017 and FY2018 kept at GAAP (the batch's EPS call).** Both years carry large listed one-off benefits, so the mirror of the AAPL
  FY2002 test (listed one-off benefits larger than the year's income without them) was applied to the after-tax items as the company's
  own adjusted-earnings reconciliations tabulate them:
  - FY2017: the tax reform gain (about $1.9 billion attributable to NEE after tax; $4.05 a share) and the FiberNet gain ($685 million,
    $1.45) against $5,378 million ($11.38): about $2.6 billion against $2.8 billion without them, not met;
  - FY2018: the NEP investment gains ($2,863 million, $5.97) and the tax reform-related items ($436 million, $0.90) against $6,638 million
    ($13.88): $3,299 million against $3,339 million without them, **not met by $40 million** ($6.87 against $7.01 a share; the GOOG FY2017
    precedent, $69M short). The FY2018 10-K's own footnotes name gross components, "an after-tax gain of approximately $3.0 billion
    related to the deconsolidation of NEP" and "approximately $497 million relating to a reduction of differential membership interests",
    which together would meet the test; the components net of the other items in the same lines are what the company tabulates, so the
    net lines were used (decided here, disclosed).
  No filing publishes either year excluding only its one-offs (the adjusted $6.70 and $7.70 also remove the recurring mark-to-market
  items), so both stand at GAAP and are in the P/E window. FY2019 and FY2020 are GAAP with smaller items (2020's $1,208 million Mountain
  Valley Pipeline impairment against $2,919 million of income: the AAPL test not met). Measured below (FY2017 and FY2018 at the company's
  adjusted figures, a stand-in for an exclusion the builder does not encode).
- **No guide gives a field** (the PEP 2008 core rule, as before). Every expectation of 2018-2021 is adjusted earnings per share: FY2018
  $7.45-7.95 (from the Q4 2017 release, which raised it for the tax reform benefit; "targeting the midpoint of $7.70" from Q2 2018);
  FY2019 $8.00-8.50 (Q4 2018), then "at or near the top" of 6% to 8% growth off the 2018 base of $7.70 (words; "$8.32" if achieved, Q3
  2019); FY2020 $8.70-9.20 (Q4 2019 to Q2 2020), restated by the Q3 2020 release, a week before the split, on the post-split basis to
  $2.18-2.30 (quoted with the release's own sentence on the split); FY2021 $2.40-2.54 (Q4 2020 to Q3 2021). Each year's records run from
  the print that makes it current; the later-year ranges and growth targets (the 8-K of 2018-05-21's $8.70-9.20 and $9.40-9.95 after the
  Florida acquisitions, the 8-K of 2020-09-14's 2021 range of $9.60-10.15, the 2022-2023 ranges) concern later years and are not quoted
  (one quote per fiscal year; a quote may name an earlier year as its base, never a later one, asserted). So the last full year's GAAP EPS
  stands: FY16's $6.25 to 2018-01-19, FY17's $11.38 from 2018-01-26, FY18's $13.88 from 2019-01-25, FY19's $7.76 from 2020-01-24 ($1.94
  from 2020-10-27), FY20's $1.48 from 2021-01-27. BASE is still the latest quarter's revenue growth as reported; no filing guides revenue or
  a margin in numbers.

  ... Trading will begin on a stock split-adjusted basis on October 27, 2020." (the 8-K of 2020-09-14, accepted 16:18 ET, so 2020-09-15;
  `NE113`), Yahoo's split date 2020-10-27: the second `splits` record. Prices stay as traded (the builder multiplies Yahoo's series by the

  share count multiplied by 4 (`on_basis`, the UNP encoding used for the 2005 split), so the P/E window is on the AS_OF share basis
  throughout. The Q4 2020 release and the FY2020 10-K report on the new basis. A print note or dividend sentence published before the
  split and shown after it gets "(per-share figures in this text before the 4-for-1 split effective 2020-10-27)" (a builder change that
  acts on no earlier date).

  stock from $0.9825 per share to $1.11 per share.", then $1.25, $1.40 and, after the split, "$0.35 per share to $0.385 per share");

## NEM (Newmont Mining Corporation): the thirty-sixth ticker, in staging, 2008-2009

The NEM series is built apart from the other thirty-five and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/NEM.json`, generated by `retro/generators/nem/gen_nem.py`), builder (`retro/build_nem.py`, the MU builder with the calendar
year, display-only outlooks and Newmont's fields) and engine (`retro/templates/nem_engine.py.tmpl`, the MU engine with a gold miner's
signals and Newmont's own rule-T thresholds). It is the first gold miner in the retrospectives. The method is still r2. No fact, parameter,
outcome or finding of another ticker enters an NEM model, and no 2026 analysis of Newmont was opened. Outputs go to
`staging/retrospective/NEM/`, with the same `index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009 ("find newest code. do
retrospective analysis for NEM, 2008-2009. same rules as before"); the code is the branch `claude/sharp-albattani-rdvlgi` (its commit
"Merge NEE 2022-2026 ... with SCHW 2008-2026"), as the coordinating session named it; nothing else was merged in.


ids are `NM1`-`NM27`. Decided on 2026-11-27, before any NEM model was built or any NEM outcome computed:

  CIK 1164727; the old Newmont, CIK 71824, is Newmont USA Limited). Yahoo's NEM series has one split (5:4, 1994), before the window, so
  its close is the price as traded ($52.42 on 2008-01-04).

  - **1998-2001 are losses** ($(3.26), $(0.62), $(0.45), $(0.27)), so FY2001 takes the years before it (the MU FY2003 rule): the history

Controls and checks (before any outcome):
- **`retro_tool run` passes on all 105 dates, with no warning.**
- **Controls** (`controls_nem.py`, in memory): altering each print's gold ounces sold (rate re-derived), each vintage's last-year revenue
  and each outlook's quoted text changes no model dated before its publication: 26 controls, 23 change the first weekly date on or after
  it and 3 are inert (the 2007-08-02, 2008-02-07 and 2009-01-28 outlooks, each superseded for its year before any built date reads it).
- **Leak scan:** 1 hit in 17,804 (model, later token) pairs, a trading-day count (the 1,392 days of the 2008-07-11 window, which equal Q3
  2008's revenue in millions): not a leak. Positive control: the latest print's tokens in 105 of 105 models. **Forward references:** 0 in 54
  facts. **Self-text scan:** 8 tokens of 583, all benign: four debt totals that are the sum of two stated lines (the note names both) and
  four "Ks" of "10-Ks".
- **Regression:** the shared code is untouched (the firewall tool gains an NEM entry, `taxonomy_eras.json` the three terms); rebuilding
  the 2008-2009 dates of MU and NEE changes nothing.
- **Firewall** (run after the build, validation outputs and README section were committed and pushed, before any outcome): it passes at
  all 11 cutoffs above (2008-01-11, every print and vintage date of the range, and 2010-01-01: 1 to 105 dates each), 0 files changed and
  no planted text. The plants: a print with absurd ounces, unit costs, revenue, margins, EPS, notes and raw figures; a later vintage whose
  texts, figures, window start and exclusions are planted; a later display-only outlook for every guided year; a dividend, a listing, a
  company name and prices from the cutoff multiplied by 10. As positive controls, a planted print dated 2008-07-01 with its own source
  reaches 2008-07-03 (its text in the model) and not 2008-06-27; the same print citing a source published after AS_OF stops at the
  builder's check that every source is public on AS_OF.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned). Newmont's GAAP EPS was low against its price in 2002-2006 (P/Es of 26-100x), so the
stock's own window has a median of 42-47x, and every anchor reads below it:
- **CHEAP and BUY on all 105 dates;** robustness 8 of 8 on 102 dates, 7 of 8 on 3.
- **FY06's $1.18** (2008-01-04 to 2008-02-15, 7 dates): $47.89-54.72 is 40.6-46.4x, the 35th-52nd percentile of a 45.2-45.5x median,
  6.8-22.0% above the EPP floor.
- **FY06's $1.25** (2008-02-22 to 2009-02-13, 52 dates): $23.82-53.63 is 19.1-42.9x, the 0th-36th percentile of a 44.9-47.3x median
  ("ex-FY07"); the price is under the floor from 2008-09-12 (-45.6% on 2008-10-24), Ratio B 0.03-0.27.
- **FY08's $1.82 and $1.80** (2009-02-20 on, 46 dates): $37.89-53.35 is 20.8-29.6x, the 5th-30th percentile of a 42.5-44.8x median, 13-35%
  under the floor on every date.
- **BASE follows quarterly revenue,** driven by the gold and copper prices and Batu Hijau's copper: Q3 2007 +49.4%, Q4 2007 -1.0%, Q1 2008
  +58.7%, Q2 2008 +19.3%, Q3 2008 -13.9%, Q4 2008 -4.8%, Q1 2009 -20.1%, Q2 2009 +6.6%, Q3 2009 +49.5% (each less the decade's dilution).
- **BEAR** is the worst year of the short history (2005: -34.1%, -33.3% on the FY2007 10-K's figures, -36.2% on the recast), BULL the
  decade CAGR from FY2002's $0.29 (+44-45%/yr in 2008, +36%/yr from FY2008; BASE's rate where higher, +46%/yr after Q3 2009) and XBULL the
  2002-2004 run (+77-80%/yr): the bull cases rest on one low year.

How far each call moves the classes (the 105 dates rebuilt with one encoding changed, classified offline with `retro_tool`'s classifier;
`sens_nem.py`; no outcome consulted):
- FY2007 and FY2008 at the company's adjusted $1.33 and $1.99 from the Q4 2008 release: no class, no tier;
- FY2007 derived without its listed charges ($1.29, no filing publishes it): no class, no tier;
- BASE on the latest quarter's gold ounces sold growth instead of revenue (the XOM production test): no class, no tier;
- every signal at its BEAR value: 2 classes (2008-02-29 to FAIR, 2008-03-14 to RICH), no tier; at its XBULL value: none.
The CHEAP calls rest on the stock's own 2002-2009 multiples of GAAP earnings, which none of the calls above moves.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the P/E window from 2002 (the 1998-2001 losses taking the years before them), whose low 2002-2006 earnings set a 42-47x median: the
  call that every class rests on, by a rule (MU FY2003) rather than a choice, but decided by a builder who knows gold's 2008-2011 run;
- GAAP rather than the company's adjusted net income (no class moves), on the reading that legacy closure obligations recur;
- FY2007 excluded as a loss (no class moves either way);
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows how ounces and unit costs ran after 2009 (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically; 2
  classes at BEAR), and rule T's mixed cost lines (total cash costs before the costs-applicable-to-sales line) and production-for-sales
  ounces in 1997-1998, as each filing tabulates them;
- the production and cost outlooks kept as display only (no input either way under r2);
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL (label only), as no 10-K calls the business cyclical, though its revenue follows the gold price;
- the parts of the filings listed as not read.

The hindsight results are in `staging/retrospective/NEM/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

### NEM 2010-2013: the FY2009-FY2012 vintages, FY2011 excluded (the Hope Bay write-down), ounces produced, the gold price-linked dividend, CLOUD out of scope

The owner asked for 2010-2013 ("find newest code. do retrospective analysis for NEM, 2010-2013. same rules as before"); the code is the
branch `claude/sharp-albattani-rdvlgi` (its commit "Merge CHTR setup ... with NEM 2008-2009 and LYB 2012-2013"), as the coordinating
session named it; nothing else was merged in. Built in a new session without opening the 2008-2009 outcomes or findings. The method is
still r2; no fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an NEM model.

```bash
python3 -I retro/generators/nem/gen_nem.py --filings <dir> --old <old> --out <scratch>/NEM_0809.json     # the 2008-2009 sheet
python3 -I retro/generators/nem/gen_nem_1013.py --filings <dir> --facts-in <scratch>/NEM_0809.json       # -> retro/facts/NEM.json
python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py <dir>/checklist_nem_1013.json                                         # 56/56
python3 retro/build_nem.py --weekly 2010-01-01 2013-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/NEM/201[0-3]-*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series NEM
for c in 2010-02-26 2010-04-28 2011-02-25 2011-10-28 2012-02-24 2012-11-02 2013-02-22 2013-07-26 2014-01-01; do
  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c NEM; done
python3 retro/generators/nem/controls_nem_1013.py --from 2009-06-01; python3 retro/generators/nem/sens_nem_1013.py <scratch>
```
