**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every document to `edgar.py`'s plain client name (no contact address). Read, by the session's
model directly with no delegated transcription: the sixteen earnings releases of Q4 2009 to Q3 2013 (8-K exhibit 99.1: the statements of
income, the balance sheets, the production and sales statistics, the costs applicable to sales tables, the adjusted net income
reconciliations and the outlook text); Items 1A, 6, 7 and 8 of the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks with each one's quarterly data note; each 10-Q's
income per share note (diluted weighted shares) and its ounces tables; the two January outlook 8-Ks (2012-01-17, 2013-01-22), the
preliminary-results 8-Ks (2011-01-20, 2012-10-16, 2013-04-17, 2013-07-10, 2013-10-10) and the 8-K of 2011-04-07 (the Investor Day growth
plan and the gold price-linked dividend policy). Every other 8-K of December 2009 to December 2013 was read by its items and exhibit
headings: the Batu Hijau divestiture and arbitration, the Indonesian court ruling, Fronteer Gold (2011), the 2012 senior notes, officers
and directors, votes, the Holt royalty, Dodd-Frank imminent-danger orders, conference and Investor Day notices; none states a guided
number. **Not read:** the Investor Day and Denver Gold Forum slides beyond their headings (the 2010 deck is an exhibit, the 2012 and 2013
decks were not filed), the 10-Qs beyond the two tables above, the proxy statements and the website presentations the releases point to.
The FY2013 10-K and every 2014 filing were deleted from the scratchpad unread once their dates were listed. Each source's date is EDGAR's
acceptance time; the new ids are `NM28`-`NM49`. The generator reads each raw figure from its own row by label (the row text is kept in
the fact), computes every rate, asserts every quote verbatim, asserts that each Q4 print's full year equals the 10-K that comes with it
and that every 2008-2009 fact is unchanged. Decided on 2026-11-27, before any 2010-2013 model was built or any outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** To Q3 2011 each earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (06:01-06:27 ET), the 10-K or 10-Q the same day; from Q3
  2011 most were accepted after the close (17:10-21:48 ET) and count from the next trading day, which is a Friday for Q3 2011, Q1 2012,
  Q2 2012, Q3 2012, Q4 2012 and Q3 2013, so that Friday is the week's date and the print is public before its open (the AVGO, CRM and
  SCHW rule; `build_nem.py` accepts "after the close: counts from AS_OF"). Q1 2011 (06:01 ET on Thursday 2011-04-21, the day before Good
  Friday) and Q2 2013 (06:00 ET on Friday 2013-07-26) meet their own day's close. Each Q4 print comes the same day as its 10-K (the FY2010
  10-K accepted 2011-02-23 20:54 ET counts from 2011-02-24, with the release at 06:10 ET), so no print carries full-year actuals.
- **Four more vintages,** the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks, each year from the latest filing that reports it (five years of Item 6; earlier years
  from the latest earlier vintage), each holding the ten fiscal years to the latest one: FY2002 and the FY2001 note leave with the FY2012
  10-K (2013-02-22), whose window is the plain ten years. Seams as published (each 10-K's reclassifications; Kori Kollo, Holloway and the
  Holt royalty in discontinued operations).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations** (FY09 $2.68, FY10 $4.61, FY12 $3.78). The releases' adjusted net income also
  removes items that recur in every year it tabulates (impairments and write-downs of assets, gains on asset sales, tax planning items),
  so GAAP stands (the PEP 2008 core rule, as in 2008-2009). FY2007 stays excluded and a gap ($(2.18), the FY2009-FY2011 10-Ks).
  - **FY2011 is excluded** by the AAPL FY2002 test: the Q4 2011 release's listed after-tax items in continuing operations (the Hope Bay
    impairment $1,609M, other impairments and asset sales $105M, Fronteer acquisition costs $18M, Boddington contingent consideration
    $1M, income tax planning $(65)M; $1,668M net) exceed the year's $502M of income from continuing operations attributable to Newmont,
    so reported EPS ($1.00) is under half the year's EPS without them, and no figure excludes only the one-offs (the adjusted $4.39 also
    removes the recurring items above). Excluded as the latest year (the NKE FY2018 and XOM FY2020 rule), its days leave the window
    ("ex-FY07 ex-FY11"), then a gap. FY2009, FY2010 and FY2012 pass the test and its mirror (their listed items are small fractions of
    income: FY2010's tax planning and asset-sale benefits $430M against $1,875M).
  - So the anchor (the rollover rule; no filing guides EPS): FY08's $1.80 to 2010-02-19 (7 dates), FY09's $2.68 from 2010-02-26 (52), FY10's
    $4.61 from 2011-02-25 (52) and, FY11 excluded, still from 2012-02-24 (52), FY12's $3.78 from 2013-02-22 (46).
- **The Q4 2011 and Q4 2012 releases print the year only** (no fourth-quarter columns). Their sales, diluted EPS from continuing operations
  and diluted shares are the 10-K's quarterly data (public the same day; `source_10k`), the pre-tax income the release's year less the
  Q3 release's nine months, both years (the F and UNH rule; `derived_note`); the release's year is asserted equal to the 10-K's four quarters.
- **The ounces signal reads consolidated gold ounces produced from Q1 2010.** From Q1 2010 the releases tabulate consolidated (and equity or
  attributable) ounces produced with a year-ago figure, but ounces sold only for Boddington or, from Q1 2011, attributable to Newmont in
  a reconciliation; the 10-Qs give consolidated ounces sold only from Q3 2010. Rule T's ounces are the company-wide line each filing gives
  (equity production in 1997-1998), so the signal takes the releases' consolidated ounces produced (`oz_basis`), Q4 2009 keeping ounces
  sold. The model names the line through `retro/templates/nem2_engine.py.tmpl`, a copy of the NEM engine whose ounces signal is named by
  `OZ_NAME` (nothing else differs); dates whose latest print is Q4 2009 or earlier keep the original engine. Thresholds unchanged.
- **Diluted shares** (display, the EPS check) from the 10-Q filed with each Q1-Q3 release (its income per share note), and from the 10-K's
  quarterly data for Q4 2010-Q4 2012; Q4 2009's release prints them.
- **No guide in numbers for revenue, EPS or a margin.** The outlooks are equity (2010) or attributable (2011-2013) gold production and costs
  applicable to sales per ounce, capital and cost components: display only (the XOM production and MSFT segment rules), one quote a fiscal
  year in the guide line, from each release and the two January outlook 8-Ks. BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth plus the buyback
  (the UNP rule): Q4 2009 +90.0%, then +46.0%, +34.4%, +26.7%, +1.2%, +9.9%, +10.7%, +5.7%, +8.5%, +8.8%, -6.5%, -9.6%, -10.5%, -18.9%,
  -10.6%, -20.0% (Q3 2013). The preliminary-results 8-Ks add nothing (operating figures the print reports within weeks, the UNP rule); the
  Investor Day growth plan of 2011-04-07 (to 2017) is no fiscal-year guide.
- **Dividends** (`dividends`, each rate from the first release that states it as declared or approved; "subject to Board approval" is not):
  $0.15 a quarter from 2010-07-28, then under the gold price-linked policy $0.20 (2011-04-21), $0.30 (2011-07-29), $0.35 (2011-10-28 to
  2012-11-02), $0.425 (2013-02-22), $0.35 (2013-04-30), $0.25 (2013-07-26), $0.20 (2013-11-01). A declared rate wins over the vintage's
  dividends declared for the year (`build_nem.py`; no 2008-2009 model changes); the vintage's $0.40 stands to 2010-07-23. The policy 8-K
  of 2011-04-07 states a policy, not a rate (text only).
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2** (the MU rule: no FY2009-FY2012 10-K calls the business cyclical; the generator asserts it), the "why"
  quoting each 10-K's own lead sentence, its price-dependence sentence and the risk factor "A substantial or extended decline in gold or
  copper prices would have a material adverse effect on Newmont." From CLOUD's live date (2012-10-30; first date 2012-11-02) the "why"

### NEM 2014-2017: the FY2013-FY2016 vintages and the 2014 recast, FY2013, FY2015 and FY2016 excluded, ounces sold again, Batu Hijau discontinued, three themes out of scope

The owner asked for 2014-2017 ("find newest code. do retrospective analysis for NEM, 2014-2017. same rules as before"); the code is the
branch `claude/sharp-albattani-rdvlgi` (its commit "Merge LYB 2014-2017 ... with NEM 2010-2013"), as the coordinating session named it;
nothing else was merged in. Built in a new session without opening the 2008-2013 outcomes or findings (`FINDINGS.md` and every earlier
`outcome.json` were left unread). The method is still r2; no fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an NEM model.

```bash
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py fetch 1164727 <dir> --from 2013-12-01 --to 2017-12-31 --forms 8-K 8-K/A 10-K 10-K/A 10-Q
python3 -I retro/generators/nem/gen_nem_1417.py --filings <dir> --facts-in <scratch>/NEM_0813.json   # the 2008-2013 sheet -> retro/facts/NEM.json
python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py <dir>/checklist_nem_1417.json                                       # 67/67
python3 retro/build_nem.py --weekly 2014-01-01 2017-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2014-01-03 .. 2017-12-29
for d in staging/retrospective/NEM/201[4-7]-*/; do

done

for c in 2014-02-21 2014-06-13 2014-07-30 2015-02-20 2015-12-14 2016-02-18 2017-02-22 2017-10-26 2018-01-01; do
  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c NEM; done
python3 retro/generators/nem/controls_nem_1417.py --from 2013-06-01; python3 retro/generators/nem/sens_nem_1417.py <scratch>
```

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every document to `edgar.py`'s plain client name (no contact address). Read, by the session's
model directly with no delegated transcription: the sixteen earnings releases of Q4 2013 to Q3 2017 (8-K exhibit 99.1: the statements of
operations, the balance sheets, the production statistics, the costs applicable to sales reconciliations, the adjusted net income
reconciliations and the outlook text); Items 1A, 6, 7 and 8 of the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks with each one's quarterly data note; the 8-K of
2014-06-13 re-filing the FY2013 10-K's Items 6-8; each 10-Q's income per share note (diluted weighted shares); the preliminary-results
8-K of 2014-01-30 and its 8-K/A of 2014-01-31 (outlook footnotes only), the 8-K/A of 2014-07-30 (a corrected copper outlook) and the 8-K/A
of 2017-02-22 (the Q4 2016 release with its attributable ounces sold corrected; no field reads that line), and the outlook 8-Ks of
2015-12-02 and 2017-12-06. Every other 8-K of December 2013 to December 2017 was read by its items and exhibit headings: Indonesia's export
ban, the Batu Hijau suspension, arbitration and memorandum, the export permits, the Barrick letter, officers and directors, votes, the
term loan and its repayment, the Waihi sale, Cripple Creek & Victor and the June 2015 common stock offering, the Batu Hijau sale agreement
and completion (with pro forma statements, unused), the Yanacocha impairment notice of 2016-12-13 (no figure), the Continental Gold
investment, website postings of outlooks and conference slides (not filed), and the tax reform notice of 2017-12-22; none states a guided
number. **Not read:** the website outlooks, presentations and Investor Day slides the 8-Ks point to (not filed), the 10-Qs beyond the
income per share note, the proxy statements. The FY2017 10-K and every 2018 filing were not downloaded. Each source's date is EDGAR's
acceptance time; the new ids are `NM50`-`NM73`. The generator reads each raw figure from its own row by label (the row text is kept in the
fact), computes every rate, asserts every quote verbatim, asserts that each Q4 print's full year equals the 10-K that comes with it, that the
10-K's fourth quarter equals the release's, and that every 2008-2013 fact is unchanged. Decided on 2026-11-27, before any 2014-2017 model was
built or any outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** Most earnings 8-Ks were accepted after the close (16:10-21:55 ET) and count from the next trading day, which is a
  Friday for Q4 2013, Q3 2014 and Q1 2015 (that Friday is the week's date, public before its open: the AVGO, CRM and SCHW rule); Q1 2014,
  Q4 2014 (Friday 2015-02-20), Q2 2017 and Q3 2017 came before the open. Each Q4 print comes the same day as its 10-K (by the same rule), so
  no print carries full-year actuals.
- **Five more vintages,** each year from the latest filing that reports it, each holding the ten fiscal years to the latest one: the
  FY2013 10-K (2014-02-21); the 8-K of 2014-06-13 (accepted 15:56 ET, during the session) re-filing its Items 6-8 for the 2014 segments and
  the deferred tax asset and stockpile revisions, a vintage of its own (the MU and MSFT recast rule, as the 8-K of 2009-09-15; FY12 $3.78 to
  $3.76, FY13 $(5.06) to $(5.21); its 'why' stays the FY2013 10-K's, as Item 1A is not re-filed); the FY2014 10-K (2015-02-20); the FY2015
  10-K (2016-02-18); the FY2016 10-K (2017-02-22), which restates 2012-2015 with Batu Hijau (sold 2016-11-02) in discontinued operations
  (FY12 $3.72, FY14 $1.30, FY15 $0.00) while 2007-2011 keep it: a seam, as published. FY2003 leaves with the FY2013 10-K, one year a vintage
  after it.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations** (the releases' adjusted net income still removes items that recur in every year it
  tabulates: impairments, asset sales, tax adjustments; the PEP 2008 core rule). FY2007 and FY2011 stay gaps.
  - **FY2013 is a loss** ($(5.06), the Q2 and Q4 2013 impairments; $(5.21) recast, $(4.71) without Batu Hijau): excluded as the latest
    year, its days out of the window, then a gap ("ex-FY13").
  - **FY2014 is kept at $1.10** (then $1.30 restated): the Q4 2014 release's listed after-tax items in continuing operations net to $(3)M
    against $548M, so the AAPL FY2002 test and its mirror both pass.
  - **FY2015 is excluded by the AAPL FY2002 test**, the FY2011 encoding: the Q4 2015 release lists $314M of after-tax items in continuing
    operations (impairments of investments $74M and long-lived assets $22M, restructuring $17M, acquisition costs $12M, asset and
    investment sales $(69)M, the TMAC deconsolidation gain $(49)M, reclamation charges $94M, the Ghana Investment Agreement $18M, tax
    adjustments $195M) against $193M of income from continuing operations attributable to Newmont, so reported EPS ($0.38) is under half
    the year's EPS without them, and the adjusted $0.98 also removes the recurring items; excluded as the latest year, then a gap. The
    FY2016 10-K's $0.00 has no P/E either (the F rule).
  - **FY2016 is a loss** ($(0.41), the $974M Yanacocha and other impairments of long-lived assets): excluded as the latest year, then a gap.
  - So the anchor (the rollover rule; no filing guides EPS): FY12's $3.78 to 2014-06-06 (23 dates), $3.76 from 2014-06-13 (36), FY14's
    $1.10 from 2015-02-20 (52) and, FY15 excluded, from 2016-02-19 (53), FY14's $1.30 from 2017-02-23 (45; "ex-FY15 ex-FY16"). The P/E
    window loses the excluded years' days: 9.0 to 10 years of calendar span holding 2008-2010, 2012, 2014 and the current year in 2017.
- **The ounces signal reads consolidated gold ounces sold again from Q2 2014.** From Q2 2014 every release's costs applicable to sales
  reconciliation tabulates 'Gold sold (thousand ounces)', the per-ounce denominator, consolidated and against the year-ago quarter; it is
  rule T's line (consolidated ounces sold from the FY2005 10-K/A) and the 2008-2009 prints', while the production table the 2010-2013
  batch read is missing from the Q3 2014 release and from Q4 2016 on. So `oz_basis` is "sold" from Q2 2014 and those dates use the original
  engine (`nem_engine.py.tmpl`, "Gold ounces sold"); Q4 2013 and Q1 2014, with no such row, keep consolidated ounces produced and `nem2`.
  Costs applicable to sales per ounce come from the same reconciliation from Q2 2014 (the CAS table's consolidated average before).
  Thresholds unchanged. A builder who knows later production chose between two published lines here; the signals at BEAR and XBULL
  below bound the call.
- **Diluted shares** (display, the EPS check) from the 10-Q filed with each Q1-Q3 release, and from the 10-K's quarterly data for Q4.
- **No guide in numbers for revenue, EPS or a margin.** The outlooks are attributable (or, in the preliminary 8-K, consolidated) gold
  production, costs applicable to sales and all-in sustaining costs per ounce, capital and cost components: display only (the XOM
  production and MSFT segment rules), one quote a release cut to its own year, from each release, the preliminary 8-K/A of 2014-01-31 and
  the outlook 8-Ks of 2015-12-02 (FY2016) and 2017-12-06 (FY2018; no built date reads it). BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth less
  the dilution (the UNP rule): Q4 2013 -12.4%, then -19.4%, -12.5%, -13.6%, -7.8%, +11.8%, +8.1%, +16.4%, -10.0%, +3.0%, +6.8%, +14.8%,
  +23.2%, +13.5%, +12.3%, +4.9% (Q3 2017), as published (Batu Hijau out of the year-ago quarters from the Q3 2016 release).
- **Dividends** (`dividends`, each rate from the first release that states it as declared): the Q3 2013 release's $0.20 stands to
  2014-04-18, as the cut announced on 2014-02-19 was not filed (the Q4 2013 release says only "As announced yesterday ... has adjusted the
  annual payout levels"); $0.025 a quarter from the Q1 2014 release (2014-04-25), $0.05 from the Q3 2016 release (2016-10-27), $0.075 from
  the Q2 2017 release (2017-07-25).
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2** (the MU rule: no FY2013-FY2016 10-K calls the business cyclical; the generator asserts it), the "why"
  quoting each 10-K's lead sentence, its price-dependence sentence and its gold-price risk factor. The FY2016 vintage's business line
  notes the Batu Hijau sale.
- **Themes.** ECOMMERCE (2015-01-01), STREAMING (2015-08-04) and ENERGY_TRANSITION (2015-12-12) go live; the "why" quotes every live theme's
  registered scope, none of which names a miner. ENERGY_TRANSITION is scoped to "decarbonisation strands oil, gas and coal reserves and
  refining": Newmont holds none, so it is read as out of scope, and from its live date the "why" also quotes the vintage's own risk factor
  "Regulations and pending legislation governing issues involving climate change could result in increased operating costs which could
  have a material adverse effect on our business." (`climate_words`, text only, the UNH `cloud_words` encoding). The builder still refuses
  any other live theme and any event.
- **Anachronism list:** no new term; Ahafo North, Newmont Goldcorp and Nevada Gold Mines appear in no model.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):
- **`retro_tool run` passes on all 209 dates.** 43 carry the calendar-year warning, every one checked by script: a trading-day count in the
  P/E-window comment (2,015 days on the seven dates of January-February 2014) or the FY2013 tax rate 0.2094 (36 dates).

  costs applicable to sales per ounce), free cash flow and sales by metal come from its "Results and Highlights" table and statements.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations** (the releases' adjusted net income still removes items that recur in every year it
  tabulates: impairments, asset sales, changes in the fair value of investments, reclamation charges, tax items; the PEP 2008 core rule).
  The Q4 release's reconciliation lists the year's items with a "Tax effect of adjustments" line and tax lines; the tests sum every listed
  line, recurring ones included (the FY2011 and FY2015 encoding).
  - **FY2017 is a loss** ($(0.11), then $(0.14); the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act re-measurement and restructuring): excluded as the latest
    year, then a gap.
  - **FY2018 is excluded by the AAPL FY2002 test**: the Q4 2018 release's items in continuing operations net to $438M (the $369M
    impairment of long-lived assets in Nevada, the $158M valuation allowance and other tax adjustments, investment items, the Emigrant
    leach pad write-down, less the $100M of asset sales and the tax effect) against $280M of income from continuing operations
    attributable to Newmont, so reported EPS ($0.53) is under half the year's EPS without them ($1.34 adjusted, which also removes recurring
    items); excluded as the latest year, then a gap.
  - **FY2019 is excluded by the mirror of the AAPL FY2002 test** (method r2, the AVGO FY2018 rule): the Q4 2019 release's items net to
    $1,907M of benefits (the $2,390M gain on the formation of Nevada Gold Mines above all) against $970M of income without them, so
    reported EPS ($3.91) is more than double the year's EPS without them ($1.32 adjusted); excluded as the latest year, then a gap.
  - **FY2020 is kept at GAAP $3.31**: its items net to $526M of benefits (the Kalgoorlie and Continental sales, the investment marks, the
    valuation allowance, less reclamation, impairment, pension, COVID-19 and debt costs) against $2,140M without them, neither test met.
  - So the anchor (the rollover rule; no filing guides EPS): FY14's $1.30 to 2018-04-20 (16 dates), $1.28 from 2018-04-27 to 2021-02-12
    (147), with FY2015-FY2019 all gaps ("ex-FY15 ex-FY16 ex-FY17 ex-FY18 ex-FY19"), then FY20's $3.31 from 2021-02-19 (46). The P/E window
    loses the excluded years' days: by 2020 it holds only 2010, 2012, 2014 and the current year (756 trading days in ten calendar years).
- **The ounces signal stays consolidated gold ounces sold** (each release's costs applicable to sales reconciliation, 'Gold sold (thousand
  ounces)'; from Q3 2019 the release also tabulates NGM and gold-equivalent ounces separately: the consolidated gold line is kept, rule T's
  line). Thresholds unchanged.
- **A year-ago EPS of $0.00** (Q4 2018's and Q2 2019's continuing EPS, "—") leaves the Q4 2019 and Q2 2020 prints with no EPS growth rate:
  None, n/m, scoring BASE and printing "n/r" (the F rule) through `nem3_engine.py.tmpl`, a copy of the original engine tolerant of None

  quarters, then +4.8% to +29.6%, -8.7% on Q3 2021.

applied at this build's time. Those batches were built during the session of 2026-11-27 and so end on 2026-11-20; this one has one more

done

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every document to `edgar.py`'s plain client name (no contact address; the owner's email was
not used). Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the twenty earnings releases of Q4 2021 to Q3 2026
(8-K exhibit 99.1: the statements of operations, the balance sheets, the costs applicable to sales reconciliations, the 'Summary of
Results' tables from Q4 2025, the adjusted net income reconciliations, the dividend lines and the outlook bullets); the FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks'
results and highlights tables, statements of operations, balance sheets and cash flow lines, Items 1 and 1A (the 'why', the climate,
crypto and AI words) and the dividend sentence of the FY2023 10-K; the 10-K/A of 2022-07-28 (it re-files Item 8 only to amend NGM's
auditor's report: "there have been no changes to the Company’s financial statements"); the 8-K of 2023-07-20 recasting the FY2022 10-K's
Items 1, 2, 7 and 8 for the new segments (its statements of operations asserted equal to the FY2022 10-K's). Every other 8-K of January
2022 to November 2026 was read by its items and exhibit headings, and the filed earnings presentations and call excerpts (2023-02-24,
2023-04-28, 2023-07-21) and the Newcrest investor presentations (2023-05-16, 2023-05-20) were searched for a revenue, EPS or margin guide:
none states one. **Not read:** the 10-Qs (no figure the models read comes from them: the releases' own statements give the diluted
shares), the proxy statements, the Newcrest scheme booklet and S-4 materials, the pro forma statements (8-K/A of 2023-11-20, 8-K of
2024-07-26; unused, as before) and the website guidance and presentations not filed. Each source's date is EDGAR's acceptance time; the
new ids are `NM98`-`NM102` (the 10-Ks) and `NM103`-`NM122` (the releases). The generator reads each raw figure from its own row by label,
computes every rate, asserts every quote verbatim, asserts that each Q4 print's year equals the 10-K that comes with it, that each Q4
adjusted net income reconciliation adds up, and that every 2008-2021 fact is unchanged. Decided on 2026-11-27/28, before any 2022-2026
model was built or any outcome computed:

- **Release timing.** To Q1 2024 every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (07:00-07:03 ET); the Q1 2022 release came on a Friday
  (2022-04-22) and dates its own week ("day of the print, public before the open"). From Q2 2024 every release was accepted after the
  close (16:01-16:06 ET) and counts from the next trading day (the AVGO, CRM and SCHW rule, already in the builder): Q2 and Q3 2024 and
  Q1 2025 on a Wednesday (dated Thursday, the week's date Friday); Q4 2024, Q2 and Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 to Q3 2026 on a Thursday (dated
  Friday, meeting that Friday's close). The 10-Ks came the same day as the Q4 releases (FY2021 and FY2022 before the open; FY2024 at
  20:20 ET and FY2025 at 16:18 ET, both dated the next day with their release), except FY2023's (below).
- **Five more vintages,** each from its 10-K, each holding the ten fiscal years to the latest one. The FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks reserve Item 6
  (asserted), so each vintage takes its three years from the statements of operations and keeps the earlier years as the previous vintage
  holds them (the FY2020 and ACN FY21 rule); the franchise line (consolidated gold ounces sold, costs applicable to sales per ounce), free
  cash flow, sales by metal and the regular dividends declared come from the results and highlights table. Neither the 10-K/A of
  2022-07-28 nor the segment recast of 2023-07-20 changes a figure the models read, so neither is a vintage (the 8-Ks of 2009-09-15,
  2014-06-13 and 2018-04-26 were vintages because they restated EPS; decided here, no class either way).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations,** each Q4 release's listed items summed, recurring ones included (the FY2011, FY2015
  and FY2018 encoding), as the adjusted net income still removes items that recur (the PEP 2008 core rule):
  - **FY2021 is excluded by the AAPL FY2002 test:** the Q4 2021 release's items in continuing operations net to $1,262M (the $983M of
    reclamation and remediation charges, mainly the non-operating Yanacocha sites, the $372M loss on assets held for sale, the investment
    marks, the valuation allowance, less the $212M of gains on asset sales and the tax effect) against $1,109M of income from continuing
    operations attributable to Newmont, so reported EPS ($1.39) is under half the year's EPS without them ($2.96 adjusted, which also
    removes recurring items); excluded as the latest year, then a gap. **The batch's largest call** (below).
  - **FY2022 is a loss** ($(0.58); the Q4 2022 release's adjusted $1.85) and **FY2023 is a loss** ($(2.97) in the Q4 2023 release,
    $(3.00) in the FY2023 10-K; adjusted $1.61, then $1.57): each excluded as the latest year, then a gap.
  - **FY2024 is kept at GAAP $2.86** (its items net to $711M of charges, the $1,114M loss on the non-core assets held for sale above all,
    against $3,280M) and **FY2025 at GAAP $6.39** (items net to $549M of charges against $7,085M: the $1,066M gain on the non-core sales
    against the $841M of impairments and the $883M valuation allowance), neither test met.
  - So the anchor (the rollover rule; no filing guides EPS): FY20's $3.31 from the FY2020 10-K to 2025-02-14 (163 dates of the range),
    with FY2021-FY2023 all gaps ("ex-FY21 ex-FY22 ex-FY23" beside the 2015-2019 gaps), FY24's $2.86 from 2025-02-21 (52) and FY25's $6.39
    from 2026-02-20 (41). By 2024 the P/E window holds only 2014, 2020 and the current year's days; by 2026 only 2020, 2024 and 2025.
- **A Q4 print ahead of its 10-K.** The Q4 2023 release (2024-02-22, before the open) came a week before the FY2023 10-K (2024-02-29) and
  is preliminary ("Newmont’s actual consolidated financial results remain subject to completion of our annual audit procedures"). Its
  year extends the FY2022 vintage from the print until the 10-K (`fy_actual`, the NEE and LYB encoding, new in `build_nem.py`): FY2023 at
  $(2.97), a loss, so an excluded year, with the release's revenue, diluted shares, pre-tax margin, tax rate and franchise line; one date
  (2024-02-23). The 10-K's $(3.00) and pre-tax $(2,031)M (the release's $(1,971)M) take over from 2024-03-01. No class moves either way
  (FY2023 is a loss on both).
- **Two release layouts.** To Q4 2023 the statements give the quarter against the year-ago quarter; from Q1 2024 they give the prior
  year's four quarters and its year, then the current year's quarters (the balance sheets the quarter-ends), so each figure is read from
  its column by the quarter's position, the header asserted, and the year-ago quarter is the column the release prints ("Certain amounts
  ... reclassified to conform", as the release shows it). Diluted shares come from each release's own statement of operations (earlier
  batches read the 10-Q filed the same day; from Q1 2024 the 10-Q came days later). In 2026 the releases print no discontinued operations
  and one diluted EPS line, which is read as the continuing figure (the eps note says so).
- **The costs applicable to sales signal from Q4 2025.** The releases' reconciliation now gives only the by-product figure ("Total Gold
  CAS per ounce (by-product)"); the co-product figure, the series' line, is still printed in each release's 'Summary of Results' table
  ("Gold Co-Product CAS ($/oz)", by quarter), so the signal reads that row against its year-ago column (`cas_source`; asserted equal to
  the Q4 2024 reconciliation's $1,096 where they overlap). The by-product reading moves 1 class. The ounces signal stays consolidated gold
  ounces sold (the 'Total Newmont' line from Q4 2025).
- **Newcrest (completed 2023-11-06) and the non-core divestitures are in the figures as published**; the pro forma statements are unused.
  BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth (the UNP rule): +0.3% (Q4 2021), +5.3%, -0.2%, -9.0%, -5.6% (Q4 2022), -11.4%, -12.3%,
  -5.4%, then +23.7% (Q4 2023), +50.2%, +64.1%, +84.7% (Q3 2024: Newcrest's quarters and the gold price), +42.8% (Q4 2024), +24.5%,
  +20.8%, +20.0%, +20.6% (Q4 2025), +45.8%, +15.1%, +15.2% (Q3 2026).
- **No guide in numbers for revenue, EPS or a margin.** The outlooks are attributable gold production and CAS and AISC per ounce, and
  sustaining and development capital: display only, one quote a release cut to its own year (asserted: no quote names another year), the
  five-year production profiles, the 2023 dividend payout range ("Annualized dividend payout range of $1.40 to $1.80 per share", text
  only), the Newcrest synergies and the capital allocation frameworks not quoted.
- **Dividends** (each rate from the first filing that states it as declared): $0.55 a quarter through Q3 2022; $0.40 from the Q4 2022
  release (2023-02-23); $0.25 from the FY2023 10-K ("In February 2024, the Board declared a dividend of $0.25 per share"; the Q4 2023
  release states no rate, so $0.40 stands to 2024-02-29); $0.26 from the Q4 2025 release (2026-02-20). The releases' "$0.251" is the
  rate with a footnote marker; each record quotes the footnote's own sentence.
- **Kind: CYCLICAL** in every vintage ("The metals markets are cyclical", asserted in each 10-K). NYSE: NEM throughout (the ASX and PNGX
  listings from the Newcrest closing are display-irrelevant); Newmont Corporation throughout, no change of name.
- **Themes.** GENAI (2022-11-30) and GLP1 (2023-08-08) go live; the "why" quotes every live theme's scope, none of which names a miner.
  From the FY2023 10-K the 'why' also quotes the 10-K's own AI words (an operating tool and a cybersecurity risk: "our use of artificial
  intelligence, fleet electrification, and autonomous vehicles", then "the adoption of emerging technologies such as artificial

  CRYPTO and ENERGY_TRANSITION stay out of scope with each vintage's own words quoted (`crypto_words`, `climate_words`; the FY2023 10-K
  breaks the climate sentence at a page end, so its quote ends at "costs to comply with..."; the FY2025 10-K adds "nature-").
- **Adds nothing:** the Newcrest proposal, agreement, clearances, meeting and completion 8-Ks (2023-02-06 to 2023-11-06), the exchange

## LYB (LyondellBasell Industries): the thirty-seventh ticker, in staging, from its 2010 share issue

The LYB series is built apart from every other ticker and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/LYB.json`, generated from the filings by `retro/generators/lyb/gen_lyb.py`), builder (`retro/build_lyb.py`, the KMI
new-listing builder with LYB's encodings) and engine (`retro/templates/lyb_engine.py.tmpl`, the KMI engine with chemical and refining
signals). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an LYB model; there is no LYB profile in
`data/business_profiles.json`. Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/LYB/`.

```bash
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py index 1489393 <dir>                            # the downloads (outside the repository)
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py fetch 1489393 <dir> --from 2010-04-01 --to 2014-03-31 --forms 10-K 10-Q 8-K 8-K/A 10-12B 10-12B/A
python3 -I retro/generators/lyb/gen_lyb.py --filings <dir>                  # retro/facts/LYB.json and <dir>/checklist_lyb.json
python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py <dir>/checklist_lyb.json                 # 155/155
python3 retro/build_lyb.py --weekly 2012-02-06 2013-12-31                   # 100 dates, 2012-02-10 .. 2013-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/LYB/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series LYB
python3 retro/generators/lyb/controls_lyb.py                                # 20 controls
python3 retro/generators/lyb/sens_lyb.py <scratch>                          # the sensitivity below
for c in 2012-02-11 2012-02-29 2012-03-01 2012-04-30 2012-05-02 2012-07-27 2012-07-28 2012-10-26 2012-10-27 2013-02-01 2013-02-02 \
         2013-02-12 2013-02-13 2013-04-26 2013-04-27 2013-05-28 2013-07-26 2013-10-29 2013-10-31 2014-01-01; do
  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c LYB; done
```

### LYB 2008-2009: requested, no date can be built

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** On 2026-11-27 the owner asked for LYB 2008-2009 on the same rules. Under method
r2 **no date of 2008-2009 can be built**, and none was. Nothing was invented to fill the gap (the BKR 2018, CTVA and KMI 2008-2009
precedents). Checked against the filings, before any price or outcome was read (Yahoo was asked for its series metadata only):

- **No company and no share.** "LyondellBasell Industries N.V. was incorporated under Dutch law by deed of incorporation dated October 15,
  2009." Its first SEC filing is the Form 10 of 2010-04-28 (EDGAR submissions, CIK 1489393), and "Our capital was issued effective April
  30, 2010 in connection with our emergence from bankruptcy proceedings." The 10-K's performance graph runs "since April 30, 2010, the
  first date on which we had issued capital as a publicly traded company" (FY2010 10-K, accepted 2011-03-18 06:02 ET). Yahoo's LYB
  series starts on 2010-04-28 (`firstTradeDate` and the first point; none in 2008-2009).
- **The predecessor was private.** The 2008-2009 parent, LyondellBasell Industries AF S.C.A., was owned through a Luxembourg company
  "affiliated with Access Industries (“Access Industries”), which is a privately held industrial group based in the United States
  (“U.S.”)." (FY2010 10-K, note 1), and "From January 2009 through April 2010, LyondellBasell AF and 93 of its subsidiaries were debtors
  in jointly administered bankruptcy cases". No equity of it was listed.
- **No predecessor price under LYB (why the BKR/BHI route does not apply).** BKR's 2008-2017 dates are Baker Hughes Incorporated because
  BHI was listed on those dates and Yahoo serves its history under BKR. The listed Lyondell company of the years before, Lyondell Chemical
  Company (NYSE: LYO, CIK 842635), left the NYSE when Basell acquired it: on December 20, 2007 "each share of common stock of the Company
  outstanding immediately prior to the effective time of the Merger was converted into the right to receive $48.00, without interest, and
  requested that the NYSE file with the Securities and Exchange Commission an application on Form 25 to remove the shares from listing on
  the NYSE" (8-K accepted 2007-12-26 16:46 ET; the Form 25 of 2007-12-21 and the Form 15-12B followed). Its FY2007 10-K (accepted
  2008-03-31 07:43 ET): "There is no established public trading market for the common stock of Lyondell" and "As a privately held
  company, all of the members of Lyondell’s Board of Directors are selected by its sole shareholder, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary
  of LyondellBasell Industries". Lyondell kept filing through 2008-2009 as an issuer of public debt only. Yahoo serves nothing under LYO
  ("No data found, symbol may be delisted"). A 2008-2009 model of LyondellBasell would have no price, no P/E of its own and no per-share
  EPS of a traded share; a model of Lyondell Chemical before 2008 would be an LYO retrospective, not LYB's.

So, as the request provides, the ticker is set up anyway and its first buildable dates are built in this session, to 2013-12-31 (next
part). Sources (each quoted string checked with `verbatim.py` against its own filing, 9/9): EDGAR submissions for CIK 1489393 and CIK
842635; FY2010 10-K 0000950123-11-026580; Lyondell Chemical 8-K 0000842635-07-000164 and FY2007 10-K 0000842635-08-000019; Yahoo chart API,
LYB, LYO, LALLF and LYBAF, read 2026-11-27 (metadata only).

### LYB from the share issue: 2012-02-10 to 2013-12-31

**What could be built.** Under method r2 **the first date that can be built is 2012-02-10**; this part builds the 100 weekly dates to
2013-12-31. No date from 2010-04-30 to 2012-02-03 (93 weeks) is built: a model needs the stock's own P/E, and LyondellBasell's first
full year of EPS is 2011, published in the Q4 2011 release. Building that gap takes a new rule (an EPS anchor for a period that is not a
year, or the Successor's eight months annualized), which is the owner's call and a method note; nothing was invented to fill it (the KMI
2011 precedent).

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every filing document to the plain client name of `edgar.py` (no contact address; the owner's
email was not used). Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the FY2010-FY2012 10-Ks (selected financial
data, the MD&A's combined 2010, the statements of income and cash flows, the segment notes, the EPS notes, Items 1A and 5), the nine
earnings releases from Q3 2011 to Q3 2013 (Tables 1, 2, 8, 9 and 11), the 10-Qs of Q3 2011 and Q2 2012 (dividends), and every other
8-K of October 2011 to December 2013 by its item text and exhibits. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted
rows: each figure is read from its labelled row, the row is asserted present in its own filing, and every growth rate, margin, tax rate
and rule-T value is computed, not typed; 155 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing, and all 155 were
found. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (ET); the source ids are `LB1`-`LB3` (the 10-Ks), `LB10`-`LB18` (the
releases), `LB20`-`LB21` (the 10-Qs) and `LB30` (the 8-K of the 2013 annual meeting). Decided on 2026-11-27, before any LYB model was
built or any LYB outcome computed:

- **The listing.** LyondellBasell Industries N.V.'s ordinary shares: quoted on the Pink Sheets from 2010-04-30 ("From April 30, 2010
  until October 13, 2010, our shares they were quoted in the Pink OTC Markets, Inc."), on the NYSE as LYB "since October 14, 2010"
  (FY2010 10-K, Item 5). The window runs from 2010-04-30, the day the capital was issued (`listing.first_trading_day`, the listing rule);
  Yahoo's two points of 2010-04-28 and 2010-04-29 precede the issue and are left out. Yahoo records no split or distribution, so its
  close is the price as traded. The special dividends ($4.50 in December 2011, $2.75 in December 2012) are cash dividends, not
  distributions of shares: Yahoo leaves its close unadjusted for them, and so does the model.
- **2010 is not a year of EPS.** The FY2010 10-K reports 2010 as two periods: the Predecessor (LyondellBasell AF, January 1 to April 30)
  and the Successor (May 1 to December 31, after fresh-start accounting), with diluted EPS of $2.67 from continuing operations for the
  Successor's eight months only. It is excluded like KMI's 2011, and its days leave the P/E window ("ex-FY10"), which therefore starts on
  2011-01-03 (1.1 years on the first date, 3.0 on the last).
- **The combined 2010 is a year of revenues, never of EPS.** Each 10-K's MD&A prints the combined periods as the year ("References in
  the following discussion to results for the year ended December 31, 2010 are to the combined Successor and Predecessor periods", "a
  non-GAAP presentation", FY2010 10-K; "We had revenues of ... $41,151 million in 2010", then "$38,939 million in 2010" without the
  Berre refinery, FY2012 10-K), and the Q4 2011 release tabulates it ("Combined ... YTD"). So 2010 is in the revenue history and rule T
  as the company prints it, from the latest filing that prints it; KMI's 2007 was two periods that no filing combined.
- **Release timing.** The Q4 2011 release's 8-K was accepted 2012-02-10 10:09 ET, during the session, on a Friday: the week has no
  trading day after it, so that day's date meets it (the UNP Good Friday and SCHW rule, "released during the session"); the first date is
  2012-02-10. Q2 2012 (Friday 2012-07-27, 09:48 ET) is the same case. Q3 2012, Q4 2012, Q1 2013 and Q2 2013 (Fridays, 08:10-09:15 ET)
  were accepted before the open and date their own Fridays; Q1 2012 (Monday 2012-04-30, 11:44 ET) and Q3 2013 (Tuesday 2013-10-29, 09:46
  ET) date the next trading day. The 10-Ks are dated 2011-03-18 (06:02 ET), 2012-02-29 (13:11 ET) and 2013-02-12 (15:29 ET).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations where the filing reports it, each year from the latest filing that reports it.**
  FY2011 is $3.74 from the Q4 2011 release and the FY2011 10-K (no discontinued operations yet); the Q2 2012 release moves the Berre
  refinery to discontinued operations ("Berre refinery moved to discontinued operations; business segments have been realigned by moving
  Oxyfuels to Intermediates and Derivatives") and republishes 2011 at $4.32 from continuing operations and $48,183M of revenues, which
  restate FY2011 from that release until the FY2012 10-K (`restates` on the print, the LMT, PFE and CB print-level rule). FY2012 is
  $4.96 from the Q4 2012 release and the FY2012 10-K.
- **GAAP, not the company's adjusted EPS.** The releases print an adjusted EPS ($4.71 for 2011, $5.22 for 2012) that removes every item
  of their Table 2, including items that recur in every quarter (the warrants' mark to market, impairments, the lower of cost or market
  inventory adjustments), so it is not a figure excluding only one-offs (the NKE FY2007, AVGO, PFE and V rule).
- **The one-off test, both years kept.** FY2011: Table 2's "After-tax effect of net charges (credits)" of $567M against $2,147M of net
  income attributable to the Company; FY2012: $163M against $2,848M. Both are net charges, so the mirror test does not arise.
- **No guide in numbers.** No release, 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K of 2011-2013 guides revenue, EPS or a margin: each release's "OUTLOOK"
  is the chief executive's words. So current-FY EPS is the last full year's (the PFE rule), BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth as
  reported plus the buyback (the SO, UNP and KMI no-guide rule), and there is no margin step.
- **History.** Revenues from 2006: 2006 from the FY2010 10-K's selected data (the Predecessor, Basell without Lyondell Chemical), 2007
  from the FY2011 10-K (Lyondell Chemical from December 21, 2007), 2008-2012 from the latest 10-K (from continuing operations from the
  FY2012 10-K; 2006-2007 keep Berre, a seam). Diluted shares from 2010 (564M for the Successor's eight months, then 572M, 577M); the net
  buyback is measured from the first count to the last, so it reads as dilution (-1.1%/yr on the first three dates, -1.4%/yr from the
  FY2011 10-K, -1.1%/yr from the Q4 2012 print). The repurchase program of
  "up to 10% of the Company’s outstanding shares" (8-K of 2013-05-28) is shown in the capital-return text; its effect reaches the share
  counts as they are reported.
- **The rollover rule and the bounds rule.** To the Q4 2012 print the history has one year of EPS, so BEAR is the 0% cap, BULL takes
  BASE's rate and XBULL BULL's; from it, FY2011 ($4.32 restated) to FY2012 ($4.96) is the only change (+14.8%), so BEAR stays at the cap
  and BULL and XBULL take that rate.
- **Dividends:** each declared interim rate from the first filing that states it: $0.20 a quarter (the Q3 2011 10-Q), $0.25 (the FY2011
  10-K, paid December 16, 2011), $0.40 (the Q2 2012 10-Q), $0.50 (the 8-K of 2013-05-28: "The dividend of $0.50 per share represents a
  25% increase over the Company’s first quarter interim dividend"). The special dividends are not a rate (the SPGI 2012 rule). The FY2010
  10-K: "We have not yet paid any dividends on our shares."
- **Signals.** Five, with the house weights, each against the year-ago quarter as the release shows it: O&P–Americas operating income
  growth (0.20) and Intermediates & Derivatives operating income growth (0.20), the two segments with the largest operating income in the
  FY2010 10-K, the last 10-K before the first date (O&P–Americas $1,363M and I&D $669M of the combined 2010, ahead of O&P–EAI's $526M),
  from each release's Table 8; revenue growth (0.15), the operating margin change (0.15) and the pre-tax margin change (0.15; income from
  continuing operations before income taxes on revenues, reorganization items in, as reported), from Tables 1 and 11; the theme slot at
  2/4. From the Q2 2012 release Oxyfuels is in Intermediates & Derivatives, each release recasting its own year-ago quarter (a seam in
  the I&D series against rule T's values, which are on the old segment).
- **Thresholds by rule T over the years the filings public on 2012-02-10 report** (the FY2010 10-K and the Q4 2011 release; the bounds
  rule), each change from the latest filing that reports both years, as reported. 2008's goodwill impairments ($4,982M) made both
  segments' operating income losses, so 2009's segment changes are no growth rates and leave rule T (the KMI rule):

  | Signal | Annual values | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | O&P–Americas operating income | 2010-2011: 706.5, 36.2 % | -299 / 36 / 371 / 707 % |
  | Intermediates & Derivatives operating income | 2010-2011: 167.6, 28.8 % | -41 / 29 / 98 / 168 % |
  | revenue | 2007-2011: 29.9, 196.2, -39.2, 33.5, 24.0 % | -108 / -39 / 30 / 196 % |
  | operating margin change | 2009-2011: 1272.0, 612.0, 68.0 bp | -480 / 70 / 610 / 1270 bp |
  | pre-tax margin change | 2009-2011: 226.0, 3546.0, -1532.0 bp | -3290 / -1530 / 230 / 3550 bp |

  The 2010 values are the trough recovery and, for the pre-tax margin, the combined Predecessor's $7,365M of reorganization items (the
  discharge of liabilities and fresh-start accounting); rule T takes them as reported, so the segment and operating margin signals score
  BEAR on most quarters and the pre-tax margin signal BASE.
- **Durability: CYCLICAL, risk 2.** Each 10-K calls its own business cyclical: "Our businesses are highly cyclical, in addition to
  experiencing some less significant seasonal effects." (FY2010 and FY2011 10-Ks), "Our businesses’ results are impacted by seasonal
  effects and are highly cyclical." (FY2012 10-K), quoted in the "why" (the CB, GOOG and CAT reading). No theme in the registry is live
  for a chemicals and refining company on these dates: OFFSHORE (live throughout) is scoped to Indian IT services, CLOUD (live
  2012-10-30) to on-premise hardware and data centers, and no LYB 10-K names cloud or offshore delivery; from 2012-10-30 the "why" quotes
  every live theme's scope (the SCHW wording). ENERGY_TRANSITION, whose scope names refining, is live only from 2015-12-12. The watch
  list is empty and the builder refuses events.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the latest 10-K's segment revenues from customers (the Successor's May-December 2010
  on the three dates before the FY2011 10-K, with no prior year); the EPS check runs on the last year's pre-tax margin and tax rate.
- **The FY2010 revisions add nothing.** Three filings revise the FY2010 statements before the first date: the 8-K of 2011-06-22 (a
  guarantor note), the 8-K/A of 2011-08-15 (Revisions I and II: "the Company has revised its consolidated financial statements for the
  four months ending April 30, 2010 to correct for an overstatement of goodwill and deferred income taxes with corresponding adjustments
  to Reorganization items and Benefit from income taxes") and the 8-K of 2011-10-21 (the MD&A). They change only the Predecessor's
  January-April 2010 reorganization items, taxes and balance sheet: every figure the FY2010 vintage gives a model (revenues, diluted
  shares, cash flows, segment revenues and operating income) is identical in the revised statements (the generator asserts it), and
  rule T takes the combined 2010 from the Q4 2011 release, which reflects them. So they are not a vintage of their own.
- **Adds nothing:** the Berre 8-Ks of 2011-10-03 and 2012-01-31 (Item 2.05: the costs reach the prints), the debt, credit facility,
  receivables securitization and secondary-offering 8-Ks (the selling shareholders' underwriting agreements of 2012-2013), the officer,
  director and vote-result 8-Ks, the 8-K of 2013-06-07 on the tax residence's move to the United Kingdom and the 8-K of 2013-06-17 on
  LYB International Finance B.V.: none guides revenue, EPS or a margin.

Controls and checks (before any outcome):
- **Controls** (`controls_lyb.py`): raising each print's O&P–Americas operating income (its growth re-derived), each Q4 print's
  full-year revenue, the Q2 2012 restatement's EPS, each vintage's last revenue, each dividend and the repurchase program's text changes
  no model dated before its publication and changes the first weekly date on or after it: 20 of 20. The Q3 2011 print and the Q3 2011
  10-Q's dividend, both published before the first date, reach it as they should (the previous print's segment growth; the rate in force).
- **Leak scan:** the distinctive texts and figures of every print, vintage, dividend and source appear in no model before their
  publication (`leak_scan.py`: 11,605 pairs, 1 hit, read and cleared: the 2012-06-15 close of $38.94 matches the FY2012 10-K's 2010
  revenues of $38.939B to two decimals, a coincidence of a price). `forward_refs.py`: 0 forward references in 33 dated facts.
  `selftext.py --allow "MD&A" Ks`: 0 misses in 480 tokens (the two allowed are method words: the MD&A, and the "Ks" of "10-Ks").
- **Years after the as-of date:** none in the 100 models and reports other than the FY horizon labels.
- **`retro_tool run`:** passes on all 100 dates, with no warnings.
- **Firewall** (run after the build was committed, before any outcome): passes at the 20 cutoffs above, with 0 files changed and no
  planted text (1 to 100 dates each). The plants: a print whose segment operating income, revenue, margins, EPS, notes and raw figures
  are absurd, with absurd full-year actuals for the year after the latest vintage and a restatement of every year of the history, a
  later vintage with planted texts, figures, kind and an excluded year, a later guide, dividend, repurchase program and company name,
  and every price from the cutoff on multiplied by 10.

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **Totals: RICH 100.** The legacy tier is AVOID on all 100 dates, and robustness is 8 of 8 on every date.
- **The window.** The P/E window holds only 2011-2013 days on one or two anchors (FY11's $3.74, then $4.32 restated, then FY12's $4.96),
  so it is short and its median low: 8.8-10.3x, against a current P/E of 9.9-16.2x on the last full year's EPS, the close ranging from
  $37.04 to $80.28 ($44.75 on the first date, $80.28 on the last). The current P/E is at or above the window's 75th percentile on 91
  dates (the 90th on 83; the 42nd at its lowest), so Ratio B is infinite (the price above BULL) on 40 dates and 2.9x or more on the rest.
- **BASE follows revenue as reported, less the dilution:** +6.9%/yr on the first dates (Q4 2011 revenues +7.9%), then +6.5%, -4.4%, -16.9%
  (Q2 2012 revenues -15.5%), -11.3%, -0.0%, -10.2%, -2.4% and -2.2%/yr. BULL and XBULL take BASE's rate to the
  Q4 2012 print, then +14.8%.
- **The EPP floor** is $26-30: a 7x floor on $3.74, 6x on $4.32 (7x on the four dates of January 2013, when 2013's first low joins
  the calendar-year lows), 6x on $4.96.

Sensitivity (each call changed alone, the 100 dates rebuilt and reclassified offline with `retro_tool`'s own classifier; no outcome
consulted; `sens_lyb.py`):
- **the combined 2010 not a year of revenues**, **the revenue history from 2008** (no Basell-only 2006-2007), **the company's adjusted
  EPS** ($4.71, $5.01, $5.22), **share counts from 2011 only**, **2010's days in the P/E window on FY2011's EPS**, **every signal at its
  BEAR value** and **at its XBULL value**: no class, no tier;
- **the Q2 2012 restatement unused** (FY2011 at $3.74 until the FY2012 10-K): no class, 2 tiers.
No tested encoding moves a class: the RICH calls rest on the short window (2011-2013 days only) against a price that rose faster than the
last full year's EPS.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the combined 2010 as a year of revenues and in rule T (the company's own MD&A presentation; no class moves without it in the revenue
  history, but rule T cannot be measured for four of the five signals without it);
- 2010 excluded as two periods (the window then holds 2011 on; 2010's days at FY2011's EPS move no class);
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows 2012-2013: the two segments ranked by the FY2010 10-K's operating income, revenue and two
  GAAP margins (rule T then sets the thresholds mechanically, from two to five years that include the 2009-2010 trough and recovery);
- GAAP rather than the adjusted EPS (no class moves);
- CYCLICAL on the 10-Ks' own words;

layout (from Q1 2014 the segment reconciliation is Table 7, the income statement Table 10 and the charges Table 11, found by title; the

  2013 print, then $6.76, $8.00, $9.60, $9.15), BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth as reported plus the buyback, and there is no
  margin step.

  FY16 $9.15; the 10-Ks' Item 6 restates nothing). From Q4 2014 Table 1 adds an "Excluding LCM Impact" block (FY14 $8.92, FY15 $10.35,
  FY16 $9.20): it removes the lower of cost or market inventory adjustments, which recur (in nine of the twelve quarters from Q3 2014 to
  Q2 2017, both ways), so it is not a figure excluding only one-offs (the NKE FY2007, AVGO, PFE and V rule, as for 2011-2013's adjusted
  EPS). No release republishes a year on a new basis, so no `restates`.
- **The one-off test, every year kept.** Each Q4 release's charges table, "After-tax effect of net charges" for the year, against net
  income attributable to the Company: FY2013 $5M against $3,857M (the Q4 2013 release's Table 2), FY2014 $431M against $4,174M, FY2015 $373M
  against $4,476M, FY2016 $51M against $3,836M. All are net charges, so the mirror test does not arise. FY2013's $353M release of French
  valuation allowances (a tax benefit, the 10-K's Item 6 note) is not in the release's table; against $3,857M it meets neither test.
- **Release timing.** The Q4 2013 8-K was accepted on Friday 2014-01-31 at 10:13 ET, during the session: the week has no trading day
  after it, so that Friday meets it (the Q4 2011 rule, "released during the session"). The Friday releases of 2014-2017 (Q2 and Q3 2014,
  Q1 and Q3 2015, Q1 and Q2 2016, Q4 2016, Q1-Q3 2017) were accepted before the open and date their own Fridays; the Tuesday releases
  (Q1 2014, Q4 2014, Q2 2015, Q4 2015, Q3 2016) date the next trading day. The 10-Ks are dated 2014-02-20 (14:15 ET), 2015-02-18 (accepted
  2015-02-17 17:12 ET), 2016-02-17 (accepted 2016-02-16 16:21 ET) and 2017-02-17 (13:01 ET).
- **History.** Each vintage takes Item 6's five years from its own 10-K (from continuing operations) and earlier years from the latest
  earlier vintage, the ten fiscal years to the latest one (2006 leaves with the FY2016 10-K). 2010 stays the FY2012 10-K's combined
  $38,939M: the FY2013 and FY2014 10-Ks show its two periods, whose sum the generator asserts equal to it, and no later 10-K prints the
  combined year. Diluted shares from each EPS note (570M, 521M, 466M, 420M); the net buyback, measured from the Successor's 2010 count,
  reads as dilution to the FY2013 10-K (-1.1%/yr, then -0.4%/yr) and as a buyback from it (+2.0%/yr, +3.9%/yr, +5.0%/yr in BASE).
- **Dividends:** each interim rate from the first filing that states it, all releases: $0.60 (Q4 2013, 2014-01-31: "Increased interim
  dividend by 20 percent to $0.60 per share"), $0.70 (Q1 2014), $0.78 (Q2 2015: "78 cents per share"), $0.85 (Q2 2016), $0.90 (Q2 2017).

  10% of the Company’s shares" (8-Ks dated 2014-04-22, 2015-05-12, 2016-05-17, 2017-06-01), after the 2013 program.

  release shows it. Segment operating income is tabulated in every release of the range; from the FY2016 10-K the segment note's measure
  is EBITDA (ASC 280), which leaves the release-based signal as it was. The thresholds stay rule T's of 2012-02-10, measured on the
  2007-2011 values that include the 2009-2010 trough and recovery, so the segment and operating margin signals score at or near BEAR on
  most quarters (the batch's largest call, below).
- **Durability: CYCLICAL, risk 2.** From the FY2013 10-K the risk factor reads "Our business operations are subject to the cyclical and
  volatile nature of the supply-demand balance in the chemical and refining industries." (each of the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks), quoted in
  the "why"; "highly cyclical" no longer appears, so the key trigger line says "cyclical and volatile" from the FY2013 vintage.
- **Themes.** ECOMMERCE (live 2015-01-01) and STREAMING (2015-08-04) name no chemicals or refining business, and no LYB 10-K names
  e-commerce or streaming (nor cloud; the FY2013 10-K's one "Offshore" is the name of an Iranian company in the Section 13(r) note); the

  U.S. Gulf Coast." (each vintage's own wording), and its greenhouse gas risk factor: "Compliance with these or other changes in laws,

  increase our costs or reduce demand for products we produce." That is the XOM, SO and KMI case (in scope, company-acknowledged, no
  market read): CYCLICAL stands, the watch list quotes the vintage's 10-K (`refining_quote`, `transition_quote`, `tenk_label`), and the
  theme signal, its name and the summary follow it. Text only: no factor pair, the theme slot at 2/4 (new for LYB; the KMI encoding).
- **Adds nothing:** the senior notes, guaranteed notes, credit facility, securitization and indenture 8-Ks, the officer, director and
  compensation 8-Ks (the CEO succession of 2014-2015 included), the November 2013 secondary offering, the vote results beyond the
  repurchase authority: none guides revenue, EPS or a margin. No acquisition or disposal changes the prints beyond what they report

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **Totals: RICH 183, CHEAP 21, FAIR 5.** RICH on all 52 dates of 2014 but one (FAIR 2014-12-12) and all 53 of 2015; CHEAP on 2016-02-03
  and 2016-02-12 and on 19 dates from 2017-03-24 to 2017-08-18; FAIR on 2016-02-19 and 2016-06-24 to 2016-07-08. The legacy tier is AVOID
  on 36 dates, all in 2014 (the last 2014-10-10), BUY on 124, ACCUMULATE 26, WATCHLIST 23. Robustness 8 of 8 on 129 dates.
- **The window** grows from 3.0 to 7.0 years ex-FY10 and its median stays 9.1-10.1x; the current P/E on the last full year's EPS runs
  from 17.0x (early 2014, on FY12's $4.96) to 7.8x (mid-2016), at the 8th to 100th percentile of the window; the close from $70.61 to
  $114.59 ($78.71 on the first date, $110.32 on the last).
- **BASE follows revenue as reported, plus the buyback:** -2.2%/yr on the first dates, +0.0 to +8.7%/yr in 2014, -5.6% after Q4 2014,
  -22.5% to -28.9%/yr through 2015 as crude fell (Q1-Q4 2015 revenues -24.5% to -31.3%), -7.7% to -16.0% in 2016, then +14.6% to +30.0%/yr
  in 2017. BEAR is the 0% cap to the Q4 2016 print, then FY15 to FY16's -4.7%; BULL and XBULL the history's CAGR and best two-year run.
- **The EPP floor** is $40-67.
- So the RICH calls of 2015 rest on BASE's negative revenue growth (a falling-revenue quarter carried forward as EPS growth), the
  signals' low scores and a current P/E at the 52nd-96th percentile of the window; the CHEAP calls of 2017 come with BASE at +14.6% to
  +30.0%/yr and the P/E near the window median.

### LYB 2022-2026: three-year 10-Ks, no consolidated operating income in any release, the refinery exit, FY2025 a loss and excluded, the last date 2026-11-20

255 weekly dates, 2022-01-07 to 2026-11-20 (52, 52, 52, 52, 47), on the same fact sheet, generator, builder and method (r2), with the
rule-T thresholds of 2012-02-10 frozen. Built on 2026-11-27 at the owner's request ("find newest code. do retrospective analysis for LYB,
2022-2026. same rules as before"), **in a new session that did not open the 2012-2021 outcomes, `SERIES.md` or `FINDINGS.md`**; every
decision below applies a rule that existed before (the house rules and the 2012-2021 encodings) or is disclosed as new. The newest code
is the coordinating session's branch (`claude/sharp-albattani-rdvlgi`: LYB to 2021-12-31, NEM to 2017, CHTR 2019-2021), checked out as
the base; nothing else was merged in. The series was built on Friday 2026-11-27 during the session (Yahoo's bar for that day is not a
close), so the range ends on 2026-11-22 and the last date is 2026-11-20 (the CRM, SCHW and NEE 2022-2026 rule). A rebuild after a later
close adds dates; it does not move these. The newest dates have no outcome yet.

```bash
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py fetch 1489393 <dir> --from 2007-01-01 --to 2026-11-27 --forms 10-K 10-Q 8-K 8-K/A 10-12B 10-12B/A
python3 -I retro/generators/lyb/gen_lyb.py --filings <dir>                  # 61 prints, 16 vintages, 17 dividends, 16 repurchase authorities
python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py <dir>/checklist_lyb.json                 # 989/989
python3 retro/build_lyb.py --weekly 2012-02-06 2013-12-31                   # regression: the 100 earlier models byte for byte
python3 retro/build_lyb.py --weekly 2014-01-01 2017-12-31                   # regression: the 209 earlier models byte for byte
python3 retro/build_lyb.py --weekly 2018-01-01 2021-12-31                   # regression: the 209 earlier models byte for byte
python3 retro/build_lyb.py --weekly 2022-01-03 2026-11-22                   # 255 dates, 2022-01-07 .. 2026-11-20
python3 retro/generators/lyb/controls_lyb.py 2022-01-03 2026-11-22          # 164 controls
python3 retro/generators/lyb/sens_lyb.py <scratch> 2022-01-03 2026-11-22    # the sensitivity below
for c in <each fact date of 2022-2026 and the day after it, and 2026-11-23>; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c LYB; done   # 61 cutoffs
```

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every filing document to the plain client name of `edgar.py` (no contact address; the owner's
email was not used). Read by the session's model directly: the twenty earnings releases of Q4 2021 to Q3 2026 (Exhibit 99.1: Table 1,
the EBITDA reconciliation, the identified items, the outlook and capital-return text; Exhibit 99.2: the segment overview tables), the
fifteen 10-Qs of Q1 2022 to Q3 2026 (the statement of income; the dividend tables searched for each rate), the FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks (the
statements of income and cash flows, the EPS note, the segment note, the dividend table and MD&A dividend lines, Items 1 and 1A), and
every other 8-K of January 2022 to November 2026 by its items and exhibits. **Not read:** the proxy statements, the investor and Capital
Markets Day presentations and call transcripts (not filed), and the debt offering documents beyond their 8-Ks' item text. The generator
keeps its 2012-2021 code; a new block reads the 2022-2026 layouts by table title, and the regenerated sheet's 2012-2021 facts are an
exact prefix of the new one (asserted, with `cmp` of the old generator's output against the committed sheet first). Sources `LB110`-`LB114`
(the FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks), `LB120`-`LB139` (the releases), `LB140`-`LB154` (the 10-Qs), `LB160`-`LB164` (the annual meetings' 8-Ks).

- **No guide in numbers, again.** Every release's "OUTLOOK" is words (demand, margins, maintenance; from 2025 expected operating rates,
  which are no revenue, EPS or margin); no 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K guides revenue, EPS or a margin. Read and set aside: the Q1 2023
  release's 2027 targets ("Launched new strategy targeting net income(b) of $6.3 billion and $10 billion of normalized EBITDA(a)(b) by
  2027", footnote (b): "Reflects a 2022 year-end asset portfolio with 2013-2022 historical average margins and operating rates"), a
  mid-cycle aspiration four years out, no current-year field (the LLY mid-term floors rule); the refinery exit 8-K of 2022-04-21 (Item
  2.05, cost ranges); the Value Enhancement Program's and the Cash Improvement Plan's EBITDA and cash targets; the NATPET, EO&D, Dutch PO
  and European asset sale 8-Ks. So the last full year's GAAP EPS stands (FY20's $4.25 to the Q4 2021 print, then $16.75 and $16.77,
  $11.81 and $11.83, $6.46 and $6.48, $4.15 and $4.14, then $4.39 restated), BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth as reported plus
  the buyback, and there is no margin step.
- **No release prints the consolidated operating income (new encoding for the fourth quarters, disclosed).** From Q4 2021 the releases
  are Exhibit 99.1 (Table 1 and the EBITDA reconciliation) and Exhibit 99.2 (segment operating income); none has a statement of income or
  a segment reconciliation with a consolidated row. For Q1-Q3 the operating income comes from the quarter's 10-Q, each accepted the same
  Friday during the session (12:14-14:29 ET; `oi_source`, the 2018-2021 rule; the generator asserts the dates equal and the revenues
  equal the release's). The fourth quarter has no 10-Q and no filing prints a fourth-quarter operating income (the 10-Ks have no
  quarterly data), so **a Q4 print's operating margin is n/r** (None, scored at BASE) through `lyb2_engine.py.tmpl`, the None-tolerant
  copy (the BKR, SPGI, SCHW and NEE `nr_engine` encoding), used only when the latest print has a None margin. Deriving it as the 10-K's
  year less the Q3 10-Q's nine months (the CRM and NEM derivation) is a sensitivity (2 classes).
- **The pre-tax income.** Income from continuing operations plus the provision for income taxes from the EBITDA reconciliation, as in
  2018-2021, through Q4 2024 (for Q1-Q3 the generator asserts it equals the 10-Q's income from continuing operations before income taxes).
  From Q1 2025 the reconciliation starts from net income (the refining business discontinued, its results an identified item), so Q1-Q3
  take the 10-Q's line and **Q4 2025's pre-tax margin is n/r**; FY2025 between its release and its 10-K (three dates) keeps the FY2024
  vintage's pre-tax margin and tax rate (the builder says so in the model), as the release prints no pre-tax income for the year.
- **EPS: GAAP diluted from continuing operations where the filing reports it, each year from the latest filing that reports it.** The
  10-Ks give FY21 $16.77, FY22 $11.83, FY23 $6.48, FY24 $4.14, and the FY2025 10-K restates FY23 to $5.68 and FY24 to $4.39 (the refining
  business discontinued: as published, the earlier vintages unchanged) with FY25 $(2.48). Between a Q4 release and its 10-K the year is
  the release's figure on net income (FY21 $16.75, FY22 $11.81, FY23 $6.46, FY24 $4.15, FY25 $(2.34)). The company's EPS "excluding
  identified items" removes the LCM adjustments and the "asset write-downs in excess of $10 million in aggregate for the period", which
  recur (impairments or write-downs in each year of 2021-2025), so it is not a figure excluding only one-offs (the 2014-2021 rule); GAAP
  stands (the batch's largest EPS call: 26 classes).
- **The one-off test, FY2021-FY2024 kept; FY2025 a loss, excluded.** From Q4 2021 each Q4 release's Table 2 lists the identified items
  after tax ("Net income excluding identified items", from Q4 2021 "excluding LCM and impairment"), so the test takes that table's total,
  charges net of benefits (the 2014-2017 table rule): FY2021 $481M against $5,617M (the text's $102M of debt extinguishment costs, not in
  the table, would leave it kept), FY2022 $213M against $3,889M, FY2023 $717M against $2,121M, FY2024 $734M against $1,367M. All are net
  charges, so the mirror test does not arise. **FY2025** is a loss ($(2.34) on net income in the Q4 2025 release, $(2.48) from continuing
  operations in the FY2025 10-K), so it has no P/E and is excluded as the latest year, its days out of the window ("10-yr ex-FY25"; the MU
  FY2003 and NEM FY2007 rule; a new `eps_gaap` field carries the loss for the builder's check). From the Q4 2025 print the current year is
  FY2026 and FY24's EPS stands ($4.14, then $4.39 from the FY2025 10-K).
- **History.** Item 6 is "Reserved" in the FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks, so each vintage takes three years from its own statement of income, EPS
  note and cash flow statement (the SCHW and NEE 2022 encoding), earlier years from the latest earlier vintage, the ten fiscal years to
  the latest one. **New: the EPS history is cut to the ten years too** (no vintage had held more than ten years of EPS before; 2011 leaves
  with the FY2021 10-K, and 2010's exclusion note with it): keeping 2011 on moves 10 classes (sensitivity). The FY2025 10-K's revenues are
  from continuing operations without the refining business for 2023-2025 (2023 $33,336M against the FY2023 10-K's $41,107M); 2016-2022
  keep it (a seam, as published).
- **The refinery exit and Q1 2025.** "In February 2025, we ceased business operations at our Houston refinery. Accordingly, our refining
  business, previously disclosed as the Refining segment, is reported as a discontinued operation." (Q1 2025 release); from it each release
  shows its year-ago quarter without refining (noted on the Q1-Q4 2025 prints), and the segment tables have five segments.
- **Q3 2026 (new encoding, disclosed).** Exhibit 99.2 of the Q3 2026 release prints no third quarter 2025 column (the quarter, the previous
  quarter, then the nine months). The segment signals take the year-ago quarter as the Q3 2025 release printed it (O&P–Americas $246M,
  I&D $194M; the LMT year-ago-release rule), and the generator asserts that the Q3 2026 release's nine months of 2025 equal the Q3 2025
  release's (no recast). Both n/r instead moves 1 class.
- **Adds nothing:** the 8-K/A of 2024-11-01 (accepted 15:04 ET, the release's day) re-files Q3 2024's Exhibit 99.2 to correct one word of
  its text ("438 million shares" to "438 thousand shares"; asserted the only change); the 8-Ks of 2023-03-07 (2020-2022 on the segment
  structure effective January 1, 2023) and 2023-05-12 (the FY2022 10-K's items recast for it) change segments only, and the revenues, EPS
  and shares a model reads are the FY2022 10-K's (asserted), so they are not a vintage of their own (the UNH 2011-05-23 segment recast
  precedent); the special dividend of $5.20 (8-K of 2022-05-31) is not a rate, and Yahoo's close is unadjusted for it (no split or
  distribution in the series).
- **Release timing.** All twenty releases were accepted before the open (06:31-06:51 ET) on Fridays and date their own day.
  The 10-Ks are dated 2022-02-25 (accepted 2022-02-24 16:32 ET), 2023-02-23 (13:54 ET), 2024-02-22 (15:28 ET), 2025-02-27 (14:10 ET) and
  2026-02-20 (14:59 ET).
- **Dividends:** each interim rate from the first filing that states it: $1.19 (the Q2 2022 10-Q, 2022-07-29: "Dividends - common stock
  ($1.19 per share)"), $1.25 (the Q2 2023 release), $1.34 (the Q2 2024 release), $1.37 (the Q2 2025 10-Q), $0.69 (the FY2025 10-K, 2026-02-20:
  "In February 2026, we declared a quarterly dividend of $0.69 per share, representing a $0.68 per share reduction from our fourth quarter
  2025 dividend."). The vintages' rates are each 10-K's dividend table's December row (FY2025: the $0.69 sentence).
- **Repurchase authorities** (display only, the share counts carry them): each annual meeting's program of up to 10% of the issued share
  capital (8-Ks of 2022-05-27, 2023-05-19, 2024-05-24, 2025-05-23, 2026-05-22); the model text gives the share count only.
- **Durability: CYCLICAL, risk 2,** on each 10-K's risk factor: "... in the chemical and refining industries." (FY2021-FY2023), "...
  in the chemical industry." (FY2024, FY2025), quoted in the "why".
- **Themes.** **GENAI** (live 2022-11-30) and **GLP1** (live 2023-08-08) join the live themes the builder quotes: no FY2021-FY2025 10-K
