## CHTR (Charter Communications): the thirty-eighth ticker, in staging, built from 2019-02-01 (to 2026-11-20 so far)

The CHTR series is set up apart from every other ticker and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/CHTR.json`, generated by `retro/generators/chtr/gen_chtr.py` from the filings and extended with 2014-2017 by
`gen_chtr_1417.py`), builder (`retro/build_chtr.py`, a gate that
decides whether method r2 can build a date and writes nothing when it cannot) and engine (`retro/templates/chtr_engine.py.tmpl`, a copy
of the CMCSA cable engine with every signal threshold unset, so no CMCSA value is carried and no model can run on it). The method is
still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker (CMCSA included) enters CHTR's files, and neither does any 2026
profile in `data/business_profiles.json`. Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/CHTR/`, which holds only `GATE.md`, the builder's
refusal of each date.

```bash
python3 retro/build_chtr.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2009-12-31                  # 105 dates, every one refused, nothing written
python3 retro/build_chtr.py --weekly 2010-01-01 2013-12-31                  # 209 dates, every one refused, nothing written
python3 retro/build_chtr.py --weekly 2014-01-01 2017-12-31                  # 209 dates, every one refused, nothing written
python3 retro/build_chtr.py --weekly 2018-01-01 2021-12-31                  # 56 refused, 153 built ("CHTR 2018-2021")
python3 retro/build_chtr.py --weekly 2022-01-03 2026-11-22                  # 255 built ("CHTR 2022-2026")
for c in 2008-02-27 2009-01-01 2009-03-16 2009-04-07 2009-12-01 2010-01-01 2010-03-01 2010-09-14 2011-03-01 2012-02-27 \
         2013-02-22 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CHTR; done   # the gate's firewall (below)
for c in 2014-03-01 2015-02-05 2015-02-24 2016-02-04 2016-02-10 2016-05-18 2017-02-16 2017-06-30 2018-01-01; do
    python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CHTR; done                           # its 2014-2017 cutoffs ("CHTR 2014-2017")
python3 retro/generators/chtr/controls_chtr.py                              # the gate's controls, 2008-2017
```

From 2019-02-01 the dates pass the gate and are built (the next part's commands; "CHTR 2018-2021").

### CHTR 2008-2009: requested, no date can be built (nor any to 2013-12-31)

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** On 2026-11-27 the owner asked for CHTR 2008-2009 on the same rules, and the
coordinating session asked, if none could be built, for the ticker to be set up anyway and its first buildable dates up to 2013-12-31
built. Under method r2 **no weekly date from 2008-01-04 to 2013-12-31 can be built** (314 dates), so none was, and nothing was invented
to fill the gap (the BKR 2018, CTVA and KMI precedents). Checked against the filings, before any price level or outcome was read (Yahoo
was read for its CHTR series' first date and trading days only):

- **No positive year to anchor a P/E (the loss rule of F, MU and CRM).** Charter Communications, Inc. (CIK 1091667, Nasdaq: CHTR) has a
  loss per share in every fiscal year its 10-Ks report, from the 1999 listing year to 2013. Diluted EPS as each Item 6 table prints it:
  1999 $(2.22), 2000 $(3.80), 2001 $(4.33), 2002 $(8.55), 2003 $(0.82) (FY2003 10-K); 2004 $(14.47), 2005 $(3.13), 2006 $(4.13), 2007
  $(4.39), 2008 $(6.56) (FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks; the FY2009 10-K restates 2006 and 2007 for the convertible debt guidance to $(4.38) and
  $(4.17), 2008 unchanged); then the Successor's 2010 $(2.09), 2011 $(3.39), 2012 $(3.05) and 2013 $(1.65) (FY2010-FY2013 10-Ks). A loss has no P/E, and
  no year in any vintage is positive, so no history can anchor the window, the EPP floor or the scenarios.
- **The two positive periods of 2009 are not years (the CTVA 2017 rule).** The FY2009 10-K reports 2009 as two periods: the
  Predecessor's eleven months to 2009-11-30 ($12.61 diluted, $30.00 basic) and the Successor's one month to 2009-12-31 ($0.02). The
  eleven months are also distorted: their $9,748M of income before income taxes includes the gain due to Plan effects ($6,818M) and the
  gain due to fresh start accounting adjustments ($5,659M), without which they are a loss (the mirror of the AAPL FY2002 test), and their
  per-share figures belong to the cancelled stock. The 10-K itself says the post-emergence information "is not comparable to our financial
  information from prior periods".
- **No Charter close in 2008-2009 (the listing rule).** Yahoo's CHTR series is the Successor's Class A common stock from its first point,
  2010-01-05 (`firstTradeDate`); it serves nothing under CHTR before that, and nothing under CHTRQ or CCMM. The Class A traded in 2008
  (the FY2007 10-K: "Charter’s Class A common stock is quoted on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol “CHTR.”"), fell below
  NASDAQ's $1.00 bid (8-K of 2008-04-18), was suspended after the 2009-03-27 Chapter 11 petitions ("trading of the Company's Class A
  common stock will be suspended at the opening of business on April 7, 2009", 8-K of 2009-03-31; Form 25-NSE of 2009-04-22), traded on
  the OTC Bulletin Board or the Pink Sheets, and was cancelled on the Plan's Effective Date, 2009-11-30 (Form 15-12G of 2009-12-02). The
  new Class A was quoted on the OTC Bulletin Board as "CCMM" from December 2009 (FY2009 10-K) and listed on the NASDAQ Global Select
  Market as CHTR on 2010-09-14 (Form 8-A12B; FY2010 10-K).
- **From the emergence, only the Successor's years count (the BKR 2018 rule).** A date from 2009-11-30 prices the new shares, so the
  Predecessor's years (losses in any case) are not their history; the Successor's first full year is 2010, a loss, and so are 2011-2013.

So 2008-2009 fails twice (no close, no positive year) and 2010-2013 once (no positive year). The fallback range of 2010-2013 is the
coordinator's; it too gives nothing. The first date that could be built lies after 2013-12-31 and was **not determined** in this session:
the FY2013 10-K (2014-02-21) is the last filing read, and finding it means reading later filings, which is a new batch and the owner's
call.

**What was set up.** The fact sheet holds only what decides buildability: the Item 6 history of nine 10-K vintages (FY2003, FY2006,
FY2007, FY2008, FY2009, FY2010, FY2011, FY2012, FY2013: revenues, diluted EPS and EPS from continuing operations where printed, diluted
shares, each period with its months and its issuer as that filing names it), the FY2009 10-K's two gains and its comparability sentence,
eight listing facts, two 10-Ks' words that no dividend was paid ("Charter has not paid stock or cash dividends on any of its
common stock", FY2007; "Predecessor and Charter have not paid ...", FY2009) and the price basis. No print, guide, signal, rule-T value or theme event is transcribed;
the builder stops at any date that passes the gate rather than build from a partial sheet. The engine's signals (video customers,
revenue, operating cash flow margin, capital intensity, operating margin) are placeholders from the cable sibling with thresholds unset:
choosing CHTR's signals and deriving their rule-T values from Charter's own 1997-2006 filings is the first buildable batch's decision.
"Charter Spectrum" (2014-02-21), "Liberty Broadband" (2014-10-10) and "Spectrum Mobile" (2017-12-22) join the anachronism list, each at
the first hit of EDGAR full-text search under CIK 1091667 (approximate); no model contains any of them.

Decided here (no outcome exists to consult):
- **Vintage dates.** Each 10-K is dated by its acceptance time (ET): FY2003 2004-03-16 (2004-03-15 16:55, after the close), FY2006
  2007-02-28, FY2007 2008-02-27, FY2008 2009-03-16 (14:54, during the session), FY2009 2010-03-01 (2010-02-26 16:43, after the close),
  FY2010 2011-03-01, FY2011 2012-02-27, FY2012 2013-02-22, FY2013 2014-02-21 (each before the open). The Q4 releases were not
  transcribed: each was accepted the same morning as its 10-K or after it (the Q4 2009 release on 2010-03-02), so no year's EPS was
  public earlier than its vintage. The FY2004 and FY2005 10-Ks were not read: no 2008-2013 date can use them (the FY2006 10-K supersedes
  them before 2008-01-04).
- **Labels.** The vintages filed before the emergence name the issuer "Charter Communications, Inc.", as those filings do; "Predecessor"
  and "Successor" appear only from the FY2009 10-K, which introduces them (a self-text scan caught the first draft's use of them on
  earlier facts, and it was corrected before any commit).
- **The Successor's December 2009.** One month is not a year, and annualizing it ($0.02 to about $0.24) would be a new rule; so would
  anchoring on the eleven months. Either is the owner's call and a method note.

Checks (no model exists, so `retro_tool.py run`, outcomes, the index and the series table have nothing to process; `staging/
retrospective/index.json` gains no row):
- **Verbatim:** 56 of 56 strings (every Item 6 header and row behind a figure, the two gains, and every quoted listing and dividend sentence), each
  against its own filing (`python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py`).
- **Forward references** (`forward_refs.py CHTR`): 0 in 33 dated facts. **Self-text** (`selftext.py CHTR`): 2 misses of 139 tokens, both
  figures the generator computes in the FY2009 vintage's note ($12,477M, the sum of the two gains, and $2,729M, the loss without them).
  **Leak scan:** not applicable (no model to scan).
- **Controls:** setting each vintage's latest full year to a positive EPS changes the gate's result for exactly the weekly dates from that
  vintage's publication to the next vintage (or to the emergence, for the pre-emergence vintages), and lets them pass the gate only where a
  Charter close exists and the year is the Successor's (FY2010-FY2012 vintages: 52, 51 and 46 dates): 9 of 9 vintages behave so.
- **Firewall** (the gate's version, in `firewall.py`'s CHTR branch: in memory, a later vintage with a positive year for both issuers and a
  later listing): at the 12 cutoffs above no refusal of a date before the cutoff changes, and every date between the planted vintage and
  the next real one changes (the control): all 12 pass.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight (the builder knows what Charter's stock and earnings did after 2013):
- that the partial periods of 2009 are not years (the CTVA 2017 rule applied by this session; the alternatives are named above);
- that the Successor's dates use only the Successor's years (the BKR 2018 rule; moot while every year is a loss);
- stopping at the gate rather than transcribing 2008-2013 prints that no model would use;
- the placeholder signal names in the engine template, chosen by a builder who knows the cable industry's later course (no threshold
  is set, and no model runs on them).

The SEC documents came from `www.sec.gov` with `edgar.py`'s plain client name (no contact address); every filing was read by the session's
model. No outcome was computed, so there is no `FINDINGS.md`.

### CHTR 2014-2017: requested, no date can be built

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** On 2026-11-27 the owner asked for CHTR 2014-2017 on the same rules; the
coordinating session asked for the series to start at its first full year that can anchor a P/E (the KMI and CTVA "no date precedes the
first full year" precedent, the F, MU and CRM loss rules), with no new 2009 rule, and, if no 2014-2017 date could be built either, for the
gate to be extended through 2017 and the batch to stop there. Under method r2 **no weekly date from 2014-01-03 to 2017-12-29 can be built**
(209 dates), so none was, the engine stays as it was (every threshold unset, no signal chosen, no rule-T value derived) and the gate now
refuses all 523 weekly dates of 2008-2017, each with its reason (`GATE.md`). The first buildable date lies after 2017-12-31 and was **not
determined**: FY2017's Q4 release and 10-K were filed in 2018 and were not read in this batch, as the coordinator's scope ends with 2017.
Checked against the filings, before any price level or outcome was read (Yahoo was read for its trading days and its event list only):

- **Every year to 2015 is a loss (the loss rule).** Diluted EPS as each Item 6 table prints it: 2014 $(1.70) (FY2014 10-K; the Q4 2014
  release prints the same figure 19 days earlier) and 2015 $(2.43) (FY2015 10-K and the Q4 2015 release), beside the Successor's
  2010-2013 losses of the 2008-2009 section. The FY2016 10-K recasts every per-share figure for the Parent Merger Exchange Ratio
  ("Weighted average number of shares outstanding for all periods presented has been recast to reflect the application of the Parent
  Merger Exchange Ratio."): 2012 $(3.38), 2013 $(1.83), 2014 $(1.88), 2015 $(2.68), all still losses.
- **FY2016, the one positive year, is distorted by a listed one-off benefit (the mirror of the AAPL FY2002 test).** Diluted EPS $15.94 on
  net income attributable to Charter shareholders of $3,522M: income before income taxes $820M, an income tax benefit of $2,925M, $223M to
  the noncontrolling interests. The benefit is "approximately $3.3 billion" of Legacy Charter's valuation allowance reversed after the TWC
  Transaction's deferred tax liabilities made the deferred tax assets realizable, and the 10-K lists it as a one-off itself: "absent
  non-recurring impacts such as the reversal of the income tax valuation allowance in the second quarter of 2016, we may incur net losses
  in the future." Without it the year's income is $222M, so the listed benefit ($3,300M) exceeds the income without it and reported EPS is
  more than double the EPS without it. No filing publishes a figure excluding only it, so FY2016 is excluded like a depressed year, as the
  latest year (method r2, "A year distorted by one-off benefits"). The test is met on every reading of the filing's own figures, by a
  wide margin: the tax note's $3,171M change in valuation allowance against $351M; the reversal plus the $899M of other pension benefits
  less the $900M of merger and restructuring costs and the $111M loss on extinguishment of debt (each pre-tax item taken whole, the CB
  FY2005 netting), $3,188M against $334M.
- **The Q4 2016 release's pro forma figure is not an anchor.** It prints 2016 diluted EPS of $3.91 "Pro Forma" ("Pro forma results reflect
  certain acquisitions of cable systems in 2016 as if they occurred as of the earliest period presented."): Legacy TWC and Legacy Bright
  House added from 2015-01-01, not the company's figure excluding only one-offs, so it is unused (the CB, SCHW and LLY pro forma rule).
- **No guide in numbers.** No 8-K exhibit of 2014-2017 guides revenue, EPS or a margin (the exhibits searched for "guidance" and
  "outlook" and for EPS outlook wording; the hits are the 2014 transaction presentations and agreements, a 2015 Form S-4 amendment
  and Bright House's 2015 financial statements, none with an EPS outlook for Charter), so nothing could stand in for a year's EPS even
  if the method allowed it.

So 2014-2016 fail the anchor (losses to 2015, FY2016 distorted) and 2017 too (FY2016 is still the latest year on every date to
2017-12-29). Every date of 2014-2017 has a Charter close (Yahoo's CHTR series, NASDAQ: CHTR throughout).

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every filing document to `edgar.py`'s plain client name (no contact address; the owner's email
was not used). Read by the session's model directly, with no delegated transcription: the FY2014, FY2015 and FY2016 10-Ks (Items 5 and 6,
the MD&A's overview, results of operations, other operating expenses and income taxes, the income tax note), the Q4 2014, Q4 2015 and Q4
2016 releases (the summaries and the addendum's statements of operations), and the Q2 2016 release's valuation allowance sentences. The
other 8-K exhibits were searched by keyword as above; the 10-Qs were downloaded and not read (no quarter can anchor a year). The sheet is
extended by `retro/generators/chtr/gen_chtr_1417.py`, which reads each figure from its labelled row, asserts each quotation in its own
filing, computes the one-off test, refuses an input sheet holding any fact after 2014-02-21, asserts every earlier fact unchanged and only
appends (the source ids `CH15`-`CH17` for the 10-Ks, `CH18`-`CH20` for the releases). Decided on 2026-11-27, before any CHTR outcome
existed (none was computed):

- **Vintage dates.** The FY2014 10-K was accepted 2015-02-23 19:13 ET and the FY2015 10-K 2016-02-09 19:19 ET, both after the close, so
  they are dated 2015-02-24 and 2016-02-10; the FY2016 10-K 2017-02-16 07:10 ET, before the open. The Q4 releases were accepted before the
  open on 2015-02-05 (08:03 ET), 2016-02-04 (08:06 ET) and 2017-02-16 (07:05 ET).
- **The Q4 releases' years (`q4_actuals`).** A Q4 release's full year extends the vintage from its own date until the 10-K that reports
  the year (the vintage rule every builder applies to a Q4 print): FY2014 from 2015-02-05 (3 weekly dates before the 10-K), FY2015 from
  2016-02-04 (1 date), FY2016 the same morning as its 10-K (no date). Each release's year equals its 10-K's (the generator asserts the
  revenues, net income and EPS). The 2008-2013 vintages had no such gap, as each Q4 release was accepted with or after its 10-K. The refusals
  of 2008-2013 are byte-identical to the 2008-2009 batch's.
- **Labels (`priced_issuers`).** The FY2014-FY2016 10-Ks print only the years after the emergence (2010 on) and name no Predecessor or
  Successor, so each of their periods is a year of the priced shares, and the gate's text names the issuer as those filings do
  ("Charter Communications, Inc."). From the FY2016 10-K the issuer is the new Charter of the 2016-05-18 Parent Merger, which reports
  Legacy Charter's years as its own; the shares stayed NASDAQ: CHTR ("Charter’s Class A common stock is listed on the NASDAQ Global Select
  Market under the symbol “CHTR.”", FY2014-FY2016 10-Ks), so the BKR 2018 rule (a new company's history) does not arise.
- **The Parent Merger Exchange Ratio (`parent_merger`), recorded and not encoded.** Each Legacy Charter Class A share became 0.9042 of a
  new Charter share on 2016-05-18 (FY2016 10-K). Yahoo's CHTR series records no split or other event for it, and the FY2016 10-K recasts
  every earlier per-share figure. No date is built, so no price encoding was chosen; the batch that builds the first date whose P/E window
  holds days before 2016-05-18 must decide one first (the splits and distributions rules).
- **No dividend.** "Charter has not paid stock or cash dividends on any of its common stock." (FY2016 10-K, `no_dividend`.)
- **The gate (`retro/build_chtr.py`)**, extended in three places and in its docstring: the Q4 actuals, the priced issuers, and the one-off
  test (`one_off_tests` on the vintage and on the release: a positive year whose listed one-offs distort it, with no published figure
  excluding only them, does not anchor). The builder still stops at any date that passes the gate rather than build from a partial sheet.

Checks (no model exists, so `retro_tool.py run`, outcomes, the index and the series table have nothing to process; `staging/
retrospective/index.json` gains no row):
- **Verbatim:** 48 of 48 strings (every Item 6 header and row behind a figure, the release rows, the statement-of-operations, tax and
  other-operating-expense rows behind the one-off test, every quotation), each against its own filing (`python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py`).
- **Forward references** (`forward_refs.py CHTR`): 0 in 50 dated facts (a first draft of the pro forma note cited a precedent by a later
  year, "SCHW 2020", and was corrected before any commit). **Self-text** (`selftext.py CHTR --from 2014-02-22`, 91 filings): 0 misses in
  121 tokens. **Early figures in `GATE.md`:** each source's id and its distinctive figures (FY2016's $15.94, $3,300M and $3,522M, the
  recast 2012-2015 losses) appear in no refusal dated before its publication; the only earlier hits are FY2014's $(1.70) and FY2015's
  $(2.43) in the three and one weekly dates after their Q4 releases, which published them. **Years after the as-of date:** none in the
  2014-2017 refusals. **Leak scan:** not applicable (no model to scan).
- **Controls** (`retro/generators/chtr/controls_chtr.py`, in memory): each vintage's latest full year, each Q4 release's year set to a
  positive EPS and the FY2016 one-off test marked not distorted change the refusals on exactly the weekly dates from the fact's
  publication until a later fact supersedes it (until the emergence for a Predecessor year), and on no date before: 16 of 16. Kept at
  GAAP, FY2016 would let the 46 dates from 2017-02-17 pass the gate; the Q4 2016 release is inert (its 10-K came the same morning).
- **Firewall** (the gate's version in `firewall.py`'s CHTR branch, extended: a later Q4 release with a positive year, and a planted

  changes and every control date after it does; all 9 pass, and so do 2008-02-27, 2010-03-01 and 2014-01-01 with the extended plants
  (run again on the committed fact sheet, gate and README: 12 of 12 pass, 0 files changed).

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight (the builder knows what Charter's earnings and stock did after 2016):
- FY2016 excluded by the mirror of the AAPL FY2002 test: the rule existed before, and the margin is wide on every reading, but it is the
  call that decides the batch (kept at GAAP $15.94, 46 dates of 2017 would pass the gate; the pro forma $3.91, unused by the pro forma rule,

- the FY2014-FY2016 vintages' years read as the priced shares' (moot while no year anchors);
- the exchange ratio left unencoded (moot while no date is built);
- the 8-K exhibits other than the Q4 releases searched by keyword, not read in full; the 10-Qs not read;
- stopping at 2017-12-31 without reading FY2017 (the coordinator's scope; the builder knows that FY2017 carries the Tax Act, which no 2017

No outcome was computed, so there is no `FINDINGS.md`.

### CHTR 2018-2021: FY2017 excluded, FY2018 the first anchor, the first 153 dates built (2019-02-01 to 2021-12-31)

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** On 2026-11-27 the owner asked for CHTR 2018-2021 on the same rules; the
coordinating session asked for the series to start at its first full year that can anchor a P/E under the existing rules (no new rule),
for the same one-off tests to be applied to each year, and, if a date passed, for CHTR's own signals and rule-T thresholds, a decision on
the 2016-05-18 Parent Merger Exchange Ratio's price encoding, and every weekly date from the first buildable one to the end of 2021.
Under method r2 **the first date that can be built is 2019-02-01**, and the 153 weekly dates from it to 2021-12-31 are built. The gate
refuses the 56 weekly dates of 2018-01-05 to 2019-01-25 with its reason (`GATE.md`, which now holds every weekly date of 2008-2021: 579
refused, 153 built; its 2008-2017 refusals are byte-identical to the earlier batches'). Nothing was invented to fill the gap.

```bash
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py index 1091667 <dir>
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py fetch 1091667 <dir> --from 2010-02-01 --to 2021-12-31 --forms 10-K
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py fetch 1091667 <dir> --from 2018-01-01 --to 2021-12-31 --forms 8-K 8-K/A
python3 -I retro/generators/chtr/gen_chtr_1821.py --filings <dir> --facts-in <the 2008-2017 sheet>   # retro/facts/CHTR.json
python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py <dir>/checklist_chtr_1821.json                                    # 619/619
python3 retro/build_chtr.py --weekly 2018-01-01 2021-12-31                  # 56 refused, 153 built (2019-02-01 .. 2021-12-31)
python3 retro/build_chtr.py --gate-md                                       # GATE.md
for d in staging/retrospective/CHTR/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series CHTR
python3 retro/generators/chtr/controls_chtr.py 2008-01-01 2021-12-31        # the gate's controls: 35 of 35
python3 retro/generators/chtr/controls_chtr_models.py                       # the models' controls: 39 of 39
python3 retro/generators/chtr/sens_chtr.py <scratch>                        # the sensitivity below
for c in 2008-02-27 2014-01-01 2017-02-16 2018-01-01 2018-02-02 2018-10-26 2019-01-31 2019-02-02 2019-04-30 2019-07-26 2019-10-25 \
         2020-01-31 2020-05-01 2020-07-31 2020-10-30 2021-01-29 2021-04-30 2021-07-30 2021-10-29 2022-01-01; do
  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c CHTR; done
```

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every document to `edgar.py`'s plain client name (no contact address; the owner's email was
not used). Read by the session's model directly, with no delegated transcription: the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks (Items 1, 1A, 5, 6 and 7, the
statements of operations, cash flows and balance sheets), the FY2011-FY2016 10-Ks again for rule T (Item 6, the MD&A's Adjusted EBITDA
tables, the statements of operations and cash flows, Item 1's customer tables), the 13 earnings releases of Q3 2018 to Q3 2021 and the
Q4 2017 release; the other 8-Ks of 2018-2021 were searched by keyword for guidance and outlook wording (the hits are the releases'
capital expenditure sentences, debt pricing term sheets and indentures, the 2020-07-10 and 2021-02-01 rural build-out 8-Ks, none with a
revenue, EPS or margin outlook); the 10-Qs were not read (every print figure is in its release). The sheet is extended by
`retro/generators/chtr/gen_chtr_1821.py`, which reads each figure from its labelled row, asserts each quotation in its own filing,
computes every growth rate, margin, one-off test and rule-T value, refuses an input sheet holding any fact after 2017-12-29, asserts
every earlier fact unchanged and only appends; the source ids are `CH21`-`CH27` (the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks and the Q4 2017 release) and
`CH30`-`CH42` (the prints). Decided on 2026-11-27, before any CHTR outcome existed (none had been computed for any date):

- **FY2017 is excluded by the mirror of the AAPL FY2002 test.** Diluted EPS $34.09 on net income attributable to Charter shareholders of
  $9,895M, of which "an income tax benefit of approximately $9.3 billion" is the remeasurement of the net deferred tax liabilities at the
  Tax Reform rate (FY2017 10-K; the Q4 2017 release, the same morning, says the same). Without it the year's income is $595M, so the
  listed benefit exceeds the income without it; no filing publishes a figure excluding only it (Charter publishes no adjusted EPS). So
  the latest year is again distorted on every date from the FY2017 10-K (2018-02-02) to 2019-01-25, and those 52 dates are refused, as
  are the 4 of January 2018 (FY2016 still the latest year).
- **FY2018 is the first anchor.** GAAP $5.22 (net income attributable $1,230M), published by the Q4 2018 release (accepted 2019-01-31
  07:02 ET) and the FY2018 10-K (07:13 ET) the same morning, so no Q4 release ever extends a vintage in this batch. The one-off test,
  on the MD&A statement of operations' items outside the recurring operating lines, each pre-tax and taken whole (the CB FY2005
  netting): 2018's charges $422M (other operating expenses, the loss on financial instruments, other expense) against $1,230M and its
  benefits $192M (other pension benefits) against $1,038M without them; 2019's charges $386M against $1,668M; 2020's $313M against
  $3,222M. No year is distorted either way: FY18 $5.22, FY19 $7.45 and FY20 $15.40 are GAAP.
- **The history and the window start with 2018.** Once FY2018 is in, FY2017 is a distorted year that is not the latest, so the history
  and the P/E window start after it (method r2, "A distorted year with no published adjusted figure"; the ACN FY02, AAPL FY2002 and CMCSA
  2003 rule; `history_start`), and the loss years and FY2016 before it go with it. The window runs from 2018-01-02 (1.1 years on the first
  date, 4.0 on the last), and the bounds rule applies (method r2, "A history too short to measure a rule"): on the FY2018 vintage BEAR is
  the 0% cap, BULL takes BASE's rate and XBULL BULL's, there is no net buyback (one share count) and the growth factor is 0; from the
  FY2019 10-K the history has two years (BEAR still 0%, as EPS rose), from the FY2020 10-K three. The engine takes the AVGO engine's
  short-history lines.
- **No guide in numbers.** No release, 10-K or other 8-K of 2018-2021 guides revenue, EPS or a margin: current-FY EPS is the last full
  year's (the rollover rule: FY18's $5.22 from 2019-02-01, FY19's $7.45 from 2020-01-31, FY20's $15.40 from 2021-01-29), BASE and the
  growth factor take the latest quarter's revenue growth as reported plus the net buyback (the KMI, LYB and CMCSA no-guide rule), and there
  is no margin step. From the Q3 2019 release each release's capital expenditure outlook ("Charter currently expects 2020 cable capital
  expenditures to decline as a percentage of cable revenue versus 2019", and the like) is words and a cost component, shown in the guide
  line only (the CMCSA capex-guide rule; `capex_outlook`).
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (07:01-07:09 ET) except Q2 2020's (2020-07-31 11:48 ET, during the
  session). Ten fell on a Friday, so their week's date is that Friday (the UNP Good Friday, LYB and SCHW rule: before the open or during
  the session); Q4 2018 (Thursday) dates 2019-02-01 and Q1 2019 (Tuesday) 2019-05-01. Each 10-K came the same morning as its Q4 release.
- **Prices as traded; the Parent Merger needs no encoding.** Yahoo records no split or other event for CHTR, so its close is the price as
  traded. The 0.9042 Parent Merger Exchange Ratio of 2016-05-18 (recorded in "CHTR 2014-2017") precedes every day a model reads: the P/E
  window and its calendar-year lows start on 2018-01-02 and the 52-week statistics in 2018 or later, so no price before the ratio enters
  any statistic, and the per-share history the models use (2018 on) is on the new shares by construction. Neither the splits rule nor the
  distributions rule therefore has anything to restate; the builder asserts that no statistic reads a day before 2016-05-18, and a batch
  whose window reached earlier days would have to decide it.
- **Signals: CHTR's own, by a mechanical choice, with rule T on Charter's own filings.** Five, with the house weights: total customer
  relationships growth (0.20; the first customer line of every release's highlights and key operating results, the BKR "first line of
  every release" criterion, replacing the cable sibling's video customers), revenue growth (0.20), the Adjusted EBITDA margin change
  (0.15; Adjusted EBITDA as the release's statement of operations prints it), the capital intensity change (0.15; purchases of property,
  plant and equipment from the statement of cash flows on revenues, lower is better) and the operating margin change (0.15), with the
  theme slot at 2/4; each against the year-ago quarter in the same release (the customer table's year-ago column as that release prints
  it). **Rule T over the decade of the FY2018 10-K** (2009-2018), the vintage public on the first date (the F rule for a series first built
  late; the BKR 2019 rule for the years after an emergence), the Successor's years only (the BKR 2018 rule; 2009 is two periods), so the
  changes are 2011-2018, each from the latest 10-K published by 2019-02-01 that reports both years, as reported (the 2016 Transactions
  in, as published; FY2016 income from operations as the FY2018 10-K recasts it for ASU 2017-07). Total customer relationships are
  tabulated from the FY2015 10-K only (the FY2013 and FY2014 10-Ks give residential and commercial relationships with no total, and no
  sum is formed: the AVGO and F rule):

  | Signal | Annual changes | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | total customer relationships | 2015-2018: 5.57, 292.64, 3.79, 3.47 % | 2 / 3 / 5 / 293 % |
  | revenue | 2011-2018: 2.05, 4.16, 8.68, 11.69, 7.09, 197.34, 43.37, 4.94 % | -4 / 2 / 8 / 197 % |
  | Adjusted EBITDA margin change | 2011-2018: 31, -123, -85, -3, -10, 160, 28, 0 bp | -240 / -120 / 0 / 160 bp |
  | capital intensity change (lower is better) | 2011-2018: 107, 505, -87, 201, -553, -50, 252, 3 bp | 960 / 510 / 60 / -550 bp |
  | operating margin change | 2011-2018: -6, -219, -104, -49, 76, -295, 140, 210 bp | -560 / -290 / -30 / 210 bp |

  The 2016 values (the TWC and Bright House Transactions) set XBULL for relationships and revenue, mechanically.
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2; STREAMING on the watch list.** Each 10-K's "Seasonality and Cyclicality" paragraph ("Our business is
  subject to seasonal and cyclical variations.", "Our revenue is subject to cyclical advertising patterns and changes in viewership
  levels.") names seasonal service areas and advertising patterns, not the cycle of the business's earnings, so the kind stays DURABLE
  (the SPGI reading of a customers' cycle; the CB and LYB readings are of 10-Ks that call the business itself cyclical); the "why" quotes
  both sentences and the 10-K's own description ("We are the second largest cable operator in the United States ...", FY2018 and FY2019;
  "We are a leading broadband connectivity company and cable operator ...", FY2020). STREAMING (scoped to "cord-cutting / streaming
  displaces linear TV networks and pay-TV bundles", live from 2015-08-04) covers a pay-TV bundle, and each 10-K says "As the proliferation of
  online video services grows, however, services from V-MVPDs and new direct to consumer offerings, as well as piracy and password sharing,
  could negatively impact the growth of our video business." (FY2018; "negatively impact the number of customers purchasing our video
  product.", FY2019 and FY2020), so STREAMING is on the watch list from each 10-K, company-acknowledged, in the latest 10-K's words (the
  CMCSA encoding: `streaming_company_acknowledged`, a factor pair that nets to zero, own "a cloud-based guide incorporating online video
  services" +0.2 against the online-video competition -0.2; text and labels only). The registry's market-pricing evidence (Disney's
  2015-08-04 outlook) names no Charter fact, so nothing is re-filed. The other live themes (OFFSHORE, CLOUD, ECOMMERCE,
  ENERGY_TRANSITION, from 2020 EV and CRYPTO) are quoted with their scopes, none naming a cable operator; the builder refuses a live theme
  the 10-Ks were not read for.
- **No dividend.** "Charter has not paid cash dividends on its common stock and does not intend to do so in the foreseeable future."
  (FY2018-FY2020 10-Ks.) The releases' share repurchase sentences are shown in the capital-return text; the repurchases reach BASE through
  the diluted share counts as each 10-K reports them (235.5M in 2018, 223.8M in 2019, 209.3M in 2020: +5.2%/yr from the FY2019 10-K, +5.7%/yr
  from the FY2020 10-K).
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the 10-K's revenues by service offering (residential, small and medium business,
  enterprise, advertising, mobile, other); the EPS check runs on the consolidated pre-tax margin before the noncontrolling interest and
  the year's tax rate, so it overstates EPS (display only).
- **The listing** is the latest 10-K's sentence ("Charter’s Class A common stock is listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the
  symbol “CHTR.”", FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks, appended to `listings`).

Seen in the build (method behaviour, not tuned):
- **CHEAP and BUY on all 255 dates.** The stock's own P/E window holds only 2018 on, and its first years are a high-multiple regime on
  small EPS (FY18 $5.22 at $271-505), so the window's median falls from 47x to 15x over the batch while the current-FY P/E is 40-12x in 2022
  ($303-610 on FY20's $15.40, then FY21's $24.47), 16-11x in 2023, 13-9x in 2024, 12-6x in 2025 and 7-3x in 2026 ($103-239 on FY24's $34.97,
  then FY25's $36.21): the 0th-28th percentile of the window on every date.
- **BASE** is the latest quarter's revenue growth plus the buyback: +3.1% to +9.2% in 2022, +0.2% to +3.5% in 2023-2025, -2.3% to -1.0% in
  2026 to the Q3 2026 print, then +9.1% with Cox in the actual figures.
- **The EPP floor's panic multiple** (the median of the calendar-year P/E lows) falls to 10x by 2026-11-20 (the median of 2018's 50.0x
  to 2026's 2.8x) as the low years of 2022-2026 join the window.

Sensitivity (each call changed alone, the 255 dates rebuilt and classified offline with `retro_tool`'s classifier; no outcome consulted;
`sens_chtr_2226.py`): **no tested encoding moves a class.** Every signal at its BEAR value 0, at XBULL 0; no net buyback 0; FY2017 kept at
GAAP $34.09 (the history and window from 2017) 0 classes and 3 tiers; the Q3 2026 print on its pro forma columns 0; its customer
relationships against the pro forma year-ago column 0; and a five-year P/E window (the LLY and UNH regime test) 0: the current-FY P/E sits low in any window that holds 2018-2021, and from 2023 the window's own later years are low too.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight (the builder knows what Charter's earnings and stock did after each date):
- the history and P/E window starting in 2018 (the 2018-2021 batch's FY2017 exclusion): the window's own regime is what every CHEAP date
  rests on (see the five-year window above);
- the Cox Transactions in the Q3 2026 actual figures as published, and the year-ago customer relationships from the addendum's actual
  table rather than the first table's pro forma column (no class moves either way);
- Adjusted EBITDA from the reconciliation of non-GAAP measures from Q2 2022 (equal to the statement's row where both exist);
- the one-off item lists read from the statements' lines outside operations (no year is close: the largest ratio is 17%);
- the capital expenditure outlooks read as a cost component (display only), and the Cox synergy and savings targets left unencoded;
- DURABLE on the "seasonal and cyclical variations" paragraph, STREAMING on the watch list, GENAI out of scope with the 10-K's own AI words
  quoted (labels and text only);
- the 8-Ks other than the releases searched by keyword and their Item 7.01 and 8.01 text read, not read in full; the 10-Qs, 425s and
  proxy statements not read; the last date set by the build time (2026-11-20).

Hindsight outcomes and findings, labelled as such, are in `staging/retrospective/CHTR/FINDINGS.md`: hypotheses, never inputs.

## FANG (Diamondback Energy): the thirty-ninth ticker, in staging, built from 2014-02-21 (to 2026-11-27 so far)

The FANG series is set up apart from every other ticker and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/FANG.json`, generated from the filings by `retro/generators/fang/gen_fang.py`), builder (`retro/build_fang.py`, a gate
that decides whether method r2 can build a date and writes nothing but `GATE.md` when it cannot; the CHTR encoding) and engine
(`retro/templates/fang_engine.py.tmpl`, a copy of the XOM oil and gas engine with every signal threshold unset and the signals renamed as
placeholders for an onshore producer, so no XOM value is carried and no model can run on it; from "FANG 2014-2017" a copy of the LYB
engine with FANG's own signals and rule-T thresholds, and the builder builds the dates that pass the gate). The method is still r2. No fact,
parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker (XOM included) enters FANG's files, and neither does any 2026 analysis
(`data/business_profiles.json`, `scripts/quality_classify.py`, `reports/*.json`, any live `*_signal_model.py`). Outputs go to
`staging/retrospective/FANG/`, which held only `GATE.md`, the builder's refusal of each date, until "FANG 2014-2017" built its models. "FANG 2018-2021"
extends the series to 2021-12-31 (`gen_fang_1821.py`), with the dividend and the distorted-year encoding in the builder; "FANG 2022-2026"
to 2026-11-27 (`gen_fang_2226.py`), with a Q4 release's restated prior year, the base dividend and the EV and AI words.

```bash
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py index 1539838 <dir>                            # the downloads (outside the repository)
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py fetch 1539838 <dir> --from 2012-02-01 --to 2014-03-31 --forms 10-K 10-K/A 10-Q 10-Q/A 8-K 8-K/A 424B4
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py fetch 1539838 <dir> --from 2012-10-01 --to 2012-10-31 --acc 0001193125-12-419254 0001193125-12-420871
python3 -I retro/generators/fang/gen_fang.py --filings <dir>                # retro/facts/FANG.json and <dir>/checklist_fang.json
python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py <dir>/checklist_fang.json                # 33/33
python3 retro/build_fang.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2009-12-31                  # 105 dates, every one refused, nothing written
python3 retro/build_fang.py --weekly 2010-01-01 2013-12-31                  # 209 dates, every one refused, nothing written
python3 retro/build_fang.py --gate-md                                       # staging/retrospective/FANG/GATE.md (both ranges)
python3 retro/build_fang.py --pro-forma --weekly 2008-01-01 2013-12-31      # the sensitivity below (writes nothing)
python3 retro/generators/fang/controls_fang.py                              # the gate's controls (4)
for c in 2008-02-01 2009-01-01 2010-01-01 2011-06-01 2012-02-14 2012-10-01 2012-10-13 2012-11-01 2013-01-15 2013-03-03 \
         2013-06-01 2014-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c FANG; done   # the gate's firewall (below)
```

### FANG 2008-2009: requested, no date can be built (nor any to 2013-12-31)

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** On 2026-11-28 the owner asked for FANG 2008-2009 on the same rules, and the
coordinating session asked, if none could be built, for the ticker to be set up anyway and its first buildable dates up to 2013-12-31
built, or, if none of those either, for a gate that refuses them with its reason. Under method r2 **no weekly date from 2008-01-04 to
2013-12-31 can be built** (314 dates: 105 in 2008-2009, 209 in 2010-2013), so none was, and nothing was invented to fill the gap (the
BKR 2018, CTVA, KMI, LYB and CHTR precedents). Checked against the filings, before any price level or outcome was read (Yahoo was read
for its FANG series' first date, its trading days and its event types only):

- **No share before 2012-10-12 (the listing rule).** Diamondback Energy, Inc. (CIK 1539838) "was incorporated in Delaware on December
  30, 2011, and did not conduct any material business operations until October 11, 2012 when Diamondback merged with its parent entity,
  Diamondback Energy LLC" (FY2012 10-K). Its first SEC filing is the S-1 of 2012-02-14; Amendment No. 6 (2012-10-10): "This is the
  initial public offering of our common stock. Prior to this offering, there has been no public market for our common stock."; the
  Form 8-A12B of 2012-10-11 registers the common stock on The NASDAQ Stock Market LLC; the 424B4 (accepted 2012-10-15 17:04 ET, dated
  2012-10-16): "We have been approved to list our common stock on The NASDAQ Global Select Market under the symbol “FANG.”"; the FY2012
  10-K: "The registrant’s common stock began trading on the NASDAQ Global Select Market on October 12, 2012." Yahoo's FANG series
  starts on 2012-10-12 (`firstTradeDate` and the first point; Yahoo's events for FANG hold dividends only, no split), so the 249 weekly
  dates before it have no close.
- **The predecessors had no shares and are not substituted (the KMI, CTVA and LYB rule).** The history before 2012-10-11 is that of
  "Windsor Permian LLC, or Windsor Permian" and "Windsor UT LLC" (the "Predecessors"), entities of "Wexford Capital LP, or Wexford, our
  equity sponsor", combined under common control; "The operations of Windsor Permian and Windsor UT, as limited liability companies,
  were not subject to federal income taxes." (FY2012 10-K). Neither had listed equity or shares, so no per-share history of a traded
  share exists for 2007-2011 (the offering documents and the 10-K print net income for those years, never an EPS).
- **No full year of the company's own EPS in any filing to 2013-12-31 (the loss and gap rules; pro forma unused).** The only per-share
  figures are pro forma: in the offering documents, "Pro forma income (loss) per common share — basic and diluted" of $(0.04) for 2011
  (a loss) and $1.07 for the six months of 2012 (not a year), computed "as if" the shares to be issued in the merger were outstanding;
  in the FY2012 10-K, 2012's "Pro forma earnings per common share" of $0.60 diluted, with "a pro forma income tax provision as if the
  Company and the Predecessors were subject to income taxes since December 31, 2011" on shares "as if the common shares issued upon the
  Merger were outstanding for the entire year". The statements of operations print no GAAP earnings per share for any year, and the Q4
  2012 release (8-K accepted 2013-02-25 21:53 ET) prints no per-share earnings figure at all (the generator asserts it). Pro forma
  figures are never an EPS anchor (the CTVA rule, "the only per-share history is pro forma"; CHTR's pro forma $3.91 unused).
- **FY2012 is distorted besides (the AAPL FY2002 test).** GAAP 2012 is a net loss of $36.521M: "On the date of the merger, a
  corresponding “first day” tax expense to net income from continuing operations was recorded to establish a net deferred tax liability
  for differences between the tax and book basis of Diamondback’s assets and liabilities. This charge was $54,142,000.", against
  $18.382M of income before income taxes. The charge exceeds the year's income before it, and no filing publishes a per-share figure
  excluding only it (the pro forma figure also replaces it with a hypothetical full year of tax at an as-if share count), so even a
  GAAP per-share figure, had one been printed, would leave the year excluded.

So 2008-2012-10-05 fails twice (no close, no year of EPS) and 2012-10-12 to 2013-12-31 once (no year of EPS). The first full year of
Diamondback's own EPS is FY2013; EDGAR lists its Q4 2013 release and FY2013 10-K as accepted on 2014-02-19 after the close (8-K
0001539838-14-000010, 10-K 0001539838-14-000007), but neither was read, so the first date that could be built lies after 2013-12-31 and
was **not determined** in this session: finding it, and choosing the signals and their rule-T values, is a new batch and the owner's
call (the CHTR stop).

**The first buildable date, as far as the filings to 2013 show it** (the owner's instruction, relayed by the coordinator: start a short
history at its first usable point). No filing to 2013-12-31 contains a full year of Diamondback's own EPS, so the first buildable date
cannot come before the first filing that reports FY2013. EDGAR's index (filing metadata, not content) dates the Q4 2013 release and the
FY2013 10-K 2014-02-20 (both accepted 2014-02-19 after the close), so the earliest candidate is the week of 2014-02-17: 2014-02-20 under
the builders' earnings-week rule (the first trading day after the release), 2014-02-21 as the gate's last trading day of the week. It is
a candidate only: it holds if FY2013 is a positive GAAP year that passes the AAPL FY2002 test and its mirror, which was not checked
because those filings were not read. From that date the bounds rule covers the short history (one year: BEAR at the 0% cap, BULL at
BASE's rate, XBULL at BULL's) and the listing rule the window (from 2012-10-12), as for AVGO, V, KMI, CTVA and LYB. The next range
session starts there. Starting earlier would need a new rule (an anchor on a partial year, a pro forma figure or Windsor Permian's
history), each the owner's call: only the pro forma $0.60 would add dates (44, below).

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every filing document to the plain client name of `edgar.py` (no contact address; the owner's
email was not used). Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the S-1/A Amendment No. 6 and the 424B4
(the selected historical data, the pro forma per-share rows, the cover and the listing sentences), the Form 8-A12B, the FY2012 10-K
(Items 5 and 6, the statements of operations, notes 1, 7, the income tax note and the quarterly data), the FY2012 10-K/A (Part III only:
"to incorporate information previously omitted from Part III, Items 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 and to amend and restate the Exhibit Index.",
so not a vintage) and the Q4 2012 release; the 2013 10-Qs and the other 8-Ks of 2012-2013 were downloaded and searched only for later
names (below), as no quarter is a year. The fact sheet is generated by a script from the filings' converted rows: each figure is read
from its labelled row, the row is asserted present in its own filing, and 33 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its
own filing, and all 33 were found. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (ET); the source ids are `FG1` (S-1/A No. 6,
2012-10-10 09:05, before the open), `FG6` (8-A12B, 2012-10-11 14:50, during the session), `FG2` (424B4, dated 2012-10-16), `FG4` (the Q4
2012 release, dated 2013-02-26), `FG3` (the FY2012 10-K, accepted 2013-03-01 16:52 ET, dated 2013-03-04) and `FG5` (the 10-K/A, dated
2013-04-11).

**What was set up.** The fact sheet holds only what decides buildability: three history vintages (S-1/A No. 6 and the 424B4, each with
Windsor Permian LLC's 2008-2011, the six months of 2011 and 2012 and the 2007 period from inception; the FY2012 10-K with 2008-2012 of the
combined company and Predecessors: revenues, net income, income before income taxes, the GAAP EPS as `null` where none is printed and
the pro forma per-share figure apart), the FY2012 one-off note, four listing facts, the no-dividend sentence ("We have not paid any cash
dividends since our inception.", FY2012 10-K) and the price basis. No print, guide, signal, rule-T value or theme event is transcribed;
the builder stops at any date that passes the gate rather than build from a partial sheet. The engine's signals (oil-equivalent
production, oil production, revenue, lease operating expense per Boe, pre-tax margin) are placeholders with thresholds unset: choosing
FANG's signals and deriving their rule-T values from Diamondback's own filings is the first buildable batch's decision. "Viper Energy"
(2013-11-06: exhibit 10.3 of the Q3 2013 10-Q, the first of the downloaded Diamondback filings to name it; "Viper" alone is a 2013 well
name) and "Rattler Midstream" (2017-04-26, the first hit of EDGAR full-text search under CIK 1539838) join the anachronism list
(approximate); no model contains either, and no existing model of any ticker does.

Decided here (no outcome exists to consult):
- **Vintages before the 10-K.** From 2012-10-10 the latest offering document is the vintage (S-1/A No. 6, then the 424B4); the S-1 of
  2012-02-14 and Amendments No. 1-5 were not read, because every weekly date before Amendment No. 6 precedes the listing and fails on its
  price alone (the gate says so in the refusal).
- **Periods.** A period counts only if it is twelve months (the six months of 2012 and 2011 and the 2007 period from inception, about
  two months, are not years: the CTVA 2017 rule).
- **The pro forma figures are not EPS** (above), and the FY2012 10-K/A and the Q4 2012 release add nothing to the gate.

Checks (no model exists, so `retro_tool.py run`, outcomes, the index and the series table have nothing to process; `staging/
retrospective/index.json` gains no row):
- **Verbatim:** 33 of 33 strings (every table header and row behind a figure, and every quoted sentence), each against its own filing
  (`python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py`).
- **Forward references** (`forward_refs.py FANG`): 0 in 16 dated facts. **Self-text** (`selftext.py FANG --allow FG`): 0 misses of 79
  tokens (the six allowed are the source ids `FG1`-`FG6`, method words). **Leak scan:** not applicable (no model to scan).
- **Controls** (`controls_fang.py`): setting each vintage's latest full year to a positive GAAP EPS changes the gate's result for exactly
  the weekly dates from that vintage's publication to the next vintage, and lets each of them pass (S-1/A No. 6: 2012-10-12; the 424B4: 20
  dates, 2012-10-19 to 2013-03-01; the FY2012 10-K: 44 dates, 2013-03-08 to 2013-12-31), with none before its publication; a FANG close a
  year before the series start removes only that year's price reason (52 dates, each still refused): 4 of 4.
- **Firewall** (the gate's version, in `firewall.py`'s FANG branch: in memory, a later 10-K vintage with a positive GAAP year, a later
  listing and a later no-dividend statement): at the 12 cutoffs above no refusal of a date before the cutoff changes (5 to 314 dates
  each), and every weekly date between the planted vintage and the next real one changes (the control; 1 to 10 dates): all 12 pass.

Sensitivity (the gate re-run, nothing written; no outcome consulted): **counting the pro forma per-share figures as EPS**
(`--pro-forma`) lets the 44 weekly dates from 2013-03-08 to 2013-12-31 pass the gate on FY2012's $0.60 (the offering documents' only
full-year pro forma figure, 2011's $(0.04), is a loss); every date before stays refused. Those 44 dates would still need the 2012-2013
prints, guides and signals, which are not transcribed.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight (the builder knows what Diamondback's stock and earnings did after 2013):
- the pro forma figures unused, in particular FY2012's $0.60 (the CTVA and CHTR rule; the alternative admits 44 dates and is the
  batch's deciding call, the owner's);
- the 2007 period and the six-month periods not years (the CTVA 2017 rule; moot, as no period has a GAAP EPS);
- the predecessors' LLC years not substituted (the KMI, CTVA and LYB rule; they have no per-share figure in any case);
- stopping at the gate rather than reading the FY2013 filings or transcribing 2012-2013 prints that no model would use;
- the placeholder signal names in the engine template, chosen by a builder who knows the Permian's later course (no threshold is set,
  and no model runs on them).

No outcome was computed, so there is no `FINDINGS.md`.

### FANG 2014-2017: FY2013 the first anchor, FY2015 and FY2016 losses excluded, FANG's own signals, 202 models from 2014-02-21

rules as before"), with the coordinating session's instruction for a short history: start the series at its first known point, the first
weekly date where the frozen method has a usable history. The newest code is the coordinating session's branch
(`claude/sharp-albattani-rdvlgi`, with the FANG setup of "FANG 2008-2009" and 38 other tickers), checked out as the base; nothing else was
merged in. This batch is on `claude/fang-retro-2014-2017`. There were no earlier FANG outcomes or findings to open. **7 dates are refused
and 202 built:** 2014-01-03 to 2014-02-14 fail the gate (the FY2012 10-K is still the latest vintage, with no GAAP year), and 2014-02-21
to 2017-12-29 pass it on FY2013's $1.29 (45 dates in 2014, then 53, 52, 52). `GATE.md` now holds all 523 weekly dates of 2008-2017 (321
refused, every one before 2014-02-21; the 314 lines of 2008-2013 unchanged).

         2016-08-04 2017-02-16 2017-02-17 2017-08-03 2017-11-08 2018-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c FANG; done

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every document to `edgar.py`'s plain client name (no contact address; the owner's email was
not used). Read by the session's model directly, with no delegated transcription: the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks (Item 1's opening, Item 1A's
risk factors searched for the cyclical, price and climate sentences, Item 2's production and price history, Items 5 and 6, the statements
of operations and of cash flows), the FY2012 10-K again (Item 2's 2010-2012 production table, for rule T only) and the 17 earnings releases
of Q3 2013 (the previous print of the first date) to Q3 2017 (each one's statement of operations, selected operating data and adjusted net
income table). The other 8-Ks of 2014-2017 were searched by keyword for guidance and outlook wording: every hit is a production, unit-cost
or capital spending outlook (the 8-Ks of 2014-07-21, 2016-01-19 with item 2.02, an "interim Q4 2015 operational update and preliminary 2016
guidance" with no earnings figure, 2016-07-18 and 2016-12-14, and the releases' own guidance tables); the 10-Qs were not read (every print
figure is in its release). The sheet is extended by `retro/generators/fang/gen_fang_1417.py`, which reads each figure from its labelled
row, asserts each quotation in its own filing, computes every growth rate, margin, one-off test and rule-T value, refuses an input sheet
whose 2008-2013 facts differ, and only appends; the source ids are `FG7`-`FG10` (the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks) and `FG20`-`FG36` (the prints).
Decided on 2026-11-28, before any FANG outcome existed (none had been computed for any date):

- **FY2013 is the first anchor, and the first date is 2014-02-21.** GAAP diluted EPS $1.29 on net income of $54.587M (FY2013 10-K, Item 6;
  the Q4 2013 release the same evening). The one-off test: the releases' adjusted net income removes only the non-cash derivative marks for
  2013, which recur every quarter (the NEE and PEP 2008 core rule), so no listed one-off exists and the year is kept. The 10-K was accepted
  on 2014-02-19 at 17:29 ET and the release at 20:59 ET, both after the close, so each is dated 2014-02-20, and the builders' earnings-week
  rule (the first trading day after the 'published' date) makes the week's date 2014-02-21. "FANG 2008-2009" named 2014-02-20 as the
  candidate (the day after the release); the rule as coded gives the Friday, as for every after-close release of every builder.
- **EPS is GAAP diluted EPS on net income attributable to Diamondback** (Viper Energy Partners' noncontrolling interest out, as each
  statement prints it), each year from the latest 10-K that reports it (no 10-K of the batch restates an EPS). The one-off test (the AAPL
  FY2002 test and its mirror) runs on each Q4 release's adjusted net income table, twelve months, with the impairment of oil and gas
  properties (the full cost ceiling test), the loss on extinguishment of debt and the (gain) loss on sale of assets as the listed items,
  pre-tax against income before income taxes (the CHTR encoding: the releases give one tax adjustment for all items together, the marks
  included). The non-cash derivative marks are left out as recurring:
  - FY2013 $1.29: no listed item; kept. FY2014 $3.64: a $1.4M loss on sale against $305.0M; kept. (With the 2014 marks, a $117.1M gain,
    read as a one-off benefit, the mirror test is still not met: $117.1M against $187.9M without it.)
  - FY2015 $(8.74) and FY2016 $(2.20): GAAP losses, after impairments of $814.8M and $245.5M (FY2016 also a $33.1M debt extinguishment
    loss). The company's adjusted figures ($1.81 and $1.87) also remove the marks, which recur, so no figure excludes only the one-offs:
    each year is excluded as the latest year and then a gap (the MU, NEM and LYB loss rule), its own days out of the P/E window ("ex-FY15",
    "ex-FY16"). So FY14's $3.64 is the anchor from the Q4 2014 print (2015-02-19) to the last date, and the history holds FY13 and FY14 only.
  - 2012 stays excluded (no GAAP EPS, pro forma only; "FANG 2008-2009"), so its days (2012-10-12 to 2012-12-31) leave the window too.
- **The window runs from the listing** (2012-10-12, the listing rule), 1.1 years on the first date and 5.0 on the last, less the excluded
  years' days ("1.1-yr ex-FY12" to "5.0-yr ex-FY12 ex-FY15 ex-FY16"). **The bounds rule** covers the short history: on the FY2013 vintage
  BEAR is the 0% cap, BULL takes BASE's rate and XBULL BULL's; from the Q4 2014 print the one EPS change (FY13 to FY14, +182.2%) is BULL's
  CAGR, BEAR stays at the 0% cap (EPS rose) and XBULL takes BULL's rate (no two-year run).
- **No guide in numbers.** Every outlook in the filings is production (MBoe/d), unit costs ($/Boe), well counts and costs or capital
  spending; none is revenue, EPS or a margin. So current-FY EPS is the last full year's (FY13's $1.29, then FY14's $3.64), BASE and the
  growth factor take the latest quarter's revenue growth as reported plus the net buyback (the KMI, LYB and CHTR no-guide rule), and there
  is no margin step; the guide line says so. Diamondback issued shares for its acquisitions and offerings (diluted shares 42.3M in 2013,
  53.3M in 2014, 63.0M in 2015, 75.1M in 2016), so the "buyback" is negative: -20.7%/yr from the FY2014 vintage, -18.1% and -17.4% after.
- **Revenue** is total revenues as each statement prints it (one line, "Oil and natural gas revenues", to 2016; "Total revenues" with lease
  bonus and midstream services from 2017). The history takes each year from the latest filing that reports it: 2009-2013 from the FY2013
  10-K's Item 6 and 2008 from the FY2012 10-K, the Predecessors' years (Windsor Permian LLC and Windsor UT LLC, combined under common
  control) as the 10-Ks present them (the LYB rule for a revenue history; their EPS is never used). The 2014-2016 Q4 releases' years
  extend the history from each release until its 10-K, with the release's own prior-year growth.
- **Release timing.** Q1 2014, Q3 2014, Q4 2014 and Q4 2015 were accepted during the session (10:05-10:34 ET; 09:41 ET for Q4 2015) and

### FANG 2018-2021: FY2019 distorted and FY2020 a loss, FY18's $8.06 the anchor from 2019, the dividend, 209 models

209 weekly dates, 2018-01-05 to 2021-12-31, requested by the owner ("find newest code. do retrospective analysis for FANG, 2018-2021. same
rules as before"). The newest code is the coordinating session's branch (`claude/sharp-albattani-rdvlgi`, with "FANG 2014-2017" and the
other tickers merged), checked out as the base; nothing else was merged in. This batch is on `claude/fang-retro-2018-2021`. It was built
in a new session without opening the earlier FANG outcomes or findings (`staging/retrospective/FANG/FINDINGS.md`, `SERIES.md`, any
`outcome.json`), and no 2026 analysis was read. **All 209 dates pass the gate and are built** (52, 52, 53, 52 a year); `GATE.md` now holds
the 732 weekly dates of 2008-2021 (321 refused, every one before 2014-02-21; the earlier lines unchanged).

```bash
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py index 1539838 <dir>
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py fetch 1539838 <dir> --from 2017-10-01 --to 2021-12-31 --forms 10-K 10-K/A 8-K 8-K/A
python3 -I retro/generators/fang/gen_fang_1821.py --filings <dir>              # appends to retro/facts/FANG.json
python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py <dir>/checklist_fang_1821.json              # 263/263
python3 retro/build_fang.py --weekly 2014-01-01 2017-12-31                     # regression: the 202 models byte-identical
python3 retro/build_fang.py --weekly 2018-01-01 2021-12-31                     # 209 built (2018-01-05 .. 2021-12-31)
python3 retro/build_fang.py --gate-md
for d in staging/retrospective/FANG/20{18,19,20,21}-*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series FANG
python3 retro/generators/fang/controls_fang.py 2008-01-01 2021-12-31           # the gate's controls: 12 of 12
python3 retro/generators/fang/controls_fang_models.py 2017-12-30 2021-12-31    # the models' controls: 46 of 46
python3 retro/generators/fang/sens_fang_1821.py <scratch>                      # the sensitivity below
for c in 2018-01-01 2018-02-14 2018-02-15 2018-05-09 2019-02-20 2019-02-25 2019-08-07 2020-01-01 2020-02-19 2020-02-27 2020-05-05 \
         2020-10-21 2021-02-23 2021-02-26 2021-08-03 2021-11-02 2022-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c FANG; done
```

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every document to `edgar.py`'s plain client name (no contact address; the owner's email was
not used). Read by the session's model directly, with no delegated transcription: the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks (Item 1's opening and climate
section, Item 1A's risk factors searched for the cyclical, price, greenhouse gas, conservation and dividend sentences, Item 5, Item 6, the
statements of operations and cash flows, the FY2017 income tax note), the FY2018 10-K/A (a reserve report only: "is being filed solely to
include a report of Ryder Scott ... of Energen Corporation", so not a vintage), and the 16 earnings releases Q4 2017 to Q3 2021 (each one's
statement of operations, selected operating data, adjusted net income table and dividend declaration). Every other 8-K of 2018-2021 was
read by its items and searched by keyword for guidance: the Item 7.01 8-Ks post investor presentations to the website (not filed, unused)
or announce board, officer and notes matters; the Energen merger 8-K's slides say "Accretive on All Metrics ... 2019+ Earnings per share"
in words; the 8-K of 2021-04-12 (item 2.02) is a first-quarter operational update and revised production and capital guidance with no
revenue, earnings or margin figure, so no print; the 10-Qs were not read (every print figure is in its release). The sheet is extended by
`retro/generators/fang/gen_fang_1821.py`, which reads each figure from its labelled row, asserts each quotation in its own filing,
computes every rate, margin and one-off test, refuses an input sheet whose 2008-2017 facts differ, only appends, and regenerates the sheet
byte for byte (from the committed sheet or from the 2008-2017 one). The source ids are `FG11`-`FG14` (the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks) and
`FG37`-`FG52` (the prints). Decided on 2026-11-28, before any outcome of the range existed:

- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS on net income attributable to Diamondback, each year from the latest filing that reports it, ten fiscal years
  to the latest.** The FY2017-FY2019 10-Ks print five years in Item 6 (the FY2019 10-K in rounded millions, which replace the earlier exact
  figures for 2015-2019); the FY2020 10-K reserves Item 6, so its statements' three years (2018-2020) stand and the earlier years are
  carried from the latest earlier vintage (`carried_from`; the SCHW and NEE rule). Revenue, EPS and the diluted share count all follow it,
  so FY13 and FY14 stay in the EPS history after the five-year Item 6 drops them (a sensitivity below: no class moves). No 10-K of the
  batch restates an EPS (asserted).
- **The one-off test** (the AAPL FY2002 test and its mirror) runs, as in 2014-2017, on the items each Q4 release's adjusted net income
  table removes besides the non-cash marks, which recur (the derivative marks and, from 2018, the "revaluation of investment" marks: the
  NEE and PEP 2008 core rule), each at its twelve-month amount where the release's statement of operations prints a line for it, else the
  table's own figure (the Q4 2017 and Q4 2020 tables are three months only):
  - **FY2017 $4.94: kept.** Listed: the "Income tax benefit relating to change in statutory tax rate and change in valuation allowance"
    ($21.4M after tax, three months; a tax item has no pre-tax amount, the CHTR encoding) and a $0.069M gain on sale, against $497.2M of
    income before income taxes. On the FY2017 10-K's full-year reconciliation ($67.9M rate change and $127.5M valuation allowance) the year
    is still kept (`tenk_check`).
  - **FY2018 $8.06: kept.** Listed: the $36.8M Energen merger and integration expense (a charge) and $87.4M of "Other income" (a benefit),
    against $1,113.3M.
  - **FY2019 $1.47: distorted, excluded.** The $790M full cost ceiling impairment and the $56M loss on extinguishment of debt ($846M)
    exceed the year's $362M income before income taxes. The company's adjusted $6.93 also removes the derivative marks, so no figure
    excludes only the one-offs: the year is excluded as the latest year and then a gap (the NEM FY2011, FY2015 and FY2018 encoding),
    "ex-FY19". **This is the batch's deciding call** (below).
  - **FY2020 $(28.59): a loss** after $6,021M of impairments, excluded the same way ("ex-FY20").
  So the anchor is FY14's $3.64 to the Q4 2017 print, FY17's $4.94 from 2018-02-15, and **FY18's $8.06 from the Q4 2018 print
  (2019-02-21) to the last date**, as FY2019 and FY2020 leave gaps. The builder's text for a Q4 release's excluded year now names a
  distorted year as such (it named only losses before; no earlier model changes).
- **No guide in numbers.** Every outlook is production (MBoe/d, MBO/d), unit costs, well counts or capital spending (the 2021 operational
  update included), and the Energen slides' accretion words have no figure. So current-FY EPS is the last kept year's, BASE is the latest
  quarter's revenue growth as reported plus the net share change (the Energen shares of Q4 2018, the 2019 repurchases, Guidon and QEP in
  2021: -16.6% to -20.2%/yr over the history's share counts), and there is no margin step.
- **Dividends, each annual rate from the release that first states it** (`dividends`, read by the builder as LYB's are): $0.50 from the
  Q4 2017 release ("Initiating annual cash dividend of $0.50 per common share to be payable quarterly beginning with Q1 2018", dated
  2018-02-14), $0.75 from the Q4 2018 release (its "As previously announced" points to no earlier filing: the January 2019 investor
  presentation was posted to the website, not filed), $1.50 from the Q4 2019 release, $1.60 from Q4 2020, $1.80 from Q2 2021 and $2.00 from
  Q3 2021. The FY2017 and FY2018 10-Ks still say "We have not paid any cash dividends since our inception." beside the initiation; the
  release's rate wins, and no new no-dividend fact is added. The balance and capital-return lines now name the rate and leave the share
  count's change to BASE (the 2014-2017 text "no share repurchases" would be wrong from 2019).
- **Units.** From Q1 2019 the releases print millions (shares in thousands); each print records its unit from the statement's header.
- **Release timing.** All 16 releases were accepted after the close and are dated the next trading day; the 10-Ks came one to eight trading
  days after their releases (FY2017: release dated 2018-02-14, 10-K 2018-02-15; FY2019: 2020-02-19 and 2020-02-27; FY2020: 2021-02-23 and
  2021-02-26), so the Q4 2019 and Q4 2020 releases' years extend their vintages on the earnings-week dates 2020-02-20 and 2021-02-24.
- **Signals and rule T unchanged** (frozen on the filings public on 2014-02-21; "FANG 2014-2017"): the Q2 2020 and Q2 2021 pre-tax margin
  changes (-77,239bp and +75,263bp against the COVID quarter) land beyond BEAR and XBULL, mechanically.
- **Durability: CYCLICAL, risk 2**, on the same sentences in each 10-K (the business, "The oil and natural gas industry is cyclical, ..."
  and the price sentence). **ENERGY_TRANSITION stays on the watch list**, in each 10-K's own words: the FY2017-FY2019 risk factor heading
  "Regulation of greenhouse gas emissions could result in increased operating costs and reduced demand for the oil and natural gas we
  produce."; the FY2020 10-K drops that heading, so its Item 1 climate sentence, present in every 10-K of the batch, is quoted: "Restrictions
  on emissions of methane or carbon dioxide that may be imposed could adversely impact the demand for, price of, and value of our products
  and reserves." (labels only, no factor pair). **EV (live 2020-01-01) is out of scope**: its scope names ICE powertrains, auto parts
  suppliers and fuel retail; Diamondback produces and sells crude oil, gas and NGLs and has no retail outlets, and the 10-Ks' "Conservation
  measures and technological advances could reduce demand for oil and natural gas." is the demand risk ENERGY_TRANSITION already carries
  (quoted in the "why"). **CRYPTO (2020-10-21)** is scoped to payments, banks and exchanges; no 10-K of the batch contains "electric
  vehicle", "crypto", "blockchain" or "bitcoin" (asserted by the generator).
- **Energen (2018-11-29), the 2019 Rattler Midstream IPO, the Viper drop-down, Guidon and QEP (2021)** are in Diamondback's figures as its
  filings consolidate them; no subsidiary's price or per-unit figure is used, and no pro forma figure. No model names Viper, Rattler,
  Energen, QEP or Guidon (grep: 0 models), and the anachronism list's two FANG notes now say 2014-2021.
- **A text slip carried, not fixed:** the 2014-2017 prints' `next_print` names the month of the print's own release, not the next one
  ("Q4 2017 release (early November)"); fixing it would change earlier facts, which the generator refuses, so the 2018-2021 prints compute
  their own correctly and the earlier text stands (display only).

section, Item 1A searched for the cyclical, price, greenhouse gas, conservation, electric vehicle, AI and dividend sentences, Item 5, Item 6
"[Reserved]", the statements of operations and of cash flows), the 20 earnings releases Q4 2021 to Q3 2026 (each one's statement of
operations, selected operating data, adjusted net income table and dividend declaration; Q1 2026's exhibit 99.2, the stockholder letter,
for its dividend sentence), and every other Item 2.02 8-K: 18 of them carry no release (each quarter's realized prices, derivative
activity and share counts, the cash settlement note of 2022-04-07, the operational updates of 2024-10-01 and 2025-04-16, and the
Endeavor merger 8-K of 2024-02-12 with preliminary Q4 2023 operating results), and none prints revenues, income before income taxes or an
EPS (asserted by the generator), so none is a print (the 8-K of 2021-04-12 encoding). The other 8-Ks were read by their items (notes,
credit agreements, officers, meetings, the merger agreements). No 10-K/A was filed. The sheet is extended by
`retro/generators/fang/gen_fang_2226.py`, which reads each figure from its labelled row, asserts each quotation in its own filing,
computes every rate, margin and one-off test, refuses an input sheet whose 2008-2021 facts differ, only appends, and regenerates the sheet
byte for byte. The source ids are `FG15`-`FG19` (the FY2021-FY2025 10-Ks), `FG53`-`FG72` (the prints), `FG73` (the merger 8-K's exhibit
99.2) and `FG74` (the Q1 2026 letter). Decided on 2026-11-28, before any outcome of the range existed:

- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS on net income attributable to Diamondback, each year from the latest filing that reports it, ten fiscal years
  to the latest.** Every 10-K of the batch reserves Item 6, so each takes its statements' three years and carries the earlier ones from
  the latest earlier vintage (the FY2020 encoding). **One restatement:** from the Q4 2022 release the per-share figures are computed "using
  the two-class method in accordance with GAAP" (its footnote), and its prior-year column and the FY2022 10-K print FY2021 at $12.24 (the
  Q4 2021 release and the FY2021 10-K: $12.30) and FY2020 at $(28.61); the release's restated prior year enters the history from the
  release (`prior_eps_gaap` in `fy_actual`, a new builder line that touches no earlier model), the 10-K's from the 10-K. No other 10-K
  restates an EPS (asserted).
- **The one-off test** (the AAPL FY2002 test and its mirror) runs, as before, on the items each Q4 release's adjusted net income table
  removes besides the non-cash derivative marks, which recur (the NEE and PEP 2008 core rule): at the statement of operations' twelve-month
  line where the table is three months only (Q4 2021-Q4 2023) and the line exists, else the table's own three-month figure; from the
  table's year column where it has one (Q4 2024, Q4 2025). "Other non-cash transactions" is read as a listed item, as the table lists it
  (it decides no year):
  - **FY2021 $12.30 (then $12.24): kept.** $78M of merger and integration expense and a $75M debt extinguishment loss against $2,907M.
  - **FY2022 $24.61: kept** ($114M against $5,736M). **FY2023 $17.34: kept** ($12M against $4,248M). **FY2024 $15.53: kept** ($303M of
    merger and integration expense, against $64M of benefits and $4,501M).

  from 2024-02-22, FY24's $15.53 from 2025-02-26 and, as FY2025 is excluded, **FY24's $15.53 still from the Q4 2025 print (2026-02-25) to

The TRGP series is built apart from every other ticker and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/TRGP.json`, generated from the filings by `retro/generators/trgp/gen_trgp.py`), builder (`retro/build_trgp.py`, the LYB
new-listing builder with TRGP's encodings and a gate that refuses every date before the first full year of EPS) and engine
(`retro/templates/trgp_engine.py.tmpl`, the LYB engine with midstream signals). The method is still r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or
finding of another ticker enters a TRGP model (KMI, the other midstream company, lent only its listing and first-full-year precedents);
there is no TRGP profile in `data/business_profiles.json`, and no 2026 analysis (`scripts/quality_classify.py`, `reports/*.json`, a live
`*_signal_model.py`) was read. Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/TRGP/`.
