### TRGP 2008-2009: requested, no date can be built

**What the owner asked for and what could be built.** On 2026-11-28 the coordinating session asked, for the owner, for TRGP 2008-2009 on
the same rules. Under method r2 **no date of 2008-2009 can be built**, and none was; nothing was invented to fill the gap (the BKR 2018,
CTVA, KMI and LYB 2008-2009 precedents). Checked against the filings before any price or outcome was read (Yahoo was asked for its series
metadata only):

- **No TRGP share traded before December 2010.** The IPO prospectus: "No public market currently exists for our common stock." (424B1,
  accepted 2010-12-07 17:23 ET); the FY2010 10-K: "Our common stock has been listed on the New York Stock Exchange since December 7, 2010
  under the symbol “TRGP.”" and, on its cover, "As of June 30, 2010, the last day of the registrant’s most recently completed second
  quarter, the registrant’s common stock was not publicly traded." Through 2007-2009 Targa Resources Corp. (CIK 1389170, then a private
  company) filed only Forms 3 and 4 and a Schedule 13D as an owner of Partnership units, no 10-K or
  10-Q (EDGAR submissions). Yahoo's TRGP series starts on 2010-12-07 (`firstTradeDate` and the first point) and records no split.
- **No EPS to common shareholders in 2008-2009.** "For 2008 and 2009, there was no net income available to common shareholders as the
  preferred shareholders are entitled to all undistributed earnings. As such, there were no earnings per share to our common shareholders
  during 2008 and 2009." (FY2010 10-K, the EPS note). So even a price would have had no P/E.
- **The listed Targa security of those years was another one (why the BKR/BHI route does not apply).** "Targa Resources Partners LP
  (NYSE: NGLS), a publicly traded Delaware limited partnership" (the prospectus) listed in February 2007; TRC owned its general partner,
  its incentive distribution rights and some of its common units, and consolidates it. But NGLS's units are a partnership's, with their
  own earnings per unit and distributions, priced under their own symbol; a 2008-2009 model of them would be an NGLS retrospective, not
  TRGP's, and its per-unit history is never substituted (the KMI and CTVA rule). Yahoo serves nothing under NGLS (HTTP 404). What TRC's own
  filings consolidate (the Partnership's revenues and segment margins) is in the TRGP models as published.

So, as the request provides, the ticker is set up anyway and its first buildable dates are built in this session, to 2013-12-31 (next
part). Sources: EDGAR submissions for CIK 1389170; the 424B1 0000950123-10-111598; the FY2010 10-K 0001389170-11-000003; Yahoo chart
API, TRGP and NGLS, read 2026-11-28 (metadata only).

### TRGP from the first full year: 2012-02-24 to 2013-12-31

**What could be built.** Under method r2 **the first date that can be built is 2012-02-24**; this part builds the 98 weekly dates to
2013-12-31. No date from the 2010-12-07 listing to 2012-02-17 (63 weeks) is built: a model needs the stock's own P/E, and TRC's first full
year of EPS is 2011, published in the Q4 2011 release. 2010 is a loss per share ($(30.94): a net loss available to common shareholders
of $(202.3)M, after the Series B dividends and $177.8M of dividends on common equivalents, on 6.5M weighted shares before the Series B
converted into 35.4M shares on 2010-12-10), so it has no P/E (the F, MU and CRM loss rule), and 2008-2009 have none to common
shareholders. Building that gap takes a new rule (an EPS anchor for a loss year, or 2011's quarters annualized), which is the owner's
call and a method note; nothing was invented to fill it (the KMI 2011 and LYB 2010 precedents). The builder refuses each of those dates,
and every date of 2008-2009, with its reason (`first_buildable`, the listing check).

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every filing document to the plain client name of `edgar.py` (no contact address; the owner's
email was not used). Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the IPO prospectus (424B1), the FY2010-FY2012
10-Ks (selected financial data, the statements of operations and cash flows, the segment notes and the MD&A by segment, the EPS notes,
Items 1A and 5) and their 10-K/As (the FY2010 one adds the parent-only schedule, the FY2011 one only the XBRL exhibit: neither changes a
figure the models read, so neither is a vintage), the nine joint earnings releases of Targa Resources Partners and TRC from Q3 2011 to
Q3 2013 (TRC's consolidated statement of operations, the Partnership's segment reviews, the TRC dividend and distributable cash flow), the
outlook 8-K of 2012-10-17, and every other 8-K of 2011-2013 by its item text and exhibits. The fact sheet is generated by a script from
the filings' converted rows: each figure is read from its labelled row, the row is asserted present in its own filing, and every growth
rate, margin, tax rate and rule-T value is computed, not typed; 197 strings were checked with `verbatim.py`, each against its own filing,
and all 197 were found. Each source's date comes from EDGAR's acceptance time (ET); the source ids are `TG1`-`TG3` (the 10-Ks),
`TG10`-`TG18` (the releases) and `TG30` (the outlook 8-K). Decided on 2026-11-28, before any TRGP model was built or any TRGP outcome
computed:

- **The listing.** Targa Resources Corp.'s common stock, NYSE: TRGP, from 2010-12-07 (`listing.first_trading_day`, the listing rule);
  the window's 2010 days leave it with the loss year ("ex-FY10"), so it runs from 2011-01-03 (1.1 years on the first date, 3.0 on the
  last). Yahoo records no split or distribution, so its close is the price as traded.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of the range but one was accepted before the open (07:18-08:20 ET; the joint calls at 10:00 a.m. to
  1:00 p.m. ET), so the print is public that day and the week's date is the next trading day; the Q1 2013 release (Friday 2013-05-03,
  07:19 ET) has no trading day after it in its week, so that Friday meets it (the UNP Good Friday rule, public before the open). The Q3
  2013 8-K was accepted after the close (2013-11-04 16:51 ET), so it is dated 2013-11-05 and its week's date is 2013-11-06. The outlook
  8-K of 2012-10-17 (16:15 ET) is dated 2012-10-18. The 10-Ks are dated 2011-02-28 (2011-02-25 18:12 ET), 2012-02-28 (2012-02-27 17:08 ET)
  and 2013-02-20 (2013-02-19 16:47 ET).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS, each year from the latest filing that reports it.** FY2011 $0.74 (the Q4 2011 release and the FY2011 10-K),
  FY2012 $0.91 (the Q4 2012 release and the FY2012 10-K). TRC prints no EPS excluding one-offs (its non-GAAP measure is distributable
  cash flow, display only). The history starts with 2011; 2010 is in `eps_excluded` with its reason, and its days leave the window.
- **The one-off test, both years kept.** FY2011: the release lists no TRC item; the Partnership's $7.2M of non-cash derivative charges
  recur and, even all credited to TRC, are under its $30.7M of net income. FY2012: the release's only listed item, "approximately $6
  million of transaction costs related to the Badlands acquisition" (the Partnership's, pre-tax), against TRC's $38.1M.
- **No guide in numbers.** No release, 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K of 2011-2013 guides TRC's revenue, EPS or a margin: the outlooks are the
  Partnership's Adjusted EBITDA and distribution growth and TRC's dividend growth ("TRC expects to be in a position to increase dividends
  by 25% to 30%+ in 2013 compared to 2012", the 8-K of 2012-10-17; "in excess of 25% compared to 2013" for 2014, the Q3 2013 release).
  So current-FY EPS is the last full year's (the PFE rule), BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth as reported plus the buyback (the
  SO, UNP, KMI and LYB no-guide rule), and there is no margin step; the dividend outlooks are shown in the guide line, display only (the
  KMI rule). Their own years (2013, then 2014) are the 20 calendar-year warnings of `retro_tool run` (2012-10-19 to 2012-12-28 and
  2013-11-06 to 2013-12-31): forecasts the filings state, not leaks.
- **History.** Consolidated revenues from 2006 (the Partnership in, as TRC consolidates it): 2006 from the FY2010 10-K's selected data,
  2007-2012 from the latest 10-K that reports each (2009 and 2010 restated by the FY2011 10-K). Diluted shares from 2011 (41.4M, then
  41.8M): 2010's 6.5M is a weighted average of the pre-IPO common shares before the Series B conversion, not comparable, so it is left
  out; the net buyback is measured from the first count to the last (none on the first date's one count; -1.0%/yr from the Q4 2012 print).
- **The rollover rule and the bounds rule.** To the Q4 2012 print the history has one year of EPS, so BEAR is the 0% cap, BULL takes
  BASE's rate and XBULL BULL's; from it, FY2011 to FY2012 is the only change (+23.0%).
- **Dividends:** each quarter's declared rate from its release ($0.3075 for Q3 2011 to $0.57 for Q3 2013; $1.345 to $2.28 a year).
- **Signals.** Five, with the house weights, each against the year-ago quarter as the release shows it: the Partnership's Natural Gas
  Gathering and Processing operating margin growth (Field plus Coastal Gathering and Processing; 0.20) and Logistics and Marketing operating
  margin growth (Logistics Assets plus Marketing and Distribution; 0.20), the two divisions the 10-Ks report, segment operating margin
  being the measure "Targa senior management reviews ... monthly" (hedging, in Other, left out); revenue growth (0.15), the operating
  margin change (0.15) and the pre-tax margin change (0.15; income before income taxes on revenues, before the noncontrolling interests),
  from TRC's consolidated statement of operations; the theme slot at 2/4.
- **Thresholds by rule T over the years the filings public on 2012-02-24 report** (the FY2010 10-K and the Q4 2011 release; the bounds
  rule), each change from the latest filing that reports both years, as reported:

  | Signal | Annual values | BEAR / BASE / BULL / XBULL |
  |---|---|---|
  | Gathering and Processing operating margin | 2009-2011: -44.4, 26.2, 34.2 % | -115 / -44 / 26 / 34 % |
  | Logistics and Marketing operating margin | 2009-2011: 93.2, 4.5, 43.9 % | -35 / 5 / 44 / 93 % |
  | revenue | 2007-2011: 19.0, 9.6, -43.3, 20.6, 27.7 % | -106 / -43 / 19 / 28 % |
  | operating margin change | 2007-2011: -3.0, -91.0, 186.0, -120.0, 144.0 bp | -240 / -120 / 0 / 190 bp |
  | pre-tax margin change | 2009-2011: 28.0, -63.0, 189.0 bp | -150 / -60 / 30 / 190 bp |

  The segment values are the Partnership's on its common control basis (the FY2010 10-K's MD&A by segment for 2008-2010; the Q4 2011
  release's 2010 matches it to the decimal, asserted); the pre-tax margins start with 2008, the first year of the FY2010 10-K's statements.
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2.** No 10-K calls the business cyclical; each says "The Partnership’s primary natural gas gathering and
  processing arrangements that expose it to commodity price risk are its percent-of-proceeds arrangements." and, of its distribution
  policy, that reserves keep distributions steady "even if the Partnership’s business experiences fluctuations in its cash from operations
  due to seasonal and cyclical factors": boilerplate of the policy, not a statement that the business is cyclical (the CHTR reading of

  and CLOUD is live, so a later date needs its own reading first). The watch list is empty and the builder refuses events.
- **Segment bridge and EPS check** (display only): the latest 10-K's segment operating margin by segment as the split; the EPS check runs
  on the consolidated pre-tax margin and tax rate before the noncontrolling interests (the Partnership's other unitholders), so it
  overstates TRC's own EPS several times over, as its note says (the KMI note).
- **Adds nothing:** the outlook 8-K of 2011-10-19 and its 8-K/A of 2011-10-21 (the Partnership's preliminary third-quarter results and

- the non-earnings 8-Ks read by their item text and exhibits for guided numbers only.

209 weekly dates, 2014-01-03 to 2017-12-29, on the same fact sheet, generator discipline, builder, engine and method (r2), with the
rule-T thresholds of 2012-02-24 frozen. Built on 2026-11-28 at the owner's request ("do retrospective analysis for TRGP, 2014-2017, same
rules as before"), in a new session that did not open the 2012-2013 outcomes, `SERIES.md` or `FINDINGS.md`; every decision below applies
a rule that existed before (the house rules and the 2012-2013 encodings) or is disclosed as new. NGLS's unit prices and per-unit figures
are never used: the Atlas mergers (2015-02-27) and TRC's acquisition of the Partnership's public common units (2016-02-17) are in the
figures as TRC's own filings publish them.

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` again served every filing document to the plain client name of `edgar.py` (no contact address; the
owner's email was not used). Read by the session's model directly, with no delegated transcription: the sixteen earnings releases from Q4
2013 to Q3 2017 (joint releases of the Partnership and TRC to Q4 2015, TRC's own from Q1 2016), the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks (Item 6, the
statements of operations and cash flows, the selected quarterly data, the segment note, Items 1, 1A and 7A), the 8-K of 2016-05-23 that
recasts the FY2015 10-K's Items 1, 6, 7 and 8, the 8-K of 2014-10-23 that revises revenues, the six 10-Qs of 2016-2017 (EPS and shares),
and every other 8-K of 2014-2017 by its item text and exhibits. `gen_trgp_1417.py` loads the 2012-2013 sheet, refuses one that already
holds a later fact, appends, and asserts every earlier fact, source and rule-T value unchanged (the CHTR, NEM and SCHW extension pattern);
`gen_trgp.py` still regenerates the 2012-2013 sheet byte for byte. Sources `TG4`-`TG7` (the FY2013-FY2016 10-Ks), `TG8` (the recast),
`TG40`-`TG55` (the releases), `TG60` (the revenue revision), `TG61`-`TG66` (the 10-Qs), `TG31`-`TG32` (the Atlas and buy-in 8-Ks).

- **No guide in numbers, again.** No release, 10-Q, 10-K or other 8-K of 2014-2017 guides TRC's revenue, EPS or a margin: the outlooks are
  the Partnership's Adjusted EBITDA and capital spending (to 2015), TRC's dividend growth ("approximately 35%" for 2015 pro forma for the
  Atlas mergers, the 8-K of 2014-10-14; "dividend growth of 15% for 2016", the buy-in 8-K of 2015-11-03) and, for 2017, volumes, capital
  spending and dividend coverage "assuming a $3.64 per common share 2017 dividend" (the Q4 2016 release). So the last full year's GAAP EPS
  stands, BASE is the latest quarter's revenue growth as reported plus the buyback, and there is no margin step; the dividend outlooks are
  shown in the guide line, display only (the 2012-2013 and KMI rule). Their own years are the calendar-year warnings of `retro_tool run`
  (forecasts the filings state, not leaks; the buy-in 8-K's "through 2018" is shown to 2017-02-10, while 2016 is the current year).
- **EPS: GAAP diluted EPS, each year from the latest filing that reports it.** FY13 $1.55, FY14 $2.43, FY15 $1.09 (each Q4 release and its
  10-K); FY2016 $(1.80), a loss. TRC prints no EPS excluding one-offs. From Q4 2015 TRC's releases state "net income attributable to common
  shareholders before impairment of goodwill" ($83.9M for 2015) in dollars, never per share, so EPS stays GAAP (the SCHW 2010-2013 rule).
- **The one-off test.** FY2013: the release lists no TRC item; the Partnership's $14.7M of losses on debt redemptions and its $15.3M gain
  from eliminating the Badlands contingent consideration net to a $0.6M benefit against $65.1M. FY2014: the $12.4M loss on the 7 7/8% notes
  and $8.0M of other expense ("primarily attributable to transaction costs related to the pending Atlas Mergers"), even all credited to
  TRC, against $102.3M. **FY2015 (the batch's largest EPS call):** the one item the release states on TRC's basis is the $290.0M
  provisional goodwill impairment, whose effect on TRC is $25.6M (its $83.9M before the impairment less the $58.3M reported): kept, at
  GAAP $1.09. The Partnership's other items (a $32.6M impairment charged to depreciation, Atlas merger costs in other expense, a $30.6M
  gain on the redemption value of the joint ventures' preferred interests) are before the noncontrolling interests, with no TRC share
  stated; counted in full against TRC they would approach or pass its income, which is the reading the sensitivity tests. **FY2016 is a
  loss** ($(278.1)M attributable to common shareholders after the Series A preferred dividends; $(1.80) a share in the 10-K), excluded as the
  latest year and then a gap, its days out of the window ("ex-FY10 ex-FY16"), so FY15's $1.09 anchors every date from the Q4 2015 print.
  The Q4 2016 release prints no per-share figure, so the year is a loss by its reported net loss from the release (`eps_gaap` None; the
  builder's loss test reads the income when no EPS is printed, new and disclosed).
- **TRC's own releases from Q1 2016 print no EPS or share count** (only the summary table, the segment reviews and the reconciliations).
  The quarter's EPS and diluted shares come from its 10-Q from the 10-Q's own date, and Q4 2016's EPS from the FY2016 10-K's selected
  quarterly data (`restated`, the JPM and SCHW encoding, now in `build_trgp.py`); until then the model shows EPS as n/r through
  `trgp2_engine.py.tmpl`, the None-tolerant copy (the BKR, SPGI, SCHW and LYB encoding; 4 dates: 2016-04-29, 2016-05-06, 2016-11-03,
  2017-02-16), and the EPS check's share count is the latest public one, named (display only). Income before income taxes, which these
  releases do not tabulate, is net income less the income tax line (the LYB 2018 derivation; it matches the FY2016 10-K's statement).
- **The revenue revision of 2014-10-23.** The 8-K (Items 2.02 and 8.01, accepted 08:58 ET) revises revenues and product purchases to report

  2016-08-04 to 2017-04-28; CHEAP from 2017-05-05 to 2017-07-28; FAIR from 2017-08-04 to 2017-12-22 but RICH on 2017-10-06 and 2017-12-29.
  Legacy tiers: BUY 97, AVOID 44, WATCHLIST 44, ACCUMULATE 24 (2015: BUY on all 53).
- **The anchors and the multiple.** FY13's $1.55 against $87-142 (56-92x), FY14's $2.43 against $16-107 (7-44x; the close fell from $106.84
  to $16.28 between the Q4 2014 and Q4 2015 prints), FY15's $1.09 against $26-61 (23-56x). The window grows from 3.0 to 7.0 years ex-FY10
  (ex-FY16 from 2017-02-16) and its median stays 44-51x, so the 2015 dates sit at the 0th-39th percentile of the window and are CHEAP.
- **BASE follows revenue as reported, plus the buyback:** +40.6% to +67.5%/yr in 2014 (the Q4 2013 to Q3 2014 prints' revenue growth),
  -4.0% to -29.3%/yr through 2015 as NGL prices fell, -25.3% to -5.1% in 2016 (with -6.3%/yr of dilution), then -0.9% to +23.4% in 2017
  (Q1-Q3 2017 revenues +18% to +47% less 23.1%/yr of dilution from the FY2016 10-K). BEAR is the 0% cap to the Q4 2015 print, then FY14 to
  FY15's -55.1%; BULL and XBULL the history's CAGR and best two-year run, floored at BASE.
- **The EPP floor** is 52x on FY12 (the first 6 dates), 39-43x on FY13, then 35x (2015's low of 23.6x and 2016's 14.2x join the lows).

Sensitivity (each call changed alone, the 209 dates rebuilt and reclassified offline with `retro_tool`'s own classifier; no outcome
consulted; `sens_trgp_1417.py`):
- **every data signal at its BEAR value**: 96 classes (CHEAP to RICH 39, FAIR to RICH 40, CHEAP to FAIR 17); **at XBULL**: 33;
- **FY2015 excluded as distorted** (the Partnership's items counted in full against TRC; FY14's $2.43 then anchors 2016-2017): **75
  classes** (RICH to CHEAP 41, FAIR to CHEAP 34, all from 2016-04-22), 87 tiers; **FY2015 at a derived $1.57** (TRC's $83.9M before the
  goodwill impairment on 53.6M shares, a figure no filing prints per share): 70 classes, 87 tiers;
- **BASE on TRC's dividend outlooks** (25% for 2014, 35% for 2015, 15% for 2016, 0% for 2017's held dividend): 43 classes, 29 tiers;
- **2016's share count (the buy-in) out of the buyback**: 13 classes (2017-03-10 on), 21 tiers;
- **the revenue revision of 2014-10-23 unused** and **CYCLICAL instead of DURABLE**: no class, no tier; ENERGY_TRANSITION in scope would
  be text only (no factor pair), so no class by construction.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- the signal set and rule T's thresholds, frozen from 2012-02-24 (chosen by a builder who knew 2012-2013, measured on 2009-2011): the
  signals at BEAR move 96 of the 209 classes, the largest call of the batch;
- FY2015 kept at GAAP $1.09 on the one TRC-basis item its release states (75 classes if excluded, 70 at a derived $1.57), by a builder who
  knows how TRGP traded in 2016-2017;
- FY2016 excluded as a loss (its days out of the window) and the last full year's EPS standing when no EPS is guided;

  (13 classes);
- the Atlas mergers and the buy-in in the figures as published (no pro forma), the Partnership's consolidated revenues and segment margins

### TRGP 2018-2021: every year a loss, the estimated net income as a GAAP earnings guide, EV and CRYPTO out of scope

209 weekly dates, 2018-01-05 to 2021-12-31, on the same fact sheet, generator discipline, builder, engines and method (r2), with the
rule-T thresholds of 2012-02-24 frozen. Built on 2026-11-28 at the owner's request ("do retrospective analysis for TRGP, 2018-2021, same
rules as before"), in a new session that did not open the 2012-2017 outcomes, `SERIES.md` or `FINDINGS.md`; every decision below applies
a rule that existed before (the house rules and the 2012-2017 encodings) or is disclosed as new. NGLS's unit prices and per-unit figures
are never used; the Series A preferred stock, the development joint ventures' preferred interests, the Badlands interest sale, the
Partnership's notes and the 2020 repurchase program are in the figures as TRC's own filings publish them.

python3 retro/generators/trgp/controls_trgp.py 2018-01-01 2021-12-31         # 80 controls
python3 retro/generators/trgp/sens_trgp_1821.py <scratch>                    # the sensitivity below
for c in 2018-02-15 2018-02-16 2018-02-20 2018-02-21 2018-05-03 2018-05-04 2018-05-05 2018-08-09 2018-08-10 2018-11-08 2018-11-09 \
         2019-02-20 2019-02-21 2019-03-01 2019-03-02 2019-05-07 2019-05-08 2019-05-09 2019-08-08 2019-08-09 2019-08-10 2019-11-07 \
         2019-11-08 2019-11-09 2020-01-01 2020-02-20 2020-02-21 2020-02-22 2020-05-07 2020-05-08 2020-08-06 2020-08-07 2020-10-05 \
         2020-10-06 2020-10-21 2020-11-05 2020-11-06 2021-02-18 2021-02-19 2021-05-06 2021-05-07 2021-08-05 2021-08-06 2021-11-04 \

  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c TRGP; done                             # 46 cutoffs

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` again served every filing document to the plain client name of `edgar.py` (no contact address; the
owner's email was not used). Read by the session's model directly, with no delegated transcription: TRC's sixteen earnings releases from
Q4 2017 to Q3 2021, the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks (Item 6, the statements of operations and cash flows, the selected quarterly data to FY2019,
the segment note, Items 1, 1A and 7A), the twelve 10-Qs of 2018-2021 (EPS and shares), the outlook 8-K of 2020-10-05, and every other 8-K
of 2018-2021 by its item text and exhibits. `gen_trgp_1821.py` loads the 2012-2017 sheet, refuses one that already holds a later fact,
appends, and asserts every earlier fact, source, revenue revision and rule-T value unchanged (the 2014-2017 extension pattern). Sources
`TG70`-`TG73` (the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks), `TG80`-`TG95` (the releases), `TG100`-`TG111` (the 10-Qs), `TG33` (the 8-K of 2020-10-05).

- **Every year a loss.** FY2017 $(0.31) (net loss attributable to common shareholders of $(63.4)M after the Series A preferred dividends,
  with the $378.0M impairment of property, plant and equipment and the $269.5M discrete deferred tax benefit of the Tax Act), FY2018
  $(0.53), FY2019 $(1.44), FY2020 $(7.26) (the $2,442.8M impairment of long-lived assets of Q1 2020). Each is excluded as the latest year
  and then a gap, its days out of the window (the F, MU and CRM loss rule, as FY2016), so the window is "ex-FY10 ex-FY16 ex-FY17 ex-FY18
  ex-FY19" and from the FY2020 10-K "10-yr ex-FY16 ex-FY17 ex-FY18 ex-FY19 ex-FY20", and FY15's $1.09 is the last full year of EPS on
  every date. The Q4 releases print no per-share figure, so each year is a loss by its reported net loss (`eps_gaap` None, the 2014-2017
  encoding) until its 10-K; the listed items are recorded for completeness (a loss year has no P/E either way). TRC prints no EPS
  excluding one-offs (its non-GAAP measures are Adjusted EBITDA, distributable cash flow and adjusted free cash flow).
- **New: a GAAP earnings guide (decided before any 2018-2021 model was built; no earlier output changes, so still r2).** From the Q4 2018
  release each release reconciles its Adjusted EBITDA outlook to an "Estimated Net Income attributable to TRC" for the year, a GAAP
  figure in numbers ("Net income attributable to TRC | 44.0", the Q4 2018 release; none in the Q1-Q3 2018 or Q1-Q3 2019 releases). By
  the KMI 2019-2022 rule a GAAP net income guide sets current-FY EPS; TRC's EPS is to common shareholders after the Series A preferred
  dividends, and its releases print no share count, so the per-share figure is that estimate less 4 x the release's own quarter's Series
  A dividends (cash and deemed, as its statement prints them) over the latest basic weighted-average share count public on the guide's
  date (a 10-Q's quarter or a 10-K's year; basic because the numerator is to common shareholders before the if-converted test). A guide
  whose figure is a loss has no P/E and is read as no numeric guide, so FY15's $1.09 stands (the LLY 2008 and CRM 2010 rule):
  - FY2019: $44.0M less $122.4M = $(78.4)M, a loss (2019-02-21 to 2020-02-14 keep FY15's $1.09);
  - FY2020: $203.0M less $126.4M over 232.7M shares = **$0.329** (the Q4 2019 release, 11 dates 2020-02-21 to 2020-05-01); then the Q1
    and Q2 2020 releases, the 8-K of 2020-10-05 and the Q3 2020 release estimate net losses ($(1,706.0)M, $(1,627.5)M, $(1,480.5)M twice,
    the impairment of long-lived assets in), so FY15's $1.09 stands from 2020-05-08 to 2021-02-12;
  - FY2021: $300.0M less $137.6M over 232.2M = **$0.699** (the Q4 2020 release, from 2021-02-19), $435.0M less $87.2M over 228.5M =
    **$1.522** (Q1 2021), $485.0M over 228.6M = **$1.740** (Q2 2021), $555.0M over 228.8M = **$2.045** (Q3 2021; the deemed dividends
    end with Q4 2020 and the cash dividend falls to $21.8M a quarter).
  The Adjusted EBITDA, capital spending and volume outlooks stay display only, in the guide line; no filing guides revenue or a margin,
  so BASE is still the latest quarter's revenue growth as reported plus the buyback, with no margin step.
- **EPS of the quarters.** TRC's releases print no EPS or share count: each quarter's EPS and diluted shares come from its 10-Q from the
  10-Q's own date, and a fourth quarter's EPS from the next 10-K's selected quarterly data (Q4 2017 from the FY2017 10-K, Q4 2018 and Q4
  2019 likewise; `restated`, the 2014-2017 encoding). The FY2020 10-K has no selected quarterly data, so Q4 2020's EPS stays n/r through
  `trgp2_engine.py.tmpl` on its 11 dates (2021-02-19 to 2021-04-30), and on the few dates between a Q4 release and its 10-K. The FY2018
  10-K's fourth quarter has net income attributable to common shareholders of $(137.3)M against the release's $(137.0)M: only its EPS is
  used, and the note says so.
- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted before the open (06:14-07:31 ET), none on a Friday, so each print's week date is the
  next trading day. The 10-Ks are dated 2018-02-20 (2018-02-16 16:20 ET), 2019-03-01 (13:01 ET), 2020-02-21 (2020-02-20 17:10 ET) and
  2021-02-18 (15:38 ET); the 10-Qs from their own acceptance times (the same day as the release or the next trading day). The FY2019 and
  FY2020 10-Ks are public by the first weekly date after their releases, so the Q4 2019 and Q4 2020 releases' full years never reach a
  model alone (the controls find them inert).
- **History.** Each vintage takes Item 6's five years from its own 10-K (the FY2020 10-K still has Item 6) and earlier years from the latest
  earlier vintage, the ten fiscal years to the latest one; 2018 on are under ASC 606 and 2017 and earlier as first reported (a seam, stated
  in the revenue note). Diluted shares from each statement of operations (206.9M for 2017, 224.2M, 232.5M, 232.2M), so the net buyback,
  measured from 2011's 41.4M as before, is dilution of about 21%/yr in BASE.
- **Dividends:** each quarter's declared rate from its release, $0.91 to Q4 2019 and **$0.10 from the Q1 2020 release** (2020-05-07). The
  $500M common share repurchase program of the 8-K of 2020-10-05 is not encoded (`buyback_programs` stays empty; the share counts measure
  any repurchase).
- **Signals:** unchanged, each against the year-ago quarter as the release shows it. From the Q4 2019 release Logistics and Marketing is
  named Logistics and Transportation ("The change in naming convention did not impact previously reported results for the segment.",
  quoted in `segment_rename`), read as the same division. The impairments are in income from operations as published, so the margin
  signals read -10407bp in Q1 2020 and +11087bp in Q1 2021, against it.
- **Durability: DURABLE, risk 2.** Each 10-K keeps the percent-of-proceeds sentence and the dividend policy's "seasonal and cyclical factors"
  (the CHTR reading, as before); the FY2020 10-K's cash-flow risk factor adds "supply, demand", quoted in the "why".
- **Themes.** **EV (live 2020-01-01) and CRYPTO (live 2020-10-21) are out of scope**: their scopes name ICE powertrains, auto parts and fuel
  retail, and payments networks, banks, exchanges and remittance, not midstream energy, and no FY2017-FY2020 10-K names electric vehicles,
  crypto, blockchain or bitcoin (the generator asserts it). ENERGY_TRANSITION stays out of scope (the BKR reading): no reserves of
  Targa's, refinery services that are NGL balancing for refiners, and the Channelview Splitter as each 10-K describes it (from the FY2019
  10-K "a 35,000 Bbl/d nameplate capacity crude oil and condensate splitter" that Targa "owns and operates", after Vitol terminated the
  Splitter Agreement in December 2018), a terminaling asset of the Logistics and Transportation segment rather than a refining business;
  the FY2019 and FY2020 10-Ks' climate risk factor ("Our and our customers’ operations are subject to a number of risks arising out of the
  threat of climate change ...") is quoted in the "why". The FY2018 10-K names cloud only in an accounting standard's title; the others do
  not name it (`cloud_text`, text only). The watch list stays empty and the theme slot at 2/4, so no class moves either way.
- **Adds nothing:** the 8-Ks of 2019-01-10 and 2021-01-19 (Item 7.01: excerpts of the Partnership's offering memoranda, no figure the
  models read), the Item 2.02 8-K of 2021-02-24 (the Q4 2020 call's prepared remarks, the Adjusted EBITDA outlook again), the Item 8.01
  8-Ks of 2020-03-25 (a director's margin sale), 2020-11-13 and 2021-02-25 (10b5-1 plans), the notes, credit and tender 8-Ks, and the
  officer, director and vote-result 8-Ks.

## OKE (ONEOK, Inc.): the forty-first ticker, in staging, 2008-2009

The OKE series is built apart from the other forty and shares nothing with them but the machinery: its own fact sheet
(`retro/facts/OKE.json`, generated by `retro/generators/oke/gen_oke.py`), builder (`retro/build_oke.py`, the KMI builder with EPS-guide
midpoints, Yahoo's later factors undone and ONEOK's fields) and engine (`retro/templates/oke_engine.py.tmpl`, the KMI engine with ONEOK's
signals and its own rule-T thresholds). KMI is the other midstream company; ONEOK's natural gas distribution segment is a regulated
utility (the SO and NEE line), and its signal set has one regulated line (Distribution) beside the consolidated ones. The method is still
r2. No fact, parameter, outcome or finding of another ticker enters an OKE model, and no 2026 analysis of ONEOK was opened (the live
`oke_signal_model.py`, OKE's profile in `data/business_profiles.json`, `scripts/quality_classify.py` and `reports/*.json`). ONEOK
Partners, L.P. (NYSE: OKS) was a separate listed entity: its units' prices and per-unit figures are never used; what ONEOK's own filings
consolidate (ONEOK Partners from 2006-01-01, under EITF 04-5) is in as published. Outputs go to `staging/retrospective/OKE/`, with the same
`index.json` and their own `SERIES.md`. The owner asked for 2008-2009 ("find newest code. do retrospective analysis for OKE, 2008-2009. same
rules as before"); the code is the branch `claude/sharp-albattani-rdvlgi` (its commit "Merge NEM 2022-2026 ... NEM complete to
2026-11-27"), as the coordinating session named it; nothing else was merged in.

```bash
python3 -I retro/generators/oke/gen_oke.py --filings <dir>                  # -> retro/facts/OKE.json
python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py <dir>/checklist_oke.json                  # 191/191
python3 retro/build_oke.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2009-12-31                   # 105 dates, 2008-01-04 .. 2009-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/OKE/20*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective series OKE
for c in 2008-01-11 2008-02-27 2008-05-02 2008-08-07 2008-11-07 2009-02-10 2009-02-25 2009-05-01 2009-08-06 2009-11-05 \
         2010-01-01; do python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c OKE; done
python3 retro/generators/oke/controls_oke.py; python3 retro/generators/oke/sens_oke.py <scratch>
```

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every filing document to `edgar.py`'s plain client name (no contact address), and
`efts.sec.gov` (the full-text search) answered the same client for the anachronism dates.

Read, by the session's model directly with no delegated transcription: the ten earnings releases of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 (8-K exhibit 99.1:
the statements of income, balance sheets, cash flows, the 'Information at a Glance' segment tables and the guidance paragraphs); the
guidance 8-Ks (Item 7.01) of 2007-09-17, 2008-01-10 and 2009-02-09; the dividend 8-Ks (Item 8.01) of 2007-07-20, 2008-01-22, 2008-07-18
and 2009-07-17 (and those declaring an unchanged rate, by their text); Items 1, 1A, 6, 7 and 8 of the FY2006, FY2007 and FY2008 10-Ks and
the FY2006 10-K/A (an exhibit's signature date only); and, for rule T and the history, the statements of income, the Distribution segment
tables and Item 6 of the FY1998-FY2005 10-Ks (FY1998-FY2001 plain text). Every other 8-K of 2007 to January 2010 was read by its items and
title (conference and webcast notices, officers and directors, by-laws, the El Paso and Oklahoma rate cases, the D-J Basin lateral, credit
agreements, registration statements, the auditor change, the share repurchase agreement, the annual meeting): none states a guided
number. The 8-K of 2010-01-22 (the 2010 guidance) and later filings were listed only. **Not read:** the 10-Qs beyond their listing (the
releases carry every figure the models use), the proxy statements, ONEOK Partners' own filings, and the presentations the releases point
to on the website (not filed). The fact sheet is generated by a script: in the HTML filings every figure is read from its labelled row of
a named table (the row text is kept in the fact), in the plain-text ones typed once with the snippet that holds it (asserted present);
every rate, margin and rule-T value is computed; every quote is asserted verbatim (191/191 with `verbatim.py`). Each source's date is
EDGAR's acceptance time (before 2002 the filing date only); the source ids are `OK1`-`OK28`. Decided on 2026-11-28, before any OKE model
was built or any OKE outcome computed:

- **The company and its listing.** ONEOK, Inc. (CIK 1039684, the company formed in the November 1997 transaction with Western Resources),
  NYSE: OKE on every date ("ONEOK, Inc. (NYSE: OKE)", the releases). Yahoo's OKE series is split-adjusted to today's shares: its 2:1 of
  2001-06-12 precedes the P/E window, and its 2:1 of 2012-06-04 and its 11422:10000 factor of 2014-02-03 (the ONE Gas separation, a
  distribution recorded as a split) follow every built date, so the builder multiplies Yahoo's close by both (x2.2844), which is the
  close as traded ($44.33 on 2008-01-04, $29.12 on 2008-12-31, $44.57 on 2009-12-31). The builder asserts those two factors and refuses
  dates from 2012-06-04 until they are encoded.

Judgement calls that could carry hindsight:
- FY2001 excluded by the AAPL FY2002 test on the latest filing's continuing-operations basis (43 classes if kept), which also keeps the
  August fiscal years and the transition period out of the window: a rule applied as written, but on a basis (the FY2005 10-K rather than
  the FY2001 10-K) chosen by a builder who knows how ONEOK traded;
- BASE on revenues as reported when no revenue is guided (28 classes on net margin), for a company whose revenues are mostly commodity
  pass-through;
- the signals, chosen by a builder who knows 2008-2009: net margin, the Distribution segment, revenue and two margins on revenues (rule T
  then sets the thresholds mechanically over the 1997-2006 filings; 43 and 41 classes at BEAR and XBULL), and rule T's computed lines in the
  FY1998-FY2002 statements (operating and pre-tax income summed from the printed lines) and the calendar 2000 against fiscal 1999 seam;
- 2005 and 2006 at the company's figures without the gains on sale (23 classes, 60 tiers at GAAP);
- the guide midpoints as GAAP current-FY EPS (20 classes without them), and the segment operating income guides kept as components;
- DURABLE rather than CYCLICAL (label only), as no 10-K calls the business cyclical, though its revenues and ONEOK Partners' margins follow
  commodity prices;
- the parts of the filings listed as not read.

### OKE 2010-2013: Q4 2009 from the 10-K, net income guides per diluted share, the retail marketing business discontinued, the 2012 split, the energy services wind down, CLOUD out of scope

The owner asked for 2010-2013 ("find newest code. do retrospective analysis for OKE, 2010-2013. same rules as before"); the code is the
branch `claude/sharp-albattani-rdvlgi` (its commit "Merge OKE 2008-2009 ... OKE 2008-01-04 to 2009-12-31"), as the coordinating
session named it; nothing else was merged in. Built in a new session without opening the 2008-2009 outcomes or findings
(`staging/retrospective/OKE/FINDINGS.md`, the `outcome.json` files, the hindsight part of `SERIES.md`); the live `oke_signal_model.py`,
OKE's profile in `data/business_profiles.json`, `scripts/quality_classify.py` and `reports/*.json` were not opened.

```bash
python3 retro/tools/edgar.py fetch 1039684 <dir> --from 2009-10-01 --to 2013-12-31 --forms 8-K 8-K/A 10-K 10-K/A 10-Q
python3 -I retro/generators/oke/gen_oke_1013.py --filings <dir> --facts-in <the 2008-2009 sheet>   # -> retro/facts/OKE.json
python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py <dir>/checklist_oke_1013.json             # 241/241
python3 retro/build_oke.py --weekly 2010-01-01 2013-12-31                   # 209 dates, 2010-01-08 .. 2013-12-31
for d in staging/retrospective/OKE/201[0-3]-*/; do python3 retro/retro_tool.py --archive staging/retrospective run "$d"; done
for c in 2010-01-25 2010-02-23 2011-02-22 2012-02-21 2012-06-04 2012-10-31 2013-02-26 2013-06-12 2013-11-06 2014-01-01; do
  python3 retro/tools/firewall.py $c OKE; done
python3 retro/generators/oke/controls_oke_1013.py; python3 retro/generators/oke/sens_oke_1013.py <scratch>
```

**A full-data batch.** `www.sec.gov` served every filing document to `edgar.py`'s plain client name (no contact address).

99.1: the statements of income, balance sheets, 'Information at a Glance' and the guidance paragraphs); the guidance 8-Ks (Item 7.01) accepted
after the close on 2010-01-22, 2010-10-04, 2011-01-20, 2011-09-28, 2012-01-20, 2012-09-24, 2013-06-11 and 2013-12-02 (labelled in the models
by the day each counts from: 2010-01-25, 2010-10-05, 2011-01-21, 2011-09-29, 2012-01-23, 2012-09-25, 2013-06-12; the last gives 2014 only); the dividend 8-Ks (Item 8.01), those
raising the rate by their sentence and those keeping it by their text; the split 8-Ks of 2012-02-17, 2012-05-25 and 2012-06-05; Items 1,
1A, 6, 7 and 8 of the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks; the FY2009 10-K/A of 2010-10-12 ("The purpose of this Amendment No. 1 ... is to re-file
Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2", "this Amendment No. 1 does not change any previously reported financial results": no vintage); and, for Q4 2009's
nine months, the Q3 2009 release (OK21). Every other 8-K of 2010-2013 was read by its items and title (conferences, officers and
directors, credit agreements, notes, ONEOK Partners' distributions and projects, the Overland Pass transaction, the retail marketing sale,
the ONE Gas announcement, rate cases): none states a guided number for ONEOK. **Not read:** the 10-Qs beyond their listing (the releases
carry every figure the models use), the proxy statements, ONEOK Partners' own filings, the earnings tables and guidance tables the releases
point to on the website (not filed) and the conference presentations. The sheet is generated by a script (each figure from its labelled
row, the row text kept; every rate computed; every quote asserted, 241/241 with `verbatim.py`); the source ids are `OK29`-`OK64`, each
dated by EDGAR's acceptance time. Decided on 2026-11-28, before any OKE 2010-2013 model was built or any of its outcomes computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K but two was accepted after the close (17:08-18:43 ET) and counts from the next trading day; the
  Q4 2010 and Q4 2011 releases were accepted before the open (2011-02-22 07:12 and 2012-02-21 07:50 ET) and count from their day. Each Q4
  print came a trading day or less before its 10-K (Q4 2009 on the 10-K's own day, 2010-02-23; the FY2010, FY2011 and FY2012 10-Ks the
  next trading day), and no weekly date falls between them (the generator and the builder assert it), so no print carries full-year actuals
  of its own.

  count from the same day.
- **Four history vintages,** each year from the latest filing that reports it, the ten fiscal years to the latest one, revenues and diluted
  shares from each statement of income (three years), EPS from each Item 6 (five years): the FY2009 10-K (2010-02-23), the FY2010 10-K
  (2011-02-23), the FY2011 10-K (2012-02-22) and the FY2012 10-K (2013-02-27). Each year keeps its own filing's publication date
  (`eps_published`, `shares_published`), which the split helper reads. 2005 and 2006 stay at the company's figures without the gains on

and title (conferences and investor days, officers and directors, by-laws, credit agreements and notes, ONEOK Partners' distributions and
projects, the KCC settlement, the merger agreement and its closing 8-K of 2017-07-03, the Series E preferred stock, Hurricane Harvey, the

ids are `OK65`-`OK97`, each dated by EDGAR's acceptance time. Decided on 2026-11-28, before any OKE 2014-2017 model was built or any of
its outcomes computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K of the range was accepted after the close (16:33-17:30 ET) and counts from the next trading day;
  the week's date is the trading day after that (the builder's rule), which for each Q4 print is its 10-K's own day (Q4 2013 from
  2014-02-25 and the FY2013 10-K 2014-02-26; Q4 2014 2015-02-24 and 2015-02-25, the 10-K accepted during the session; Q4 2015 2016-02-23 and
  2016-02-24; Q4 2016 2017-02-28 and 2017-03-01), so no print carries full-year actuals of its own (the generator asserts it).

  SPGI `distributions` rule, no new rule). "ONEOK will distribute one share of common stock of ONE Gas, par value $0.01 per share, for
  every four shares of ONEOK common stock held by ONEOK shareholders of record as of the close of business on January 21, 2014" (8-K of
  2014-01-09, public 2014-01-10); "On January 31, 2014, ONEOK completed the Distribution and the separation of ONE Gas from ONEOK."
  (8-K of 2014-02-05, public 2014-02-06, the record's source; no weekly date falls between the effective date and it). Yahoo books it as an
  11422:10000 split on 2014-02-03, the first day without ONE Gas; from that date the builder undoes the factor for the days before it, so
  every price is the close as traded and the drop stays in the series, the window's earlier days priced with ONE Gas (the SO Mirant
  reading); per-share facts are not restated. The builder's stop at 2014-02-03 is replaced by the record; it checks Yahoo's factor from
  the effective date and still refuses any unencoded split or distribution. The history keeps the distribution business until a filing
  restates it: the FY2013 10-K (2014-02-26) has it in continuing operations (the separation came after the year), the FY2014 10-K
  (2015-02-25) restates 2010-2014 without it.

  ('Earnings per share - continuing operations', five years), revenues and diluted shares from each statement of income (three years):

99.1: the statements of income, balance sheets, the highlights tables, the guidance paragraphs and guidance tables); the guidance 8-K of
2018-01-23 (Item 7.01, counted from 2018-01-24) and the capital spending 8-K of 2020-03-12 (Item 7.01, counted from 2020-03-13); every
dividend 8-K (Items 7.01 and 8.01), those changing the rate by their sentence and those keeping it by their text; Items 1, 1A, 6, 7 and 8
of the FY2017-FY2020 10-Ks. Every other 8-K of 2017-12 to 2021-12 was read by its items and title (conferences, credit agreements and notes,
growth projects, by-laws, officers and directors, the annual meetings, the sustainability report, the emissions target) and its text
searched for a net income or EPS guide (none). **Not read:** the 10-Qs beyond their listing (the releases carry every figure the models use),
the proxy statements, the earnings tables, presentations and supplemental guidance materials the releases point to on the website (not
filed). **From the Q4 2017 release every earnings release is a set of page images with a text layer** (Workiva slides, as LLY's Q1 2018
release): the tables have no cells, so the generator reads each figure from the converted text layer, a label followed by the table's
numbers (`trow`, new in `gen_oke_1821.py`), and the matched text goes to the verbatim checklist; the 10-Ks are HTML tables, read by row as
before. Every quote is asserted (221/221 with `verbatim.py`); the source ids are `OK98`-`OK128`, each dated by EDGAR's acceptance time.
Decided on 2026-11-28, before any OKE 2018-2021 model was built or any of its outcomes computed:

- **Release timing.** Every earnings 8-K was accepted after the close (16:28-17:16 ET) and counts from the next trading day, except the
  Q3 2019 release (accepted 2019-10-30 09:14 ET, before the open: it counts from that day, and the week's date is 2019-10-31). Each Q4 print
  came a trading day before its 10-K, the week's date being the 10-K's day (2018-02-28, 2019-02-27, 2020-02-26, 2021-02-24; asserted), so no
  print carries full-year actuals of its own. The dividend 8-K of 2019-04-19 was accepted on Good Friday, a market holiday, and counts from
  2019-04-22 (the UNP Good Friday rule; new in the generator's `pub`).
- **The ONEOK Partners merger** (closed 2017-06-30) is in the figures as ONEOK's filings publish it: no OKS price or per-unit figure, no
  pro forma statement. The FY2017 diluted shares are the year's 299.8M (the 168.9M exchange shares from July), 2018 on about 414-448M. The
  engine's buyback term is the vintage's diluted-share change since its first year, so from 2018 it reads the merger and the 2018 and 2020
  equity offerings as dilution (-11%/yr on the FY2017 vintage, -7% to -8% later): as published, the KMI and TRGP reading of share
  issuance.
- **Four history vintages,** each year from the latest filing that reports its EPS from continuing operations, the ten fiscal years to the
  latest one, revenues and diluted shares from each statement of income (three years):

    and Jobs Act: the Q4 2017 release lists the Act's $141.3M (47 cents for the year), the $20.2M impairments (4 cents) and about $50M of
    merger costs (10 cents), 61 cents against $1.90 without them, under half, and no filing publishes a full-year EPS without them (the

  - FY2018 10-K (2019-02-27): its Item 6 prints 'Earnings per share - total' only, so 2016-2018 come from the statement of income's diluted

## Categories change with the era

The five base kinds (DURABLE, CYCLICAL, STRUCTURAL, TURNAROUND, SPECIAL) are
timeless. `AI_EXPOSED` is not: it is the current instance of a recurring
pattern, a franchise that is cheap because the market prices a substitution
story. A retrospective uses the kind `DISRUPTION_EXPOSED` plus the theme live
on its date, and the class names follow the theme:

| theme (label) | live from | first market pricing | class family |
|---|---|---|---|
| GENAI (AI) = today's `AI_EXPOSED` | 2022-11-30 | 2023-05-02 (Chegg) | AI-FEAR BASKET / AI-EXPOSED, … |
| CLOUD | 2012-10-30 (earliest verified 10-K) | 2015-04-23 (AWS disclosed) | CLOUD-FEAR BASKET / … |
| ECOMMERCE (AMAZON) | ~2015 | 2017-06-16 (Whole Foods) | AMAZON-FEAR BASKET / … |
| STREAMING | 2015-08-04 | 2015-08-04 (ESPN subs) | STREAMING-FEAR BASKET / … |
| ENERGY_TRANSITION | 2015-12-12 | 2020-08-31 | TRANSITION-FEAR BASKET / … |
| EV | ~2020 | 2020-12-21 (TSLA in S&P) | EV-FEAR BASKET / … |
| CRYPTO | 2020-10-21 | 2021-04-14 | CRYPTO-FEAR BASKET / … |
| GLP1 (GLP-1) | 2023-08-08 | 2023-08-08 (SELECT) | GLP-1-FEAR BASKET / … |
| OFFSHORE | 2004-11-05 (earliest verified 10-K) | not established | OFFSHORE-FEAR BASKET / … |

What the gates enforce:

- **Before `live_from`.** The theme cannot be assigned, and it cannot even sit on
  the `theme_watch` list. A 2016 analysis that mentions GenAI fails.
- **On or after `live_from`.** The theme still needs dated evidence that the
  market was pricing it *for this company* (`PIT_PROFILE.evidence`). A theme that
  is live but where the stock is priced as a beneficiary stays on `theme_watch`.
  That was ACN in 2023: AI was live, but ACN traded near or above its own median
  multiple, not at an AI discount.
- **Themes that fizzled stay in the registry** (CRYPTO, ENERGY_TRANSITION). A
  registry of only the themes that later mattered would itself be hindsight.
- **What this means by depth.** For shallow dates (late 2025 on), the categories
  are today's, but each ticker's kind must still be re-earned from evidence dated
  by then. For mid-depth dates (2023 to 2024), AI is live but mostly a watch item.
  For deep dates (2016 and earlier), the disruption slot belongs to cloud,
  Amazon, streaming or the energy transition, and `AI_EXPOSED` is illegal.
  IT services in 2008 had their own live theme: offshore delivery. ACN's FY2007 10-K
  names Indian providers "often at highly competitive prices". ACN in January 2008
  carries it on the watch list, not AI.
  From its FY2012 10-K (2012-10-30), ACN also carries CLOUD on the watch list: company-acknowledged,
  no market read. Its earlier 10-Ks mention cloud only as an offering. Its FY2016 10-K (2016-10-31) goes
  further: cloud-based services, artificial intelligence and automation "have reduced and replaced some of our
  historical services and solutions". That changes the quoted wording, not the status: it is still the company's
  own statement, and no dated evidence shows the market pricing it for ACN.
  LOW carries ECOMMERCE on the watch list the same way from its FY2015 10-K (2016-03-29), the first whose risk factors
  name "growing competition from online and multi-channel retailers" ("LOW 2015-2016"). It stays there after the
  theme's market-pricing date (2017-06-16, a grocers' sell-off): no dated evidence shows the market pricing it for
  Lowe's ("LOW 2017-2018", "LOW 2019-2020", "LOW 2021-2023", "LOW 2024-2026").
  AAPL in 2008 carries none: no theme in the registry is live for a personal-computer and consumer-electronics maker
  (CLOUD from 2012-10-30; OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services), so its watch list is empty ("AAPL"). It stays empty through 2026:
  CLOUD's scope is on-premise enterprise IT, STREAMING's linear TV and ECOMMERCE's physical retail, and Apple's FY2012-FY2019
  10-Ks name cloud and streaming only as its own services ("AAPL 2012-2015", "AAPL 2016-2019"); GENAI's scope (from 2022-11-30),
  EV's, CRYPTO's and GLP1's name none of Apple's products ("AAPL 2020-2023"), and the FY2024 and FY2025 10-Ks name artificial
  intelligence only as Apple's own features and their risks ("AAPL 2024-2026").
  NKE in 2008-2014 carries none either: no theme in the registry is live for an athletic footwear and apparel brand (ECOMMERCE
  from 2015-01-01, scoped to physical retail; OFFSHORE to IT services), so its watch list is empty ("NKE", "NKE 2009-2011",
  "NKE 2012-2014"). Its FY2015 and FY2016 10-Ks name e-commerce only as NIKE's own channel, so the list stays empty; from its
  FY2017 10-K (2017-07-21), the first whose risk factors name "the rising trend of digital commerce" as "a risk factor
  implicating our DTC and wholesale operations", NKE carries ECOMMERCE on the watch list, company-acknowledged, with no market
  read ("NKE 2015-2017"). The FY2018 and FY2019 10-Ks repeat the sentence (for "our NIKE Direct and wholesale operations") and
  the FY2020-FY2023 10-Ks name "the continued proliferation of digital commerce", so it stays there through 2023 ("NKE 2018-2020",
  "NKE 2021-2023"). The FY2024-FY2026 10-Ks drop that phrase but say NIKE Direct competes "with digital commerce platforms" and
  keep "shifts in the ways in which consumers shop" as a risk factor, so it stays there through 2026, a judgement call
  ("NKE 2024-2026").
  AVGO in 2009-2015 carries none: no theme in the registry is live for an analog semiconductor maker (CLOUD from 2012-10-30, scoped
  to on-premise IT; OFFSHORE to IT services; GENAI from 2022-11-30), and its FY2012-FY2015 10-Ks name cloud only for their own IT
  service providers, so its watch list is empty ("AVGO", "AVGO 2010-2012"). From the FY2016 10-K of Broadcom Limited (2016-12-23),
  the first whose risk factors name "the shift to cloud-based IT solutions and services, such as hyperscale computing" as a risk to
  its wired infrastructure and enterprise storage segments, AVGO carries CLOUD on the watch list, company-acknowledged, with no
  market read ("AVGO 2013-2016"). The FY2017 10-K repeats that sentence and the FY2018-FY2020 10-Ks of Broadcom Inc. name the shift
  as affecting sales "for use in traditional enterprise data centers", so it stays there through 2020; EV and CRYPTO, live from
  2020, are scoped to other industries ("AVGO 2017-2020"). The FY2021-FY2023 10-Ks repeat that sentence, so it stays there through
  2023. GENAI, live from 2022-11-30, stays off the list: its scope names none of Broadcom's products, and the FY2022 and FY2023 10-Ks
  name AI only as features of its own products and in one regulatory risk, never as a substitute for them ("AVGO 2021-2023").
  The FY2024 and FY2025 10-Ks keep the cloud risk (sales "for use in traditional enterprise data centers", then "for use in enterprise
  data centers"), so CLOUD stays through 2026; they name AI as Broadcom's own market, a possibly unsustainable upturn, a source of

  evidence shows the market pricing generative-AI substitution of Google Search, so CYCLICAL stands ("GOOG 2022-2026").

  JPM in 2008-2009 carries none: no theme in the registry is live for a bank holding company (OFFSHORE, from 2004-11-05, is scoped to IT
  services; CRYPTO, the one theme that names payments and banking, is not live before 2020-10-21), so its watch list is empty and the
  FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks' dependence on markets and economic conditions and their "increasing competition in the financial services
  industry" stay in the "why" (the PEP obesity rule) ("JPM"). It stays empty through 2013: CLOUD, live from 2012-10-30, is scoped to
  public cloud displacing on-premise IT, and the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks keep the same two risk factors ("JPM 2010-2013"). It stays empty
  to 2020-10-14: CLOUD, ECOMMERCE, STREAMING and ENERGY_TRANSITION are scoped to other industries, and the 10-Ks' "financial technology
  companies" (FY2015 on) and cryptocurrency sentence (FY2017 on) stay in the "why" ("JPM 2014-2017", "JPM 2018-2021"). From 2020-10-23,
  the first weekly date after CRYPTO's live date, JPM carries CRYPTO on the watch list, company-acknowledged, with no market read, in the
  words of the 10-K in force ("JPM 2018-2021"). It stays there through 2026-11-13: the FY2021-FY2024 10-Ks keep the sentence, and the
  FY2025 10-K's names tokenized securities and distributed ledger technology and lists stablecoins among non-depository products; GENAI's
  scope names no bank, so the FY2025 10-K's words on AI agents stay in the "why" ("JPM 2022-2026").

  V in 2009 to 2020-10-16 carries none: no theme in the registry is live for a payments network before CRYPTO (2020-10-21), the one theme
  whose scope names payments networks (CLOUD, ECOMMERCE, STREAMING and ENERGY_TRANSITION are scoped to other industries), so its watch list
  is empty and the 10-Ks' competition and spending sentences stay in the "why" ("V", "V 2010-2013", "V 2014-2017"). From 2020-10-23 V
  carries CRYPTO on the watch list, company-acknowledged, with no market read, in the words of the 10-K in force, and from the FY2021 10-K,
  which names a crypto offering of Visa's own, with a factor pair that nets to zero ("V 2018-2021"). It stays there through 2026-11-13: the
  FY2022-FY2024 10-Ks name no offering of Visa's own, so the pair leaves; the FY2025 and FY2026 10-Ks name one again (crypto and stablecoin
  cards, the Visa Stablecoin Platform), and the FY2026 10-K says stablecoins "could disrupt existing payment networks", the company's own
  reading, so the stock is not re-filed. GENAI's scope names no payments network, so the 10-Ks' words on generative AI and Visa's
  value-added services stay in the "why" ("V 2022-2026").

  CB (ACE Limited) in 2008-2009 carries none: no theme in the registry is live for a property and casualty insurer (OFFSHORE, from
  2004-11-05, is scoped to IT services; CLOUD is not live before 2012-10-30, CRYPTO before 2020-10-21), so its watch list is empty and the
  FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks' cycle and catastrophe risk factors stay in the "why" (the PEP obesity rule) ("CB"). In 2010-2013 it carries none
  either: CLOUD, live from 2012-10-30, is scoped to on-premise IT, and the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks repeat the same two risk factors ("CB
  2010-2013").

  LLY (Eli Lilly) in 2008-2009 carries none: no theme in the registry is live for a pharmaceutical company (GLP1, from 2023-08-08, is
  scoped to snacks, beverages and devices; OFFSHORE to IT services), so its watch list is empty and the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks' risk factor
  on intellectual property protection and generic competition stays in the "why"; patent expiry is the business's own cycle, not a
  substitution theme (the PFE and BMY reading) ("LLY").

  LLY 2010-2013 carries none either: CLOUD, live from 2012-10-30, is scoped to on-premise IT, and the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks' risk factors
  ("We depend on patent-protected products for most of our revenues, cash flows, and earnings") stay in the "why"; the 2012-2013
  releases' "counter-cyclical growth" names growth areas outside the patent cycle, not a cyclical business ("LLY 2010-2013").

  LLY 2022-2026 carries none: GENAI (from 2022-11-30) is scoped to AI substituting software seats, IT services, information, search,
  education and mobility, and the FY2023-FY2025 10-Ks name artificial intelligence only as Lilly's own use of it and its regulation; GLP1
  (from 2023-08-08) is scoped to the snacks, beverages and devices that GLP-1 obesity drugs displace, and Lilly makes those drugs (the PFE
  Metsera reading). The 10-Ks' patent, competition and compounded-incretin risk factors stay in the "why" ("LLY 2022-2026").

  UNH (UnitedHealth Group) in 2008-2009 carries none: no theme in the registry is live for a health benefits company (OFFSHORE, from
  2004-11-05, is scoped to IT services; CLOUD is not live before 2012-10-30), so its watch list is empty and the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks'
  medical-cost risk ("We must effectively manage our health care costs.", then "If we fail to effectively estimate ... and manage our health
  care costs") and the FY2008 10-K's proposed health care reforms stay in the "why": the underwriting risk is the business's own, and reform
  is policy, not a substitution theme in the registry ("UNH").

  UNH 2010-2013 carries none either: CLOUD, live from 2012-10-30, is scoped to on-premise hardware, storage, databases and data-center
  outsourcing, and no FY2009-FY2012 10-K contains "cloud" or "offshore"; from 2012-11-02 the "why" quotes every live theme's registered
  scope (the CB 2014-2017 wording, used here from the first date it applies). The health reform legislation the 10-Ks discuss is
  regulation, not a substitution theme, and the medical-cost risk factor stays in the "why" ("UNH 2010-2013").

  UNH 2022-2026 carries none: GENAI (from 2022-11-30) is scoped to AI substituting software seats, IT services and BPO hours, information,
  search, education and mobility, and the FY2023-FY2025 10-Ks name generative AI only in UnitedHealth Group's own information systems and
  products; GLP1 (from 2023-08-08) is scoped to the snacks, beverages and devices that GLP-1 drugs displace, and no FY2021-FY2025 10-K names
  GLP-1 drugs. The medical-cost risk factor stays in the "why" ("UNH 2022-2026").

  CRM (salesforce.com) in 2008-2009 carries none: no theme in the registry is live for a subscription software company (OFFSHORE, from
  2004-11-05, is scoped to IT services; CLOUD is not live before 2012-10-30), so its watch list is empty. The FY2008 and FY2009 10-Ks' cloud
  computing words ("Cloud computing refers to the use of Internet (“cloud”) based computing, storage and connectivity technology", FY2009)
  describe salesforce.com's own model, the side that displaces on-premise software, and stay in the "why" with the 10-Ks' competition from
  Oracle, SAP and Microsoft (the PEP obesity rule); whether these earlier filings should move CLOUD's live date is left to the owner (the
  MSFT and XOM precedent) ("CRM"). CRM 2010-2012 carries none either: from CLOUD's live date the "why" quotes both live themes' scopes
  (from 2012-11-02), and the FY2010-FY2012 10-Ks name cloud computing as salesforce.com's own model ("enterprise cloud computing", then
  "enterprise cloud computing and social enterprise solutions") and no offshore delivery ("CRM 2010-2012").

  SCHW (The Charles Schwab Corporation) in 2008-2009 carries none: no theme in the registry is live for a securities broker and bank
  (OFFSHORE, from 2004-11-05, is scoped to IT services; CLOUD is not live before 2012-10-30; CRYPTO, the one theme whose scope names banks
  and exchanges, not before 2020-10-21), so its watch list is empty and the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks' market-environment and price-competition
  risk factors stay in the "why": a cycle and a competitive field, not a substitution theme in the registry ("SCHW"). It stays empty
  through 2021: CRYPTO (from 2020-10-21) is the first live theme whose scope names banks and exchanges, but no FY2017-FY2020 10-K names
  cryptocurrency, blockchain, digital assets or a distributed ledger, so nothing dated ties it to Schwab (the "why" says so; the SPGI
  2018-2021 reading, where JPM and V rest on their own 10-Ks' crypto words), and EV and the rest are scoped to other industries
  ("SCHW 2018-2021").

  NEE (FPL Group) in 2008-2009 carries none: no theme in the registry is live for an electric utility before ENERGY_TRANSITION (2015-12-12;
  OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services), so its watch list is empty and the FY2006-FY2008 10-Ks' environmental risk factor on "climate change"
  (FY2008: also "greenhouse gas emissions, CO2 emissions" and "renewable portfolio standards") stays in the "why" (the PEP obesity rule), as
  for SO ("NEE"). It stays empty through 2013: from 2012-11-02 the "why" quotes every live theme's scope (OFFSHORE, CLOUD), neither of which
  names an electric utility, and the FY2009-FY2012 10-Ks keep the GHG risk factor in the "why" ("NEE 2010-2013").

## Workflow

```bash
# 1. add newly published facts to retro/facts/ACN.json (each with source + published date)
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2023-01-01 2023-06-30        # dates chosen by rule, models generated
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2008-01-01 2008-01-31        # any era with a history vintage in the fact sheet
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2008-05-05 2008-09-30        # start a range on a Monday when the prior week is built
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2008-10-06 2008-12-31
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2009-01-05 2009-12-31
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2010-01-04 2010-12-31
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2011-01-03 2011-12-31
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2012-01-02 2012-12-31
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2013-01-07 2014-12-31
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2015-01-05 2016-12-31
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2017-01-02 2018-12-31
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2019-01-07 2020-12-31
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2021-01-04 2022-12-31        # the 2023 range continues it ("The 2023 pilot, harmonized")
python3 retro/build_acn.py --weekly 2023-07-03 2026-10-23        # last date 2026-10-22 (see "July 2023 to October 2026")
python3 retro/build_acn.py 2008-02-08 2008-02-15 2008-02-22 2008-02-29 2008-03-07 2008-03-14 2008-03-20 \
                           2008-03-28 2008-04-04 2008-04-11 2008-04-18 2008-04-25 2008-04-30   # built by date; include in regressions
for d in archive/retrospective/ACN/2023-*/; do
  python3 retro/retro_tool.py run "$d" && python3 retro/retro_tool.py outcome "$d"
done
python3 retro/retro_tool.py series ACN                           # -> archive/retrospective/ACN/SERIES.md
```

**Picking the weekly dates.** The builder uses one date per ISO week: the last
trading day, except in an earnings week, where it takes the first trading day
*after* the release. The release and the market's reaction are then both in the
information set.

**Scoring a single stock.** One stock's 2-year point return depends on where the
price happened to be that day. ACN entries from January–February 2023 land on the
February 2025 peak; those from April 2023 land after the drop. Judge a series by
`return_to_avg_price_m12_m24_pct` and treat `call_check_2y` as a rough tick. One
stock over a few months mostly tests "buy lower". Testing stock selection needs
many tickers on the same dates.

### Adding dates (the per-year procedure)

Each step exists because skipping it once let something through. Tools are in `retro/tools/`; downloaded
filings go in the session scratchpad, not the repo (every source's URL is in the fact sheet).

1. **List the filings** from `data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json` (older years are in the paginated
   `filings.files`). Keep `acceptanceDateTime`: it is UTC, and a filing accepted after 16:00 ET counts from the
   next trading day. Read every 8-K in the period (items 2.02, 7.01, 8.01) for guidance changes, not only earnings.
   `python3 retro/tools/edgar.py index CIK <dir>` writes `<dir>/allrows.json` (every page), and
   `edgar.py list <dir> --from START --to END --forms 8-K 10-Q 10-K` prints them with their items.
2. **Download** with a generic `User-Agent` (never the owner's email), convert with
   `python3 -I retro/tools/html2rows.py <file.htm>`. `edgar.py fetch CIK <dir> --from START --to END --forms ...`
   does both: full submissions into `<dir>/tenk|tenq|eightk|other/<ACC>.txt`, split into `<ACC>/<TYPE>__<file>` with a
   `.rows.txt` beside each HTML document (`edgar.py split` on a file already downloaded). Keep `<dir>` in the scratchpad.
3. **Note the release time** (the conference-call time in the release): before the open or after the close.
   `edgar.py when <dir> ACC --ticker T` prints the acceptance time in ET and the date the fact gets, in the words the
   fact sheets' `filed` fields use.
4. **Transcribe** prints, the history vintage and 10-K theme events into `retro/facts/ACN.json`. Rules that
   recur: numbers only (a guide restated in words keeps the last numeric range), company figures excluding
   one-offs when published, bookings growth in local currency derived from the FX impact the release states,
   group dollar weights year to date with the latest quarter's LC growth, the ten fiscal years to the latest one.
   A generator script beats hand transcription: it reads each raw figure from its own row by label, computes every rate,
   asserts each quotation in its own filing and writes the verbatim checklist. `retro/generators/schw/` is a worked
   example (gen_schw.py's docstring lists the downloads); commit the generator with the sheet, so a later session can regenerate the
   sheet byte for byte from the filings and extend it without retyping.
5. **Check every value word for word** with `python3 -I retro/tools/verbatim.py checklist.json`, each string
   against its own filing.
6. **Regression:** rebuild every earlier range; `git status archive` must show nothing.
7. **Build** the new range (`build_acn.py --weekly START END`; start on the Monday after the last built week),
   then `retro_tool.py run` and `retro_tool.py outcome` on each new date, `retro_tool.py index` and `series ACN`.
8. **Firewall:** commit, then `python3 retro/tools/firewall.py <first day after the range>` must report 0 changes.
   Controls: alter one value of each new print or vintage and check that exactly the dates after its release change:
   `python3 retro/tools/controls.py T START END` (in memory, nothing on disk changes; the builders with the common
   `build(as_of, facts, raw, spx, engine, out)`; exits non-zero if a control changes an earlier date).
9. **Scan** the new outputs for years after the as-of date (other than FY labels, SEC accession numbers and the
   `generated` stamp), anachronistic vocabulary, and facts from the next print appearing early. Three scans take any
   fact sheet (`retro/tools/factwalk.py` reads every dated fact, nested restatements and `*_later` fields as facts of
   their own dates):
   - `python3 retro/tools/leak_scan.py T [--from START]`: no model holds a string or 4-digit figure of a later fact
     (hits must be read: SCHW's three were trading-day counts in the P/E-window comment);
   - `python3 retro/tools/forward_refs.py T [--from START]`: the author's own words in a fact (quotations, rows and
     `next_print` left out) name no later quarter, year or date;
   - `python3 -I retro/tools/selftext.py T --filings <dir> [--from START]`: every capitalized name, dollar figure and
     year in a fact's own words is in a filing published by its date (method words and tickers pass; `--allow` more).
   They were checked on SCHW (0 leaks, 0 forward references, 0 misses, each catching a planted later fact). Run on the
   other sheets, `forward_refs.py` also lists words copied from filings outside single quotes and dates the filings
   state themselves (notes due 2018, buybacks through 2009): review aids, not findings, and not yet reviewed there.
10. **Commit and push**; report the judgement calls plainly.

Shell pitfall: write any text with a `$` in it (findings, README sections, notes) through a quoted heredoc (`<<'EOF'`)
or a file, never an unquoted one. Unquoted, the shell expands `$0`, `$1`, ... inside it: the SCHW findings once lost
"$0.68" to "/bin/bash.68" and needed a corrective commit. And check each step's exit status before a chained `git commit`.

**A new ticker** needs its own fact sheet. The engine is generic except for its
signal names and thresholds, so give it a sibling template if the business needs
different signals.

Data sources that worked from the cloud session:

- **Prices and dividends:** the Yahoo chart API (cached in `retro/.cache/`).
- **EPS, revenue and share history with filing dates:** SEC XBRL company facts
  (`data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK##########.json`). SEC asks for a
  `User-Agent` with a contact. Use a project or role address, not a personal one.
- **Quarterly detail:** the 8-K earnings exhibits listed in
  `data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK##########.json`.
- **SEC's two hosts differ** (seen 2026-11-27, CRM 2013-2017). `data.sec.gov` (the submissions index and XBRL company facts) accepted
  a plain client name. `www.sec.gov` (every filing document) refused it, and a GitHub no-reply address too, with "Your Request
  Originates from an Undeclared Automated Tool". Ask the owner for a deliverable project or role contact before a batch starts.
  Never guess one, and never use the owner's personal email. Without one, only the XBRL company facts can be read: the reduced-data
  batch of "CRM 2013-2017". On 2026-11-27 (CRM 2022-2026, and SCHW 2008-2009 the same day) `www.sec.gov` served every
  document to a generic client name with no contact address, so try it first at the start of each batch and say in the
  section which data the batch had: the refusal may not recur.

## Which model to run it on

Pricing per million tokens, input / output (cached 2026-10-06): Haiku 5.5
$0.10 / $0.50, Sonnet 5.5 $2 / $10, Opus 5.5 $4 / $20, Fable 5.1 $10 / $50.

With the builder, the model's job is to **extend fact sheets**: read a filing,
transcribe dated numbers, cite them. Dates, statistics, scenarios and
classification are code.

- **Sonnet 5.5** (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) at effort `high` is the cheapest model
  that does this reliably.
- **Opus 5.5:** use it to set up a new ticker (choosing signals, era themes and
  evidence) and to review fact sheets.
- **Haiku 5.5:** can do raw extraction if every number is checked against the
  filing.

No model is blind: every current model knows what happened after 2023. The
protection is the dated fact sheet, the frozen rules and the validator, not the
choice of model.
